dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level for students at the Diploma schools reachable from Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai. Each is matched to one subject and one level rather than to a general curriculum label, because in the Diploma that is the unit that determines whether an hour converts into marks.

intro.heading: A proximity search answers the wrong question
paragraphs: Al Mankhool sits in a dense part of old Dubai where almost everything is close. The Bur Dubai schools are minutes away, Karama is across the road, Oud Metha's school belt is a short drive, and the creek and Deira are not far. A search for an IB tutor near me in Al Mankhool therefore returns plenty of results, and the parent is left comparing them on the only axis the search offered: how close they are.

Distance is not the variable that decides whether the sessions work. The Diploma is six subjects drawn from six groups, taken at two levels, each with its own written components, its own internally assessed piece and its own grading criteria. A tutor who is strong in Economics Standard Level is not therefore useful for Biology Higher Level, and a tutor who is excellent at Mathematics has no particular insight into what a History essay has to do to reach the top band. Within the Diploma, subject and level is the unit of competence. Everything else, including geography, is secondary.

This is where a lot of Diploma tuition in this district quietly underdelivers. A family finds somebody nearby who teaches the IB, the sessions are pleasant and well-organised, and the student's marks move slightly or not at all. The tutor was competent. They were simply not a specialist in the component that was losing the marks, and nobody had established which component that was.

So this page starts from the syllabus rather than from the neighbourhood. What each subject group's assessment actually consists of, and where its marks are habitually lost. What the command terms demand, because in the Diploma the difference between describe, explain, discuss and evaluate is worth more marks than most content gaps. What each subject's internal assessment is, and exactly where a tutor's legitimate help ends. What Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay require, since they are the two components almost nobody tutors competently. And how to use a past paper properly, which almost no student does.

One structural fact about this district is worth holding onto while you read. Because the schools in Bur Dubai, Karama and Al Mankhool largely run to sixteen, most Diploma students here have moved campus, and their six-subject combination was settled at a school the family had known for weeks rather than years. Nobody at home has a long history with the way that school runs its internal deadlines, which supervisor takes which Extended Essay subject, or how its mock papers are marked. That is a real information gap, and it is the reason the first useful conversation with a tutor is about components and criteria rather than about topics.

A note on what you will not find here. No IB session or results date is published on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and a date a family plans around should not rest on a guess. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org. Everything else below is either from a named source or is a description of how the assessment works, and we would rather say nothing than publish a figure we cannot stand behind.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and a student in this district may be at any point in it. What a tutor should be doing differs completely between the stages, because the assessment model changes rather than merely getting harder.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects from six groups, three usually at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries written components and an internally assessed piece. Grades are awarded 1 to 7 per subject against published criteria, with additional points available from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision near Al Mankhool sits mostly outward from the district - Al Jaddaf, across the creek toward Festival City, and out toward Nad Al Sheba - because the schools in Bur Dubai and Karama largely run to sixteen. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 places in total, so that map is still changing.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each on a 1-8 scale, with no terminal examination papers in most schools. Because the criteria reward process and reflection rather than recall, a student can be strong in MYP and still be unprepared for the Diploma's written components - and the reverse is also true.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student continues from MYP into the Diploma at the same school, the internal assessment skills transfer and the written-paper discipline is the gap. Where a student arrives from IGCSE instead, written papers feel familiar and the internally assessed work is the unfamiliar part. Knowing which of the two your child is predicts most of what they will need.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and an exhibition in the final year. Support at this stage is about literacy and numeracy fundamentals and about the habits of structured written explanation, which is where the eventual Diploma marks begin even though nothing is being assessed for a grade yet.
programmes.countryNote: Several continuum schools within reach of Al Mankhool run the PYP, and families who intend the Diploma later sometimes assume the pathway makes preparation automatic. It does not. The written discipline the Diploma rewards has to be built deliberately somewhere between Year 5 and Year 11, and the earlier it starts the cheaper it is.

programmes.name: The IGCSE route into the Diploma
programmes.description: The majority route in this part of Dubai, since the schools in Bur Dubai, Karama and Oud Metha largely run Cambridge or Pearson qualifications to sixteen. Subject choices at this stage constrain which Higher Levels are realistic afterwards, with mathematics and the sciences the usual pinch points.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for a family in Al Mankhool is that the Diploma usually means a change of campus, a longer day and an unfamiliar assessment model all arriving in the same September. A short bridging block in the summer beforehand, aimed at the specific subjects chosen, is the cheapest intervention available in the whole two years.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects fail in characteristic ways, and the characteristic failure is usually more recoverable than the content. Below are the subjects students in this district most often need, with where the marks actually go in each.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Marks are lost on analysis that describes a text's content instead of examining how the writer produces an effect. The individual oral and the paper on unseen texts both reward a line of argument sustained across the response rather than a sequence of observations.

subjects.name: English B and language acquisition
subjects.description: Students with strong conversational fluency frequently underperform because the assessment rewards register, structure and the handling of a specific text type. Learning the conventions of each required text type moves marks faster than general practice does.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra and calculus route. The commonest loss is method marks forfeited by working mentally and writing only an answer, followed by question misinterpretation - executing a correct technique on a question that asked for something else.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. Marks go missing in the written interpretation rather than the arithmetic: a model's limitations have to be stated and evaluated, and students who compute well often say nothing about what the model cannot do.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, so students revise by reading and feel prepared. The marks sit in data interpretation, in the precision of definitions and in explaining mechanisms step by step rather than naming them. Past-paper work exposes this within one session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic chemistry take most of the hours. The extended-response questions reward linked reasoning rather than a list of correct facts, which is a trainable structure and therefore one of the cheaper things to fix.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Often a mathematics problem wearing a physics badge: the student explains the mechanism correctly and then cannot rearrange, resolve components or read a gradient. Diagnose which before buying physics hours, because the two need different teaching.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams and evaluation carry the upper bands. Students who learn definitions and ignore the evaluation requirement cap themselves in the middle of the range however much content they add. Higher Level's quantitative element catches out those who chose it as a non-mathematical subject.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the specific case is what distinguishes the bands. Generic answers about a concept score poorly against answers that use the given organisation's actual circumstances, and that discipline is quick to teach and rarely taught.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Argument rather than narrative. The most frequent failure is a chronological account where the question asked for an evaluation of causes or significance, and the source paper demands a specific technique for comparing and assessing provenance.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence for a claim, not recounted. Marks are lost by describing research in detail without connecting it to the question's demand, and by neglecting the critical evaluation the upper bands require.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and the arts group
subjects.description: Assessment rests on the comparative study, the process portfolio and the exhibition, all of which reward documented thinking over finished output. Students who make strong work and document it thinly lose marks they have already earned.

sections.heading: Six subject groups, six different assessments
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a parent can understand about the Diploma is that it is not one qualification with six subjects in it. It is six separate assessment regimes that happen to be sat by the same student. The sciences carry an internally assessed investigation and reward precise mechanism. The language A subjects carry an oral and reward sustained argument about how a text works. Mathematics carries an exploration and rewards visible method. The individuals and societies group rewards evaluation and the handling of sources. The arts reward documented process.

That is why the question "can you tutor the IB?" has no useful answer. The right question names a subject and a level and then asks what that subject's components are and which one the student is losing marks on. A tutor who cannot answer that for your child's specific subject within the first session is not going to be able to fix it in the tenth.

The practical consequence for a family in Al Mankhool with two children or with a child needing two subjects is that one tutor is rarely the efficient answer. Two specialists on two subjects, each knowing one set of criteria properly, outperform one capable generalist across both - and because delivery is online the scheduling of two back-to-back hours is straightforward rather than a logistical problem.

The table below sets out what each group's assessment actually consists of and where the marks habitually go. Confirm component weightings from your school's subject outline; the shape of the assessment is what is described here, not the percentages.

sections.heading: Command terms are the cheapest marks in the Diploma
paragraphs: Across every Diploma subject, the instruction at the start of the question determines the shape of the answer that scores. State wants a fact with no justification. Describe wants an account of features. Explain wants a mechanism or a reason. Compare wants similarities and differences held together rather than two separate descriptions. Discuss wants a balanced consideration. Evaluate and to what extent want a judgement, supported, with the counter-case acknowledged.

Students lose enormous numbers of marks to this and almost nobody teaches it, because it is not content and so does not feel like teaching. The pattern is always the same: a student who knows the material writes a competent description in response to an explain command and scores half the available marks. They leave the exam feeling it went well, because they did write everything they knew. The gap between what they know and what their grade says is sitting entirely in the verb.

This is the first thing to look for in a marked script, and it is visible within minutes. Take the script, find every question where the student scored below half, and read the command term. If the same verb keeps appearing, that is the plan for the next three sessions, and it will move more marks per hour than any topic work. It also transfers across subjects, which is rare: a student trained to answer evaluate properly in Economics writes better History essays as a side effect.

The table gives the common terms, what the examiner is looking for, and the wrong answer students reliably produce instead. Subject guides define command terms formally - take the authoritative wording from your child's own subject guide.

sections.heading: Every subject's internal assessment, and where help has to stop
paragraphs: Each Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component written by the student, at home, over weeks, against published criteria. These components are where the most marks are available per hour of work and where the most marks are casually thrown away - and they are the part of the Diploma most exposed to help that crosses a line.

The boundary is not vague, and stating it plainly is a service rather than a disclaimer. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards and in what band. A tutor may test whether a research question, topic or prompt can actually sustain the work required. A tutor may model a technique on a completely different example. A tutor may read the student's own draft and question reasoning that does not hold. A tutor may point out that a section does not address the criterion it is meant to address. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of it.

IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work. That matters commercially as well as ethically, because this search result contains operations that do: one sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published dirham price. Under IB academic-honesty rules that is a malpractice trigger, and the finding lands on the student rather than on the seller. A parent buying it is buying a risk on their child's behalf.

We also do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those are published and owned by the IB, your child's school holds the current versions, and a tutor's work is to teach against them rather than to hand them over. sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which almost nobody tutors well
paragraphs: Two components sit outside the six subjects and carry points toward the Diploma total: the Extended Essay, an independent research piece, and Theory of Knowledge, assessed through an exhibition and an essay. Together they are the most neglected part of the Diploma in the tutoring market, partly because they are hard to teach and partly because neither fits the subject-specialist model that the rest of the programme rewards.

The Extended Essay fails for a predictable reason: the research question. A question that is too broad produces a summary rather than an argument; a question that is too narrow runs out of material; a question in the wrong subject cannot be assessed against that subject's criteria. All three are fixed cheaply at the start and expensively later, which is why the useful sessions happen before the student has written anything rather than after they have written a draft they are attached to.

Theory of Knowledge fails differently. Students treat it as an essay about opinions and write assertively without the discipline the criteria actually ask for: working with knowledge claims, examining how different areas of knowledge justify what they claim, and using examples that do real argumentative work rather than decorating a point already made. It is teachable, it is rarely taught, and the marks are available.

The supervisor for both is appointed by the school, and the school's internal deadlines govern the timetable. A tutor's role is explicitly subordinate to that: coaching the thinking, testing the question, explaining the criteria, questioning the draft. Not writing it, not editing it to completion, and not replacing the supervisor. Ask the school for the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge deadlines at the start of the year; they are earlier than students assume and they are the dates everything else has to fit around.

sections.heading: How to use a past paper, since almost nobody does
paragraphs: Past papers are the most available and least well used resource in the Diploma. The typical pattern is that a student attempts one, checks the answers, notes that they got some wrong, and moves on. That extracts perhaps a tenth of the value. A paper used properly produces a diagnosis that redirects the next month of work, and the process takes about twice as long as sitting the paper.

Sit it under real conditions first: full time, no notes, no pausing, no looking anything up. A paper attempted at leisure tests knowledge; a paper attempted under time tests the thing the exam tests. Then mark it against the official mark scheme rather than against a general sense of whether the answer was right, because the mark scheme is where the marks actually are and it frequently awards credit a student did not know they had earned, and withholds credit they assumed was theirs.

Then audit. For every lost mark, assign one of four causes: the content was not known, the method was not shown, the question was misread, or the time ran out. Count the four. In most scripts the first is not the largest, which is uncomfortable because it is the one tuition is usually bought to address. The other three are faster to fix and the repairs are specific rather than general.

Finally, keep the script. A single marked and audited paper is worth more to a tutor in the first session than any amount of description of how the student is getting on, and a sequence of them across a year shows whether the plan is working. Families in this district who bring one marked script to a trial lesson get a materially better diagnosis than those who bring a report card.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level are not the same job
paragraphs: Three of the six Diploma subjects are usually taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and the difference is not simply volume. Higher Level carries additional content, an additional written component in several subjects, and - most importantly for planning - a cumulative structure in the sciences and mathematics where later topics assume fluency with earlier handling. A student who got through the first year on intuition meets the consequence in the second.

That changes what the weekly hour is for. A Standard Level student is generally well served by an hour tracking the school's current topic. A Higher Level student in a cumulative subject needs part of most sessions spent keeping earlier material alive, which students resist because it feels like going backwards. Skipping it is why Higher Level grades sometimes fall in the second year despite steady work.

The level mix also determines where a limited budget should go. A Higher Level subject that the student intends to use for university entry, with a cumulative structure and an internally assessed component, is worth more support than a Standard Level subject that is already stable. Spreading support thinly across all six is the most common way to spend a Diploma tuition budget without changing a single grade.

sections.heading: What a specialist costs in this market, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families start and it is worth understanding what the money buys. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At that level the tutor is typically a university student, and for consolidating a Standard Level subject the student already broadly understands, that can be a reasonable purchase. What it does not buy is somebody who knows a specific Higher Level subject's criteria band by band.

The next step up is the qualified subject tutor working online, which Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026, puts at AED 150 to 300 an hour, and Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200. Above that sits specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. Each of those figures belongs to the provider named, and none is an IB Gram price.

The question is not which band is best but which band the specific job needs. A component repair block on the History source paper needs a specialist and is short - three to five sessions - so the hourly rate matters less than the match. A year of consolidation in a stable Standard Level subject needs competence rather than specialism and should not be bought at the specialist rate. Buying the specialist band for everything is how a Diploma budget disappears without a grade moving.

Monthly figures make this easier to see. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, near AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, near AED 200 to 225 for the same eight hours. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes inspection reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

On the tutor side there is a check a parent can make for themselves. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Operating without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

A separate instrument governs tutoring businesses with premises: a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, no regulator accreditation and no UAE office, and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. One further rule: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Finally, the mandatory block, which affects every Diploma timetable in Dubai. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited.

process.title: Name the subject and the level
process.description: Not "IB tutoring" but Chemistry Higher Level, or History Standard Level, or Mathematics Applications and Interpretation Higher Level. That is the unit we match on, because the components and criteria differ so much between subjects that a general IB tutor is a weaker match than a narrow specialist.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: The most recent marked paper or piece of coursework, however poor. A marked script tells a tutor in five minutes what a report comment cannot say in an hour: whether the losses are content, method, command-term misreading or timing.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the specialist
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video at no charge, with the tutor matched to that subject and level. It is a teaching session, not a sales call, and the output should be a named diagnosis rather than a general impression of how things went.

process.title: A plan sized by the diagnosis
process.description: Sometimes a term of weekly work on a cumulative Higher Level subject. Often a three-to-five session component repair block aimed at one question type. We would rather sell the shorter thing that fixes the problem than the longer thing that postpones it.

process.title: Core components on the school's calendar
process.description: If the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge or an internal assessment is in play, we work from the school's internal deadlines rather than from the exam window, because those are the dates that actually govern the work and they are earlier than students expect.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level
whyPoints.description: The Diploma is six assessment regimes sat by one student. We match a specialist to one subject at one level rather than offering general IB tutoring, because knowing one subject's criteria band by band is what converts an hour into marks.

whyPoints.title: Command terms taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: The gap between what a student knows and what their grade says usually sits in the verb at the start of the question. We train describe, explain, discuss and evaluate directly on the student's own scripts, and the training transfers across subjects.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks where short blocks fix it
whyPoints.description: A single failing component - the History source paper, the Economics evaluation question, Biology data analysis - is usually three to five sessions, not a term. We scope from a marked script and stop when the component is reliable.

whyPoints.title: The Extended Essay and TOK taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Both carry points toward the Diploma total and both are neglected in this market. We work on research-question viability and on the criteria that actually distinguish bands, inside the school supervisor's authority rather than around it.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, test topics, model techniques on other examples and question the student's own draft. They do not write, draft, rewrite or supply any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, and we supply no board documents.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be shown
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no UAE office, no grade guarantees, no IB dates we have not verified, and every dirham figure attributed to the provider that published it with the month it was read. Ask any provider claiming more to evidence it.

faqs.question: Why does matching on subject matter more than finding a tutor close to Al Mankhool?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma is six separate assessment regimes rather than one curriculum. The sciences carry an investigation and reward precise mechanism; the language A subjects carry an oral and reward sustained argument; individuals and societies rewards evaluation and source handling. A tutor strong in one of those has no particular advantage in another. In a dense district like this one, plenty of tutors are nearby, and the one that matters is the one who knows your child's specific subject and level criteria band by band.

faqs.question: My child knows the material but the grades do not reflect it. Where is it going?
faqs.answer: Usually into the command term. State, describe, explain, compare, discuss and evaluate each demand a different shape of answer, and a student who writes a competent description in response to an explain command scores roughly half the available marks while feeling the exam went well. Take a marked script, find every question scored below half, and read the verb. If the same verb recurs, that is the next three sessions, and it moves more marks per hour than topic work. It also transfers to other subjects.

faqs.question: How should we actually use a past paper at home?
faqs.answer: Sit it under real conditions - full time, no notes, no pausing - because a paper attempted at leisure tests knowledge rather than what the exam tests. Then mark it against the official mark scheme, not against a general sense of correctness. Then audit every lost mark into one of four causes: content not known, method not shown, question misread, time ran out, and count them. In most scripts the content category is not the largest, which redirects the plan. Finally keep the script; it is the most useful document a tutor can see.

faqs.question: Is one tutor across two Diploma subjects a sensible saving?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and this is one of the few places where buying twice is cheaper in outcome. The criteria, components and mark-scheme habits of two subjects in different groups have almost nothing in common, so a single tutor covering both is a generalist in each. Two specialists running back-to-back hours cost more per week and produce more per hour. Because sessions are delivered online rather than by somebody driving between appointments, arranging two consecutive hours is straightforward rather than a logistical problem.

faqs.question: Which components are worth paying a specialist for, and which are not?
faqs.answer: Pay specialist rates where the subject is cumulative, taken at Higher Level, carries an internally assessed component, and is named by the university route your child is actually pursuing. Do not pay specialist rates for consolidating a Standard Level subject that is already stable - competent, cheaper support handles that. The most common way a Diploma budget disappears without a grade moving is buying the specialist band thinly across all six subjects rather than concentrating it on the two that matter.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Explain what each criterion rewards and in which band. Test whether a chosen topic, research question or prompt can sustain the work required. Model a technique on a completely different example. Read the student's own draft and question reasoning that does not hold. Point out where a section fails to address the criterion it is meant to. What a tutor may not do is write, draft, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of it. IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work, and the malpractice finding would land on your child.

faqs.question: How do we stop the Extended Essay going wrong?
faqs.answer: Get the research question right, because that is where the grade is decided and it costs nothing to fix at the start. Too broad produces a summary rather than an argument; too narrow runs out of material halfway; the wrong subject cannot be assessed against that subject's criteria. All three are cheap to correct before anything is written and expensive afterwards, once the student is attached to a draft. Ask the school for the supervisor's name and the internal deadlines at the start of the year rather than in the term they fall.

faqs.question: Can anybody actually teach Theory of Knowledge, or is it unteachable?
faqs.answer: It is teachable and it is rarely taught, which is why marks are available there. Students treat it as an essay about opinions and write confidently without the discipline the criteria ask for: working with knowledge claims, examining how different areas of knowledge justify what they assert, and using examples that do genuine argumentative work rather than illustrating a point already made. Those are specific, trainable moves. The school appoints the supervisor and sets the deadlines, and a tutor's role sits inside that authority rather than replacing it.

faqs.question: My child's Higher Level grades fell in the second year despite steady work. Why?
faqs.answer: Most often because the subject is cumulative and the first year was got through on intuition rather than on secure method. In the sciences and mathematics, later topics assume fluency with the handling of earlier ones, so a student who never consolidated the early material meets the consequence twelve months later rather than immediately. The fix is unpopular: part of each session spent revisiting earlier handling, which feels like going backwards. An audit at the end of year one against what year two assumes prevents it entirely.

faqs.question: We are moving from IGCSE into the Diploma. What is the real gap?
faqs.answer: The assessment model more than the content. An IGCSE student arrives comfortable with written papers and unfamiliar with internally assessed work, extended independent research and criteria-based marking. A student arriving from MYP has the opposite profile: at ease with criteria and process, less drilled on timed written papers. Identify which of the two your child is, because it determines what the first term needs. A short bridging block in the summer beforehand, scoped to the actual subjects chosen, is the cheapest intervention in the two years.

faqs.question: What does IB tutoring cost around Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates start at AED 33 to 65 an hour - Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 - which typically buys a university student rather than a subject specialist. Qualified online tuition runs AED 150 to 300 on Bestimate's Dubai rate table, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB provision is AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500. All read October 2026, all theirs rather than ours.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an Al Mankhool apartment?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. For Diploma work that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: the pool becomes every specialist on your child's exact subject and level rather than the few qualified people prepared to drive into this district at a fixed hour, and marked scripts and diagrams sit on a shared screen both people can annotate.

faqs.question: How do we verify that a private tutor is permitted to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask, and know what a correct answer looks like. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs the tutor nothing, no part of a quoted rate is a permit fee. Working without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, nobody should be quoting you an amount.

faqs.question: Should we ask a teacher at my child's own school for private lessons?
faqs.answer: Better not to. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on exact wording, but the principle is sound and the conflict of interest is real. A specialist with no stake in the school's own results is a cleaner arrangement for everybody involved.

faqs.question: Can you confirm the session and results dates so we can plan the year?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them from the IB itself. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and a date a family plans a year around should not rest on a secondary guess. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org. What we can plan from are the school-set milestones that actually govern the work: internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay deadline, and the mock window.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist in our subject and level is free?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of filling the hour with a general IB tutor. Common combinations usually match quickly; narrower ones - a less-taught language, a specific arts route, some Higher Level options - take longer, and the honest choices are to wait for the right person, to start with a related specialist on a clearly stated interim basis, or not to book. Because delivery is online, the pool is every specialist available on that subject and level rather than only those who would travel into Al Mankhool.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.closingHeading: Name the subject, bring a script, take the trial
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mankhool.closingBody: Three things turn a search for a nearby tutor into a plan that works. Name the subject and the level rather than the curriculum, because that is the unit the Diploma assesses and the unit a specialist occupies. Bring one marked script, however poor it looks, because it shows in minutes whether the marks are going to content, method, command terms or the clock. Then take a free trial lesson with the specialist matched to that subject and let the diagnosis decide whether you need a term of weekly work or a three-session repair block. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mizhar.tutorsIntro: These are the IB specialists currently taking students from Al Mizhar and the neighbouring eastern communities, listed by subject and level. The same list is available whichever of these districts you live in, which is the point of this page.

intro.heading: Al Mizhar against the next district over, and the answer that does not change
paragraphs: Parents comparing neighbourhoods for tutoring are doing something sensible, because neighbourhoods in this part of Dubai genuinely differ. Al Mizhar is villa territory beyond Mirdif, with large plots, long school bus routes and almost no commercial provision inside it. Mirdif has the schools and the shopping. Al Khawaneej sits further out again with the longest journeys in the cluster. Al Warqa has the biggest cohorts. Al Rashidiya, west towards the airport, is compact and apartment-heavy with no school of its own.

Those differences matter for several things. They change what an in-home tutor charges, because the rate carries a round trip and the trip to Al Khawaneej is not the trip to Al Rashidiya. They change what time a lesson can start, because a collecting bus route out of Al Warqa is not a fifteen-minute run from Al Garhoud. They change whether there is anywhere nearby to take a group class. They change the practicalities of the household: a villa usually has a room with a door, an apartment sometimes does not.

What they do not change is the thing a Diploma student actually needs, which is somebody who has taught the specific component their marks are leaving from. The Diploma is six subjects at two levels plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Higher Level chemistry, the mathematical exploration and the individual oral in English A are three narrow specialisms, and the IB accounts for roughly seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on a UK curriculum. The pool of local people who have taught any one of those components is small in Al Mizhar, and it is equally small in Mirdif, Al Khawaneej, Al Warqa and Al Rashidiya.

That is the comparison this page makes. Everything that varies between these districts is logistics, and logistics is the part online delivery removes. IB Gram teaches one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service offered only in India, so nobody is driving to any of these addresses. The result is that a family in Al Khawaneej and a family in Mirdif get the same shortlist, drawn from everybody who teaches the component rather than from everybody willing to make that particular drive.

It is worth saying what this page is not. It is not an argument that neighbourhoods are interchangeable, because they plainly are not: a family choosing where to live in this corridor is choosing an hour of their child's day either way, and that is a real decision with real consequences for homework, sleep and sport. The argument is narrower. Of the handful of variables a tutoring arrangement depends on, the ones the map controls are the ones online delivery makes irrelevant, and the one it cannot control is the one that decides the grade.

The rest of this page sets out the district comparison with figures, then turns to the things that are genuinely the same everywhere: what the Diploma assesses, which components are scarce, what the Internal Assessment demands, and what changes if your family moves to another emirate, which in this corridor happens more often than people expect.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mizhar.programmesIntro: The programmes available to a family in this cluster are the same whichever of the five districts they live in, because the schools are shared. These are the stages we cover.

programmes.name: The Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the subject groups, typically three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Each subject carries internally assessed work alongside written examinations, and the Diploma is scored out of 45 with core points available from the two core written components combined.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision for this cluster sits mainly in the Mirdif and Al Garhoud directions, so an Al Mizhar family and an Al Khawaneej family are frequently choosing between the same two or three schools. Cohorts are modest, which gives continuity and leaves little slack. Confirm every structural detail with your school's IB coordinator rather than from any third-party page.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria per subject rather than paper marks, which builds research and reflection well and timed-paper technique less well. The step into the Diploma is largely about that technique, with one genuine content exception in mathematics, where the standard MYP route leaves algebraic fluency to be built before Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: Uptown International School is the nearest continuum option for all five of these districts, which means families comparing neighbourhoods are often comparing commutes to the same school. The MYP decision that matters most locally is the Year 9 mathematics streaming, because it follows a student into Diploma course choice two years later.

programmes.name: IGCSE into the Diploma
programmes.description: The commonest crossing in Dubai given that UK-curriculum schools dominate enrolment. IGCSE produces students strong on recall and standard calculation and short on three Diploma habits: justifying a method, handling uncertainty, and writing to command terms that ask for evaluation rather than description.
programmes.countryNote: Students in all five districts make this crossing from British-curriculum schools in Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Mirdif into Diploma places nearby. A bridging block of six to ten sessions in the summer before DP1 removes most of the first-term shock and costs considerably less than the remediation block families otherwise buy in November.

programmes.name: Moving emirate mid-programme
programmes.description: More common in this corridor than families expect, and worth planning for. The Diploma itself is the same qualification wherever it is taught, but the regulator, the inspection regime and sometimes the school calendar change at the emirate border, and school places are not interchangeable. An online tutoring arrangement is the one part of the week that survives the move intact.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai private schools are regulated by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods, not merely inspect.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-mizhar.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects families in this cluster ask about, with a note on how locally scarce each specialism actually is. The scarcity is the same in every one of these districts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic technique and proof, expected by most engineering and physical science degrees. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors, plus a third paper. Locally scarce at Higher Level, and no scarcer in Al Mizhar than in Mirdif.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and data with a heavier statistics load and technology assumed. Not an easy option. Specialists are scarcer than for Analysis and Approaches, because fewer tutors have taught the statistics content to Higher Level standard.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, with Higher Level extensions throughout and fields the commonest breaking point. The narrowest specialism on most Diploma timetables and the clearest case for matching by component rather than by postcode.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity, with the mole underpinning everything and equilibrium the largest conceptual hurdle. Widely needed for medicine-adjacent routes, which makes Higher Level demand high and local supply thin across all five districts.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume plus precision. Extended responses want specific terminology in a specific order, and data-based questions reward analysis rather than recall. More widely covered locally than physics, but still narrow at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the marks, and the internally assessed commentaries on real-world articles have their own timetable. A subject where a specialist and a generalist produce visibly different results.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus material rather than recall of theory, plus a research project on a real organisation. Local availability is better than in the sciences, which makes it a sensible subject to resolve with a general tutor if budget is tight.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing how a text produces an effect, with the individual oral rewarding close reference to specific passages. The oral is the component most often left unrehearsed, and the one where a specialist earns their fee fastest.

subjects.name: History and Global Politics
subjects.description: A sustained argument supported by evidence, with source-based questions rewarding provenance and limitation analysis that students treat as preamble. Reasonable local coverage at Standard Level, thinner at Higher.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition, contributing to the core points. Very few tutors anywhere have taught it properly, which makes it one of the components where geography is entirely irrelevant to finding the right person.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent research essay with a word limit and a supervised process, where the research question decides most of the mark and the process reflections are assessed alongside the essay. Supervision belongs to the school; a tutor coaches method only.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, taught from the school's own approved material. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects, because expectations and the language of instruction differ.

sections.heading: What genuinely differs between these districts, with numbers
paragraphs: Here is the district comparison, built from the three variables that actually move: the length of the school run, what an in-home tutor would be pricing in travel, and what the household can offer in the way of a quiet hour. Every AED figure is from a provider's own published page and is attributed; none is an IB Gram rate.

In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted across a wide band, AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. That band exists largely because the travel component varies, and in this cluster it varies in a predictable order: Mirdif cheapest to reach, then Al Rashidiya and Nad Al Hamar, then Al Warqa and Al Mizhar, then Al Khawaneej. A family comparing quotes between districts is mostly comparing petrol and traffic.

The school run varies in the same order and for the same reasons, and it sets the earliest workable lesson time. Mirdif families can hold an earlier slot; Al Khawaneej and Al Warqa families are usually looking at 6.30pm or a weekend morning. That is a real difference between neighbourhoods and it is worth planning around, whichever kind of tutoring a family buys.

The third variable is the quiet room, and it cuts the other way. The villa districts generally have one; apartment-heavy Al Rashidiya more often does not, and a lesson held in a busy living room at 6pm produces less than the same hour at a bedroom desk. It is worth solving in the first week rather than discovering in month two, and it is the one item on this list a family can fix for nothing.

sections.heading: What does not differ, and why the answer is the same everywhere
paragraphs: Now the other half of the comparison. The Diploma is six subjects at two levels plus three core elements, and each subject carries its own internally assessed work with its own criteria. A student losing marks on Higher Level physics fields, or on the individual oral in English A, or on the mathematical exploration, needs somebody who has taught that component. Not the subject in general. The component.

Those specialisms are scarce in absolute terms, not in local terms. The IB accounts for roughly seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, physics is a minority Diploma choice, Higher Level a minority within that, and Theory of Knowledge is taught properly by very few tutors anywhere. Narrowing that already small population by asking who will drive to Al Mizhar on a Tuesday evening removes most of the remainder, and it removes exactly the same proportion if you ask who will drive to Mirdif or Al Khawaneej.

This is why the district comparison, done honestly, resolves to a single answer. Everything that varies between these neighbourhoods is logistics, and logistics is what online delivery takes off the table. A family in Al Khawaneej with the longest commute in the cluster and a family in Mirdif with the shortest get the same shortlist from us, because the shortlist is built from everybody who teaches the component rather than from everybody within range of a particular villa.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. So the comparison in the table below is between what a map can tell you and what it cannot, and the honest conclusion is that for a Diploma student the map answers the less important question.

sections.heading: If you move emirate: five regulators, one qualification
paragraphs: Families in this cluster move more often than the housing market suggests, and a move to Abu Dhabi, Sharjah or further out changes more than the commute. The Diploma itself is the same qualification wherever it is taught, but the body regulating the school changes at the emirate border, and so does what that body controls.

Dubai private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there and is named by almost nobody writing about tutoring in this market. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

One difference is worth knowing in advance. The Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. Abu Dhabi has its own professional-ethics position too: ADEK's rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct barring the same thing. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document before relying on it.

The practical point for tutoring is simple and slightly surprising. Of everything in a family's week, an online one-to-one arrangement is the part that survives a move between emirates unchanged, because there is no address involved. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the MoHRE, and claims none; what we can do is explain what each body governs and link to its own pages.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what else that money could do
paragraphs: The in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour exists against a published AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and in this cluster the difference is almost entirely the journey. It is worth asking what else the same premium could be spent on, because the answer is not nothing.

Spent on travel, it buys physical presence, which has real value for a younger or restless student and none at all for a Diploma student working through past questions with a mark scheme open. Spent on scarcity instead, the same money moves a family from the qualified-tutor band into the named-specialist band, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table runs AED 200 to 450 and above. That is the difference between somebody who teaches the subject and somebody who has taught the component.

The monthly figures make the choice concrete. Packages in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours. Those are different products rather than different prices, and comparing them requires looking at the session count and length rather than the total. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support.

At the bottom of the market, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour online and Tutopiya's published panel starts lower again, which is a genuine service for middle-years consolidation and thin for Higher Level work. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, which is identical in every district
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed work, and in the sciences and mathematics it commonly accounts for around a fifth of the final grade. That makes it the largest single component outside the written papers, and the single most postcode-independent thing on this page.

What it consists of differs completely between subjects, which is why generic advice about it is worthless. A mathematical exploration is independent written mathematics. A science investigation is experimental or data-based work with a research question and an evaluation. Economics sets commentaries on real-world articles. Business Management sets a project on a real organisation. Languages set oral and written tasks. The criteria, lengths and internal deadlines differ in each case, and the school sets the timeline.

The common factor is that the decisive step is early. In almost every subject the choice of topic, question or article sets the ceiling, and careful writing afterwards does not raise it. Four sessions in DP1 on criteria and on choosing properly protects a fifth of the grade at ordinary rates, where a rescue block in the final weeks costs more, arrives at exam-year rates, and cannot change the choice.

The boundary is the same everywhere. A tutor may teach the criteria, model method on a different example, question the student's draft and point out where a claim is unsupported. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of a submission. One page in the researched competitor set sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is a malpractice route and the student carries the finding while the seller carries nothing.

sections.heading: Group classes, the one thing geography does decide
paragraphs: There is one tutoring option where the district genuinely determines the answer, and it is worth being straight about. Mirdif has commercial provision; the villa communities around it do not. A family in Mirdif can reach a tuition centre in ten minutes, and a family in Al Khawaneej cannot do so twice a week without rearranging the evening entirely.

Whether that matters depends on the student rather than the distance. A group class is cheaper per student and is the right purchase when the whole group shares the same gap: revising a topic a class is collectively weak on, or working through a common examination technique. It is the wrong purchase for the situation most Diploma families are actually in, where one student is losing marks on a component the others handle fine, because the hour then runs at the group's pace.

The hidden cost for the outer districts is the journey rather than the fee. Two trips a week into Mirdif or Al Qusais during the afternoon peak, for a family already running a school bus and a second school run, is several hours a week that does not appear on the invoice. For a Diploma student in DP2 that time is worth more than the saving.

So the honest summary is that the group-class option narrows as you move east, and that for most Diploma needs it was not the right option anyway. Where it is right, it is right, and we will say so rather than talk a family out of something cheaper that would work.

sections.heading: Starting, and the limits we will name
paragraphs: Send four things, and the district you live in is not one of them: the subject and level, which component is losing marks, a photograph of a marked paper or the latest report, and the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon. The last one is where the neighbourhood matters, because an Al Khawaneej arrival time and a Mirdif arrival time are genuinely different.

The free trial lesson runs about forty minutes on a past question from your child's own subject and level, with your child working and the tutor teaching. Ask how many questions the tutor plans to cover; one or two with the mark scheme open is the right answer, and a whole paper read out is the other approach. Afterwards you receive a written read on the loss pattern and the weeks it implies.

Sometimes nobody suitable is free. Higher Level specialists in narrow components, Theory of Knowledge, minority languages and late-evening Gulf Standard Time slots are the four that run short, and a request a fortnight before final papers is the hardest. We give a realistic match time rather than filling the hour with a generalist. That answer is the same in every district in this comparison, which is itself the point.

What we ask for is limited to what matching needs: subject, level, component, school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history across every subject. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we hold, and the privacy link on this page sets out what is kept and how to have it removed.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find an IB tutor in Mirdif than in Al Mizhar?
faqs.answer: For an in-home tutor, yes, and for the tutor who will actually change a grade, no. Mirdif has the schools, the commercial provision and the shortest journey, so local in-home supply is better and rates carry less travel. But the person a Diploma student needs is somebody who has taught the specific component their marks are leaving from, and that scarcity is absolute rather than local. Higher Level physics fields, the mathematical exploration and Theory of Knowledge are equally thin on the ground in both districts.

faqs.question: What actually differs between Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three things, all logistical. The school run is longer from Al Khawaneej, which pushes the earliest workable weekday slot to around 6.30pm or towards a weekend morning. An in-home tutor is pricing a longer round trip, so quotes sit higher inside the published AED 180 to 500 band. And reaching a tuition centre in Mirdif twice a week is a bigger ask. What does not differ is which specialists exist, because that depends on the component rather than on the postcode.

faqs.question: Why do in-home tutoring quotes vary so much between neighbourhoods here?
faqs.answer: Because the quoted band, AED 180 to 500 an hour, largely reflects travel. Bestimate's Dubai table runs AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500, and within that spread the predictable order in this cluster is Mirdif cheapest to reach, then Al Rashidiya and Nad Al Hamar, then Al Warqa and Al Mizhar, then Al Khawaneej. A family comparing quotes across districts is mostly comparing petrol and afternoon traffic rather than teaching quality.

faqs.question: If the teaching is online, does our neighbourhood matter at all?
faqs.answer: In one respect, yes: the hour. Your child's arrival home after the school bus sets the earliest workable lesson slot, and that varies by nearly two hours across these districts, from around 5pm in Mirdif to 6.30pm or a weekend morning in Al Khawaneej and Al Warqa. The second thing is the quiet room, which villa districts usually have and apartment housing in Al Rashidiya sometimes does not. Beyond those two, the neighbourhood stops mattering once no tutor has to drive anywhere.

faqs.question: Could we get a cheaper rate by using a tutor who lives nearby?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking against what else the money buys. An in-home tutor nearby may quote at the lower end of the AED 180 to 500 band. A qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to 300, and a named specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. So the premium you would pay for proximity is close to the premium that would move you from a generalist to a component specialist, which for a Diploma student is usually the better purchase.

faqs.question: We are moving to Abu Dhabi next year. What changes?
faqs.answer: The regulator and the school, not the qualification. Dubai private schools fall to KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation there. ADEK also has professional-ethics rules prohibiting private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, which is worth verifying against the current policy document. The Diploma itself is identical, and an online one-to-one arrangement is the part of the week that moves with you, because no address is involved.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers schools in Sharjah and the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there. Both also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. For Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, the federal Ministry of Education plays the supervising role. ADEK is mentioned by almost nobody writing about tutoring in this market, and SPEA by very few.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Mirdif a sensible option from Al Mizhar?
faqs.answer: Only if the whole group shares your child's gap. A group class is cheaper per student and works well for revising a topic a class is collectively weak on. It works poorly for the common Diploma situation where one student is losing marks on a component the others handle, because the hour runs at the group's pace. The hidden cost from Al Mizhar is the journey: two trips a week into Mirdif during the afternoon peak, for a household already running a school bus and possibly a second school run.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components are hardest to find a tutor for locally?
faqs.answer: Higher Level physics, particularly the fields theme, Higher Level Analysis and Approaches including the third paper, and Theory of Knowledge, which very few tutors anywhere have actually taught. Higher Level Applications and Interpretation statistics is scarcer than people expect, because fewer tutors have taken that content to examination standard. The IB accounts for roughly seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, so Diploma cohorts here are small to begin with and these are minorities within them.

faqs.question: Does the quiet room really make a difference to an online lesson?
faqs.answer: A visible one. A Diploma lesson needs a desk, a closed door, paper and a laptop on a stable surface rather than a phone on a sofa. Households in these districts are busy in the early evening with siblings, dinner and visiting family, and an hour held in the middle of that produces noticeably less than the same hour at a bedroom desk. It is the one item in this comparison a family can fix for nothing, and it is worth settling in the first week rather than month three.

faqs.question: How many questions should a Diploma tutoring session cover?
faqs.answer: One or two, with the mark scheme open and in your child's hands. The sequence that moves marks is: attempt the question under something close to timed conditions, mark it against the published scheme, identify precisely where the answer diverged from what was rewarded, name the error, then do a second question of the same type to test the diagnosis. A tutor expecting to cover a whole paper in forty minutes is reading out answers, which is cheaper to deliver and worth considerably less to buy.

faqs.question: What is the Internal Assessment worth, and when should it start?
faqs.answer: In the sciences and mathematics it commonly carries around a fifth of the final grade, which makes it the largest component outside the written papers. It should start in DP1, because the decisive step is early: the choice of topic, research question or article sets the ceiling and careful writing afterwards does not raise it. Four early sessions on the criteria and on choosing properly cost a fraction of a rescue block in the final weeks, which cannot change the choice anyway. Your school sets the internal deadlines.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supervise my child's Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: No. Supervision belongs to the school and is part of the assessed process, including the reflections, which are marked rather than administrative. What a tutor can usefully do is interrogate the research question early, because a question too broad produces a survey with nothing argued and one too narrow produces a page and a half, and then respond to drafts with questions. No part of the essay or the reflections is written, drafted or edited to completion by us, and that boundary does not move as a deadline approaches.

faqs.question: Do you charge differently depending on which district we live in?
faqs.answer: No, because nobody is travelling. That is the structural difference between an online arrangement and an in-home one: the published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour varies partly by how far a tutor drives, while an online rate cannot vary by postcode because there is no journey in it. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages, and home visits are a service we offer only in India, so there is no UAE delivery option whose price could depend on where your villa is.

faqs.question: What should we send before booking from Al Mizhar or anywhere nearby?
faqs.answer: Four things, and your address is not one of them. The subject and the level. Which component is losing marks, which turns a broad request into a narrow brief. A photograph of a marked paper or the latest report. And the time your child is realistically through the door on a bad traffic afternoon, which is the one place the neighbourhood genuinely counts. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history; UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs what is held.

They do not differ in whether somebody nearby has taught Higher Level physics fields or coached a mathematical exploration, because that scarcity is absolute. dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-muteena.tutorsIntro: These tutors work to the Diploma assessment grid: which paper, which weighting, which command terms and which criteria. Each one teaches a named subject at a named level rather than covering the Diploma as a single body of work.

intro.heading: Proximity is the wrong filter for a Diploma tutor
paragraphs: A near-me search is a sensible instinct applied to the wrong problem. For a piano lesson or a football coach, distance is the deciding variable. For the IB Diploma it is close to irrelevant, because the thing that moves a grade is detailed knowledge of how one subject at one level is assessed, and that knowledge is not distributed by neighbourhood. Al Muteena is a dense residential district in older Dubai with relatively few IB schools nearby; the probability that the person who best understands Chemistry Higher Level paper structure lives within a short drive is low.

What makes the Diploma unusual is how specific the assessment arithmetic is. Each subject is graded 1 to 7 from a combination of external papers and internal assessment, and the share each component carries is published. A student who spends equal effort on every component is over-investing in the small ones. A student who neglects the internal assessment because it feels like coursework rather than an exam is giving away a fixed, knowable fraction of the grade before the papers start.

On top of the six subject grades sits the core: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which together contribute additional points on a published matrix, and CAS, which is a completion requirement rather than a graded one. A student who treats the core as administrative overhead can lose points that cost less to earn than the equivalent movement in a subject grade would. That is a planning insight, not a motivational one, and it is why a good tutor asks about the Extended Essay subject early.

The other thing a Diploma tutor needs is command-term fluency. The IB publishes its command terms and they carry distinct expectations: state, outline, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss, justify. A paper answer written at the wrong command level is capped regardless of how much the student knows. This is the single most common reason a bright Diploma student scores a 5 and cannot work out why, and it is diagnosable from one marked paper.

Internal assessment is where the honesty boundary lives. A tutor can teach the science, interrogate the methodology, explain the published criteria and give feedback on the student's draft. A tutor cannot write it, cannot edit it to completion and cannot supply a model to be submitted. That boundary matters commercially as well as ethically in this market, because operations selling finished Internal Assessments exist in the Gulf search results and the consequence of using one falls on the student.

So the honest reframe of the near-me search is this: for the Diploma, choose on assessment literacy and on availability at the hour your child is actually free, and accept that the tutor will not be in Al Muteena. Everything below is written to make that choice easier, starting with what each component of a Diploma grade is actually worth.
