dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-muteena.programmesIntro: An Al Muteena family searching for IB support is usually at one of three points in the sequence, and each one needs a different kind of help.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Subject grades run 1 to 7, giving 42 from the six, with up to three further points from the core. HL courses carry more teaching hours, an extra paper in several subjects, and content the SL syllabus does not examine.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma is taught in a minority of private schools; International Baccalaureate students are roughly seven per cent of the emirate's private pupils against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula. For an Al Muteena family that usually means a commute to an IB school in Al Garhoud, Oud Metha or further south, and a small cohort in each subject at each level.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's pre-Diploma programme, assessed against four criteria per subject out of eight each rather than on papers. Strong MYP students frequently struggle in Diploma term one on timed writing alone, because nothing in MYP requires producing a complete argument against a clock without resources.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 and Diploma from Year 12, while most schools near Al Muteena run IGCSE instead. A student arriving in the Diploma from IGCSE and one arriving from MYP need different first-term support: the IGCSE student has examination technique and weaker independent research habits, the MYP student the reverse.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A less common IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Available in a small number of UAE schools. Students take individual DP subjects within it, so subject tutoring works identically; the core requirements differ.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing about because a family comparing schools in Dubai may be shown it as an alternative to the full Diploma. For university entry and for Ministry of Education equivalency the two are not interchangeable, so ask the school directly what the certificate at the end actually is.

programmes.name: International A Level, the alternative at 16
programmes.description: The route most schools near Al Muteena offer instead of the Diploma: three or four subjects, modular at AS and A2, examined in June and November windows. Narrower and deeper than the Diploma, with no core and no compulsory mathematics or second language.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, plus five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or better. No IB points threshold has been published that we can source, so we state none.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-muteena.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by its assessment shape, because that is what decides where a Diploma student should spend the next eight weeks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic, proof-oriented route. HL adds an extra paper and substantially more content, and the exploration is internally assessed against published criteria. Marks concentrate in the long structured questions, where partial credit for method survives an arithmetic error and an unexplained answer does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, technology-permitted throughout. Suits students heading to business, social sciences and design. Some engineering and mathematics degrees specify Analysis and Approaches, so the route choice needs checking against intended destinations rather than against comfort.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: HL adds content and an extra paper, and the data-based questions reward careful uncertainty handling. Organic mechanisms and energetics produce the most predictable losses, and the scientific investigation carries a published share of the grade that students routinely under-plan.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency is the gatekeeper: students who cannot rearrange confidently lose marks they understand conceptually. Fields, circular motion and the HL extensions are where SL-trained habits break down, and graph interpretation carries disproportionate weight.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content makes it feel like a memory subject, and it is marked on applied explanation. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments reward a student who has practised reading a graph and stating a limitation, not one who has reread the notes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams earn marks explicitly: axes labelled, curves named, shifts shown and explained in words. HL adds quantitative questions and a further paper. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on real published articles, and article choice determines how much of the syllabus a student can actually show.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed across unseen analysis, a comparative essay and an oral on a global issue, with HL adding a further written component. Students who write fluently but never anchor a claim to a specific textual feature plateau, because the criteria reward supported interpretation over confident assertion.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, contributing core points alongside the Extended Essay on a published matrix. Students who treat it as an opinion piece score poorly; the criteria reward a tightly argued line with clear real-world examples.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent research essay in a chosen subject, with a word limit and a formal supervision process. The research question is the whole ballgame: too broad and the essay cannot be argued, too narrow and there is nothing to find. Most of the recoverable marks are decided before any writing begins.

sections.heading: What a Diploma grade is actually made of
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject grade comes from a published combination of components, and the published shares are the most useful planning document a Diploma family will ever read. In most sciences the external papers carry the large majority of the grade and the scientific investigation carries a fixed, meaningful remainder. In Economics the internal commentaries carry a published share and the papers the rest, with HL adding a further paper. In the language subjects the balance between unseen analysis, essay and oral work differs again.

Two consequences follow. The first is that effort should be weighted, not spread. A student who puts three weeks into polishing a component worth a small share of the grade while a heavily weighted paper goes unpractised has made a measurable error, and it is the sort of error nobody notices because it feels like hard work. The second is that the internal assessment is not optional revision territory: it is a known fraction of the grade that can be secured in advance, under no time pressure, with feedback available throughout.

The arithmetic above the subjects matters too. Six subjects at 1 to 7 give a maximum of forty-two points, and the core adds up to three more through a published matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades. CAS is a completion requirement rather than a points earner, but failing to complete it has consequences no amount of subject performance offsets.

This is why a first session with a Diploma student starts with their subject list, levels, current grades and the state of each internal assessment and the Extended Essay, rather than with a topic. Fifteen minutes on that inventory frequently reveals that the fastest available points are not in the subject the family was worried about.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level: what the difference actually is
paragraphs: Parents often read Higher Level as simply harder, which undersells what changes. HL courses carry more teaching hours, additional syllabus content that the SL course does not examine at all, and in several subjects an extra paper. That means an HL student is not sitting a sterner version of the SL paper; they are sitting a different set of papers over a larger syllabus.

The practical consequence shows up in subject choice. A student who needs a particular subject at HL for a university course has to carry that extra content for two years, and a student who selected HL for prestige rather than purpose is spending hours that another subject needs. In mathematics the choice is doubled, because Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses before the level question even arises, and some degree programmes specify one of them.

For tutoring the HL and SL distinction changes the plan rather than the intensity. An SL student near a boundary usually needs technique: command-term discipline, paper timing, data-question method. An HL student in trouble more often has a content gap in the HL extension material, because that content arrives later and is taught faster. Treating both as needing more practice papers helps one and wastes the other's time.

This is also where honest advice matters more than reassurance. A student carrying three HL subjects that all demand heavy independent work, plus the Extended Essay in one of them, may be over-committed in a way no tutoring fixes. Saying so in month two of Year 12, while a level change is still administratively possible at the school, is more useful than saying it after the first mock series.

sections.heading: Command terms: the reason a knowledgeable student scores a 5
paragraphs: The IB publishes its command terms and defines them, and they are the most under-taught part of the Diploma. State asks for a specific answer with no supporting argument and gives nothing for one. Describe asks for an account without explanation. Explain asks for reasons or causes and credits a causal chain. Analyse asks for the parts and their relationships. Evaluate and discuss ask for judgement supported by weighed evidence, and an answer that presents one side scores in the lower bands however well written.

The failure pattern is consistent. A student who knows a topic thoroughly answers an evaluate question with a detailed explanation, receives a middling mark, and concludes they do not know the material well enough. They then revise more content, answer the next evaluate question the same way, and the mark does not move. The problem was never knowledge; it was the verb at the start of the question.

Fixing it is quick and dull. Take a set of past questions on one topic, sort them by command term, and write only the first two sentences of each answer, checking against what the term demands. A student who does that for an hour across two sessions usually changes shape immediately, because the behaviour is mechanical once noticed.

This also interacts with timing. Evaluate and discuss answers take longer and are worth more, so students who spend equal time per question routinely run out of clock on the questions carrying the most marks. Reading the paper's mark allocation before writing and budgeting minutes against marks is a separate discipline worth building in the same sessions.
bullets: State and describe credit no explanation; explain credits a causal chain

sections.heading: Internal assessment: where marks are won, and where the line sits
paragraphs: Internal assessment is the component families most often misread. It carries a published share of every subject grade, it is produced over months rather than hours, and feedback is permitted within defined limits. In principle it is the most controllable part of a Diploma grade. In practice it is the part most often left until a deadline turns it into a rushed piece of work that caps the subject.

The marks are mostly decided early. In the sciences the investigation's research question and methodology determine how much of the criteria the student can even reach: a question that cannot generate meaningful data makes good analysis impossible later. In Economics the choice of published article determines how much syllabus the commentary can demonstrate. In mathematics the exploration topic decides whether genuine mathematical engagement is possible or whether the student is describing arithmetic. An hour spent interrogating the question at the start is worth more than a week of polishing at the end.

What a tutor may do here is clear, and worth stating plainly because the market is not clean. A tutor can teach the underlying subject, question the design, explain each published criterion, give feedback on the student's own draft and ask what the evidence actually supports. A tutor must not write any part of it, must not edit it to completion and must not supply a model for submission. The work has to be the student's own, and IB academic-honesty rules make the consequences of breaching that the student's to carry.

Some providers in the Gulf market advertise completed Internal Assessments for sale at a fixed price. A family evaluating any tutoring arrangement should ask directly what the provider will and will not produce, and treat an evasive answer as an answer. The legitimate version of this help is slower, duller and genuinely moves grades, because a student who has argued their own methodology can defend it in a viva and write about it coherently.

sections.heading: The May session, counted backwards from an Al Muteena desk
paragraphs: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. Internal deadlines, not the examination window, are what structure the two years, and those deadlines belong to the school rather than the board. Each subject's internal assessment has a school submission date, the Extended Essay has a sequence of supervision checkpoints, and Theory of Knowledge has its own exhibition and essay deadlines. A family that knows those dates can plan; a family that does not spends two years reacting.

A workable backwards plan looks like this. Year 12 is for the Extended Essay research question, the subject selection confirmed, and the internal assessment topics chosen and approved. The winter of Year 13 is for completing internal assessment to a real standard and sitting mocks. The final term is the paper phase: full papers under timed conditions, losses categorised, command-term work, and no new content unless a gap is named.

We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family acts on has to be right. Confirm the session and results dates with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly, and treat any third-party calendar, including ours, as a prompt to check rather than a source.

For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications sat alongside, the published position is firmer. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres, with the February/March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: What Diploma tutoring costs in Dubai, cheapest band first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because the bottom is where most families begin and where the mismatch is largest. Tutopiya publishes online rates from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. That band is largely university students and group-adjacent delivery, and for Diploma work it struggles, not because the tutors are weak but because Diploma grades turn on assessment detail that takes years of teaching the same syllabus to internalise.

The next band is qualified subject tutors working online, published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 an hour. Above that sit specialists: TutorChase lists around AED 270, Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits are published at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. All of these are the providers' own published figures, not IB Gram's prices.

The monthly frame is the one that actually governs a household decision. Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages circulating in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

For a Diploma family the sharpest question is not the hourly rate but how many subjects to buy. Three HL subjects plus Extended Essay coaching is three or four recurring commitments, and most families cannot sustain that for two years. The version that works is a weighted one: one subject weekly at specialist level, short coaching blocks on the internal assessments and the Extended Essay at the points where marks are decided, and an intensive final-stretch block. Spread thinly across six subjects, the same budget changes nothing measurable.

sections.heading: Online rather than near me: the trade spelled out
paragraphs: A near-me search for a Diploma tutor in Al Muteena returns a small pool, and the limiting factor is not the district's affluence but IB density. International Baccalaureate students are a minority of Dubai's private-school population and that minority is concentrated in newer communities rather than the older northern grid. A tutor who teaches Chemistry Higher Level every week is unlikely to be the tutor who will drive to Al Muteena at five on a Tuesday.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Dubai. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the paper, the criteria and the student's draft shared on screen. For Diploma work that is a genuine fit: almost everything a session needs to look at is a document.

The in-home market exists and is priced accordingly, at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for comparable online work. What the difference buys is physical presence, which helps some students, and a round trip through Dubai traffic at the hour the whole city is moving, which helps nobody. For a Diploma student the cost is also time: an in-home arrangement is hard to move when a mock week or an internal deadline lands, and Diploma deadlines land constantly.

The honest caveat is motivation. A student who will not work unsupervised does not become self-directed because the lesson is on video, and for that student the format is not the problem to solve. What online delivery removes is the geography constraint on who teaches them, which for a Diploma subject at Higher Level is usually the constraint that matters most.

sections.heading: Regulators, equivalency and the questions a Dubai IB family should actually ask
paragraphs: The regulator map for UAE private schools is worth knowing because it is poorly covered elsewhere. Dubai private schools fall under KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods, so the emirate regulator does more than inspect.

None of those bodies regulates private tutoring. Individual tutoring in the UAE is governed by permit through MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and individuals offering private tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted.

Equivalency is the other thing Dubai families ask about and almost no competitor page covers. For the British track the Ministry requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or better, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Math. No IB points threshold has been published that we can source, so we do not state one; verify with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority.

Two things follow for a family hiring a tutor. First, no tutoring provider is KHDA approved in the sense the phrase implies; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises, and we hold none. Second, ask a prospective tutor whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, because the parent can ask and the answer tells them something real about how the arrangement is being run.

process.description: Sessions go where the recoverable marks are: a heavily weighted paper that has never been practised, or an internal assessment whose research question still cannot generate data. Spreading hours evenly across six subjects is the most common way a year of tutoring produces no movement.

process.title: Book the internal assessment checkpoints early
process.description: Coaching is front-loaded to the moments where marks are decided: question setting, methodology, criteria reading and a halfway review. The student writes every word; the tutor questions and gives feedback on drafts against the published criteria.

process.title: Switch to papers for the final stretch

whyPoints.description: Every subject grade is a published combination of components. We plan from those shares rather than from how worried the family feels, because effort spread evenly across unequal components is a measurable waste of hours.

whyPoints.title: Command terms treated as a skill
whyPoints.description: A bright student scoring a 5 is usually answering the wrong verb. Sorting past questions by command term and writing only opening sentences changes the shape of answers within two sessions, and it costs almost nothing.

faqs.question: Does it matter that an IB Diploma tutor is not based near Al Muteena?
faqs.answer: For the Diploma, very little. What moves a grade is detailed knowledge of how one subject at one level is assessed, and that is not distributed by neighbourhood. International Baccalaureate students are a minority of Dubai's private pupils and are concentrated in newer communities, so the northern districts have thin local IB supply whichever one you search. Choosing on assessment literacy and on availability at the hour your child is genuinely free produces better results than choosing on drive time, and online delivery removes distance from the decision entirely.

faqs.question: My daughter says she is aiming for 38 points. Where do those points come from?
faqs.answer: Six subjects graded 1 to 7 give a maximum of forty-two points. Up to three further points come from the core, awarded on a published matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades. CAS is a completion requirement rather than a points earner, but it must be completed. Each subject grade itself combines external papers with internal assessment at shares the IB publishes per subject. That last detail is the one families most often miss, and it is where most of the planning value sits.

faqs.question: Why is my child scoring a 5 when they clearly know the subject?
faqs.answer: Most often because of command terms. The IB defines state, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate and discuss with distinct expectations, and an answer written at the wrong level is capped regardless of knowledge. A student who answers an evaluate question with a detailed explanation gets a middling mark, concludes they need more content, revises harder and scores the same. Sorting past questions by command term and writing only the first two sentences of each answer fixes this faster than any amount of further revision does.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma subject grade is the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A published share that differs by subject and level, and in every case enough to decide a boundary. The IB publishes the weighting in each subject guide, and the school will confirm it. The important point is that the internal assessment is produced over months, with feedback permitted within defined limits and no clock, which makes it the most controllable part of a grade. It is also the part most often rushed into a deadline, which turns a controllable component into the one that caps the subject.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes, and the process is where most of the marks are decided. A tutor can interrogate the research question until it is narrow enough to argue, help plan backwards from the school's supervision checkpoints, read the published criteria with the student and give feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor cannot write any part of it, cannot edit it to completion and cannot supply a model essay. The supervision relationship with the school's supervisor remains the formal one, and the tutor works alongside it rather than replacing it.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Higher Level and Standard Level?
faqs.answer: More than difficulty. Higher Level carries more teaching hours, additional syllabus content the Standard Level course never examines, and in several subjects an extra paper. An HL student sits a different set of papers over a larger syllabus rather than a harder version of the same one. For tutoring that changes the plan: an SL student near a boundary usually needs technique, while an HL student in trouble more often has a content gap in the HL extension material, which arrives later in the course and is taught faster.

faqs.question: Should my son take Maths Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Check the destination before the preference. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented route; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with technology throughout. Several engineering, mathematics, physics and economics degrees specify Analysis and Approaches, and a student who chose Applications for comfort can find a course closed two years later. Read the entry requirements of a handful of plausible universities before the choice is locked, and ask the school what each route's cohort typically goes on to study.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to homes in Al Muteena?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. For Diploma work the format suits the material, because the paper, the published criteria and the student's draft are documents that share better on a screen than across a table. The in-home market in Dubai publishes AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 300 for comparable online work.

faqs.question: When do Dubai IB students sit their final exams?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the IB's own website blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. A date a family plans around has to be right, so confirm the session and results dates with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge qualifications sat alongside, UAE centres sit the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we actually pay for tutoring in?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. Three Higher Level subjects plus Extended Essay coaching is three or four recurring commitments, and very few households sustain that across two years. The shape that works is weighted: one subject weekly at specialist level, short coaching blocks at the points where internal assessment marks are decided, and an intensive block before the session. The same budget spread thinly across six subjects reliably produces no measurable change in any of them.

faqs.question: What does IB tutoring cost in Dubai at the specialist end?
faqs.answer: Published figures put specialist work at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above in Bestimate's rate study, with TutorChase listing around AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for premium named tutors. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. At the lower end, Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which for Diploma work usually buys content help rather than assessment literacy. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

faqs.question: Is any tutoring provider in Dubai KHDA approved?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense the phrase implies. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, through a process requiring initial approval and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no accreditation claim. Individual private tutoring is regulated separately, by permit through MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. If a provider describes itself as KHDA approved, ask to see the permit number, because the phrase is used loosely in this market.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and can I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

faqs.question: Can the core really change my child's total by three points?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families consistently underrate it. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combine on a published matrix to award up to three additional points on top of the forty-two available from six subjects. Three points is the difference between many university offers, and it is often cheaper to earn there than through lifting a subject grade, because both components are written over months with supervision rather than sat under a clock. A student treating the core as paperwork is leaving the most available points on the table.

faqs.question: My child joined the Diploma from IGCSE and is struggling in term one. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is common and the reason is usually specific. IGCSE trains examination technique and rewards tightly bounded answers; the Diploma asks for sustained independent work, longer argued writing and research the student designs. Students arriving from MYP have the opposite profile: comfortable with inquiry and process, unpractised at writing to a clock. Either way, term one is where the gap is cheapest to close. Name which of the two profiles your child has and the first eight weeks of support write themselves.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for our subject at the time we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot. Diploma specialisms are narrow, and a particular subject at a particular level at a particular hour does occasionally come up empty, especially in the weeks before a session when demand peaks. The options then are a different time, a different tutor with a proper handover of the student's component plan, or a wait with a date attached. A mismatched tutor in a Diploma subject costs a term the student does not have spare.

intro.heading: What a ten-minute radius buys in Al Nahda, and what it quietly costs
paragraphs: The phrase near me is a proxy for something more specific: a person who can be with your child inside the window the day leaves open. In Al Nahda that window is tight and predictable. Schools across this catchment finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:15. Buses along Al Nahda Road and Damascus Street put most students home between 15:00 and 15:45, later for those travelling to Al Garhoud, Festival City or across the Sharjah boundary. From 16:30 Al Ittihad Road beside the neighbourhood carries one of the heaviest commuter flows in the country.

So the honest translation of near me in this neighbourhood is: somebody who lives within about ten minutes of Al Nahda Pond Park and is free at 16:00 or 20:00. That is a small set of people, and it is small for reasons that have nothing to do with whether they know your child's subject. A family filtering that way is not choosing the best available tutor. They are choosing the best tutor inside a circle drawn by traffic. A circle on a map is a poor proxy for a teacher who knows the course your child is actually sitting, and in this neighbourhood the circle is drawn tighter than almost anywhere in the emirate.

What the circle costs becomes clear once you look at the Diploma properly. A Diploma student takes six subjects, three usually at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Mathematics alone is four distinct courses. Chemistry HL under the current guide is a different teaching job from Chemistry SL. English A Language and Literature is not English B. Across six subjects, the chance that the right specialist for the one that is actually failing lives inside a ten-minute radius of Al Nahda is low, and it does not improve by searching harder.

There is also a load question nobody in this market writes about. A Dubai Diploma student carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, because KHDA requires them in all private schools regardless of curriculum. Those are real lessons with real homework, and KHDA calculates their instructional time using a 40-minute lesson unit while allowing schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met. Any plan that treats the Diploma as six subjects plus free evenings is a plan built on a week that does not exist.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, stated identically on every UAE page here so a reader can check it is policy. What that gives an Al Nahda family is the ability to put the right specialist in the 16:00 or 20:00 slot rather than the nearest one, and to move the slot without anybody having to cross the city.

sections.heading: The radius trade-off, written out: what you gain and lose by searching nearby
paragraphs: Set the two filters side by side rather than arguing for one. Filtering by distance gives you presence, a short commute for nobody, independence from broadband, and a tutor who may know your child's school by reputation. Those are real benefits and for some students they are decisive. Filtering by course gives you a specialist in the exact syllabus your child sits, availability across the whole Gulf evening rather than one neighbourhood's spare hours, and the ability to replace a bad fit without restarting the search.

The question is which of those matters more for the specific problem in front of you. For a Year 8 who needs supervision and company while they work, proximity is a reasonable buy. For a Year 13 three weeks from a chemistry investigation deadline, or a Year 12 who has just discovered that Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, the specialist matters and no amount of proximity substitutes.

There is a second-order effect worth naming. A tutor chosen for proximity is usually asked to cover more than one subject, because the family has already accepted the constraint and wants value from the relationship. That is how a maths tutor ends up handling physics, and how a physics hour quietly becomes another maths hour. A tutor chosen by course does one job and is judged on it, which is less convenient and considerably more honest.

Finally, the replacement question. If a nearby tutor turns out to be a poor fit, the family is back to a short list defined by the same circle. If a course-matched tutor turns out to be a poor fit, the next candidate comes from the same large pool. Fit failures are common and usually have nothing to do with competence - pace, manner, how much the student is allowed to speak - so the cost of replacement is part of the decision rather than a footnote to it.

sections.heading: The Diploma week in Al Nahda with the mandatory UAE subjects counted in
paragraphs: Most tutoring plans fail on arithmetic rather than on teaching, and the arithmetic that is usually missing is the mandatory subject load. In Dubai, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA stating that the requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These are timetabled lessons that set homework, not a cultural footnote.

KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time using a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. It also requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

Add that to six Diploma subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge sessions and whatever CAS commitment the school runs, and the genuinely free evening time in a term-time week is smaller than almost any family estimates before they write it down. The practical consequence is that a Diploma student in Al Nahda can sustain one or two outside sessions a week, not four, and that choosing which subject gets them is the real decision.

The week below is how the families we work with in this catchment actually describe it. Note what it implies: the short weekday window is for correction and drilling, the evening window is for anything that needs an unbroken run, and Saturday morning is the only block in the week where a timed paper can be sat properly and marked. A plan that uses Saturday for a general catch-up has wasted the most valuable hour available to it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the subjects nobody tutors for
paragraphs: This is one of the clearest gaps in the whole UAE tutoring market. Across the competitor pages researched for these queries, Arabic appears as a subject chip and almost never as a section, and Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies barely appear at all. Yet every Dubai private school student carries them alongside the Diploma or IGCSE, they generate homework and reports, and a weak Arabic grade sits on the same report as the subjects everyone is paying attention to.

The rules are specific and worth understanding before arranging any help. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

There is also a constraint on material that any tutor should know about. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That means a tutor cannot sensibly bring their own alternative curriculum to these subjects, and should be working from what the school actually uses. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects - a credential point that applies to school staff and is worth knowing exists.

Practically, for an Al Nahda family: establish which stream your child is in - Arabic as a first language or as an additional language, Islamic Education for Arabs or non-Arabs - because the course, the language of instruction and the expectations all differ. Then decide whether the problem is language acquisition, content, or written expression under assessment, since those need different help. Support here is usually about building reading fluency and written accuracy over a sustained period rather than a short exam push.

sections.heading: The deadline stack: why the Diploma feels harder than its subjects
paragraphs: Families often arrive looking for help with a subject when the real problem is a calendar. A Diploma student carries an internal assessment in most of their six subjects, each with its own criteria and its own school-set deadline, plus the Extended Essay with a supervisor and interim deadlines, plus Theory of Knowledge with an essay and an exhibition. None of those deadlines is set by the IB directly for the student; they are set earlier by the school so that marking and uploading can happen in time.

The consequence is a stack rather than a sequence. Year 12 term two is when Extended Essay topics and several internal assessment proposals land together. Year 12 term three carries the first full internal examinations. Year 13 term one is when the Extended Essay goes to the school, several internal assessments are submitted and TOK work is completed. Year 13 term two is mocks, which generate the predicted grades universities see. By the May session there should be nothing left to learn.

This is why the most valuable early conversation with a tutor is often about sequencing rather than content. A student three weeks from two internal assessment deadlines does not need a syllabus plan; they need to know which to finish first and what good enough looks like against the criteria for each. A student in Year 12 term one needs the opposite: content diagnosis and a bridging list, because that is the only term in which there is time to use one.

We do not publish IB session or results dates on these pages. The IB sets them, secondary sources disagree, and a date a parent acts on has to be right - so confirm every IB deadline with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications on the way in, the published pattern is firmer: Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson runs May/June and November, its November final timetable having run from late October to 19 November 2026.

sections.heading: What a parent can verify before paying, nearby or not
paragraphs: Whichever filter you use, the checks are the same and most of them cost nothing. Start with the permit, because it is public and free. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a working tutor has no financial reason to lack one, and anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Second, verify the course rather than the subject. Ask which exact Diploma course the tutor teaches - Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard - and which component of it they have worked on most recently. Then ask what they would refuse to do on an internal assessment. The right answer is explicit: they will not write it, redraft it to completion, choose the topic or supply the content, because the work must be the student's own under IB academic-honesty rules.

Third, verify the price claim. Every AED figure on this page is somebody else's published rate, read in October 2026, and you can check each one: Bestimate's Dubai rate table for the in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 350 and the specialist band of AED 200 to 450-plus; Unitors for IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650; Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end. A provider who will not name a source for a figure has given you a reason to discount it.

Fourth, treat statistics as claims. If a tutoring page shows a satisfaction percentage, a star rating or a student count, ask for the underlying data with the number of respondents, the date and the method. Research into this market found pages publishing two different review scores on the same page, and one showing a rating from twenty reviews beside a claim about its own student numbers in the thousands. We publish none of those figures, which is less persuasive and more defensible.

sections.heading: When the Diploma itself is the problem rather than one subject
paragraphs: A meaningful share of the enquiries we take from this catchment name a subject and turn out to be about load. The student is not failing chemistry; they are failing to finish anything, because six subjects, three internal assessments in flight, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, a CAS commitment and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education homework have produced a week with no slack in it. Buying a weekly chemistry hour against that does not help, and sometimes makes it worse by adding another stream of homework.

The diagnostic question is simple and rarely asked: in the last fortnight, what did your child start and not finish, and why did it stop? If the answer is that the work was too hard, it is a subject problem and a specialist is the right purchase. If the answer is that something else became more urgent, it is a sequencing problem, and the right purchase is one or two sessions on triage rather than a term of teaching. The two feel identical to a parent and need opposite responses.

Triage in the Diploma has a fairly standard shape. List every outstanding deliverable with its real school deadline, not the one the student remembers. Identify which are criterion-marked and therefore have a defined standard to reach rather than an open-ended one. Decide what good enough looks like for the lowest-stakes item and finish it first, because momentum matters more than order of difficulty. Then protect one evening a week with nothing scheduled in it at all, which is the single change that most often holds a term together.

There is a point at which a tutor is the wrong person to ask, and a page like this should say so. If a student has stopped sleeping, stopped attending or stopped caring, that is a conversation with the school's IB coordinator and the pastoral team rather than a purchase. We would say the same to a family in Al Nahda who asked us, and we would rather lose the booking than take money for something tutoring cannot fix.

sections.heading: Getting started from Al Nahda, and the fallback when nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: Send the subject block rather than a subject. The six Diploma courses with their levels, which one is actually the problem, the school and the emirate it sits in, the year group, and the two time windows that genuinely work on a school night. Most enquiries from this neighbourhood name a subject and omit the window, and the window is what determines whether a plan holds past week three given the arrival times and mandatory-subject load described above.

The first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor - one lesson, one tutor, with the fee discussed afterwards. It is a fit decision, not a sales call. The tutor teaches something real rather than interviewing your child, and you and the student both say afterwards whether the explanation landed. If it did not, say so and we match again, which is the main practical advantage of choosing from a large pool rather than a small circle.

On availability, stated plainly because most providers do not. Higher Level specialists concentrate in the same two hours of the Gulf evening, and in October and in the weeks before mocks those hours fill. If nobody suitable is free in your window, you hear it at the match stage with three options: a different slot with the right specialist, a tutor with adjacent expertise starting now while we hold the specialist slot, or a wait with a date attached. A disclosed wait is cheaper for a family than a confident mismatch.

And the limits, since this page is about honesty regarding what near me buys. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We operate no office, centre or branch in the Emirates. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. And we will not write a student's internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, whatever the deadline pressure.

faqs.answer: Substantially, and almost no tutoring page mentions them. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates their instructional time using a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises at least 25 minutes per mandatory-subject lesson. They are timetabled lessons with homework, so the genuinely free evening time in a term-time week is smaller than families estimate before writing it down.

faqs.question: Can we get tutoring for Arabic or Islamic Education alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It is worth asking about and the rules matter. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Also note that using different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so support should work from what the school actually uses.

faqs.question: Which Diploma courses are hardest to find a tutor for near Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: Higher Level chemistry organic mechanisms and Higher Level physics, followed by anything involving marking an internal assessment against published descriptors. Those require someone who has taught the current guide rather than someone who studied the subject, and proximity does nothing to improve the odds. Biology and Standard Level content are better supplied, and for those a nearby tutor may genuinely be a reasonable match. We say which category your request falls into at the match stage rather than after a payment.

faqs.question: What is the deadline stack and why does it matter more than the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Each of a Diploma student's six subjects carries an internal assessment with its own criteria and school-set deadline, alongside the Extended Essay with interim dates and Theory of Knowledge with an essay and exhibition. Those deadlines cluster in Year 12 term two and Year 13 term one rather than arriving in sequence. A student three weeks from two submissions needs help deciding which to finish first and what meets the descriptors, not a syllabus plan. Sequencing is frequently the most valuable thing an outside tutor provides.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish IB exam and results dates on this page?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them from the IB itself, and a date a parent acts on has to be right. Secondary sources disagree with each other, and the cost of being wrong is a family planning a revision schedule or a flight around a date that moves. Confirm every IB session, upload and results date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. Cambridge and Pearson dates are better documented and we do cite those, with the live official timetable as the authority.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor before paying, whether they are nearby or online?
faqs.answer: Four things. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit - it is free for two years, so there is no cost reason not to. Which exact Diploma course do you teach, and which component have you worked on most recently. What will you refuse to do on an internal assessment - the right answer names writing, redrafting to completion, choosing the topic and supplying content. And for any figure or statistic they quote, what is the source and the date. Evasion on any of these is itself an answer.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use the school's own support rather than a tutor?
faqs.answer: Often, and we recommend it to families who are close to coping. Subject surgeries, the IB coordinator, the Extended Essay supervisor and the school's own revision sessions are already paid for in the fees. The sensible arrangement for many Al Nahda households is to use all of that and buy one targeted outside session for the single subject that is genuinely failing, which costs a third of a multi-subject plan. That needs a diagnosis first so the hour is aimed correctly rather than spread.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for an Al Nahda Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For well-supplied requests - Standard Level content, biology, IGCSE-to-Diploma bridging - usually within a few days. For a named Higher Level specialist, longer, because demand concentrates in the same two hours of the Gulf evening and those hours fill in October and before mocks. You hear the position at the match stage with three options: a different slot with the right specialist, adjacent expertise starting now while we hold the specialist slot, or a wait with a date against it.

faqs.question: Do you provide IB tutors who travel to homes in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we operate only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates. The Dubai market does supply in-home tutors at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with monthly packages around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Where presence genuinely matters - a young child who will not use a screen - that is the right purchase and we say so.

faqs.question: Our broadband is unreliable. Is online tutoring still workable?
faqs.answer: Check it before committing, because this is one of the two cases where we would not argue with a family choosing presence instead. A lesson that drops out twice an hour is worse than no lesson, and no amount of course-matching fixes it. Test a video call at your intended session time, since evening congestion differs from daytime. If it holds, the format works well for written subjects in particular. If it does not, buy presence and accept the premium and the lower session frequency deliberately.

faqs.question: Does our school being in Sharjah rather than Dubai change the plan?
faqs.answer: It can, because Al Nahda spans the boundary. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods as well as regulating quality, while the Dubai side answers to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Term dates, internal assessment calendars and even the board a school uses can differ. Tell us which emirate the school sits in and send its calendar, so the schedule is built around your dates rather than the Dubai default.

faqs.question: What happens if the first matched tutor is not right for our child?
faqs.answer: You say so and we match again, from the same large pool rather than from a neighbourhood circle. That is the practical argument for course-matching that families notice most. Fit failures are common and usually have nothing to do with competence - pace, manner, how much the student is allowed to talk, whether the tutor asks or tells. The free trial lesson exists for exactly this decision, which is why it is one lesson with the matched tutor and why the fee is discussed afterwards.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-nahda.closingHeading: Replace the radius with the course
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-nahda.closingBody: Searching for an IB tutor near me in Al Nahda is a search for someone who can be with your child in the window the day leaves open, and that window is real: home between roughly 15:00 and 15:45, Arabic and Islamic Education homework to do, Al Ittihad Road solid from 16:30. What changes the outcome is replacing the radius with the course - the exact Diploma course and the component that is actually failing - and keeping the slot where your household can hold it. Send the subject block, the school, the emirate and your two workable windows, and the first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Near me is a map answer to a calendar question
paragraphs: Typing IB tutor near me in Al Quoz produces a list sorted by distance. That is a reasonable way to find a dentist and a poor way to find a Diploma Programme teacher, because distance has no relationship to the thing that decides your child's grade. What decides it is whether the person teaching them knows the assessment architecture of one specific subject, and where in the two-year clock the student currently sits.

Al Quoz makes the point by accident. The district is mostly industrial by land area, with housing concentrated in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3 between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road. A map search centred there returns tuition centres, nurseries and general tutors in large numbers, and almost none of them is a Higher Level Chemistry specialist who can tell you that the internal assessment is worth 20 per cent and that a research question too broad to measure in a school laboratory caps the analysis criterion before the student writes a word.

Meanwhile the clock is running. The Diploma Programme is a two-year structure with most of its decisive moments inside the school rather than in the examination hall: subject and level choices at the end of Year 11, internal assessment topics through DP1, the first Extended Essay reflection, Theory of Knowledge exhibition, internal assessment final drafts across the DP2 terms, the school's mock window, then the May session. Each of those has a point after which it cannot be influenced.

That is why this page is organised as a calendar and a set of reference tables rather than as a description of our service. You will find the two-year clock set out term by term, the word and page limits across DP components in one place, the internal assessment criteria discussed by letter with the marks attached, and the Mathematics Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation decision laid against what universities actually ask for. These are the things families most often discover late.

There is a second reason the map is a poor tool here, and it is about supply rather than quality. A tutor who drives can fit two or three sessions into a weekday evening; a tutor who does not can fit four or five, and can take a later slot for a family that needs one. So the early-evening hours Al Quoz parents want most are exactly the hours the in-home model rations hardest, and the rationing gets worse in the weeks before the May session when every DP2 household in Dubai is asking for the same time.

One premise first, stated plainly because the rest only works if it is honest. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Al Quoz homes as live online video sessions, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we offer in India only. The gain from working that way is precisely the one a map search cannot give you, which is selection by subject and level instead of by driving distance.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz.programmesIntro: Al Quoz children meet the IB at different points, and which point they are at changes what support means. Below, each programme is described by its assessment structure, because that is what a tutor works against.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run 1 to 7, giving 42 points, with up to three further points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix for a maximum of 45. Every subject also carries internally assessed work marked by the school and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: This is where nearly all Al Quoz enquiries sit, and the shape of them is consistent. A student arrives from IGCSE comfortable with content recall, meets Higher Level work that rewards reasoning instead, and loses a term before anyone names the difference. The schools in the central corridor across Al Khail Road all run this programme on their own internal deadlines.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. MYP Year 5 includes the Personal Project, which the student develops independently with a process journal. The criterion language is the part families find hardest, because a fluent piece of work can still sit mid-band if it never addressed what the criterion asked for.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is where the habits that decide DP outcomes are formed, particularly the habit of reading a criterion before writing rather than after. GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail in Al Quoz 2 and several schools in the Al Barsha cluster run it, and their Personal Project deadlines fall in different terms from each other.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based, with no external examinations, closing with the Exhibition in the final year. Reporting is against learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning rather than subject percentages, which is why PYP reports read so differently from the British curriculum reports many Al Quoz parents grew up with.
programmes.countryNote: Support at this stage is about reading fluency and number sense, not examination technique, because there is no examination. The families who benefit most are those moving from a British or Indian primary into an IB middle school, where the reporting language changes overnight.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma Programme courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, service learning, personal and professional skills and language development. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools rather than being generally available, and it suits a student who wants IB subject rigour alongside an applied qualification.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Quoz family on the CP route is usually travelling further for school than a Diploma family. The tutoring demand comes from the DP courses inside the programme, which are assessed exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so the reference tables on this page apply to them unchanged.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Quoz families ask for, described by assessment structure. Where a component has a stated limit or weighting, it is named, because that is the information a map search will never give you.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a longer two-part investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade, which schools often reach late so students practise it least. The internal assessment is an exploration with a page guideline rather than a word count, and most lost marks are notation and justification.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use, with fluent graphical display calculator work assumed throughout. Higher Level also carries Paper 3. The usual failure is a correct calculation presented without the sentence of interpretation that answers the question actually asked.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the most Higher Level weight. The internal assessment is typically 20 per cent, assessed against lettered criteria, and the commonest structural error is a research question that cannot be measured properly with school equipment, which caps analysis and evaluation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 combines multiple choice with data analysis, Paper 2 is extended response and Paper 3 covers experimental work and the option. Uncertainty treatment, graph gradients used without units, and descriptions offered in place of applied principles are where the marks go.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume invites memorisation, and memorisation is not what is marked. Command terms decide the grade: an answer that states everything known about a topic scores less than one that answers only what was asked. Statistical treatment is the weak point in most Higher Level internal assessments.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, correct labelling and evaluation that reaches a judgement. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published news articles, each with a strict word limit, and students lose marks by choosing an article that does not actually illustrate the syllabus concept they intended to analyse.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, and the Individual Oral connects a global issue to two texts. Higher Level adds the essay. Weak responses summarise; strong ones analyse how meaning is constructed and hold that line across the whole answer.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under time pressure plus an internal assessment on a real organisation. Choosing a company the student cannot get usable evidence about is the single most common planning error, and it is usually discovered too late in DP2 to change without losing weeks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and by an essay on a prescribed title. It contributes to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Students who treat the prescribed title as a topic rather than an arguable question lose marks they never see coming.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, with required reflection sessions recorded with the supervisor. The strongest essays have narrow, arguable questions; the weakest have broad topics. Subject-specific criteria differ, so the subject choice changes what a good essay looks like.

sections.heading: What a near me search returns, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in Al Quoz search returns results ranked by proximity. IB Gram answers the underlying need differently: one-to-one Diploma teaching delivered into Al Quoz homes as live online sessions on Gulf Standard Time, matched on subject and level. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, because home visits are a service we run only in India.

The map is not lying to you, it is answering a different question. Proximity is a genuine convenience when the service is interchangeable. Diploma teaching is not interchangeable. A Higher Level Chemistry candidate losing marks on organic mechanisms needs someone who has taught that content and marked that paper; a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches candidate losing Paper 3 marks on notation needs someone else entirely. Neither need is affected by which side of Al Khail Road anyone lives on.

There is also a supply problem built into the district. Al Quoz is predominantly industrial by land area, so the residential population it supports is smaller than the map suggests, and the subset of that population who are qualified Diploma subject teachers, free at 5pm, and holding the MoHRE private tuition work permit required of individuals offering private lessons, is smaller still. Narrow the request to Higher Level Physics and the local list can be empty on the exact day you need it.

What follows replaces the map with a calendar and four reference tables: the two-year clock, the component limits, the internal assessment criteria letters, and the Mathematics route decision. Those are the four things Al Quoz families most often tell us they wish they had known a year earlier.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma clock, term by term
paragraphs: Most of what decides a Diploma score happens before the examination hall, and almost all of it is scheduled by the school rather than the board. The table sets out the sequence so a family can locate their own child on it. Note that the useful column is the last one: what has to be true already, because that is where the realistic plan comes from.

The first term of DP1 is the highest-value and least-used entry point. A student who has just met Higher Level content and is reasoning the way IGCSE rewarded can be redirected in a handful of sessions. The same student in the second term of DP2, with internal assessments due and mocks approaching, needs those sessions plus repair of everything built on the gap in between, and has less time to use them in.

The second thing the table shows is which doors close. Subject and level choices made at the end of Year 11 cannot be revisited from DP2. An internal assessment research question that cannot generate usable data is fixable in DP1 and expensive in DP2. The Extended Essay subject choice shapes what a strong essay even looks like, and it is made early.

IB session and results dates are deliberately absent from the table. ibo.org blocks automated access, so nothing specific has been verified for this project, and a date a parent acts on must come from the school's IB coordinator rather than from any tutoring page, including this one. UAE schools sit the May session; that much is safe to plan around.

sections.heading: Word and page limits across Diploma components, in one place
paragraphs: Nobody publishes this table, which is odd, because limits are the first thing a student needs and the last thing they are told clearly. Running over a limit does not earn extra credit; in several components it costs marks directly, and in all of them it costs the student time they did not have. Running well under usually means a criterion has been skipped rather than that the work is efficient.

The figures below are the widely published component limits, and they are the ones to confirm against the current subject guide your school holds. We deliberately do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes, because that material is the IB's copyright. Your child's subject teacher has the authoritative current version and the school's own interpretation of it.

The practical use of the table is planning rather than compliance. A 4,000-word Extended Essay with a required reflection process is a different project from a set of three Economics commentaries with a strict limit on each, and a student carrying both in the same term needs those two workloads sequenced rather than stacked. Families who draw this out on a single calendar in DP1 have a markedly easier DP2.
One more use: it exposes the component nobody has started. If your child can tell you the limit for every piece except one, that is the piece to ask about this week.

It is worth adding why under-length work is a warning rather than a relief. A short Extended Essay almost always means the reflection process has not happened, and a short science report usually means the evaluation criterion was reached at midnight. Length is not the thing being marked, but in both of those cases it is a visible symptom of something that is.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, by letter and by mark
paragraphs: Of all the gaps in this market, this is the widest: across the competitor pages researched for Dubai IB queries, not one names a single internal assessment criterion. Yet the criteria are the whole of the marking, and a student who cannot say what criterion C is asking for is writing blind into 20 per cent of a subject grade.

The letters matter because the marks are not evenly distributed. In the sciences, the criteria run from the research design through data analysis to conclusion and evaluation, and the heaviest weight sits in the middle, on what the student does with the data rather than on how the report reads. Students who spend their effort on presentation and their last evening on evaluation have the allocation exactly inverted.

The table below describes the criterion structure in the terms a parent can act on. Confirm the exact current letters, names and mark totals in the subject guide your school holds, because the IB revises them and we do not republish the guides. What does not change is the relationship: design constrains analysis, analysis constrains conclusion, and evaluation is marked on whether the student can see the weaknesses in their own method.

This is also where the honesty boundary is clearest. A tutor can teach what a criterion demands and tell a student their draft does not yet meet it. A tutor cannot write the section. Knowing the criteria by letter is what makes that distinction workable in practice, because the feedback becomes specific enough to be teaching rather than editing.

sections.heading: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision Al Quoz families revisit most and understand least, and it is taken at the end of Year 11 when the degree the student will apply to is often still vague. Getting it wrong is recoverable in DP1 and not recoverable in DP2, so it belongs on this page rather than in a conversation nobody has.

Analysis and Approaches is the proof, calculus and algebraic route. Applications and Interpretation is the statistics, modelling and technology route. Both are real Mathematics and both come at Higher and Standard Level; the difference is what they prepare a student to do next. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses commonly expect the Analysis route at Higher Level, and a student who arrives with Applications may find a prerequisite unmet after offers have been made.

The test is not which course sounds harder. It is which one the student can work in fluently, read against the subjects they want to study. A student who enjoys structure, proof and algebraic manipulation is in the wrong course in Applications even if the grade looks better; a student who thinks in data and context is often stronger in Applications and will produce a better internal assessment there.

Check the prerequisite with the universities themselves, including UAE institutions, because requirements differ by programme and they change. What a tutoring page can usefully tell you is that this decision has a deadline, that it is your school's deadline, and that it is worth a conversation with the Mathematics department before it passes rather than after.

sections.heading: The travel premium, and what the market charges in AED
paragraphs: Most price comparisons in this market start at the premium end, which flatters the premium end. Start instead with the question a near me search is implicitly asking: what does physical proximity cost? The answer is visible in the bands. Market rates for an in-home one-to-one visit in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel built in, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table and providers' own published rates.

That spread is the travel premium, and it buys a person in the room rather than better teaching. It also buys a smaller pool to choose from, because a tutor who drives fits two or three sessions into an evening where a tutor who does not fits four or five, and the scarce early-evening slots go to the families closest to them. In the weeks before the May session, that is exactly when Al Quoz parents are competing for the same hour.

The specialist bands are separate from the format question. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are published at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase showing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the top. Budget online provision starts far lower, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, and at that level the service is general support rather than Diploma component diagnosis. Every figure here is another provider's published rate as at October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the variable line in an education budget, which is why a plan with a stated end point matters more than an hourly rate.
