sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the shape of the UAE academic year
paragraphs: No competitor page in this research set discusses this, and every UAE family plans around it. The academic year here has a rhythm of its own: shortened days during Ramadan, a long summer that falls between the examination session and the start of the next year, and a winter break that lands in the middle of DP2 at a point when internal assessments are usually overdue.

During Ramadan the school day is shortened and household routines reshape around Iftar. In practice tutoring sessions move to post-Iftar slots for the month, which is agreed with the tutor rather than imposed, and attention in those sessions is often better than in a 5pm slot during a fasting day. Families who try to keep the pre-Ramadan timetable unchanged usually lose a fortnight to cancellations instead.

The winter break is the most undervalued block in the DP2 year. It falls after internal assessment drafts should exist and before the mock window, which makes it the one period when a student can work on a component without a competing deadline. Al Quoz families who use four sessions in that break typically arrive at mocks with the component already fixed rather than still diagnosing it.

Summer works the same way for DP1 students moving into DP2, and for IGCSE students entering the Diploma. Nothing is tied to a Dubai address, so lessons continue while the family travels, at a time that works in both zones. The practical point is that holiday weeks are not lost time; they are the only uncrowded time the year offers.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the line this market keeps crossing
paragraphs: One operator researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not a grey area; it is an academic honesty breach that can cost a student the entire Diploma, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller. IB Gram does not write, complete, edit to completion or supply coursework of any kind, and no tutor working through us is permitted to.

What a tutor does instead is teach the assessment. That means explaining each criterion in the IB's own terms, pressing on a research question until it can actually generate data, reading the student's own draft and saying where it sits against the criteria and why, and teaching whatever skill the draft shows is missing. The student writes every word. The useful test after a session is whether the student could explain and defend every change in their own words.

A second boundary concerns materials. We do not publish, reproduce or offer IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads, because that material is the boards' copyright and, for unreleased content, a malpractice exposure. We cite the official source and link to it, and the school holds proper access.

There is a related claim worth refusing explicitly. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office or centre. We describe what those bodies do. Any tutoring page implying endorsement is describing something it cannot show you.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Quoz, and the limits we will tell you about
paragraphs: The sequence is short and the first step does most of the work. Send the subject, the level, the school and the last two marked pieces, whether that is a paper or an internal assessment draft. A specialist reading those can usually name the failing pattern in one sentence, and the free trial lesson exists to do exactly that before any money changes hands.

Then the honest part. Narrow Diploma specialisms at popular hours are genuinely constrained in the weeks before the May session, when a large share of Dubai's DP2 students want the same early-evening slot. When that happens you get told, offered the nearest workable alternative, and given a realistic view of when the slot you wanted opens. No generalist is quietly substituted for the specialist you asked for, which is the standard failure mode in this market.

A few facts to carry into any conversation with any provider, including this one. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is granted free of charge for two years, and those operating without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so no amount is quoted here. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

Finally, nobody can promise a grade, and tutoring is not required for equivalency, university admission or school progression. What is being offered is a specialist who knows the component, a plan with an end point, and a review at which stopping is a legitimate answer.

process.title: Locate the student on the DP clock
process.description: DP1 first term and DP2 second term need completely different plans, and the same symptom means different things at each point. Telling us which term your child is in, and what is due next, shapes the whole conversation more than the subject does.

process.title: Send marked work, not just a grade
process.description: A grade says there is a problem. A marked script or a returned internal assessment draft says where. Photographs are fine, and a specialist reading two of them can usually say whether the issue is content, technique, timing or design before the first session.

process.description: One live session before any payment. By the end you should have the failing pattern named in a sentence, an estimate of how many sessions it takes, and a straight answer if the honest estimate is fewer sessions than you expected to buy.

process.title: Book a slot the school run survives
process.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around the real end of the day, which for Al Quoz usually means 5pm to 7pm on weekdays, with weekend mornings used when a DP2 block needs two sessions and the evenings cannot hold them.

process.title: Review at the next internal deadline
process.description: The plan is reviewed against the next school assessment, mock or internal assessment checkpoint. If the component is fixed, stopping is the right call. The expensive pattern in this market is a standing session nobody examines until the session has already happened.

whyPoints.description: A near me search ranks by distance; Diploma teaching does not vary by distance. Because lessons are online, an Al Quoz family reaches the same Higher Level Physics specialist as a family in Sobha Hartland, and the 5pm car journey stops rationing who is available.

whyPoints.title: Criteria discussed by letter
whyPoints.description: Across the competitor pages researched for Dubai IB queries, not one names a single internal assessment criterion. Feedback that identifies which criterion a draft fails, and by how many marks, is teaching. Feedback that says the work needs improving is not.

whyPoints.description: The 4,000-word Extended Essay, the strictly limited Economics commentaries, the page-guided Mathematics exploration and the 20 per cent science internal assessment weighting are all on this page, with a pointer to the school's own current subject guide to confirm them.

faqs.question: Why does a near me search not find the IB tutor we actually need?
faqs.answer: Because it ranks by distance and Diploma teaching does not vary by distance. A map search centred on Al Quoz returns tuition centres and general tutors, very few of whom can tell you that a science internal assessment is typically 20 per cent of the grade or which criterion your child's draft is failing. The useful filter is subject, level and component. Once lessons are delivered online, which is how we work, that filter is the only one that needs applying.

faqs.question: Do you send an IB tutor to our address in Al Quoz?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one Diploma tuition into Al Quoz homes over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to any address in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. Dubai providers who do visit homes charge roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour with travel included, per Bestimate's 2026 rate table. What online delivery buys you is the ability to pick the subject specialist rather than the nearest available person.

faqs.question: How long is the IB Extended Essay and when should it be started?
faqs.answer: It is 4,000 words with a required reflection process recorded with the school supervisor, and it should be started in DP1 rather than DP2. The strongest essays have narrow, arguable research questions; the weakest have broad topics that cannot be answered in the word count. Because the subject-specific criteria differ, the subject choice changes what a good essay looks like. Confirm the current requirements with the subject guide your school holds rather than with any tutoring website.

faqs.question: What is the internal assessment worth in IB sciences?
faqs.answer: Typically 20 per cent of the subject grade, marked by the school against lettered criteria and moderated by the IB. The marks are not evenly spread across those criteria: the heaviest weight sits on what the student does with their data rather than on how the report reads. That is why a research question too broad to measure with school equipment caps the available marks before any writing happens, and why design work in DP1 is worth more than polishing in DP2.

faqs.question: Which IB Maths course should my child take for an engineering degree?
faqs.answer: Engineering, physics and mathematics courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a student arriving with Applications and Interpretation can find a prerequisite unmet after offers are made. But verify the requirement with the specific programmes and universities on the list, including UAE institutions, because requirements differ by course and change. The decision is taken at the end of Year 11 to a school deadline, so it is worth a conversation with the Mathematics department before that date passes.

faqs.question: My child found IGCSE easy but is struggling in DP1. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the two reward different things. IGCSE rewards accurate recall and method; Higher Level work rewards reasoning, justification and the ability to apply a named principle rather than describe a phenomenon. A student who got by on recall arrives in DP1 with a strategy that quietly stops working, and the grades fall before anyone names the cause. It is a handful of sessions to redirect in the first DP1 term, and considerably more by the second term of DP2.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at my child's internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the most useful things a tutor does. They can explain what each criterion demands, say where the draft currently sits against it and why, press on a research question that cannot generate usable data, and teach a skill the draft shows is missing. They cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it. The test afterwards is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words; if not, the line has been crossed.

faqs.question: Which term of the Diploma is the best time to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: The first term of DP1, which is also the least popular answer because nothing feels urgent yet. At that point a student can be redirected from IGCSE habits to Higher Level reasoning in a small number of sessions, and internal assessment research questions can still be chosen well. By the second term of DP2 the same gap needs those sessions plus repair of everything built on top of it, with internal assessments due and mocks approaching, so the hours cost more and buy less.

faqs.question: Does it matter that Al Quoz is mostly an industrial district?
faqs.answer: It matters for the map search and for nothing else. Al Quoz Industrial 1 to 4 are warehouses, workshops, showrooms and the Alserkal Avenue arts spaces, with housing concentrated in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3. So a proximity search returns a tutor count that has little to do with families living there, and the pool of qualified Diploma subject teachers who are both nearby and free at 5pm is smaller than the result list suggests. Online delivery removes the issue entirely.

faqs.question: How should we use the winter break in DP2?
faqs.answer: As the one uncrowded block in the year. It falls after internal assessment drafts should exist and before the mock window, which means a student can work on one component without a competing deadline for the first time since September. Four focused sessions across that break typically mean arriving at mocks with the component fixed rather than still being diagnosed. Nothing is tied to a Dubai address, so the sessions continue if the family travels, at a time that works in both zones.

faqs.question: Does the Ramadan timetable disrupt a DP2 revision block?
faqs.answer: Only if you leave the slot where it was. Most Al Quoz families move the session to a post-Iftar time for the month. The school day shortens and the household rhythm reshapes around Iftar, so a 5pm session during a fasting day is usually worse than a later one. The slot is agreed with the tutor rather than imposed by a timetable. Families who try to keep the pre-Ramadan schedule unchanged tend to lose a fortnight to cancellations, which in DP2 is a fortnight that was carrying an internal assessment deadline.

faqs.question: What happens to the three bonus Diploma points?
faqs.answer: They come from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, which combines performance on both into up to three additional points on top of the 42 available from six subjects. Students routinely treat both as administrative obligations and then discover in DP2 that they are three points short of an offer. Both reward the same thing: a narrow, genuinely arguable question. A prescribed TOK title treated as a topic rather than an argument cannot reach the upper bands.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP2 student need?
faqs.answer: One a week per subject during term, rising to two in a defined block before mocks or the session. More than two a week in one subject rarely helps, because the student needs the days in between to practise independently and that is where the learning consolidates. If two subjects are failing at once, one session each works better than two in whichever feels most urgent this week. The block should carry a review date from the start.

faqs.question: What if no specialist covers our subject at the time we need?
faqs.answer: We say so and give you a realistic date, rather than substituting someone general. Narrow Higher Level specialisms at early-evening hours are genuinely constrained in the weeks before the May session, when a large share of Dubai's DP2 cohort wants the same slot. You will be offered the nearest workable alternative and told when the one you wanted is likely to open, so the decision to wait or proceed stays with you rather than being made quietly on your behalf.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz-4.tutorsIntro: Below are the kinds of tutor Al Quoz 4 households ask for most: Diploma subject specialists who teach the same syllabus every week, plus Middle Years teachers who know what the four criteria reward. Every match starts from the subject and level, then the time slot, then the person.

intro.heading: The search is about time, not distance
paragraphs: Al Quoz 4 sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, a pocket of villas wedged against one of the busiest road junctions in Dubai. Almost nobody in Al Quoz 4 attends school in Al Quoz 4. Children leave at seven in the morning for Al Barsha South, Al Safa, Umm Suqeim, Nad Al Sheba or Al Jaddaf, and they come back on a bus that threads three sub-communities before it reaches the gate. That daily shape, not the map, is what decides whether tutoring works here.

So the honest version of the question is this: at what hour can a tired fourteen-year-old sit down with a Chemistry teacher and actually learn something? The answer in Al Quoz 4 is almost never four o'clock, which is exactly the slot most agencies offer because it is the slot that suits a tutor driving between two villas. A session that starts before the child has eaten is a session that teaches half of what it should.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video, so the slot is chosen by the family rather than by traffic on Umm Suqeim Street. A 19:30 Tuesday is as easy to staff as a 16:00 Tuesday. A Saturday morning before the heat is easier still. Nobody is billing you for the twenty-five minutes it takes to get from Al Quoz 3 to your gate.

The second thing this frees up is the tutor pool. A family limited to tutors who can reach Al Quoz 4 by car is choosing from whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive and happens to be free at the one hour the drive allows. A family on video is choosing from every specialist available in that subject at that hour. For a Diploma subject with a narrow pool, Physics HL, Economics HL, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, that difference is the whole thing.

What follows is written for the Al Quoz 4 evening specifically: when the day ends at each of the schools this area feeds, what the drive does to a 16:00 start, what Dubai families pay a month rather than an hour, how to read a KHDA inspection band before you decide the teaching is the problem, and the line a tutor may not cross on an Internal Assessment. Everything with a number attached carries its source.

One caution before any of that. Al Quoz 4 is a small enough pocket that recommendations travel fast between neighbours, and a tutor who was excellent for a Year 7 mathematics student is not automatically the right person for a Diploma 2 student taking Physics at Higher Level. The subject and the component matter more than the referral. Ask what syllabus the tutor teaches weekly, ask how the paper you are worried about is marked, and listen for a specific answer rather than a reassuring one. A teacher who can tell you where the marks sit in Paper 3 has taught Paper 3.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz-4.programmesIntro: Al Quoz 4 children are spread across the IB continuum because the corridor they commute into contains full continuum schools as well as Diploma-only sixth forms. Support looks different in each, and the difference is not simply difficulty.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams, which is why parents often leave it alone until Year 5. The risk is quiet: inquiry units teach a child to research and present, but arithmetic fluency and sentence construction can drift without anyone noticing, and the gap shows up two years later in MYP mathematics. Support at this stage is short, frequent and skills-based rather than content-driven.
programmes.countryNote: Al Quoz 4 primary pupils mostly travel to Al Safa, Al Barsha South or Umm Suqeim and are home by 15:00 to 15:20. A thirty-minute online block at 16:00 three times a week does more here than a ninety-minute session once. Dubai schools also run Arabic and Social Studies from the primary years under KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements, so a PYP child already carries two curricula.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks every subject against four criteria, A to D, each on a one-to-eight scale, then converts the total into a one-to-seven grade. A student can know the content and still score five because the criterion asks for evaluation and the answer only describes. Most of the work in MYP tutoring is teaching a child to read the criterion strand before writing, which is a transferable skill and the one schools have least time to teach.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 students in Al Quoz 4 are in the longest school day of the area, often off the bus at 15:45 or later after a co-curricular block. The Personal Project in MYP 5 collides with that. A tutor supervises process and questions choices; the project itself stays the student's own work, and the school's own supervisor signs it off.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service. The failure mode is not intelligence; it is the internal deadline calendar. Four or five Internal Assessments land in a nine-month window alongside mock exams, and a student who treats each one as a surprise loses marks on every one. Diploma support is half teaching and half sequencing.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Al Quoz 4 drive or get driven to Nad Al Sheba, Al Jaddaf or Al Barsha South, and several schools in that corridor run a 15:30 finish with study periods after. The practical consequence is that a Diploma student here has a usable 17:00 or 19:30 slot, and almost never a usable 16:00 one. Plan the week around that rather than against it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. It is far less common in Dubai than the Diploma, but where a school offers it the Diploma courses inside it are marked to exactly the same standard, with the same Internal Assessments and the same papers. A student on CP needs the same subject teaching as a Diploma student in that course.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools in the Al Quoz and Al Barsha corridor run the CP, so a family here is usually comparing the Diploma against A Levels rather than against the CP. Where a child is on CP, say so at matching: the tutor needs to know the course is being examined on the Diploma syllabus even though the overall qualification differs.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz-4.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and Middle Years subjects Al Quoz 4 households request most, with the part of each that actually costs marks. A good match starts here rather than with a tutor's biography.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The HL course adds Paper 3, a long problem-solving paper worth a fifth of the grade, where students meet an unfamiliar scaffolded investigation. Marks go on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers. Weekly work on proof writing and on reading a multi-part stem is what moves this grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy and calculator-dependent. The common loss is graphical display calculator technique: students who can do the maths by hand lose marks because they cannot produce the required regression output or read a distribution screen. Sessions here are part content, part machine drill.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The syllabus is not the hard part; the command terms are. A question that says explain and receives a description scores nothing. Add the data-analysis paper, where uncertainty propagation and gradient interpretation decide half the available marks, and you have the two places a Physics grade is usually lost.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and equilibrium carry most of the HL difficulty, but the mark-losing habit is arithmetic in moles questions done without units. Students who write every step with units and significant figures gain marks they were already entitled to. The Internal Assessment also rewards a narrow, measurable research question.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem. Biology rewards precise terminology over fluent prose, and a student who writes three sentences where the mark scheme wants one named process scores one mark from three. Vocabulary drilling and short, timed recall work beat re-reading notes by a wide margin.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks. A correctly labelled diagram with axes, curves and shifted equilibrium earns credit before any prose is read. HL adds the policy paper, which asks for quantitative work on real data. The Internal Assessment commentary is where most students either win or waste the easiest marks on the course.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two external papers plus an Individual Oral and, at HL, an essay. The Individual Oral is the component students prepare worst because it is internal and feels informal. It is not: it is a ten-minute argument with a global issue at its centre, and it needs rehearsing like a paper.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The tool list is finite and examinable: Ansoff, SWOT, break-even, cash-flow forecasting, investment appraisal. Students lose marks by describing a tool rather than applying it to the stimulus firm. HL adds the business research project, which needs a real organisation and a question narrow enough to answer in the word limit.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.levels: MYP and DP ab initio or B
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and non-Arab students are taught it in separate classes from first-language speakers. Many families treat it as a compliance subject until a report grade bites. Short, regular oral practice is the only thing that moves it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. Students who write about knowledge in the abstract score badly; the marks are in real, specific examples held against a clear claim. Tutoring here is argument coaching, and the writing stays entirely the student's own.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz-4.regionsIntro: Al Quoz 4 is one of four Al Quoz sub-communities and sits inside the central road corridor. These are the neighbourhoods its families share schools, buses and road congestion with, and the operational detail that actually differs between them.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: The wider Al Quoz spreads from industrial blocks to villa pockets. Al Quoz 1 to 4 are the residential ones, and the bus routes serving them usually cover two or three sub-communities in sequence, which is where the twenty-five minute lag comes from.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Apartment living, short walk to Metro, and a school run that goes outbound rather than inbound. Downtown Diploma students often have a shorter commute than Al Quoz 4 students to the same schools, so their usable slot sits half an hour earlier.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Dense towers either side of the creek extension. Families here face a lift-plus-car double journey in the morning, and parents frequently ask for a 20:00 slot because the working day in DIFC and Business Bay itself runs late.

regions.name: DIFC
regions.note: Few schools, many working parents on financial-market hours. The practical pattern is a weekend-heavy schedule: one weekday evening session and a longer Saturday morning block, which online delivery supports without a travel charge.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Home to a full IB continuum school and reachable from Al Quoz 4 on Al Khail Road in good conditions. The return leg after a 15:30 finish is the problem, not the morning, which pushes Diploma sessions towards 18:00 and later.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Several large British and IB schools with extended days and heavy co-curricular programmes. Al Quoz 4 children attending them are commonly home after 16:30, and families here are the strongest case for a late-evening or weekend slot.

regions.name: Meydan and Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Newer communities with schools built in the last decade, so inspection histories are short and parents rely more on cohort reputation than on published bands. Worth reading the actual KHDA report rather than the headline band.

schoolClusters.note: This is where most Al Quoz 4 children go to school. It holds full IB continuum schools alongside British schools running IGCSE then A Level or Diploma, which is why a single street in Al Quoz 4 can contain an MYP 4 student, a Year 11 IGCSE student and a Diploma 2 student.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB tutor near me in Al Quoz 4 is really asking
paragraphs: The short answer: it is asking for a slot that works, a teacher who knows the exact syllabus, and a price that is clear before you commit. Proximity is a proxy for all three, and in Al Quoz 4 it is a poor one, because the thing that limits tutoring here is the road network between 15:30 and 17:00 rather than the number of tutors within five kilometres.

Consider what near me buys. A tutor who lives in Al Quoz 3 can reach you quickly, which means they can offer a 16:00 slot. That is the one hour your child is least able to use: just off the bus, not fed, bag unopened. The same tutor cannot offer 19:30 because by then they are two villas away in Al Barsha. So the convenience of proximity converts, in practice, into a narrower choice of time.

Now consider what near me costs. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted across the market at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, figures drawn from published competitor rate pages and the Bestimate Dubai tutoring cost table. A meaningful part of that difference is the car. You are paying for travel time, and the tutor is pricing the trip into the hour.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Al Quoz 4 is one-to-one teaching over live video, chosen for subject depth and timed to the family's evening. The rest of this page makes that case with the local detail rather than asserting it.

sections.heading: The Al Quoz 4 school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: Bell times across the schools Al Quoz 4 feeds run from about 14:30 for primary to 15:45 for schools with an extended day, and the bus adds twenty-five to forty minutes because Al Quoz routes typically loop two or three sub-communities before reaching a gate. That lag is the single most useful number a parent can give at matching, and almost nobody volunteers it.

The table below is the shape of a normal Al Quoz 4 weekday. It is not a recommendation to book late for the sake of it; some children genuinely work well at 16:30. It is a correction to the assumption that a 16:00 start is the default. If a child arrives home at 15:55, a 16:00 session begins with a child who has not eaten, and the first fifteen minutes are spent recovering rather than learning.

Fridays are different and underused. Most Dubai private schools finish between 12:00 and 12:30 on a Friday, and the weekend then runs Saturday and Sunday. A Saturday morning block at 10:00 is the only time in the week when a student is rested, unhurried and not carrying that day's homework. Families who move their heaviest subject there usually report it is the session that gets cancelled least.

One more practical point: give the tutor the bell time and the bus arrival, not the time you would like the session to start. A tutor who knows the child walks in at 15:50 will plan a different first ten minutes from one who assumes a 15:30 finish.

sections.heading: Why the drive stopped deciding who teaches your child
paragraphs: Ten years ago the tutor pool for an Al Quoz 4 family was genuinely geographic. It is not now, and the comparison below is the honest version rather than a sales line. In-home tutoring has real advantages: a tutor in the room reads body language, cannot be muted, and keeps a reluctant eleven-year-old at the table. For a young child with attention difficulties those advantages can decide the outcome.

What in-home cannot do is widen the pool. A Diploma student taking Physics HL in Al Quoz 4 needs someone who teaches that syllabus repeatedly, knows how the data-analysis paper is marked, and can read an uncertainty calculation at a glance. The number of people who meet that description, are free at 19:30 on a Wednesday, and are willing to drive to Al Quoz 4 is small. Remove the drive and the pool widens by an order of magnitude.

Online also changes what persists after the hour. A whiteboard that can be saved, a worked solution the student can reread on Sunday, a recording of the ten minutes that finally made Paper 3 scaffolding click. None of that survives an in-home session unless somebody photographs a notebook. Over a two-year Diploma that accumulated record is worth more than most families expect.

The fair conclusion is that format should follow purpose. Young child, basic fluency, short attention: proximity matters. Diploma subject at Higher Level, specific component, limited hours before a deadline: expertise matters more, and expertise is what removing the car buys you.

sections.heading: What Dubai families pay a month, not an hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a budget conversation, because no family buys one hour. The number that matters is the monthly outgoing, and it is remarkably easy to find once you stop looking at per-hour headlines. The table below converts the published Dubai market bands into monthly figures, with the source of each band named, because an unsourced number is worth nothing to a parent comparing providers.

Start at the bottom rather than the top. The cheapest real option in Dubai is a university-student tutor online, advertised from around AED 45 to 65 an hour by EdFlik and from around AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya on their own published pages. That is genuine value for arithmetic fluency, vocabulary drilling or keeping a Middle Years student on top of homework. It is not the right spend for Chemistry HL eight weeks before a paper, and nobody should pretend otherwise.

The middle band, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online for a qualified subject tutor, is where most Diploma support sits. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes around AED 270. At one session a week that is an outgoing of roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, which matches Bestimate's own mid-band monthly estimate. Specialist exam-year support runs higher, AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above on the same source.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages, because the figure depends on subject, level and hours, and a number invented for a landing page is worse than no number. What we do publish is the market, with attribution, so you can judge any quote you receive, ours included, against it. The free trial lesson exists so the judgement happens before money moves.

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA report before you decide the teaching is the problem
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band for each school. Parents in Al Quoz 4 quote those bands constantly, and misread them almost as often, because a band is a whole-school judgement and your child sits in one subject in one year group.

The useful move is to open the actual report rather than the headline. Inspection reports break performance down by subject and by phase, and it is common for a school rated Very Good overall to carry a weaker judgement in one department or one key stage. If your daughter's Chemistry grade has slipped and the report flags secondary science attainment, that is useful information. If the report praises secondary science, the problem is more likely to be her method than the teaching.

Two further pieces of local context help. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. And Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Newer schools have short inspection histories, so a band tells you less about them than about an established neighbour.

None of this is a reason to tutor or not to tutor. It is a reason to diagnose before you spend. The first session with any IB Gram tutor starts with the student's own last assessment and its lost marks, which is a more reliable diagnostic than a school-level band ever is.

sections.heading: The Diploma two years, and where the pressure actually lands
paragraphs: Families plan Diploma support around the final papers, which are in the May session for UAE schools. The pressure does not land there. It lands in the middle, in a nine-month stretch where four or five Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, and two rounds of mocks arrive in an order nobody has written down for the student in one place.

Work backwards instead. The Extended Essay usually needs a supervised first draft well before the final Diploma year begins in earnest, because once Internal Assessments start arriving there is no spare week to find a research question. Science Internal Assessments need data collected while lab access still exists. The Mathematics exploration needs a topic narrow enough to finish, which is a decision, not a task, and students delay decisions far longer than tasks.

A tutor earns their fee here by refusing to let a deadline be a surprise. The first session of a Diploma engagement should produce a single sheet: every internal deadline the school has published, every external component, and the three weeks in the year where two of them collide. Everything after that is teaching against a known map rather than reacting to whatever arrived on Sunday.

Because no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, which blocks automated checking, this page names the May session as the one UAE schools sit and nothing more precise. Confirm every IB date with your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative version for your cohort, and plan the internal deadlines from the school calendar rather than from any website.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the clearest line in the whole market and the one most often blurred. Work submitted for IB assessment must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain the criteria, question a method, suggest reading, point at a weak paragraph and say why it is weak, and model technique on a different example. Those are all teaching.

What a tutor must never do is produce the work. No tutor at IB Gram will write the Internal Assessment, draft the Extended Essay, compose the Theory of Knowledge essay or supply coursework. We do not sell completed assessments, and we will not edit a draft into something the student could not have written. One operation in this market openly sells finished Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, and the consequence falls on the child, not the seller.

In practice the boundary is easy to hold if the session is structured right. The student brings the draft and reads a section aloud. The tutor asks what the criterion actually rewards, where the evidence for the claim sits, and what a reader would still not know. The student writes the fix between sessions. That loop improves the mark more reliably than a rewrite would, because it also improves the next piece of work.

Feedback on criteria is also where the quickest gains sit. Students routinely lose marks in a criterion they never read. A tutor who makes a student mark their own draft against the published descriptors, letter by letter, usually finds two or three marks sitting in plain sight before any new content is taught.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB in Dubai
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies whatever international curriculum it is licensed for. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines required this to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Al Quoz 4 families with children in IB programmes are therefore running two curricula at once, and only one of them generates a Diploma grade.

The rules are specific enough to matter. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed, which is a real constraint on what any tutor can offer here. Support means practising the school's own material, not substituting a better syllabus.

Where this bites is the report card. A strong Diploma candidate can carry a weak Arabic grade for years and then find it matters for a university application or for how the school streams them. Short, frequent oral practice in the school's own material is the realistic intervention, and it is far cheaper the year before it becomes urgent.

process.title: Tell us the bell time, not the ideal time
process.description: The first message should say which school, which year group, what time the day ends and when the bus actually arrives in Al Quoz 4. That single line removes most of the back-and-forth, because it tells us which slots are real for your household rather than which ones look tidy on a calendar.

process.title: Send the last marked assessment
process.description: A mock script, a report card or a returned Internal Assessment draft is worth more than a description of the problem. We read it for pattern rather than score: lost marks that cluster in one command term, in one topic, or in the last question of every paper each point at a different fix.

process.title: Meet the tutor on a free trial lesson
process.description: One trial lesson per family, booked before any payment is taken and with no card details required. It is a real lesson on real material, not a sales call, and the useful question afterwards is whether your child explained something back that they could not explain before.

process.title: Fix the slot and the first eight weeks
process.description: Agree the weekly hour, then agree what the eight weeks have to achieve: a specific paper technique, a topic rebuilt from the start, an Internal Assessment taken from question to final draft by the student. A target you can check beats a subscription you cannot.

process.title: Review against evidence, not feeling
process.description: At the eight-week mark we look at marked work again. If the lost marks have moved, the plan continues. If they have not, we change the tutor, the format or the diagnosis rather than adding hours. Re-matching costs nothing and happens from the same specialist pool.

whyPoints.title: The slot comes before the tutor
whyPoints.description: Matching starts with the hour your child can actually work, which in Al Quoz 4 is usually later than agencies assume. A brilliant tutor in a useless slot teaches a tired child. Because delivery is on video, a 19:30 Wednesday is no harder for us to staff than a 16:00 one.

whyPoints.title: Subject depth, not general tutoring
whyPoints.description: A Physics HL student is matched to someone who teaches that syllabus and knows how the data-analysis paper is marked. The pool is national rather than local, so depth is available at the hour you need instead of only at the hour a car can reach you.

whyPoints.title: Prices you can check against the market
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is the market's, with the source named, and none of it is presented as our price list. You can hold any quote you receive, ours included, against published Dubai bands. A provider who will not publish a number is asking for trust it has not earned.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody at IB Gram writes an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. Saying so plainly matters in a market where completed assessments are openly for sale.

whyPoints.title: No claim we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No regulator endorses IB Gram, and this page does not suggest one does. We name KHDA, the Ministry of Education and MoHRE to explain what they govern. There is no UAE office, no star rating we invented and no statistic without its source and date.

whyPoints.title: Re-matching is normal, not a complaint
whyPoints.description: Some pairings do not work, and the useful response is to change them quickly rather than to wait a term. Tell us after two sessions if it is not landing; we re-match from the same pool at the same rate, and the diagnosis already gathered carries across.

faqs.question: How quickly can we start if we search for an IB tutor near me in Al Quoz 4 today?
faqs.answer: For the common Diploma and Middle Years subjects, a trial lesson is usually arranged within a few days, because we are matching from a national pool of online specialists rather than waiting for someone who can drive to Al Quoz 4. Narrow combinations take longer: Higher Level Physics at a specific evening hour, or a less commonly taught language, can need a week or more. We will tell you which case you are in rather than promise a slot we cannot staff, and if nothing suitable is free we say so instead of offering a generalist.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Quoz 4 families usually commute to?
faqs.answer: Al Quoz 4 is residential, so almost every child travels out. The two main directions are the Al Barsha South and Al Safa corridor, which holds full IB continuum schools alongside British schools running IGCSE then A Level or Diploma, and the inner corridor towards Nad Al Sheba and Al Jaddaf on Al Khail Road. The practical consequence is a wide spread of finish times from one street, between about 14:30 and 15:45, and a bus that adds twenty-five to forty minutes on top. That spread is why session timing is the first thing we ask about.

faqs.question: Does a 16:00 session actually work for a child living in Al Quoz 4?
faqs.answer: For a primary child off a 14:30 bell it often does, because the bus lands around 15:00 and there is time to eat. For a secondary student from an extended-day school it rarely does: the second bus wave can reach Al Quoz 4 at 16:20, and a 16:00 start then means a session begun on the road. Our advice for Middle Years and Diploma students here is 17:00 at the earliest, 19:30 for anyone with sport or a co-curricular block, and a Saturday morning for the heaviest subject.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an Al Quoz 4 address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Al Quoz 4 families are delivered one to one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and your child's own school material on screen. We are explicit about this because the market is not: several providers route UAE enquiries to tutors who are not in the country while implying a visit. If you specifically want someone in the room, you want a different provider, and we will say so.

faqs.question: What do Dubai families typically spend a month on IB support?
faqs.answer: Taking published Dubai market bands rather than our own figures, one weekly hour with a university-student tutor online runs roughly AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's budget estimate. One weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor sits around AED 600 to 1,200. Exam-year specialist support at two sessions a week reaches AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. In-home packages seen in the market are quoted at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Judge any quote, including ours, against those bands.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives near Al Quoz 4 better than one who teaches Chemistry HL every day?
faqs.answer: For a young child who needs someone physically at the table, proximity can win. For a Higher Level Diploma subject it generally does not. The marks in Chemistry HL sit in organic mechanisms, equilibrium and a research question narrow enough to measure, and the person who can move those is the person who teaches that syllabus weekly. Restricting the search to a twenty-minute drive and a single workable hour shrinks the pool to whoever is left. Removing the drive widens it to every specialist free that evening.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit, and how would I verify it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Ask a UAE-based tutor to show their permit, and apply or check through mohre.gov.ae.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legally do with my daughter's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the content, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether her research question is answerable, suggest reading, and tell her which paragraph is weak and why. That is all teaching and all permitted. What a tutor must never do is write, draft or edit the work to completion, because the submission must be her own. We do not supply completed assessments at any price. The most productive session we run on an Internal Assessment has her marking her own draft against the published descriptors while the tutor asks where the evidence is.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 5 and starts the Diploma next year. When should support begin?
faqs.answer: The useful window is the second half of MYP 5 and the summer that follows, not the first term of Diploma 1. Two things need doing. First, the subject choice itself, particularly Mathematics, where Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation lead to different university prerequisites. Second, the habits the Diploma punishes hardest: writing to a criterion, meeting an internal deadline, and reading a command term before answering. A student who arrives in Diploma 1 already able to do those three things has a materially easier first year.

faqs.question: Does an Al Quoz 4 child study Arabic and Islamic Education on top of the IB?
faqs.answer: They sit alongside it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum, with the requirement in force from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Classes are organised separately for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are not permitted. Tutoring here means practising the school's own material, since using different or additional content without Ministry of Education permission is not allowed.

faqs.question: Do Al Quoz 4 families usually pause tutoring during Ramadan or move it later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Al Quoz 4 families ask for exactly that. Dubai schools shorten the day during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon but makes it a poor teaching window because the household is fasting and preparing. A post-Iftar slot, commonly between 20:30 and 22:00, works far better, and online delivery makes it simple to arrange because no one is driving anywhere late at night. Families who prefer to pause for the month can do that instead and resume afterwards; we would rather you paused than paid for sessions nobody used.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA rating of Good actually tell me about my child's lessons?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents assume. Good is the baseline KHDA expects of a Dubai private school, and it is a whole-school judgement covering every phase and subject. Your child sits in one subject in one year group. Open the published report and read the subject and phase tables: a school rated Good overall can be stronger in secondary mathematics than in secondary science, or the reverse. If the report praises the department your child is struggling in, the cause is more likely to be method or workload than teaching quality.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do Al Quoz 4 parents ask about most often?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, split between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and the split itself causes a good share of the enquiries because students sometimes sit in the wrong course for a term before anyone notices. Then Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level, where the data-analysis and mechanism work is the common failure point. Then Economics, where diagram marks are routinely lost. Middle Years requests cluster around mathematics and the four-criteria writing problem, and Arabic as an additional language comes up every reporting cycle.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Al Quoz 4 household share a tutor?
faqs.answer: They can share a tutor, but only usefully when they are in the same subject at the same level, and genuinely that is uncommon between siblings. What works better is two separate one-to-one slots with the same tutor back to back on the same evening, which keeps the household's schedule simple while keeping each session focused on one child's lost marks. Shared sessions across different year groups tend to become supervised homework, which is a fine thing to buy but not what a subject specialist is for.

faqs.question: The tutor and my child are not clicking after two sessions, so what then?
faqs.answer: Tell us after the second session rather than at the end of term. Fit problems show up early and almost never fix themselves: a quiet student paired with a fast talker, or a confident one paired with somebody too gentle to push. We re-match from the same specialist pool at the same rate, and the diagnosis already gathered from the marked work carries across, so the new tutor does not start from nothing. Re-matching is a normal part of the process here, not a complaint we resist.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-quoz-4.closingHeading: Start with the hour, then the subject

The piece most families have not settled is the hour, and in Al Quoz 4 that is the decision that makes or breaks the term. dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-qusais.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students at Dubai schools. Each is matched to a named subject at a named level, and each teaches over live video rather than travelling, which is why the match is not limited by who happens to live nearby.

intro.heading: Why a "near me" search is the wrong tool for this job
paragraphs: Google reads "near me" as a request for proximity and answers it with whatever business listings sit closest to your device. In Al Qusais that returns tuition centres along Damascus Street, individual tutors with a mobile number and a subject list that runs from Year 2 to A Level, and agency pages that mention Al Qusais in a drop-down menu. The ranking signal is distance and listing quality. It is not subject expertise, and nothing in the result tells you which of those options has ever taught a Higher Level option paper.

The IB Diploma is unusually unforgiving about this. Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, each with an internal assessment moderated by the IB, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. The core contributes up to three points of the 45. Each subject has its own command terms, its own paper structure and its own internal assessment criteria, written as lettered strands with mark allocations. A tutor who cannot name those strands for your child's subject is not going to move the mark on them.

Where the Diploma differs from an examined linear course is in timing. A large part of the grade is fixed during the two years rather than in the final fortnight. Internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay process and the TOK exhibition and essay all fall across DP1 and DP2 on the school's internal calendar. A family that starts looking for help in the spring of DP2 is shopping after the coursework marks have already been set, which is why this page spends more space on the calendar than on the subjects.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, which is what allows the match to be made on subject and level instead of on driving distance from Al Qusais. The practical consequence for a parent here is that the pool stops being whoever is free in north-east Dubai and becomes whoever is free at 17:30.

The rest of this page is built for someone who has typed that search and wants something useful back. It counts the two Diploma years backwards from the May session, sets out which authority regulates your child's school and why that may not be your own emirate, explains what a tutor can legitimately do with the core, maps school finish times onto workable session slots for this district, and describes what a trial lesson should have told you within forty minutes. It also says plainly which exam session your child is actually entered for, because a plan counted back from the wrong window wastes a term, and the only dates worth working from are the ones your school's IB coordinator has issued in writing.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-qusais.programmesIntro: The three IB programmes run by Dubai schools need different kinds of help. The shorthand: inquiry habits in primary, criteria in the middle years, and components in the Diploma.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Assessment is split between externally marked papers and an internally marked component in every subject, moderated by the IB. Grades run 1 to 7 per subject, with up to three further points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combined. Minimum requirements apply across the whole diploma, not subject by subject, which is why one weak Higher Level subject can be more dangerous than it looks.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools sit the May session, so the internal calendar matters more than the external one for an Al Qusais family. By February of DP2 the coursework marks are largely fixed and the remaining work is paper technique, which is a different and cheaper kind of tutoring than the design work needed a year earlier.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D in each subject group, with achievement levels converted to a 1 to 8 grade. There is no content syllabus to revise in the familiar sense, which is why strong students sometimes stall: they know the material and lose marks against a criterion strand they have never had explained to them.
programmes.countryNote: Schools serving Al Qusais vary in how long they run MYP. Some carry it to Year 11 with eAssessment, others switch to IGCSE after Year 9. Those two paths need completely different Year 9 preparation, so the first thing worth checking is which one your child's school takes.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examination, closing with the Year 6 exhibition. Reporting is narrative rather than numerical, which makes it hard for parents to judge whether a child is behind in arithmetic or reading until a transition exposes it.
programmes.countryNote: For families in this part of Dubai, the common trigger is a move into a PYP school from a school with weekly tests and ranked positions. The child is not weaker; the feedback has gone quiet. A short, specific arithmetic and reading check is usually all that is needed to find out.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects below are the ones Dubai students most often need help with outside maths and the physical sciences. Each note names the component where marks are most reliably recovered.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Built around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and continuity. The internal assessment is where Standard Level students gain the most ground, because the research design criterion rewards a narrow controlled question and most students submit one that is far too broad to analyse.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be used as evidence, not recited. Students lose marks by describing an experiment in detail and never linking it to the question's demand. The Higher Level extensions and the approaches to research section reward precise terminology about sampling and ethics.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall is necessary and not sufficient; the marks sit in applying a named place to a specific process. The fieldwork internal assessment stands or falls on whether the method generated data that can actually be analysed statistically.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a source-based assessment with a fixed structure that can be drilled, which makes it the fastest component to improve. The historical investigation needs a question narrow enough to answer in 2,200 words and a genuine evaluation of two sources.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 rewards precise definitions on systems and data structures. The solution development internal assessment fails most often on documentation rather than code: students build something that works and lose marks on criteria about planning and testing evidence.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study for Paper 1 is a known quantity and should be worked systematically from the term it is released. Application marks need the actual business named in the answer, which is the single most common omission in this subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A technology-assumed course where the examiner wants interpretation. A correct chi-squared value with no statement about the hypothesis earns partial credit. Graph theory at Higher Level and the normal distribution at Standard are the usual weak points.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course that can satisfy two group requirements. Students underestimate the systems vocabulary and the value judgements strand, both of which carry marks that pure content revision never touches.

subjects.name: Spanish and French ab initio
subjects.description: Designed for near beginners and assessed across prescribed themes with writing, listening, reading and an individual oral. Progress is highly responsive to weekly spoken practice, which is the one thing a crowded Diploma timetable rarely leaves room for.

sections.heading: What a proximity search actually ranks, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: A local search result is assembled from business listings, categories, reviews and distance from the device. Those are reasonable signals for a dentist. For Diploma tutoring they are close to useless, because none of them encodes the only fact that matters: has this person taught this subject at this level and seen this internal assessment marked.

The listings themselves make it worse. An individual tutor advertising in Al Qusais typically lists a dozen subjects across ten year groups, because a narrow advert gets fewer calls. A tuition centre lists curricula rather than syllabuses. Neither is dishonest, but both are optimised for enquiry volume rather than for match quality, and the parent is left guessing.

There is a second-order problem specific to the IB. Because the Diploma cohort is small relative to the British and Indian curriculum cohorts in this part of Dubai, the tutors who advertise locally are mostly serving those larger markets. Their IB experience is often genuine but thin: one or two students, one subject, one level. That is enough to be credible on a phone call and not enough to be useful on a Higher Level Paper 3.

The replacement test is simple and takes a few minutes on the phone. Ask what the internal assessment in that subject is marked against, by criterion. Ask what each paper is worth. Ask which topic the student most recently lost marks on and what the command term in that question was asking for. Somebody who teaches the subject regularly answers immediately; somebody who does not changes the subject to motivation and rapport.

sections.heading: The two Diploma years counted backwards
paragraphs: Dubai IB schools sit the May session. Work backwards from there and the shape of the two years becomes obvious, and so does the point at which tutoring stops being able to change certain marks. Specific IB examination and results dates are set by the IB and should be confirmed with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org; they are deliberately not restated here, because a date a parent plans around has to come from the source that sets it.

What can be planned confidently is the internal calendar, because the school sets it and tells you. Subject choices are fixed early in DP1. Internal assessment proposals follow in the second half of DP1 for most subjects, with first drafts in the autumn of DP2 and final submissions through the winter. The Extended Essay runs on its own track with a supervisor and reflection sessions. TOK has an exhibition and an essay, each with its own deadline.

The expensive misunderstanding is treating all of this as one deadline in May. By the time a student sits the papers, a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade is already banked in the internal assessment, and up to three diploma points have been settled by the Extended Essay and TOK. A family starting support in March of DP2 can still improve the examined papers, which is worth doing, but the other half of the grade is closed.

The practical version for an Al Qusais family is to ask the school for its internal deadline calendar in September of DP1, and to book tutoring against that rather than against the exam. sections.heading: Which authority regulates your child's school, and why it may not be your emirate
paragraphs: Families along the Dubai-Sharjah corridor ask this constantly, and the answer is that the regulator follows the school, not the home address. A child living in Al Nahda on the Sharjah side who attends a school in Al Garhoud is at a KHDA-regulated school. A child living in Al Qusais who attends a school across the boundary is at a school answering to the Sharjah Private Education Authority.

The full map is worth knowing because it is almost entirely absent from competing pages. Dubai private schools fall to KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The powers are not identical. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits with the emirate regulator and not only inspection. At federal level, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is what every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement is built on.

For a tutoring decision this matters in two concrete ways. Inspection reports are published by the relevant authority, so you read KHDA for a Dubai school and SPEA for a Sharjah one, and the subject-level commentary in those reports often tells you more than the headline band. And term calendars can differ between emirates, which in a two-school household is the practical reason a shared tutoring slot keeps collapsing in the spring.

sections.heading: The core: three points almost nobody tutors
paragraphs: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together contribute up to three points to the 45-point diploma total. Three points is the difference between a conditional offer and a rejection at plenty of universities, and it is available for work that is not examined under time pressure. It is also, in this market, barely tutored at all, because it is harder to sell than a subject and harder to explain than a paper.

The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece in a subject the student is studying, supervised by a school teacher with formal reflection sessions. Most of the marks that go missing are lost at the start, in a research question that is either unanswerable in the word count or answerable in a paragraph. A tutor's most valuable hour here is spent long before drafting, interrogating the question until it is both narrow and genuinely open.

Theory of Knowledge has an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. The common failure is writing about the topic rather than arguing the title, using real-life situations as decoration instead of as evidence. This is teachable in a way that feels unfamiliar to students who have spent five years being rewarded for content recall, and it responds quickly to being made to defend a claim out loud.

The boundary is firm and worth stating. A tutor does not write the Extended Essay, does not write the TOK essay, and does not supply paragraphs for a student to adapt. The tutor teaches the criteria, questions the argument, and marks a draft against the published descriptors so the student knows which criterion is costing them. The school supervisor's role and deadlines stand untouched. Any provider offering a finished essay is offering the student an academic-honesty investigation.

sections.heading: From MYP into the Diploma: where the eighteen-month gap shows
paragraphs: A student who has spent five years being assessed against criteria A to D on a 1 to 8 scale arrives in DP1 and meets papers marked against assessment objectives on a 1 to 7 scale. The two systems are related and they do not feel related. Strong MYP students are often the ones who struggle most in the first term, because the habits that earned them a 7 on a criterion do not automatically earn them a 5 on a Diploma paper.

The gap shows up in three specific places. First, timed written answers: MYP assessment often allows planning time and redrafting, while a Diploma paper rewards a structured answer produced in twelve minutes. Second, algebraic fluency, where MYP mathematics can be navigated with a calculator and a method sheet and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches cannot. Third, command terms, which carry specific meanings in the Diploma that MYP uses more loosely.

There is a parallel gap for students coming from IGCSE, and it is almost the opposite. An IGCSE student has strong exam technique and weak independent research experience, so they handle Paper 1 confidently and flounder on the internal assessment. An MYP student usually arrives with the reverse profile. Knowing which of the two your child is makes the first term of DP1 much cheaper to fix.

The useful intervention is short and early. A diagnostic in the first six weeks of DP1 on timed writing, algebraic manipulation and command-term reading will show which of the three gaps is present. Six to eight weekly sessions on the specific gap generally closes it, after which most students need subject work rather than transition work. Families who miss that window usually end up buying a full year of support instead.

sections.heading: Finding a session slot that survives the Al Qusais school run
paragraphs: This is the unglamorous reason tutoring arrangements fail, and it is entirely predictable. A slot agreed in September at 16:30 is already wrong if the child gets home at 16:20, because nobody can walk through the door and start a Higher Level chemistry session. Three cancellations later the arrangement quietly ends, and the family concludes that tutoring did not work.

Work it out properly once. Note the actual school finish time, not the published one. Add the bus route, which from Al Garhoud into Al Qusais is twenty to thirty minutes in term time and longer if the route serves Mirdif first, and from Academic City can be forty-five. Add twenty minutes for arriving, eating and changing. That gives the earliest honest start. For most Diploma students in this district it lands between 16:45 and 17:30.

Then decide how many sessions the week can carry. A student on a long bus route who leaves at 06:30 manages one weekday session well and two badly. A student with a short journey can carry two. Weekend slots are more reliable than Thursday evenings for almost everyone, and during Ramadan the whole pattern shifts, with post-Iftar sessions working better than late afternoons.

Because lessons are delivered over live video, moving a slot costs nothing but a message, which is the practical advantage over an arrangement that requires somebody to drive into Al Qusais. A session displaced by a fixture or a school revision clinic moves to another evening the same week instead of being written off. Over two Diploma years that recovers a meaningful number of hours.

sections.heading: What a trial lesson should have told you in forty minutes
paragraphs: A trial is a diagnostic, not a sales meeting, and it should be judged on what it produced rather than on whether everyone enjoyed it. By the end of forty minutes you should know three things: what the tutor identified as the actual problem, why they think that, and what they would do about it in the first three sessions.

The first signal is whether the tutor worked on real material. A trial conducted on a generic worksheet tells you nothing about your child's course. A trial worked on this week's class topic or last term's mock script tells you whether the tutor can read a script, spot the pattern in the errors, and say something specific about it. Ask for your child's current material to be used, and treat reluctance as information.

The second signal is the diagnosis itself. "She needs to build confidence" is not a diagnosis. "She can differentiate correctly but loses the chain rule inside a product, and she is not reading the command term before she starts, so she is describing where the question asks her to evaluate" is a diagnosis. The second kind can be worked on next Tuesday. The first kind cannot be worked on at all.

The third signal is your child's reaction, which is worth more than most parents allow. A student who comes out of a trial able to explain what they got wrong has been taught. A student who comes out saying it was fine has been entertained. If the fit is wrong, say so and ask for a different tutor; a provider that resists that conversation is telling you how the next six months will go.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the shape of the UAE school year
paragraphs: A tutoring plan written in September that ignores the UAE calendar will be rewritten twice by March. School hours shorten during Ramadan, the pattern of the day changes, and revision that was going to happen in the late afternoon needs to move. Families who plan for this keep their momentum; families who do not lose four to six weeks at the point in DP2 where those weeks are most expensive.

The practical adjustment is straightforward. Sessions move to post-Iftar slots, which for many students are genuinely more productive than a late afternoon in a normal term because the day's obligations are done. Session length often drops while frequency rises, because concentration in a shorter block is better than endurance in a long one. Internal assessment deadlines that sit just after Ramadan need their real work pulled forward rather than squeezed.

The long summer break is the other structural feature, and it is used badly more often than well. Three months of nothing costs a Diploma student real fluency in mathematics and in a language acquisition subject. Three months of daily tutoring is unnecessary and usually abandoned by August. A light, specific schedule, one or two sessions a week on the two subjects that decay fastest, holds the ground without burning the holiday.

For students between DP1 and DP2 the summer has a specific job: the internal assessment. This is the one period with time to think about a research question properly, collect data without a timetable in the way, and get a draft to a stage where the autumn deadline is a formality instead of a crisis. An Al Qusais family that uses six weeks of the summer this way buys back the whole autumn term.
