faqs.question: Does it matter that an IB tutor is not physically near Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: For the teaching, no. For the match, it matters a great deal in your favour. Requiring proximity restricts the choice to tutors who can reach your building, and in a district where the Diploma cohort is small that removes most genuine specialists. Lessons through IB Gram are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the question becomes who is free at 17:30 rather than who lives near Damascus Street. Home visits are something IB Gram runs only in India, which is stated here rather than discovered later.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IB tutor on the first phone call?
faqs.answer: Three questions. What is the internal assessment in this subject marked against, criterion by criterion? What is each paper worth at this level? And given this mock script, which topic and which command term lost the marks? Someone who teaches the subject regularly answers all three without hesitating. Someone who does not will redirect to motivation, rapport and years of experience. Years of experience across ten year groups and four curricula is not the same credential as having taught this course this year.

faqs.question: How much of the Diploma grade is already fixed before the final exams?
faqs.answer: A substantial share. Every subject carries an internally marked assessment, moderated by the IB, typically worth somewhere between a fifth and a quarter of the subject grade. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together contribute up to three points of the 45. Those marks are settled across DP1 and DP2 on the school's internal calendar. That is why support starting in the spring of DP2 can improve the examined papers but cannot touch half of what has already been banked.

faqs.question: My child lives in Al Nahda and goes to a Dubai school. Which regulator covers them?
faqs.answer: The school's regulator, not the home's. A school in Dubai answers to KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes inspection ratings. A school across the boundary in Sharjah answers to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there and also approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. In a household with children on both sides, that means two sets of inspection reports and sometimes two term calendars to plan around.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for tutoring on the Extended Essay and TOK?
faqs.answer: Often it is the best value on the whole diploma, because the two together carry up to three points and almost nobody tutors them. The marks are lost early: a research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words, or a TOK essay that discusses a topic instead of arguing the prescribed title. A tutor teaches the criteria, interrogates the question and marks drafts against the published descriptors. The student writes every word, and the school supervisor's role and deadlines stand unchanged.

faqs.question: My child did MYP and is struggling in the first term of DP1. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Common enough to be predictable. Five years of criterion-referenced assessment on a 1 to 8 scale does not prepare a student for timed papers marked on a 1 to 7 scale against assessment objectives. The gap usually shows in three places: producing a structured written answer in twelve minutes, algebraic fluency without a method sheet, and reading Diploma command terms precisely. Six to eight sessions on whichever of those is actually missing generally closes it, which is far cheaper than a year of general subject support.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start for a student travelling back from Academic City?
faqs.answer: Later than most families first assume. A bus route from Academic City into Al Qusais takes thirty-five to fifty minutes in term time, so a 15:30 finish means arriving home around 16:20 at best, and 17:30 to 18:00 is the earliest honest start once eating and changing are counted. A student on that route carries one weekday session well and two badly. Weekend slots are usually the more reliable half of a two-session week, and online delivery means a displaced slot moves rather than disappears.

faqs.question: How do I tell a specialist from a general tutor who also lists the IB?
faqs.answer: By what they can describe without preparation. A specialist names the internal assessment criteria for the subject, says what each paper is worth at Higher and Standard Level, and can tell you which option topics their students usually find hardest. A generalist talks in terms of curricula rather than syllabuses, lists a wide year range, and answers questions about assessment with answers about motivation. Both can be perfectly competent teachers; only one of them is going to move a Higher Level Paper 3 mark.

faqs.question: Should tutoring continue through the summer between DP1 and DP2?
faqs.answer: A light schedule, yes, and for one specific reason: the internal assessment. The summer is the only period with enough space to choose a research question properly, collect data without a timetable interfering, and get a draft to a state where the autumn deadline is routine rather than a crisis. One or two sessions a week on the subjects that decay fastest, usually mathematics and a language acquisition subject, holds fluency. Daily tutoring across six subjects gets abandoned by August and wastes the money.

faqs.question: How do lessons change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the whole day reshapes, so sessions move rather than pause. Post-Iftar slots work well for many students because the day's obligations are finished, and shorter, more frequent sessions beat long ones. The planning point is to pull forward real work on any internal assessment deadline that falls just after Ramadan, because the weeks immediately before it are not going to deliver what a September plan assumed. Because teaching is online, moving a slot costs a message rather than a journey.

faqs.question: Is it sensible to use the same tutor for two of my child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because there is real overlap between mathematics and the physical sciences, and between the essay-based humanities. Where it stops working is at the top of Higher Level, because each subject's Paper 3 or equivalent rewards quite specific habits. For a student stabilising a grade 4 in two related subjects, one tutor is efficient. For a student chasing a 6 or 7 in both, two specialists usually produce more than one generalist splitting the hour.

faqs.question: What does a tuition centre near Al Qusais offer that online one-to-one does not?
faqs.answer: A room, a fixed timetable and other students, which suits some children genuinely well. What it does not offer is a subject-level match: a centre staffs for the curricula in local demand, which in this district means British and Indian curriculum work rather than Diploma Higher Level options. Group sessions also move at the group's pace. A centre operating with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a reasonable thing to ask to see.

faqs.question: When should we stop tutoring?
faqs.answer: When the component that was broken is fixed, which is usually earlier than a provider will volunteer. The honest marker is the error log: when the same mistakes stop recurring in timed questions and the student can explain their own method without prompting, the weekly session has done its job. Many families reduce from two subjects to one after the mocks, and that is normally the right call. An open-ended arrangement that nobody reviews is how tutoring budgets quietly double.

faqs.question: Do you teach the MYP as well as the Diploma for students in this area?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the work looks different. MYP subjects are assessed against criteria A to D with achievement levels converted to a 1 to 8 grade, so the useful teaching is often about what a criterion strand actually asks for rather than about content. Schools in this corridor vary in how long they run MYP, with some continuing to Year 11 and eAssessment and others switching to IGCSE after Year 9. Those two routes need different Year 9 preparation, so we ask which one your school takes.

intro.heading: A calendar problem dressed up as a search for somebody nearby
paragraphs: Al Rashidiya is well placed for IB provision by the standards of the eastern suburbs. Dubai Festival City is next door and holds two of the nearest Diploma schools, one running the full continuum. Mirdif is a short drive east and adds continuum provision, and Nad Al Sheba sits within the realistic school-run radius. So unlike many Dubai neighbourhoods, a family here does not have to travel far for the programme itself.

What they do have to manage is time, and the Diploma is unusually unforgiving about it. It is a linear two-year course with no mechanism for catching up: a gap left in the first term is still costing marks in the final paper. Internal assessments in six subjects, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and CAS all have deadlines, most of them set by the school rather than published centrally, and several of them land in the same weeks as mock examinations.

Against that, the school week shrinks as the course proceeds. In the first year the evenings are broadly available. From January of the second year, school revision programmes take the early evening, co-curricular commitments continue, and the practical result in this area is one usable weekday hour at half past seven plus a Saturday morning. Any plan that assumes more than that will fail, and the failure will be blamed on the tutor rather than on the arithmetic.

This is why distance is the wrong filter. A tutor five minutes away who is only free at five o'clock is useless to a second-year Diploma student in Al Rashidiya. A specialist in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level who is free at half past seven on a Tuesday is exactly what the household needs, and where that person physically sits makes no difference to the lesson provided it is live, one-to-one and on Gulf Standard Time.

For completeness, since the search was for somebody nearby: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India, and the published Dubai market rate for in-home visits is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included if that is the route you want to compare. Everything described here happens over live video, matched on course and level and on the hour your calendar actually allows, with a free trial lesson before anything is charged.

Nothing on this page promises a grade. The papers are marked externally, the internal assessments are marked by the school and moderated, and the performance belongs to the student. What a correctly timed plan changes is how many marks are lost to collisions in the calendar rather than to anything a student could not do, and on the Diploma that number is larger than most families realise until the second year arrives.

sections.heading: What "near me" actually reaches from Al Rashidiya
paragraphs: Taking the search literally for a moment, here is what is genuinely within reach. The table sets out the communities around Al Rashidiya with the realistic drive, what IB provision each contains, and, separately, how deep the local pool of Diploma subject specialists is. Those last two columns are different things and conflating them is the mistake the search encourages: a district can contain an excellent IB school and almost no private tutors who know the programme.

The picture is that provision is close and specialism is not. Festival City is minutes away and holds Diploma schools. Mirdif and Nad Al Sheba add continuum provision within a reasonable drive. But the private tutoring supply across the eastern suburbs is dominated by Indian and British curriculum teaching, because that is what the overwhelming majority of nearby students are doing, with International Baccalaureate accounting for about 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment overall.

Which means the honest answer to "is there an IB tutor near me" depends entirely on the subject. For Mathematics, Chemistry and Biology, somebody competent is reachable and will travel, at the published in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. For Higher Level Physics the pool thins. For Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts, Film, Theatre or a first-language literature option other than English, the realistic answer is that no such person is nearby, and that is a supply fact rather than a search failure.

The lever that works is widening the geography, which is what a live video lesson does. It also, in this area specifically, improves the thing the household actually needs most: availability at half past seven on a weekday. A UAE-based teacher with a day job frequently cannot take that hour. A specialist in another time zone often can, which is why the format solves the calendar problem and the supply problem at the same time.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: This is the document a Diploma family should have on the wall in the first term and almost nobody does. The written examinations are the last thing that happens; everything that determines the result happens earlier, and most of it is dated by the school rather than published centrally. Internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay drafts and supervisor meetings, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, CAS completion, mock windows and the school's own upload deadlines are all school-set, and they vary between Dubai schools.

So the first action is not booking a tutor, it is asking the IB coordinator for the school's two-year component calendar. That single request, which costs nothing, usually reveals two or three weeks in which four things fall due simultaneously, and knowing about them in October rather than discovering them in February is the difference between planning and triage.

The table below is the sequence in order, with who sets each milestone and what should be true by then. Note that we do not publish IB examination or results dates on these pages. The International Baccalaureate's own site cannot be fetched automatically, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family acts on must come from the IB or the school's coordinator rather than from a tutoring page. UAE schools sit the May session; confirm the specifics with your coordinator.

Where board dates can be verified, we give them with their source. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, allocating every centre to one of six administrative zones and stating that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: The core components, and the weeks where everything lands at once
paragraphs: Six subjects would be manageable. What makes the Diploma a scheduling problem is the core: Theory of Knowledge with an exhibition and an essay, the Extended Essay with a supervisor process and multiple drafts, and CAS, which demands participation and reflection across both years. None of these is examined in a hall at the end. All of them have internal deadlines, and schools in this part of Dubai set them differently.

The collision that catches most families is in the second year, when an internal assessment deadline, an Extended Essay draft and the mock examination window fall inside the same three or four weeks. A student with no plan for that period will do the mocks badly, submit a weak draft, or both, and neither outcome is about ability. Families who have the component calendar in the first year can see the collision coming and front-load the Extended Essay work into the preceding summer, which is the single most useful scheduling move available on the Diploma.

CAS deserves a specific mention because it is the one students deprioritise and schools chase. It is not graded, but it is a requirement, and an incomplete CAS record is a problem at the end rather than a minor administrative matter. Its demand on the week is real and it is usually scheduled at exactly the times a tutoring slot would otherwise sit, which is why it belongs on the same calendar rather than being treated as separate.

On the Extended Essay specifically: it is marked out of 34 across five criteria, and criterion C, Critical thinking, carries 12 of those marks on its own. Together with the Theory of Knowledge grade it feeds a matrix worth up to three Diploma points, on top of the 42 available from six subjects. Those are frequently the cheapest points a family can influence, and they are only influenceable while the drafts are open, which makes them a calendar item rather than a revision item.

sections.heading: How the first and second year fit into a week differently
paragraphs: The two years of the Diploma consume a household's evenings in different shapes, and a tutoring plan that ignores that will be built for the wrong year. In the first year the load is steady, the deadlines are mostly internal and distant, and the evenings are broadly available. In the second year the load is spiky, the deadlines are immediate, and the school takes the early evening for revision programmes from January onwards.

The table sets this out so the planning follows the reality. The practical conclusion for an Al Rashidiya family is to establish the slot in the first year, when it can be placed where you want it, and to accept in the second year that it moves to half past seven or to Saturday morning. A slot that exists before January survives January. A slot created in January is competing with the school's own programme for the same hour and usually loses.

The second conclusion concerns intensity. First-year support should be steady and unhurried: one subject, weekly, with the internal assessment question raised early. Second-year support should be short, bounded and precisely aimed, because the available room is small. Families who try to run first-year-style weekly coverage across three subjects in the second year do not simply overspend; they produce a student who is sleeping less and achieving no more.

There is a third pattern worth naming, specific to this area. Second-year students in the eastern suburbs often lose the slot entirely during the mock period and then try to restart afterwards, by which time the tutor's availability has gone. The better approach is to keep the hour and change what happens in it: during mock weeks the session becomes review of marked mock work, which is more useful than new content anyway and costs the same.

sections.heading: The weeks that disappear, and how to spend the ones that remain
paragraphs: Count a Diploma year honestly and a surprising number of weeks are unavailable. The winter break, when families travel. Eid holidays, which move. Ramadan, when school days shorten and the evening is reorganised around Iftar. The mock period, when the student is sitting papers rather than preparing for them. Study leave, which is not free time. And the final examination weeks themselves. What remains is roughly three productive stretches a year, and the first of them is the autumn term that almost nobody uses.

Ramadan in particular needs agreeing in advance rather than improvising. A six o'clock slot that worked in November no longer fits, and families who settle the arrangement before the month starts keep continuity through it while those who do not generally lose the month and restart behind. Post-Iftar sessions work well for some households, late mornings on non-school days for others, and a deliberate pause for others again. The only approach that reliably fails is cancelling week by week.

The summer between the two Diploma years is the most under-used asset available to a family in this area. There is no competing homework, no school run, no revision programme and no mocks. It is the natural window for the Extended Essay's Critical thinking work, for settling an internal assessment question that is still vague, and for rebuilding a foundational gap from the first year before the second begins. A short summer block is frequently worth more than a term of in-year sessions.

Study leave deserves the opposite advice. Taper rather than intensify. Students on study leave are sitting papers, recovering between them, and following the school's own revision schedule, and additional sessions booked into that period are typically cancelled or unproductive. Whatever intensive work is needed belongs in the eight to ten weeks before leave starts, finishing as it begins.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: This is the part of a Dubai Diploma student's week that families consistently leave out of their planning, and it is not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 applying to schools whose year begins in April.

The structural rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. For these mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which is a genuine constraint on how any support in these subjects can be described.

The planning consequence for an Al Rashidiya household is simply that the week is fuller than six Diploma subjects and the core suggest, and the hour you add has to come from somewhere real. That constraint is the whole argument for one subject at a time, aimed at a specific failure, rather than general coverage. A student carrying six subjects, three core components and three mandatory UAE subjects does not have room for two hours of unfocused tutoring, and adding it costs more in sleep than it returns in marks.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the seven emirates
paragraphs: Worth knowing if your family may move within the UAE, which in this area is common, because the regulator changes and so does what it governs. The five bodies below are the complete map for UAE private schools, and the research behind these pages found that ADEK is named by none of the competitors examined and SPEA by only one. A family relocating from Dubai to Abu Dhabi or Sharjah is moving between genuinely different regulatory regimes.

In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

One substantive difference is worth highlighting. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval, not just inspection, sits with the emirate regulator there. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

None of these bodies accredits, licenses or endorses IB Gram, and we hold no permit, partnership or approval from any of them, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what they do and point you to them. No tutoring provider should describe itself as approved by KHDA unless it actually holds the Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes with premises, and you are entitled to ask to see that permit.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Rashidiya, and how a match actually happens
paragraphs: Send four things. The exact course title and level as the school writes it, because Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level are different tutors. The school's two-year component calendar from the IB coordinator, which is the document this whole page has been arguing for. The most recent marked script. And the hour you intend to keep.

We then look for a specialist in that exact course at that level who is free in your hour. Those two constraints together are what make a match take time: Mathematics, Chemistry and Biology typically reach a trial within a few days; Higher Level Physics, Economics and English A take four to eight; Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts and first-language literature options can take a fortnight, and the specialist is frequently outside the UAE teaching at a Gulf Standard Time slot. We will tell you the wait rather than filling the hour with an adjacent-subject teacher.

The free trial runs in your nominated hour with the tutor who would teach your child. Use it for three checks. Can the tutor describe the assessment components and weightings for that exact course from memory. Will they state unprompted what they will not do with an internal assessment. And was your child still thinking at the end of the hour, which is a question about the slot rather than about the tutor.

Then agree one capability to be true by session six, checkable on marked work, and a plan for the collisions the component calendar has already revealed. If the honest conclusion is that the household should buy a short Extended Essay block in the summer and nothing else, we will say that. If it is that the IB coordinator should be asked whether a Higher Level subject can be stabilised rather than pushed while points are recovered elsewhere, we will say that too, and both conversations cost us the booking.

faqs.question: Is there an IB specialist within reach of Al Rashidiya?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject rather than on the distance. Diploma provision is unusually close for this side of the city, with schools in Dubai Festival City minutes away and continuum provision in Mirdif and Nad Al Sheba. Private tutoring supply is a different matter: the eastern suburbs are dominated by Indian and British curriculum teaching, because International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment. Mathematics, Chemistry and Biology are reachable. Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts and most first-language literature options are not, locally, at any price.

faqs.question: What should I ask the IB coordinator before booking a tutor?
faqs.answer: For the school's two-year component calendar: internal assessment deadlines by subject, Extended Essay draft and supervisor meeting dates, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay deadlines, CAS expectations and the mock examination windows. It is free and most families never request it. It typically reveals two or three weeks in which four things fall due at once, and knowing that in the autumn of the first year rather than discovering it in the spring of the second is the difference between a plan and triage.

faqs.question: When does the Diploma week stop having room for a tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: January of the second year, in this area reliably. School revision programmes take the early evening, co-curricular commitments continue, and what remains is one weekday hour at half past seven plus a Saturday morning. The practical implication is to establish the slot in the first year while it can be placed where you want it. A slot that exists before January survives January; a slot created in January is competing with the school's own free programme for the same hour and usually loses.

faqs.question: Should we pause sessions during the mock examination period?
faqs.answer: No, repurpose them instead. Families in this area typically drop the hour during mocks and then find the tutor's availability has gone when they want to restart. Keeping the slot and using it to go through marked mock work is more useful than new content anyway: the scripts show whether the loss is content, technique or pacing, which determines what the remaining weeks should contain. It costs the same as a normal session and protects the continuity that was most of what the hour was buying.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components are worth planning a session around?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay above all, because it is marked out of 34 with criterion C, Critical thinking, carrying 12 marks on its own, and because with the Theory of Knowledge grade it feeds a matrix worth up to three Diploma points on top of the 42 available from six subjects. Those are frequently the cheapest points a family can influence, and only while the drafts are open. Internal assessment questions are the second, because a question tested for viability early protects marks that cannot be recovered later.

faqs.question: When are the IB exams and when do results come out?
faqs.answer: We do not publish IB session or results dates on these pages, and you should be cautious of any tutoring site that does. The International Baccalaureate's own site cannot be fetched automatically, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around has to come from the IB or from your school's coordinator. UAE schools sit the May session. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the dates are published and verifiable, and the live official timetable is the document to use rather than any restatement of it.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a Diploma tutoring schedule?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and Iftar reorganises the evening, so a six o'clock slot that worked in November no longer fits. Agree the arrangement before the month begins rather than improvising in the first week. Post-Iftar sessions work well for some households, late mornings on non-school days for others, and a deliberate pause for others again. All three are workable. What loses the month is cancelling week by week, because by the time the household wants the hour back it has been given to somebody else.

faqs.question: Is the summer between the two Diploma years worth using?
faqs.answer: It is the most under-used window available to a family here. No competing homework, no school run, no revision programme and no mocks. It is the natural time for the Extended Essay's Critical thinking work, for settling an internal assessment question that is still vague, and for rebuilding a foundational gap from the first year before the second begins. A short summer block is frequently worth more than a term of in-year sessions, and it also front-loads work away from the second-year collisions.

faqs.question: How many subjects can a second-year Diploma student be tutored in?
faqs.answer: One, and even that takes planning. A Dubai Diploma student is carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, plus Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, which KHDA requires in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and times on a 40-minute lesson unit. There is one reliable weekday hour in the second year. Families who buy three do not simply overspend; they produce a student sleeping less and achieving no more, which is a worse outcome than buying nothing.

faqs.question: Does it matter that mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education are on the timetable?
faqs.answer: It matters for capacity planning. These subjects are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibiting combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. The effect is that the week is fuller than six Diploma subjects suggest, which is the whole argument for one tutored subject aimed precisely.

faqs.question: We may move to Abu Dhabi or Sharjah. Does the regulator change?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference is substantive. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator there rather than only inspection.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match an IB tutor for a specific subject?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, Chemistry and Biology typically reach a trial lesson within a few days. Higher Level Physics, Economics and English A take four to eight days. Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts, Film, Theatre and first-language literature options other than English can take a fortnight, and the specialist is frequently outside the UAE teaching at a Gulf Standard Time slot. Two constraints are being satisfied at once: the exact course and level, and your nominated hour. We publish the wait rather than filling the slot with an adjacent-subject teacher.

faqs.question: Why would a tutor in another time zone suit us better?
faqs.answer: Because of the hour rather than the teaching. The slot a second-year Diploma household in this area needs is half past seven on a weekday, and a UAE-based teacher with a day job frequently cannot take it. A specialist teaching from a different time zone often can, which means the format solves the supply problem and the calendar problem simultaneously. The lesson itself is live, one-to-one and on Gulf Standard Time, with work set in a shared document and marked before the following session.

faqs.question: What should happen during study leave?
faqs.answer: Taper rather than intensify. Students on study leave are sitting papers, recovering between them and following the school's own revision schedule, and additional sessions booked into that window are typically cancelled or unproductive. Whatever intensive work is needed belongs in the eight to ten weeks before leave begins, finishing as it starts. If anything runs during leave it should be short, timed practice on a paper not yet sat, and nothing new. A provider selling extra hours into study leave is selling reassurance.

Send us that calendar, the exact course title and level, the most recent marked script and the hour you intend to keep, and we will match a specialist who is free in it. The trial lesson runs in your slot and nothing is charged before it.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-safa.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and MYP subjects to students in Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah. Each is listed by subject and level rather than by location, because an IB Diploma tutor in Al Safa is useful only if they teach the specific course and level on your child's timetable.

intro.heading: What the phrase 'near me' hides on an IB search
paragraphs: A parent in Al Safa 1 types a location into Google because location is the only variable they can see. It is also the variable that matters least to an IB grade. The Diploma is assessed against published descriptors by examiners who never meet the student: a marker in Cardiff reading a Chemistry Paper 2 script has no idea whether the candidate lives on Al Wasl Road or in Hamburg. What the marker can see is whether the answer used the right command term, whether the working was shown at the step the mark scheme awards, and whether the Internal Assessment hit the criteria in the order they are written.

That reframes the search. The useful question is not which tutor sits closest to Safa Park, but which tutor has read the current subject guide for your child's course, knows how the weightings fall between papers at that level, and can name the three places in that syllabus where Al Safa students most often drop marks. Geography answers none of that. Subject knowledge answers all of it.

There is a practical reason the distance filter fails here too. A Diploma student in Al Safa is typically taking six courses, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge and an Extended Essay. A single tutor who can cover Maths Analysis and Approaches HL, Chemistry HL and History SL to examination standard is not a person who exists; a generalist who claims all three will teach the first competently and the other two from a textbook. Narrowing to a twenty-minute drive narrows the pool to whoever happens to live nearby and then forces a compromise on the thing that actually matters.

IB Gram works the other way round. We ignore the radius and match on the course code and level, then deliver the lesson over live video so the geography never enters the decision. Online IB tutoring in Al Safa means a student sitting at the family dining table with the tutor's screen shared, working through a past paper question in real time, with the annotated script saved afterwards. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. That is a deliberate limit, not an apology, and the rest of this page explains what the limit buys.

What follows is the subject detail a parent needs before paying anybody. The Diploma's assessment architecture, group by group. The command terms that carry different mark tariffs. The Internal Assessment criteria and the word limits attached to them. Where marks are lost, by subject area. How to use a past paper so it teaches something rather than just producing a score. And the one boundary a tutor must not cross on assessed coursework, because crossing it ends a Diploma rather than improving it.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-safa.programmesIntro: Al Safa families arrive at the Diploma by three routes: through an IB Middle Years Programme at a school like Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, through IGCSE at a British school and then across to DP1, or from a different system entirely after a move to Dubai. The programme notes below cover what each route leaves to fix.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, drawn one from each of five groups plus a sixth free choice. Each subject is graded 1-7 from external papers plus one internally assessed task. The core adds Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The total sits at 45 points: 42 from subjects and up to three from the TOK and EE grade matrix. A diploma requires 24 points and clears a list of failing conditions on top.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma is a minority route by headcount. Of the 387,441 pupils in Dubai private schools in 2024-25, International Baccalaureate programmes accounted for seven per cent, against thirty-seven per cent on a UK curriculum. For an Al Safa family that means fewer DP cohorts nearby, smaller subject sets at each school, and a real chance that the Higher Level combination your child wants is taught in a group of four. Thin groups are where one-to-one teaching earns its money.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0-8 and converted to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. There are no public examinations until the optional eProject and on-screen assessments in MYP 5. The programme teaches inquiry and criterion-referenced writing well and leaves a measurable gap in procedural fluency, which is the thing DP1 exposes in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in Al Safa typically transfer into DP1 at the same school, so the gap nobody flags is content coverage rather than skill. A student arriving in DP1 Maths from MYP 5 has met trigonometry and quadratics but not binomial expansion, compound angle identities or integration. We treat the first six weeks of DP1 as a repair window and work through those specific topics rather than reviewing MYP material the student already passed.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and a language development component. The DP courses inside it are examined on exactly the same papers as the full Diploma, which is the part parents miss.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by only a handful of Dubai schools and none in Al Safa itself, so most local enquiries about it come from families considering a move across the city. The tutoring request is almost always for the embedded Diploma courses, which we treat identically to full-Diploma teaching, and for the reflective project, where our role is process coaching against the published criteria and nothing more.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed by a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects with a 950-word commentary. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece in a subject the student chooses, supervised by a school teacher. Together they contribute up to three points through a published matrix, and a failing grade in either blocks the diploma regardless of subject points.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where Al Safa families most often ask for outside help and where the honesty boundary is tightest. A Theory of Knowledge tutor in Dubai can teach the prescribed title, unpack the knowledge questions and mark a draft against the assessment instrument. Extended Essay supervision in Dubai belongs to the school supervisor by IB rule; what a tutor adds is subject-specific reading guidance and feedback on the student's own argument.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-safa.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Al Safa households request most, with what each actually assesses and where the marks tend to go. Levels are listed because the paper structure, and therefore the teaching, changes between Standard and Higher Level in every one of them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level this is three papers plus a 20-mark exploration: Paper 1 without a calculator at thirty per cent, Paper 2 with one at thirty per cent, Paper 3 as two extended problem-solving questions at twenty per cent. Paper 3 is where HL grades are decided, because it rewards structured investigation rather than recall of a method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and discrete mathematics with calculator use assumed throughout. Standard Level is two papers at forty per cent each plus the exploration. The common failure is treating it as the easier course: the data-handling questions demand precise interpretation of output, and marks go on unjustified conclusions rather than arithmetic.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Under the current subject guide the course is organised around Structure 1-3 and Reactivity 1-3, examined by Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent and Paper 2 at forty-four per cent, with the scientific investigation at twenty per cent. Organic mechanisms and energetics calculations are the two topics Al Safa students most often arrive with half-learned.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 is structured and extended response. Higher Level adds depth in fields, induction and quantum physics rather than extra topics. Marks are lost on unit prefixes, on failing to state which direction is positive, and on describing a graph instead of interpreting its gradient.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The current guide is built on four themes and two levels of organisation, with unifying concepts running across both. Assessment mirrors the other sciences. The characteristic Diploma error is answering a six-mark question with a list of memorised facts and no causal chain, which the mark scheme does not reward.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, two at Standard, plus a portfolio of three commentaries at 800 words each built on published news articles. Diagram accuracy carries real marks: an unlabelled axis or a shift drawn in the wrong direction costs more than a weak paragraph of analysis does.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided textual analysis of unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, plus an individual oral and, at Higher Level, a 1,200-1,500 word essay. Students lose marks by summarising content when the task asks for an analysis of authorial choice and its effect.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based Paper 1, essay Paper 2 on world history topics, and at Higher Level a regional-depth Paper 3. The Internal Assessment is a 2,200-word historical investigation. Paper 1 question four is the reliable mark-dropper: it needs sources integrated with own knowledge, not a narrative with quotations bolted on.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study examination plus an internally assessed business research project at Higher Level and a written commentary at Standard. Marks go on applying a named tool to the specific firm in the stimulus rather than describing the tool in general terms, which is what most first drafts do.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 on core and, at Higher Level, additional topics; Paper 2 on the case study published annually; plus a developed solution as the internal assessment. The solution is where supervision matters most, because the criteria reward documented design decisions as heavily as working code.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, with Higher Level extensions and an experimental study as the internal assessment. Command terms do the damage here: a question asking students to contrast two studies earns nothing for describing them in sequence without a point of comparison.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run alongside the Diploma in every Dubai private school under KHDA requirements, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These are graded on the school's own reporting rather than the IB scale, and families often need support in them on top of Diploma subjects.

The notes below are about Diploma teaching specifically: which programmes the surrounding communities feed into, and what the local school mix means for subject availability.

regions.note: Villa streets running off Al Wasl Road, within walking distance of several British secondaries. Most Diploma enquiries from here are DP1 students who crossed from IGCSE in the same school group and need maths and science bridging.

regions.note: The quieter half, bordering Al Quoz 1 across Sheikh Zayed Road. Families here commonly split children across a British primary and an IB secondary, which produces the awkward MYP-to-DP transition requests we see most.

regions.note: Directly inland from Al Safa along Al Wasl Road. Shares the same school catchment entirely, so a tutoring pattern that works for an Al Wasl Diploma student works unchanged for an Al Safa one.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB tutor near me in Al Safa should actually be filtering on
paragraphs: An IB tutor is useful to the exact degree that they know one course at one level. That is the filter. The Diploma publishes a subject guide for every course, revised on a cycle, specifying the syllabus content, the assessment objectives, the paper structure, the durations and the internal assessment criteria. A tutor who has read the current guide for Chemistry HL can tell you in one sentence that Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent and what kind of question sits in it. A tutor who has not will talk about confidence and foundations.

So the three questions worth asking before anybody is paid are these. Which course and level does my child take, exactly as it appears on the school's report? Which subject guide edition is their cohort examined on, and has the tutor taught that edition? And what are the three topics in that syllabus where students most reliably lose marks? A specialist answers all three inside a minute. Anyone who needs to check is not the right match, and finding that out during a free trial lesson costs nothing.

The location filter does something actively harmful here. Restricting to tutors who can reach Al Safa in twenty minutes shrinks the available pool to a geographic accident, then forces the family to accept whichever subject that pool happens to cover. IB Gram does not run that trade. We match on course and level across the whole tutor base and deliver over live video, which is why an Al Safa student can be taught History HL Paper 3 by somebody who specialises in it rather than by the nearest available graduate.

There is a second-order benefit parents notice later. Because the lesson is shared-screen, the past paper the student worked on, the annotations the tutor made and the mark scheme they were held against all survive the session as a file. A whiteboard in a living room does not. Over a two-year Diploma that archive becomes the revision resource the student actually uses in the final term.

sections.heading: The Diploma's assessment architecture, group by group
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject is a split between externally examined papers and one internally assessed task, and the split is not the same across groups. Knowing your child's split tells you where tutoring hours should go. A student two terms from the examinations with an unfinished internal assessment is in a different situation from one whose coursework is banked and whose Paper 1 technique is weak, even if both are sitting on a predicted 4.

The internal component is the part parents systematically underweight. In the sciences it is a single scientific investigation worth twenty per cent of the final grade, marked out of 24 against four criteria of six marks each, with a 3,000-word ceiling. In mathematics it is an exploration worth twenty per cent, marked out of 20 across five criteria. In history it is a 2,200-word investigation; in economics, a portfolio of three commentaries at 800 words each. These are not minor pieces of homework. They are a fifth of the grade, produced under the student's own control, over months, with feedback permitted.

The external papers then divide differently by group. The sciences run two papers under the current guides, with Paper 1 split into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Mathematics runs two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher, with the extra Higher paper being extended problem-solving rather than more content. Language A runs a guided analysis paper, a comparative essay paper and an individual oral. Each of those formats needs a different kind of practice, which is why generic revision help produces so little movement.

The practical consequence for an Al Safa family is a planning one. Work out which components are still open, what each is worth, and how long each takes to fix. An internal assessment at criterion level can usually be moved inside a few focused sessions because the criteria are explicit and the student controls the text. Paper technique takes a term, because it is a habit. Content gaps take as long as the content takes. Those three are not interchangeable and should not be bought as a single block of hours.

sections.heading: Command terms: the three-word difference between two marks and five
paragraphs: The IB publishes command terms in every subject guide, grouped by assessment objective, and markers apply them literally. A question that says state wants a single statement with no justification and awards one mark. A question that says explain wants the mechanism or the reason and will not award full marks for a correct statement alone. A question that says evaluate wants weighted judgement with both sides present. Students who read all three as write what you know about this lose marks they have the knowledge to win.

This is the cheapest improvement available in the Diploma and it is almost never taught deliberately. The pattern we see in Al Safa students arriving from a strong MYP background is a habit of discursive writing that scored well under MYP criteria and scores poorly against DP command terms. The student is not weaker. They are answering a different question from the one printed. A term of drilling IB command terms against real past paper questions typically shifts the structured-response marks before any new content is learned.

The drilling has to be done on real questions with the real mark scheme in view, which is why we do it in session rather than setting it as homework. The student attempts the question, the tutor shares the mark scheme, and the student sees that the two marks they missed were available for naming a direction or stating a unit. That moment is worth more than an explanation of the same point, because the student has their own script in front of them.

The terms below are the ones that cost Al Safa students the most, taken from the question types where our tutors see repeated losses. The mark tariffs are indicative rather than fixed: the IB sets marks per question, and the same term can carry different weight in different papers. What is consistent is the kind of answer each term demands.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing, by subject area
paragraphs: Mark loss in the Diploma is patterned rather than random, and the patterns differ by group. In mathematics the loss is procedural: unsimplified exact forms where the question demanded them, calculator use on the non-calculator paper topics, and method marks forfeited by writing only a final answer. A student who reliably reaches the right number but shows no intermediate step loses marks on every multi-step question in Paper 1, which is thirty per cent of a Higher Level grade.

In the sciences the loss is linguistic and dimensional. Unit prefixes dropped or mis-converted. Graph questions answered by describing the shape rather than extracting and interpreting a gradient or an area. Six-mark extended responses written as a list of true statements with no argument connecting them. The data-based section of Paper 1 punishes imprecision specifically: a tolerance band on a reading, an uncertainty not propagated, a conclusion stated more strongly than the data supports.

In the humanities and languages the loss is structural. History Paper 1 question four requires source material integrated with the student's own knowledge; a narrative with quotations appended reads fluently and scores in the middle band. Language A Paper 1 asks for analysis of authorial choice and its effect; summary of content, however accurate, does not meet the task. Economics punishes diagram errors harshly because the diagram carries explicit marks that prose cannot recover.

What this means operationally is that a diagnosis should come before a teaching plan. Our first full session on a new student is normally a past paper attempted to time and marked in front of them, precisely so the plan addresses their losses rather than the subject's average losses. A student who already shows working does not need working drilled; a student who writes beautifully and never judges needs the evaluate questions, not more content.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment, criterion by criterion, and what a tutor may legitimately do
paragraphs: IB Internal Assessment support in Dubai is sold by a lot of people, and some of what is sold is an academic malpractice risk dressed up as help. The line is drawn clearly in the IB's own academic integrity rules. The work must be the student's own. A supervisor or tutor may discuss the topic, teach the underlying content, comment on a draft and explain what the criteria require. They may not write any part of the text, correct it to completion, or supply a finished piece for the student to submit. A student who submits work that is not their own faces an academic misconduct finding, and the consequence is the loss of the diploma rather than a lower grade.

Inside that line there is a great deal a specialist can do, and most of it is about the criteria rather than the content. The criteria are published, explicit and marked harshly against specific absences. On the sciences investigation, research design carries six marks and fails most commonly because the research question is not focused enough to be answerable with the apparatus described. Data analysis fails on uncertainties not propagated through the calculation. Conclusion fails when it is not compared against accepted values or published literature. Evaluation fails when weaknesses are listed without being linked to their effect on the result.

On the mathematics exploration, the same principle applies with different letters. Presentation rewards a coherent structure a reader can follow without re-reading. Mathematical communication rewards correct notation and defined variables, and is where competent students routinely drop marks for using a symbol they never defined. Personal engagement is not a paragraph about why the student likes the topic; it rewards evidence of independent thinking inside the mathematics. Reflection rewards critical commentary at the points where the work turned, not a summary at the end. Use of mathematics carries the most marks and rewards work at a level commensurate with the course.

Our role on these tasks is therefore specific and bounded. We check the topic is feasible before weeks are spent on it. We teach whatever content the chosen topic requires. We read the student's own draft and return criterion-level feedback saying what each criterion currently earns and what is missing. The student then makes every change themselves, and we mark the next draft the same way. No tutor at IB Gram will write the IA, draft the Extended Essay or produce the exploration on a student's behalf, and we will tell a family plainly when a request has crossed into territory we decline.

sections.heading: Using past papers so they teach something
paragraphs: Most Diploma students in Al Safa already have access to past papers through their school, and most are using them in the way that produces the least learning: attempt a paper, check the answers, note the score, move on. The score is the least informative output of the exercise. What matters is which marks were available and not taken, and why, and whether the same reason recurs across papers.

The method we use instead has three steps and takes longer per paper, which is the point. First the paper is attempted to time, with the real duration enforced, because time pressure is itself a skill and a paper done leisurely tests different things. Second the paper is marked with the student watching the mark scheme being applied question by question, so they see where a mark was given for a step they omitted rather than for the answer they got right. Third the losses are classified: content not known, method not shown, command term misread, time ran out. That classification drives the next session.

Over a term the classification becomes the most useful document the student has. A list showing that eleven of their last thirty lost marks were method marks on multi-step questions is actionable in a way that a sequence of percentages is not. It also tells a parent whether tutoring is working, which is otherwise difficult to see: grades move slowly and noisily, but the recurring loss categories shrink visibly.

One caution on materials. We reference and link official syllabus documents, specimen papers and mark schemes on ibo.org and the board sites, and we work from the student's own school-issued copies. We do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes or subject guides, because those are copyright documents and circulating them is a liability for everybody involved. Your child's subject teacher or IB coordinator is the correct source for them.

sections.heading: The core, and the honesty boundary that comes with it
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three points between them through a published matrix, and a failing grade in either prevents the award of the diploma whatever the subject points say. That makes the core disproportionately important relative to the attention it gets in a family's tutoring budget. A student sitting on 36 points who loses the core entirely does not get 36 points. They get no diploma.

Theory of Knowledge is teachable and is most often taught badly. The essay responds to one of six prescribed titles set by the IB for each session and is capped at 1,600 words. Students who treat it as a philosophy essay write abstractly and score poorly; the assessment instrument rewards engagement with knowledge questions grounded in specific areas of knowledge, with real examples carrying the argument. The exhibition requires three objects and a 950-word commentary linking each to a selected prompt, and marks are lost most often on objects chosen for their symbolism rather than their usefulness as evidence.

The Extended Essay is supervised by a teacher at the school by IB requirement, and that is not a formality a tutor can take over. The supervisor signs off on the authenticity of the work and conducts the reflection sessions that feed the assessment. What a subject specialist adds, legitimately, is reading guidance in the subject, help narrowing a research question to something answerable in 4,000 words, and feedback on the student's own draft against the published criteria. Extended Essay supervision in Dubai is not something IB Gram provides in place of the school; we work alongside it.

The boundary is worth stating plainly because the UAE market for this is not clean. There are operations selling completed Internal Assessments and Extended Essays to IB students in this city, at prices that suggest the demand is real. Buying one is academic misconduct, it is detectable, and the penalty falls on the student. We teach, we review, we give criterion-level feedback, and we decline the rest. A family that wants the other thing should know we are not the provider for it.

sections.heading: Al Safa's school mix, the regulator, and what an inspection report tells you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Its annual inspections rate schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the reports are published. For a parent choosing between schools in Al Safa and Jumeirah, the report is the only comparable evidence available, and it is more useful read for its subject-level detail than for its headline band.

The market context is worth having. In 2024-25 Dubai had 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with UK provision at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian at twenty-six, American at fourteen and International Baccalaureate at seven. Seven new private schools are opening for 2026-27, four of them UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, and enrolment grew by six per cent in 2025-26. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

Alongside whatever curriculum a school is licensed to teach, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every Dubai private school. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools are advised to keep any mandatory-subject lesson to at least 25 minutes. These subjects sit on a Diploma student's timetable in addition to their six IB courses, which is a workload fact families moving to Dubai consistently underestimate.

What an Al Safa parent should take from a KHDA report is narrower than the band. Look at the attainment and progress judgements in the specific subjects your child takes, at the sixth-form or post-16 section if the school runs the Diploma, and at the identified areas for improvement, which are written specifically enough to be actionable. A school rated Very Good overall can have a weak judgement in one science, and that is the judgement that affects your child.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this market, and what a permit check costs you
paragraphs: Three of the six ranking pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. So here is the market in the currency Al Safa parents actually transact in, attributed to who publishes it. A budget online tutor, usually a university student, is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market figures with sources attached, not IB Gram's price list. What they show is a structural point: the in-home band sits above the equivalent online band by roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour, and that gap is travel. It buys a tutor in the room. It does not buy a better-matched specialist, and on a Higher Level subject in a thin local pool it frequently buys a worse-matched one. For an Al Safa family the decision is therefore not online versus in-home on price alone; it is whether the premium is better spent on travel or on getting the person who actually teaches Paper 3.

The other thing that costs nothing and is worth doing is checking the tutor is permitted to work. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a two working day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

One further point specific to UAE families. ADEK's professional ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on it. The direction of travel is clear enough: an offer to arrange your child's own classroom teacher privately is an offer to put that teacher in breach.

sections.heading: When Al Safa does not have the specialist, and what we do about it
paragraphs: Availability is the thing nobody in this market discloses, so here it is. For common Diploma courses at Standard Level, a matched tutor is usually available in the same week. For Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, the pool is narrower and a match can take longer, particularly in the weeks before the May session when the specialists who teach those courses are already full. For the smaller group 3 and group 6 subjects, and for languages beyond the common set, there may be no UAE-based tutor at all in a given term.

What happens then is the part that should be written down before a family pays anything. We say so. If no specialist in that course and level is free, we tell you that rather than offering a generalist and calling it a match, and we will either hold the request until one is or decline it. An IB HL tutor in Dubai who does not teach your child's course is not a partial solution; they are a term of wasted sessions and a student who concludes that tutoring does not work.

Where we can solve it, we often solve it by ignoring geography entirely. Because teaching is over live video and timed to Gulf Standard Time, the tutor pool for an Al Safa student is not the set of people who can drive to Al Wasl Road. A Higher Level History specialist teaching at 5pm Gulf Standard Time can be anywhere that makes 5pm workable, and that widening is the single largest practical advantage of the online format. It is also why IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at all: the radius that in-home delivery imposes is the constraint we are trying to remove.

For an Al Safa family planning ahead, the implication is to request early for anything Higher Level and anything unusual. A family that asks in September for Physics HL support in the spring gets a choice of specialists. A family that asks in March gets whoever is left. That is not a pressure tactic; it is just how a thin specialist pool behaves in a city where the Diploma cohort is seven per cent of the school population.
