faqs.question: Does an IB tutor near me in Al Safa actually need to be near me?
faqs.answer: No, and insisting on it narrows the choice to a geographic accident. The Diploma is examined against published descriptors by markers who never meet your child, so what matters is whether the tutor knows that course at that level. IB Gram teaches Al Safa students one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which means the tutor pool is the whole base rather than whoever can reach Al Wasl Road by five. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IB tutor before the first paid session?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which paper carries the most marks in this course, and what percentage is it? How is the internal assessment marked, and what are the criteria called? What is the word or page limit on that task? And which three topics in this syllabus cost students the most marks? A genuine specialist answers all four without checking. Anyone who talks about confidence and foundations instead has not read the current subject guide. The free trial lesson is the right place to ask.

faqs.question: How much of my child's IB grade comes from coursework rather than exams?
faqs.answer: Typically twenty per cent per subject, which parents consistently underweight. In the sciences it is a single scientific investigation marked out of 24 across four criteria, capped at 3,000 words. In mathematics it is an exploration marked out of 20 across five criteria. History uses a 2,200-word investigation; economics, three commentaries of 800 words each. Because the student controls the text and feedback is permitted, these marks are the most coachable in the Diploma, and they are usually the fastest place to gain ground.

faqs.question: Can an Al Safa tutor help with the Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may discuss the topic, teach the content it needs, explain what each criterion requires and comment on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of the text, edit it to completion or supply a finished piece. No tutor at IB Gram will write the IA, draft the Extended Essay or produce the exploration for a student. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic misconduct and costs the diploma, not a grade.

faqs.question: Why do IB command terms matter so much to the mark?
faqs.answer: Because markers apply them literally and they carry different mark tariffs. State wants one fact with no reasoning. Explain wants a causal chain and will not award full marks for a correct statement. Evaluate wants weighted judgement with a conclusion. Students who read all three as write what you know lose marks they have the knowledge to win. Drilling command terms against real past paper questions usually shifts structured-response marks before any new content is taught, which makes it the cheapest available gain.

faqs.question: My child came through MYP and is struggling in DP1. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Usually content coverage rather than skill. MYP teaches criterion-referenced writing and inquiry well, and leaves specific procedural gaps that DP1 exposes in the first term. In mathematics a student arriving from MYP 5 has met quadratics and trigonometry but not binomial expansion, compound angle identities or integration. We treat the first six weeks of DP1 as a repair window and work through those named topics rather than revisiting MYP material the student already passed.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used so they actually teach something?
faqs.answer: Attempt the paper to its real duration, then mark it with the student watching the scheme being applied question by question, then classify every lost mark as content, method, command term or time. The score is the least useful output. The classification is the useful one: a student who learns that eleven of their last thirty lost marks were method marks on multi-step questions has something to fix. We do this in session rather than setting it as homework for exactly that reason.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL have the narrowest pools and book out earliest, particularly in the weeks before the May session. Smaller group 3 and group 6 subjects, and languages outside the common set, may have no UAE-based specialist in a given term. We disclose that before you pay: if nobody suitable is free we hold the request or decline it rather than substituting a generalist and letting you discover the mismatch in March.

faqs.question: What permit should an Al Safa family ask a private tutor to show?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website or e-services, with a two working day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Is it a problem to hire my child's own schoolteacher privately?
faqs.answer: It can put the teacher in breach. ADEK's professional ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the live policy, so verify it with the school or the regulator. Either way, it is not an arrangement worth the risk to a teacher's position.

faqs.question: What do Arabic and Islamic Education mean for a Diploma student's workload?
faqs.answer: They are additional. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed to teach, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student that means those subjects sit on the timetable alongside six IB courses, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, which families relocating to Dubai routinely underestimate.

faqs.question: Can you supervise the Extended Essay instead of the school?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody legitimately can. The IB requires a supervisor at the school, who signs off on authenticity and runs the reflection sessions that feed the assessment. What a subject specialist adds alongside that is reading guidance, help narrowing a research question to something answerable in 4,000 words, and criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft. We work alongside the school supervisor rather than replacing them, and we say so when a family asks us to take the role over.

faqs.question: How quickly can an Al Safa family start, and what does the trial involve?
faqs.answer: For a common Standard Level course, usually within the same week. The first lesson is free, one per student, with no card details taken, and it runs with the specialist we are actually proposing rather than a sales call. Treat it as an interview and ask the subject questions. If the match is wrong, tell us and we propose someone else. If it is right, the next session is normally a diagnostic past paper marked in front of your child.

faqs.question: What should we be able to measure after six weeks of sessions?
faqs.answer: By watching the loss categories rather than the grades. Grades move slowly and noisily over a Diploma, so a percentage after six weeks tells you very little. What moves visibly is the count of marks lost for a given reason: method marks not shown, command terms misread, uncertainties not propagated. We report those each half term in writing, with what the next six weeks target. If nothing has moved we say so and change the plan or the tutor.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers, mark schemes or subject guides?
faqs.answer: We reference and link the official sources and we work from your child's school-issued copies, but we do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes or subject guides. Those are copyright documents and circulating them exposes everyone involved, including the student. Your child's subject teacher or IB coordinator is the correct source. For dates and current specifications, ibo.org and the board sites are authoritative and we point you there rather than restating figures that get revised.

faqs.question: Which exam session should we plan around, and can you confirm the dates?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools sit the May session, with November available as a retake route. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than no date when a family acts on it. Confirm the exact window with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For planning purposes, work backwards from internal coursework deadlines, which usually bite months before the papers do.

intro.heading: What the search "IB tutor near me" is really asking in Al Satwa
paragraphs: The phrase is a proxy. Nobody actually wants a tutor because of their postcode. What an Al Satwa parent wants is somebody who has taught the exact course their child is sitting - Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, say, or Biology at Standard Level with an Internal Assessment due in eleven weeks - and who can be in front of the child this week. Proximity became the search term because for a generation it was the only way to get both. In Dubai in 2026, for a syllabus this specific, it is the thing that gets in the way.

Al Satwa sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and the Jumeirah coast, bordered by Al Hudaiba, Al Bada'a and the older blocks around 2nd December Street. It is one of the least car-dependent neighbourhoods in Dubai: Al Jafiliya and World Trade Centre metro stations are close, the streets are narrow, and most homes are apartments rather than villas. It is also a neighbourhood with very few international private schools inside its own boundary. Children living here are driven or bussed out - to Jumeirah, Al Safa, Umm Suqeim, Oud Metha or Al Barsha - because that is where the IB World Schools and the British-curriculum schools are.

That one fact decides what a proximity search can and cannot return. Private tutors cluster where schools cluster, because teachers live near the campus they work at and take private students from the families they already know. A neighbourhood that exports its pupils imports almost nothing in the way of specialist tuition. Search "IB tutor near me" from an Al Satwa address and you will get three kinds of result: a tuition centre in Karama or Oud Metha teaching mixed-curriculum groups, a general home-tutor listing that claims every subject from Year 2 to Year 13, and a marketplace profile whose nearest actual IB Diploma teacher is in Al Barsha.

None of those is dishonest. They are simply answering a different question. A tuition centre running an after-school group can be genuinely useful for IGCSE Maths revision; it is a poor fit for a student who needs Chemistry HL Topic 20 organic mechanisms unpicked before a mock. A generalist who covers Years 2 to 13 is not lying either, but a tutor who teaches everything is, by arithmetic, specialist in nothing. The Diploma is a two-year course with internally assessed components, command terms that carry mark-scheme weight, and a grade awarded on a 1-7 scale that behaves nothing like a British A*-E. It rewards a teacher who has marked it.

So this page answers the question you typed rather than deflecting it. It says what the local supply honestly looks like, what the Dubai market charges in AED for each tier of tutor, what travelling to your door actually costs you when you pay for it inside an hourly rate, and how a live-video one-to-one lesson removes the trade-off instead of pretending the trade-off does not exist. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - and that is the whole reason an Al Satwa family can be matched with a Chemistry HL teacher instead of the closest available generalist.
Read the cost table before the rest. It is the part no competitor in this search result publishes, and it is the part that changes decisions.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-satwa.programmesIntro: An IB enquiry from Al Satwa can mean any of four very different things, because the IB is a continuum rather than a single course. Which programme your child is in decides what help is useful, how it is assessed, and how far ahead you need to plan.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised around transdisciplinary themes and units of inquiry, and reporting is against learner-profile attributes and conceptual understanding rather than paper marks. Support at this stage is about literacy fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud - the thing that later becomes a written justification in an MYP criterion or a Diploma command term. Parents often arrive wanting worksheets and leave with a reading-aloud routine instead.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Satwa family, PYP support is usually a response to a mid-year arrival from a different system - a CBSE or American primary, or a British school where the child was reading well but had never been asked to inquire. Dubai schools absorb new arrivals constantly, and the gap that shows is rarely content. It is the expectation that a nine-year-old can say why an answer is right.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, labelled A to D, every criterion carrying a 0-8 band descriptor. Sciences use Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. Those criterion letters are where marks are lost, because a student who knows the content can still score 4 on Criterion C for presenting data without uncertainties. MYP Year 5 students may also sit eAssessment for the MYP certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Al Satwa children in the MYP are usually at a continuum school a 15-25 minute drive away, which means homework starts late and criterion feedback often arrives from the school in a format parents find hard to read. The practical job in Years 9 to 11 is translating a Criterion B comment into something the child can act on next time, and building the lab-report habits the Diploma IA will assume.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, with externally marked papers taking the rest. The arithmetic matters: a strong Internal Assessment banks marks months before the papers, and a weak one cannot be recovered in the exam hall. Most UAE candidates sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: This is what the majority of Al Satwa IB enquiries are about, and almost always for a named subject at a named level rather than general help. The common pattern is a Year 12 student who was comfortable through IGCSE, met Higher Level in October, and discovered that recall no longer earns anything. That is a specific, fixable problem and it needs a teacher who has marked the subject.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and a language-development component. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is frequently confused with the Diploma by parents comparing options. Where a student takes DP courses inside a CP framework, those courses are assessed exactly as a Diploma student's are, with the same papers and the same internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: CP enquiries from central Dubai are rare but they are real, and they matter for university planning because a CP certificate is not the Diploma. If your child is on a CP pathway and intends to apply to a UAE federal university, the Ministry of Education equivalency route is the thing to check first, directly with the authority, before any tutoring decision is made.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-satwa.subjectsIntro: An Al Satwa enquiry almost never says "IB help". It says a subject and a level. These are the Diploma courses that come up most from central Dubai, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. At HL, Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving pair of questions that cannot be prepared by topic-spotting. Marks go on unjustified steps, missing domains, and proof by induction attempted without the inductive step written out. The IA exploration needs a genuine mathematical question, not a survey.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics course, with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout. Students lose marks by reporting a regression coefficient without interpreting it in context, and by choosing a statistical test the data does not support. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding modelling than most students expect from the "easier" maths.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Conceptually unforgiving in two places: circular motion and fields at SL, and quantum and nuclear physics at HL. The common failure is algebraic rather than conceptual - a correct method abandoned halfway because the student cannot rearrange. Uncertainties and error propagation in the IA are where otherwise strong candidates lose a whole criterion.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics separate grades. HL adds entropy, equilibrium calculations and the harder spectroscopy work. Marks are lost on state symbols, significant figures, and explanations that describe an observation instead of giving a reason. Paper 2 extended-response questions reward command-term discipline more than extra content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem, not difficulty. The syllabus rewards precise terminology and penalises near-miss vocabulary, so a student who says "the cell takes it in" where the mark scheme wants active transport against a concentration gradient earns nothing. Data-based questions on Paper 2 need practice reading graphs nobody has pre-digested.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are the grade. A correctly labelled, correctly shifted diagram with the new equilibrium marked earns marks that no amount of prose recovers. The internally assessed portfolio of commentaries is where students lose time, usually by choosing an article that does not actually illustrate the syllabus concept they wanted to write about.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed through Paper 1 guided textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral and, at HL, the HL Essay. Students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing, and by choosing global issues for the Individual Oral that are too broad to evidence from two extracts in ten minutes.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course that many strong speakers underestimate. Marks come from register, text type conventions and audience awareness, not from vocabulary breadth. The writing task is marked against a specified text type, so an email written as an essay loses a criterion before the content is read.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based: Ansoff, SWOT, break-even, ratio analysis, investment appraisal. The weakness is applying a tool without reference to the case-study organisation, which caps the response. HL adds the business research project, where the real difficulty is scoping a question narrowly enough to answer with available evidence.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Dubai families often run Arabic as a Diploma course and as a KHDA-mandated school subject at the same time, with different expectations in each. The Diploma course is assessed on text type and register; the mandatory school strand follows the Ministry's own content. Treating them as one subject is how students end up behind in both.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by the TOK exhibition and the prescribed-title essay. Students lose marks by writing about the world instead of about knowledge, and by choosing real-world examples that do not test the knowledge claim. Support here is argument structure and question discipline; the essay has to be the student's own work and is reviewed, never drafted for them.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay in a subject, with a supervisor at school and a reflection process that is itself assessed. The usual failure is a research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words. A tutor's legitimate role is coaching the question, the method and the reading - never producing the text.

sections.heading: The honest answer: who actually teaches the IB near Al Satwa
paragraphs: A proximity search cannot find what is not there. Al Satwa has few international private schools inside its own boundary, so it has very few resident teachers who hold a current Diploma teaching load. The teachers who do are concentrated around the campuses: the Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim coastal strip, the Al Barsha cluster inland, and the older Oud Metha and Garhoud schools across Sheikh Zayed Road. That is not a judgement about Al Satwa. It is how private tutoring markets form everywhere - supply follows the staff room.

What that means in practice is that the nearest person who will answer a "tutor near me" enquiry from Al Satwa is usually not the nearest person who has taught your child's course. For a broad subject at a broad level - primary maths, Year 9 English, IGCSE Biology revision - the distinction may not cost you anything. For Diploma Higher Level Chemistry, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL, Physics HL or any Group 2 language at a specific level, it costs you the whole point of hiring a tutor. These courses are taught by a small number of people in any city, and the probability that one of them lives within two kilometres of a given Al Satwa apartment is low.

The second thing a proximity search cannot tell you is whether the person is permitted to teach privately at all. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A listing that is near you tells you nothing about that. A question you ask before the first lesson does.

So the honest answer to "is there an IB tutor near me in Al Satwa" is: there are tutors near you, there are fewer Diploma specialists near you than the search results imply, and the way to get the specialist is to stop filtering by distance. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE - that is an India-only service - which is precisely why an Al Satwa enquiry can be matched against a Chemistry HL teacher rather than the closest available generalist.

sections.heading: What a nearby generalist can and cannot cover
paragraphs: It is worth being specific about where the local pool stops being sufficient, because the blanket claim that only specialists matter is marketing, not truth. A capable, permitted, experienced tutor who has never taught the Diploma can be entirely adequate for a Year 8 student who needs number fluency, or a Year 10 who has fallen behind in IGCSE Maths topics that are stable across every board. The content is widely taught, the assessment is familiar, and good general teaching transfers.

The transfer fails at the point where the assessment design, rather than the content, is what is being tested. The Diploma does this deliberately. Paper 3 at HL Mathematics is a sustained investigation that a strong tutor unfamiliar with the format will mistake for a long question. Internal Assessment criteria are published letter by letter with specific descriptors, and a tutor who has not marked against them will coach towards general quality instead of towards the band. Command terms - evaluate, justify, distinguish, suggest - carry mark-scheme consequences that an experienced marker knows and a newcomer guesses.

The table below is the honest map of that boundary, written for a parent deciding how much specialism to pay for. It is not an argument that every subject needs a specialist. It is an argument that you should know which column you are in before you pay for twenty hours.

One further point. Where a subject sits in the right-hand column, the practical question is not "local or online" but "specialist or nothing". An Al Satwa family that insists on a tutor within a short drive for Chemistry HL is not choosing between two tutors. It is usually choosing between a generalist nearby and a specialist further away who, over live video, is not further away at all.

sections.heading: What Dubai families actually pay, starting from the cheapest option
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market, because that is where most searches begin. The cheapest tuition an Al Satwa parent will be quoted is a university student or recent graduate working online: EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33-52. At that price the tutor is usually a capable young person who did well in the subject recently. That can genuinely work for primary support and for MYP content catch-up. It does not buy somebody who has marked a Diploma Internal Assessment, and nothing at that price will.

The next band up is where most serious Diploma tuition sits. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted around AED 150-300 an hour across the Dubai market - Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that, named IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists are quoted roughly AED 200-450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table showing 200-450+. At the top, examiner-led or premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650.

The in-home column is the one worth reading twice. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The arithmetic is unavoidable: the in-home option delivers half the sessions for roughly double the monthly outlay, because somebody is being paid to drive across Dubai twice.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page, and that is deliberate rather than evasive. What a block costs depends on subject, level and how many weeks remain before the assessment that triggered the enquiry, and a figure typed into a landing page is a figure that goes stale. The free trial lesson and the consultation that follows it are where a real number is given. What the table below gives you is the market you are negotiating inside, which is more useful than a number with no context - and more than any competing page in this search result will tell you.

sections.heading: What distance costs you when it is inside the hourly rate
paragraphs: The in-home premium is not a surcharge a tutor adds out of greed. It is the only way to price an hour that takes two and a half hours to deliver. A tutor coming to an Al Satwa apartment from the Al Barsha school cluster is driving Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Wasl Road in the late afternoon, parking in a neighbourhood with narrow streets and limited visitor space, and then doing the same journey in reverse. The hour of teaching is unchanged. The cost of producing it has roughly doubled, and the rate reflects that.

There is a second, quieter cost. A tutor who travels can only serve the families inside their driving radius, which is why in-home tuition is always general tuition in practice. The economics force it: nobody can specialise in Chemistry HL and fill a week from the households within twenty minutes of their own flat. Travel time converts specialists into generalists. That is the real reason an in-home-only search in central Dubai returns the profiles it does.

And a third, which parents discover after booking. Travel introduces failure modes that have nothing to do with teaching. Traffic turns a 4.30pm session into a 4.50pm start, and the lost twenty minutes are not refunded. One tutor stuck on Al Wasl Road cancels the whole week because there is no substitute inside the radius. Rain, roadworks or a school event moves everything. Over a two-year Diploma those are not edge cases - they are a predictable tax on contact hours.

Set against that, the honest case for in-home tuition is real and worth stating: a younger child who will not sit still at a screen, a household where supervision matters more than specialism, or a family who simply learns better with a person in the room. Those are legitimate reasons, and if that is your situation the Dubai market has plenty of providers. IB Gram is not one of them. sections.heading: The questions that actually identify a specialist
paragraphs: If you take one thing from this page, make it this section. The way to replace a distance filter is with four or five questions that a specialist answers instantly and a generalist cannot answer at all. They take two minutes, they work on any platform including ours, and they are far more predictive than a profile photograph and a star rating.

Start with the course code, not the subject. Ask which exact course your child is in - Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard - and whether the tutor has taught that one. A specialist will ask you back, because the two maths routes are different courses with different papers and different university consequences. A generalist will say "maths, yes". That single exchange sorts most enquiries.

Then ask about the internally assessed component: what the criteria are called in that subject, what each one is worth, and what a mid-band response looks like. This is the question essay mills and generalists both fail, for opposite reasons. Ask what the tutor will and will not do with an Internal Assessment draft; the correct answer is that they will teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work, and that they will not write or complete any part of it. An offer to produce the work is an IB academic-honesty breach and the risk falls on your child, not on the provider.

Finish with the practical two. Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit, or how the provider verifies it - the permit is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no reason for anyone to be without one. And ask what happens if this tutor is not the right fit after two sessions. A provider with a real bench answers that without hesitating. A single tutor with a driving radius cannot.
bullets: Which exact course and level - AA or AI, HL or SL - and have you taught that one?
Name the internal assessment criteria in this subject and what each is worth

Can I see your MoHRE private tuition work permit, or how do you verify it?

sections.heading: KHDA, the regulator, and what it does not cover
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. That report is a genuinely useful document for an Al Satwa parent, and it is free. It tells you how the school teaches your child's subject, not just how the school performs overall.

What KHDA does not do is inspect private tutors. There is no KHDA rating for an individual tutor, and the phrase "KHDA-approved tutor" describes nothing that exists. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to a training institute with premises in Dubai, involving initial approval, a maximum six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold one, does not operate premises in the UAE, and does not claim regulator approval of any kind. Any provider that claims it should be asked for the permit number.

Dubai is also not the whole picture, and it is worth knowing the map because families move between emirates. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which u.ae says supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge - both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education.

One piece of regulator news belongs in any cost conversation. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family budgeting tuition on top of school fees, a fee freeze is the difference between a tutoring decision and a tutoring argument.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you found legally permitted to teach?
paragraphs: This is the part of a proximity search that should worry a parent more than the distance does. A listing that appears near your address has passed no check at all. The UAE position is clear and easy to verify: individuals providing private lessons need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anybody.

The permit is deliberately accessible. MoHRE grants it free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, a tutor without one has chosen not to have one.

There is a second rule that catches a specific and very common Dubai arrangement. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is unambiguous: your child's own classroom teacher, paid privately, is the one arrangement to avoid even when it is offered kindly.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IB assessment
paragraphs: The IB assesses work that must be the student's own, and the consequences of getting this wrong land on the student. A finding of malpractice can cost a Diploma, not a grade. That makes the boundary a practical safety issue for an Al Satwa parent buying coursework support, and it is worth knowing exactly where the line sits before money changes hands.

Legitimate support is substantial and it is teaching. A tutor can explain what a criterion descriptor means in plain words. They can interrogate a research question until the student can answer it in one sentence. They can teach the statistical test the data needs, or the uncertainty treatment a physics investigation requires. They can mark a practice paper, identify why a response that reads well scores in the middle band, and set another one. They can read a draft the student wrote and respond with questions and comments on it.

Illegitimate support is anything that produces text or results the student did not generate. Writing a section. Rewriting a paragraph "to show how it should sound". Supplying a dataset. Drafting a research question the student then adopts without understanding. Editing a draft to completion. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying that is not a shortcut; it is handing a malpractice case to an IB coordinator, and the student carries it.

A useful test for a parent with no IB background: could your child explain, unprompted, every decision in the document? If the method, the question and the conclusions are all things they can defend to a supervisor who asks why, the support was teaching. If any part of it would need to be looked up, it was not. Ask the tutor to state their own boundary in the first conversation, and be wary of a vague answer. A specialist states it crisply because they have had the conversation before.
bullets: Teaching a criterion, a method or a command term: legitimate and valuable

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Most UAE candidates sit the IB in the May session, and the thing nobody tells a Year 12 parent is that the grade is substantially decided before the papers. Internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay process and the TOK essay all land across the two years, and each of them banks or loses marks on a date that has nothing to do with the exam window. A family that starts support in the spring of the exam year has already passed several of the moments where help is cheapest.

Counting backwards is the planning tool. From the exam window, the final weeks are past-paper work under timed conditions. Before that is the mock round, which is the last honest diagnostic the school will give you. Before that, the Extended Essay and TOK essay are finished and away, and subject Internal Assessments are at final-draft stage. Before that, in the first Diploma year, is when an IA topic is chosen - and a bad choice made early costs more than any amount of late help can recover.

A note on dates, because this page will not give you ones it cannot verify. IB exam and results dates in this project have not been confirmed against ibo.org, which blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date appears here. Confirm every IB date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates are sourced and can be given: Cambridge runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and each centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, with Cambridge warning that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam. The February/March series is offered in India only and does not apply to UAE candidates.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: This is the part of a Dubai timetable that catches international families off guard, and no competitor page in this search result mentions it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. A Diploma student in Dubai is therefore carrying mandatory subjects on top of six IB courses plus the core.

The rules are more specific than most parents realise. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

There are two further constraints worth knowing. Schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects - a concrete, checkable credential point. And for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That last rule shapes honestly what any tutor can do with these subjects: reinforce the school's own material and the skills behind it, not substitute a parallel syllabus.

The practical consequence for an Al Satwa family planning Diploma support is timetable arithmetic. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Those lessons are already in the week. When you add a weekly tutoring hour, you are adding to a timetable that is fuller than the IB subject list suggests - which is an argument for one well-chosen hour rather than three scattered ones.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free, and what we say instead of guessing
paragraphs: Availability transparency is the gap nobody in this market fills, so here it is plainly. Some Diploma subjects at Higher Level are taught by a small number of people, and there are weeks - particularly the run-up to the May session - when the right specialist for a narrow subject does not have a slot at the hour an Al Satwa family needs. Pretending otherwise is how a parent ends up with a tutor who nodded at a subject they have not taught.

What happens instead is a disclosure and a choice. If the exact match is not available at your preferred time, we say so and offer the alternatives honestly: a different time with the right specialist, a short wait with a date attached, or a closely adjacent specialist who can cover the component you need now. For a student who needs Chemistry HL energetics in three weeks, an adjacent specialist who has taught the topic is a better answer than a perfect match in six.

The second disclosure concerns where the tutor sits. Delivery is online, which means the specialist may not be in the UAE. Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around your school run, and a tutor's location is stated rather than hidden behind a local-sounding number. Two competitors in this market route UAE parents to Indian phone numbers without saying so; we would rather tell you up front, because an Al Satwa family choosing a Diploma specialist over a nearby generalist deserves to know what they are choosing.

The last point is the simplest. The trial lesson exists so that none of this has to be taken on trust. One free lesson, with the student's own marked work in front of the tutor, tells you more about fit than any profile. If it does not work, nothing further is owed and no block has been bought.

process.title: Tell us the course, not the subject
process.description: The first message that saves a week is the specific one: the exact course and level, the school, the component that triggered the enquiry and the deadline attached to it. "Chemistry HL, mock in four weeks, energetics and Topic 20" is actionable. "IB help for my son" needs two emails before anything can start.

process.title: Send the marked work
process.description: The most useful thing an Al Satwa parent can attach is the last marked paper or the teacher's criterion feedback, however blunt. A specialist reads a marked script diagnostically: where the method stopped, which command terms went unanswered, whether the loss is content or format. Nothing substitutes for it.

process.title: See who is proposed and why
process.description: You get a named tutor with their subject and level experience, and the reasoning behind the match. If availability means the exact specialist is not free at your preferred hour, you are told that rather than quietly given somebody adjacent. The choice stays with you.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, at no cost, with the student's own work on screen. It is a diagnostic as much as an introduction: by the end you should know what the actual problem is and whether this tutor and this student can work together. Nothing is owed afterwards if the answer is no.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot around the school run
process.description: Al Satwa children travel out to school, so arrival home is later than the timetable suggests. The slot is set against your real return time, not an idealised one, and it holds each week so progress accumulates. Rescheduling does not depend on anybody's drive across Dubai.

process.title: Review against the school's own deadlines
process.description: Progress is checked against the dates the school set - mock results, IA draft deadlines, predicted grades - rather than against a tutoring report nobody else uses. If the plan needs changing after a mock round, it changes then, and you hear why in language you can take to the coordinator.

whyPoints.title: The distance filter comes off
whyPoints.description: Matching by syllabus and level instead of by postcode is the whole mechanism. An Al Satwa family gets the person who has taught and marked the exact course, rather than the person who will drive to Al Satwa at 5pm. For Diploma Higher Level subjects those are rarely the same person.

whyPoints.title: Nobody is paid to drive
whyPoints.description: In-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180-500 an hour because travel sits inside them. Remove the travel and the same money buys more contact time, or the same contact time costs less. Published monthly packages make the comparison plainly: roughly eight online sessions against four in-home visits.

whyPoints.title: The boundary on coursework is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nothing is written, redrafted or completed for a student, on any IB component, at any price. In a market where completed Internal Assessments are openly sold, the boundary is the protection your child needs.

faqs.question: Is there an IB Diploma tutor living near Al Satwa, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: There are tutors near you. There are far fewer Diploma specialists near you than the search results suggest, because Al Satwa has almost no IB World School inside its own boundary and specialist tutors cluster around campuses. Whether it matters depends on the subject. For primary support or IGCSE revision, a nearby capable tutor is fine. For Higher Level Maths, Physics or Chemistry, or for any Internal Assessment, the format is the difficulty and you need somebody who has marked it. Lessons with IB Gram are one-to-one over live video, which is how distance stops being the constraint on who teaches your child.

faqs.question: Why does a search for an IB tutor near me in Al Satwa return tuition centres and generalists?
faqs.answer: Because that is what is physically nearby. A proximity search ranks by location, and the businesses with a location near Al Satwa are tuition centres in Karama and Oud Metha teaching mixed-curriculum groups, plus general home-tutor listings covering everything from Year 2 to Year 13. Diploma subject teachers live near the schools they teach at, which in central Dubai means the Jumeirah coastal strip and the Al Barsha cluster. None of those results is dishonest; they are answering a question about distance when your real question is about syllabus. Filtering by course and level instead changes the answer completely.

faqs.question: How does IB Gram teach an Al Satwa family if nobody comes to the apartment?
faqs.answer: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The tutor and student share a screen, so the student's own marked papers, the mark scheme they already hold and an Internal Assessment draft are all visible to both. Work is annotated live and the student keeps it. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - and that is deliberate rather than a limitation: it is what allows an Al Satwa family to be matched with a Chemistry HL specialist rather than the nearest available generalist.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to cover from a local tutor pool?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Mathematics in either route, Physics HL, Chemistry HL and any Group 2 language at a specific level. These are taught by a small number of people in any city, and the difficulty is the assessment design rather than the content: Paper 3 at HL Maths is a sustained investigation, HL Physics carries topics that do not appear at Standard Level, and Chemistry HL adds entropy and harder spectroscopy work. Internal Assessment coaching is similarly specialist in every subject, because the criteria are published letter by letter with band descriptors a tutor either knows or guesses at.

faqs.question: What does an hour of Diploma tuition cost around central Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours. A university-student tutor online is advertised from roughly AED 33-65 an hour by EdFlik and Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor online runs about AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB specialists are quoted AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, with premium or examiner-led rates reaching AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits are quoted AED 180-500 because travel is priced into the hour. IB Gram's own figure comes from the consultation after the free trial, not from a landing page.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both Higher and Standard Level for an Al Satwa student?
faqs.answer: Usually yes within a subject, and that is often the sensible arrangement when a household has two children on different levels of the same course. A teacher who covers Chemistry HL can teach Chemistry SL comfortably, because SL content sits inside HL. The reverse is not reliable: a tutor whose experience stops at Standard Level will not know the HL-only topics or the extended-response demands of the higher papers. Across different subjects it is different again - one person covering Maths HL and Physics HL to a high standard is possible but uncommon, and worth checking specifically rather than assuming.

faqs.question: How can an Al Satwa parent tell which IB maths course their child is actually in?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the course title in full, because the two routes are different courses rather than tiers of one. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is algebra and proof led, with an HL Paper 3 extended investigation. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout. They have different papers, different internal assessment expectations and different university consequences, so a degree that requires strong pure mathematics generally expects the Analysis route. A tutor who does not ask which one your child is in has told you something important about their experience.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legally do with my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: They may explain what each criterion means, interrogate the research question until the student can defend it, teach the method or statistical treatment the investigation needs, mark practice work and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. They may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph to show how it should sound, supply data or a finished research question, or edit a draft to completion. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying that hands an academic-honesty case to the IB coordinator and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a family in Al Satwa need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: A tutor delivering private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE states a two-working-day completion time, and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published so no amount should be quoted at you. Since it costs nothing, ask to see it.

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as a KHDA-approved private tutor?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA regulates and inspects Dubai's private schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that operate premises in the emirate, but it does not rate or approve individual private tutors. "KHDA-approved tutor" describes nothing that exists, and a provider using the phrase is either confused or hoping you are. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, operates no premises in the UAE and claims no regulator approval. What KHDA does publish, and what is genuinely worth reading, is your child's school inspection report with its band from Outstanding to Very Weak.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, rather than quietly given somebody adjacent. Narrow Higher Level subjects are taught by few people and the weeks before the May session are the tightest. The honest options are a different time slot with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date attached, or a closely adjacent specialist who has taught the specific component you need now. For a student with a mock in three weeks, the adjacent specialist who knows the topic is usually the better answer than a perfect match in six weeks' time.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around a Diploma timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They are mandatory. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, prohibits combined classes, and sets the language of instruction for each strand. Instructional time is counted in 40-minute units with 25 minutes advised as a minimum lesson. So a Dubai Diploma student carries more weekly lessons than the six-subject list suggests, which argues for one well-chosen tutoring hour rather than three scattered ones.

faqs.question: How far before the May session should an Al Satwa family start support?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, because the grade is substantially decided before the papers. Internal Assessment topic choices in the first Diploma year, the Extended Essay reflection process and the TOK essay all bank or lose marks on dates unrelated to the exam window. The cheapest intervention is at IA topic choice; the most expensive is after a mock round in the exam year. If you are already late, the mock results are the best diagnostic available and a short intensive block scoped to one component is the realistic play. Confirm all IB dates with your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: Can an Al Satwa family shift the weekly slot to after Iftar in Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many households that is the better slot. School days shorten during Ramadan, afternoon energy drops and traffic patterns change around Iftar, so a post-Iftar session often works better than the usual late-afternoon hour. Because lessons are delivered over live video, moving the time does not depend on anybody's drive across Dubai - the slot simply moves. The same applies to school holidays and to travel: a family spending part of the summer away can keep the weekly hour running on Gulf Standard Time or shift it to suit a different time zone.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Satwa children usually travel to for the IB?
faqs.answer: Out of the neighbourhood, in most cases. Al Satwa has very few international private schools inside its boundary, so families use the Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim coastal campuses, the inland Al Barsha cluster, or the older Oud Metha and Garhoud schools across Sheikh Zayed Road. That daily journey is the thing that shapes tutoring logistics: a 20 to 30 minute return in term-time afternoon traffic pushes homework and any session later than the school timetable implies. Schools named on this page are context for planning only; IB Gram is not affiliated with any of them.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai school inspection band tell me whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: Not directly, but it tells you more than the overall label does. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the report breaks performance down by subject and by phase. A school rated Outstanding overall can still have a weaker phase or department, and that is the part worth reading if your child is struggling in one subject. Use it as evidence about the teaching your child actually receives, then decide. A band is a school judgement, never a judgement about a student.

intro.heading: What an IB tutor costs in Al Sufouh, before anyone talks about outcomes
paragraphs: An Al Sufouh parent typing "IB tutor near me" into Google at nine in the evening is usually trying to answer two questions at once: can someone fix this, and what will it cost. The pages that come back answer neither. Three of the six strongest competitors in this search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. One of them asks the price question in its own FAQ list and then declines to answer it. So the first thing this page does is publish the numbers.

Across the Dubai market, hourly rates for academic tutoring run from roughly AED 45 at the budget online end to AED 650 for a single premium named tutor. The useful part of that spread for an IB family sits between AED 200 and AED 450 an hour, which is the band published for IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists. Below AED 150 you are generally buying supervision: a capable graduate who can keep a fourteen-year-old working through a problem set. Above AED 500 you are buying scarcity rather than a different quality of teaching. The whole table, with each figure attributed to the provider that published it, sits further down this page.

The second number nobody shows an Al Sufouh family is the cost of the slot itself. An in-home visit is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour in Dubai, and the gap between that and the online band is not teaching quality. It is the drive. A tutor coming into Al Sufouh at four in the afternoon loses twenty to forty-five minutes each way on Al Sufouh Road and Hessa Street, and that time is inside the rate whether it is itemised or not. It also shrinks the pool of people who will take the booking down to whoever lives close enough, which is how a family ends up with a generalist teaching Higher Level Chemistry.

That is the argument for the way IB Gram works. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates; in-home teaching is a service that exists only in India. Removing the drive is not a convenience point. It means an Al Sufouh student who needs Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is matched with someone who teaches that course and that paper, instead of the best available person within a twenty-minute radius of Al Sufouh 2.

The third number is the one families get wrong most often, and it is not a rate at all. It is how many hours they buy. A family spending AED 300 an hour on two subjects twice a week has committed to roughly AED 4,800 a month before anybody has diagnosed anything. The same budget spent on one subject, once a week, with an agreed six-week review and a clear list of the topics being fixed, usually moves the grade further. The sections below set out where the money goes, where it is wasted, and what a two-year Diploma plan actually costs in AED from start to finish.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-sufouh.programmesIntro: Al Sufouh sits beside the Knowledge Park corridor, and the schools in and around it run the IB in three different shapes: the continuum from primary, the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma, and the Diploma taken after IGCSE. Each shape has a different cost profile for a family, because each one puts the pressure in a different year.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examination, which changes what tutoring is for. There is no paper to prepare and no mark scheme to decode, so the honest use of a tutor at this stage is a specific skill gap: number fluency that has not become automatic, reading stamina, or written English that lags behind spoken English in a household where another language is used at home. Sessions are short and the useful measure is whether the gap closes, not whether a grade moves.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Sufouh and Al Barsha the PYP question is usually a transfer question. A child arriving mid-year from a British or Indian primary meets an inquiry structure with no textbook spine, and parents read the absence of worksheets as an absence of progress. A few weeks of targeted number and writing work, run alongside the school rather than against it, costs far less than the blanket twice-weekly package families often buy in panic.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and reported as a 1-7 grade generated from those criteria rather than from a percentage. Parents who understand percentages find this opaque, and students who are strong on knowledge can still score poorly on the criteria that reward process: investigating, communicating, reflecting. Most MYP tutoring value lies in reading the criteria descriptors with the student and matching their work to the wording, which is unglamorous and cheap.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP years are where Al Sufouh families tend to overspend. A Year 9 report with two 4s triggers a two-subject, twice-weekly booking that can run past AED 3,000 a month for two years. The same report usually describes a criterion problem, not a knowledge problem, and six to eight sessions resolve it. Spend the money later, in the Diploma years, when the assessment is external and the hours genuinely convert.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries an internally assessed component and externally examined papers, and the HL papers add both content and a separate extended-response demand. This is where tutoring has the clearest return, because the assessment is external, published and specific: a Higher Level Paper 3 is a different skill from a Paper 1, and it can be taught directly.
programmes.countryNote: Al Sufouh Diploma students sit the May session, the one UAE schools use. The spend that matters here is concentrated: the first term of DP1, when the step up from IGCSE lands, and the twelve weeks before the May papers. Families who hold a steady weekly hour across both of those windows typically pay less in total than families who buy nothing until February and then book three sessions a week in a scramble.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by far fewer schools than the Diploma, and the tutoring need is narrower: the DP courses inside it are examined exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so a CP student taking Business Management SL needs the same paper preparation as a Diploma student taking it.
programmes.countryNote: Few schools in the Al Sufouh catchment run the CP, so a family here usually encounters it only as an alternative raised in a Year 11 meeting. If that happens, the cost-relevant question is which DP courses sit inside the CP offer, because those are the components that carry external papers and therefore the components where paid tutoring converts into marks.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: An IB tutor in Al Sufouh is not a generalist, and the rate you pay should track the specificity of the subject and level. The courses below are the ones Al Sufouh and Al Barsha families ask for most, with what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof. HL adds a Paper 3 of two extended problems, which is where the HL grade is usually decided. Marks are lost less on the final answer than on unjustified steps: a correct result with no reasoning collects very little on a method-marked question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. The calculator is assumed rather than optional, and the common failure is treating a modelling question as an algebra question. HL statistics and the regression work carry more marks than students expect from the lesson time spent on them.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Conceptual questions punish learned procedure. Students lose marks on units, significant figures and uncertainty treatment in the data-analysis questions, and on explanation questions where a correct equation is written but the physics is never stated in words.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the usual pressure points, and the data booklet is a skill of its own. A student who has not practised locating values under exam pressure loses time on questions that should be mechanical, which costs marks at the end of the paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content plus precision of command terms. "Outline" and "explain" carry different mark tariffs, and students who write a paragraph for a two-mark outline lose time they need for the extended-response question later in the paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the internal assessment portfolio. Labelled axes, correctly shifted curves and an explicit link to the question wording carry marks that content knowledge alone does not. HL adds quantitative questions that reward arithmetic discipline.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application rather than recall. The pre-released case for the HL paper rewards weeks of structured preparation, and students who revise theory without mapping it onto the named business consistently underperform their knowledge.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis, the individual oral and the HL essay. The oral is a ten-minute performance against two extracts and a global issue, and it is the component most improved by rehearsal with someone who knows the criteria wording.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Productive writing in a defined text type, plus listening and reading papers. Marks are lost on register and text-type conventions rather than on vocabulary, which is why generic English support rarely moves this grade.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data structures and the internal assessment solution. The IA is a working product with documentation, and students routinely build something impressive while under-documenting the design criteria that carry the marks.

sections.heading: What that search actually returns in Al Sufouh, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in Al Sufouh is a proximity search for a service where proximity has stopped mattering. The phrase is a habit from a time when a tutor was someone who drove over, and the search engine still reads it that way: it returns agency landing pages, map listings for training institutes in Knowledge Park and Media City, and classified adverts from individuals whose qualifications are a single line of self-description.

What those results do not contain is the information that decides whether the money works. None of the strongest pages in this search publishes an AED rate card. None names a subject and level together. None explains that a Higher Level Physics tutor and a Middle Years science tutor are different people with different rates, or that a tutor who has never read a Paper 3 mark scheme cannot teach Paper 3 regardless of how good their degree is.

The useful version of the question is not who is nearby. It is who teaches this exact course, at this exact level, and can show how they know it. For an Al Sufouh family that reframing is almost pure gain. The catchment holds a small number of households and a smaller number of specialist tutors who happen to live inside it, so a proximity filter removes most of the people who could actually teach the subject.

That is what IB Gram does differently, and it is a structural difference rather than a claim about quality. Matching happens on subject and level first and the lesson runs one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. An online IB tutor in Al Sufouh is chosen from everyone who teaches the course, not from everyone who can reach Al Sufouh 2 by half past four.

sections.heading: What Dubai families pay per hour, cheapest tier first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most families start and where most of the disappointment lives. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is published from around AED 45 an hour, and the honest description of that tier is supervision: a capable person, often a university student, who will keep a student working and answer questions as they arise. For a Year 8 student who simply is not doing the homework, that may be exactly the right purchase.

The middle band, AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online, is where a trained subject teacher appears. The difference a parent can actually detect is mark-scheme literacy: this tutor knows that "state" and "explain" carry different tariffs, knows which topics the examiner has returned to in the last four sessions, and marks the student's work the way the paper will be marked. The top band, AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, is IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists, where the figure buys level-specific depth rather than a better personality.

Above AED 500 the market is pricing scarcity. A single named tutor with a reputation, a full diary and no incentive to discount will quote AED 650 an hour, and that figure is published rather than inferred. It is not a fraud, but it is not a different category of teaching either, and an Al Sufouh family on a two-year Diploma budget should understand that they are buying availability.

sections.heading: What the in-home premium buys in Al Sufouh, counted in minutes
paragraphs: The in-home band sits roughly AED 50 to AED 200 above the online band for comparable teaching, and the honest accounting of that gap is travel. A tutor who lives in Al Barsha and teaches a 16:00 session in Al Sufouh 1 commits between two and two and a half hours to deliver sixty minutes. No business absorbs that, so it is priced in, either as a higher rate or as a minimum two-hour booking.

The second cost is less visible and matters more. A fixed physical slot can only be filled by someone willing to make that journey at that time, which collapses the available pool. An Al Sufouh family wanting Chemistry at Higher Level discovers that the shortlist is three people, none of whom has taught the current syllabus, and the choice becomes a compromise framed as a convenience.

Scheduling is the third cost. An in-home session cannot easily move by twenty minutes when a school fixture overruns, cannot split into two shorter sessions in exam week, and cannot happen at all when the family travels. Over a two-year Diploma that produces a steady trickle of cancelled and part-used hours that nobody adds up.

This is why IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all. Home tutoring is a service offered only in India, and the UAE model is one-to-one teaching over live video, which keeps the full hour and keeps the choice of tutor open. A parent who wants to compare on cost should compare the delivered teaching minute, not the headline rate.

sections.heading: Five ways IB tutoring money gets wasted in this catchment
paragraphs: The first is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A family books two subjects twice a week in September on the strength of a June report, and by November nobody can say which topics have been fixed. One session spent reading the student's last three assessments against the mark scheme will usually redirect the whole plan, and it costs one hour.

The second is paying specialist rates for supervision work. If the problem is that a Year 10 student does not start their homework until 22:00, an AED 400 specialist is an expensive solution to a scheduling problem. The reverse error is just as costly: paying AED 90 for group revision when the issue is a Higher Level Paper 3 technique that a group cannot address.

The third is the untracked package. Monthly bundles in this market are published at AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours, and both are reasonable value if used. Families routinely use five of eight, then renew. The fourth waste is the opposite shape: nothing bought until February of the exam year, then three sessions a week at panic rates for twelve weeks, which costs more than two years of a steady weekly hour.

The fifth is paying for the wrong level of the same subject. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are different courses with different papers, and Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework. A tutor who knows the subject but not the level will teach competently and still miss the assessment the student is actually sitting, which is the most expensive kind of waste because it looks like progress.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma budget for an Al Sufouh family, written out
paragraphs: Set the tutoring number beside the school number and it stops feeling arbitrary. Dubai had 387,441 students enrolled across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for around seven per cent of that enrolment. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family already committed to a Diploma place, that freeze is the one fixed line in the budget.

Against that, published market estimates for weekly one-hour tutoring run at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are Bestimate's own monthly figures for weekly sessions, and they are the right order of magnitude to plan with. One subject, one hour a week, for the two Diploma years, at the mid band, is somewhere between AED 14,000 and AED 29,000 across twenty-four months.

That total is usually a surprise, and the surprise is useful. It forces the question of which single subject most deserves it, which is a better question than whether to tutor at all. Most Al Sufouh Diploma students who get real value from paid tutoring get it in one or two subjects, concentrated in the first DP1 term and the final twelve weeks, rather than spread thinly across six.

sections.heading: Is the person you are paying permitted to tutor in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is the cheapest piece of due diligence available to an Al Sufouh family. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the official service page lists a two-working-day completion time with applications made through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit costs nothing and takes two days, a tutor who does not hold one has either not bothered or is not eligible, and neither answer is good. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you either.

There is a second rule a parent should know, because it affects a popular shortcut. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Hiring your child's own class teacher privately is therefore not the easy win it appears to be.

A business is a different animal from an individual. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind and makes no such claim: it is a matching platform whose tutors teach online, and the permit question belongs to the individual tutor, verifiable by asking to see it.
