sections.heading: What a paid tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary where money buys the most trouble. Internal assessments carry real weight in every Diploma subject, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge feed the bonus points, and the deadlines land in the busiest months of DP1 and DP2. Demand for help is therefore intense, and part of this market has answered it by selling finished work. One operator in this search publishes a price for completed Internal Assessments; that is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

The permitted version is narrower and genuinely useful. A tutor can teach the method: how to narrow a research question until it is answerable in the word count, how an experimental design controls a variable, how to read the published criteria descriptors and recognise what each one is asking for. A tutor can read the student's own draft and say which criterion is weak and why. A tutor can teach referencing and citation properly, which prevents the accidental breaches that cause most trouble.

What a tutor must never do is produce the work. No writing the IA, no redrafting it to completion, no supplying the data, no handing over a structure that only needs filling in. IB Gram's position is explicit about this, and it is stated here rather than buried, because the families who get burned are usually the ones who were never told where the line sat.

There is also a practical reason to accept the boundary. An IA the student did not write cannot be defended in a viva or a follow-up conversation with a supervisor, and it teaches nothing that transfers to the written papers, which carry the larger share of the grade. IB Internal Assessment support in Dubai is worth paying for when it makes the student better at the next one.

sections.heading: Equivalency, attestation and what money cannot accelerate
paragraphs: Al Sufouh families planning on a UAE university place meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process, and it is worth understanding before paying anyone to help with it. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details inside that matter to planning. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which changes how a student counts their certificate list. And the subject count is five, not six, although at least one ranking competitor in this market publishes six; a wrong number on a regulatory requirement is the kind of error that costs a family a year.

For the American track the published requirements are different again: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB specifically, no points threshold is published that this page can verify, so none is stated here. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the school's IB coordinator and treat any site quoting a confident IB number without a source with suspicion.

Equivalency is a documentation process run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authorities. IB Gram does not perform it, cannot expedite it and makes no claim about it. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression, and anybody telling you otherwise is selling urgency rather than teaching.

sections.heading: Starting, pausing and stopping without wasting money
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing. A free trial lesson with a matched specialist, one hour, in the actual subject and at the actual level, is the only reliable way to find out whether this particular tutor and this particular student work. A trial is not a sales call: the student brings their last assessment or a piece of work they struggled with, and the hour is spent on it.

After the trial the useful commitment is small and time-boxed. One subject, one hour a week, six weeks, with a written list of the topics being addressed. At week six the list either has ticks against it or it does not, and that is a decision a parent can make without a progress meeting. Buying twenty-four sessions up front removes exactly that decision point.

Pausing should be free and frequent. Dubai school holidays, family travel, a heavy internal-assessment fortnight and the exam period itself are all reasons to stop for a few weeks, and a structure that penalises pausing quietly converts into unused hours. Online delivery makes the opposite move possible too: a student travelling over the winter break can keep the same tutor and the same slot, which is not an option when the model depends on somebody driving to a Dubai address.

The last honest point concerns availability. Some combinations are scarce: Higher Level Physics in the week before mocks, Computer Science at Higher Level, Arabic as a first language for a specific MoE-mandated stream. If no specialist is free for the slot a family needs, the right answer is to say so and offer the nearest real alternative, rather than to fill the slot with someone who does not teach the course. An IB Higher Level tutor in Dubai who is honest about the diary is worth more than a confident one who is not.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor near me in Al Sufouh cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai for IB tutoring run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour for a subject specialist, with Bestimate publishing that band for IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists and TutorChase quoting AED 270. Below that, qualified online subject teachers are published from around AED 150 to AED 300, and budget online tutoring starts near AED 45. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour because the drive is inside the rate. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list; the honest first step here is a free trial lesson and a conversation about the subject and the number of weeks left.

faqs.question: Is online IB tutoring genuinely cheaper than a home tutor for an Al Sufouh family?
faqs.answer: On published rates, yes: the online specialist band sits below the in-home band by roughly AED 50 to AED 200 an hour, and the gap is travel rather than teaching. The larger saving is in delivered minutes. An in-home session in Al Sufouh commits the tutor to forty to ninety minutes of driving, which is priced in and often enforced as a two-hour minimum booking. Online, the hour starts on the hour. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home teaching is a service that exists only in India, and UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: Why do IB rates run higher than IGCSE rates in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, and both are visible in the published bands. The pool of tutors who can teach a Diploma course at Higher Level is smaller than the pool who can teach IGCSE, because the content sits a year or two beyond A-Level foundations in several subjects. Scarcity moves price. The second reason is component complexity: a Higher Level Paper 3, an Internal Assessment and a Theory of Knowledge essay are three different skills, and a tutor who can handle all three has invested time most generalists have not. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which is the clearest illustration available.

faqs.question: What should an Al Sufouh family budget per month for one IB subject?
faqs.answer: Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are Bestimate's figures. For planning across the two Diploma years, one subject at the mid band comes to somewhere between AED 14,000 and AED 29,000 in total, which is worth knowing before the first booking rather than after the eighteenth. The number usually leads families to concentrate spend on one or two subjects in the periods where it converts.

faqs.question: Does a quoted Dubai tutoring rate include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, every time, and get the answer in writing before the first session. This page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that is a Federal Tax Authority question and no FTA citation is being relied on here. What a parent can and should establish is simple: whether the AED figure quoted to them is the figure that will be invoiced, whether the provider holds a tax registration number, and whether any booking or platform fee sits on top. A provider who cannot answer those three questions clearly is telling you something useful about their administration.

faqs.question: Do IB tutoring rates in Dubai rise as the May exams approach?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than list prices changing, and the effect on a family's bill is the same. In the twelve weeks before the May session the specialists with strong reputations fill their diaries, so what remains is either a less experienced tutor at the same rate or a premium individual quoting at the top of the market, where published figures reach AED 650 an hour. The practical consequence is that a steady weekly hour held from September costs less in total than a compressed block bought in February, and it secures the tutor you actually want.

faqs.question: How long should an Al Sufouh family give a new tutor before judging the match?
faqs.answer: Six, with a written list of the topics being addressed, after a free trial lesson. Six weeks is long enough for a tutor to see a pattern in the student's work rather than a single bad afternoon, and short enough that a family is not committed to a plan nobody is measuring. At week six the topic list is either closed or it is not. Prepaid packages of twenty or thirty sessions remove that decision point, which is precisely why they are easy to sell and easy to underuse.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both of my child's Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but do not treat it as a saving by default. Some combinations sit naturally with one specialist, particularly Mathematics with Physics, where the same algebraic fluency serves both. Others do not: Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Economics have nothing in common at the level of mark schemes and command terms. The test is whether the tutor has taught both courses at that level, not whether they feel confident. Two specialists at one hour each will usually beat one generalist at two hours.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit, and can I check it myself?
faqs.answer: Yes, and yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time, with applications through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, a tutor without one has either not bothered or is not eligible. Ask to see the permit rather than a description of it. Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: What extras tend to appear on a Dubai tutoring invoice?
faqs.answer: Four recur. A minimum booking length, often two hours for an in-home visit, which turns a one-hour need into a two-hour charge. A travel or fuel line for addresses outside the tutor's usual radius, which Al Sufouh sometimes is. A registration or matching fee charged once before any teaching happens. And a materials charge for printed past papers and worksheets. None of these is unreasonable if disclosed in advance; all of them are worth asking about before the first session rather than after the first invoice.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Al Barsha better value than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: Per hour, a centre group of two to four is published at roughly AED 90 to AED 180 per student, which is genuinely lower. The question is what the hour contains. A group moves at one pace, and the specific reason a student is losing marks, say unjustified steps in a method-marked calculus question, cannot be addressed without stopping the group. Add the drive to Al Barsha or Knowledge Park and the fixed weekly slot, and the saving narrows. Groups suit broad revision of shared content; they do not suit a diagnosed individual gap.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write my child's Internal Assessment if we pay extra?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider who agrees to is putting your child at risk rather than helping them. Producing an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay for a student is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the candidate. One operator in this market publishes a price for completed IAs, which is exactly the practice to avoid. What a tutor can legitimately do is teach the method, help narrow the research question, read the student's own drafts and give feedback against the published criteria, and teach referencing properly.

faqs.question: Do we keep paying through Dubai school holidays and travel weeks?
faqs.answer: You should not have to, and a structure that penalises pausing is one to avoid. Dubai's academic year has substantial breaks, families here travel, and there are fortnights in DP1 and DP2 where internal assessment deadlines leave no room for anything else. Pausing a weekly online slot for three weeks and resuming with the same tutor costs nothing. Online delivery also allows the opposite choice: a student abroad over the winter break can keep the same tutor and the same hour, which is impossible when the model depends on somebody travelling to a Dubai address.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You are told. Certain combinations are genuinely scarce, particularly Higher Level Physics and Computer Science in the weeks around mocks, and Arabic as a first language for the KHDA-mandated stream. The wrong response is to fill the slot with a tutor who does not teach that course and hope the parent cannot tell, which is common in this market. The right response is to say what is unavailable, offer the nearest genuine alternative, give an honest timeline for the specialist you asked for, and let the family choose with the facts in front of them.

faqs.question: Does paying for tutoring help with UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not directly, and nobody should sell it that way. Equivalency is a documentation process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authorities, assessed against published requirements. For the British track that means five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Tutoring can help a student reach those grades. It cannot accelerate the process, and IB Gram does not perform or guarantee any part of it.

intro.heading: What does the nearest IB tutor in Al Twar actually cost you?
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market, because that is where most searches for a nearby tutor begin in practice. In Dubai the published budget end is genuinely cheap: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both for online tutoring, with the broader budget and university-student band running from roughly AED 45 to 150. For plenty of jobs that is a fair price for a fair service. Supervising homework so it gets finished, drilling recall, keeping a student ticking over between harder sessions: a careful tutor at AED 60 does those things perfectly well.

What the budget band almost never buys is diagnosis. Diagnosis is watching a student attempt a question and knowing, from the first wrong line, which of four possible faults is actually present. It takes a tutor who has seen that error a hundred times in that subject at that level. In a six-subject Diploma with interlocking content, a tutor without it spends three sessions discovering what a specialist identifies in twenty minutes, and the cheap hours stop being cheap.

Move up a band and you reach qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that sit IB and IGCSE specialists at about AED 200 to 450 or more, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey agrees on the range. At the top, BartyED advertises a named tutor at AED 650. None of those numbers is ours; each belongs to the provider that published it, read in October 2026.

Now the part that this particular search makes relevant. A tutor who is physically near Al Twar is not drawn from the same pool as a tutor who teaches your child's subject. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors, and that premium pays for a car crossing the city at the evening peak. Worse, it narrows the shortlist to people willing to make that drive, which in a Higher Level subject can mean paying a premium rate for availability rather than expertise. That is the most expensive purchase in this market and it never looks like one on the receipt.

So the honest statement of what we do. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Diploma and MYP tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We make that trade because it removes the travel premium and the pool restriction in a single move, which means the money buys teaching rather than driving. The trial lesson is free, so you can test the format before any of this matters.

sections.heading: Working up from the cheapest option in Al Twar
paragraphs: Most pricing pages in this market start at the top and work down, which flatters the expensive option. Start at the bottom instead. The cheapest published tutoring available to an Al Twar family is online and advertised from AED 33 to 52 an hour by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik. A university student or a recent graduate at that rate can mark a problem set, keep a student company through homework, and drill recall until it is automatic. Those are real services and they are correctly priced.

The step that matters is the one to roughly AED 150 to 300, where qualified subject tutors sit and where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. What you are buying with that step is not enthusiasm; it is pattern recognition. A tutor who has taught Diploma physics for several years knows that a student who gets the right number with the wrong unit has a different problem from one who gets the wrong number with the right method, and treats them differently. That distinction is the entire justification for the price difference.

Above that, the specialist band at roughly AED 200 to 450 or more buys depth in a narrow area: Higher Level content, internal assessment supervision in a specific subject, or examination technique on a particular paper. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey places specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. At the top, BartyED advertises AED 650 for a named tutor, and at that price the purchase is a specific individual rather than a category of service.

Read as a decision, the ladder is less about status than it looks. The right answer for most Al Twar households is a mixture: the specialist band for the one or two subjects where marks are genuinely being lost for reasons nobody has explained, and the budget band or nothing at all for the rest. The expensive mistake is uniformity in either direction. Every figure above is a market rate published by the provider named, read in October 2026; IB Gram publishes a free trial and a consultation rather than an hourly price list.

sections.heading: Group, centre or one-to-one: price per student against value per student
paragraphs: Group tutoring is the obvious way to reduce the hourly figure, and in the right circumstances it is good value rather than merely cheap. The circumstances are narrow: two or three students at the same level, on the same paper, with the same specific weakness, taught by somebody who has checked that this is true. Under those conditions the discussion between students adds something a one-to-one session cannot, and the cost per family falls substantially.

The conditions usually do not hold. The commonest group in a district like Al Twar is assembled because three families live nearby and all want maths help, which produces a session running at the pace of its least prepared member while every family pays. The cost per hour is lower and the cost per useful minute is often higher. Ask who else is in the group, at what level, and on which paper, before agreeing to anything.

Tuition centre classes sit lower again on price and lower again on diagnosis. A centre class is structured recall work delivered to a room, which is a legitimate product and is not a substitute for somebody watching your child's working. Note too that a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific licence, and a provider without premises should not be describing itself in those terms.

One-to-one is the only format that reliably diagnoses, and the published bands above are what it costs. The sensible way to use the comparison is by job rather than by budget: a centre class for recall, a matched pair for shared paper practice, and one-to-one for the subject where nobody can explain why the marks are being lost. Buying all three for the same student at once is how a household spends more than it meant to and improves less than it hoped.

sections.heading: Which subjects actually repay an expensive hour
paragraphs: The question nobody asks at the point of purchase is which subject the money should go into. Students nominate the subject they dislike. Parents nominate the subject with the worst grade. Neither is reliably the subject where an hour buys the most marks, and the gap between them is where several thousand dirhams a year disappears in this district.

The test is whether the loss is explained. If a student is losing marks and the school can tell you exactly why, that is usually a technique or practice problem and the mid band fixes it. If a student is losing marks and nobody can say why, including the student, that is a diagnostic problem and it is the one place the specialist band is clearly worth the difference. Paying AED 300 an hour for a tutor to supervise work the student could do alone is the most common misallocation we see.

Subject matters too, because the subjects differ in how interlocked they are. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most unforgiving: a sequence breaks in October and everything downstream fails until somebody finds the break. Chemistry and physics are intermediate, with distinct fault types that look alike. Biology and the humanities are more forgiving, because the content is more modular and a gap in one topic does not propagate.

The core components are the outlier, and they are consistently mispriced by families. Narrowing an Extended Essay question, framing a TOK knowledge question, and scoping an internal assessment are small jobs with large consequences, and they cost almost nothing when done early. Done late, the same jobs cannot legitimately be done at all, because the only remaining help would cross the academic-honesty line. We will not write, draft, complete or edit any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay.

sections.heading: Why the nearest tutor is often the dearest per useful hour
paragraphs: Proximity has a price and it is not the one on the invoice. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 350 according to Bestimate, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Set against qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, the difference is the cost of a car crossing Dubai at the evening peak, paid by the hour. For a family in Al Twar, where the drive from central Dubai takes forty to sixty minutes each way, that premium is being earned honestly and spent reluctantly.

The deeper cost is the shortlist. An in-home arrangement in this district can only use tutors prepared to drive to Al Twar on a weekday evening. For a Standard Level humanity that is an acceptable constraint. For Higher Level physics, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or an Extended Essay supervisor in a specific discipline, the list of nearby candidates can collapse to one person, and at that point you are not choosing a tutor; you are accepting one. A shortlist of one is the single most expensive condition in tutoring, and nothing on the receipt reveals it.

There is a third effect that is specific to villa districts. Because the drive is long, in-home tutors in Al Twar price for and plan around back-to-back appointments, which means the session has a hard stop and the last ten minutes, the part where a student finally asks the question they were embarrassed about, gets cut. Over a term that is a meaningful share of the value, lost for logistical reasons that have nothing to do with teaching.

This is why we deliver one-to-one over live video rather than sending anybody to a UAE address, and why the saving is not the main argument. The main argument is that the same money buys a tutor selected for the subject and the level instead of a tutor selected for being willing to drive. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and we would rather state it plainly than let a page imply otherwise.

sections.heading: Two budgets: one that assumes nothing goes wrong, one that does not
paragraphs: Families plan the first budget and live the second. The optimistic version has one subject tutored weekly through the year at the mid band, which on Bestimate's monthly estimates is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, and nothing else. It is a perfectly reasonable plan and it holds for about one household in three. The other two meet something unplanned: a second subject that slips in DP1 spring, an internal assessment that needs supervision, or a mock result that triggers an eight-week block.

The realistic version therefore reserves rather than allocates. Commit the monthly figure for one subject, and set aside a block budget for one dated intervention per Diploma year: roughly ten hours at the mid-to-specialist band, which at AED 200 to 450 an hour is somewhere between AED 2,000 and 4,500 as a one-off. Planning that reserve is the difference between a household that absorbs a bad mock and a household that panics and buys at the premium band in week one of the crisis.

At the top end, the honest numbers are worth stating. Two subjects at the specialist band through DP2, using Bestimate's specialist monthly estimate of AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more per subject, is AED 2,000 to 4,000 a month. Across a two-year Diploma, a household running that pattern throughout is spending a figure in the tens of thousands of dirhams. Very few families decide to do that; a good many end up doing it by adding one more subject at a time.

The table sets out three shapes. The point of it is not to recommend one but to make the totals visible before they accumulate, which is the single most useful thing a cost page can do. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total, so this is a year in which the tutoring line is the one genuinely under a household's control.

sections.heading: How to buy diagnosis rather than company
paragraphs: The practical test fits into a trial lesson, and it has nothing to do with how well the tutor explains things. Almost every tutor at every band can explain something clearly; that is the easy half of the job. What separates the bands is what happens in the thirty seconds after your child gets something wrong. A tutor who re-explains has given you company. A tutor who asks a question designed to find out which of three possible misunderstandings is present has given you diagnosis, and that is what the price difference is for.

Ask two questions before booking as well. First: what would you do in the first three sessions? A specialist answers with a diagnostic plan, something like a diagnostic set, then the two topics the set exposes, then a timed question to check it transferred. A weaker answer is a list of topics, which is a syllabus rather than a plan. Second: what would make you tell us to stop? A tutor who can answer that honestly is one who will tell you when the money has stopped working.

Separate two problems before you spend anything, because they have different and differently priced solutions. Will not and cannot look identical on a report card. A student who is not doing the work needs structure, supervision and possibly a conversation that has nothing to do with tutoring, and the budget band is the correct purchase. A student who is working hard and still losing marks needs diagnosis, and the specialist band is the correct purchase. Buying the specialist solution for the structural problem is the commonest overspend in this market.

Finally, use the school. Your child's IB coordinator will usually tell you frankly which subject is costing the grade and why, and that single conversation reliably changes which tutor you should buy. Students nominate the subject they find unpleasant; coordinators nominate the subject that is losing marks. It costs an email and it routinely saves a term of well-intentioned spending in the wrong place.

sections.heading: Free checks that lower the bill before it arrives
paragraphs: Three things cost nothing and improve the purchase more than comparing providers does. The first is the permit question, which doubles as an honesty test because the permit itself is free. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone who tells you the permit is costly or optional has told you something checkable and wrong, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so ignore any specific figure.

The second is the regulator. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes inspection outcomes on its own site; Abu Dhabi's ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate, and the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Read a school's rating from the regulator rather than from a tutoring page, this one included.

The third is the accreditation check, which is free and decisive. Nobody selling you private tutoring in Dubai is accredited, approved or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson to do it. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with physical premises. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and occupies no UAE premises; we name regulators to explain what they do. If a provider claims otherwise, ask for the permit number before you ask for a price.

And one note on claims that cost you money indirectly. Treat any published rating, student count or success percentage without a stated sample size, date and method as decoration. Competitor pages in this market show different ratings in different places on the same page, and one shows five stars from twenty reviews alongside a headline student count in the thousands. A provider that cannot show its arithmetic on something that simple is not a provider whose diagnostic claims should be taken on trust.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to get IB tutoring in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: The published budget end of the Dubai market is online and starts at roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, read in October 2026. At that band you are buying supervision, recall drilling and homework completion, which for several subjects in a six-subject Diploma is genuinely all that is needed. What it does not buy is diagnosis of an error pattern nobody has been able to explain, and that is the one job worth paying more for.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives near Al Twar work out cheaper?
faqs.answer: Rarely, once the real costs are counted. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 350 according to Bestimate, and up to AED 500 with independent home tutors, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject tutors. The premium pays for forty to sixty minutes of driving each way at the evening peak. The larger hidden cost is that the nearby pool is small, so for a niche Higher Level need you may be paying a premium for availability rather than for expertise.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send somebody to our home in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Diploma and MYP tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason is the one this whole page is about: removing the drive removes both the travel premium and the restriction of the tutor pool, so the same money buys a tutor selected for the subject rather than for willingness to cross the city.

faqs.question: What am I actually paying extra for at AED 300 an hour?
faqs.answer: Pattern recognition. A tutor who teaches that subject at that level weekly knows that a student producing the right number with the wrong unit has a different fault from one producing the wrong number with the right method, and treats them differently. That is diagnosis, and it means the actual problem is found on the first attempt rather than the third. In an interlocked subject such as Higher Level mathematics, that difference is worth considerably more than the hourly gap suggests.

faqs.question: Is group tutoring better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Only when the group is genuinely matched: two or three students at the same level, on the same paper, with the same specific weakness. Then the cost per family falls and the discussion adds something. The common failure is a group assembled because three families live nearby and all want maths help, which runs at the pace of its least prepared member while everyone pays. Ask who else is in the group, at what level and on which paper before agreeing to anything.

faqs.question: Which subject should we spend the tutoring budget on?
faqs.answer: Ask the IB coordinator rather than the student. Students nominate the subject they find unpleasant; coordinators nominate the subject that is losing marks, and those are frequently different. Then apply one test: if the school can explain why marks are being lost, it is a technique problem and the mid band fixes it. If nobody can explain it, including your child, it is a diagnostic problem and that is where the specialist band earns its fee.

faqs.question: How much should a whole Diploma year cost in tutoring?
faqs.answer: It depends on the shape you choose, and seeing the totals first is the point. One subject weekly at the mid band is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's monthly estimates, or AED 7,200 to 14,400 a year. Adding a reserved one-off block of about ten hours at AED 200 to 450 takes that to roughly AED 9,200 to 18,900. Two subjects at the specialist band through DP2 is AED 2,000 to 4,000 a month, which annualises into the tens of thousands.

faqs.question: Why do families end up spending more than they planned?
faqs.answer: Because tutoring accumulates one subject at a time. A household commits to one subject in September, adds a second after a disappointing DP1 mock, adds internal assessment supervision in the summer, and buys an emergency block in the spring. No single decision was unreasonable and the total was never agreed. The fix is to name a monthly figure and a one-off reserve at the start of the year, then allocate within them, which is also the only way to notice when the money has stopped working.

faqs.question: Is a premium tutor at AED 650 an hour ever worth it?
faqs.answer: For a narrow, specific, high-stakes job occasionally, and as a default never. BartyED advertises AED 650 for a named tutor, and at that price you are purchasing one individual's attention rather than a category of service. If the requirement is genuinely singular, such as one paper in one Higher Level subject where a specific person has deep expertise, a small number of hours can be defensible. As a standing arrangement across a programme it is a poor use of a household budget.

faqs.question: Can a cheap tutor supervise an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: They can supervise the process honestly at any band, and no band may do more than that. Legitimate support means questioning the research question until it is answerable, challenging an uncontrolled variable, teaching conventions in general terms, and giving feedback on the student's own draft. We will not write, draft, complete or edit any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay at any price. IB academic-honesty rules make that a malpractice question and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest moment to fix an Extended Essay problem?
faqs.answer: At the question stage, months before the deadline, when three or four sessions at any competent band can turn an unanswerable question into an answerable one. That is the lowest-cost, highest-value purchase in the entire Diploma and families routinely skip it. Bought late, the same intervention cannot legitimately be made at all, because the only remaining help would involve producing the student's work. Timing, not rate, is what determines the value of core support.

faqs.question: Should I pay a deposit or a term in advance for a lower rate?
faqs.answer: Be cautious. The discount is real and so is the risk attached to it: tutor and student mismatches usually become clear in weeks two to four, and a family holding a dozen pre-paid sessions tends to persist with a poor match rather than write off the balance. That costs far more than the discount saved. Our arrangement handles the same risk from the other side: a free trial lesson before any payment, and a change of tutor at no cost if the match turns out to be wrong.

faqs.question: How do I tell a diagnostic tutor from a well-spoken one?
faqs.answer: Watch what happens immediately after your child gets something wrong. A tutor who re-explains the topic has given you company. A tutor who asks a question designed to establish which of several possible misunderstandings is present has given you diagnosis. Then ask what the first three sessions would contain: a diagnostic set, the topics it exposes, and a timed check is a plan, while a list of topics is just the syllabus read back to you.

faqs.question: Does the private tutor permit cost the tutor anything?
faqs.answer: No, and that is why the question is a useful honesty test. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. A tutor who tells you it is expensive or unnecessary has said something checkable and wrong. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Should I trust a tutoring site's star rating when comparing prices?
faqs.answer: Only if it shows its arithmetic. Treat any rating, student count or success percentage published without a sample size, a date and a method as decoration rather than evidence. Pages in this market display different ratings in different places on the same page, and one shows five stars from twenty reviews beside a headline student count in the thousands. A provider that cannot be accurate about something that simple should not be trusted on the harder claim that its tutors diagnose well.

faqs.question: What is the smallest sensible purchase to start with?
faqs.answer: A free trial lesson followed by three or four sessions in one subject, with a review at the end. That is enough to establish whether the tutor diagnoses or merely explains, whether the slot works in a real Al Twar week, and whether anything has moved. It is also small enough that getting it wrong costs very little. Starting with five subjects and a term paid up front maximises both the spend and the chance of discovering a mismatch too late to act on.

intro.heading: What a radius search cannot tell you about an IB tutor
paragraphs: A near-me search is a request for convenience, and in most categories convenience is a reasonable thing to optimise. A plumber twenty minutes away is better than one an hour away, because the skill is broadly uniform and the travel is the variable cost. Tutoring inverts that. The skill is enormously variable, the travel is dead time somebody pays for, and the thing a parent actually needs is a person who has taught the specific syllabus at the specific level and knows exactly where the marks go.

Al Warqa makes the inversion obvious. The community sits in eastern Dubai, with its school supply spread across Al Qusais, Mirdif, Festival City and Academic City, and most of that supply is CBSE or British rather than IB. So the pool of people living within a short drive who can teach Diploma Higher Level content is genuinely small. A radius search in this postcode is not filtering a large set down to the convenient ones. It is showing you almost everyone available and calling it a shortlist.

The cost side is just as concrete. Published Dubai rates put online qualified tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's table showing 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting 200 to 500. That gap is a commute charge. Converted into the only unit that matters, AED 1,000 buys between three and seven teaching hours online and between two and five and a half once somebody has to drive to Al Warqa'a 3 and back at six in the evening.

IB Gram's position needs stating before any of this reads as a sales argument. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE. That is an India-only service, and it is stated on every country page on this site. Al Warqa lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We are not claiming that a screen beats a kitchen table for every child. We are claiming that for a Diploma subject in this particular part of Dubai, the realistic alternative to a specialist online is a generalist nearby, and that the specialist is the better purchase.

What follows is therefore built around supply rather than around us. A map of what the eastern Dubai tutor pool actually contains. The premium proximity adds, in dirhams and in hours. An honest account of which subjects are well covered and which take a week to staff or get declined. The regulator map for all seven emirates, because families here move between them more often than anyone plans for. And a worked calculation a household can check against its own budget, with real figures rather than a range so wide it cannot be argued with.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-warqa.programmesIntro: Al Warqa families reach the IB through schools in Mirdif, Festival City and Academic City. These notes cover what each programme demands and what a near-me search typically gets wrong about it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. External papers sat in the May session carry most of each grade, with internal assessment contributing a published share. Higher Level adds syllabus content and, in several subjects, an additional paper, so a tutor competent at Standard Level is not automatically competent at Higher.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the proximity problem bites hardest for Al Warqa. Diploma Higher Level teaching is a narrow specialism, the nearest Diploma schools are a twenty-five minute drive away in Festival City or Mirdif, and the number of people living within ten minutes of Al Warqa'a 4 who can teach Higher Level Physics well is not a number worth filtering on.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups across five years, each marked against four criteria scored 0 to 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. There is no external examination, which means that general revision changes very little: marks move when the weak criterion is identified and practised specifically.
programmes.countryNote: MYP tutors are easier to find locally than Diploma specialists, because the content sits closer to general secondary teaching. The criterion descriptors are the specialism, and a nearby tutor who has never read them will produce pleasant sessions and a flat report. Ask which lettered criterion they are targeting before anything else.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no criterion marks and no examinations, reported against learner-profile attributes. The narrow, useful targets at this stage are number fluency, reading stamina and early written structure. Everything broader is supervision, and should cost what supervision costs.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one stage where a near-me search is reasonable, because what a young child needs is consistency and somebody present, and that is a service proximity genuinely improves. For families who still prefer online, short sessions with a fixed routine work better than long ones.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course, assessed through a mix of DP external papers and course-specific coursework. It is a legitimate IB route for a student who wants depth in two or three subjects alongside an applied qualification.
programmes.countryNote: Offered by a small number of Dubai schools. It belongs on this page because a student struggling with six Diploma subjects has options other than more tutoring, and any adviser who never mentions them is selling hours rather than advising.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-warqa.subjectsIntro: Coverage differs sharply by subject, and that is the real constraint rather than distance. Each note says what the subject assesses and how easily it can be staffed for an Al Warqa student.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof, with a third paper at Higher Level and the exploration as internal assessment. Well covered: this is the most requested Diploma subject in the UAE, so a match is usually available within days at any level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving. Reasonably covered, though fewer tutors are confident at Higher Level, where the statistical content and the modelling paper demand genuinely different preparation from Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields and the scientific investigation, with uncertainties and graph work as the predictable mark losses. Higher Level coverage is good but not deep; a Higher Level match sometimes takes a few days longer than Standard Level.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium, plus data-based questions that reward careful reading. Among the best-covered sciences, and one where a specialist genuinely outperforms a generalist because the common failure points are narrow and well known.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology volume conceals an application problem: students who can recite a process often cannot answer it in an unfamiliar organism. Well covered, with past-paper discipline and command-term work doing most of the useful lifting.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the grade, with commentaries as internal assessment. Coverage is moderate; Higher Level quantitative content and the policy paper narrow the pool more than parents expect.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis under time pressure, the individual oral and the Higher Level essay. Well covered. The common fault is summarising content rather than analysing technique, which responds quickly to targeted work.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks are easy to learn and hard to apply to case material. Moderately covered, with the internal assessment research question as the usual place marks are quietly lost before anyone notices.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Critical evaluation of methodology, ethics and generalisability separates grades, and the internal assessment demands correct statistical reporting. Coverage is thinner than the sciences, so a match can take about a week.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Argument structure, scoping and reflective writing. Support here is teaching and feedback on the student's own drafts only. Coverage is reasonable, but quality varies more than in any subject, so ask directly what the tutor will refuse to do.

sections.heading: What a near-me search returns in Al Warqa, and what it hides
paragraphs: Search results for a tutor near Al Warqa are assembled from advertising spend, business listings and approximate distance. None of those three correlate with teaching a named Diploma subject at a named level. What the result set hides is the thing that determines whether the money works: whether this person has taught Higher Level Chemistry to a candidate who was losing marks on energetics, and knows what that specific failure looks like on a script.

Three further things are invisible in a map result. The first is permit status, which is a genuine compliance question in the UAE and has a free, two-working-day answer. The second is whether the tutor is barred from teaching your child at all: a teacher at your child's own school cannot be paid to tutor them, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The third is availability, because a listing does not go grey when the person is fully booked.

The honest reframing is to stop asking who is near and start asking who is free and qualified at the hour your child can actually work. In Al Warqa that hour is typically 17:15 or later on a weekday, because the school run reaches Mirdif, Festival City or Academic City and the return leg is unpredictable. Fix the hour, name the subject and level, and the radius stops being a useful filter at all. What remains is a short, true list, which is less satisfying to look at than a map full of pins and considerably more use.

sections.heading: The eastern Dubai tutor supply map, honestly drawn
paragraphs: Supply in this part of Dubai follows the schools, and the schools around Al Warqa are mostly CBSE and British. That produces a resident teaching population strong in those curricula and thin in IB Diploma specialisms. It is not a criticism of anybody: a CBSE physics teacher with fifteen years of experience is a genuinely good teacher and the wrong purchase for a Higher Level internal assessment on uncertainty propagation.

The nearest concentration of IB teaching is Mirdif, around Uptown International School, and Festival City, around Deira International School and Universal American School. Both are fifteen to twenty-five minutes from the middle of Al Warqa at pickup time and considerably more at the hour a tutor would travel. And teachers at those schools are precisely the people who cannot tutor the students most likely to live nearby, because of the rule against tutoring one's own enrolled students.

Academic City and Silicon Oasis add a different kind of supply: university students and technical graduates, who are explicitly eligible for the MoHRE private tuition permit and who dominate the AED 33 to 65 band where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise. That tier is useful for routine work and poorly suited to Higher Level teaching. Which leaves a plain conclusion for a Diploma family in Al Warqa: the specialist you need almost certainly does not live near you, and the question is only whether you accept that or pay somebody to drive. Both are defensible answers, and only one of them is usually presented to a parent as a choice.

sections.heading: The proximity premium, in dirhams and in teaching hours
paragraphs: Price the drive rather than arguing about it. Market in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's table at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference is roughly AED 100 to 200 an hour, and in Al Warqa it covers a round trip of eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes from central Dubai.

Converted into teaching, the comparison gets uncomfortable. A household with AED 2,400 a month gets eight to sixteen hours online and four to thirteen in-home. Over a two-year Diploma that difference is not a nicety, it is a whole second subject. And the premium buys something with a negative side effect: a tutor making a long round trip accepts fewer slots, so the arrangement is more fragile and collapses the first time Ras Al Khor Road does.

None of this makes in-home tutoring a bad product. For a young child who will not work without an adult physically present, it is the right product and worth paying for. For a Year 13 working on an internal assessment in Higher Level Chemistry, the premium buys a commute and costs a specialist. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE at all, so this comparison is published as market information rather than as a choice we are offering. The figures come from published Dubai rate cards read in October 2026, and any household can check them against two or three quotes of its own in an afternoon.

sections.heading: Buying availability instead of distance
paragraphs: If distance is the wrong filter, availability is the right one, and the uncomfortable part of saying so is that availability has limits. No platform covers every subject at every level at every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise are the ones that match a Business Management student to a general economics tutor and hope nobody checks. Publishing the thin spots is the only version of this that is useful to a parent.

For Al Warqa Diploma enquiries the pattern is stable. Mathematics in both routes, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English A are well covered and normally matched within a few days at Standard Level and a little longer at Higher. Economics, Business Management and Psychology sit in the middle, usually about a week. Less commonly taken subjects and some language options are genuinely thin, and the right answer there is sometimes a decline rather than a match.

Where a near alternative is useful, it is offered as an alternative and named as one. A Chemistry specialist can do real work with a Biology student whose problem is data-handling, because the skill transfers; a family should be told that is what is happening rather than discovering it. And where the match is a specialist outside the UAE teaching at Gulf Standard Time, that is disclosed before booking, because nothing about the delivery was ever going to be in-person in this country. A family that would rather wait a fortnight for a UAE-based specialist than start next week with one elsewhere is entitled to make that choice with the facts in front of them.

sections.heading: Which regulator covers your child's school, and why Al Warqa families should care
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are regulated emirate by emirate, and families in eastern Dubai move across those borders more often than they expect, usually because of a job in Abu Dhabi or Sharjah. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate.

The map completes with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, which also regulates private education in its emirate, and the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities additionally approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates curriculum and fee approval sit with the regulator rather than only inspection.

Two practical consequences for an Al Warqa household. A school report from Dubai carries a KHDA inspection context that does not transfer directly to an ADEK or SPEA setting, so comparing two schools across emirates means comparing two different frameworks. And none of these authorities accredits, licenses or endorses a tutoring platform: IB Gram holds no permit or approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, and anybody who claims one should be asked to produce the number.

sections.heading: A worked calculation for an Al Warqa household
paragraphs: Take a concrete case rather than a range. A family in Al Warqa'a 2 has a Year 12 who is losing marks in Higher Level Chemistry and an MYP 4 sibling whose Sciences criterion B has dropped. The Chemistry student needs a specialist; the MYP student needs somebody who has read the criterion descriptors. The household has roughly AED 2,000 a month available and a usable window between 17:15 and 19:30 on two weeknights.

In-home, at AED 250 to 400 an hour, that budget supports five to eight hours a month across two children, which is one hour each per fortnight, and both children have to fit the same tutor's travel schedule or two premiums get paid. Online, at AED 180 to 280, the same budget supports seven to eleven hours, enough for a weekly hour each with room for an extra session before a mock, and the two children can be taught by two different specialists on the same evening without anyone waiting.

The second part of the calculation is the shape rather than the total. Spending the Chemistry hours on the internal assessment during Year 12, when there is still time to choose scope, is worth more per dirham than the same hours spent on general revision in Year 13. Spending the MYP hours on criterion B specifically, rather than on Sciences broadly, is the difference between a report that moves and one that does not. Neither of those decisions has anything to do with how far away anybody lives.

sections.heading: The four questions a map result cannot answer
paragraphs: First: what did you see in the marked work? A tutor who answers with a pattern across two papers has done the job of the first session already. One who answers with a list of qualifications has told you nothing about your child. Ask it before any package is quoted, because a provider quoting a monthly figure before seeing the work is selling hours rather than diagnosing a problem.

Second: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's own service page listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time via its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so no figure is quoted here. Because the permit is free and fast, there is no reasonable excuse for not holding it.

Third: what will you refuse to do with the internal assessment? The answer should be immediate: no text, no data, no analysis, no editing that changes authorship. A provider who hesitates is offering something that puts an IB registration at risk. Fourth: how do we stop? Six weeks, a review against the school's own marks, then extend, switch or end. An arrangement without a review point becomes a standing order, and that is how a sensible monthly figure turns into a two-year total nobody agreed to.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in Al Warqa who teaches Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Within a short drive, probably not in most Higher Level subjects. The schools immediately around Al Warqa and Al Qusais are largely CBSE and British, so the resident teaching population is strong in those curricula and thin in IB Diploma specialisms. The nearest concentration of IB teaching is Mirdif and Festival City, fifteen to thirty minutes away, and teachers at those schools cannot be paid to tutor their own enrolled students. Matching by subject and level over live video reaches a far deeper pool than any radius around this postcode.

faqs.question: Does distance actually matter when choosing an IB tutor?
faqs.answer: It matters for a young child who needs an adult physically present to work at all. For a Diploma subject it mostly matters as a cost: in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online, and that gap covers an eighty to one hundred and twenty minute round trip to Al Warqa from central Dubai. The gap also shrinks the pool to tutors willing to make the journey, and willingness to drive does not predict knowing where Higher Level Chemistry candidates lose marks.

faqs.question: What does the commute premium cost an Al Warqa family over two years?
faqs.answer: On a budget of AED 2,400 a month, online at AED 150 to 300 an hour buys eight to sixteen teaching hours while in-home at AED 180 to 500 buys four to thirteen. The difference is roughly three hours a month. Across a two-year Diploma that is somewhere near seventy hours, which is a whole additional subject of weekly support. Whether that trade is worth making depends on the child, but it should be made with the arithmetic visible rather than by default.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher tutor them privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and this is a point families regularly get wrong. A teacher cannot be paid to provide private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit it explicitly. Verify current wording against the authority's own policy document, and never arrange it regardless of who suggests it.

faqs.question: Which subjects can you actually cover for an Al Warqa IB student?
faqs.answer: Mathematics in both routes, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English A: Language and Literature are well covered and usually matched within a few days at Standard Level, a little longer at Higher. Economics, Business Management and Psychology sit in the middle at roughly a week. Less commonly taken subjects and several language options are genuinely thin and are sometimes declined. Where a near-subject specialist would genuinely help, it is offered as an alternative and named as one rather than quietly substituted.

faqs.question: Who regulates my child's school if we move from Dubai to Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. Dubai's authority is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Comparing schools across emirates means comparing two different inspection frameworks, not two scores on one scale.

faqs.question: What time does a weekday session realistically start for Al Warqa families?
faqs.answer: Al Warqa'a 1 households with short runs to Al Qusais schools can usually hold 16:30. Al Warqa'a 2 and 3, running to Mirdif or Festival City, should plan for 17:15 or 17:30. Al Warqa'a 4 and 5 families driving to Academic City often need 17:45. Fixing the window before choosing the tutor matters more than it sounds, because the commonest way a good match fails is not a bad tutor but a slot that never worked on an ordinary Tuesday.

faqs.question: Why do near-me tutoring results change every time I search?
faqs.answer: Because the ranking is assembled from advertising spend, business listings and approximate distance, none of which is stable and none of which describes teaching quality. A listing also does not grey out when the person is fully booked, so a result that looks available may not be. The four things that actually decide whether the money works, subject experience at the right level, permit status, genuine availability at your hour, and what they refuse to do with coursework, are all invisible in the result.

faqs.question: Is a budget online tutor good enough for IB Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends what the problem is. The AED 33 to 65 band, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, buys supervision and question-answering from a university student or recent graduate, and that genuinely helps a student whose issue is sitting down and finishing the work. It does not diagnose why marks are lost against a mark scheme. Where the weakness is technique or internal assessment method, the AED 150 to 300 band is the honest minimum, and paying less is paying for the wrong thing.

faqs.question: Do you have an office in Al Warqa or anywhere in Dubai we can visit?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram operates no premises in the UAE and does not claim to. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry; we do not hold one because we do not run premises here. Two competitor pages researched for this project show a UAE footer address on a page for a different emirate, which is a misrepresentation worth noticing.

faqs.question: How quickly can an Al Warqa family get started?
faqs.answer: For the well-covered subjects, a free trial lesson is usually arranged within a few days once the subject, level and usable window are known. For subjects in the middle band expect about a week. For the thin ones you get a date rather than a reassurance, and occasionally a decline. Nothing here is instant because the matching is done on subject and level rather than by handing you the first available person, and that distinction is the whole point of the arrangement.

faqs.question: Should we pay a premium rate for an examiner for an Al Warqa student?
faqs.answer: Be careful with the claim rather than the price. Premium bands in Dubai reach AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Examiner status is only meaningful if it is current and evidenced, and it never implies access to marking, boundaries or paper content. For most Diploma problems, a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 who can read a mark scheme properly achieves the same thing. Reserve the top of the market for one subject in a short final block, if at all.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both our children if they study different programmes?
faqs.answer: Usually not well, and it is worth resisting. An MYP 4 student needing criterion B in Sciences and a Year 12 needing Higher Level Chemistry are two different specialisms, and the second is narrow. Online, the two can be taught by two different specialists on the same evening from the same house with nobody waiting. With a visiting tutor you either compromise on one child or pay two travel premiums, which is a poor use of the same monthly figure.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we are matched with turns out to be wrong for our child?
faqs.answer: You change the match, without penalty, and sooner rather than later. The free trial exists precisely to surface a mismatch before money moves, and the six-week review exists to catch the slower kind, where the sessions are pleasant and the marks do not move. A provider who makes changing difficult has aligned its incentives against yours. There is no fixed term here, which is the only arrangement under which a review point means anything at all.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-warqa.closingHeading: Give us the subject, the level and the hour that actually works
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-warqa.closingBody: Skip the radius. Tell us the subject and level, send two recently marked pieces of work, and say which hour genuinely survives the Al Warqa school run. We will match from everyone qualified and free at that time, tell you honestly if the subject is thin, and give you a free trial lesson that ends with a named weakness and an estimate in weeks. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Nothing is promised about a grade, and nobody is sent to a UAE address because we do not offer that here.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-wasl.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below teaches one or two Diploma subjects at a named level rather than the Diploma in general. The matching question we ask first is which subject and which level, because that is what determines whether somebody can help, and it has nothing to do with how far they live from Al Wasl Road.

intro.heading: Six subjects, two levels, and the question behind the search
paragraphs: Al Wasl is a villa district on the Al Wasl Road corridor, minutes from the Al Safa school cluster and a short run from Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim. A parent searching 'IB tutor near me' from here is asking a geographical question and wanting an academic answer. The academic answer is that the Diploma is not one thing. It is six subjects drawn from six groups, each taken at Higher or Standard Level, each with its own papers and weightings, each with an internally assessed component, and all of it sitting alongside Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and a service commitment.

No individual is a specialist across that. The person who can take a Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches student from a 5 to a 7 is not the person who should be teaching Language and Literature Paper 1, and a tutor who offers both across four curricula is describing availability rather than expertise. That is the real reason a proximity search disappoints: it optimises for the one variable that has no bearing on teaching quality, and it narrows the shortlist for a Higher Level science to whoever happens to be free and willing to drive.

The scale of the market makes this concrete. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment and International Baccalaureate programmes at roughly 7%. A Higher Level subject is a minority product inside a minority curriculum. Filter for somebody who has taught it in the last two academic years, is free at a particular hour in Gulf Standard Time, and will cross Dubai on a weekday afternoon, and the list for Higher Level physics or chemistry is very short in Al Wasl and equally short in Al Safa, Jumeirah and City Walk, because they share one road network.

IB Gram's answer is stated plainly. Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Dropping the travel requirement is the only one of the four constraints that costs nothing academically, and dropping it means the shortlist for an Al Wasl student is drawn from everybody who has taught the subject at the level required. Published Dubai in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tutors show what the travel requirement costs in cash as well.

The rest of this page is the subject answer. It sets out the six groups with where marks are actually lost in each, compares Higher and Standard Level on the things that differ, explains the command-term vocabulary that is identical across all six subjects and taught in almost none of them, sets out the internally assessed components that nobody plans for, explains how the core contributes points, publishes a past-paper protocol that works across six subjects at once, and states where specialist availability is genuinely thin.
