dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-wasl.programmesIntro: An Al Wasl family searching this phrase is usually at one of four points, and the useful first move differs at each. These are the four, with what each one most needs.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: Six subjects, three or four at Higher Level and the rest at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment is predominantly external, with an internally assessed component in nearly every subject, usually around a fifth of the grade in the sciences. The core contributes up to three points of its own.
programmes.countryNote: Al Wasl students are taught at the Al Safa, Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim campuses, and subject availability differs between them: not every school offers every group six subject, and timetable blocking can force a student to choose between two Higher Levels they wanted. Where the school cannot resolve a clash, the content missed has to be rebuilt outside school hours, which is the most common reason a family here starts looking in October.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme into the Diploma
programmes.description: Criterion-marked across eight subject groups, four criteria per subject each out of eight. Students arrive in the Diploma strong on inquiry, independence and documentation, and thinner on timed examination stamina and fast content recall. Both deficits are addressable in the summer before Year 12 and considerably harder to fix in the second term.
programmes.countryNote: One IB continuum school sits in Al Safa within minutes of Al Wasl, with others in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, so this route exists locally but serves a minority of households in a corridor dominated by British-curriculum schools. Families on it will field constant comparison with neighbours sitting Year 11 qualifications, which is a reporting difference rather than an attainment one.

programmes.name: A Year 11 qualification into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the dominant route in this corridor. Extended or Higher tier content is what Diploma courses assume: the algebra, the quantitative science and the essay structure all reappear at speed in Year 12 and are not retaught. A Core or Foundation background is a genuine obstacle for Higher Level sciences and mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: The summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the highest-value support window available to an Al Wasl family and almost nobody uses it. Six weeks on algebraic speed, quantitative fluency and timed writing is cheaper than a term of rescue in Year 12 and removes the three most common causes of an early Diploma stumble before any of them happen.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the internal assessments
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through a prescribed-title essay and an exhibition; the Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a school supervisor. Together they contribute up to three points. Each subject also carries its own internally assessed component. All of it is the student's own work.
programmes.countryNote: This is the part of the Dubai market an Al Wasl parent should be most careful about. One provider in this cluster has been documented selling completed internal assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student. Schools here run originality checks and supervisors sign declarations, so the exposure is concrete.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-wasl.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects Al Wasl families most often need, with what each one is actually assessed on. The point of the detail is that it is what a tutor should be matched against, rather than a postcode.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested subject in this corridor and the one where a proximity search fails most often. Higher Level requires fluent calculus, proof, complex numbers and vectors taught at pace, and comfort with Standard Level does not imply comfort with Higher. Ask a prospective tutor which Higher Level topics they have taught in the last two years.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led with graphing technology assumed throughout. Standard Level is easier to staff than Analysis and Approaches because more general mathematics teachers can cover it well. Higher Level, with its statistical inference and modelling, is a genuinely different course and a much smaller pool of teachers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two written papers and one scientific investigation, with no third paper in the current course. The scarcest science locally and the one where families most often end up with a mathematics teacher covering it. The data-based section and the uncertainty arithmetic are the specialist parts.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Six themes, two written papers and one scientific investigation. The quantitative chain from moles to concentration to yield breaks at a link the student cannot locate alone, and the organic mechanisms theme needs volume with correction rather than explanation. Thin availability at Higher Level across every Dubai district.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Better covered locally than physics or chemistry, with a large recall load and the same investigation criteria as the other sciences. The specialist value is in command-term discipline and in teaching the student to answer the question that was asked rather than the one they revised for.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Internally assessed commentaries or a project alongside the examinations, with Higher Level adding quantitative content in economics. Popular in this corridor, reasonably well staffed, and the place where a specialist earns the rate by teaching the assessment criteria rather than improving the writing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, an individual oral, and at Higher Level a further essay. The individual oral is the component families underestimate most and the one that benefits most from being rehearsed properly rather than discussed. Widely available in principle, with a wide quality spread.

subjects.name: Language acquisition: French, Spanish and Arabic
subjects.levels: Higher Level, Standard Level and ab initio
subjects.description: Availability depends sharply on the language and the level. Arabic at a high level is better served in Dubai than in most markets; ab initio Spanish or French in a specific evening slot is harder to fill. Oral components need a tutor who will conduct them under timed conditions rather than talk about them.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects, contributing points alongside the Extended Essay. Science and mathematics students often find the exhibition harder than the essay, because it asks for an argument about knowledge rather than about content, and it tends to be neglected until Year 13.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent 4,000-word piece with a school-allocated supervisor who holds the formal meetings and signs the declaration. A tutor may coach the subject content and the assessment criteria and may not write, edit or supply any part of it. Narrowing the research question early is the single most useful hour available.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-wasl.regionsTitle: Al Wasl and where its Diploma students are taught
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-wasl.regionsIntro: What differs between the districts around Al Wasl is which schools and which subject offerings sit inside each drive, not how many Diploma specialists live there. These are the areas and what each contains.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: Villas and compounds along Al Wasl Road with no substantial secondary campus inside the district, so every Diploma student commutes, most often a short run west into Al Safa. The shortest school run in this group, which makes a 17:00 session realistic for a Year 12 student.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: The densest school cluster in this part of Dubai, with British-curriculum sixth forms and one IB continuum school among them. This is where most Al Wasl Diploma students are taught, and where subject availability within a single timetable is widest.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Established villas with long-standing British-curriculum provision close by. Strong on A Level sixth forms and thinner on Diploma provision, so an Al Wasl family set on the Diploma is usually looking at Al Safa or further west rather than here.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Two substantial campuses including an IB continuum school, which is where the full Middle Years Programme into Diploma route is clearest within reach. The longest afternoon return in this group, which pushes weekday sessions towards 17:30.

regions.name: City Walk
regions.note: Low-rise apartments immediately north with no secondary campus. Students there share classes, teachers and tutors with Al Wasl students, which is the clearest demonstration that the specialist pool is the city's rather than the district's.

regions.note: Villas running west along the coast with primary provision nearby and secondary a slightly longer run. Widening a school search here changes the commute and the community rather than the range of Diploma subjects available.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Selective British campuses alongside IB continuum provision, twenty to thirty minutes out. Students travelling here from Al Wasl arrive at the Diploma with strong Year 11 foundations, so support is more often about pace and papers than about gaps.

regions.name: Al Manara and Al Quoz
regions.note: Inland, with newer campuses and a different school profile. Worth including in a school search where a specific Higher Level subject is not offered at the nearer schools, which happens more often than families expect in group six and in the less common languages.

sections.heading: What 'near me' actually gets you, and what it does not
paragraphs: A proximity search is a reasonable instinct and a poor filter. What it gets an Al Wasl family is a list of people who are willing to drive to Al Wasl Road on a weekday afternoon, which is a selection criterion with no relationship to whether somebody can teach Higher Level chemistry. What it does not get is the thing the parent actually wants, which is a person who has taught the specific subject at the specific level and can name where this particular student is losing marks by the end of the first hour.

The four constraints on a match are subject, level, hour and location, and they multiply rather than add. Requiring a specific subject cuts the pool hard. Requiring a specific level cuts it again, because comfort with Standard Level does not transfer upwards. Requiring a specific weekday hour cuts what remains, since the best tutors are teaching full days and have a small number of evening slots. Requiring physical presence in one district cuts it a fourth time, and that is the only one of the four a family can remove without giving up anything academic.

There is a test that settles this in one question, and it works on any provider including this one. Rather than asking whether they cover Al Wasl, ask how many tutors on their books have taught your child's exact subject at your child's level in the last two academic years and are free between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time. A provider drawing on the whole country can answer with a number. A provider drawing on a twenty-minute radius will talk about experience instead. The answer tells a parent more than any list of neighbourhoods on a landing page.

sections.heading: The six groups, and which of them need a specialist
paragraphs: The Diploma draws six subjects from six groups: studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the arts, with a second subject from another group permitted in place of the arts. Each group is assessed differently, each loses marks in a characteristic place, and the depth of local specialist supply varies enormously between them. The table below sets that out, and the last column is the one that matters when a family is deciding where a limited budget goes.

The pattern is consistent across Dubai and not specific to this corridor. Higher Level sciences and Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are the tight spots. English A and the essay-based individuals and societies subjects are reasonably well staffed, with a wide spread in quality that is hard to judge from a profile. The less commonly taught languages and ab initio levels are genuinely scarce, and group six arts subjects are the hardest of all to match, because the assessment is portfolio-based and few tutors have examined it.

One further point about the group structure is worth making because it changes priorities. A student is not trying to improve six subjects. They are trying to improve a points total, and the marginal point is cheapest to win where the student is closest to a boundary and where the assessment is most responsive to technique. A subject at 5 with technique losses is a better investment than a subject at 3 with foundational gaps, and the second of those is where families instinctively put the money. That arithmetic is the honest basis for deciding which subject gets the funded hour.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, compared properly
paragraphs: Parents are told that Higher Level is harder, which is true and not useful. What a family needs is the specific nature of the difference, because it determines how many hours a plan needs and whether a Standard Level tutor can help. In the sciences the component weightings are identical between the levels and the extra Higher Level load arrives as additional depth within the same themes plus longer papers; the practical consequence is that the algebra gets heavier rather than the concepts getting stranger. In mathematics the two levels are substantively different courses with different content lists.

The second real difference is pace, and it is the one that catches out able students in Year 12. A Higher Level course covers more content in the same number of weeks, which means a week missed through illness or a school trip costs more and a topic not understood the first time is not revisited. Students who coped comfortably through a Year 11 qualification often meet their first genuine difficulty in the second term of Year 12, and the cause is usually accumulation rather than difficulty: three partially understood topics behaving like one large gap.

The third is the university question, which should be settled by reading rather than by assumption. Some engineering and physical-science programmes name Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specifically, and some require a Higher Level science. Requirements differ between institutions and between years, and they are published. Twenty minutes spent reading the actual entry requirements of the universities on a student's list, in Year 12 rather than Year 13, prevents a subject change that cannot be undone. No tutoring page should be the source of that information, and this one is not.

sections.heading: Command terms, which are identical across all six subjects
paragraphs: This is the cheapest intervention available to a Diploma student and the one almost no school teaches explicitly, because teachers reasonably assume it is absorbed. Command terms are defined, they ask for a specific shape of answer, and marks are allocated on the assumption that the student responded to the term rather than to the topic. 'State' asks for a specific answer with no supporting argument. 'Outline' asks for a brief account. 'Describe' asks for detail without reasons. 'Explain' asks for reasons or causes, and is where most losses live because students describe instead.

The higher-order terms are where a Higher Level student loses the marks that separate a 6 from a 7. 'Deduce' requires a conclusion drawn from the information given, which means the answer must reference that information. 'Determine' requires a quantity, which means a number with its unit. 'Evaluate' requires strengths and limitations and a judgement, so an answer that lists advantages caps the mark however accurate it is. 'Discuss' requires a balanced review. 'Justify' requires the evidence behind a statement. 'Suggest' invites a plausible answer where more than one exists and rewards a student who commits and defends.

The reason this belongs on a page about proximity is that it is the one piece of work that pays off in all six subjects at once. A student who learns to read command terms properly gains marks in chemistry, in economics, in biology and in history in the same term, from a single block of three or four sessions. It is the highest-return hour in the Diploma and it is almost never what a family asks for, because it does not map onto a subject. A tutor who identifies that pattern in a diagnostic lesson and recommends it rather than a year of subject sessions is giving the more useful answer.

sections.heading: Internal assessments: the fifth of the grade nobody plans for
paragraphs: Nearly every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, and in the sciences it is around a fifth of the grade. The mathematics exploration, the science investigation, the economics commentaries, the language oral and the arts portfolio are all assessed against published criteria and all produced in the student's own time. Collectively they represent a substantial share of a points total, and they are the part of the Diploma most consistently left to drift, because the deadlines are internal and therefore feel negotiable until they are not.

Two things follow for an Al Wasl family planning support. The first is that these components reward front-loading rather than rescue. In the sciences the failure mode is a research question too broad to answer with the data it generates, which cannot be repaired once the data exists. In mathematics it is an exploration with no genuine mathematical content beyond the syllabus level. In economics it is a commentary that summarises an article instead of applying a specific diagram and theory to it. All three are fixed cheaply at the planning stage and expensively afterwards.

The second is the boundary on help, which we state rather than imply. A tutor may teach what each criterion rewards, interrogate a proposed research question, challenge whether a conclusion follows from the evidence, explain word limits and referencing conventions, and point out that an evaluation has identified nothing systematic. A tutor may not write, edit, restructure or supply any part of the work, may not choose the research question, and may not produce the analysis. One provider in this market has been documented selling completed internal assessments at AED 3,750; that is a malpractice trigger and the student carries it. For the Extended Essay specifically, supervision is a school role that cannot be outsourced: the supervisor is allocated by the school, holds the formal meetings and signs the declaration.

sections.heading: The core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the points
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points to a Diploma total, awarded from a published matrix that combines the grades achieved in each. The exact combinations are set out in the matrix the school's Diploma coordinator can show you, and it is worth asking for rather than relying on a tutoring page; what matters for planning is the shape of it. Strong performance in both produces the maximum; weak performance in one is partly offset by strength in the other; and a sufficiently poor grade in either is a failing condition for the diploma regardless of how high the subject points are.

That last point is the one families do not know and it changes behaviour. A student with 38 subject points who neglects the core entirely is not safe, because the core carries conditions as well as points. Science and mathematics students are the most at risk here, for a predictable reason: Theory of Knowledge asks for an argument about how knowledge is produced and justified, which is a different intellectual activity from anything else on their timetable, and the exhibition in particular asks them to build a case from three objects. It gets postponed, and then it is Year 13.

The useful intervention is small and early. For the Extended Essay, one or two hours narrowing the research question before any research begins, because an unbounded question cannot be rescued. For Theory of Knowledge, a session on what the exhibition is actually asking and a second on structuring an argument around a prescribed title. For both, the boundary is the same: the tutor coaches the criteria and questions the reasoning, the school supervises and authenticates, and the student writes every word. Two or three hours spent on the core in Year 12 is worth more in points than the same hours spent on a sixth subject already at a 5.
bullets: Up to three points from the combination of the two core grades

sections.heading: A past-paper protocol that works across six subjects
paragraphs: A Diploma student cannot run six separate revision systems, and attempting to is why Year 13 revision so often produces activity without improvement. What works is one protocol applied to every subject, with the definition of 'a paper' adjusted per subject type. The protocol has four steps: sit the thing under genuine time with no resources, mark it against the published mark scheme rather than a worked solution, assign every lost mark to one of five categories, and spend the next session on the largest category rather than on the topic that produced the most losses.

The five categories are content not known, command term misread, notation or units, missing reasoning step, and arithmetic or accuracy. They are deliberately few, because a taxonomy a student will not maintain is worthless. Counting them across all six subjects produces the single most useful piece of information in Year 13: whether the student has a subject problem or a habit problem. Command-term losses spread evenly across four subjects point to one block of work that fixes all four. Content losses concentrated in one subject point to teaching in that subject and nowhere else.

The table below adjusts the protocol for subject type, because 'a past paper' means different things in an essay subject, a quantitative subject and a language. Two design notes carry across all of them. Volume should fall in the final fortnight rather than rise, since by then the useful work is targeted repair and a student sitting three full papers a week is exhausting themselves. And every lost question should be re-attempted once, days later, because marking without re-attempting measures a weakness without addressing it.

sections.heading: Online delivery, availability, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Start with where the marginal hour buys the most. A Diploma student is optimising a points total, not six separate grades, and the cheapest point to win is usually in a subject sitting just below a boundary with technique losses rather than in the weakest subject with foundational gaps. The published Dubai rates are the same whichever subject the hour goes into: qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650, budget online provision at AED 33 to 52 from Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 from EdFlik, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 rate table with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Those are other companies' published figures, named and dated.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Availability is finite and we publish where it binds. Higher Level physics, chemistry and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches may take up to a week to fill in a narrow weekday window. Ab initio and less commonly taught languages, and group six arts subjects, take longer. Standard Level sciences, English A, economics and history are usually matched in two or three days. When the first choice is unavailable we name which of three applies: a different hour with the right specialist, an adjacent specialism with the limitation stated, or a wait. No competitor page in the researched set publishes a coverage limit at all.

The claims declined. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB organisation, Cambridge or Pearson; a KHDA educational services permit belongs to training institutes with premises and we hold none. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE. Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws with no published schedule of amounts, so none is quoted. No IB session or results date appears here, because the IB organisation's site blocks automated checking and a date a parent acts on must come from the school's coordinator. And no tutor can guarantee a grade or a points total.

process.title: Send one marked paper per subject you are worried about
process.description: A marked script is data; a predicted grade is a summary. With two or three scripts a tutor can say whether this is a content problem in one subject or a command-term problem across four, and those two findings lead to completely different plans and completely different costs.

process.description: No charge and no card details. Sometimes the answer is the command-term block rather than any subject.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives near Al Wasl teach the Diploma any better?
faqs.answer: No, and the question is worth answering directly because the instinct behind it is reasonable. Proximity selects for willingness to drive across Dubai on a weekday afternoon, which has no relationship to whether somebody has taught Higher Level chemistry in the last two years. What it does affect is the length of your shortlist: requiring physical presence in one district removes most of the people who could help. Published Dubai in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour sit above the AED 150 to 300 online band, so the proximity requirement costs money as well as choice.

faqs.question: Which of the six Diploma groups is hardest to find a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Group six, the arts, by a clear margin, because the assessment is portfolio and performance based and very few tutors have examined it. After that, ab initio and less commonly taught languages, where the pool is small and oral components need somebody who will conduct them properly rather than discuss them. Then Higher Level sciences, with physics thinnest, and Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. English A, economics, business management and history are reasonably well staffed, with a wide spread in quality that is difficult to judge from a profile alone.

faqs.question: How much harder is Higher Level than Standard Level in practice?
faqs.answer: In the sciences, the component weightings are identical and the extra load arrives as additional depth within the same themes plus longer papers, so the algebra gets heavier rather than the concepts getting stranger. In mathematics the two levels are substantively different courses. The difference that catches out able students is pace: more content in the same number of weeks, so a fortnight missed costs more and a topic not understood the first time is rarely revisited. Most Year 12 difficulty in this corridor is accumulation rather than difficulty, which is why early support is cheaper than late.

faqs.question: How many of the six subjects should we actually get help with?
faqs.answer: One, usually, or two in an exam year. A Diploma student carries six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and a service commitment, and cannot absorb more than one or two tutored hours a week without displacing the independent work that produces most of the improvement. The decision about which subject should be made on where the marginal point is cheapest: a subject just below a boundary with technique losses beats the weakest subject with foundational gaps, which is the opposite of what most families choose.

faqs.question: What proportion of a Diploma subject grade is internally assessed?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject, and in the sciences it is around a fifth: the scientific investigation carries 20% of the grade while the two written papers carry 36% and 44%. Mathematics has an internally assessed exploration, economics has commentaries, the languages have oral components and the arts have portfolio work. Across six subjects that is a substantial share of a points total, and it is the part most consistently left to drift because the deadlines are internal and feel negotiable. It is also the part that rewards front-loading and resists rescue.

faqs.question: How many points do Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay contribute?
faqs.answer: Up to three, awarded from a published matrix that combines the grades achieved in the two components. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator for the current matrix rather than relying on any tutoring page, including this one. What matters for planning is the shape: strong performance in both produces the maximum, weakness in one is partly offset by strength in the other, and a sufficiently poor grade in either is a failing condition for the diploma regardless of subject points. That last part is the piece most families do not know.

faqs.question: Can a grade in the core stop my child getting the diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. The core carries failing conditions as well as points, which means a student with a strong subject total is not automatically safe if Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay has gone badly. Science and mathematics students are the most exposed, for a predictable reason: Theory of Knowledge asks for an argument about how knowledge is produced and justified, which is unlike anything else on their timetable, so it gets postponed until Year 13. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the exact current conditions, and treat two or three hours of core coaching in Year 12 as insurance rather than enrichment.

faqs.question: What does 'evaluate' want in a Diploma answer?
faqs.answer: Strengths and limitations, and then a judgement. An answer that lists advantages accurately and stops will be capped, because the command term asked for an assessment rather than a description. This matters across all six subjects, since the command terms are defined the same way everywhere: 'explain' needs reasons, 'describe' needs detail without reasons, 'deduce' needs a conclusion drawn from the information given, 'determine' needs a number with its unit, and 'justify' needs the evidence behind a statement. Three or four sessions on this raises marks in every subject at once, which makes it the highest-return work available.

faqs.question: How should a Year 13 student mark their own papers across six subjects?
faqs.answer: With one protocol rather than six. Sit the paper under genuine time with no resources, mark against the published mark scheme rather than a worked solution, and assign each lost mark to one of five categories: content not known, command term misread, notation or units, missing reasoning step, arithmetic or accuracy. Count the categories across all six subjects. Then re-attempt every lost question a few days later, because marking without re-attempting measures a weakness without addressing it. The tally is the measurement that tells you whether this is a subject problem or a habit problem.

faqs.question: Is it better to raise one subject from 5 to 6 or two subjects from 4 to 5?
faqs.answer: Numerically the same, which makes the question about which is more achievable rather than which is worth more. A subject at 5 with technique losses, where the student knows the content and is losing marks to command terms, units or unshown working, is usually the cheaper point, because those are habits and habits move in weeks. A subject at 4 with foundational gaps needs teaching across months. Diagnose from marked scripts before deciding, and be wary of the instinct to put the money into the subject that worries the household most.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma student start past papers?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do, and in smaller units. In Year 12 a past-paper section is a diagnostic rather than a rehearsal: it establishes whether the student can handle the question style and where the losses cluster, which informs the whole two-year plan. Full papers under time belong to Year 13. The volume should rise through the autumn, peak around the mocks, and then fall in the final fortnight, when the useful work is targeted repair. A student sitting three full papers a week in April is exhausting themselves for diminishing returns.

faqs.question: My child's predicted grades have dropped. What does that actually mean?
faqs.answer: It means the school's current best estimate has changed, usually on the evidence of a mock or a recent assessment, and it is a measurement rather than a verdict. The useful response is to find out what produced it: which paper, marked against which scheme, and what the losses were. A drop caused by meeting terminal conditions for the first time is a practice problem. A drop caused by content not covered after a staff change is a teaching problem. Ask the subject teacher which of those applies before buying anything, because the two need different plans.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subject pairs can sensibly share one tutor?
faqs.answer: In a few genuinely adjacent pairs, yes, and where it works the saving is real. Physics with mathematics is the clearest case, because a tutor who recognises that a physics error is actually a logarithm error fixes it in minutes rather than reteaching the physics. Chemistry with biology and economics with business management also work. The test is whether the tutor can diagnose across both, and the diagnostic lesson is where to test it. Where they cannot, two subjects with one tutor is worse than one subject done properly, and we will say so.

faqs.question: What is the earliest useful point to get Diploma support?
faqs.answer: The summer between Year 11 and Year 12, and it is the window almost nobody in this corridor uses. Six weeks on algebraic speed, quantitative fluency and timed writing removes the three most common causes of an early Diploma stumble before any of them happen, and it costs a fraction of a rescue block in Year 13. After that, the first half of Year 12 is the cheapest paid time in the course: the same hourly rate does roughly twice the work it will do eighteen months later, because foundational repair is still possible.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for our Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: We say so and name which of three options applies. A different hour with the right specialist is usually the best outcome and the one families resist most. A tutor with an adjacent specialism, with the limitation stated openly, works for some situations and not for a Higher Level push. A short wait is sometimes simply correct. What we will not do is place a generalist into a Higher Level slot and let the family find out at the January mock, which is the outcome a proximity-driven search produces most often. No competitor page in the researched set publishes a coverage limit at all.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-al-wasl.closingBody: Send the subject and the level, the school and the year group, one marked paper per subject you are worried about, and two evening windows that survive the return journey from Al Safa, Jumeirah or Umm Suqeim. The note afterwards will say which subject the first funded hour should go into, and sometimes it will say that three sessions on command terms across four subjects would do more than a year in any single one.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.tutorsIntro: The teachers below are matched to a Diploma subject and level rather than to a map pin. Tell us the course, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, and the evening that works once the bus reaches Arabian Ranches, and we will tell you who is genuinely free rather than who is geographically convenient.

intro.heading: Why a radius is the wrong filter for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: A near-me search does something very specific. It takes your location, draws a circle around it, and ranks what it finds inside the circle by a mixture of proximity, prominence and relevance. That works beautifully for a dentist, a locksmith or a padel court. It works badly for Higher Level Chemistry, because the thing that makes a Chemistry teacher useful has no spatial distribution at all. The circle is doing its job. It is simply answering a different question from the one you asked.

Run from Arabian Ranches, the circle contains Ranches Souk, the villa clusters, a primary school, and then a widening ring of apartment communities. What it does not contain, at any radius a car will tolerate at four in the afternoon, is a meaningful number of people who have taught the Diploma. Those teachers are employed by schools in Dubai Hills, Al Barsha, Nad Al Sheba and Umm Suqeim, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition work permit bars them from privately tutoring students enrolled at their own school.

So the comparison worth running is not Arabian Ranches against Arabian Ranches 2 or against Dubai Hills Estate. Communities on this belt share one travelling pool and one group of schools, and the answer comes out the same from every one of them. The comparison worth running is between the ways IB tuition is actually sold: an online match, a specialist agency, an international marketplace, a freelance tutor, a tuition-centre group class, and whatever the school already provides after hours. Those six differ enormously, and almost nobody sets them side by side.

This page does that, with the figures each model publishes, and it adds the number that decides most of it: cost per useful hour rather than cost per booked hour. A booked hour and a useful hour are different quantities once you account for a cancelled drive, a shared class or an hour spent on the wrong component. Several of the cheapest options in this market look expensive once that arithmetic is done, and one of the dearest looks reasonable.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; sending tutors to houses is a service we operate only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing for past papers, working and internal assessment drafts. That is a real trade and it is set out as one: you give up the person in the room, and you gain the entire pool of people who can teach the subject at the hour your child is free. For a Standard Level course the trade is close. For a Higher Level science in the second year it is not close at all.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.programmesIntro: The four IB programmes make very different demands on whoever teaches them, which is the practical reason a single nearby tutor rarely covers a family's whole need. Each entry below is written around the question this page is about: who can actually teach this, and does living nearby make any difference to it?

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, assessed by external papers plus internal components, with up to three further points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Teaching it well requires familiarity with the current subject guide, the command terms, the internal assessment criteria and the way each paper is structured. A subject degree is the entry requirement, not the qualification.
programmes.countryNote: This is where proximity fails hardest for families in Arabian Ranches. The Diploma teachers within reach are employed by schools in Dubai Hills, Nad Al Sheba and Al Barsha, and most of them are unavailable privately to their own students. The pool a radius returns is therefore the pool that happens to drive, which is a different thing from the pool that can teach.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, with no external examination before the final year. Teaching it requires reading the school's own task sheets and criterion clarifications, because there is no public syllabus code and no bank of past papers to work from. Framework knowledge matters as much as subject knowledge here.
programmes.countryNote: A nearby tutor is no more likely to have read an MYP criterion grid than a distant one, and a parent cannot tell from a profile. The useful screening question is what a task-specific clarification is and who writes it. Anyone who has taught the programme answers in a sentence; anyone who has not will talk about topics instead.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary years with no external examination, closing with the PYP Exhibition. Reporting is built around learner-profile attributes rather than marks. Useful support at this stage is reading fluency, number confidence and the habit of writing down a method, none of which needs a programme specialist so much as a good primary teacher.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one age at which a nearby tutor genuinely has an advantage, because a young child often works better with an adult in the room and the subject depth required is modest. It is also the age at which families in Arabian Ranches have the most local options, since primary provision inside these communities is strong.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses paired with a career-related study and a core of personal and professional skills, a reflective project, service learning and language development. Licensed by a small number of Dubai schools. Support needs are narrower than a full Diploma: usually the two or three Diploma courses plus the reflective project.
programmes.countryNote: Rare enough in Dubai that a local search will not return anyone who has taught it. If a student in Arabian Ranches is on this route, the honest route to support is to name the specific Diploma courses being taken and treat the rest as process coaching, rather than to look for a Career-related Programme specialist who probably is not there.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: The reason distance stops mattering is visible subject by subject. Below, each course is described by what it assesses and by how specialised the teaching has to be, which is the honest basis for deciding whether a strong local graduate will do or whether you need somebody who has marked the component.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at Standard Level, three at Higher, plus the exploration. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended structured investigation and is the component that most clearly separates a mathematician from somebody who has taught the course. Specialisation required: high, and higher again in the second year.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and heavy technology use, with its own exploration. The content is more approachable than Analysis and Approaches, but the exploration demands a genuine data set and a defensible method. Specialisation required: moderate at Standard Level, high at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Papers plus the scientific investigation. Uncertainty handling is the component where strong IGCSE students are most often caught, because nothing in IGCSE asked for it. Specialisation required: high; this is the course Dubai is shortest of at Higher Level in an evening slot.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Papers plus the investigation. Organic mechanisms, energetics and the precise level of detail each command term expects carry most of the marks that move. Specialisation required: high, and a graduate chemist without teaching experience will usually over-answer rather than under-answer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Papers plus the investigation, with statistics inside it. The subject punishes volume: a student who writes everything they know scores below one who answers the command term exactly. Specialisation required: moderate for content, high for the investigation and for examination technique.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Papers plus three internal assessment commentaries built from recent news articles, with word limits and diagram requirements. Higher Level adds quantitative work. Specialisation required: high for the commentaries, because the rubric is specific and rarely guessed correctly from first principles.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Papers plus an experimental study at Standard Level and additional Higher Level content. Students lose marks by describing studies rather than using them as evidence in an argument. Specialisation required: moderate, and a psychology graduate usually adapts quickly with the current guide in hand.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Papers plus fieldwork written up as internal assessment. Command terms and the use of case-study detail carry the marks; the fieldwork write-up has its own criteria and word limit. Specialisation required: moderate, rising sharply for the fieldwork component itself.

subjects.name: Language B and ab initio
subjects.description: Reading, listening, writing and an individual oral, with the oral weighted heavily. The teaching requirement is a near-native speaker who also knows the assessment format, which is a narrower pool than either qualification alone. Specialisation required: high, and the language is rarely available locally on demand.

subjects.description: Up to three points, supervised inside the school. A tutor may teach argument, structure and question framing, read the student's own drafts and give written feedback. A tutor may not produce any part of the work. Specialisation required: moderate, but the honesty boundary matters more here than expertise does.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.regionsTitle: The communities a near-me search includes, and what each one actually offers
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.regionsIntro: A radius drawn around Arabian Ranches sweeps through ten communities in roughly the order below. The notes describe what each one contributes to the pool a local search returns, which turns out to be less than the map suggests and is the reason this page argues for dropping the radius entirely.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Inside the circle: the villa clusters, Ranches Souk and JESS Arabian Ranches, which serves primary years. Secondary and Diploma students travel out. Local supply is good for primary support and almost absent for Higher Level courses.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Casa, Rosa and Palma. Adds households rather than teachers, which is the pattern across the whole belt. A tutor living here is a tutor who commutes to the same schools everyone else does, usually in the opposite direction at the relevant hour.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: The newest cluster, furthest from the Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim schools. A five-kilometre radius drawn here contains fewer Diploma-capable teachers than the same radius drawn almost anywhere else in the city.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: The one community in this comparison where proximity buys something real, because several schools sit inside or beside it. It is also where travelling tutors tend to live, which shows up as lower quoted in-home rates into Dubai Hills than into the outer communities.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Apartment communities with tuition centres operating locally. These add group capacity rather than one-to-one specialists, and a group class is a different purchase from a tutor, which the comparison table further down sets out properly.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills, DAMAC Hills 2 and Remraam
regions.note: The outer edge of any sensible radius. Travelling tutors frequently decline bookings here or price the return journey into the hour, which makes the effective rate the highest on the belt for the same teaching.

regions.name: Town Square and Mudon
regions.note: Townhouse communities with growing numbers of Year 10 and Year 11 students, so demand here is mostly IGCSE rather than Diploma. That changes which subjects are scarce in an evening slot and is worth saying rather than assuming.

regions.name: The Sustainable City and Al Barari
regions.note: Adjacent Dubailand communities sharing the same school runs, with Fairgreen International School inside The Sustainable City. Families here face the same arithmetic and reach the same conclusion, which is the point this page keeps arriving at.

schoolClusters.city: Where the Diploma teachers inside any radius actually work
schoolClusters.note: Schools offering the Diploma within reach of the Dubailand communities. Their staff are the pool a local search is implicitly hunting, and most of them cannot privately tutor their own students. Students we support attend schools in this group; nothing more is implied by naming them.

schoolClusters.city: The schools inside the radius itself
schoolClusters.note: What a five-kilometre circle around Arabian Ranches genuinely contains. Strong primary and all-through provision, and very little Diploma teaching, which is the asymmetry the rest of this page is built on. Licensed curricula are published by KHDA and change between years.

sections.heading: What a near-me search actually returns from Arabian Ranches
paragraphs: Open the search from a phone sitting in a villa off Al Qudra Road and look at what comes back. Agency landing pages with the community name inserted. A map pack of tuition centres, most of them in Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Al Barsha. A marketplace listing prices in dollars. Possibly a classified advert from an individual. What does not come back is a list of people who have taught the Diploma, because that is not an entity the search index holds and not a thing proximity predicts.

The honest reading is that the query is a proxy. Nobody actually wants the nearest tutor; they want a good tutor and they are using distance as a filter because it is the only filter available on a phone at nine in the evening. That filter has a hidden cost, and the cost is specific: it removes from consideration every teacher who cannot or will not drive to this community at the hour your child is free, and that is most of the people who can do the job.

What replaces the filter is not a slogan, it is three questions. Which course and level, exactly? What does the last marked piece of work show? And what evening actually exists once the bus has arrived? Answer those and the shortlist builds itself from capability rather than from geography. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service, so the trade is stated plainly here rather than discovered later. You give up the person in the room and you gain the whole pool.

sections.heading: The radius test: what each distance band actually contains
paragraphs: It is worth being concrete about the circle, because the intuition most families have about it is wrong. A radius that feels generous on a map is not generous in traffic, and a radius that would genuinely solve the problem is one no tutor will drive. Setting out the bands makes the trade visible instead of leaving it as a vague preference for somebody local.

Read the third column carefully. Inside the community the honest answer is primary support and early secondary homework help, which is a real and useful service. At fifteen kilometres you reach most Standard Level courses and a few Higher Level sciences. At thirty kilometres you are finally in the areas where Diploma teachers work, and you are also asking somebody to spend an hour each way in Dubai's worst traffic window to deliver a sixty-minute lesson. That is why the rate rises and why the booking gets declined.

The last row is the one this page argues for. Removing the radius entirely costs exactly one thing, which is the physical presence, and buys access to every teacher who can take the subject at the hour you need. For a Diploma student working on a screen anyway, with a draft in a shared document and past papers as PDFs, the loss is smaller than it sounds and the gain is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available. One caveat belongs with that, and it is an age caveat rather than a subject one: a nine-year-old who will not settle without an adult beside them is a genuine case for the person in the room, and no amount of arithmetic about pools and radii changes it.

sections.heading: Six ways IB tuition is sold in Dubai, compared on model rather than brand
paragraphs: Every provider in this market compares itself favourably to an unnamed alternative. That is useless to a parent, so the comparison below is between models rather than brands, and the only rates quoted are ones a provider has published about itself. Six models exist here: an online matching service, a specialist agency, an international marketplace, a freelance tutor, a tuition-centre group class, and the support the school already provides after hours.

Three columns decide most purchases and almost nobody publishes them. Whether the permit can be verified, because private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tuition work permit and a parent is entitled to see it. What happens if the match is wrong, because the answer ranges from the teacher being changed on request to starting the search again from nothing. And where the rate came from, because a figure without a source is an advertisement rather than information.

The school's own support deserves a mention it rarely gets on pages like this. It is already paid for, the teacher already knows the student, and in many Dubai schools it is genuinely good. The honest reasons it is not always enough are that it is group-based, that it runs on the school's timetable rather than your child's, and that a teacher cannot supervise their own student's internal assessment and also tutor it privately. Ask what exists before buying anything; it is the cheapest option on the table and the first one to check.

sections.heading: What the neighbour's recommendation is actually worth
paragraphs: On a belt of villa communities with active parent groups, most tutors are found by recommendation, and a recommendation carries real information. It tells you the person turns up, is pleasant with teenagers, communicates with parents and does not waste the hour. Those things are genuinely hard to find and genuinely worth knowing, and no profile page conveys them. Take the recommendation seriously on exactly those points.

What it does not transfer is subject fit. The tutor who was excellent with a Year 7 struggling with fractions is being recommended for a different job from the one you have, and the recommender cannot tell the difference because they never saw the harder job attempted. A Diploma parent hiring on a Year 7 recommendation is relying on evidence about punctuality to make a decision about Paper 3 technique. The two are unrelated, and the mismatch usually surfaces in February.

A simple protocol makes recommendations useful. Ask the recommender what year and what course their child was taking. Then ask the tutor one hard question about your course: how uncertainty is handled in a Physics investigation, what the three Economics commentaries require, how Paper 3 in Analysis and Approaches is structured. A specific answer confirms the fit; a general answer about building confidence tells you the recommendation was about something else. Nothing about this is rude, and a good tutor expects it, because the same question is being asked of them in every serious enquiry they receive.

sections.heading: Where a strong generalist stops working on a Diploma course
paragraphs: Hiring nearby usually means hiring a generalist, because the local pool is a pool of qualified adults rather than a pool of Diploma teachers. Generalists are not useless; a good one is worth a great deal in the first Diploma year when the problem is often confidence and missing IGCSE foundations. The question is where the generalist runs out, and the answer is component-specific rather than subject-specific, which is why the table below is organised that way.

The pattern across every row is the same. The generalist can do the academic content. What they cannot do is predict what the mark scheme rewards, because that knowledge comes from having marked the component or taught it through a full cycle. A chemist who writes a beautiful mechanism may still not know how much detail the command term deduce expects in that question, and the student loses marks while understanding the chemistry perfectly. That specific failure mode is invisible to a parent until a mock arrives.

The useful consequence is that you can buy both, in sequence. A generalist for foundations in the first year, when content is the problem, and a specialist for the final year, when technique is the problem. That sequencing costs less over two years than a specialist throughout and works better than a generalist throughout, and it is a decision you can only make if somebody has told you the difference exists. The switch point is usually the first internal assessment draft, because that is the first task where the mark depends on criteria rather than on getting the content right, and it arrives earlier in the Diploma than most families expect.

sections.heading: Cost per useful hour, which is not the advertised rate
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how this market advertises and they are a poor basis for comparison, because an hour booked is not an hour spent teaching your child the thing they need. Three leaks sit between the two: attention shared with other students, sessions lost because somebody had to drive, and hours spent on content when the problem was technique. Correct for those and the ranking of options changes, sometimes dramatically.

The published figures are the starting point. Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the homework-help end. Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table at AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist and AED 180 to 350 for an in-home visit, with independent providers quoting up to AED 500. BartyED at AED 650 for examiner-led work. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for exam-year specialist help.

Now apply the leaks. A group class of six costs little per hour and delivers a fraction of a teacher's attention, so it is cheap per hour and expensive per minute spent on your child's actual gap. An in-home booking out here loses a session now and then to traffic or a cancelled drive, which raises the effective rate by a third. A cheap hour spent revising content when the mock showed a timing problem has an effective cost of infinity, because it bought nothing. Every figure here belongs to the provider named, on the date its own page carried it; IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page and the first lesson is free so the teaching can be judged before any money moves.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the seven emirates
paragraphs: Families on this belt move, and they move between emirates more often than between communities. A transfer to Abu Dhabi, Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah changes the regulator, and the regulator changes what is inspected, who approves fees and curricula, and which professional-ethics rules apply to the teachers your child meets. None of the competitor pages researched for this project names more than one of these bodies, and ADEK appears in none of them.

Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there, and whose professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Sharjah's Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge both regulate private education and approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

For a tutoring arrangement the practical consequence is simple and it supports this page's whole argument. A teacher matched online and teaching over video does not change when the family moves emirate; the slot, the teacher and the plan carry over. An in-home arrangement does not survive a move to Abu Dhabi at all. For a household on a Dubai posting that may become an Abu Dhabi posting, that difference is worth more than a short drive, and it is the sort of thing nobody mentions until the move is already happening.

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor you found nearby
paragraphs: If you do hire locally, the checks are short and worth making. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with no fee and a stated two-working-day completion time on MoHRE's own service page. Because it costs nothing, there is no financial reason not to hold one. Ask to see it in the tutor's own name and ask when it expires.

Then ask the question most families skip: do you teach at my child's school? The permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules state the same for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff. The conflict is obvious once named, because the person coaching the work would also be the person marking it. A teacher from a different school gives you the same subject knowledge without the conflict.

Two more checks are worth a minute each. Ask who will actually teach the lessons, because on marketplaces and at some agencies the person who answers the enquiry is not the person who arrives. And ask what happens if the match is wrong, in writing, before any payment: the honest answers range from a teacher changed on request to nothing at all, and that difference is worth more than twenty dirhams an hour. Nobody should be promising a grade, and anyone offering to produce an internal assessment or an Extended Essay should end the conversation there.

sections.heading: What happens when near me has no answer
paragraphs: Sometimes the honest response to the search is that nobody suitable is available, and this is the part of the market that nobody publishes. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit or a fallback policy. Several route UAE parents to telephone numbers in other countries without saying where the teaching comes from, which is the same information withheld rather than given.

Our version is plain. Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Economics and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the courses this city is shortest of in an evening slot, and Language B in a less common language can be thinner still. When the right person is not free for the hour you need, the options are a different evening, a short wait for a slot to open, or a specialist outside the UAE whose location and time zone we state before you agree to anything. What we will not do is put a strong generalist in the slot and let the gap appear in a mock script in February.

Scheduling flexes in two directions that matter on this belt. Ramadan shortens the school day and families move an afternoon slot to after Iftar, which an online lesson absorbs without renegotiating a drive. And the long summer empties much of Arabian Ranches, so a student in London, Mumbai or Toronto in July keeps the same teacher and the same slot, time-converted. Both are ordinary requests here. Neither works when the arrangement depends on somebody's car reaching Al Qudra Road.

process.title: Say the course and the level before anything else
process.description: Higher Level Physics and Standard Level Physics are different staffing problems, and the level decides how much scheduling flexibility exists. Naming it first saves a round of messages and stops a shortlist forming around people who cannot take the course once the real requirement appears.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a description
process.description: The last marked assessment or internal assessment draft shows which component is losing marks, which is almost never the component a parent would have named. Two minutes with a script beats twenty minutes on a call, and it is the difference between a plan and a quotation.

process.title: Use the diagnostic hour before buying a block
process.description: One session that reads the work and reports what is wrong frequently changes the purchase. The result is often narrower and cheaper than the plan a family arrives with, and occasionally it is wider, which is worth knowing in November rather than in March.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson on its own terms
process.description: One lesson at no charge, booked before any payment and with no card details taken first. It runs as a working session with written feedback afterwards. Judge it on whether your child can now do something they could not do an hour earlier, not on how friendly the call felt.

process.title: Agree the replacement policy in writing
process.description: Before money moves, get the answer to one question: what happens if the match is wrong? Ours is that the teacher changes on request. Asking it of every provider you are considering will separate them faster than any comparison of hourly rates, including the table on this page.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the course, not on the map
whyPoints.description: The pool of people who can teach a Higher Level science in an evening slot is small and lives near the schools that employ them. Removing the radius is the only move that widens your choice, and it costs exactly one thing, which is stated on this page rather than hidden.

whyPoints.title: Models compared, brands left alone
whyPoints.description: The comparison here is between an online match, an agency, a marketplace, a freelance tutor, a centre class and the school's own support, using rates each provider published about itself. Comparing against an unnamed straw man is the industry habit and it tells a parent nothing.

whyPoints.title: Cost per useful hour, shown with its arithmetic
whyPoints.description: Shared attention, lost drives and misdirected hours all sit between a booked hour and a useful one. The table on this page does that arithmetic in dirhams. No ranking page researched for this project cites a source for a single AED figure, let alone adjusts one.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered properly
whyPoints.description: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE permit that is free and valid for two years, and a parent is entitled to see it. We also say which question matters more: whether the tutor teaches at your child's own school, which the permit's code of conduct prohibits.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits and the move between emirates
whyPoints.description: Where a course is thin, this page says so and sets out what is offered instead. And because the teaching is delivered over video, a family transferring from Dubai to Abu Dhabi or Sharjah keeps the teacher, the slot and the plan rather than starting again.

faqs.question: What does a near-me search for an IB tutor actually return in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Agency landing pages with the community name inserted, a map pack of tuition centres mostly in Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Al Barsha, a marketplace quoting US dollars, and sometimes a classified advert. What it does not return is a list of people who have taught the Diploma, because that is not something proximity predicts and not an entity the index holds. The search is doing its job; it is answering a radius question. The question you have is which teacher knows your child's course, and distance has no bearing on it.

faqs.question: How far would a tutor realistically travel to Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Indicatively, a travelling tutor based near the Al Barsha, Dubai Hills or Umm Suqeim schools reaches Arabian Ranches in twenty-five to forty minutes at four in the afternoon, which turns a sixty-minute lesson into a two-hour commitment and limits them to one booking that evening. Further out, into DAMAC Hills 2 or Remraam, the journey often runs to an hour and bookings get declined or priced to cover the return trip. That is why in-home quotes rise with distance and why the pool shrinks as the radius grows.

faqs.question: Is an agency, a marketplace or a freelance tutor better value in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They fail differently, which matters more than the price. A specialist agency publishes rates around AED 200 to 450 and above and usually offers some replacement policy, often only after a term. An international marketplace frequently quotes US dollars and rarely surfaces the tutor's permit to the parent. A freelance tutor can be excellent and cheap, with rates from AED 45 to 500 depending on level, and offers no fallback at all if the match is wrong. Ask all three the same two questions: can I see the permit, and what happens if this does not work.

faqs.question: A neighbour recommended a tutor. Is that a good enough reason to book?
faqs.answer: It is good evidence about reliability, manner and communication, which are genuinely hard to judge from a profile and worth a lot. It is not evidence about subject fit, because the recommendation almost certainly came from a different year group and a different course. Ask the recommender what year and subject their child was taking, then ask the tutor one hard question about your own course. A specific answer confirms the fit; a general answer about building confidence tells you the recommendation was about something else entirely.

faqs.question: How do I work out the real cost per useful hour of a tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Start with the published rate, then subtract the leaks. Divide by your child's share of the teacher's attention, so a group of six costs roughly six times its headline rate per minute spent on their actual gap. Add the sessions lost to traffic or a cancelled drive, which out here raises an in-home rate by around a third over a month. Then ask whether the hour is spent on the component that is losing marks. A cheap hour aimed at the wrong component has an effective cost of everything, because it buys nothing at all.

faqs.question: Can a strong graduate teach Higher Level Chemistry, or does it need a specialist?
faqs.answer: A strong graduate can teach the chemistry. What they usually cannot do is predict what the mark scheme rewards, because that comes from having marked the component or taught a full cycle. The classic failure is a beautifully drawn mechanism answered at the wrong level of detail for the command term, so the student understands the chemistry and still loses the marks. In the first Diploma year a generalist is often fine and cheaper. In the final year, on a Higher Level science, the technique is the problem and a specialist is the answer.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in each emirate of the UAE?
faqs.answer: Five bodies cover the country. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and both approve fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods as well as regulating. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. All five appear on the u.ae private schools page.

faqs.question: We may move to Abu Dhabi next year. Does the tutoring arrangement survive that?
faqs.answer: Yes, completely, which is one of the less obvious arguments for teaching over video. The teacher, the slot and the plan carry over to a new emirate without interruption, because nothing in the arrangement depends on an address. An in-home arrangement does not survive the move at all: you start the search again in a new city, with a new regulator, in the middle of a Diploma year. For families on postings that move within the UAE, that continuity is worth more than the convenience of somebody living nearby.

faqs.question: What replacement policy should I expect if the tutor is not right?
faqs.answer: Ask for it in writing before paying anything, because the honest answers vary enormously. A freelance tutor offers nothing; you simply start again. Agencies often change a tutor, sometimes only after a term has been paid for. Marketplaces generally leave you to rebook yourself. Our position is that the teacher changes on request, and the reason the question matters is that first matches fail for ordinary reasons: pace, manner, or a student who needed a different component addressed. A provider who cannot answer this plainly is telling you something.

faqs.question: Should I pay more per hour for an examiner-led tutor?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and for a narrow purpose. Published examiner-led rates reach AED 650 an hour, and the honest use for that money is two or three sessions on one stubborn component rather than a weekly arrangement. Two cautions. Current examiner status is hard for a parent to verify and should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. And a rate at that level buys experience of a component, not an outcome, since nobody can promise a grade in any subject at any price.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Motor City a better option than a one-to-one tutor?
faqs.answer: For covering content across a shared syllabus, often yes: the price per student is lower and a well-run group moves faster than a student working alone. For a specific weakness, an internal assessment or a timing problem, no, because the hour belongs to the group and your child's particular gap may never be reached. Count the drive each way as part of the cost. A centre operating with premises and staff needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a fair thing to ask to see before enrolling.

faqs.question: How quickly can a first IB lesson be arranged from Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level sciences, Business Management and most languages, often within the same week. For Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Economics or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in an evening slot, usually several days, because those are the courses this city is shortest of. We give a match time rather than a promise of availability, and if the slot you want cannot be filled we say so with the alternatives rather than holding the enquiry open while you wait.

faqs.question: Does the school's own after-hours support make a private tutor unnecessary?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is the first thing to check because it is already paid for and the teacher already knows your child. The honest limits are that it is usually group-based, that it runs on the school's timetable rather than your child's, and that a teacher supervising an internal assessment cannot also tutor it privately. Ask what is actually offered, for which subjects, and on which days. If it covers the gap, buy nothing. If it covers content but not technique, that tells you exactly what to buy.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking three providers for a quote?
faqs.answer: Four things, and the same four to each of them. The course and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. The school, so the timetable and assessment calendar are known. The last marked assessment or internal assessment draft, which is the single most informative item. And the evening window that genuinely exists once the bus has arrived. Then ask each provider the same three questions: who will teach, can I see the permit, and what happens if the match is wrong. The replies will separate them faster than the rates will.

faqs.question: How do I know the tutor is actually the person who will teach my child?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and ask before paying. On some marketplaces and at some agencies the person answering the enquiry is a coordinator, and the teacher is assigned afterwards from whoever is free. That is not dishonest in itself, but it means the profile you read may not be the person who arrives. The practical test is to insist the teacher runs the trial lesson. If a provider cannot name the teacher before the first session, you are buying a process rather than a person.

faqs.question: What if there is genuinely nobody available for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the real options rather than a holding reply. Those are a different evening, a short wait for a slot to open, or a specialist outside the UAE whose location and time zone we state before you agree to anything. Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Economics and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the thinnest, and a less common Language B thinner still. No competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why this answer exists in writing here.
