intro.heading: There is no Diploma campus in the community, so the commute sets the timetable
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches 2 sits past the original Ranches off Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street, spread across Palma, Rosa, Lila, Yasmin, Camelia, Casa and Reem, with Ranches Primary School inside it for the early years. Everything after primary happens somewhere else. For a Diploma student that means a daily journey out and back, and the journey rather than the subject is what decides whether a weekday session is possible at all. Parents search for a tutor near me and are actually asking whether the evening has room in it.

The honest answer begins with the clock rather than with teaching. A child leaving Camelia at seven in the morning for a campus in Al Barsha South is not reliably back in the community before half past four, and later once activities or a sports fixture are involved. From Dubai Hills Estate the return is quicker. From The Sustainable City it varies with the Al Qudra Road traffic. Those differences are small on paper and decisive in practice, because a session that starts half an hour too early simply does not happen.

The second part of the answer is about supply, and it is less comfortable. A search for a tutor near me returns people who live near you. In Arabian Ranches 2 that is a residential villa community a long way from where Dubai's Diploma teaching capacity actually lives. For a widely taught subject there may be someone within a few minutes. For Physics Higher Level, Economics Higher Level, or Theory of Knowledge support, the chance that the right specialist happens to live in Lila is close to nil, and a proximity filter removes them before you have read a single profile.

IB Gram resolves both problems the same way. Every lesson for a UAE family is delivered live over video, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to an address in Arabian Ranches 2 or anywhere else in the Emirates; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India, and that is stated on all forty-eight of our country pages. What a family here gets instead is a specialist chosen for the subject and a slot chosen for the commute, with nothing in between that can be delayed by traffic.

The rest of this page is practical. It sets out when the academic day ends at each campus Arabian Ranches 2 households use, when a child is realistically free, how a Diploma week fills up once creativity, activity, service and internal assessment deadlines are counted, what Ramadan and the shortened Friday do to a fixed slot, and how two children in two different year groups can be scheduled without a household losing every evening of the week.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Arabian Ranches 2 families ask about most, described by where they sit in the week rather than by syllabus content, because scheduling is what this page is about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most frequently requested Diploma subject in this community and the one that benefits most from a consistent weekly slot rather than an intensive block. Little and often works because fluency is built by repetition, so a fixed hour on the same evening each week outperforms three hours crammed before a test.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led, with coursework that lands in DP1 alongside the sciences. The scheduling implication is a cluster of internal assessment deadlines in the same term, which is the point at which a family usually needs one session a week rather than one a fortnight.

subjects.name: Physics HL and SL
subjects.description: A thin tutor market, which means a slot has to be arranged earlier than for mathematics and is harder to move once set. Physics work also benefits from longer sessions, since a past-paper question and its review rarely fit into forty-five minutes.

subjects.name: Chemistry HL and SL
subjects.description: Similar supply picture to physics and the same preference for longer sessions. Chemistry support tends to concentrate around the scientific investigation in DP1 and around organic mechanisms in DP2, so the intensity across the year is uneven rather than steady.

subjects.name: Biology HL and SL
subjects.description: Better supplied than physics and chemistry, so slots are easier to arrange at short notice. Biology revision is content-heavy, which makes it one of the subjects where a weekend session genuinely works as well as a weekday one.

subjects.name: Economics HL and SL
subjects.description: Internal assessment commentaries arrive in DP1 with firm school deadlines, and essay technique carries most of the marks. A fortnightly slot often suffices outside the commentary windows, with a short intensive block when they land.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Individual oral preparation and essay work dominate, both of which are better served by longer, less frequent sessions than by short weekly ones. Scheduling around the oral is worth planning a term ahead, because the school sets the window.

subjects.name: Business Management HL and SL
subjects.description: Case-study technique and command-term discipline carry the marks. Because the work is written rather than cumulative, this is one of the easier subjects to schedule flexibly around a fixture-heavy week.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay both have school deadlines that collide with subject internal assessments. Support here is best bought as two or three sessions near each deadline rather than weekly, which makes it easy to fit into an already full term.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Spread across DP1 and the start of DP2 with school-set interim deadlines. The supervisor stays the school's. Tutoring is confined to teaching the underlying subject, discussing method and giving feedback on drafts the student has written, scheduled around the school's own checkpoints.

subjects.name: MYP subject groups
subjects.description: Assessed against four criteria out of eight per subject. Task deadlines cluster, so MYP support is usually a short block around a specific criterion rather than a standing weekly slot, which makes it the easiest stage to schedule in a busy household.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and they occupy real timetable and homework hours. A family planning an evening schedule should count them, because they are frequently the homework that is still unfinished when a tutoring slot arrives.

sections.heading: What a proximity search actually returns from Arabian Ranches 2
paragraphs: Typed from a villa in Palma or Reem, a search for a tutor near me sorts by distance. That is the right behaviour for a dentist and the wrong behaviour for a Diploma subject specialist. Distance is a good proxy for convenience when the service is widely available and a poor one when it is scarce, and Diploma teaching in Dubai is scarce in exactly the subjects families most often need: Physics Higher Level, Chemistry Higher Level, Economics Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge, and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.

Arabian Ranches 2 compounds the problem because it is residential rather than central. It is a villa community off Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street with no campus inside it above primary level, which means the local population includes very few people who teach the Diploma for a living. A proximity search will return somebody, because it always does, and the question nobody asks is what was filtered out in order to produce that result.

What was filtered out is most of the relevant pool. The useful comparison is not between a tutor fifteen minutes away and a tutor forty minutes away; it is between a tutor who happens to live nearby and a specialist who teaches the exact course at the exact level. Once a lesson is delivered over video, distance stops carrying any information at all, and the only remaining variables are subject fit and whether the slot works with your commute.

The honest limits are worth stating alongside the argument. Online delivery requires a quiet room and a working connection, and it is less effective for a younger child who will not engage with a screen without an adult present. It also means IB Gram cannot offer what a family that specifically wants someone physically present is asking for: we do not send tutors to UAE addresses, and that service exists only in India. For a sixteen-year-old working on Paper 2 technique, none of those limits bite.

sections.heading: The school run from Arabian Ranches 2, campus by campus
paragraphs: Every scheduling decision in this community starts with one number: when the child is actually home. That is later than the end of the academic day, because the bus or the car has to cross Dubai in the late afternoon, and later again on any day carrying an activity or a fixture. Families consistently underestimate it by about thirty minutes, which is why a five o'clock slot booked in September is a half past five slot by October.

The table below sets out the pattern for the campuses Arabian Ranches 2 households use. Timings are indicative rather than official, they vary by year group, and every school publishes its own daily schedule, which is the document to use rather than this one. What the table is for is relative comparison: the gap between a JESS Arabian Ranches student and an Al Barsha South student is close to an hour, and that hour is the difference between a comfortable weekday slot and no weekday slot.

Two features of the local geography drive the differences. Al Khail Road and Hessa Street absorb the western Dubai evening traffic badly between five and seven, so campuses reached by either are the latest home. Al Qudra Road moves more freely, which makes The Sustainable City one of the more predictable journeys despite the distance. Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road is the least predictable of the three, and a schedule that depends on it should be built around the worst evening of the week rather than the average one.

The practical recommendation that follows is simple and it saves families a term of frustration. Set the slot thirty minutes later than feels necessary, and protect it rather than moving it. A session at six that always happens is worth more than a session at five that happens three weeks in four, because the weeks it does not happen are the weeks the student most needed it.

sections.heading: Where a session fits in a Diploma week
paragraphs: A Diploma student carries six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Written out as a list that looks manageable. Written out as a week it is not, because the three core commitments do not appear on a subject timetable and the activity component is frequently at the campus rather than in the community, which extends the day a second time on the days it falls.

The pattern that emerges in Arabian Ranches 2 households is consistent. Monday through Wednesday are the hardest evenings, because the commute, the homework and the activity commitments all land together and the student is tired from a day that started before seven. Thursday is the most reliable weekday evening in the week. The weekend offers the longest sessions and the least competition, which matters for subjects where a past paper and its review need ninety minutes rather than sixty.

The worked week below is a planning tool rather than a prescription, and no two households will match it. Its purpose is to make the competing commitments visible before a slot is chosen, because the common failure is to book the first available evening and then discover that it collides with the one fixture the student will not miss. Ten minutes spent mapping the week prevents a term of rescheduling.

One further point specific to the Diploma. Internal assessment deadlines cluster, and they cluster differently in DP1 and DP2. In DP1 the sciences, mathematics and Economics commentaries frequently land inside the same six weeks, alongside the Extended Essay interim deadline. A family that has mapped its week can absorb that by adding a short block rather than by abandoning the weekly slot, which is the response that actually works.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened Friday and the UAE calendar
paragraphs: The UAE school and working week has run Monday to Friday since 2022, with Friday shortened in the public sector and in many private schools. Dubai private schools set their own daily timings within the regulator's framework, so the only reliable source for your own child's Friday is the campus calendar. For tutoring the practical implication is that Friday is the least predictable slot in the week across this community and should not be the anchor of a schedule.

Ramadan reshapes the timetable more substantially. School hours are reduced across the month, the whole household rhythm shifts around Iftar, and the useful tutoring window moves from late afternoon to after the evening meal. Because Ramadan falls earlier in the Gregorian calendar each year, it moves through the academic year and will sit at different points relative to mock examinations in successive years, which is worth checking against the school calendar rather than assumed.

The arrangement that works is to rebuild the slot once rather than renegotiate it weekly. A family that agrees a post-Iftar time at the start of the month keeps the continuity, and a family that improvises loses two or three sessions to confusion. Tutors working with UAE households expect this and plan for it; a provider that cannot accommodate a post-Iftar slot is telling you something about how much UAE work it actually does.

Two other calendar features matter for a Diploma student here. School examination weeks are the point at which a tutoring slot should usually pause rather than intensify, because the student needs the evening to revise rather than to be taught. And the long summer break is when the cheapest and most useful work happens: a bridging block between MYP 5 and DP1, or between DP1 and DP2, costs the same per hour and achieves considerably more than the same hours bought in the spring.

sections.heading: Internal assessment deadlines against the school run
paragraphs: The Diploma deadlines that matter most to an Arabian Ranches 2 family are set by the school rather than by the IB. Each campus publishes its own internal calendar for science investigations, mathematics explorations, Economics commentaries, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, and the Extended Essay interim and final drafts. Those internal dates sit months ahead of anything the IB itself requires, and they are the dates a tutoring plan should be built from.

The IB's own examination and results dates should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator or read on ibo.org rather than taken from a tutoring page, because published dates can be revised and a revision plan built on a wrong date is worse than one with no dates at all. What can be said with confidence is the structure: Dubai schools sit the May session, entries and internal deadlines precede it by many months, and the enquiry-upon-results process afterwards runs through the school rather than through a family directly.

For the British board sitting at 16, the published dates illustrate how far ahead deadlines sit. Count a Cambridge June series backwards from the papers: the exam window falls across May and June, forecast grades and coursework marks are collected in the weeks before it, and final entries close in the spring, with the exact day on the centre's statement of entry. A candidate not entered by then is waiting for the November series, and those two windows are the only ones open to someone sitting in the UAE. Pearson Edexcel's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026.

The scheduling consequence for this community is specific. Internal deadlines arrive in clusters, and a student who is commuting ninety minutes a day has fewer spare evenings in which to absorb a cluster than a student living beside their campus. The response that works is to put the school's internal calendar on the wall in September, mark the clusters, and plan short blocks into them in advance rather than reacting when three drafts are due in the same fortnight.

sections.heading: Two children, two year groups, one evening
paragraphs: A large share of Arabian Ranches 2 households have more than one child in school, frequently at different campuses with different end times. The scheduling problem that produces is not about tutoring at all; it is about an evening that already contains two commutes, two sets of homework and at least one activity. Adding two tutoring sessions to the same evening is the most common reason a family abandons both within a month.

The arrangement that holds separates them properly. The younger child takes the earlier slot, often earlier in the week as well, because primary and lower secondary days end sooner and a nine-year-old cannot work usefully at seven in the evening. The Diploma student takes a later slot after the longer commute, on a different day. Each child keeps their own tutor, because a Year 5 reading problem and a Physics Higher Level problem are not the same job and sharing a tutor serves neither.

Where siblings genuinely are doing the same thing, a shared session can work and costs less. Two children in the same MYP year group, in the same subject group, with the same weak criterion, is a real case and it is worth asking about. Two children two years apart in the same subject is not, however convenient it looks on the calendar, because the material diverges faster than families expect and one of the two always ends up watching.

The practical mechanism is one shared household calendar and one point of contact rather than two separate arrangements that collide. When a fixture moves or a deadline cluster arrives, a family should be able to make one request rather than two, and the two tutors should know about each other's slots so that a rescheduled session does not land on the sibling's evening. That is an administrative point rather than an academic one, and it is the thing that makes a two-child schedule survive a term.

sections.heading: What it costs, and what a parent can check for nothing
paragraphs: Price belongs on this page only briefly, because the scheduling question is the one this community actually asks, but the published market is worth stating. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 research puts qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, TutorChase lists AED 270, and BartyED's examiner-led tier is AED 650. At the budget end EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52.

In-home visits across Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with monthly packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online ones. Those figures are the publishers' own and they make the scheduling point better than the cost point: a visiting tutor who has to reach Arabian Ranches 2 by five o'clock is charging for the journey and is also constrained by it, which is why in-home slots in this community are so often offered at weekends.

Two checks cost nothing and are worth more than most price comparison. The first is the permit: private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services system under Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Ask whether a tutor holds one. No schedule of fines is published, so any penalty figure quoted at you is invented.

The second free check is the school. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes an inspection report for every private school in the emirate. Those reports are specific by subject and phase and they are free to read. For completeness: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, claims no partnership with any school, and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

process.title: Tell us the campus, not just the subject
process.description: The campus decides the commute and the commute decides the slot. A first message naming the school, the year group, the subject and the level lets a tutor be matched to the subject and a time to be matched to your actual evening, instead of a default slot being offered that will not survive October.

process.title: Map the week before choosing the day
process.description: Write down the activity commitments, the fixtures and the days the student is home latest. Thursday and the weekend are the most reliable windows in this community; Monday and Tuesday are the least. Ten minutes on this prevents a term of rescheduling and is the step families most often skip.

process.title: We match the specialist, then fit the time
process.description: Subject fit comes first and timing second, because a tutor who teaches the exact course at the exact level is scarcer than a free hour. If nobody suitable is free in your window we say so and offer a named alternative time or start date rather than filling the slot with a generalist.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One full session before anything is paid, at the time you intend to use, so the slot itself gets tested as well as the tutor. No card details are needed. If the match or the timing is wrong, say so and we change one or both; nothing is owed either way.

process.title: Protect the slot, and rebuild it once for Ramadan
process.description: A slot that holds is worth more than a slot that is theoretically earlier. We agree the term's day and time, pause it through school examination weeks by arrangement, and rebuild it once around Iftar for Ramadan rather than renegotiating it week by week.

process.title: Review against the deadline calendar
process.description: At the halfway point you get a short written note on progress and on what the next deadline cluster requires. That is usually the moment to add a short block for an internal assessment or to step the weekly slot down, and we will say which rather than leaving it to drift.

whyPoints.title: The slot is set from your commute
whyPoints.description: There is no Diploma campus inside Arabian Ranches 2, so every student here is home later than a timetable suggests. We set the start time from the campus and the approach road rather than offering a standard evening slot, because a session booked thirty minutes too early quietly stops happening.

whyPoints.title: Specialist first, distance never
whyPoints.description: A proximity search filters out most of Dubai's Diploma teaching capacity before you see a profile, and in Physics or Economics at Higher Level it filters out nearly all of it. Over video, distance carries no information, so the match is made on the course and the level alone.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan and Friday handled properly
whyPoints.description: The UAE week runs Monday to Friday with Friday shortened at many schools, and Ramadan moves the usable window to after Iftar. We rebuild the slot once for the month rather than improvising weekly, which is the difference between keeping continuity and losing three sessions.

whyPoints.title: Deadline clusters planned in advance
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment deadlines arrive several at once, set by your child's own school rather than by the IB. We work from the school's internal calendar, add short blocks into the clusters, and keep the weekly slot intact instead of abandoning it when three drafts fall in a fortnight.

faqs.question: What time does the school day actually end for Arabian Ranches 2 children?
faqs.answer: The academic day ends in the mid afternoon at most Dubai campuses, but the time that matters is when a child is home, which is later. From JESS Arabian Ranches next door that can be mid afternoon. From The Sustainable City or Dubai Hills Estate it is late afternoon. From Al Barsha South or Emirates Hills it is early evening, and later again on a day carrying an activity or a fixture. Each school publishes its own daily timings, and that document rather than any general estimate is the one to plan from.

faqs.question: When can an IB session realistically start on a weekday in Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: For a student at JESS Arabian Ranches, half past four is realistic because the commute is short. From Motor City or The Sustainable City, five o'clock. From Dubai Hills Estate or The Meadows, half past five. From Emirates Hills or Al Barsha South, six. The advice families most often ignore and most often need is to book the slot thirty minutes later than feels necessary, because a session that always happens is worth considerably more than an earlier one that happens three weeks in four.

faqs.question: Which schools do Arabian Ranches 2 families use once their child reaches DP1?
faqs.answer: Most commonly JESS Arabian Ranches next door, which runs the English National Curriculum to IGCSE and then the IB Diploma, or one of the IB campuses a drive out: GEMS International School Al Khail in Dubai Hills Estate, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Emirates International School Meadows, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills or Nord Anglia International School Dubai. Each publishes its own timings and internal deadline calendar. Check the current KHDA inspection report for any campus you are considering rather than relying on a summary.

faqs.question: Is there any IB Diploma school inside Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: No. Ranches Primary School sits inside the community for the early years on the British curriculum, and everything above primary happens elsewhere. That single fact shapes every scheduling decision a Diploma family here makes, because it means a daily journey out and back and a later realistic session start than in a community with a campus inside it. The nearest Diploma provision is JESS Arabian Ranches in the original Ranches community next door.

faqs.question: How long is the school bus run from Arabian Ranches 2 to an IB campus?
faqs.answer: It depends on the campus and the road rather than the distance. Al Qudra Road towards The Sustainable City moves fairly predictably. Al Khail Road towards Dubai Hills Estate and Hessa Street towards Al Barsha South both carry heavy evening traffic between five and seven. Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road is the least predictable of the three. A bus route also makes several stops, so it is usually slower than a car on the same journey. Ask the school for its own route timings for your community.

faqs.question: Does searching for an IB tutor near me in Arabian Ranches 2 find anyone qualified?
faqs.answer: It will find somebody, because a proximity search always returns a result. Whether that person teaches your child's course at your child's level is a separate question, and in a residential villa community with no campus above primary level the odds are poor for scarce subjects such as Physics or Economics at Higher Level. The useful comparison is not nearby against far away; it is a neighbour against a specialist. Over live video the distance stops mattering and only subject fit and timing remain.

faqs.question: Should an IB session happen before or after evening sport and activities?
faqs.answer: After, almost always, and on a day that carries neither if possible. A student arriving at a session straight from a fixture is not in a state to work on Paper 2 technique, and one who has to leave halfway through loses the review that makes the session useful. In this community Thursday evening and the weekend are the most reliable windows precisely because activity commitments cluster earlier in the week. Map the commitments before choosing the day rather than after.

faqs.question: How do weekend sessions work for Arabian Ranches 2 students?
faqs.answer: They are the most reliable slots available here, because no commute and usually no activity is competing with them. They also allow a longer format, ninety minutes or more, which suits physics, chemistry and essay subjects where a past paper and its review do not fit inside an hour. Saturday tends to be better for past-paper work and Sunday for essay drafting and review before the week begins. Many Diploma families here run one weekday slot and one weekend block during examination terms.

faqs.question: Can IB lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the arrangement we recommend rather than an exception we tolerate. School hours are reduced during Ramadan and the household rhythm shifts around Iftar, so the usable tutoring window moves to after the evening meal. The approach that works is to rebuild the slot once at the start of the month and hold it, rather than renegotiating week by week, which is how families lose two or three sessions to confusion. Check your campus calendar for its reduced timings.

faqs.question: How many weekday evenings should a DP1 student give to tutoring?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, held consistently. A Diploma student already carries six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service, and in this community they also carry a daily commute. Two weekday evenings becomes sensible only where a whole subject is missing rather than drifting. Where more intensity is needed, a short block around a deadline cluster or a longer weekend session is usually better than a second weekday evening, because the student still has to do their own work.

faqs.question: What happens to the schedule during Dubai school exam weeks?
faqs.answer: The slot should usually pause rather than intensify. During a school examination week a student needs the evening to revise in their own way rather than to be taught something new, and a session that arrives in the middle of it competes with the thing it is supposed to support. The exception is a single review session on a specific paper the student has just sat and will sit again in the real series. Agree the pause in advance with the tutor rather than cancelling at short notice.

faqs.question: Does the Friday half-day change when an IB session can be booked?
faqs.answer: It can, and that is exactly why Friday is a poor anchor for a weekly slot. The UAE week has run Monday to Friday since 2022 with Friday shortened in the public sector and at many private schools, but Dubai private schools set their own daily timings, so Friday varies between campuses and sometimes between year groups at the same campus. Confirm your own school's Friday schedule, and if a Friday slot is wanted, treat it as a second session rather than the main one.

faqs.question: How do we fit IA deadlines around the Arabian Ranches 2 school run?
faqs.answer: By planning the clusters rather than reacting to them. Internal assessment deadlines are set by your child's school, not by the IB, and they arrive several at once, often with an Extended Essay interim deadline alongside. Put the school's internal calendar up in September, mark the weeks where three things are due, and plan a short block into each cluster in advance. A student commuting ninety minutes a day has fewer spare evenings to absorb a cluster than one living beside their campus.

faqs.question: Can a sibling in MYP share the same weekly slot pattern?
faqs.answer: Share the pattern, not the session. A Middle Years Programme student finishes school earlier than a Diploma sibling and works better earlier in the evening, so the sensible arrangement is an earlier slot on a different day with a different tutor matched to the subject group and criterion. Shared sessions only make sense where two children are in the same year group, the same subject group and have the same weakness. The scheduling, though, should be handled as one household calendar so no evening carries both.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost for a family in Arabian Ranches 2?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai research, with IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, Unitors quoting IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED's examiner tier at AED 650. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 because the drive is inside the price, which is also why in-home slots in this community are so often weekend-only. Those are other companies' rates; IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page.

intro.heading: Why "near me" is the wrong filter for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in Arabian Ranches 3 is a search with a hidden assumption inside it: that the right tutor is a person who can reach your villa. Arabian Ranches 3 sits on the far side of Al Qudra Road, in the Dubailand belt, with Emirates Road on one flank and the Dubai-Al Ain corridor on the other. Draw a twenty-minute drive radius around it in the evening and you capture a few thousand households, a handful of tuition centres on Hessa Street and whoever happens to be free between six and eight. Draw the same circle around a Diploma syllabus instead and you capture a different, much more useful set of people.

The Diploma is not one qualification. It is six courses, each with its own assessment grid, sat at Standard or Higher Level, plus three core components that are marked against published criteria. A tutor who is strong on Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is usually not the same person who can take apart a Chemistry internal assessment or coach a Theory of Knowledge exhibition. Hiring by postcode means hiring whoever is nearest and hoping the subject match follows. It rarely does, and the cost of the mismatch is a term.

This page is written from the syllabus rather than the map. It sets out what the Diploma actually assesses, which command terms carry which marking expectations, where students in this part of Dubai lose marks in each subject group, how the internal assessment criteria are weighted letter by letter, and how past papers should be worked so that they teach something rather than confirm what a student already knows. It also states the market price for tuition in the Dubailand villa communities in AED, with the source of each band.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one to one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a recording your child can rewatch before a test. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches 3 or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate limit, not an apology. It is the reason a family on this side of Al Qudra Road can book a Physics Higher Level specialist for a Tuesday at seven rather than settling for a generalist who lives in Motor City.

What follows is long because the Diploma is detailed and because the pages currently ranking for this search are not. The best of them runs to roughly 2,300 words and carries no data table at all. If you only have five minutes, read the command-terms table, the internal assessment table and the AED rate table, then skip to the fourteen questions at the end.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.programmesIntro: Children in Arabian Ranches 3 sit in three different IB stages depending on which Dubailand or Nad Al Sheba school the family chose, and the tutoring each stage needs is not the same work. Here is what each stage assesses and what it means for a household out here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry and finishes with the Grade 5 Exhibition, in which a child plans, researches and presents an inquiry of their own. Tutoring at this stage is about securing number fluency, reading stamina and written structure, because none of these are examined and a gap can sit unnoticed for years.
programmes.countryNote: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City runs the IB continuum from primary upwards and is the closest full-continuum option to Arabian Ranches 3. Several nearby schools, including Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, are primary-only, so an Arabian Ranches 3 family often changes campus at Year 6 anyway. Fixing a maths gap in Year 5 is far cheaper than discovering it in MYP 4.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks every subject against four criteria, A to D, each out of 8, with published descriptors. Grades are converted to a 1-7 scale by boundaries the school sets within IB guidance. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project, assessed on planning, action and reflection. Students who have never been shown the criteria tend to write good work that scores in the middle band.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma step is where Arabian Ranches 3 parents most often call. MYP assessment rewards process and reflection; the Diploma rewards precision against a mark scheme. A student used to criterion-based feedback meets Paper 1 timing for the first time in DP1 and the grade drops a band before Christmas. Eight weeks of structured past-paper work in the summer between closes most of that gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, graded 1-7 for a maximum of 42, plus up to 3 points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. The core adds a 4,000-word Extended Essay, a 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay with a three-object exhibition, and CAS. Most subjects also carry an internal assessment worth around a fifth of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter candidates for the May session, so a DP2 student in Arabian Ranches 3 is working to internal coursework deadlines set by their own coordinator months before the papers. The IB does not publish its timetable through any channel we can verify automatically, so confirm every date with your child's DP coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including ours.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and suits a student who wants Diploma-level academic subjects alongside an applied qualification. The DP courses inside it are examined exactly as they are in the full Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubailand schools run the CP, so an Arabian Ranches 3 family considering it is usually looking further afield or at the DP courses in isolation. Where a student takes two DP subjects inside a CP, the tutoring is identical to full Diploma tutoring for those subjects: same papers, same weightings, same internal assessment criteria, same command terms.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects Arabian Ranches 3 households request most, with what each one actually assesses and the point in it where marks reliably disappear. The description is the diagnostic; it is what a first session is spent establishing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, calculus. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage happens. Marks go on unjustified steps, missing 'hence' links and algebra done in the head. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and harder integration.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same five topic headings with a modelling and technology emphasis, and a graphic display calculator permitted in every paper. Students lose marks by quoting calculator output without the statistical reasoning behind it, misreading regression context and skipping units. HL carries matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical testing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-analysis section; Paper 2 is short and extended response. Marks go on describing a graph instead of explaining the physics behind it, on uncertainty treatment, and on fields and circular motion. HL extends every theme rather than adding separate options.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised around structure and reactivity, with a data booklet available in the examination that many students never learn to use at speed. Losses cluster in organic mechanisms drawn without curly arrows, energetics sign conventions and equilibrium explanations that restate Le Chatelier rather than applying it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led, with heavy demand on precise terminology and on reading unfamiliar data. Students who revise by rereading notes stall at a 4 or 5. The gain comes from writing answers to the command term and from practising the graph and table questions that carry a disproportionate share of Paper 2 marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the grade more than content recall. Axes mislabelled, no shift arrow, no reference to the diagram in the prose: three marks gone before the argument starts. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, each with a tight word allowance, and HL adds quantitative policy work.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided textual analysis of unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works. Students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing, and by writing about theme while ignoring how the text is built. The individual oral needs a global issue narrow enough to argue in ten minutes.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-led: students must apply named frameworks to a case rather than describe them. Marks go on generic answers that would fit any company and on ignoring the stimulus material. HL adds depth in operations and a business research project with a strict word limit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects answering an internal assessment prompt. The common failure is writing about the topic instead of about knowledge. Coaching consists of question framing, counter-argument structure and object selection, with the writing left entirely to the student.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in one subject, supervised by a teacher at school. Marks go on a question too broad to answer, a method section that cannot be replicated and an engagement record completed the week before submission. Support means question narrowing, source criticism and structural feedback only.

sections.heading: The Diploma as a tutor reads it: six groups, two levels, one core
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate takes one subject from each of six groups — studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the arts, with a second subject from groups one to five permitted instead of an art. Three are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard. Each is graded 1 to 7, giving a maximum of 42 subject points, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix contributes up to 3 more for a ceiling of 45.

The level difference is content, not polish. An SL course is built on 150 teaching hours and an HL course on 240. Those ninety extra hours are additional syllabus, longer papers and, in several subjects, an extra paper. A parent who assumes HL means the same material taught harder will misread why their child is suddenly behind: the HL class has simply covered things the SL class never meets. This is the single most common misunderstanding in a first consultation from this community.

The core is where points are quietly won and lost. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words of independent research in one subject with a named supervisor at school. Theory of Knowledge is a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. Both are marked against published criteria, both are submitted to internal deadlines set by your child's coordinator, and neither may be written by anyone other than the student. A tutor's job on the core is to interrogate the question and the method, then hand the writing back.

sections.heading: Command terms: the part of the mark scheme nobody is taught
paragraphs: Every IB question opens with a command term, and every command term has an assessment objective attached to it. A student who answers 'explain' with a description has written something true and scored nothing. This is the cheapest grade in the Diploma to recover, because it costs no new content: it is a reading habit, and eight weeks of deliberate practice fixes it. It is also almost never taught explicitly, because class time goes on syllabus coverage.

The diagnosis is quick. Take a marked Paper 2 and highlight the command term in each question the student lost marks on. The pattern is usually one of two things: the student answered a lower-order term when a higher-order one was asked, or they answered the right term but stopped before the mark scheme did. 'Evaluate' without a judgement, 'justify' without a reason, 'compare' with two separate paragraphs and no point of contact — each of these is a specific, repeatable loss.

The table below lists the terms that cause the most damage in science, maths and individuals-and-societies papers, with what the mark scheme expects and the loss that follows when a student misreads it. Work through it with your child's own script in front of you, question by question, rather than reading it as a reference list. The terms are defined in the subject guides on ibo.org; read them there for the exact wording for your subject, because the emphasis shifts slightly between guides and a term that means one thing in Biology can carry a narrower expectation in Economics.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing, subject by subject
paragraphs: Grades do not fall evenly across a paper. In almost every Diploma subject the losses concentrate in two or three identifiable places, and a tutor who knows where they are can diagnose a script in a single session. This is the difference between a specialist and a capable graduate: both can do the maths, but only one can look at a lost mark and name the habit that caused it.

In Mathematics Analysis and Approaches the non-calculator paper is the hinge. Students who have done all their practice with a graphic display calculator cannot manipulate surds and logarithms at speed, and they lose method marks for steps done mentally. In Physics the loss is uncertainty and graph interpretation: a candidate who can calculate a gradient but cannot say what it represents forfeits the explanation marks that carry the band. In Chemistry it is organic mechanisms and the sign conventions in energetics.

In the humanities the pattern inverts: content is rarely the problem, structure is. Economics candidates lose marks on diagrams that are drawn but never referenced in the prose. English candidates write about what a text says instead of how it works. Business Management candidates apply a framework in the abstract rather than to the stimulus company. None of these is a knowledge gap, which is why rereading notes does not move the grade and marked past-paper work does. A single session spent reading two marked scripts against the published scheme will usually identify every one of them by name, and that list is what the first month of tutoring should be built around.

sections.heading: Internal assessment, criterion by criterion and mark by mark
paragraphs: Most Diploma subjects carry an internal assessment worth around a fifth of the final grade, marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Because it is coursework, it is the most controllable component on the whole programme — and because it is coursework, it is where academic-honesty rules bite hardest. A student who knows the criterion letters and their mark allocations is working to a visible target. One who does not is guessing.

The criteria are not interchangeable between subjects. A Mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with the mathematics itself carrying the largest share and personal engagement and reflection carrying three marks each. The science investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each, which means evaluation is worth exactly as much as data analysis — a distribution that surprises most students, who spend their time on the practical and their last evening on the evaluation.

A tutor's role here is bounded and worth stating plainly. The tutor may help narrow a research question, question a method, point to a criterion the draft does not yet address and explain what the descriptor means. The tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply content. IB Gram does not produce assessed work for students, and a tutor who offers to is putting the candidate at risk of a malpractice finding that no grade is worth. Ask any tutor you hire, here or elsewhere, where they draw that line before the first session.

sections.heading: Past papers, worked so that they teach instead of confirm
paragraphs: Most students use past papers as a thermometer. They sit one, score what they always score, feel briefly worse and move on. Used properly a past paper is the single most efficient teaching tool in the Diploma, and the difference is entirely in the order of operations. Read the mark scheme for a question before answering it, not after. A student who has seen how the marks are allocated writes a different answer, and the habit transfers to questions they have never seen.

The second change is to stop sitting whole papers for most of the term. Whole papers measure; question sets teach. Pick the six questions on one topic across six sessions, work them under time, then mark them against the scheme and write one line in an error log naming the cause of each lost mark. After four weeks that log, not the scores, is the tutoring plan. Nearly every student's log collapses into three or four recurring causes, and those are fixable in a term.

Sourcing matters too, and here the honest answer is a limit. IB Gram does not host or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those are the boards' copyright and your child's school holds the licensed access. Ask the subject teacher or the DP coordinator for the papers, work from the official subject guides on ibo.org, and treat any website offering a free library of recent IB papers with real caution.

You send the subject, the level, the school and the last marked piece of work; we read the script before the call rather than after it; a specialist is proposed with their subject background stated; a trial session runs before a block is booked. Nothing in that sequence requires anybody to drive anywhere, which is why a 7pm Tuesday slot is actually a 7pm Tuesday slot.

Sometimes the answer is that nobody suitable is free. Niche Higher Level combinations — Further Mathematics, a less commonly taught group 2 language, Music, some Design Technology work — have thin coverage inside the UAE, and when they do we say so rather than placing a generalist and hoping. The alternative we offer is a specialist outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, disclosed in advance, with the time-zone implication stated before you commit. One legal point worth knowing before you hire anyone, in or out of this community. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted by MoHRE work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. faqs.question: Why does hiring an IB tutor by distance from our villa go wrong so often?
faqs.answer: Because distance selects for availability rather than subject. The Diploma is six separate courses with six separate mark schemes, and the person who can diagnose a lost mark in Chemistry Higher Level is usually not the person who can do it in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. A twenty-minute evening radius around Arabian Ranches 3 contains a few thousand households and no subject panel. faqs.question: What is the real difference between a Standard Level and a Higher Level course?
faqs.answer: Content, and the hours to deliver it. An SL course is built on 150 teaching hours, an HL course on 240. Those extra ninety hours are additional syllabus rather than the same material taught more intensively, and in several subjects they bring an extra paper: Mathematics adds Paper 3, English Language and Literature adds the HL essay. A student struggling in an HL class is often not behind on the shared content at all — they are meeting syllabus their SL classmates never see.

faqs.question: How many points does my child actually need, and where do the last three come from?
faqs.answer: Six subjects graded 1 to 7 give a maximum of 42 points. The final three come from a matrix combining the Extended Essay grade with the Theory of Knowledge grade, for a ceiling of 45. The Diploma is awarded at 24 points subject to conditions on individual grades and on completing the core, which your child's coordinator will confirm. University offers in the UAE and abroad are quoted in total points with subject-specific requirements attached, so check the exact HL grades a target course asks for before fixing a revision plan.

faqs.question: My child understands the content but keeps losing marks. What is usually causing that?
faqs.answer: Almost always the command term. Every IB question opens with one, each has an assessment objective behind it, and answering 'explain' with a description scores nothing even when everything written is true. Take a marked Paper 2, highlight the command term on every question that lost marks, and the pattern appears within ten minutes. It is the cheapest recovery in the Diploma because it needs no new content — just deliberate practice against the definitions published in the subject guides.

faqs.question: How are the marks split inside a science internal assessment?
faqs.answer: The scientific investigation in Physics, Chemistry and Biology is worth 20% of the final grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Evaluation therefore carries exactly as much weight as data analysis, which surprises most students, because the practical work gets weeks and the evaluation gets one evening. Knowing the split changes how the time is spent, and that is usually worth more than any single piece of subject teaching.

faqs.question: Exactly what can a tutor do on a Mathematics exploration without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor can test whether the topic is broad enough to sustain course-level mathematics, check that the mathematics used matches the level, explain what each criterion descriptor means, and mark a draft against those descriptors so the student knows which criterion is weak. A tutor cannot write any part of it, cannot rewrite passages, cannot edit it to completion and cannot supply the mathematics. The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and the writing must be the student's own throughout.

faqs.question: Who should supply the IB past papers and mark schemes our child practises on?
faqs.answer: From your child's school. Schools hold licensed access to IB, Cambridge and Pearson material, and the DP coordinator or subject teacher can release papers and mark schemes appropriately. IB Gram does not host, supply or distribute papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, because those are the boards' copyright. Use the official subject guides on ibo.org for syllabus detail, and treat any site offering a free library of recent IB papers with real caution — much of that material is hosted without permission.

faqs.question: What time can lessons realistically start for a child bussed home to this community?
faqs.answer: For most families here, 6.30pm or later. A child travelling back from Nad Al Sheba, The Villa or Al Barsha South is not home, changed and fed before six, and a session that starts while a student is still eating teaches very little. Because lessons run over video there is no additional travel to absorb at either end, so a 6.30pm start is a 6.30pm start. Weekend morning slots work well for internal assessment and Extended Essay sessions, which need longer blocks.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and how do we check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is permitted through a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, the MoHRE service page lists a two-working-day completion time, and applications go through the MoHRE app, website or e-services. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it; those operating without one face penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tuition in DP1 or should we wait until the final year?
faqs.answer: DP1 is where the cheap gains are. The content taught in the first year reappears in the final papers, the internal assessment is usually started in DP1, and the habits that cost marks — mental algebra, unreferenced diagrams, uncertainty ignored — are easier to change before they have been rehearsed for eighteen months. Families who start in the final term of DP2 are paying for a rescue rather than a build, and the realistic target narrows accordingly. No tutor can promise a particular outcome at any point in the programme.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two of my child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches with Physics is a common and genuine pairing, because the mathematical technique overlaps. Chemistry with Biology is less often a real pairing than it looks, because the extended-response demands differ. We would rather tell you that two specialists are needed than place one tutor across two subjects for convenience, and the subject background of each proposed tutor is stated so you can judge the overlap yourself.

No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to a foreign number without saying where the tutor sits.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still have to be studied alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Support for these subjects is a separate stream from Diploma subject tuition, and material must follow the approved content.

intro.heading: The question behind the search is about supply, not distance
paragraphs: A parent does not really want a tutor who lives nearby. They want somebody who knows what the mark scheme awards in their child's subject, at their child's level, and who is free at a time their child is awake. Proximity got into the search because that is the word Google understands, and because it is the only one of those three things a map can measure.

Bluewaters Island makes the gap between the question and the search unusually visible. It is a small residential community on reclaimed land off JBR, reached by one road bridge and a pedestrian link, with no school on it. Every child commutes. So there is no local school staff room from which a nearby IB teacher could plausibly emerge, and the tutors a map will return are people who live within a short drive of the bridge rather than people who teach the Diploma.

The honest supply picture across Dubai is worth stating plainly, because nobody in this market does. KHDA figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. Seven new private schools arrive for 2026-27, three of them IB, adding 16,846 places. The IB is a minority provision in a very large market, and Diploma teaching at Higher Level in a specific subject is a minority within that minority.

Which produces the result this page exists to explain. Standard Level Mathematics is findable almost anywhere. Chemistry at Higher Level with current knowledge of the scientific investigation criteria, available at half past five on a Tuesday, is not, and no amount of local searching changes it. The pool is small because the teaching population is small, not because Bluewaters is awkward.

What we do about that is take geography out of the equation. IB Gram teaches every UAE student one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. That removes the filter that has nothing to do with the grade and leaves the one that does, which is whether the person knows the component your child is being marked on.

It does not remove scarcity, and we will not pretend otherwise. Some subject and slot combinations are genuinely unavailable for days at a time. This page sets out which ones, what we do instead, and four questions you can use to test any tutor, ours included, in the first twenty minutes of a trial lesson. Reviewed October 2026, with every figure attributed to the source it came from rather than asserted.

sections.heading: The honest answer about local IB supply
paragraphs: There are IB tutors who could reach Bluewaters Island. There are far fewer who teach the specific subject your child takes at the specific level they take it, and fewer again who are free in the narrow evening window a commuting Diploma student is actually available. The three conditions rarely coincide in one person locally, and that is a structural fact about the teaching population rather than a comment on the island.

The arithmetic runs like this. KHDA recorded 387,441 students across 227 Dubai private schools in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of students against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum. Diploma teachers are therefore a small group to begin with. Divide that group by subject, then by level, then by who is willing and free to teach at half past five after their own school day, and the remainder is small.

Bluewaters sharpens it in one specific way. There is no school on the island, so unlike a community built around a campus there is no local staff room from which a nearby teacher might emerge. The people a map returns as near you are residents of the Marina and JBR who happen to tutor, which is a different population from the people who teach the Diploma in Al Barsha and Emirates Hills.

The useful conclusion is not that Bluewaters families are badly served. It is that the proximity filter is costing them access rather than buying them anything, at Diploma level. Remove it and the pool becomes everybody who teaches that subject at that level and can hold a Gulf Standard Time slot, which is a much better pool and still not an unlimited one.

sections.heading: What a near-me search is actually ranking
paragraphs: Search results for a near-me query are ordered by proximity and by whoever has invested most in local listings, reviews and location pages. Neither signal measures subject knowledge. That is not a criticism of the search engine, which is doing what it can with what it can see, but it does mean the top result is answering a different question from the one the parent asked.

The signals that would actually help are all invisible to a map. Which syllabus version the tutor teaches. Which board, where a student sits both IB and Cambridge qualifications. Whether they have supervised an internal assessment against the published criteria. Whether they can explain a lost mark in mark-scheme language. Whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition permit. Whether they are free in the slot your child is awake for.

Review signals deserve particular scepticism in this market. Competitors in our research publish conflicting review counts on the same page, and one shows five stars from twenty reviews beside a claim of 2,500 students. Self-asserted ratings in structured data are against Google's own structured data policy and are a manual action risk, which tells you something about how carefully the claims were made. We publish no aggregate rating, because we have none we could evidence.

So the practical approach is to use the search to generate candidates and then apply your own filters, which the next section sets out. Twenty minutes of a trial lesson is a far better instrument than any ranking, and it is free.

sections.heading: Four questions that test any tutor in twenty minutes
paragraphs: These are the questions we would want a parent to ask us, and they work on anybody. They take twenty minutes of a trial lesson and they are more discriminating than any credential list, because they test current working knowledge rather than history.

First, ask whether they want to see a recent marked script before teaching anything. A specialist does, because the diagnosis is in what the student actually wrote. Somebody working from a textbook asks which topic to cover, which sounds accommodating and tells you they intend to deliver content rather than fix a specific problem.

Second, ask them to explain one lost mark from that script in mark-scheme language. The answer should name marks and criteria: this line earns the method mark and this one does not, the band descriptor needs a judgement here, that answer describes where the command term said explain. An answer given purely in subject content, however accurate, means they are teaching the subject rather than the assessment.

Third, ask directly whether they can get your child from a 4 to a 7 by the May session. The correct answer declines to promise a grade and instead names what is achievable and what is not. Anybody who promises a specific score is either misunderstanding how the Diploma is marked or betting your money on it, and both are disqualifying. Fourth, ask what they would do with a draft internal assessment. The only acceptable answer is feedback against criteria on work the student wrote.

sections.heading: What we do when the answer is no
paragraphs: No competitor page in our research discloses a coverage limit. Several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number. We publish ours, because a parent who is told the truth about a ten-day wait can plan around it, and a parent given a substitute loses the term and only finds out in March.

When no specialist in your subject, level and slot is free, you get a date. Not a promise to look, a date. If that date is nine days away we say nine days, and we suggest what is worth doing in the meantime where there is something genuinely useful a student can do alone, which is often past-paper reading rather than past-paper answering.

We do not substitute across subjects or levels. A biology specialist in front of a chemistry student at Higher Level will teach competent science and miss the mechanism notation that the mark scheme is awarding. A Standard Level teacher covering Higher Level will teach the overlapping content well and not know what the third paper wants. Both arrangements feel like progress for about a month.

Where the only available specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book and you may decline and wait. sections.heading: Where proximity does earn its place
paragraphs: This page argues against the proximity filter at Diploma level, so it should be equally clear about where proximity genuinely helps. For a Primary Years child, having an adult physically in the room is worth something that a screen does not replicate: a hand kept on the page, an immediate redirection when attention drifts, a visible reaction that tells a seven-year-old somebody is paying attention.

The same applies to a student with particular support needs where physical presence materially changes how a session goes, and to the youngest end of the Middle Years where self-management is still developing. In those cases, an independent local tutor working across the Marina and JBR can be the right choice for a Bluewaters family, and we will say so rather than arguing for a format that does not suit the child.

What proximity does not buy, at any age, is subject expertise. A local tutor who is excellent with a Year 4 reader is not thereby a Chemistry HL specialist, and the mistake families make is extending a good experience at one stage into a booking at another. The two jobs are genuinely different jobs.

There is also a cost dimension. In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 table, rising to AED 500 at specialist levels, against roughly AED 150-300 for the same tier online. That AED 50-150 travel premium is reasonable to pay for a young child who needs presence. It is harder to justify for a sixteen-year-old working on Paper 3 technique, where it buys a narrower choice of teacher.

sections.heading: What it costs, and where scarcity should not be priced
paragraphs: Scarcity is a real feature of Higher Level Diploma supply, and it is also a convenient story for charging more. The distinction worth holding is that scarcity in Computer Science HL is genuine, while scarcity in Standard Level mathematics is not, and a rate justified by the second is a rate justified by nothing.

The Dubai bands, read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led from AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650.

The specialist band is doing real work for internally assessed components, third papers and core essays, where criterion and mark-scheme knowledge changes the outcome. It is not doing real work for content revision in a widely taught subject, and if a provider cannot explain which of those your purchase is, that is informative. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Set those hourly bands against the bill they sit beside rather than against each other, because a Bluewaters family is choosing between Diploma tuition and everything else the school year already claims. The larger number is now fixed: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A flat fee bill means the tuition decision is made against a known total for the first time in several years, which argues for buying fewer hours at the specialist band rather than more hours at the cheap one. Everything quoted above is a market figure read from other people's published pages, not an IB Gram price. We publish no price list on these pages, and the first lesson is a free trial.

sections.heading: The claims to check before you believe anybody
paragraphs: This market has a credential problem, and a parent asking an honest question deserves to know what to discount. The single most dangerous phrase available to pages like this one is approval by a regulator. KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge and Pearson do not accredit tutoring platforms, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai.

IB Gram does not hold one. We are not IB authorised, KHDA approved, ADEK approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, and we have no UAE office. What we can do is explain what each body governs and link its own page, which is a different and smaller claim. Ask any provider describing itself as approved exactly which permit it means, and ask for the number.

Second, examiner status. Several pages in this market describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners. Current examiner status is verifiable and should be evidenced on request, and it should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content, because no such access exists. Third, statistics: no figure should appear without a sample size, a date and a method, and claims like a 96 per cent satisfaction rate or a median tutor score are unverifiable by construction.

Fourth, assessed work. One operator in our competitor research sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750. A tutor teaches criteria, questions method and gives feedback on the student's own drafts; a tutor never writes, rewrites or completes assessed work or generates data. The consequence of crossing that line is an academic malpractice finding carried by the student.

sections.heading: Starting, with the availability question answered first
paragraphs: Send the subject, the level, the school and the slot you need, plus a recent marked script if you have one. We will tell you within a day whether a specialist in that exact combination is free, and if not, when. That order matters: the availability answer should come before any discussion of hours or rates, because a plan built around a tutor who does not exist this month is not a plan.

If a match exists, you get one named tutor with their background and where they are based, and a free trial lesson in the slot you intend to use weekly. The trial is a real teaching hour on the current sticking point rather than a consultation, with a short written note afterwards. No card is held, nothing renews, and if the match is wrong we rematch once at no charge.

If no match exists, you get a date and, where there is something genuinely useful, a suggestion for the interim. We will also tell you if the honest answer is that your problem does not need us: a student who needs reading practice at Primary Years level, or whose real issue is a conversation with the school about Language Acquisition phase placement, should not be buying Diploma specialist hours.

Bluewaters sessions usually land at 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time or later on weekdays, with weekend mornings better for anything demanding. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots are a normal request and the slot is held. What we will not do, on the island or anywhere in the UAE, is send a tutor to your address; that service runs in India only.

faqs.question: Is there genuinely an IB tutor near Bluewaters who knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: For some subjects yes, for others honestly no. There is no school on the island, so there is no local staff room producing nearby IB teachers, and the people a map returns are Marina and JBR residents who tutor rather than Diploma teachers. Standard Level mathematics, biology and English A are findable. Chemistry at Higher Level with current investigation criteria knowledge, free at half past five on a Tuesday, usually is not within a drive. Removing the drive widens the pool substantially; it does not make it unlimited.
