sections.heading: What a two-year Diploma support plan actually costs
paragraphs: Pricing an hour tells a parent almost nothing about a Diploma, because a Diploma is a two-year commitment and the sensible question is what a plan costs across it. Working from published market rates, Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 an hour. One weekly hour in a single subject from the start of DP1 to the examinations is roughly sixty teaching weeks allowing for holidays, so from around AED 12,000 across the two years. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table estimates AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more a month for specialist exam-year support, which annualised sits in a similar place for the second year alone.

Most families do not buy that, and most should not. The pattern that produces the best return is narrower: one subject weekly across both years where there is a genuine persistent weakness, plus two short blocks — one for the internally assessed component in whichever subject it matters most, and one for paper technique before the final mocks. On published rates that comes to something in the region of AED 12,000 to AED 16,000 across two years rather than a figure several times larger for six subjects.

The cheaper tiers have a place and it is worth being specific about where. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Those rates buy a university student or a generalist, which is reasonable for MYP homework supervision and not reasonable for Maths AA HL Paper 3. At the top, TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for named or examiner-linked tutors; we would add that examiner status should not be accepted without evidence, and that it does not confer access to marking, boundaries or paper content. In-home delivery sits at AED 180 to AED 350 per Bestimate and AED 200 to AED 500 for independent home tutors, with the travel inside the rate.

For household context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Fees are flat; tutoring is the discretionary line. Every figure in this section belongs to the provider named beside it and none is an IB Gram price. We quote after the free trial, once the subject, the level and the frequency are known.

sections.heading: Coverage, matching and the answer when it is no
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes where their coverage runs out, and that is why families go through the near-miss sequence. Ours: Mathematics in both routes, Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English A are well covered at Higher and Standard Level, because they are the highest-volume Diploma subjects in Dubai. Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge process coaching is well covered. Group 6 arts subjects, Environmental Systems and Societies, Global Politics and the less common languages are thinner, and we will say so before you book.

When a request cannot be matched well the options are a named wait with a date, a different hour where a better-matched tutor is free, or a tutor strong in the adjacent subject with the specific gap stated openly so you can judge it. What we will not do is put a Business Management tutor on an Economics HL request because the subjects look similar from outside, since the papers, the internal assessment and the quantitative demands differ substantially.

Demand is concentrated and worth naming. Across Business Bay, Downtown and DIFC the requested window is roughly 6pm to 8pm on weekdays, because every family is working around the same bus returns. When that window is full for a given subject, saying so is more useful than filling it. A Maths AA HL student put with a generalist loses a term before anyone notices, and a nine-day wait is a better outcome than that.

Two disclosures to close. Some of our Diploma tutors are UAE residents and others teach from India, where our in-home service operates, working with Dubai students over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not route UAE families to a non-UAE number while implying a local presence. And IB Gram operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE and sends no tutors to homes anywhere in the country, since home visits are a service we offer only in India.

process.title: Decide what you are actually buying
process.description: A subject, an internally assessed component, paper technique, or the core. Those are four different purchases with different durations and prices. Most families ask for a subject when a component block would do more for less, and the mock papers usually show which it is.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Economics HL internal assessment is a precise request; IB tutor is not. With the subject, the level, the specific component and the hour your child is realistically home from the bus, we can tell you within a day whether we have a strong match or a thin one.

process.title: Hear an honest coverage answer
process.description: If we have a tutor who has taught that subject at that level, we say so. If the match is adjacent rather than exact, we describe the gap so you can decide. A named wait is a legitimate answer and we would rather give it than fill a Maths AA HL slot with a generalist.

process.title: Use the free lesson as a subject test
process.description: One real lesson at no charge, no card, no obligation. Ask the tutor what the internally assessed component is worth in your child's subject and how it is marked. A precise answer is the signal you are looking for; a vague one means we should rematch.

process.title: Fix the hour and log the deadlines
process.description: The slot stays at the same time weekly in Gulf Standard Time. In the first session we log the school's internal deadlines for every internally assessed component, because those dates bind and they are set by the school rather than by the IB.

process.title: Review on marked papers, not impressions
process.description: Progress is read from marked past-paper work and from drafts measured against published criteria. If nothing has moved in six weeks we change the approach or the tutor, instead of letting a standing weekly arrangement run unexamined into DP2.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject depth, not driving distance
whyPoints.description: Distance is the one filter that removes good tutors without improving a lesson. We drop it and keep the two that matter: the named subject at the right level, and availability in the hour your child's bus actually permits. That is the whole of the argument and the arithmetic is on this page.

whyPoints.title: The district comparison tested honestly
whyPoints.description: Business Bay, Downtown, DIFC, Al Jaddaf and Meydan are compared on IB school access, local subject depth, session timing and what a local search returns. Al Jaddaf and Meydan could have broken the pattern; we show why having an IB school nearby does not produce IB tutors nearby.

whyPoints.title: Priced as a two-year plan
whyPoints.description: A Diploma is a two-year commitment, so we price plans rather than hours and show which plan gives the best return. Every figure is attributed to the provider that published it, and we quote our own fee after the trial rather than advertising one.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits published, including the thin ones
whyPoints.description: We name the subjects where our coverage is strong and the ones where it is narrow, with the fallback in each case. That disclosure is uncomfortable to publish and it is the reason families stop running through three tutors before finding one who fits.

whyPoints.title: The core taken seriously
whyPoints.description: TOK and the Extended Essay carry three of the 45 points and almost no teaching time. We coach scope, argument and deadlines, and we draw the authorship line clearly: the objects, the research and every word remain the student's own work.

whyPoints.title: No UAE premises, no home visits, no borrowed authority

faqs.question: Why does searching for an IB tutor near me in Business Bay return so few real specialists?
faqs.answer: Because a near-me search sorts by distance and prominence, which selects for businesses with local addresses rather than for people who have taught your child's subject at Higher Level. The IB is around 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, so Diploma specialists are a small pool spread across the city. Require the right subject, a free hour in the Business Bay evening window, and a short drive to Marasi Drive, and you have intersected three filters on a small pool. The listings you see are mostly agencies with addresses, not available subject specialists.

faqs.question: Does having an IB school ten minutes away make it easier to find a Diploma tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and this surprises families in Al Jaddaf and Meydan who assumed it would. Schools employ teachers who are already fully occupied, and tutoring their own enrolled students privately is a conflict that ADEK explicitly prohibits for Abu Dhabi school staff and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also addresses. A nearby IB school produces a nearby IB community, not a nearby pool of available tutors. Local Diploma subject depth is effectively the same in Business Bay, Downtown, DIFC, Al Jaddaf and Meydan.

faqs.question: What part of the IB Diploma gives the best return on tutoring money?
faqs.answer: The internally assessed component in whichever subject is weakest, almost always. It carries 20% or more of a subject grade, the student controls it directly, and the marks are won by narrowing the scope early and handling the method properly rather than by knowing more content. After that, paper technique in a subject where your child understands the material and underperforms on the page. Content teaching across a whole subject is usually the most expensive and least necessary purchase, because the school is already doing it.

faqs.question: How many points do TOK and the Extended Essay actually add?
faqs.answer: Up to three, through a published matrix combining the grades awarded for each. Six subjects at a maximum of 7 give 42, and those three take the maximum to 45. Three points is the difference between 36 and 39, which changes which offers are reachable at selective universities. They are also the two components that receive the least timetabled teaching, which is why they get neglected. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words; the TOK essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title, alongside an exhibition of three objects.

faqs.question: My child chose Maths AI and now wants engineering. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Act immediately and talk to the school rather than to a tutor first. Engineering, physics and mathematics programmes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while Applications and Interpretation is more often accepted for business, management and design. Requirements are set by each institution and change between cycles, so read the prerequisite page for the specific programme including at UAE universities. A route change is usually only practical in the first weeks of DP1, and after that the conversation becomes which programmes accept AI.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without breaching academic honesty?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary. A tutor can discuss candidate research questions and say which are answerable in 4,000 words, point out that an experimental question cannot be answered with the apparatus available, coach the structure of an argument, teach referencing conventions, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write any section, redraft to completion, produce the analysis or supply text. Most weak Extended Essays failed at the question stage, so the valuable intervention is in the first month rather than the last.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection band tell me about my child's Diploma teaching?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a rating on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, assessed against a framework covering attainment, progress, teaching, leadership and the mandatory subjects. That band aggregates across every phase and subject in the school, so it cannot tell you whether Diploma Chemistry is taught well this year. Use the band as a first screen, then ask the Diploma coordinator directly for subject-level results and teacher continuity in the subjects your child is taking.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates private schools in each emirate?
faqs.answer: KHDA in Dubai, which oversees the quality of private education there. ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, which supervises licensing and accreditation. The Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, and the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, both of which also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK in particular is named by almost no tutoring provider in this market, which is worth knowing if you are comparing schools across emirates.

faqs.question: What does two years of Diploma tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Working from published rates, Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 an hour, so one weekly hour in a single subject from the start of DP1 to the examinations is from around AED 12,000 across roughly sixty teaching weeks. The pattern with the best return we see is that one subject weekly plus two short blocks, which lands around AED 12,000 to AED 16,000. Bestimate estimates AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more a month for specialist exam-year support. These are published provider figures rather than IB Gram prices; we quote after the free trial.

faqs.question: Should I pay more for a tutor described as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Only if the status is evidenced, and not because of what it is implied to confer. Examiner status does not provide access to marking in progress, unreleased papers or grade boundaries, and any suggestion otherwise should end the conversation. BartyED publishes AED 650 an hour for named or examiner-linked tutors, which is the top of this market. For most students the determining factor is whether the tutor has taught that subject at that level to examination standard and can diagnose a weakness quickly, and that is testable in a single free lesson.

faqs.question: What time should a Diploma session start for a Business Bay student?
faqs.answer: Around 6pm for most families here. Children are bussed out of the district and return between about 4pm and 5pm depending on whether the school is in Al Quoz, Oud Metha, Al Safa, Hartland or Meydan, and two afternoons a week usually carry a co-curricular commitment. Downtown returns run about thirty minutes earlier, so a 5.30pm start works there. DIFC parents more often want a later slot because they work in the towers above. Online delivery means no part of the window is spent on travel at either end.

faqs.question: Do you cover every IB Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: No, and we would rather say so. Mathematics in both routes, Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Economics, Business Management and English A are well covered at Higher and Standard Level, as is process coaching for the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Group 6 arts subjects, Environmental Systems and Societies, Global Politics and the less commonly taught languages are thinner. When we cannot match well the options are a named wait, a different hour, or an adjacent-subject specialist with the gap described openly so you can judge it.

faqs.question: Is my child too far into DP2 for tutoring to make a difference?
faqs.answer: It depends what you ask it to do. With a short runway there is no time to re-teach a two-year subject, so the work becomes triage: identify the two highest-value gaps from the mock papers, fix command-term responses so the knowledge already there earns full marks, and drill the specific question types that reliably cost marks. That is narrow by design, because narrow is what works in six weeks. Bring the marked mocks to the free lesson and the tutor can name the two targets within the hour.

faqs.question: Do you have a Dubai office we can visit?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram operates no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, which is why no address appears on this page. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal, and we hold no such permit and do not claim one. Everything we do for a Business Bay family happens live online in Gulf Standard Time, and the free first lesson is the way to test it rather than a meeting.

faqs.question: Are your IB tutors based in the UAE, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: Some are and some are not. A number of our Diploma tutors are UAE residents; others teach from India, where our in-home service operates, and work with Dubai students over live video scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not route UAE families to a non-UAE phone number while implying a local presence, and we claim no UAE premises. What affects your child's lesson is whether the tutor has taught their subject at their level and is awake at the hour that suits the bus, and both are testable in the free lesson.

intro.heading: What a City Walk parent is really asking when they search for an IB tutor
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in City Walk is rarely a general request. By the time a parent types it, something specific has happened. A mock Paper 2 came back three marks under the predicted grade. A Biology internal assessment draft was returned with a comment about the research question being too broad to generate a trend. A Maths Analysis and Approaches student has stopped being able to do Topic 5 calculus questions that they could do in December. The search looks generic. The problem never is.

That is the reason this page is built from the syllabus rather than from the neighbourhood. City Walk sits on the Al Safa and Al Wasl Road side of Jumeirah, a short drive from Jumeirah College, Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, Safa British School and Horizon English School, and within twenty minutes of most of the Diploma-running schools between Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. Families here have no shortage of schools. What they are short of is somebody who knows what a 4-mark Physics explain question wants in the second sentence, or which criterion a Chemistry investigation is losing its marks under.

The IB Diploma is assessed in a way that rewards that kind of precision and punishes its absence. Every subject splits into external papers and at least one internally assessed component, and the internal piece is worth a fifth to a quarter of the final grade in most subjects. Those marks are available months before the examination hall. They are also the marks most commonly thrown away, because an internal assessment is marked against published criteria that most students have never read in full and most parents have never seen at all.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one tuition over live video. There is no tutor arriving at a City Walk address: home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and that is stated on every country page on this site. What a City Walk family gets instead is a specialist for the actual component. If your child needs Chemistry Higher Level with real fluency in the Reactivity 3 mechanisms, the match is a chemist who teaches that, not whoever happens to live close enough to Al Wasl Road to drive over by four o'clock.

The rest of this page does four things. It sets out the assessment architecture of the Diploma so you can see where the marks sit. It names the places those marks are lost, subject group by subject group. It publishes what the Dubai tutoring market actually charges in AED, with the source for each band, because most pages competing for this search publish no price at all. And it draws the line on academic honesty, which matters more in the IB than in any other curriculum your child could be sitting.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-city-walk.programmesIntro: City Walk children are spread across the full IB continuum, from Primary Years classrooms a few minutes away to Diploma cohorts sitting their final papers. The three programmes assess in entirely different ways, so the tutoring problem changes shape as a child moves up.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised into transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and the exit point is the Year 6 exhibition, a long collaborative inquiry presented to the school community. Assessment is continuous, evidence-based and reported against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages, which is why PYP reports read so differently from the British or Indian reports a family may be used to.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the PYP sits alongside KHDA's mandatory subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are compulsory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes expressly prohibited. For a City Walk family that means two parallel reporting systems from Year 1 onwards.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks every subject against four criteria lettered A to D, each scored out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Mathematics marks Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Sciences mark Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. A student can know the content and still score 4 if they cannot write to the criterion.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within reach of City Walk run MYP Years 4 and 5 as an alternative to IGCSE, which creates a specific Dubai dilemma: the MYP produces no externally recognised certificate at 16 unless the school enters students for eAssessment. Families planning a move abroad, or a switch to A Levels, should ask the school directly which exit qualification their Year 11 cohort actually holds.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subjects are graded 1-7 for a maximum of 42 points, with up to 3 further points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix, giving the familiar 45. The core is where many Dubai students lose points they assumed were safe, because the TOK exhibition and the Extended Essay are long-horizon tasks with no weekly homework rhythm to carry them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma students sit the May session, which is the session UAE schools are built around. Confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator rather than a tutoring page: the IB revises its assessment calendar, and no date in this project has been verified against ibo.org directly. What does not change is that internal deadlines at a Dubai school fall months before the external window.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines two or more DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning requirement, personal and professional skills, and a language development portfolio. It is far less common than the Diploma in Dubai, but a handful of schools offer it to students who want DP-level rigour in two or three subjects without carrying six.
programmes.countryNote: Because the CP is rare locally, tutoring demand for it is thin and schools rarely have in-house specialists for the career-related component. Online matching is the practical route: a CP student in City Walk needing DP Business Management alongside a reflective project will not find that combination within driving distance.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-city-walk.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects City Walk families ask for most often, with the component that usually triggers the request. Levels are given as the school offers them; what matters for tutoring is which paper or criterion is bleeding marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage happens: algebraic fluency that a graphing display calculator has been hiding collapses under exam conditions. Topic 5 calculus and Topic 1 proof carry the heaviest Higher Level marks and reward written argument, not just a correct final line.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Every paper is calculator-permitted, so marks move to modelling, interpretation and statistical reasoning. Students lose marks by giving an unrounded answer with no units, or by reporting a correlation coefficient without saying what it means for the context in the question stem.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The 2023 syllabus organises content into themes A to E, from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics. Paper 1 mixes multiple choice with a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response. Explain questions want a causal chain, and a student who writes the conclusion without the mechanism scores one of four.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and Reactivity replaced the old topic numbering. Reactivity 3 mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics generate most Higher Level requests. The data booklet is supplied in the examination, so recall of constants earns nothing; using the right value from it under time pressure earns a great deal.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The concept-based syllabus runs on the unity and diversity, and form and function, axes. Students who revise by topic list rather than by concept struggle with synthesis questions that cross themes. Statistics in the internal assessment is the single most common source of lost criterion marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, and the Individual Oral is internally assessed on a global issue through one literary and one non-literary extract. Weak Individual Oral marks almost always come from an unfocused global issue rather than from weak reading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries, each on a published news article and each tied to a different unit of the syllabus. Students lose marks for diagrams that are not referenced in the text, and for commentaries written about an article older than the permitted window.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Higher Level internal assessment is a research project on a real organisation using primary research; Standard Level writes a commentary from supplied secondary sources. The usual failure is a research question too broad to answer in the word limit, which caps the evaluation criterion before a word is written.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a replication of a simple published experiment with a full statistical treatment. Students who choose a study they cannot ethically or practically replicate in a Dubai school lose criterion marks on exploration and analysis that no amount of essay polish recovers.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK is assessed by an exhibition of three objects answering an IA prompt, and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. It contributes up to three points with the Extended Essay. Most point losses come from objects described rather than justified against the prompt.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, with a reflection record completed with a supervisor. The commonest cap is a question that is descriptive rather than arguable. Tutors coach the research process and give feedback; the writing is the student's own, without exception.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: A and B, plus KHDA mandatory streams
subjects.description: Arabic runs as a Diploma language option and separately as a KHDA mandatory subject with its own requirements. KHDA requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and that mandatory-subject content follows the Ministry of Education material without unapproved additions.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually sit in the IB Diploma
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is a sum of components, and the components are not equal. Most subjects split roughly four-fifths externally examined and one-fifth internally assessed, though the internal share rises in subjects with a substantial practical or performance element. Understanding that split is the difference between revising hard and revising where the marks are.

The internal piece deserves particular attention from a City Walk parent because it is the only part of the grade that can be influenced calmly, months in advance, with feedback loops. External papers are a one-shot event in a hall. An internal assessment is a document that passes between student and teacher several times before it is marked. A student who understands the criteria by letter on the first draft is working with the grading system; a student who writes first and reads the criteria afterwards is working against it.

The table below sets out the shape of the assessment across the subject groups City Walk families ask about most. Weightings are the published structure as schools currently teach them, and your child's subject teacher or IB coordinator is the authority for the current version: the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle, and the 2023 science guides changed the paper structure substantially from what an older sibling would have sat.
Read the final column first. It is the one that tells you what a tutor can realistically change in a term, and it is the question most tutoring enquiries are actually asking without saying so.

sections.heading: The command terms that decide a four-mark answer
paragraphs: IB papers are written in a controlled vocabulary. State, outline, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss, justify, compare and contrast, to what extent: each has a defined meaning in the subject guide, and each implies a shape of answer and a number of marks. A student who answers every question with everything they know is guaranteed to lose marks on the low-tariff questions and run out of time before the high-tariff ones.

This is the most mechanical improvement available in Diploma tutoring, and the fastest. A Physics student who writes four sentences of mechanism for an explain question and one sentence for a state question is not being more thorough than a student who does it the other way round; they are answering the paper. In practice a specialist can get a student to read command terms properly in two or three sessions, and the mark gain shows up in the next timed paper rather than in a year's time.

The second mechanical gain is mark-per-minute arithmetic. If a Paper 2 carries 95 marks in 135 minutes, that is roughly 1.4 minutes a mark, and a six-mark question that has taken fifteen minutes has already cost marks elsewhere whatever it scores. Students almost never do this calculation. Tutors who teach examination technique do it in the first session and then enforce it with a timer.

A tutor working this way asks for the actual mark scheme wording, not a textbook explanation. The mark scheme is the specification for the answer, and reading it alongside a student's own script is the single most useful hour available in a Diploma year.
bullets: State and outline want recall with no justification; evaluate wants a judgement with criteria
Analyse expects the parts and their relationship, not a description of the whole
To what extent requires an explicit degree, not a balanced list with no verdict
Compare and contrast needs both similarities and differences, or half the marks are gone
Justify demands reasons for a choice already made, not a fresh exploration of options

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, by letter, and where they leak
paragraphs: Every IB internal assessment is marked against lettered criteria with published descriptors and a fixed maximum for each. The letters differ by subject, but the pattern does not: there is always a criterion for framing the task, one or two for the technical work, and one for communication or evaluation. The framing criterion is worth the fewest marks and controls the most, because a weak research question caps the technical criteria no matter how well the work is executed.

The commonest pattern in Dubai schools is a student who produces a technically competent piece against a question that was never going to generate a result. A Biology investigation with no measurable trend cannot score highly on analysis or conclusion, however careful the method. A Mathematics exploration that restates textbook content has nothing to reflect on, so the reflection criterion closes. A Business Management project on a company that will not answer an email cannot do primary research, which is the Higher Level requirement.

That is why internal assessment support has to start before the first draft. A tutor's most valuable contribution is an hour spent interrogating the question: can this be measured, with what, over what range, and what will the data look like if the hypothesis is wrong. Once there is a draft, the ceiling is already set. The work after that is recovering communication marks, which are real but small.

IB Gram tutors teach the criteria, question the design and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not write, co-write, rewrite or polish the work to completion. That boundary is stated to the student in the first session, and it exists because crossing it puts the student's entire Diploma at risk, not because of a policy preference.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs in the Dubai market, and who charges it
paragraphs: Begin with the monthly figure, because that is the number a household budget deals with. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-range, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Packaged offers in the market sit near those edges: online packages around AED 799 a month for eight sessions, in-home packages around AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

Convert that back to an hourly band and the market separates into tiers by who is teaching. University-student and budget online tutoring is advertised from AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate reporting AED 200-450 or more. Named or examiner-level tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650.

The in-home column is the one worth staring at. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate reporting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200-500. The premium over an equivalent online rate is not buying better teaching. It is buying the tutor's car, their fuel and the hour of their evening that Al Wasl Road takes, and it is priced in because that hour is real.

Everything above is a market rate published by somebody else, cited so a City Walk parent can check it. None of it is an IB Gram price list. sections.heading: Online or in-home for a City Walk household
paragraphs: This is a genuine question and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. In-home tutoring has real advantages. A younger child who cannot yet self-manage benefits from an adult physically present. A household with unreliable connectivity has a problem online that it does not have in person. A parent who wants to overhear the lesson gets that for free in a living room.

Against that, the arithmetic of a City Walk weekday is unforgiving. A tutor travelling from Al Barsha to City Walk at five o'clock is committing well over an hour to the journey, and that hour is in the rate. It also shrinks the pool: the people who will make that drive are the people who live close enough, which is not the same set as the people who teach Chemistry Higher Level with real command of the Reactivity 3 mechanisms. A family optimising for proximity is, without intending to, optimising against specialism.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so there is no commercial reason to pretend the comparison is one-sided. Home tutoring is a legitimate product that other providers sell and that some families should buy. What this page argues is narrower: for a Diploma student with a specific component problem, the specialist matters more than the postcode, and online delivery is what makes the specialist reachable from Al Safa Street.

The practical form it takes is unremarkable and that is the point. A scheduled video room, a shared whiteboard the student writes on, screen sharing for past papers, and a recording the student can rewatch before the next timed paper. Sessions sit on Gulf Standard Time around the school day, and shift to post-Iftar slots through Ramadan when families ask.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an IB tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: This section exists because the search results for IB tutoring in Dubai contain businesses that sell completed internal assessments. One researched operator advertises finished IA work at a fixed price. Buying that is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the vendor: an investigation can cost a subject grade and, in a confirmed case, the Diploma itself.

The boundary is not subtle. A tutor may teach the content, explain the criteria, model a worked example on a different question, question the research design, point at a section and say the reasoning does not follow, and ask what the student meant by a sentence. A tutor may not write any part of the submission, draft the research question in their own words for the student to adopt, correct the text line by line until it is theirs rather than the student's, or supply data the student did not collect.

Schools in Dubai are reasonably alert to this. Internal assessment work typically passes through a draft-and-comment cycle with the subject teacher, candidates sign academic-honesty declarations, and a sudden change in voice between a classroom essay and a submitted piece is noticeable to anybody who has taught the student for a year. The sensible position for a family is to keep the tutoring visible: tell the school a tutor is involved, and keep a record of what each session covered.

There is a second, quieter reason to hold the line. A student who has been edited to a 6 cannot replicate it in the examination hall, where there is no editor. The marks that transfer are the ones that came from the student understanding the criterion, and those are the only marks a tutor should be in the business of producing.

sections.heading: The Dubai school market around City Walk, and what a KHDA rating means
paragraphs: Dubai's private-school sector is the context every tutoring decision in City Walk sits inside. The Dubai Media Office reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. That last figure explains something families notice: IB provision is a minority of a very large market, so Diploma specialists are correspondingly scarcer than IGCSE ones.

The sector is still growing. KHDA reported that Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Separately, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

KHDA is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on the federal u.ae portal as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Its inspection reports grade schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the report itself is more useful than the headline band: it is published per subject and per phase, so a school rated Good overall may be Very Good in secondary science and Acceptable in the subject your child is struggling with. That is the page worth reading before concluding the school is the problem.

Elsewhere in the country the regulator changes. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in that emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no approval, licence or accreditation from any of them, and no page on this site should be read as implying otherwise.

sections.heading: Permits, mandatory UAE subjects and Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, not informal. The federal u.ae portal records that the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, that it is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. A family hiring any individual tutor in Dubai can reasonably ask to see the permit. Note separately that an operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; IB Gram has no UAE premises and holds no such permit.

Alongside the Diploma, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, states that combined classes are strictly prohibited, calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, advises a minimum lesson length of 25 minutes, and prohibits any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission.

For university entry inside the UAE, Ministry of Education equivalency is the process that matters, and it is worth knowing the sourced numbers. On the British track a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five. On the American track, English proficiency requires IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math. There is no sourced IB points threshold, so none is published here: verify the IB route on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly. IB Gram describes this process and does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of it.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: The useful first message names the paper, the criterion or the topic. Physics Paper 2 extended response, or the analysis criterion on a Biology investigation, or Topic 5 calculus without a calculator. That one sentence is what turns a general enquiry into a specific match, and it is the difference between a good pairing and an average one.

process.title: A diagnostic, not a sales call
process.description: Before a tutor is proposed, somebody looks at the evidence: a recent mock script, the school's feedback on an internal assessment draft, the predicted grade and the target. The question being answered is where the marks are going, because that determines which specialist the student needs rather than which one is free.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the named tutor
process.description: The first 45-minute lesson is free and happens with the actual tutor who would teach the course, not a demonstrator. No card details are taken before it. The student should finish it able to say what the tutor noticed that their school had not, which is the only test of a match worth applying.

process.title: A written plan with dates on it
process.description: After the trial you get a short plan: the components to be worked on, the order, the past papers to be sat, and the school deadlines the block is built around. If the student is eight weeks from mocks, the plan counts backwards from mocks rather than forwards from today.

process.title: Weekly work that is marked
process.description: Each session sets work and the next session begins with it marked against the published mark scheme, with the mark allocation shown. Parents get the written feedback. The visible number is the mark on the question, not an impression of effort, because that is the number the Diploma will eventually produce.

process.title: Re-match or stop, without friction
process.description: If the pairing is wrong, say so and the match changes at no charge. If the problem is solved, stop. A tutoring arrangement that continues out of habit after the marks have recovered is spending a family's money on reassurance rather than on teaching, and nobody should pretend otherwise.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, the pool is every available specialist rather than only those who will drive to Al Safa Street. For a Higher Level subject or a core component, that is the whole argument: the thinner the specialism, the more the geography hurts, and City Walk is a short drive from many schools but not from many Chemistry Higher Level specialists.

whyPoints.description: Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. This page publishes AED bands with the provider who published each one and the month they were read. You can check them before you talk to anybody, which is how a parent should be able to approach a tutoring decision.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not write internal assessments, Extended Essays or TOK essays, and they say so to the student in the first session. In a search result that contains vendors selling completed coursework, saying this plainly is a differentiator rather than a disclaimer.

whyPoints.title: Built around the school's own deadlines
whyPoints.description: Internal deadlines at a Dubai school land months before any external window, and they are what actually governs a term. Session plans are built backwards from the school's draft dates and mock weeks, and shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, because a plan that ignores the calendar is a plan the family abandons by week three.

whyPoints.title: Regulatory facts, cited and not borrowed
whyPoints.description: Permit rules, mandatory-subject requirements and equivalency thresholds on this page come from u.ae, MoHRE, KHDA and a dated press source, each named in the text. One ranking competitor publishes the wrong IGCSE subject count for equivalency. Getting that right is cheap and it is the kind of detail a parent can verify in a minute.

whyPoints.title: No invented numbers anywhere
whyPoints.description: There is no satisfaction percentage on this page, no star rating, no tutor headcount and no average score, because none of those could be published with a sample size, a date and a method behind them. Every figure here is either a cited market rate or a published regulator statistic, and the source is on the page.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor near me in City Walk, or is everything online?
faqs.answer: Everything IB Gram provides for a City Walk family is online: one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. There is no tutor who travels to a City Walk address, and home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. Independent in-home tutors do exist in the area, and the Dubai market quotes them at roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel included. The trade-off is pool size. A tutor who will drive to Al Safa Street by five o'clock is a much smaller group than every specialist available for a Higher Level subject, and that gap matters most for the subjects where help is hardest to find.

faqs.question: Which IB components do City Walk families ask about most?
faqs.answer: Three cluster together. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Paper 1, because it is sat without a calculator and exposes algebra that a graphing display calculator had been covering. Science internal assessments, because the research question is usually settled before anybody reads the criteria. And the core, meaning the Extended Essay and the TOK exhibition, because they have no weekly homework rhythm and so drift until a deadline arrives. The common thread is that all three are fixable early and expensive to fix late, which is why a diagnostic conversation at the start is worth more than an extra hour at the end.

faqs.question: How much of an IB grade is the internal assessment worth?
faqs.answer: In most Diploma subjects the internally assessed component is worth around a fifth of the final grade, rising to a quarter or more in some subject groups and in languages. The precise weighting is published in each subject guide and your child's teacher or IB coordinator will confirm the current version, since the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle. What matters practically is that those marks are decided over months with feedback available, unlike the external papers. A student who reads the criteria before the first draft is working with the grading system rather than discovering it afterwards.

faqs.question: Where is the line between IA feedback and a tutor writing it?
faqs.answer: No, and no reputable tutor will. A tutor may teach the criteria, model a worked example on a different question, stress-test the research question, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write any part of the submission, supply data the student did not collect, or edit the text until the voice is the tutor's. Crossing that line is academic misconduct under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student, up to the loss of the Diploma. One operator in this search sells completed internal assessments; buying it is the single worst decision available in a Diploma year.

faqs.question: What do IB tutors cost per hour in the Dubai market?
faqs.answer: Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. Those are other providers' published rates as read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices. IB Gram quotes after the free trial, when there is a named tutor and a session length.

faqs.question: My child is eight weeks from mock examinations. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is enough for examination technique and for one or two topic repairs, and not enough to rebuild a two-year course. The sensible shape is a timed diagnostic paper in week one, marked against the real scheme, then hours allocated by where the marks went rather than by syllabus order. Command-term discipline and mark-per-minute pacing are the fastest gains available and often show up in the next timed paper. What eight weeks cannot do is fix an internal assessment whose research question was never going to produce a result, which is why that piece needs attention far earlier.

faqs.question: Under which resolution is a Dubai private tutor permit issued?
faqs.answer: Yes. The federal u.ae portal records that the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time. You can reasonably ask any individual tutor to show you theirs.

faqs.question: Which schools near City Walk run the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The immediate Al Wasl, Al Safa and Jumeirah cluster includes Jumeirah Baccalaureate School on the IB side alongside strongly British-curriculum schools such as Jumeirah College, Safa British School and Horizon English School. Diploma provision thickens in the next ring out, around Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, and again inland at campuses running the full IB continuum. Schools are named here only as context for the area's market: IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them. Check the current programme offering on the school's own site, because sixth-form routes change.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection rating actually tell me about my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume from the headline band. KHDA is described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and its reports grade on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The useful part is inside: ratings are published by phase and by subject area, so a school rated Good overall can be Very Good in secondary science and Acceptable in the subject where your child is struggling. Read that detail before concluding the school is the cause. It also tells you whether the gap is the teaching or the student's examination technique.

faqs.question: How does online IB tutoring work in practice from a City Walk home?
faqs.answer: A scheduled video room, a shared whiteboard the student writes on rather than watches, screen sharing for past papers and mark schemes, and a recording the student can rewatch before a timed paper. Sessions sit on Gulf Standard Time around the school day, usually early evening, and move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan when families ask. The student needs a device, a stable connection and somewhere quiet enough to think. What a parent gets after each lesson is written feedback naming the component worked on and the mark scored on the work set.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still apply if my child is doing the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with a minimum advised lesson length of 25 minutes, and no different or additional content may be used without prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: Will an IB Diploma get my child into a UAE university without extra paperwork?
faqs.answer: Ministry of Education equivalency is a separate process from the Diploma itself, and it is the step families most often discover late. The sourced British-track rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. The American track sets IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 reading and writing for English, and at least 450 in SAT Math. No sourced IB points threshold exists in the material read for this page, so verify the IB route on moe.gov.ae directly.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's six IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Mathematics and Physics overlap enough in technique that one specialist can often carry both, and the same is true of Chemistry and Biology at Standard Level. Across subject groups it is rarer and usually worse: a tutor stretched into a second subject they teach adequately rather than well is a false economy at any rate. The better arrangement for two genuinely different problems is two specialists with a shared understanding of the student's timetable, which online matching makes practical in a way a driving radius does not.

faqs.question: What if no City Walk-ready specialist covers our Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You get told, and told quickly. Thin specialisms do exist, particularly Higher Level sciences, less common Group 2 languages and the Career-related Programme's career study component. If nobody suitable is free in the matching window, the honest answer is that nobody is free, with an estimate of when that changes. The alternative, which several providers in this market take, is to place whoever is available and hope the fit works out. That costs a family a term and is why this page says so before you ask.

faqs.question: Is a free trial lesson genuinely free, and what is the condition?
faqs.answer: The first lesson is 45 minutes, free, and taken with the tutor who would actually teach the course rather than a demonstrator. No card details are collected before it and there is no obligation afterwards. The one condition worth stating plainly is that it is one trial per student per subject, not an open-ended run of free lessons across several tutors. After the trial you get a written plan and a quote based on the named tutor, the level and the session length, and the decision to continue is made then.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a City Walk student?
faqs.answer: For a mainstream Diploma subject at Standard Level, a match is usually proposed within a couple of working days and the free trial sits in the same week. Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and core supervision take longer because the pool is smaller. The variable that slows everything is vague information: a request naming only the subject needs a diagnostic conversation first, while one naming the paper, the criterion and the deadline can usually be matched straight away. That is why the first message matters.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-city-walk.closingHeading: Start from the component your child is losing marks on
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-city-walk.closingBody: If you have a recent mock script, a returned internal assessment draft or a predicted grade that does not match the target, that is the conversation to start with. Tell us the paper, the criterion or the topic, and what the school has already said about it. A specialist for that component will take the free 45-minute trial lesson with your child, on Gulf Standard Time, over live video, before any payment or card detail is involved. You will leave the trial with a written plan built backwards from the school's own deadlines, and a quote for the work. If the match is wrong, it changes at no charge. If the problem is solved, stop.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-culture-villag.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering the IB Diploma for families in Culture Village: matched to one subject at one level with internal assessment experience, drawn from a national pool rather than a Creek-side radius.

intro.heading: Comparing Culture Village with the districts next door
paragraphs: Culture Village is Jaddaf Waterfront: Dubai Wharf and the Creek-side towers, compact, with no private school inside its boundary. Al Jaddaf is immediately adjacent and does contain one, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, running IB programmes. Dubai Creek Harbour sits across the water on the Ras Al Khor side and, like Culture Village, contains none. Those three districts are minutes apart and are routinely compared by families who are deciding where to live or which tutor to hire.

The comparison is worth doing properly, because the differences that exist are real and the differences people assume are not. What genuinely differs between the three is commute length, and therefore how early a weekday session can start, and which school clusters are practical. What does not differ is the availability of Diploma subject specialists within a short drive, because in none of these districts is there one. The IB accounted for seven per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25 against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula, and a seven per cent share spread across a city does not produce local density anywhere.

That is the uncomfortable finding of the comparison and it is the useful one. A family moving from Creek Harbour to Culture Village gains about fifteen minutes in the evening and loses nothing. A family comparing a tutor advertising in Al Jaddaf with one advertising in Culture Village is comparing two listings drawn from the same small pool, neither of which was selected on whether the tutor has taught the subject and level in question. Proximity is a real variable with a small effect, and specification match is a real variable with a large one.

IB Gram's position follows from that rather than preceding it. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Culture Village, Al Jaddaf, Dubai Creek Harbour or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. The argument is not that online is universally superior. It is that in these three specific districts the thing proximity would buy is not available locally at the level the Diploma requires.

Published prices give the comparison a number. In-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. So proximity costs somewhere between a third and double, and in return it offers a tutor drawn from whoever lives within a practical drive of the Creek. That is the trade, stated as plainly as we can state it.

What follows compares the three districts on schools, commute and session timing, sets out what proximity would have to buy to be worth that premium, compares a local radius with a national pool on the things that decide a Diploma grade, and then says what a Culture Village family should compare instead.

programmes.countryNote: This is where the district comparison matters least and the specialist comparison matters most. A Higher Level science or Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level requires a tutor who has taught that exact subject and level, including its internally assessed component, and that person is no more likely to live in Al Jaddaf than in Culture Village. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a grade from one to seven. Most years have no external examination, so the grade is built from classroom tasks and the school reporting cycle governs the work.
programmes.countryNote: Here the district comparison does have teeth, because younger students benefit more from an early session and Culture Village's short commutes genuinely deliver one. A Middle Years student at a school in Al Jaddaf or across the Creek in Dubai Festival City can start at 16:30; the same student commuting to Nad Al Sheba cannot, and the difference in what the hour achieves is visible.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led framework rather than a content syllabus, with transdisciplinary units and an exhibition in the final year. Support at this stage targets underlying literacy and numeracy fluency, usually in short blocks rather than ongoing arrangements.
programmes.countryNote: The one stage where a visiting tutor has a genuine case, and we will say so despite not offering it. Younger children benefit from an adult physically present and from physical materials, and a Culture Village family wanting that for a seven-year-old should look for a visiting arrangement rather than an online one. Our model fits a Diploma candidate and a Middle Years student considerably better than a Year 2 pupil.

programmes.name: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is limited to 4,000 words. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title limited to 1,600 words and an exhibition of three objects with a commentary limited to 950 words. Together they carry up to three of the forty-five points.
programmes.countryNote: The core is entirely indifferent to geography. Both components are supervised in school, both are written by the student, and the help that is both legitimate and useful is question scoping, criteria explanation and feedback on the student's own draft. None of that improves by being delivered in the room, which is the clearest single illustration of why the district comparison does not decide the outcome.

subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with an internally assessed portfolio of commentaries on published articles. Reasonably well served in the Creek districts, because Business Bay and Downtown attract tutors with commercial backgrounds.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title limited to 1,600 words and an exhibition with a 950-word commentary. Availability is thin everywhere, because few tutors have marked it, and it is entirely unaffected by whether they are nearby.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay, supervised in school. The useful help is question scoping and criterion feedback, which is the same service whether it happens in the room or over video, and the specialism is research method rather than geography.

sections.heading: Culture Village against Al Jaddaf against Dubai Creek Harbour
paragraphs: Here is the comparison written out, because families in these three districts make it constantly and usually from anecdote. The districts are minutes apart, share one education catchment, and differ in ways that are easy to overstate. Only one of the three contains a private school. All three send students to the same clusters south along Al Khail Road and across the Creek into Dubai Festival City.

The genuine differences come down to minutes. Al Jaddaf has the shortest runs because Swiss International Scientific School Dubai is inside the district. Culture Village is a minute or two behind it and effectively equivalent. Dubai Creek Harbour is on the far side of the water and loses roughly fifteen minutes in the evening to every destination. Over a two-year Diploma those fifteen minutes are worth something, particularly for mathematics, but they are not the difference between a good outcome and a poor one.

The difference that would matter, local specialist supply, is absent in all three. The International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula, twenty-six per cent Indian and fourteen per cent US. A seven per cent share, spread across 227 private schools and 387,441 students, does not produce a concentration of Higher Level Diploma specialists in any residential district, let alone three adjacent ones on the Creek.

So the honest comparison concludes that the three districts are close to interchangeable for the purpose of hiring a Diploma tutor. What differs is the evening timetable, and that is worth optimising. What does not differ is whether the person who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level and marked its investigation lives nearby, because in all three cases they probably do not.

sections.heading: What proximity would have to buy to be worth the premium
paragraphs: A visiting tutor costs more, and that is not a criticism: travel is real work and should be paid for. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's table and from AED 200 to AED 500 from home-tutor providers, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor online, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. The question is what the difference purchases, and it is a fair question to ask of either model.

There are three things physical presence genuinely provides. An adult in the room, which matters for a younger or easily distracted student and matters less each year after about thirteen. Physical materials and manipulatives, which matter at primary level and in some art and design work. And a guarantee against connectivity failure, which matters if a household's connection is genuinely unreliable rather than merely occasionally annoying.

For a Diploma candidate, almost none of that applies. A Year 12 or Year 13 student working on an internally assessed component needs their draft read against published criteria, their research question interrogated, and their command-term errors named. All of that happens identically over video. The Extended Essay is the clearest case: it is written by the student, supervised in school, and the useful help is conversation about scope and criteria. Nothing about it improves by the conversation occurring in a living room.

Against those three benefits sit three costs that are easy to miss. The premium itself. The constraint that a visiting tutor's diary is built on geography, so your match is limited by their route before it is limited by your child's subject. And replacement speed: if the match fails mid-term, a local substitute takes weeks because the pool is bounded by the same radius, whereas an online match can change inside a week. For a Culture Village family the third is usually the decisive one, because it bites hardest in the term when internal deadlines and predicted grades land together.

sections.heading: A Creek-side radius against a national pool
paragraphs: This is the comparison that actually decides a Diploma grade, and it is the one no provider in this market publishes. Take a radius drawn around Jaddaf Waterfront that a tutor could plausibly drive in the late afternoon and ask what it contains. Then ask the same question of a national pool. The difference is not uniform across subjects, and the pattern of where it bites is the useful finding.

For a Standard Level subject in a mainstream group, the local radius is frequently adequate. Biology at Standard Level, Business Management, English A at Standard Level: a competent local tutor exists and the gain from widening the pool is modest. A family whose need is in that category should feel free to choose on convenience, and we would rather say so than pretend otherwise.

The radius fails at the edges, and the edges are where Diploma grades are decided. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, with Paper 3 and the Exploration carrying forty per cent between them. Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level, with internally assessed investigations requiring uncertainty analysis and a heavily weighted evaluation criterion. Theory of Knowledge, which few tutors have ever marked. In those categories a local radius does not contain a credible match and a national pool does.

The second failure is temporal rather than subject-based. Internal deadlines and mock weeks arrive across Dubai schools simultaneously, because cohorts progress together. In those fortnights a local radius is at its emptiest exactly when demand is at its highest, and a replacement is hardest to find. That is the point at which the comparison stops being theoretical, and it is also the point at which most families first go looking.

sections.heading: What a Culture Village family should compare instead
paragraphs: If the district comparison is close to a tie, the useful comparison is a different one. Compare candidates on four things, in this order: whether they have taught your child's exact subject at the exact level, whether they have worked with the internally assessed component for that subject and can name its criteria, whether they can hold the slot your week actually allows, and whether they can be replaced quickly if the match does not work.

The first two are testable in one conversation. Ask which criteria the internally assessed component in this subject is marked against and roughly what each carries. Ask the word limit on the Theory of Knowledge essay, and on the exhibition commentary. Ask how the three core points are awarded between the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. A tutor who teaches the Diploma answers all of that without pausing; one who has read a syllabus summary redirects to the subject itself.

The third is a scheduling question that Culture Village answers better than most Dubai districts. Short runs to Al Jaddaf and Dubai Festival City make a 16:30 start realistic, which is worth real value for mathematics and the sciences where error rates rise sharply with fatigue. For a school further out, a weekend morning is the better instrument and it also widens the choice of tutor, because weekday evenings between 17:00 and 19:00 are the busiest hours in the UAE tutoring day.

The fourth is the one nobody asks and it is the one that matters in Year 13. Ask what happens if the match is wrong, and listen for a number of weeks rather than a reassurance. An arrangement that can be changed inside a week is a different product from one that cannot, and the difference is invisible until the term when internal deadlines, mocks and predicted grades all arrive together.

sections.heading: The Dubai picture behind the local comparison
paragraphs: Some context explains why the three districts look the way they do. KHDA reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in Dubai in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curricula at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian at twenty-six, US at fourteen and the International Baccalaureate at seven. That is a large market with a small IB share, and a small share spread across a city is what produces thin local specialist supply everywhere rather than in particular districts.

The direction of travel is upward. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, and six new schools opened during 2025-26 with enrolment rising six per cent. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package. More IB places are coming; the specialist tutor supply follows enrolment with a lag of years rather than months.

What this means for the comparison on this page is that it will not change quickly. A Culture Village family deciding today is deciding in a market where IB enrolment is growing and local specialist density is still low, and where the nearest IB school sits in the district next door rather than in their own. Over a two-year Diploma that situation is stable enough to plan around.

One negative worth repeating in this context. KHDA regulates and inspects schools and does not approve, accredit or license tutors or tutoring platforms. An inspection rating is a judgement about a school. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff, which we are not.

sections.heading: The core: the clearest case that geography is irrelevant
paragraphs: If one part of the Diploma settles the proximity argument, it is the core. Three of the forty-five points sit on the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together. The Extended Essay is limited to 4,000 words, supervised in school, and written entirely by the student. The Theory of Knowledge essay is limited to 1,600 words on a prescribed title, with an exhibition of three objects carrying a commentary limited to 950 words. Nothing in any of that benefits from a tutor being in the room.

What does help is conversation, and specifically the right conversation at the right time. An Extended Essay question too broad to answer in 4,000 words is the dominant failure, and it is visible at the question stage months before the word count becomes a problem. Two or three conversations in Year 12 protect three points. A Theory of Knowledge essay that answers an adjacent question rather than the prescribed title as written is the second dominant failure, and one session taking the title apart clause by clause prevents it.

The boundary applies regardless of delivery. A tutor may question a research question, explain what a criterion rewards, and comment on the student's own draft. A tutor may not produce the essay, restructure it to a standard, or supply the argument, and the school supervisor remains the supervisor. Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is a malpractice trigger under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the seller.

So the core is where a Culture Village family should stop thinking about distance entirely and start thinking about whether the person they are hiring has read these criteria before. That is a question about experience, not about postcode, and it is the question most likely to be answered honestly if it is asked directly.
