sections.heading: Permits, and the one comparison that is free to make
paragraphs: Whichever model a Culture Village family chooses, one comparison costs nothing and is rarely made. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free and quick, there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one, and asking which category applies is a reasonable question of any provider in any model. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified.

A boundary worth naming in a comparison page specifically. A Culture Village family may find that the most locally available option is their child's own subject teacher. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Proximity at its most extreme is also the arrangement the rules most clearly exclude.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a separate legal position requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds neither that permit nor any UAE premises, office or branch, and we state that rather than implying a local presence. One competitor in this market shows a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page, which is a misrepresentation rather than a design choice.

sections.heading: Getting started from Culture Village
paragraphs: Send the subject and level, which internally assessed component is in progress, its school deadline, and two evening windows that genuinely work from Jaddaf Waterfront after the school run. Mention a weekend morning if you have one, because it widens the specialist choice considerably and it is where sustained work belongs. We match a subject specialist and run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep.

One trial per student, nothing charged beforehand, no card details required. The tutor writes a short note on what they found and what they would address first, and that note is the thing to judge the arrangement on. If it names a specific weakness and the evidence that would show it moving, the match is sound. If it is general, nobody has diagnosed anything and more hours will not change that.

If no specialist is free in your window we say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing whoever is available. Scarcity concentrates in Higher Level sciences and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, in Theory of Knowledge, and in the deadline clusters that arrive across Dubai simultaneously. Booking before a cluster costs the same and secures a better match, which is the only free improvement in this process.

Two limits stated plainly. Nobody can promise a grade or a point total and this page does not. And nothing here implies that tutoring is required for the Diploma to be awarded, for university admission or for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency; those are institutional and regulatory processes with their own published rules, and the authority rather than any tutoring provider is where to verify them.

faqs.question: Is Culture Village better or worse served for IB tutors than Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: Practically the same, and the honest answer is that neither has a local concentration of Diploma specialists. Al Jaddaf contains Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, which shortens the commute for families enrolled there, but a school in a district does not create a tutor pool in it. The International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, and a seven per cent share spread across 227 schools does not produce local density in any residential district.

faqs.question: Would moving from Dubai Creek Harbour to Culture Village improve tutoring access?
faqs.answer: It would gain you roughly fifteen minutes in the evening and change nothing else. Both districts contain no private school, both send students to the same clusters across the Creek and south along Al Khail Road, and neither has a meaningful local specialist pool. Those fifteen minutes are genuinely worth something for mathematics and the sciences, where error rates rise sharply with fatigue, but they are not the difference between a good Diploma outcome and a poor one.

faqs.question: What would a tutor being physically present actually give my child?
faqs.answer: Three things, named honestly. An adult in the room, which matters for a younger or easily distracted student and matters less each year after about thirteen. Physical materials and manipulatives, which matter at primary level and in some art and design work. And insurance against a genuinely unreliable connection. For a Year 12 or Year 13 candidate whose draft needs reading against published criteria and whose research question needs interrogating, none of the three applies, and the premium buys logistics.

faqs.question: For which IB subjects does a local tutor genuinely work?
faqs.answer: Standard Level subjects in mainstream groups, mostly. Biology at Standard Level, Business Management, English A at Standard Level and often Economics are reasonably covered within a Creek-side radius, helped by the commercial backgrounds of tutors around Business Bay and Downtown. Where a local radius fails is at Higher Level in the sciences and in Analysis and Approaches, and in Theory of Knowledge, which very few tutors anywhere have marked. Those are the categories that decide Diploma grades.

faqs.question: Why does replacement speed matter more than the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Because of when it bites. If a match fails mid-term, a locally bounded replacement takes weeks, since the pool is the same radius that produced the first one. An online match can change inside a week. That gap is irrelevant in the autumn of Year 12 and decisive in the term when internal assessment deadlines, mock examinations and predicted-grade evidence all arrive together, which is also the term when families most often discover the match is wrong.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor really knows the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Three questions, asked before hiring. Which criteria is the internally assessed component in this subject marked against, and roughly what does each carry? What are the word limits on the Theory of Knowledge essay and on the exhibition commentary? How are the three core points awarded between the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge? Someone teaching the Diploma regularly answers all three without pausing. Someone who has read a syllabus summary redirects the conversation to the subject itself.

Across the Creek, Universal American School Dubai and Deira International School are in Dubai Festival City. faqs.question: Why is the IB core the clearest argument against paying for proximity?
faqs.answer: Because nothing in it happens in a room. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research essay written by the student and supervised in school. The Theory of Knowledge essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title, with an exhibition commentary limited to 950 words. The help that is both legitimate and useful is conversation: question scoping, criteria explanation, feedback on the student's own draft. That conversation is identical over video, and together those components carry three of the forty-five points.

faqs.question: Is the IB share of Dubai schools growing enough to change this?
faqs.answer: Growing, but not quickly enough to change a decision made today. The International Baccalaureate was seven per cent of Dubai private enrolment in 2024-25, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them IB, creating 16,846 places. Six new schools opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up six per cent. Specialist tutor supply follows enrolment with a lag of years rather than months, so the thin local picture is stable enough to plan a two-year Diploma around.

faqs.question: How early can a session start from Jaddaf Waterfront?
faqs.answer: Often 16:30 if the school is in Al Jaddaf next door or across the Creek in Dubai Festival City, because those are short runs. A student travelling to Sobha Hartland is realistically 17:00 and one commuting to Nad Al Sheba 17:15 or later. Choose the slot for the worst normal weekday rather than the best. Where the commute is long, a weekend morning does more than two additional weekday evenings and also widens the choice of specialist considerably.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office in the Creek districts?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram has no UAE premises, office or branch anywhere, which is also why it holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, since that authorisation applies to training institutes with premises and staff. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits in Culture Village, Al Jaddaf, Dubai Creek Harbour or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we operate only in India, and we state that rather than implying a local presence.

faqs.question: Can I hire the most local option of all, a teacher from my child's school?
faqs.answer: You should not, and that is the one case where extreme proximity is clearly excluded. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, the person teaching the class, setting its assessments and moderating its internal work should not be separately paid by one family in it.

faqs.question: What should I ask about a tutor's UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Which category applies and whether it is current, in whichever delivery model you choose. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service with no fee and a stated two working days, so there is no cost reason not to hold one.

faqs.question: Does a KHDA inspection rating tell me anything about a tutor?
faqs.answer: Nothing at all. KHDA is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and it regulates and inspects schools. An inspection rating is a judgement about a school's provision and does not transfer to any tutor or tutoring platform. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: If the districts are equivalent, what should actually drive my choice?
faqs.answer: Four things in this order. Whether the tutor has taught your child's exact subject at the exact level. Whether they have worked with that subject's internally assessed component and can name its criteria. Whether they can hold the slot your week genuinely allows, which for Culture Village is often as early as 16:30. And how fast they can be replaced if the match is wrong. Distance belongs well below all four, because in these three districts it varies by minutes and specialist supply does not vary at all.

intro.heading: Six providers, one set of adjectives
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in DAMAC Hills returns results that are structurally different and verbally identical. A specialist agency, an international marketplace, an independent freelance tutor, a tuition centre running group classes, a school's own after-hours support, and a matching platform all describe themselves as experienced, qualified and trusted. None of those words distinguishes them, and the differences that matter are never the ones on the page.

The differences that matter are three. What the rate actually is, in AED, published rather than quoted on enquiry. How deep the pool is for one specific course at one specific level. And what happens when the match is wrong or the tutor leaves. A tuition centre running a group class cannot match by Higher Level component; a freelance tutor has a pool of one; a marketplace has reach and no filtering; an agency has filtering and a margin.

The second comparison families run here is geographic, because the search contains 'near me'. Is DAMAC Hills better or worse served than Arabian Ranches down the road, or Mudon next door? That comparison has an answer, and the answer is that it makes almost no difference, for a reason worth spelling out: Diploma cohorts in every community in this belt are small, so nobody has a deep local pool of Higher Level specialists.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. That is a limitation stated plainly and it is also the thing that resolves the geographic comparison: once the lesson arrives over video, the question stops being who is nearby and becomes who has taught the course.

The honest version of the model comparison includes the weaknesses of the model on this page. A matching platform does not employ the teacher in the classroom, cannot supervise unaided practice, and cannot replace a school laboratory. What it can do is choose from everyone who teaches a course rather than from everyone within a drive, state its rate bands, and tell a family when nobody suitable is free rather than supplying a substitute.

That last point is the one no competitor page in this market makes. Availability limits are concealed everywhere, and several providers route UAE parents to numbers in other countries while implying a local presence. Disclosing coverage and fallback is a small thing that happens to be rare, and it is the part of this page a family can actually check.

What follows is the comparison done properly: the six models against each other, the communities against each other, in-home against online, and what a specialist reads on a marked script that a generalist does not.

sections.heading: What 'near me' returns in Dubailand, and what each result is

An international marketplace, which lists many tutors and filters lightly. An independent freelance tutor, who is a pool of one. A tuition centre, which usually means group classes at fixed times. A school's own after-hours support, where it exists. And a matching platform, which is what IB Gram is.

IB Gram's version of that is one-to-one teaching in a named course at a named level, delivered live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. A family that wants someone in the room should use a different model, and the published rates for that model are set out further down this page so the comparison can be made on numbers.

The reason the models matter more than the adjectives is that they determine what is possible. A tuition centre cannot match a student to a Higher Level component, because the class is set before the student arrives. A freelance tutor cannot replace themselves if the match is wrong. A marketplace can offer enormous choice and no judgement about which of those tutors has taught Paper 3. Each model has a shape, and the shape is more predictive than the marketing.

The comparison table below is deliberately about models rather than about named competitors, with one exception: where a provider has published a rate, that rate is quoted with the provider named and the month it was read, because a published number is a fact and an unpublished one is not. Comparing against an unnamed straw man, which is the standard practice in this market, proves nothing.

sections.heading: DAMAC Hills, the Ranches and Mudon: what actually differs
paragraphs: The geographic comparison is the one the search phrase invites, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a reassurance. What differs between these communities is which school a student attends, how long the journey home takes, and therefore when a session can start. What does not differ is the depth of the local pool of Diploma specialists, because that is set by cohort size rather than by postcode.

DAMAC Hills has a British-curriculum school inside it, and many of its secondary students travel out to Al Barsha, Jumeirah or the Ranches. Arabian Ranches has the largest Diploma cohorts in this belt and the shortest school runs for its own residents. Mudon and Town Square are younger and generate mostly primary and Middle Years requests. DAMAC Hills 2 and Remraam add bus time at both ends of the day.

Those differences are real and they change the shape of a block: the start time, whether a weekend morning is better than a weekday evening, and whether two shorter sessions beat one long one. None of them changes which tutors exist. A family that moves from DAMAC Hills to Arabian Ranches to improve tutoring access would arrive to find the same thin market for Higher Level physics.

The table sets this out so the comparison can be closed rather than left open. The practical conclusion is that the question worth asking is not which community is better served but which hour the student can realistically work in, because that is the only local variable with an effect.

sections.heading: Why both comparisons end in the same place
paragraphs: The model comparison and the community comparison converge, and the arithmetic behind that is worth stating. The IB accounts for 7% of Dubai private school pupils. Within a Diploma cohort, Higher Level physics, chemistry and Mathematics Analysis are each taken by a minority. A given school in this belt may therefore have a handful of candidates in a Higher Level science in a year.

A local tutoring market sized to that demand cannot be deep, and it cannot be deep in DAMAC Hills, Mudon or Arabian Ranches alike. There is no community in Dubailand holding a surplus of teachers who have covered the Higher Level extensions, supervised investigations and marked the extended papers. The scarcity is structural, which means it cannot be solved by choosing a different neighbourhood or a different agency with the same geographic constraint.

What can be changed is the filter. A tutor chosen from those available within a drive of DAMAC Hills on a Tuesday evening is chosen from a handful of people whose main qualification is proximity and availability. A tutor chosen from everyone who teaches that course at that level is chosen on the only criterion that predicts anything about the outcome.

That is the whole argument for the online model, and it is worth stating alongside its costs. Online delivery cannot supervise unaided practice, cannot replace a school laboratory, and does not suit every young child. For a Diploma student working through past papers and coursework criteria, those costs are small and the change in filter is large.

sections.heading: In-home against online, priced honestly
paragraphs: The in-home comparison is the one most often made with adjectives, so here it is with numbers. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in. Qualified online subject tuition sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits and around AED 799 for eight online sessions.

The overlap between those bands is narrow and the top of the in-home range sits well above the top of the online one. The difference is not teaching quality; it is a car journey, and in this part of Dubailand that journey is thirty to forty-five minutes each way at the hour it would need to happen. That time is inside the fee whether or not it appears on an invoice.

There are things a person in the room does better, and listing them is part of an honest comparison. A young primary student is easier to keep on task in person. Apparatus handled physically is not the same as apparatus described. A student with particular access needs may find a room easier than a screen. For Diploma students annotating mark schemes, the shared screen is the better surface and the session can be rewatched.

IB Gram's position needs no softening. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE, India is the only country where that service runs, and the case for the online format is in the rate bands and the pool depth rather than in a promise nobody should make.

sections.heading: What a specialist reads on a marked script
paragraphs: The difference between a specialist and a capable generalist is visible in about ten minutes, and it shows up in what they say about a marked paper rather than in what they say about themselves. A generalist describes the student: hard-working, lacking confidence, needs more practice. A specialist describes the script: this answer named the effect without the mechanism, so it took two of four; this calculation lost its final mark to a rounded intermediate value.

That is a checkable difference, and it is the single most useful screening question available to a DAMAC Hills parent comparing providers. Send a marked paper and ask what went wrong. The answers will sort themselves into two groups immediately, and the rate band will not predict which group a given provider falls into as reliably as this question does.

It matters because the diagnosis determines the block. A student losing marks mechanically needs three or four weeks of habit work and will show a visible change quickly. A student with genuinely absent content needs a longer block and should be told so. A student losing marks to timing needs papers sat to the clock, not more teaching. Those are three different purchases, and only a script-level diagnosis distinguishes them.

It also determines honesty about what is possible. Eight weeks moves technique, timing and two or three topics. It does not rebuild two years of absent foundations, and a provider who accepts that booking anyway has made a commercial decision rather than an educational one. Asking what the block will not attempt is the second screening question, and it is as revealing as the first.

sections.heading: Availability, fallback and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is strange given that every provider has one. Demand for Higher Level specialists peaks across every Dubai school in the same fortnight after mock results, and thin subjects become unbookable for a few weeks every year. Pretending otherwise means supplying a general tutor and calling them a specialist.

The policy here is to state the position. Where a specialist for the exact course and level is free, they are proposed within a day with a trial lesson in the same week. Where none is free, the family is told, given a realistic wait, and offered a referral elsewhere if the wait does not work. That is less satisfying than an immediate yes and considerably more useful than a mismatch discovered in week three.

The subjects where this bites are predictable: Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Mathematics Analysis, Theory of Knowledge, and Extended Essay support in a specific subject. Biology, English and Business Management are rarely constrained. Middle Years criterion work is constrained year-round rather than seasonally, because criterion literacy is scarcer than subject knowledge.

The practical advice that follows is to book before the mock window rather than after it. It costs nothing to ask early, the trial lesson is free, and the same enquiry made eight weeks earlier reaches a market that is not simultaneously serving every other Diploma family in the emirate.

There is one more reason disclosure matters. A family told honestly that a wait exists can act on that information: start with a different subject, use the weeks for the coursework component instead, or take a referral. A family given a substitute discovers the mismatch in week three, has spent the money, and has lost the option of doing something else with those weeks. Concealing a coverage limit does not remove it; it just moves the cost onto the student.

sections.heading: Permits, verification and the claims this page avoids
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit, and that is a verification tool a family can use. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. Because the permit is free, there is no cost reason for an eligible tutor not to hold one, which makes asking a reasonable question rather than an awkward one.

A separate point applies in Abu Dhabi, reported in the press rather than quoted from policy: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's code of conduct reported to bar the same. Verify it against the current ADEK document before relying on it. It is mentioned because 'your child's own teacher, privately' is sometimes offered and is not a proposition to accept casually.

IB Gram holds no International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. No star rating, review count, success percentage or grade outcome appears anywhere on this page. A rating nobody can audit and a statistic without a sample size, a date and a method are not evidence, however confident they look next to a comparison table.

sections.heading: The regulator and the market this sits in
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

The scale of the market explains the cohort arithmetic behind this page. KHDA reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum largest by enrolment and the IB at 7% of pupils. Seven new private schools arrive for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6%.

KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Against fees at that scale a targeted eight-session block is a small line item, which is an argument for spending it precisely rather than on an unreviewed standing arrangement.

KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. For a Diploma student that means the examined six subjects are not the whole timetable, and revision plans built from the IB subject list overstate the free hours available.

process.title: Send a marked paper and ask what went wrong
process.description: The most useful screening question available when comparing providers. A script-level answer names specific withheld marks; a generalist answer describes the student's confidence. The two sort themselves immediately, and the rate band does not predict which you will get.

process.title: Ask what the block will not attempt
process.description: An honest plan has boundaries. Eight weeks moves technique, timing and two or three topics; it does not rebuild two years of foundations. A provider who promises full coverage in a short block has made a commercial decision rather than an educational one.

process.title: Agree the hour before the subject
process.description: In DAMAC Hills the realistic start is 5.30pm or a weekend morning, because secondary students travel out and arrive home after five. A tutor who can only offer four o'clock is not a match however strong the subject knowledge.

process.title: Trial lesson with the proposed specialist
process.description: A full online session with the person who would teach the block, not a call with a coordinator. It ends with a written diagnosis and a measurable target. No card is required and there is no obligation to continue afterwards.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The target is measured in writing at the halfway point, with a continue-or-change decision. Changing tutor is treated as normal rather than as a complaint, which is the practical difference between a model with a pool and a model with one tutor.

whyPoints.title: Models compared, not adjectives
whyPoints.description: An agency, a marketplace, a freelancer, a centre and a platform are structurally different and described identically. Rate, pool depth, filtering, replacement policy and disclosure are the five variables that differ, and all five are checkable before any money is paid.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated, including the limits
whyPoints.description: No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit, though every provider has one. Where no specialist for the exact course and level is free, families are told, given a realistic wait and offered a referral rather than supplied with a substitute.

whyPoints.title: The community question answered properly
whyPoints.description: DAMAC Hills, Mudon and Arabian Ranches differ in school, commute and start time, and not in the depth of the local specialist pool. That pool is set by cohort size, so moving neighbourhood changes nothing that matters about tutoring access.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with provider and date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider that published it and the month it was read, including the in-home packages that make the comparison honest. Comparing against an unnamed competitor, which is standard in this market, demonstrates nothing at all.

whyPoints.title: The weaknesses of this model stated too
whyPoints.description: Online delivery cannot supervise unaided practice, cannot replace a school laboratory and does not suit every young child. A comparison page that lists only the advantages of the page's own model is an advertisement rather than a comparison.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: No board or regulator accreditation, no UAE office, no star rating, no review count, no success percentage, no promised grade, and no IB session dates that could not be verified at source. Each omission is deliberate rather than an oversight.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near DAMAC Hills who can visit the house?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and some agencies do offer visits in this part of Dubailand, at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted, with monthly packages advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. IB Gram does not: all UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. The comparison is on this page so the choice can be made on numbers.

faqs.question: How do I tell a specialist agency from a marketplace from a platform?
faqs.answer: By what they can do rather than what they say. An agency filters tutors and takes a margin, usually quoting on enquiry. A marketplace lists many tutors and leaves the choosing to you, often pricing in US dollars. A platform matches by course and level before proposing anyone. A tuition centre sets the class before the student arrives, so it cannot match by component at all. Ask each one which course and level the proposed tutor has actually taught.

faqs.question: Is DAMAC Hills worse served for IB tutoring than Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is structural. The IB accounts for 7% of Dubai private school pupils, and Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis are minorities within that, so a school in this belt may have a handful of candidates in a given Higher Level subject. No community holds a surplus of specialists. What differs is the commute: DAMAC Hills secondary students are usually home after five, which sets the earliest workable slot, while Ranches residents attending the local cluster are home earlier.

faqs.question: What single question best screens a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: Send a marked paper and ask what went wrong. A specialist answer names specific withheld marks: this explanation gave the effect without the mechanism, so it scored two of four; this calculation lost its accuracy mark to early rounding. A generalist answer describes the student instead — hard-working, lacking confidence, needs practice. The two sort themselves within ten minutes, and the hourly rate does not reliably predict which answer you will receive.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level specialist is available?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a realistic wait, and offered a referral elsewhere if the wait does not work. Demand peaks across every Dubai school in the same fortnight after mock results, and Higher Level Physics and Mathematics Analysis are thin all year. The alternative practice is to supply a general subject tutor described as a specialist, which costs an exam-year student weeks they cannot recover. Booking before the mock window rather than after it avoids most of the problem.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre group class work for Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: It can for content coverage in a widely taken subject, and it cannot for component-level work. The class is set before the student arrives, so it cannot be matched to the specific paper or criterion a student is losing marks on, and it cannot spend a session on one student's marked script. For Higher Level extensions or coursework criteria, one-to-one matching by course and level is the only arrangement that reaches the actual problem.

faqs.question: Why do some tutoring sites quote prices in US dollars?
faqs.answer: Because they are international marketplaces or UK-based agencies serving many countries from one page. It is a signal worth noticing: a provider that has not localised its pricing has usually not localised anything else either, which shows up as no AED figures, no UAE school names, no mention of KHDA or ADEK, and sometimes a phone number in another country. A UAE family transacts in dirhams and should be quoted in dirhams.

faqs.question: Can changing tutor be done without starting again?
faqs.answer: With a model that has a pool, yes, and it should be treated as normal rather than as a complaint. The handover is the written diagnosis and the error log from the first block, so a new tutor starts from the evidence rather than from a fresh introduction. With a freelance tutor there is no replacement by definition, and with a group class the option is to change class or leave. That difference is a property of the model, not of anybody's goodwill.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched from DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Usually within a day for a named course and level, with a trial lesson in the same week, because matching does not depend on who can drive to Dubailand on a given evening. The exceptions are the thin subjects: Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Mathematics Analysis, Theory of Knowledge and Middle Years criterion work. In those cases a short wait is stated rather than hidden, and a referral is offered if waiting does not suit.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether a tutor holds a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a reasonable question rather than an awkward one. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs nothing, there is no financial reason for an eligible tutor not to hold one. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Are online lessons a worse option for a younger child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it would be dishonest to claim otherwise. A primary-age student is usually easier to keep on task with an adult in the room, and attention spans mean sessions have to be shorter and the room has to be quiet. For Diploma students working through past papers and coursework criteria, the shared screen is the better surface and the session can be rewatched. The honest answer depends on the age and the task rather than on the format alone.

faqs.question: What does a review at four sessions actually involve?
faqs.answer: The target agreed in session one is measured in writing, ideally on a comparable timed paper under the same conditions. If it has moved, the block runs to its end. If it has not, there are three honest explanations — the diagnosis was wrong, the tutor is not the right match, or the frequency is too low — and all three are changeable at no cost. Blocks nobody reviews run to the end regardless of whether anything changed.

faqs.question: Why does this page not publish a star rating?
faqs.answer: Because a rating nobody can audit is not evidence. Providers in this market publish self-asserted ratings, sometimes two contradictory ones on the same page, and sometimes in structured data that differs from the visible figure. Self-serving review markup is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. The same applies to success percentages published without a sample size, a date and a method.

faqs.question: Is tutoring required for university admission from a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider implying it is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory and admissions process. The Ministry of Education operates an equivalency process for secondary certificates and universities set their own entry requirements; neither requires private tuition. Tutoring is useful where a specific, identified gap exists between a student's current performance and what they need. It is not a procedural step and nobody should present it as one.

intro.heading: What 'near me' actually means when you live off Al Qudra Road
paragraphs: DAMAC Hills 2 was built for space, not for proximity. It sits out along the Al Qudra corridor, past the point where Dubai's school density thins, and almost every secondary-age child in the community is driven somewhere else each morning. That single fact reshapes the tutoring question. A parent typing IB tutor near me in DAMAC Hills 2 is not usually asking which street the tutor lives on. They are asking whether anything can realistically happen between the school run and bedtime.

Work the timetable forwards. A school day ending at 3:00pm or 3:30pm in Motor City, Dubai Sports City or further into the city means collection, then the drive back out along Hessa Street or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road in the heaviest part of the afternoon. Home at 4:15pm on a good day, closer to five on a bad one. Then food, and a Diploma student with four hours of homework, a Maths Exploration deadline and a Theory of Knowledge essay they have been avoiding.

Now add a tutor who has to drive out to you. They are leaving a different part of Dubai in the same traffic. A six o'clock start is optimistic, half six is realistic, and the session ends at eight with a tired student and an invoice that silently includes eighty minutes of road. That arrangement is not bad because the tutor is bad. It is bad because the hour is wrong, and the hour is the one thing a parent in DAMAC Hills 2 cannot buy more of.

IB Gram removes the travel from both sides. Lessons for DAMAC Hills 2 families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. In practice that means a session can begin at 4:30pm or 4:45pm, the moment your child is home and has eaten, while they are still awake enough to learn something that holds.

It also means the tutor is chosen on the right criterion. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25 and the IB accounts for about 7% of them, spread right across the emirate. A specific Diploma course at Higher Level is therefore a small cohort citywide, and the subset of qualified specialists willing to drive to the Al Qudra corridor on a Tuesday is smaller still. Online, the question is only whether they have taught your child's course.

The rest of this page is built from that timetable: which schools DAMAC Hills 2 actually feeds, what time each day ends, where the gaps in a week genuinely are, and what Ramadan and the UAE school calendar do to all of it.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-damac-hills-2.programmesIntro: The right session time changes with the programme, because the homework load and the deadline rhythm change with it. These are the IB programmes we cover for DAMAC Hills 2 families and what each does to a weekday evening.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed continuously by the class teacher against learning outcomes rather than by examination, organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry, and finishing with the Year 6 Exhibition. Support here is about reading fluency, number sense and the ability to explain a method in writing, which is what the later programmes quietly assume.

programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked 0-8, differing by subject group. Mathematics marks knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying maths in real-life contexts. Year 11 adds the Personal Project with its own criteria. Reports give criterion letters rather than a single grade, which is more useful than it looks.

The Personal Project in Year 11 is the point at which an evening slot needs protecting, because it competes with everything else for the same hours.

programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked internally and moderated by the IB. The total runs to 45, including up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. UAE schools sit the May session.

A route for a student who wants Diploma-standard academic subjects with a clear applied direction rather than the full six-subject load.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-damac-hills-2.subjectsIntro: The IB subjects DAMAC Hills 2 students most often need help with, and where the marks actually go. Availability varies by level and term, and the trial lesson is where the match gets confirmed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra carries it. Marks vanish in proof, in HL calculus applications, and in unstructured Paper 2 questions with no scaffold pointing at a technique. The Exploration is a fifth of the grade and is lost on absent personal engagement more often than on weak mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and confident calculator use. The usual failure is choosing it as the lighter option and then meeting regression and hypothesis testing with no statistical vocabulary. HL adds matrices, graph theory and complex numbers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 punishes loose definitions, Paper 2 rewards visible structured working, and Paper 3 tests experimental technique that textbook revision does not build. Uncertainty propagation and graph linearisation are the recurring gaps.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the two walls. Reciting reagents is not the same as explaining why a nucleophile attacks where it does. The Internal Assessment needs a measurable variable and enough repeats to say something about uncertainty.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap rather than difficulty. Command terms decide the mark: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate each want a different answer shape, and knowledgeable students writing the wrong shape score low.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under time pressure, and most lost marks come from summarising instead of analysing how meaning is produced. The Individual Oral needs a genuine global issue and two prepared works; improvisation is audible.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams must be drawn, labelled and then used in the prose rather than placed beside it. The commentaries are assessed on application to a named real article, so the article choice sets the ceiling before any analysis is written.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks score nothing alone; marks sit in applying them to the case material and reaching a supported judgement. The HL research project needs a real organisation and a question narrow enough to answer inside the word limit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by the exhibition of three objects and the prescribed-title essay, feeding the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. The essay fails when it becomes general opinion rather than claim and counterclaim grounded in specific areas of knowledge.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research against five criteria. The research question decides most of the grade: too broad and nothing is answered, too narrow and there is no argument. A tutor coaches question, method and reflection; the writing stays the student's.

sections.heading: Which schools DAMAC Hills 2 feeds, and when each day actually ends
paragraphs: Nobody can plan a tutoring week without this information, and no competitor page publishes it. The schools DAMAC Hills 2 families use fall into two groups: a short run along the Al Qudra corridor, mostly primary and through-school, and a longer run into Motor City, Dubai Sports City and the inner Dubailand belt where most secondary students are enrolled.

The finish times matter more than the distances. A primary day ending just after two o'clock and a secondary day ending at half three produce completely different evenings, and a household with both is running two timetables at once. Add the afternoon traffic on Hessa Street, Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and the Al Qudra approach, and the gap between a short and a long run is thirty to forty minutes of a child's usable attention.

The table below is built from how the day runs rather than from any school's published bell schedule, which varies by year group and term. Use it as a shape and check your own school's times. The last column is the one to read: it is the earliest a session can realistically start if nobody is travelling to you, and the figure a visiting tutor would have to beat. Families with children at two different schools should read two rows and plan around the later one, because in practice the second pickup sets the household timetable.

One more pattern worth naming. Several of these schools finish earlier on a Friday, which creates a long usable afternoon that almost nobody books. For a Diploma student with an Internal Assessment deadline approaching, a Friday afternoon block is often the most productive two hours available in the whole week, and it competes with nothing.

sections.heading: Where the gaps in a DAMAC Hills 2 week really are
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements fail on scheduling rather than on teaching. A family agrees a time that works in theory, then football is on Tuesdays, the Extended Essay deadline lands in November, and by February the sessions have quietly stopped. Picking the slot properly at the start is worth more than any amount of mid-year rescuing.

There are really four candidate windows in a week out here. The post-school-run slot between 4:15pm and 5:30pm, which only exists if nobody is travelling. The post-dinner slot from 7pm, which competes with the student's own best independent working hour. The late slot from 8pm, which Diploma students use well and younger students cannot. And weekend mornings, which are reliable and underused.

The honest ranking depends on age. For a PYP or lower MYP child, earlier is better and 8pm is pointless. For a Year 12 or 13 Diploma student, 8pm is often the best hour of the day and 4:30pm catches them still travelling or still eating. For a household with three children at different schools, weekend mornings are frequently the only honest answer and we would rather say so than agree a weekday slot that will collapse by October.

The table maps the four windows against who they suit and what kind of work they support. Choose with your child in the room; they know which hour they can think in better than either of us. Pick one window and protect it rather than agreeing to whichever hour happens to be free in September, because the hour that is free in September is rarely the hour that survives to February.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the UAE school calendar
paragraphs: A tutoring plan written in September that ignores the UAE academic year will be broken by February. The school year here runs from late summer to the start of summer, with a winter break, a spring break and Ramadan moving through the calendar roughly eleven days earlier each year. None of that is an obstacle, but all of it has to be planned for rather than discovered.

Ramadan is the biggest change. School days shorten, the rhythm of the evening reorganises around Iftar, and students who were comfortable at six o'clock are not. DAMAC Hills 2 families typically do one of three things: shift to a late-morning or early-afternoon slot, move to a post-Iftar slot later in the evening, or pause part of the month and resume with a heavier block afterwards. All three work. Pretending the usual Tuesday at six still works is the one that does not.

Prayer times matter year-round, not only in Ramadan, and they move through the calendar. We set slots around them from the start rather than asking a family to raise it. The same applies to Islamic and public holidays, to the long summer, and to the travel weekends that are a normal part of life in this community — sessions continue while a family is away, because the tutor's location is already part of the arrangement rather than an obstacle to it.

The practical commitment is small: tell us the new pattern and we reset the fixed slot. What we try to avoid is the drift where a session is cancelled, then rescheduled, then cancelled, and nobody says out loud that the arrangement has ended.

sections.heading: Why distance stopped being the thing that matters
paragraphs: The whole premise of a near me search is that proximity is the scarce resource. For a Diploma subject in DAMAC Hills 2 it is not. The scarce resource is somebody who has taught that specific course at that specific level, and the population of such people in the Dubailand belt with a free weekday evening is small enough that for some subjects it is empty.

Consider the arithmetic. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils in 2024-25, with the IB at around 7% of enrolment, spread across the entire emirate. Only the final two years of that cohort sit the Diploma. Narrow to one subject at Higher Level and you have a small citywide group of students and a smaller group of qualified teachers, most of whom are serving school staff — and the MoHRE permit code of conduct, along with ADEK's professional-ethics rules in Abu Dhabi, bars a teacher from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

Market rates make the same point from the money side. Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: qualified online subject tutors run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; in-home one-to-one visits run AED 180-500 including travel, per Bestimate and local listings; budget online starts at AED 33-65 with Tutopiya and EdFlik. The in-home premium does not buy more expertise. It buys a car journey.

Those figures belong to the providers named and are market rates, not IB Gram prices. We do not publish a rate card on these pages, because the honest number depends on subject, level and the weeks remaining — the free trial and the consultation are where you get a real quote.

sections.heading: The workload a DAMAC Hills 2 Diploma student is actually carrying
paragraphs: Parents often underestimate this, and then read a dip in grades as a motivation problem. A full Diploma candidate is running six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, plus a 4,000-word Extended Essay, plus Creativity, Activity, Service hours, plus an Internal Assessment in every single subject. That is six separate coursework projects with six separate internal deadlines, all set by the school rather than by the IB, and all landing in the same two terms.

Add the commute. A student travelling forty minutes each way to an inner-city IB school is spending more than an hour a day in a car, which is an hour not spent on any of the above. Over a term that is a substantial fraction of the independent study the course assumes exists. It is one of the real reasons DAMAC Hills 2 Diploma families end up looking for help, and it is a structural problem rather than a failing on the student's part.

What good tutoring does in that situation is mostly triage. Not more hours of everything, but a clear view of which deadline is closest, which Internal Assessment is at risk of being designed badly rather than written badly, and which subject is losing marks to a fixable technique rather than to missing knowledge. A specialist who sees the whole picture once a week is worth more than three tutors each optimising for their own subject.

That is also why we keep a fixed slot and a single tutor where we can. The value compounds: by the third month the tutor knows which mistakes are habits, which deadline the student is quietly avoiding, and which subject the school report is overstating.

Internal deadlines are set by the school, not by the IB, and cluster in two terms

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma coursework
paragraphs: This has to be said plainly on a UAE IB page, because the search results for Dubai IB help include operators who sell finished coursework — one advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is not a shortcut with a price attached. It is an academic-honesty breach, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice.

The permitted side is broad and useful. A tutor may teach the content the assessment rests on. They may explain what each criterion asks for and what marks it carries. They may help narrow a research question until it is genuinely answerable. They may review a method and point out that it will not generate usable data. They may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it. All of that is ordinary teaching.

The line is authorship. A tutor may not write any part of the work, supply text to be inserted, rewrite the student's prose, provide a fill-in template, or edit a draft to a finish so that the submitted piece is substantially theirs. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own and the supervisor signs alongside them, so this is not a technicality.

We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to the awarding bodies. We cite them, link the official source and teach from them, which is both lawful and more useful than a folder of PDFs.
bullets: Permitted: teaching content, explaining criteria, coaching a question, reviewing method, feedback on the student's own draft
Not permitted: writing, drafting, rewriting, templating or editing coursework to a finish
No past papers or mark schemes supplied as downloads — we link the official source

sections.heading: What we will not tell you
paragraphs: A few things are missing from this page on purpose, and the omissions are worth naming because their presence elsewhere should make you suspicious.

There is no specific IB exam date. The IB's own site blocks automated retrieval, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, and we are not going to put an unverified date in front of a parent who will act on it. UAE schools sit the May session; get the exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we quote those, including the correction that Cambridge's February/March series is India-only while UAE candidates sit June and November.

There is no star rating, no satisfaction percentage and no average score achieved by our students. Competitors publish figures like 4.9 from several hundred reviews, sometimes two different versions on the same page, and none of them states a sample size, a date or a method. A number without those three things is decoration. We would rather have no number than a decorative one.

There is no regulator claim. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and will not send a tutor to a DAMAC Hills 2 address. And there is no guarantee of a grade, a points total or an improvement, because nobody can honestly offer one and the offer itself tells you what kind of operation you are dealing with.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free for your subject
paragraphs: Nobody covers every IB subject at every level in every term, and a provider implying otherwise is one to distrust. Theory of Knowledge at short notice, Higher Level Computer Science, smaller Group 2 languages, Music and Film are genuinely scarce, and a family asking in March deserves an answer rather than a holding pattern.

So: if a matching specialist is free, we propose them and you take a free trial lesson with that person. If the only available specialist works from another time zone, we say so and offer the slots that actually exist — which for most of our roster means early morning or evening in Gulf Standard Time, and for a DAMAC Hills 2 Diploma student an 8pm slot often fits better than anything local would have. If nobody suitable is free, we say that too.

What we will never offer as a fallback is a home visit, because there is no UAE visiting service to fall back on. There is also no fallback where a general tutor is quietly substituted for a Higher Level specialist eight weeks before a session. We would rather lose the enquiry, and we have.

If the match turns out to be wrong after it starts, say so in the first fortnight. A mismatch between a competent tutor and a particular student is common and is nobody's failure. It is a reason to change tutor, not a reason to spend a term hoping.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a session can start after the DAMAC Hills 2 school run?
faqs.answer: For a short run — Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, or South View in Remraam — around 4:00pm to 4:15pm, allowing a short settling gap. From Motor City or Dubai Sports City in peak traffic, 4:45pm is realistic. From an inner-city IB school in Al Barsha, 5:15pm, and many of those families choose an 8pm slot instead. The reason these times are possible at all is that nobody is driving to you. A visiting tutor leaving another part of Dubai in the same traffic is realistically starting at half six.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor who lives near DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Some, and for primary or general MYP support the local pool is adequate. For a named Diploma subject at Higher Level it is often empty. The Diploma is roughly 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils spread across the whole emirate, and only the final two years sit it, so a single course at a single level is a small citywide cohort. Most qualified teachers are serving school staff, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars tutoring students enrolled at their own school. Online matching is how that constraint gets removed.

faqs.question: Which schools do DAMAC Hills 2 children actually go to?
faqs.answer: Jebel Ali School sits in neighbouring DAMAC Hills. On the Al Qudra side families use South View School, The Aquila School, Ranches Primary School, JESS Arabian Ranches and Fairgreen International School, which runs the IB continuum. For secondary, most travel to GEMS Metropole in Motor City, the Dubai Sports City cluster including Victory Heights Primary, GEMS United and Bradenton Preparatory Academy, Dunecrest American School or Lycée Français Jean Mermoz. We name these as context and have no affiliation with any of them. The school matters because it sets both the scheme of work and the finish time.

faqs.question: Which weekly slot works best for a Year 12 student out here?
faqs.answer: Usually the late one, 8pm to 9:30pm, and usually ninety minutes rather than sixty. Diploma students work late anyway, are sharpest once the house is quiet, and need a block long enough to complete a past-paper section and mark it together rather than rushing. The 4:30pm slot suits MYP students and younger Diploma students better. The 7pm slot looks convenient but takes the student's own most productive independent hour, which is usually a bad trade in an exam year.

faqs.question: How do sessions change during Ramadan in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: They move, and they should. School days shorten and the evening reorganises around Iftar, so the usual six o'clock slot stops working. Families here typically do one of three things: switch to a late-morning or early-afternoon session, move to a post-Iftar slot later in the evening, or pause for part of the month and resume afterwards with a heavier block. Content also shifts towards consolidation rather than new teaching. Tell us which pattern suits and we reset the fixed slot deliberately rather than letting cancellations accumulate.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our house in DAMAC Hills 2 if we pay more?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE at any price — in-home tutoring is a service we offer in India only, and there is no UAE visiting arrangement to upgrade to. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published market rates of around AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from the Al Qudra corridor a fair share of that is the drive. Our position is that the premium buys presence rather than expertise, and for a Diploma subject expertise is the thing in short supply.

faqs.question: How much time does the commute cost a Diploma student here?
faqs.answer: For a student travelling to an inner-city IB school, often more than an hour a day door to door, which over a term is a substantial share of the independent study the Diploma assumes. That is one of the real reasons DAMAC Hills 2 families seek help: six subjects with six Internal Assessments, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, all competing for fewer usable hours than the course was designed around. It is a structural squeeze rather than a motivation problem, and triage across the workload helps more than extra hours in one subject.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle more than one of my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and there is a real argument for it. A tutor who sees the whole workload can weigh a Chemistry Internal Assessment deadline against a Maths mock instead of each tutor optimising for their own subject. Mathematics and Physics overlap enough that one specialist often covers both credibly. Chemistry and Biology diverge at Higher Level. What we will not do is stretch one tutor across courses they do not genuinely teach to save a second match, because two correct specialists always beat one willing generalist.

faqs.question: What do IB tutors charge for families in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market figures, read in October 2026: budget online from AED 33-65 an hour (Tutopiya, EdFlik), qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270, and in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel. Monthly packages advertised run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits. These belong to the providers named, not to us. We quote after the free trial, since the number depends on subject, level and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: When is the IB exam session for schools near DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no specific IB date, and the reason is worth knowing: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, and we will not put an unverified date in front of a parent who will plan around it. Get exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. For IGCSE siblings, Cambridge runs June and November series — the February/March series is India-only — and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

faqs.question: Where exactly does IA and Extended Essay coaching stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: With it, yes; instead of them, no. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion asks for and the marks it carries, help narrow a research question until it is answerable, review whether a method will generate usable data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply text to insert, rewrite the prose or edit it to a finish. Operators in this market sell completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice risk to the student's whole Diploma.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a Dubai family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any individual charging for private tuition in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time via its smart app, website or e-services, and eligibility covers school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see the permit and verify it with MoHRE. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published, so ignore circulating figures.

faqs.question: Who regulates the schools DAMAC Hills 2 families use?
faqs.answer: KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Elsewhere in the country it is ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None of them regulates private tutors — that sits with MoHRE's permit — so treat any tutoring provider implying regulator endorsement with caution.

faqs.question: How quickly can you arrange a tutor for a DAMAC Hills 2 family?
faqs.answer: For common Diploma subjects at Standard Level and most MYP work, usually a specialist and a trial slot within a few days. Higher Level sciences, Higher Level Computer Science, Theory of Knowledge at short notice and smaller language options take longer and sometimes cannot be covered in a given term at all. We tell you which case you are in rather than keeping the enquiry open. If the only matching specialist works from another time zone, we say so and offer the slots that genuinely exist before you commit.

faqs.question: What if the slot works but the tutor does not?
faqs.answer: Tell us in the first fortnight and we rematch. A mismatch between a capable tutor and a particular student is common and is nobody's failure — pace, explanation style and personality matter more than credentials once basic competence is established. If the trial lesson itself is wrong, nothing has been spent and we propose somebody else. The thing not to do is spend a term hoping it improves, which is how families lose the money and the term together.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-deira.tutorsIntro: The tutors here are matched to a Diploma subject, a level and a position in the two-year calendar. A DP1 autumn plan and a DP2 spring plan are different pieces of work. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Two years, and only some of the weeks are worth buying
paragraphs: Deira is dense, old and well connected. Families live in apartment blocks between the Creek and Abu Baker Al Siddique Road, children travel out to schools in Al Qusais, Al Mamzar, Bur Dubai and across the water to Al Garhoud and Festival City, and the Metro does more of the moving than cars do. Diploma students here are a smaller group than IGCSE students, because the IB accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, and that scarcity shows up in how hard it is to find the right subject specialist within any short radius.

The more useful thing to understand first, though, is the shape of the programme. The Diploma is two years, six subjects across six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus three core elements: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words, and Creativity, Activity, Service running across about eighteen months. Up to three points come from the core, out of a maximum of 45. Every subject carries internally assessed coursework. Almost all of the external assessment lands in a single session at the end.

That structure has a consequence most families only notice halfway through: the two years are not evenly loaded. DP1 is deceptively calm in its first term and then produces a pile of internal deadlines in its second and third. DP2 begins with the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay both live, runs into predicted grades and university applications, and then has a long run of revision in which almost nothing new can be learned. Buying tutoring in the quiet weeks and nothing in the heavy ones is a common and expensive error.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Deira family that solves two problems at once. The first is subject supply: matching online means a student needing Chemistry HL or History HL is choosing from every available specialist rather than from the few who will travel into this district at 5pm. The second is domestic: in dense apartment housing the quiet hour moves day to day, and an online slot can move with it.

What follows is the programme as a calendar. A term-by-term map of both years. The core counted backwards, because Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are where timelines slip. The internal assessment deadlines that sit inside the school's own calendar. Predicted grades and the university application months. A table of when tutoring money is best spent across the two years, which is the part no competitor publishes. And an honest statement about IB examination dates, which we will not print, and why.
