dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-deira.programmesIntro: The Diploma divides into four working phases rather than two years, and the tutoring question is different in each. Knowing which phase you are in is the first step to spending sensibly.

programmes.name: DP1, first term
programmes.description: Subject content starts, the step up from IGCSE or MYP becomes visible, and nothing is due yet. The quietest period of the two years and the cheapest moment to fix a gap, because a weakness identified now has eighteen months to be repaired rather than eight weeks.
programmes.countryNote: Deira students arriving from IGCSE at a Bur Dubai or Al Qusais school into Diploma provision at a Festival City school often take a term to notice the difference in written expectation. A single weekly session in this term frequently removes the need for three in DP2.

programmes.name: DP1, second and third terms
programmes.description: Internal assessment work begins in several subjects at once, the Extended Essay topic and supervisor are settled, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition falls in most schools, and CAS has to be visibly running. The busiest underestimated period in the programme.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Dubai families most often discover that two internal assessments have been set in the same fortnight. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's full internal deadline calendar at the start of the year and put it on a wall rather than in an inbox.

programmes.name: DP2, first term
programmes.description: The Extended Essay moves to completion, the Theory of Knowledge essay is drafted against a prescribed title, remaining internal assessments are finished, predicted grades are issued and university applications are submitted. Academic content teaching competes with all of it.
programmes.countryNote: University deadlines bite here. UK applications run to a mid-October date for certain courses and a late-January main deadline; United States early rounds fall in November with regular rounds in January. Predicted grades are issued by the school before these, so the work that earns them happens earlier than parents expect.

programmes.name: DP2, final terms
programmes.description: Mock examinations, the last internal deadlines, and then a long revision run into the examination session. Very little new content can be learned in this phase; what can be improved is paper technique, timing and the handful of topics a student has never understood.
programmes.countryNote: Mocks here are the most informative thing a Deira family will see before results, and the marked scripts are more useful than the grade. A session spent on the scripts, sorting lost marks by cause, is worth more than three spent revising the syllabus again.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-deira.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects Deira families ask about most, with a note on when in the two years each one tends to need help. Timing matters as much as subject choice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic and proof-heavy, with HL carrying additional content and a further paper. Cumulative, so help is worth far more in DP1 than DP2. The exploration should be topic-settled by the end of DP1, because a topic with too little mathematical substance cannot be rescued later.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics-led with heavier technology use. Easier to support late than Analysis and Approaches, because more of the marks sit in applying named techniques to given contexts. The route decision should be made against university requirements before DP1 begins.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The internal assessment needs a research question narrow enough to produce real quantitative data, and that decision belongs in DP1. Content support is most valuable across DP1; in DP2 the productive work is unfamiliar data analysis and extended written responses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity early, fields and quantum later, so a DP1 gap compounds. Written explanation quality is where most marks are lost, and it improves steadily with practice rather than suddenly, which argues for weekly work from DP1 rather than a late block.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most content-heavy of the sciences and therefore the most improvable in DP2, because command-term discipline and a condensed definition set can be built in weeks. Data-based questions reward careful reading of axes and units more than recall.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries the marks, and the internal assessment is a set of commentaries on recent news articles, each with its own deadline through DP1. Students lose marks summarising the article instead of applying a named diagram, which is a correctable habit.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks applied to real organisations, with HL adding content and a pre-seen element. The internal assessment requires genuine research access, which must be arranged early in DP1 or the project runs out of material.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis across literary and non-literary texts, an individual oral and a written component, with HL adding a further essay. The individual oral is scheduled by the school, often earlier than families expect, and needs preparation on its own timetable.

subjects.name: History and Psychology
subjects.description: Essay structure, source or study evaluation, and a word-limited internal investigation. These are the hardest Diploma subjects to staff in Dubai, so a request for either at Higher Level should be made weeks before it becomes urgent.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
subjects.description: The exhibition and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title, an Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words, and CAS across about eighteen months. Together worth up to three points. Paid support here is process coaching and nothing else: question design, research method, referencing and timeline discipline.

regions.note: Dense apartment blocks with the Metro Green Line running through. Diploma students here mostly travel south or east to school, and the practical constraint in the evening is a quiet room rather than a free hour.

sections.heading: The two years, term by term
paragraphs: Below is the Diploma as a working calendar rather than a prospectus. Dates in it are relative to the school year rather than absolute, because school internal deadlines vary and because IB external dates must come from your own coordinator rather than from any website. What does not vary is the order, and the order is what a family needs in order to plan spending.

The shape is worth stating in words first. DP1 term one has no deadlines and all the opportunity. DP1 terms two and three carry the first internal assessments, the Extended Essay topic decision and, in most schools, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition. DP2 term one is the heaviest period in the programme: Extended Essay completion, the Theory of Knowledge essay, remaining internal assessments, predicted grades and university applications all overlap. DP2 terms two and three are mocks and then revision, where the marginal value of new content teaching falls close to zero.

The single most useful action available to a Deira Diploma parent is to get the school's internal deadline calendar in writing at the start of DP1 and put it somewhere physical. Internal deadlines are what actually bind — an internal assessment due to the teacher in March is the real date, whatever the external submission window says — and they are almost always earlier than families assume. Two internal assessments landing in the same fortnight is normal and foreseeable, and it is foreseeable only if somebody has the calendar.
Use the table to locate your child, then read the spending table further down for what is worth buying from that position.

sections.heading: The core counted backwards: TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS
paragraphs: The core is worth up to three points out of 45 and causes a disproportionate share of the stress, because unlike subject content it has no weekly lesson rhythm to carry it. It is supervised rather than taught, which means a student who does nothing for two months is not noticed until a check-in, by which point two months are gone.

The Extended Essay is up to 4,000 words of independent research in a subject the student chooses, with a school-appointed supervisor and a set of internal reflection sessions. Almost every Extended Essay that goes wrong goes wrong on timeline rather than on ability. The workable shape is subject and rough question settled in DP1 term two, supervisor conversations through term three, the bulk of the research done over the summer between the years, and the essay completed early in DP2 term one — before university applications swallow the autumn.

Theory of Knowledge runs across both years, with an exhibition in most schools during DP1 and an essay of about 1,600 words on a prescribed title in DP2. The essay titles are released ahead of the session and the prescribed title choice is the single decision that determines how hard the essay will be. Students pick titles that sound interesting rather than titles they can argue with real examples, and that choice is worth one coaching session on its own.

CAS runs across about eighteen months and is not graded, but it has to be completed and evidenced, and an incomplete CAS portfolio is a genuine risk to the Diploma rather than a minor administrative matter. The only thing a tutor can usefully do here is remind a student that the reflections are the record, and that reflections written in one evening eighteen months late are visibly that.

sections.heading: The deadlines inside the deadlines: internal assessments
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed coursework, and the dates that bind are the school's, not the board's. A teacher who needs to mark, moderate and submit will set an internal deadline weeks or months before any external window, and that internal date is the one a family should be planning around. Parents who track the external window and ignore the internal one are consistently surprised.

The clustering is the real problem. Six subjects each with coursework means six internal deadlines, and because most schools set them in the same part of DP1 term three and DP2 term one, two or three regularly fall within a fortnight. A student with Chemistry, Mathematics and Economics internal assessments in the same two weeks is not short of ability; they are short of calendar. The fix is entirely preventative: get the dates, lay them out, and move the preparation for one of them forward by a month.

The other recurring error is a research question chosen for interest rather than feasibility. In the sciences this means a question that cannot generate enough quantitative data; in Mathematics, an exploration topic with too little mathematical substance to show genuine engagement; in Economics, a news article that does not actually support a named diagram. All three are discovered late and all three are cheap to prevent, which is why a single session on question design early in the process is the best-value purchase in the Diploma.

What a tutor can do here is bounded and worth stating. They may teach the underlying content, challenge whether a question is answerable with the data available, explain the criteria, mark a completed draft against them, and teach referencing. They may not write, draft, edit to completion or supply data. That boundary is covered properly further down this page.
bullets: The school's internal deadline is the real one; get all six in writing

sections.heading: Predicted grades and the university months
paragraphs: Predicted grades are issued by the school on the evidence available at the time, which means the work that earns them happens earlier than most families realise. By the autumn of DP2 a student's predicted grades are largely a function of DP1 attainment and the first internal assessments, and those are the numbers that go on a university application. A family who plans to improve in the spring of DP2 has improved after the application was submitted.

The application calendar compounds this. United Kingdom applications run to a mid-October deadline for certain courses and a main deadline in late January. United States early rounds fall in November with regular rounds in January. Applications to UAE and regional universities have their own schedules, and some require Ministry of Education equivalency documentation that takes time to assemble. All of these sit in DP2 term one, alongside the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay.

The planning consequence is clear and almost nobody acts on it. If a particular grade is needed for a particular course, the tutoring that secures the prediction has to happen in DP1 and the first weeks of DP2, not in the final two terms. This is the strongest argument there is for buying one weekly subject early rather than a large block late, and it is the opposite of what most families do.

For students aiming at UAE universities there is a further step. Ministry of Education equivalency has published requirements for the British and American tracks; for the IB there is no points threshold in the sources we can cite, so confirm it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs and is not something any tutoring provider performs, guarantees or can speed up.

sections.heading: When in the two years the money is best spent
paragraphs: This is the table that matters, and it is built on a simple observation: the value of a tutoring hour varies enormously depending on when in the Diploma it is bought, and most families buy at the point of maximum anxiety rather than maximum return. The published Dubai bands give the prices; the calendar gives the value.

The bands, with sources, read in October 2026. Budget online generalists advertise from roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialists are quoted AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table in the same range. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits run AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors, a premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour over the online equivalent that buys proximity and nothing else.

Now apply the calendar. An hour bought in DP1 term one, on the subject that will be hardest, has eighteen months to compound and can change a predicted grade. An hour bought on internal assessment question design costs the same and prevents a rescue worth ten times as much. An hour bought in DP2 term one competes with the Extended Essay and the application for the student's attention and frequently achieves less than the same hour bought a year earlier. An hour bought in the final fortnight competes with revision and usually buys parental reassurance rather than marks.

The honest summary is that the same AED 250 is worth several times more in September of DP1 than in April of DP2. Nobody selling tutoring has an incentive to tell a family that, which is exactly why it belongs on the page.

sections.heading: Match time against your deadline
paragraphs: Because the IB is a small share of Dubai enrolment, specialist supply is uneven and this is where a near-me search genuinely fails a Deira family. Mathematics and the sciences at Standard Level can usually be matched quickly. Higher Level sciences take longer. History and Psychology at Higher Level, and Group 2 languages at the right course level, can take a fortnight or more to match properly, and nobody in this market publishes that.

The reason to publish it is that it interacts with the calendar. If an internal assessment deadline is three weeks away and the realistic match time for History HL is two weeks, the honest conversation is about whether the remaining week is worth buying, not about pretending a tutor is available tomorrow. We would rather give a family a date and lose the booking than take the enquiry and fill it with somebody who has taught a different qualification.

Two practical consequences for a parent. First, request early: a DP1 enquiry made in September gets the specialist; the same enquiry in February competes with every other family who left it. Second, be specific: Mathematics AA HL and Mathematics AI SL are different requests, and saying maths produces a slower and worse match than naming the course and the level.

sections.heading: Why this page does not print an IB examination date
paragraphs: Every other page in this search result that mentions timing does so vaguely, and the few that give dates give them without sources. We are going to be explicit about a limitation instead, because a wrong date is worse than no date when a parent acts on it.

IB examination and results dates are published by the International Baccalaureate Organization, and ibo.org blocks automated access, which means no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources exist and broadly agree with each other, but broadly agreeing is not the same as verified, and a date that is wrong by a week is a date that could cost a family a flight or a revision plan. So this page states the structure — UAE schools sit the May session, with November available — and sends you to the only two sources that can confirm the specifics: your school's Diploma coordinator and ibo.org directly.

Where dates can be verified they appear on our pages with their attribution. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, for instance, the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are checkable. IB dates, at present, are not, and we would rather say so than pad the page.

The practical advice that follows is the same advice an experienced Diploma coordinator would give. Work from internal deadlines, which are the ones that actually bind. Treat the external window as fixed and unknowable in detail until the coordinator confirms it. And plan the revision run backwards from the mock results rather than forwards from a date on a website.

sections.heading: The honesty boundary across IA, EE and TOK
paragraphs: At least one operation competing for searches like this sells completed Internal Assessments. The relevant fact for a Deira family is the asymmetry: the fee is paid once, the malpractice finding attaches to the student permanently, and the possible consequence is the loss of the Diploma. The seller carries nothing. No price makes that a reasonable purchase, and this page would be dishonest if it discussed cost without saying so.

Legitimate help is narrower, cheaper and more durable. A tutor may teach the content an assessment rests on. They may question a research question until it is answerable with available data. They may explain the assessment criteria, read them with the student and mark a completed draft against them. They may teach referencing and show how to acknowledge a source properly. They may challenge a method, point out that a data set cannot support a conclusion, and hold a student to a written timeline. For Theory of Knowledge they may help the student test whether a prescribed title can be argued with real examples.

A tutor may not write, draft or edit any part of a submission to completion, supply data the student did not collect, dictate sentences for transcription, or make a product. The working test we apply is whether the student can explain, unprompted, why each sentence and each decision is in the work. If they cannot, it does not belong there.

Stated positively, the help worth paying for is the help that transfers. A student taught to interrogate their own research question will do it again in the Extended Essay, and at university. A student handed a finished internal assessment has bought one grade, learned nothing, and acquired a risk that sits on their record until somebody notices.

faqs.question: Which phase of the Diploma is the best value for tutoring money?
faqs.answer: DP1 term one, on whichever subject will be hardest. Content is cumulative, so a gap fixed then has eighteen months to compound in the student's favour, and predicted grades issued in DP2 autumn rest largely on DP1 attainment and the first internal assessments. The same money spent in the final two terms arrives after the predictions have been sent. Most families buy at the point of maximum anxiety rather than maximum return, which is the single most expensive habit in this market.

faqs.question: Why are predicted grades decided so early?
faqs.answer: Because the school issues them on the evidence available at the time, and the applications they support fall in DP2 autumn and winter. United Kingdom applications run to a mid-October deadline for some courses and a main deadline in late January; United States early rounds fall in November with regular rounds in January. That means improvement in the spring of DP2 arrives after the prediction was submitted. If a specific grade is needed for a specific course, the work has to happen in DP1.

faqs.question: When should the Extended Essay actually be finished?
faqs.answer: Early in DP2 term one, with the bulk of the research done over the summer between the two years. The failure mode is almost never ability; it is timeline, because the essay has no weekly lesson to carry it and a student who does nothing for two months is not noticed until a supervisor check-in. A workable shape is subject and rough question in DP1 term two, supervisor conversations in term three, research over the summer, completion before applications swallow the autumn.

faqs.question: How much of the Diploma score comes from the core?
faqs.answer: Up to three points out of a maximum of 45, awarded on the combination of the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay. CAS is not graded but has to be completed and evidenced, and an incomplete CAS portfolio is a genuine risk to the Diploma rather than an administrative detail. Three points sounds small until a university offer sits at a total the student misses by two, which is why the core deserves the same planning discipline as a subject.

faqs.question: Two internal assessments are due in the same fortnight. What now?
faqs.answer: That clustering is normal and foreseeable, and the fix is to move one forward rather than to work harder in the fortnight itself. Get every internal deadline from the coordinator in one list at the start of the year, lay them out on a wall calendar, and when two collide start the preparation for one of them a month earlier. If the collision has already arrived, prioritise the assessment with the larger weighting and the one whose data collection cannot be compressed.

faqs.question: Will you tell me when the IB exams are?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is worth knowing. The IB publishes session and results dates, but ibo.org blocks automated access, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources broadly agree, and broadly agreeing is not verified. A date wrong by a week is a date a family might book a flight around. UAE schools sit the May session with November available; for the specifics, ask your Diploma coordinator or check ibo.org directly.

faqs.question: How long does it take to find a History HL tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Two weeks or more, realistically, and sometimes longer. History and Psychology at Higher Level, and Group 2 languages at the right course level, are the hardest Diploma subjects to staff in this market. If your deadline is three weeks away, the honest conversation is about whether the remaining week is worth buying rather than about pretending somebody is free tomorrow. Request early: a September enquiry gets the specialist, the same enquiry in February competes with everybody who waited.

faqs.question: What should we do with the time between DP1 and DP2?
faqs.answer: Extended Essay research, and pre-teaching whichever DP2 topics the student is most likely to struggle with. The summer is the only block of the two years with no competing deadlines, morning slots are available, and work done then removes pressure from the heaviest term in the programme. Families who use it well arrive in DP2 with the essay research done and the autumn free for applications. Families who do not spend DP2 autumn doing three things at once.

faqs.question: Is a specialist worth AED 300 an hour for Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Standard Level content teaching sits comfortably in the qualified band of AED 150 to 300, where Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, and a strong graduate who has read the syllabus does it well. What the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above buys is diagnosis — why a student plateaus at a 5 — and internal assessment supervision, both of which need somebody who has marked against the criteria. Match the band to the job rather than to the subject name.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose the Theory of Knowledge prescribed title?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the best-value single sessions in the Diploma. Titles are released ahead of the session and students pick the one that sounds interesting rather than the one they can argue with real examples from their own subjects and experience. A tutor can test each shortlisted title by asking the student to produce two concrete examples on the spot; the title that survives that test is the one to write. They cannot draft the essay.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our building in Deira?
faqs.answer: Not from us. All UAE lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is part of our India service. In this district the format solves two real problems: Diploma specialists are scarce and would not reliably travel here at 5pm, and in dense apartment housing the quiet hour moves day to day. In-home tutoring exists in the Dubai market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel for families who need it.

faqs.question: My child is three weeks from the exams. What is worth buying?
faqs.answer: Almost nothing, and we will say so. In the final fortnight a student needs sleep, uninterrupted revision time and a sensible paper plan. One session on paper order and question triage can recover marks currently being thrown away by misallocated time. Beyond that, additional sessions compete with revision rather than supporting it, and in our experience they are bought to relieve parental anxiety. The money is better held back for a resit decision if one becomes necessary.

faqs.question: How do mock scripts change the DP2 plan?
faqs.answer: They should drive it entirely. Go through every lost mark and sort it by cause: content not known, method or reasoning not shown in a way the mark scheme credits, or question misread and mistimed. Those three need different work, and most students find the largest category is not the first, which is encouraging because the other two are faster to fix. A plan written from the scripts targets the largest category; a plan written from the syllabus targets everything and moves nothing.

faqs.question: Does a Maths AA or AI decision need to be made before DP1?
faqs.answer: Yes, and against named university requirements rather than against which course looks easier. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-heavy and is the usual prerequisite for engineering and quantitative economics; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-led and suits business, design and several social science routes. Some universities specify Analysis and Approaches explicitly. Check the entry requirements of two or three target courses before the choice is confirmed, because changing route mid-programme is disruptive and sometimes impossible.

faqs.question: What does equivalency require for an IB student in the UAE?
faqs.answer: That is the honest gap in the published record. The Ministry of Education requirements we can cite cover the British track — five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus an Advanced Level pass — and the American track, with English shown by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, and SAT Math of at least 450. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so none is published here. Confirm it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority.

faqs.question: Is one weekly session enough for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: In one subject, usually yes, provided it starts early. A Diploma week already contains six subjects, coursework in all of them, the core and CAS, and for a Deira student a long commute each way. One protected weekly slot that survives two years in the hardest subject, plus a short core process block and a post-mock technique block, is a complete plan. Two weekly subjects is manageable in the final year if the evenings are genuinely free. Three is not a plan.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-difc.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects at the levels DIFC families ask for most: Higher Level sciences, both mathematics routes, Economics and English. Each session runs over live video, one student to one tutor, on a slot chosen around your child's actual bus time.

intro.heading: DIFC has no school of its own, and that is the whole problem
paragraphs: The Dubai International Financial Centre is roughly half a square kilometre of towers, podium levels and a gated district of offices. It contains law firms, banks, three dozen restaurants and several thousand apartments. It contains no private school. Every child living in Index Tower, Burj Daman, Limestone House, Park Towers, Central Park Towers or the Gate District apartments leaves the district to go to school and comes back into it afterwards. That single fact is why a search for an IB tutor near me in DIFC behaves differently from the same search typed in Arabian Ranches or Jumeirah, where the school is often a ten-minute drive and a tutor who lives in the same community is genuinely nearby.

From a DIFC address the realistic school catchment runs outward in four directions, and each one carries a different journey time. Al Jaddaf and Culture Village sit across the Creek, close on a map and slow at 7am. Sobha Hartland, Meydan and Nad Al Sheba are a straight run down Al Khail Road in the morning and a crawl back at pickup. Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and the Jumeirah strip mean Sheikh Zayed Road twice a day. Academic City and Dubai Festival City are a forty-minute bus each way for the families who chose a school rather than a commute. The IB Diploma is taught at schools in all four directions, which is exactly why DIFC children are scattered across more school timetables than a villa community's children ever are.

The consequence for tutoring is arithmetic rather than opinion. A Diploma student whose bus pulls into the district at 4.10pm, who needs twenty minutes to eat and change, has one usable study block before the evening collapses: roughly 5.00pm to 7.00pm, four or five days a week. A tutor who has to drive into DIFC, find visitor parking in a basement with a barrier and a reception desk, and then drive out again, consumes a meaningful share of that block before the first question is asked. The travelling tutor is not lazy or overpriced; the geometry of a financial district simply works against them.

Online delivery removes the geometry. The session starts at 5.00pm because 5.00pm is when the student is at the desk, and it ends when the two hours of usable attention end rather than when the drive home starts. More importantly, it changes who is available. Matching by travel radius means choosing from the tutors who can reach your tower; matching by subject means choosing from the tutors who have taught your child's exact paper. For a Standard Level subject the difference is small. For Higher Level Physics, Chemistry at Higher Level, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or an Economics Internal Assessment due in eleven days, the difference is the whole point.

This page is written from the school run outward. It names the schools DIFC children actually attend and where they sit, sets out what the weekday looks like hour by hour, shows what the Dubai market charges and what the travel premium inside that price actually buys, and then deals with the parts nobody writes about: the KHDA mandatory subjects eating into the school week, the order the Diploma year arrives in, and the line a tutor may not cross on an Internal Assessment. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Everything here is delivered one-to-one over live video.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-difc.programmesIntro: DIFC children sit across all three International Baccalaureate stages, often in different schools and sometimes in the same family. What a tutor needs to know changes completely between them, so the matching question is never only 'IB' but which stage, which year and which assessment is next.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Progress is reported against transdisciplinary units of inquiry, learner-profile attributes and an exhibition in the final year. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the written and spoken English a unit of inquiry assumes, rather than examination technique. Sessions are shorter, usually forty to fifty minutes, because attention rather than syllabus coverage is the limit.
programmes.countryNote: For a DIFC family this is the stage where the commute hurts most, because a six-year-old on a forty-minute bus arrives home with very little left. Online sessions at 4.45pm, in the apartment, without a second car journey, are the only version that is realistically sustainable across a term. Several families run two shorter sessions a week rather than one long one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, lettered A to D, scored out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There is no single final paper. The Personal Project in the final year is the piece parents hear about most. Marks are lost on criterion wording far more often than on content, because students answer the question they expected rather than the criterion in front of them.
programmes.countryNote: DIFC pupils at Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, Clarion School or Dubai International Academy Al Barsha arrive in MYP from very different primary routes, and the criterion-based marking is new to almost all of them. The practical work is teaching a student to read criterion B as a set of instructions. Personal Project support is process coaching and feedback only; the project remains the student's own.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1-7 with up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. Internal Assessments carry roughly a fifth to a quarter of most subject grades and fall due across the second year, usually clustered in the same six weeks.
programmes.countryNote: This is where a DIFC address starts to matter financially. A Diploma student needing Higher Level Physics and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is looking for two narrow specialists, not one generalist, and the pool of people who can reach a DIFC tower and teach either at that level by 5.30pm is small. Online matching widens it to anyone who can teach the paper at that hour.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language-development portfolio and personal and professional skills. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools. Assessment is a mix of the Diploma's external papers for the chosen courses and internally assessed components for the rest.
programmes.countryNote: Few DIFC families encounter the CP, because it is licensed at only a handful of Dubai schools and tends to sit alongside a particular career pathway. Where it does appear, the Diploma-course component is tutored exactly as a Diploma subject is, and the reflective project is handled as process coaching: planning, sourcing and feedback on the student's own drafts.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-difc.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects DIFC Diploma and Middle Years students ask for most often, with the part that actually costs marks rather than the syllabus blurb. The pattern is consistent: the content is understood and the assessment is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation under time pressure. At Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended two-part investigation worth 20% of the grade, and it is where unprepared students lose most, because nothing in classwork resembles it. Standard Level students usually lose marks on reasoning shown too briefly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and a required graphic display calculator skill set. Students who switched from Analysis mid-course tend to underestimate the statistical inference at Higher Level. The common failure is a correct model with no interpretation sentence, which scores the method mark and nothing else.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity carry the bulk of Paper 1 and 2 marks. Higher Level adds induction and quantum topics that arrive late in the second year, often while the Internal Assessment is also due. Marks go on unit errors, significant figures and written explanations that describe rather than explain.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium. Higher Level extends every topic rather than adding separate ones, so a Standard Level gap compounds. The data-based questions reward a student who can read a table and state a trend precisely; most answers lose marks on vague comparative language.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of defined terminology plus data analysis. The frequent problem is a student who knows the process and cannot name it in the command term the question used. Higher Level adds plant and animal physiology depth that rewards diagram-based revision over rereading notes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation. Three commentaries on published news articles form the Internal Assessment, each with a word limit, and they are marked on application of theory rather than on writing. Higher Level adds policy calculation that students meet for the first time in a past paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay, and both reward a student who writes about technique rather than plot. The Individual Oral requires a global issue linked to two texts, and the planning rather than the speaking is what needs supervising.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, frameworks and a research project. Students lose marks by describing a framework instead of applying it to the case material in front of them. Higher Level adds an extended research project where the choice of organisation determines how many marks are reachable.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data structures and a solution-development project. The written papers assume fluency in a pseudocode style no school teaches consistently. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and a case study released annually, which is tutored as a reading-and-questions exercise.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Oral and written production against defined themes. For DIFC families this often runs alongside the KHDA mandatory Arabic lesson at school, which has a separate purpose and a separate language of instruction, so the two must not be treated as one subject.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-difc.regionsIntro: These are the areas a DIFC school run actually touches. The notes below are about journey time and what it does to an evening, because that is the variable a tutoring schedule has to survive.

regions.note: Walkable from parts of DIFC on a podium level, and the nearest cluster of after-school activities. A 4pm pickup here still leaves a workable evening, which is why Downtown families more often attempt back-to-back commitments.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: One junction south, and the fastest of the four corridors outside peak. Buses from Business Bay schools reach DIFC towers in minutes, so a 4.45pm session start is realistic rather than optimistic for families on this side.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Across the Creek and home to two IB World Schools. Close on the map, slow at 7.30am and at 3pm, and the return leg is the one that decides whether a 5pm session is comfortable or rushed.

regions.name: Culture Village
regions.note: Adjacent to Al Jaddaf on the Creek side, served by the same bus routes and the same bottlenecks. Families here tend to settle on a 5.30pm slot rather than fight the pickup traffic for an earlier one.

regions.name: Meydan
regions.note: A straight run down Al Khail Road and the corridor where a car journey and a bus journey diverge most. Parents driving the pickup themselves often arrive back a full twenty minutes before the school bus does.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Further out, with several large British and IB schools. The bus run is long enough that a Diploma student arrives genuinely tired, which argues for shorter, more frequent sessions rather than one long block.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: The newest school cluster within reach, close to Meydan and sharing its traffic pattern. Journey times here have shifted as the district has filled, so a timetable that worked two years ago may need rechecking.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: Industrial and residential in parts, crossed rather than lived in by most DIFC families, but on the route to the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh schools. It is the stretch where a Sheikh Zayed Road delay becomes a lost half hour.

schoolClusters.city: Al Jaddaf, Culture Village and the Creek side
schoolClusters.note: The closest cluster to DIFC by distance and not by time. All of these are reachable on a single bus route, and all of them release within about twenty minutes of each other, which is why the Creek-side bridge is the deciding factor in any DIFC evening schedule.

schoolClusters.city: Sobha Hartland, Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: The Al Khail Road corridor, and the fastest-growing school cluster within a DIFC commute. Mixed British and International Baccalaureate provision, so siblings in one family are often sitting IGCSE and the Diploma in different buildings on the same road.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and the Jumeirah strip
schoolClusters.note: The longest of the four corridors and the one with the deepest Diploma provision. Families who chose a school here accepted the Sheikh Zayed Road run twice a day, and their evening schedule has the least slack of any DIFC group.

sections.heading: What 'IB tutor near me' actually means from a DIFC tower
paragraphs: Typed from a DIFC address, the phrase does not mean what it means elsewhere. There is no IB school in the district, so there is no local school community whose teachers tutor locally in the evenings. There is no villa compound where a neighbour's tutor can walk over. What the search is really asking is: can somebody who knows this syllabus be available at the hour my child is actually at a desk, which is after a commute I do not control.

That reframing matters because the two questions have different answers. 'Who is nearest' has a short answer and a weak one: whoever happens to live in Downtown, Business Bay or Za'abeel and is willing to drive in, park in a visitor bay, sign in at a tower reception and come back out again. 'Who can teach Higher Level Chemistry at 5.30pm' has a long answer and a strong one, because once travel stops being a constraint the shortlist is drawn from everyone who teaches that paper rather than everyone within a twenty-minute radius.

The honest position is that proximity buys one real thing: a physical presence in the room, which some students genuinely need, particularly younger ones and those who drift without a person beside them. It is worth paying for where it is the deciding factor. What it does not buy is subject depth. A tutor fifteen minutes away is not more likely to have taught Paper 3 of Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level than one who is not; if anything the reverse, because the local pool is smaller.

IB Gram's answer to the search is one-to-one tuition over live video, scheduled around your child's bus. It is not a home-visit service in Dubai and the page will not pretend otherwise. The rest of this page is the detail a DIFC parent needs to judge whether that works: the schools, the timings, the costs, the calendar and the rules.

sections.heading: Where DIFC children go to school, and when the bus gets back
paragraphs: DIFC families choose schools in four directions, and the choice sets the shape of every weekday afterwards. The table below lists the clusters within a realistic daily commute, what each offers, and the honest consequence for an evening session. Journey times are indicative and depend on the route, the bus and the day; a parent can verify their own by timing the actual run twice in one week, which is more useful than any published figure.

The pattern in the table is worth stating plainly. The nearest cluster by distance, across the Creek in Al Jaddaf and Culture Village, is not the nearest by time, because the crossing concentrates traffic at exactly the hours the school run uses it. The Al Khail Road corridor to Meydan, Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba is quick outbound and slow back. The Sheikh Zayed Road corridor to Al Barsha and Al Sufouh is slow in both directions and carries the deepest Diploma provision, which is why families accept it.

A second pattern matters more for tutoring. Because DIFC children are spread across all four corridors, two Diploma students in the same tower are often following different schemes of work, sitting different Internal Assessment deadlines and taking mocks in different weeks. A tutor who knows 'the Dubai IB calendar' in general is less useful than one working from your child's own school deadline sheet, and that is the document worth having to hand at the first session.

Where a school offers both IGCSE and the Diploma, as several in the Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba cluster do, siblings in the same family end up in different assessment systems with different term rhythms. That is normal in this part of Dubai and it is the main reason a single weekly slot per child beats a shared family slot.

sections.heading: The DIFC weekday, hour by hour
paragraphs: Scheduling tuition for a Diploma student is mostly a question of finding two hours that exist. Parents tend to describe the evening as open and then discover it is not, because the hour after arrival is spent eating and decompressing and the hour before bed is unusable for anything requiring working memory. Writing the day out removes the argument.

The table below is the shape of a typical DIFC weekday for a Diploma student commuting from one of the outer clusters. It is not prescriptive and every family's version differs by thirty minutes in one direction or another, but the structure holds: a narrow usable window in the early evening, and a second, shorter one that only works for review rather than new content.

Two practical conclusions come out of it. First, a 90-minute session is only better than a 60-minute one if it starts early enough to finish inside the usable window; a 90-minute block beginning at 6.30pm ends in the part of the evening where retention falls away. Second, four shorter sessions a week beat two long ones for a student on a long bus run, and the reverse is true for a student at a Business Bay school who gets home at four.

The weekend changes the arithmetic entirely. Saturday mornings are the single most productive slot available to a DIFC family, because nobody is tired and nothing is competing, and they are the obvious home for Internal Assessment work and timed paper practice. Friday is workable in the afternoon for many families. Any plan that loads everything onto weekday evenings and leaves the weekend empty is leaving the best hours unused.

sections.heading: Why distance stops mattering once the subject gets narrow
paragraphs: The case for a local tutor is strongest at the broad end and weakest at the narrow end. A Year 7 student needing help organising homework and reading more fluently can be helped by a great many competent people, and some of them live nearby. A Year 13 student who needs Paper 3 of Higher Level Physics, or the inference section of Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, or an Economics commentary rescued from a badly chosen article, needs somebody who has taught that component to examination and has read the current subject guide.

Count the constraints and the reason becomes obvious. The tutor must teach the subject, at the right level, at the right stage of the two-year course, be free on a specific weekday at a specific hour in Gulf Standard Time, and be acceptable to the student. Each constraint cuts the pool. Adding 'and must be able to reach a DIFC tower and park' cuts it again, and it cuts it hardest precisely where the subject is narrowest, because specialists in a single Higher Level component are thin on the ground everywhere.

This is why IB Gram matches on the component rather than the postcode. If your child needs Higher Level Chemistry, the question asked is which tutors have taught Higher Level Chemistry to the current guide, not which of them is closest to Gate Avenue. Delivery over live video is what makes that ordering possible, and a shared screen with a document camera or a graphics tablet is a better surface for working through a mechanism or a calculus proof than a kitchen table with two people looking at one exercise book.

The limit of the argument should be stated too. Online is not better for every student. A child who will not sit still without an adult physically present, or who is young enough that a screen is a toy, is a poor fit, and a trial lesson exists so that this is discovered in week one rather than week nine. Where online does not work, the honest answer is that it does not, and IB Gram does not offer a home-visit alternative in Dubai to fall back on.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. So here are the numbers, attributed, as of October 2026. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, advertises from AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor online sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, runs AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-badged tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650.

The interesting figure is the gap, not the range. Compare the online qualified band at AED 150 to 300 against the in-home band at AED 180 to 500 for broadly the same level of tutor, and the difference is roughly AED 50 to 200 an hour. That difference is not teaching. It is fuel, Salik, a car, and twenty to fifty minutes of a tutor's unpaid time per visit, recovered from you. For a DIFC tower with barrier access and a visitor parking process, it sits at the higher end of that spread, because the last five minutes of the journey are the slowest.

Monthly packages make the same point more starkly. The market shows roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's own monthly estimate for one weekly hour runs AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. A parent can check all of this in an afternoon: ask three providers for a written rate per 60 minutes, ask whether travel is inside or outside the figure, and ask what happens to the fee if a session is cancelled at short notice.

IB Gram's own position is deliberately not a price list on this page. Lessons are online and one-to-one, the first one is a free trial, and the rate depends on the level and the subject, which is a conversation rather than a table. What the market table above is for is judging whether any quote you receive, from anyone, sits where it should for what is actually being delivered.

sections.heading: The Diploma year in the order it actually arrives
paragraphs: Dubai IB schools sit the May examination session, and the second year of the Diploma is best planned backwards from it rather than forwards from September. The IB's own session and results dates are published by the IB and by each school's Diploma coordinator, and they are the only sources worth acting on; this page deliberately does not restate them, because a date a parent books flights around should come from the organisation that sets it.

What can be stated is the order, and the order is where DIFC families get caught. The crush is not the examinations. It is the eight to ten weeks in the second year when the Extended Essay final draft, two or three subject Internal Assessments, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the school's own mock papers all land in the same window. A student who has not started the Internal Assessments by then is doing them alongside mock revision, and the mocks are what the predicted grades come from.

For the IGCSE siblings in the same household, dates are available and sourced. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January, as November 2025 results did on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that the correct zone timetable must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Always open the live official timetable rather than trusting a restated date.

The practical move for a DIFC parent is small and it pays for itself. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's internal deadline sheet in September of the second year, put the Extended Essay and Internal Assessment dates in a shared calendar alongside the mock window, and work backwards in four-week blocks. Tutoring then has a job in each block rather than being a general weekly presence, and the Saturday morning slot gets used for the thing that is due next.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the week your child has left
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the published report for your child's school is the single most useful free document available to a DIFC parent. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and claims no relationship with the authority; this is description, not endorsement.

The part that affects tutoring is the mandatory-subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidelines state these requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should be shorter than 25 minutes.

KHDA also requires separate classes by group, stating that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval, and for these subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited.

What a DIFC parent should take from this is arithmetic again. Those mandatory periods sit inside a fixed school week, which means the Diploma or IGCSE subjects have slightly less timetabled time than the syllabus assumes, and that pressure shows up first in the subjects with the most content. It is also why Arabic support is a separate tutoring stream rather than an add-on: the school's mandatory Arabic lesson and an IB Arabic B course have different purposes, different languages of instruction and different assessment, and conflating them wastes the hour.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the MYP Personal Project must be the student's own work, authenticated by a supervisor at the school. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion is asking for, question a research question until it is answerable, review a draft the student has written and give specific feedback on it. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it, draft sections of it, or supply a finished piece. There is no soft middle here; the IB's academic-honesty rules make the consequence a malpractice finding against the student.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the market a DIFC parent is shopping in includes providers who cross the line openly. One site found in this cluster's research sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is a route to a withdrawn diploma, and the risk sits entirely with your child rather than with the seller. Any provider who will not say plainly where their line is should be ruled out on that basis alone.

What good coursework support looks like in practice is unglamorous. The research question is pressure-tested before any writing begins, because an unanswerable question caps the mark regardless of effort. The criteria are read aloud, letter by letter, and the student says what each one wants in their own words. Word and page limits are checked against the current subject guide rather than remembered from last year. Then the student writes, and the session afterwards is spent on what the draft does and does not yet evidence.

Two further rules worth knowing. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and are referenced and linked rather than reproduced or supplied as downloads. And nobody should describe a tutor as an IB or Cambridge examiner without current evidence, or use examiner status to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because that implication is false in every case.

sections.heading: Availability, permits and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

There is a second rule a DIFC parent should know before asking a favour. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document, but the direction is clear: your child's own classroom teacher, paid privately, is the arrangement to avoid rather than the one to seek.

On availability, the honest version. A common Standard Level subject is usually matched within a few days. A narrow Higher Level component at a specific weekday hour can take longer, and occasionally the right specialist is in a different time zone and the best available slot is earlier or later than ideal. When that happens you are told before you book, not after, and the trial lesson is where you decide whether the compromise works. If nothing suitable exists, that is said plainly; a mismatched tutor at the right hour is worse than waiting a fortnight for the right one.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram operates no centre, office or branch in the UAE, holds no such permit, and does not describe itself in terms that imply one. Lessons reach DIFC over live video and nowhere else.

process.title: Tell us the bus time, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps names the school, the year, the subjects and levels, and the time your child is actually home from the cluster they commute to. The last of those is the one that decides whether a match exists, and it is the one parents leave out most often.

process.title: We shortlist by component, then by hour
process.description: Tutors are filtered first on whether they have taught that subject at that level to the current guide, and only then on who is free in your window in Gulf Standard Time. You see the shortlist with what each person has actually taught, rather than a profile written in adjectives.

process.title: Free trial lesson at your chosen slot
process.description: The trial runs at the time you intend to keep, so you are testing the slot as well as the tutor. A session that works brilliantly at 4pm on a Saturday tells you nothing about a Tuesday at 5.30pm after a bus from Al Barsha. No payment is taken before the trial.

process.title: Fix the slot and bring the deadline sheet
process.description: Once the match holds, the slot becomes fixed for the term, and the school's internal deadline sheet goes to the tutor so each block of sessions has a target: this Internal Assessment, that mock paper, this topic before the next test. The plan is written down, not assumed.

process.title: Review at six weeks, change if needed
process.description: Six weeks is long enough to judge and short enough to fix. The review looks at school assessment evidence rather than how the sessions felt. If the match is wrong, it is changed without an argument; if the schedule is wrong, the slot moves.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the paper, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: A shortlist is built from tutors who have taught your child's exact component at that level. For Higher Level sciences and the two mathematics routes, that distinction is the difference between a tutor who can mark a Paper 3 answer and one who can only check the arithmetic.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the commute, in Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled after the bus arrival time is known. That sounds obvious and is routinely ignored; a slot set to suit a tutor in another time zone is the most common reason a good match quietly stops working by half term.

whyPoints.title: Coursework help that stays inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Personal Project work is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is written for the student. The boundary is stated here because several providers in this market do not state theirs.

whyPoints.title: Numbers with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. None of them is an IB Gram price. A parent can check each one and should, including against whatever quote arrives from anywhere else.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what is not offered
whyPoints.description: There is no DIFC office, no home-visit service in the UAE, no regulator accreditation and no grade promise. Lessons are online, one-to-one, and the first is free. Knowing what a provider will not do is more useful than a list of what it claims.

faqs.question: Is there an IB school inside DIFC itself?
faqs.answer: No. DIFC is an office and residential district with no private school inside its boundaries, so every school-age child living there commutes out. The realistic catchment runs in four directions: Business Bay and Downtown, Al Jaddaf and Culture Village across the Creek, the Al Khail Road corridor to Meydan, Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba, and Sheikh Zayed Road to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Jumeirah. IB Diploma provision exists in all four, which is why children in one DIFC tower often attend four different schools with four different deadline calendars.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a weekday session can realistically start from a DIFC tower?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which corridor your child commutes. A Business Bay or Downtown school usually means a 4.45pm start is comfortable. The Creek-side cluster in Al Jaddaf and Culture Village pushes it to about 5.15pm because the crossing is slowest at pickup. The Al Khail Road corridor lands around 5.00pm to 5.30pm. From Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, 5.30pm is the honest earliest and 6.00pm is more sustainable in term time. Time the actual journey twice before fixing a slot rather than estimating it.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives closer to DIFC teach the syllabus any better?
faqs.answer: No, and often the opposite. Proximity buys physical presence in the room, which genuinely helps some students, particularly younger ones. It does not buy subject depth. The pool of people who can teach Paper 3 of Higher Level Physics to the current guide is thin everywhere, and restricting that pool to whoever can reach a DIFC tower and park makes it thinner. Matching on the component first and the hour second produces a better shortlist. Where a student truly needs someone in the room, online is the wrong fit and the trial lesson is where that becomes clear.

faqs.question: Our child attends a school in Sobha Hartland. How does that change the week?
faqs.answer: The Al Khail Road corridor is quick outbound in the morning and slow coming back at pickup, so the useful study window opens around 5.00pm to 5.30pm. Sobha Hartland and the neighbouring Meydan and Nad Al Sheba cluster mix British and IB provision, so siblings in one family are frequently sitting IGCSE and the Diploma at the same time on different term rhythms. Journey times in this district have changed as it has filled, so a schedule that worked two years ago is worth rechecking rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Is a 90-minute session better than a 60-minute one for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Only if it starts early enough to finish inside the usable evening window. For a DIFC student home at 4.50pm, that window runs to roughly 7.00pm, so a 90-minute block starting at 5.15pm works well and the same block starting at 6.30pm does not. For students on the longest bus runs, four shorter sessions a week usually outperform two long ones, because fatigue rather than time is the binding constraint. For a child home by four from Business Bay, longer blocks are the better buy.

faqs.question: Can sessions run at the weekend from a DIFC address?
faqs.answer: Yes, and Saturday morning is the most productive slot available to a DIFC family. Nobody is tired, no commute has happened and nothing competes, which makes it the natural home for Internal Assessment work and for timed paper practice that needs an uninterrupted ninety minutes. Friday afternoons work for many families too. A plan that fills weekday evenings and leaves the weekend empty is leaving the best hours of the week unused, and that is the most common scheduling mistake in this district.

faqs.question: What happens to the timetable during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, which widens the afternoon and compresses the evening around Iftar. Most DIFC families move sessions either earlier, into the newly free early afternoon, or later to a post-Iftar slot, and both work provided the choice is made for the whole month rather than negotiated weekly. Because lessons are delivered online, the change is a calendar edit and nothing more. Fix the Ramadan pattern a fortnight ahead, because the month frequently overlaps the heaviest Internal Assessment and mock window of the second Diploma year.

faqs.question: How do the KHDA mandatory subjects affect the time left for other subjects?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum is licensed, and their instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit with a weekly total that must be met. Those periods sit inside a fixed school week, so the Diploma or IGCSE subjects have marginally less timetabled time than the syllabus assumes. The pressure appears first in the most content-heavy subjects. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in these subjects, with combined classes strictly prohibited.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IB tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates as of October 2026, attributed to who publishes them: budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik and roughly AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's 2026 table and up to AED 500 independently. None of these is an IB Gram price. Ask any provider for a written rate per 60 minutes.

faqs.question: What exactly does the in-home travel premium pay for?
faqs.answer: Compare the published bands and the gap is roughly AED 50 to 200 an hour between a qualified tutor online and the same calibre of tutor visiting a home. That difference is not teaching. It covers fuel, Salik, the car, and twenty to fifty minutes of unpaid travel per visit, recovered through the hourly rate. For a DIFC tower the premium sits at the higher end, because barrier access, visitor parking and a reception sign-in make the final five minutes of the journey the slowest part of it.

faqs.question: May a tutor help with the Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each criterion asks for, pressure-test a research question, confirm word limits against the current subject guide, and give specific feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite or draft any part of it, and may not supply finished work. The assessment is authenticated by a school supervisor, and crossing the line produces a malpractice finding against your child rather than against the provider who sold it.

faqs.question: Which exam session do Dubai IB schools sit, and where do I get the dates?
faqs.answer: Dubai IB schools sit the May session. The authoritative dates come from the IB itself and from your school's Diploma coordinator, and those are the only two sources worth acting on; nothing on this page restates them, because a date a family books flights around should come from the organisation that sets it. For IGCSE siblings, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, and Cambridge International runs June and November series with centre-specific zone timetables that must be matched exactly.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tuition inside the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure as unverified.

faqs.question: What if no tutor covers my child's Higher Level subject at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: You are told before you book rather than after. A common Standard Level subject is usually matched within a few days; a narrow Higher Level component at a fixed weekday hour can take longer, and sometimes the right specialist is in another time zone and the best available slot is earlier or later than ideal. The trial lesson is where you judge whether that compromise is worth it. If nothing suitable exists, that is said plainly, because a mismatched tutor in the right slot is worse than waiting a fortnight.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same DIFC apartment share one session?
faqs.answer: Only where they are in the same year, the same subject and the same level, which in this district is uncommon because siblings frequently attend schools in different corridors with different programmes. Where it does apply, a shared session saves money and costs attention, and the saving disappears if one child is a term ahead. In practice two separate shorter slots usually deliver more for the same total spend, and they also let each child keep the time that suits their own commute.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-difc.closingHeading: Start with the timing, then the tutor
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-difc.closingBody: If your child commutes out of DIFC every morning, the deciding question is not who is nearest. It is whether a specialist in the right subject can be at a screen at the hour your child is genuinely able to work, and whether the plan for the next six weeks has a target rather than a vague weekly presence. Send the school, the year, the subjects and levels, and the time the bus actually gets back. You will get a shortlist built from people who have taught that component, a free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, and a straight answer if the right match is not available yet.
