dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-discovery-gard.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors a Discovery Gardens family is matched with for Diploma work. What matters as much as the subject is when you arrive: the same tutor achieves different things in September and in April, and will say so.

intro.heading: The calendar decides what tutoring can do
paragraphs: Two moments in the year generate almost every tutoring enquiry from this community. The first is the week after mock results, usually in the winter term. The second is around six weeks before the papers, when a student has done the arithmetic and a parent has seen the predicted grades. Both are rational moments to act. They are also, respectively, a good moment and a late one, and the difference is worth understanding before any money is spent.

The reason is structural rather than motivational. Diploma subjects carry internally assessed components worth roughly twenty to thirty per cent of each grade, and those are completed, marked and submitted months before the written papers. A family arriving in the spring is buying help with the remaining marks only. Nothing a tutor does in April reaches an Internal Assessment that went to the school in January.

That single fact reorganises everything. It means the autumn term of Diploma 2 is worth more per hour than the spring, that the mock window is a diagnostic opportunity rather than a verdict, and that an eight-week run-in has a specific and limited job: exam technique on the components still unsat. All of those are useful. None of them is a substitute for having started earlier, and a tutor who implies otherwise is selling.

Discovery Gardens shapes the practical side. It is a high-density apartment community of 291 buildings in themed districts beside Ibn Battuta, with its own Route 2020 metro station. Diploma students travel out of the community for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, so they are home from about 16:30 and sessions run at 18:00 or later. Study space is a shared desk rather than a room.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. In a calendar-driven plan that matters more than it sounds, because a session missed in the final eight weeks can be rescheduled to the next evening rather than lost to the following week, and in a short run-in a week is a large fraction of the time available.

What follows is the year laid out backwards: what each number of remaining weeks can realistically achieve, where the mock window fits, how Ramadan and the UAE academic calendar interact with revision, and what the autumn term buys that the spring cannot. We publish no specific IB exam or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in front of a parent who acts on it is worse than none. The coordinator's internal calendar is the document that matters anyway, because it carries the deadlines that decide most of the grade.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-discovery-gard.programmesIntro: Each stage has its own calendar, and the deadlines that matter are mostly internal rather than external. These are the stages a Discovery Gardens family will plan around.

programmes.name: Diploma 1, the year nobody plans
programmes.description: Six subjects begin, the Extended Essay supervisor is assigned, Theory of Knowledge starts, and in several subjects the internal component is begun. Almost no families buy support in this year, and it is the year where support is cheapest per mark protected. Students who establish command-term discipline and criteria habits here need far less later.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma 1 students in Discovery Gardens are settling into a longer commute and a heavier load at once, often having changed schools at 16 because full Diploma provision in this corridor is thinner than further north. A weekly session through this year costs less in total than a spring block in Diploma 2 and reaches marks the later block cannot.

programmes.name: Diploma 2, the year of internal deadlines
programmes.description: The year is shaped by internal submissions rather than by the examinations. Extended Essay final drafts, Theory of Knowledge essays and subject Internal Assessments cluster between the autumn and the late winter, then mocks, then the May session. Each internal deadline is a closing door on a share of a subject grade.
programmes.countryNote: This is when almost all Discovery Gardens enquiries arrive. The useful question on first contact is not which subject but which deadlines are still ahead. Where internal work is still open, the hours should go there first; where it has all been submitted, the plan is exam technique and nothing else, and saying so plainly is part of the service.

programmes.name: The mock window
programmes.description: Schools run full mock papers under exam conditions, usually in the winter term, and produce a paper-level breakdown that most families never ask for. The mock's value is almost entirely diagnostic: it shows which component is losing marks and whether the cause is content, command terms, method or timing. The grade itself is the least useful output.
programmes.countryNote: Mock results are the single most common trigger for a tutoring enquiry in this community, and the week after them is a good moment to act, provided the paper-level breakdown comes too. Without it, a tutor is working from a grade and a feeling, which produces a generic plan and a term of effort with little to show.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the years before
programmes.description: Assessed on four criteria out of eight in each subject group, with no external examinations and therefore no calendar pressure. That absence is why the stage gets skipped, and why Diploma 1 arrives as a shock. The criteria habits built here are exactly what Diploma internal components later assume.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in Discovery Gardens are home earlier, often by 16:00, so a 16:30 session is straightforward to place. Support at this stage is bought by very few families here and is the cheapest insurance available against the Diploma 2 scramble this page is largely about.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-discovery-gard.subjectsIntro: The calendar interacts differently with each subject, because the internal components fall at different times and in different forms. These notes name what is time-critical in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is worth twenty marks and its topic should be settled months before the deadline. In the run-in, Higher Level students need whole Paper 3 questions under timing rather than topic revision, and Analysis and Approaches students need non-calculator fluency maintained rather than rebuilt.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same twenty-mark exploration on the same timeline. In the final weeks the time-critical work is calculator competence on the school's own model and interpretation of results in context, both of which are quick wins late in the year if they have been neglected.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is twenty per cent and closes early, so by the spring the available work is Paper 1A timed sets, Paper 1B data processing and Paper 2 command-term discipline. Uncertainty and graph skills are the fastest late improvements in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Also twenty per cent internally assessed and also closed early. The late-year priorities are mechanism notation, energetics sign conventions and the data booklet, all of which can be fixed in a handful of sessions because they are notational rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Late work should focus on precision of language and on statistical treatment of data, both of which are reliably under-taught and reliably examined. A student who learns to name a mechanism and a direction in every answer gains marks across every paper within weeks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal commentaries spread across the course, so there is usually at least one still open when a family makes contact. Where they are closed, the late-year work is diagrams referenced explicitly in the prose and command-term discipline in extended response.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Higher Level research project needs a real organisation and primary data, so it is the internal component least recoverable from a late start: arranging access takes longer than writing. Where it is done, case-study command terms are the available late work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral is scheduled by the school and often sits earlier than students expect, which makes it a date to confirm rather than assume. Paper 1 unseen analysis responds well to late work, because the skill is a repeatable approach rather than content.

subjects.name: Language B: Arabic, French, Spanish
subjects.description: Oral components are scheduled internally and are the time-critical element. Speaking fluency for the full duration improves with frequent short practice rather than long sessions, so a late start should mean two short sessions a week rather than one long one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay is written to a school deadline from a prescribed title, and the exhibition precedes it. Both are decided by the initial choice, so late help is limited to argument structure on an existing draft. One early session on the title is worth several late ones.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Final drafts fall in the first part of Diploma 2, so by the spring this is usually closed. Where it is still open, the research question is the first thing to examine, because a question too broad for 4,000 words cannot be fixed by better writing.

subjects.name: Psychology and Geography
subjects.description: Both carry internal components with early internal deadlines and both reward evidence used rather than recited in the papers. Late-year work on using a study or case study to support an argument, rather than describing it, is among the better available improvements.

sections.heading: What the weeks you have left can actually achieve
paragraphs: The most useful thing a tutor can tell a Discovery Gardens family on first contact is what is still possible. That depends almost entirely on two variables: how many weeks remain, and whether any internal components are still open. Everything else, subject, level, current grade, matters less than those two, because they determine which marks are reachable at all.

With a full year, everything is reachable. Internal components can be planned rather than rescued, technique can be built across both papers, and content gaps can be closed properly. With a term, internal work that is still open is the priority and exam technique follows. With eight weeks, the job is narrow: the two or three most frequent causes of lost marks, drilled on whole papers under timing.

With four weeks or fewer, the honest plan is narrower still and most providers will not say so. Fresh content teaching across a syllabus is not possible in four weeks, and attempting it produces coverage without consolidation, which is worse than targeting less. What four weeks can do is fix command-term behaviour, improve timing, and drill the two highest-frequency question types in each paper.

None of this is an argument against late help. A well-targeted four-week block moves marks and is worth buying. It is an argument against pretending that a late block does what an early one does, which is the standard claim in this market and the reason families feel misled afterwards. The table below is the version we give on the phone.

sections.heading: The Diploma 2 year, read as a sequence of closing doors
paragraphs: It helps to think of the year not as a run-up to the examinations but as a sequence of doors that close one at a time. Each internal deadline closes a share of a subject grade permanently. The Extended Essay closes. The Theory of Knowledge essay closes. Each subject's internal component closes. By the time study leave begins, a substantial proportion of the final points total is already fixed and unreachable.

The order varies by school, which is why the school's own internal deadline calendar is the document that should drive any plan. Typically the Extended Essay final draft falls in the first part of Diploma 2, the Theory of Knowledge essay in the same period, and subject Internal Assessments between the autumn and the late winter, with several clustering in the same weeks. Mocks then sit in the winter term.

The practical instruction for a family is to ask the Diploma coordinator for that calendar in September of Diploma 2, or better, of Diploma 1. It is not confidential and it is rarely volunteered. With it, a parent can see where the clusters fall and plan support around them. Without it, the first indication that four deadlines share a fortnight is the fortnight itself.

We publish no specific IB exam or results dates on this site. UAE schools sit the May session and we write about it, but the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so we cannot verify a date to the standard required before putting it in front of a parent who might act on it. The coordinator's calendar is both more accurate and more useful, because it carries the internal deadlines that actually decide the grade.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE academic year and where revision actually lands
paragraphs: Any revision plan written for a UAE family has to account for the local calendar, and almost no tutoring page does. The UAE academic year runs from late summer to early summer, with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break later in the second term. That shape means the Diploma 2 run-in is interrupted twice, and both breaks are opportunities or losses depending on whether anyone planned for them.

Ramadan matters more. It moves roughly eleven days earlier each year in the Gregorian calendar, so its position relative to the school year shifts, and in recent years it has fallen in the spring term, overlapping with mock results and the start of serious examination revision. UAE schools operate reduced hours during Ramadan, which changes both the teaching time available and the shape of a student's day.

The practical adjustments are straightforward once anticipated. Reduced school hours free earlier afternoon slots, which is useful. Energy patterns shift, so a 19:00 session may work better than a 17:00 one for a fasting student, or the reverse, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Long revision blocks are less effective than shorter, more frequent ones during this period for most students.

What goes wrong is only ever the unplanned version: a family books a fixed weekly slot in January, Ramadan arrives, the slot stops working, two sessions are missed and the arrangement quietly lapses in the term that mattered most. Agreeing in advance that the slot will move for that period costs one conversation and protects the plan. In a compressed run-in, two missed sessions is a significant share of the total.

sections.heading: What a mock is for, and the document to ask for
paragraphs: Mock results are the most common trigger for a tutoring enquiry from this community and the most commonly misused document. Parents read the grade; the grade is the least informative part. What matters is the paper-level breakdown: which component the marks came from, and within it what kind of error recurred. Schools hold that information and frequently do not send it out unless asked directly.

The reason it matters is that identical grades mean opposite things. A 4 produced by one weak paper with the others solid needs targeted component work. A 4 spread evenly across every component needs broad consolidation. A 4 caused by three unfinished papers is a timing problem and nothing else. Those are three different plans, and a tutor working from the grade alone will default to content revision for all three.

A mock also provides the only realistic timing data available before the real papers. Students almost never practise under genuine exam conditions alone, so a mock is often the first full-length timed attempt. If papers were unfinished, that is the headline finding, and it is fixable with practice in a way that content gaps in April are not.

The best use of the week after mocks is therefore diagnostic: three to five sessions working through the breakdown, categorising errors by cause, and producing a written plan with a stated number of sessions. Families in Discovery Gardens who do that in the winter term rarely make a second, more expensive enquiry in the spring, which is the pattern this page is written to interrupt.

sections.heading: An eight-week run-in, week by week
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window most families in this community actually have when they make contact, so it deserves a concrete plan rather than general encouragement. The principle is narrow focus: identify the two or three highest-frequency causes of lost marks from marked papers, then spend the whole eight weeks on those using whole papers under timing. Resist the urge to cover the syllabus, which cannot be done in the time.

The first week is diagnosis and nothing else. Two marked papers, errors categorised by cause, a written plan. The second to fifth weeks are the working period: one timed paper or section set per session, marked strictly against the real scheme in the following session, with the targeted causes reviewed each time. Progress is measurable because the error categories either shrink or they do not.

The sixth and seventh weeks shift to whole papers under full timing, including the components students avoid: the data-based section in the sciences, Paper 3 in Higher Level mathematics, the unseen analysis in literature. These are the components where avoidance is most common and improvement is quickest, precisely because they have been neglected.

The final week is for exam-room behaviour rather than content: reading a paper before starting, allocating time per mark, recognising command terms, knowing when to leave a question and return. Nothing new is taught. Families who try to learn content in the last week lose the consolidation that the previous seven weeks earned, which is the commonest way a good run-in is wasted.

sections.heading: What the autumn term buys that the spring cannot
paragraphs: The strongest argument for starting early is not diligence but arithmetic. In the autumn term of Diploma 2, internal components in several subjects are still open, which means a share of twenty to thirty per cent of each of those grades is still reachable. By the spring, most of that is submitted. The same tutor, the same rate and the same number of hours therefore buy access to a smaller pool of marks.

The second advantage is specialist availability, which is a genuine market effect rather than a sales line. In September, tutors in most Diploma subjects have space, so a family in Discovery Gardens can choose on subject and level. In January and February the whole city is looking at once, and the choice narrows to whoever is free in the evening slots that this corridor's commute allows.

The third is that technique improvements compound. Command-term discipline established in October is applied across every assessment for eight months, including the mocks and the internal work. The same improvement made in April applies to the final papers only. That is the same teaching producing several times the benefit, purely because of when it happened.

The fourth is less obvious and matters to households: an early start is cheaper in total. A weekly session across a year at published mid-market online rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour is a steady, plannable commitment. A spring rescue is usually two or three sessions a week at specialist rates, bought under pressure, with a lower ceiling. Those figures are market rates read in October 2026 and not an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: Results, and the decisions that follow quickly
paragraphs: The calendar does not end with the papers. After results there is a short window in which several decisions have to be made, and families who have not anticipated them make them badly. For Diploma students that includes whether to query a result through the school's own process and how that interacts with university offers. The school is the route for all of it, and the timeline is tight rather than generous.

For families in this corridor with younger children sitting IGCSE, the parallel decision is the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. A resit is worth entering when the paper-level breakdown shows a near miss on one component in a subject needed for an offer, and usually is not when marks sat evenly below target.

The published Pearson dates give a sense of how tight the window is: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entry decisions for a November series therefore have to be made within days of August results rather than weeks, with the school's exams officer involved from the start.

The useful habit is to review results with the breakdown in hand in the first week rather than the third, and to decide on evidence rather than disappointment. A tutor can help read that breakdown honestly, including when the honest answer is that another sitting is unlikely to move the grade and the energy belongs elsewhere. We would rather say that than sell a second block by default.

sections.heading: What a calendar-led tutor does differently, and our limits
paragraphs: A tutor working from the calendar asks different questions at the start. Not what grade is the student getting, but which internal components are still open, when the school's deadlines fall, when the mocks are, and how many weeks remain. The plan then follows from the answers, and it changes shape as doors close. That is a different service from a weekly hour of general subject support, and it is what this page is describing.

It also means being willing to decline work or reduce it. Where a family arrives with three weeks and six subjects, the useful answer is to pick one subject and one component rather than spread three weeks across everything. Where internal work is still open, exam revision waits. Where the honest assessment is that a block will not move the grade, we say so, and some enquiries end there.

Our delivery limits are the same as on every page of this site. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE. In a compressed run-in the online format has a practical advantage, because a missed session moves to the next evening instead of the next week.

On internal work and claims the boundaries are fixed. Tutors read criteria with the student, question a research question, teach technique and give written feedback on the student's own drafts; they do not write, rewrite or supply content. We do not reproduce IB syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. We hold no accreditation or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and we do not guarantee grades.

process.title: Tell us how many weeks you have
process.description: Before the subject, we need the timeline: how many weeks until the papers, and which internal components are still open. Those two answers determine what is reachable, and a provider who does not ask them is going to sell you the same plan whatever month you call in.

process.title: Get the internal deadline calendar
process.description: The Diploma coordinator holds it and rarely volunteers it. It shows where internal deadlines cluster, which is what any sensible plan is built around. Ask for it in September of Diploma 1 if you can, and of Diploma 2 at the latest.

process.title: Send the paper-level breakdown
process.description: After mocks, ask the school for the component-level detail rather than accepting the grade. Identical grades mean opposite things depending on whether marks were lost in one paper, spread evenly, or lost to unfinished papers. The plan depends entirely on which.

process.title: Free trial, diagnosis first
process.description: The trial is built on two marked papers and ends with errors categorised by cause: command term, method, reading, timing, content. No payment is taken and there is no obligation. If the diagnosis says tutoring is not the right purchase for the time remaining, we will say that.

process.title: Agree a plan with a stated end date
process.description: A weekly slot for a term, a post-mock block of three to five sessions, or an eight-week run-in with a fixed finish. Knowing the number of sessions in advance is what stops a compressed run-in turning into an open monthly charge nobody reviews.

process.title: Plan around Ramadan and the breaks
process.description: Agree at the start that the slot will move during Ramadan and across the winter and spring breaks, rather than discovering it. In a short run-in, two sessions lost to an unplanned calendar clash is a large share of the total time available.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what a late start reaches
whyPoints.description: Internal components are submitted months before the papers, so hours bought in the spring cannot touch twenty to thirty per cent of each subject grade. We say that on the first call, because a family who understands it buys the right thing rather than feeling misled in July.

whyPoints.title: Plans built from the school's own calendar
whyPoints.description: The coordinator's internal deadline calendar shows where the clusters fall, and that is what the plan is organised around. Working from the examination month alone ignores the deadlines that actually decide most of the grade.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: The first session categorises errors by cause from marked papers. Nine lost marks usually come from two causes, and content revision is the default answer for all of them only when nobody has looked properly.

whyPoints.title: The UAE calendar accounted for
whyPoints.description: Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each year and UAE schools run reduced hours during it, which changes both available time and energy patterns. We agree in advance how the slot moves, rather than losing sessions in the term that matters most.

whyPoints.title: Rescheduling that protects a short window
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a missed session moves to the next evening rather than the next week. Across an eight-week run-in from this corridor, where Diploma students are home late, that difference is several usable sessions.

whyPoints.title: Willing to decline the work
whyPoints.description: Where three weeks remain and six subjects need help, the useful answer is one subject and one component. Where a block will not move the grade, we say so. That costs us enquiries and is the reason to trust the rest of the page.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before the IB papers. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a narrow plan. Eight weeks can address the two or three highest-frequency causes of lost marks, drilled on whole papers under timing, plus the components students avoid such as the data-based section in the sciences or Paper 3 in Higher Level mathematics. What it cannot do is reach submitted Internal Assessment marks, which are typically twenty to thirty per cent of each subject grade, or cover a syllabus. A plan that promises both is not a plan.

faqs.question: Why can tutoring in the spring not fix an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Because it has already gone to the school. Internal components are completed, marked internally and submitted months before the written papers, along with the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. Once submitted, those marks are fixed. Tutoring after that point works on the remaining written components only, which is a smaller pool. This is the single most important reason the autumn term of Diploma 2 is worth more per hour than the spring.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school for after mock results?
faqs.answer: The paper-level breakdown, not just the grade. Identical grades mean opposite things: a 4 from one weak paper needs targeted component work, a 4 spread evenly needs broad consolidation, and a 4 caused by unfinished papers is a timing problem with a completely different fix. Schools hold this detail and often do not send it unless asked. Without it, a tutor is working from a grade and a feeling and will default to content revision.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a Diploma revision plan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It shifts roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so its position in the school year moves, and in recent years it has fallen in the spring term overlapping mock results and the start of serious revision. UAE schools run reduced hours during it, which frees earlier afternoon slots and changes energy patterns through the day. The practical step is agreeing in advance that the session slot will move for that period, rather than losing two sessions and letting the arrangement lapse.

faqs.question: When is the best month to start IB tutoring for a Discovery Gardens student?
faqs.answer: September, and preferably September of Diploma 1. Internal components are still open then, so hours reach marks that later hours cannot. Specialist availability is also widest, so you choose on subject and level rather than on who is free; by January the whole city is looking for the same evening slots. And technique improvements made early apply to eight months of assessment including the mocks, rather than to the final papers alone.

faqs.question: Which document should drive a tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: The school's internal deadline calendar, held by the Diploma coordinator. It shows when the Extended Essay draft, the Theory of Knowledge essay and each subject's Internal Assessment are due, and crucially where those cluster, because they rarely spread evenly. Four deadlines in one fortnight is a predictable event and the commonest cause of a dropped grade. Ask for the calendar in September; it is not confidential and it is almost never volunteered.

faqs.question: What does the final week before the papers get used for?
faqs.answer: Exam-room behaviour, not content. Reading a paper before starting, allocating time per mark, checking the command term before writing, and knowing when to leave a question and come back. Nothing new should be taught. Families who try to learn fresh content in the last week lose the consolidation the previous weeks earned, which is the most common way a well-run eight-week block gets wasted at the very end.

faqs.question: Are IB exam and results dates listed on this page?
faqs.answer: No. UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session and we write about that session, but we publish no specific IB exam or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in front of a parent who acts on it is worse than no date. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds both the examination information and the internal deadline calendar, and the latter is the one that actually shapes the year.

faqs.question: My child has four weeks and six subjects. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Pick one subject and one component. Spreading four weeks across six subjects produces an hour of attention on each and no measurable change anywhere. Choose the subject where a grade boundary is closest and where the marked papers show a single dominant error cause, then spend the whole four weeks on that. It is a smaller ambition and it is the only version with a realistic chance of moving a result in the time available.

faqs.question: Should a student still do mocks seriously if the grade will not count?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more seriously than most do. A mock is usually the first full-length timed attempt a student makes, which makes it the only realistic timing data available before the real papers. If papers were unfinished, that is the headline finding and it is highly fixable. Treating mocks as a rehearsal rather than a verdict is the right framing, and the output that matters is the breakdown rather than the grade on the front.

faqs.question: What time do sessions run for a Diploma student in Discovery Gardens?
faqs.answer: Usually 18:00 or later on weekdays. Students here travel out of the community for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, so they are home from about 16:30 and later with a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment or a fixture. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time. In a compressed run-in the useful detail is that a missed session can move to the next evening rather than the next week, because nobody is travelling.

faqs.question: Is it ever right to say tutoring will not help?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we do. With two weeks left and losses spread evenly across every component in several subjects, a block of sessions will not change the outcome and the student's time is better spent on their own structured revision and sleep. We would rather say that and lose the enquiry than take a payment for a plan with no realistic path to a different result. That position is also why the rest of this page is worth believing.

faqs.question: How should the winter and spring breaks be used?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, which usually means a short block rather than either nothing or a full timetable. The breaks interrupt the Diploma 2 run-in twice, and they are the only periods with whole days available. Three or four well-targeted sessions across a break, on whole timed papers with marked feedback, is worth more than a daily schedule that collapses after three days. Agree the block before the break starts, because specialists fill those weeks quickly.

faqs.question: My younger child is sitting IGCSE. When do we decide about a November resit?
faqs.answer: Within days of August results, not weeks. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Published Pearson dates show how the calendar runs: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Review the paper-level breakdown in the first week with the exams officer involved, and decide on evidence rather than disappointment.

faqs.question: Can a tutor still help with an Internal Assessment that has not been submitted?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should take priority over exam revision while the door is open, because those marks are still available. A tutor may read the criteria strand by strand against the draft, question the research question, teach the technique the component requires, and give written feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may not write, rewrite, outline for completion or supply content. Feedback is given in writing so the school can see the nature of the support.

faqs.question: What is the single biggest calendar mistake families here make?
faqs.answer: Waiting for a bad result before acting. The result that prompts the call usually arrives after the internal components have closed, which means the enquiry happens at the exact point when the available ceiling has dropped. The second biggest is booking a fixed weekly slot without planning for Ramadan and the breaks, so sessions are lost in the term that mattered most and the arrangement quietly lapses rather than being rescheduled.

Each profile names the components that tutor works on, from Paper 3 technique to Internal Assessment criteria, so the match is made on the assessment rather than on a drive time.

intro.heading: What the words near me are really costing a Diploma family
paragraphs: Take the cheapest option first, because that is how most budgets are actually built. Online tuition in Dubai starts low: Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both staffed in good part by university-student tutors. Move up one step to a qualified subject tutor working online and the published range is AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 an hour. Specialist Diploma tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at around AED 270, and BartyED's premium named tutors at AED 650. Every one of those figures was published by the provider named beside it.

Now add geography. In-home one-to-one across Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and in a Downtown tower the figure sits in the upper half of that band for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. The tutor has to reach the building in evening traffic, find visitor parking that frequently needs a resident at a barrier, and share a lift with a few hundred other people coming home. A proximity search does not remove those minutes from the day; it just moves who pays for them.

The radius also quietly shortens the candidate list. A Diploma student needs the person who knows their specific component: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the Chemistry Paper 3 data question, the assessment criteria letters that carry marks in a Business Management Internal Assessment. Filtering first by distance means the shortlist is whoever lives nearby and is free at the hour your child is home from a school in Al Quoz or Sobha Hartland. That is a small pool, and the odds of the right specialist being inside it are poor.

The Diploma is also a two-year purchase rather than a term one, which changes the arithmetic. Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service means a family cannot afford weekly tuition in everything and should not try. The money works when it is concentrated: one or two subjects where the gap is real, a supervision block around the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay, and an intensive stretch before the final series. Spread evenly, the same spend produces no visible movement anywhere.

One delivery fact sits under all of it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at a Downtown address; home visiting is offered only in India. Support reaches a Diploma student here as one-to-one live video lessons timed to Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that the search stops being near me and starts being the right specialist for this component, which is the only version of the search that improves a grade.

programmes.countryNote: Families moving into the corridor mid-MYP from a British or Indian system meet criterion-based marking for the first time and often misread a grade 4 as a failure. One session explaining the criteria usually does more than a term of content work.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-downtown-dubai.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects families in this corridor ask for most, with the component where marks usually go missing. A tutor should be able to name that component before quoting an hourly rate, because the component decides how many hours the job takes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Higher Level course is the most requested single subject in the corridor. Paper 3 is where Higher Level candidates separate, because it asks for sustained reasoning across an unfamiliar extended problem rather than recall of a method. Proof, complex numbers and calculus beyond the Standard Level boundary are the usual pressure points.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students heading for economics, business, design or social sciences. The technology demands are real: a student who cannot drive their graphic display calculator fluently loses marks that have nothing to do with mathematics. Statistics and modelling carry more weight here than algebraic manipulation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth that changes how the whole course should be revised, not just how much. Marks are lost on derivations attempted from memory, on units dropped during substitution, and on extended-response questions where the physics is right and the explanation stops one step short of the mark.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most of the gap between a 5 and a 7. The data-based questions reward students who can read a graph and state uncertainty properly, which is a technique that can be taught in a handful of sessions and is almost never taught in class.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the trap. Students revise content and neglect command terms, so a correct biological explanation written in answer to an evaluate question scores partially or not at all. Statistical treatment of data in the Internal Assessment is a second reliable place to recover marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision and evaluation carry the grade. An unlabelled axis or a curve shifted the wrong way costs marks a student thought were safe, and the commentaries in the Internal Assessment need real published articles and real theory applied to them, not a summary of the news.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the given organisation is the whole assessment. Generic textbook answers score low. The Internal Assessment is graded against lettered criteria with fixed mark allocations, and students lose marks on structure and on the research question before anybody looks at the business content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the written assignments reward students who can sustain a line of argument about how a text works, not what it says. Students who read well often underperform because nobody has shown them the assessment criteria in the order the examiner applies them.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Common in a corridor where most households speak more than one language. The productive skills decide the grade, and timed writing with error-pattern feedback moves it faster than vocabulary work. Listening and reading components reward exam technique as much as language level.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written papers are more theoretical than students expect and the solution component needs a real client and a documented development process. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management, which is where a student with coding fluency but no formal grounding usually stalls.

modes.title: Concentrated weekly support in one or two subjects
modes.description: A fixed hour a week in the subject where the gap is widest, held for a term and reviewed against the next real school mark. At the published AED 200 to 300 band for a qualified or specialist IB tutor, one subject for a twelve-week term sits broadly inside Bestimate's AED 600 to 1,200 monthly estimate for mid-tier support. Two subjects doubles it, and three is usually a sign the plan needs rethinking rather than more hours.

Typically four to six sessions spread across the drafting period: narrowing the research question, reading the criteria in the order the examiner applies them, and commenting on a draft the student has written. The student writes every word. Nothing is drafted, completed or produced on their behalf at any price.

sections.heading: What a two-year Diploma support plan actually costs
paragraphs: A direct answer before the detail. A concentrated two-year plan for one Diploma subject, plus supervision around the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay and an intensive block before the final series, comes to somewhere between seventy and a hundred and ten tutoring hours. At the published Dubai range of AED 200 to 300 an hour for a qualified or specialist IB tutor, that is the real size of the commitment, and it is a very different conversation from an hourly rate quoted in isolation.

Most families never see that number because nobody in this market publishes it. The hourly figure is quoted, the monthly figure is occasionally quoted, and the two-year figure never is, which makes it impossible to compare a Diploma plan against the rest of an education budget. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table gives the monthly anchors: roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget support, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-tier, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Multiplied across two years with a quiet period in the middle, the table below is what results.

The other half of the context is school fees, and here Dubai has handed families an unusually stable year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A year in which the largest line in an education budget does not move is the easiest year in which to fund concentrated tutoring without increasing total spend.

What the table deliberately does not contain is an IB Gram price. These are market figures from named providers, reviewed in October 2026. If you want our own numbers, they come from a consultation and a trial session rather than from a published list, because the hour count depends entirely on which components the student is losing marks in.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level are different purchases
paragraphs: Families routinely ask for a tutor in a subject without saying which level, and the level changes the job more than the subject does. Higher Level courses carry extra syllabus content, an additional paper in most sciences and mathematics, and a markedly higher expectation of sustained reasoning in extended responses. A tutor planning for Standard Level and meeting a Higher Level student discovers the mismatch in the first hour, and the family pays for that hour.

At Higher Level the hours concentrate in a predictable place. In the sciences that is the third paper, where candidates meet data, an unfamiliar context and an expectation that they will structure an argument rather than retrieve a fact. In Mathematics Analysis and Approaches it is also the third paper, which asks for a long piece of reasoning built in stages. Students who have revised by memorising worked examples arrive at those papers with nothing to deploy, and the fix is a different kind of practice rather than more of the same.

At Standard Level the money usually goes somewhere else entirely: coverage, pace and the Internal Assessment. A Standard Level student is often carrying the subject as a requirement rather than a passion, and the efficient plan is to secure the marks that are reliably available, which means command terms, the Internal Assessment criteria and the predictable question types. Twelve well-aimed hours can be worth more at Standard Level than thirty unfocused ones.

The practical instruction is to name the level and the component in the first message. A tutor who asks which paper is where the marks are going is doing the diagnostic work before you have paid for it; a tutor who quotes a rate without asking has not yet understood the job.

sections.heading: The radius trap, and what distance actually buys
paragraphs: A near me search assumes two things: that the nearest capable tutor is capable enough, and that physical presence is worth what it costs. In a district of towers both assumptions deserve examination. The first fails whenever the need is specific, which in the Diploma it almost always is. There is no particular reason the person who can diagnose a Chemistry Paper 3 data question lives within ten minutes of the Dubai Mall, and if they do not, a proximity filter has quietly excluded them.

The second assumption is more interesting, because presence does buy something real for some students. A twelve-year-old who drifts without an adult in the room benefits from one. A household with no quiet corner for a laptop has a genuine problem that video cannot solve. Those are legitimate reasons to hire locally and to pay the AED 180 to 500 in-home band knowingly. For a sixteen-year-old working through past papers with a screen shared between them and a tutor, the benefit is harder to find and the premium is easy to measure.

What a proximity search definitely buys is scheduling fragility. A tutor who drives is a tutor who can be late, can be stuck, and can lose a slot to a better-placed client. A tutor who logs in is one whose 7.30pm is as cheap to supply as their 4pm, which in a corridor where parents commonly get home after seven is the difference between a workable plan and a plan that collapses in week three.

To state it without ambiguity: IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE and nobody will be travelling to a Downtown address, because that service exists only in India. Support is delivered as one-to-one live video lessons. The search worth running is not who is nearby but who knows this component, and that search returns a longer and better list.
bullets: Specific Diploma needs rarely map onto a short radius in any city
Presence helps a young or easily distracted student; it does less for a Year 13 past-paper session

sections.heading: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay: the cost and the hard line
paragraphs: Supervision around the Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay is the most efficient money in a Diploma plan and the most dangerous place to buy badly. Efficient, because a handful of hours spent on the research question and the assessment criteria before any writing starts prevents a rewrite that costs weeks. Dangerous, because this market contains providers selling finished work: one in the researched corpus advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and the consequence of buying one falls on the student.

The legitimate boundary is specific and worth agreeing in writing before the first session. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain the assessment criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations, help a student narrow a question that is too broad to research, ask the questions that reveal an unsupported claim, comment on a draft the student has written, and teach referencing and academic honesty. That is a full and valuable job, and it is entirely compatible with IB rules.

What must never happen is production. No tutor at IB Gram will write the Internal Assessment, draft the Extended Essay, produce the Theory of Knowledge essay or edit a piece until the thinking in it is no longer the student's. A tutor who offers that is offering an expulsion risk with an invoice attached. The related rule on materials matters too: syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked from the official site rather than copied and sent.

Priced honestly, a supervision block is four to six hours per component. At the published Dubai specialist band that is a small fraction of a two-year plan, and it protects the part of the Diploma that a student cannot retake in isolation.

sections.heading: The evening timetable from a Downtown tower
paragraphs: Cost and scheduling are the same problem in this corridor. A Diploma student at a school in Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf or Al Safa is rarely home before four, and in heavy traffic rather later. A parent working in DIFC or Business Bay is frequently not home before seven. That leaves two usable windows, roughly 4.30pm to 6pm and 7.30pm to 9pm, and the second one is where most Year 13 work genuinely happens.

A travelling tutor prices those windows differently because they cost differently to supply. The 7.30pm slot means driving home across the city at nine, which is why in-home quotes for late evenings sit at the top of the AED 180 to 500 range or carry a two-hour minimum to make the trip worthwhile. The same slot costs a video tutor nothing extra, so it is simply available, and in a household where the parent wants to be present for the first ten minutes that availability is the whole point.

Term structure matters as much as the clock. Dubai's academic year runs from late August or early September to the end of June for most schools, with a long winter break in December, a spring break around the end of March, and Ramadan shortening the school day when it falls inside term. Sessions during Ramadan move later, commonly after Iftar, and a plan that does not account for that loses three or four weeks.

The practical version: fix a slot that works in the hardest week of the term rather than the easiest, and pick a format that can hold it. A plan built around a 4pm session that only works when the roads are clear is a plan with a three-week lifespan.
bullets: Two usable windows on a weekday: roughly 4.30pm to 6pm and 7.30pm to 9pm
Late slots carry a travel premium from a driving tutor and no premium online
Ramadan shifts sessions later, often after Iftar, for several weeks of the year
Choose the slot that survives the worst traffic week, not the best one

sections.heading: Where Diploma families in this corridor overspend
paragraphs: The commonest overspend is weekly tuition in too many subjects. A family worried about the whole Diploma buys four subjects at one hour a week, which is four hours of the student's time, four invoices, and not enough depth in any single subject to shift a grade. The same budget concentrated on the two subjects actually below target, with the other four left to school teaching and the student's own revision, moves marks. Breadth is the school's job; depth is what tutoring is for.

The second is starting in the second year. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the final papers all land in Year 13, and a family that begins tutoring in September of Year 13 is bidding for specialist hours in the busiest market of the year while simultaneously needing more of them. The work that should have been spread across eighteen months gets compressed into eight, which costs more and delivers less.

The third is buying hours without a diagnosis. A 5 in Physics can mean a content gap, a technique problem, a timing problem or an Internal Assessment that has gone wrong, and the four need different plans. One paid hour spent marking the student's own most recent paper tells you which, and families who start there reliably buy fewer total hours. Skipping it is the only decision on this page that costs money in both directions at once.

A fourth, less obvious: paying a premium for an examiner-experienced tutor on work that does not need one. Examiner experience is worth something on extended-response technique at Higher Level. It is worth very little on Standard Level content coverage, and the published gap between a mid-tier rate and a premium one is wide enough that the difference should be deliberate.
bullets: Concentrate on the two subjects below target rather than buying four at an hour each
Start supervision in Year 12, when specialist hours are easier to get and fewer are needed
Pay for one diagnostic hour before any block of twenty
Match the tutor tier to the task; premium rates earn their keep on technique, not coverage

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor in Dubai, and what you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Almost nobody competing for this query explains the permit position, and it is both simple and checkable. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a MoHRE work permit created by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. The official service is listed by MoHRE as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

The eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The fine schedule has not been published, which is why no figure appears here and why a page quoting one should be read carefully.

Two related facts give a parent more to work with. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is regulated differently from an individual and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, a restriction the MoHRE permit's code of conduct mirrors.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and it occupies no office in the UAE. Naming those bodies is how a parent gets oriented; implying their endorsement would be a misrepresentation, and it is the most common failure in this SERP.

process.description: The first session uses the most recent school paper or mock rather than a fresh test, because the errors in a real script were made under real conditions. You receive a written separation of content gaps from technique losses, and an honest view of whether tutoring is the right purchase at all.

process.description: Before the second session you get a plan with a number attached: which components, in what order, how many hours, and which terms they fall in. A two-year Diploma plan is budgeted as a two-year plan rather than quoted as an hourly rate and left open.

process.title: A slot that holds in a bad week
process.description: Sessions are fixed on Gulf Standard Time and chosen to survive the worst traffic week of the term rather than the best. Because nobody travels, the late-evening slot most Downtown households actually need is available at the same rate as an afternoon one.

process.title: Re-cut the plan at every real mark
process.description: The plan changes when a school report or mock result arrives, not at the end of a prepaid package. Recovered components come off the list and hours come down. If the student has not moved, the tutor match is reconsidered rather than defended.

whyPoints.title: The two-year number, not just an hourly rate
whyPoints.description: Nobody in this market publishes what a Diploma support plan costs across both years, which makes it impossible to budget. The table on this page gives an hour count by stage and converts it at published Dubai market rates so the commitment is visible before it starts.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the drive
whyPoints.description: A near me search returns whoever is close and free. Online delivery lets the match be made on the thing that decides the grade, whether that is a Chemistry Paper 3 data question or the lettered criteria of a Business Management Internal Assessment.

whyPoints.title: Levels priced separately
whyPoints.description: Higher Level carries extra content, an extra paper in most sciences and mathematics, and a different style of question. A plan that does not distinguish it from Standard Level is guessing at the hours, and the family pays for the guess.

whyPoints.description: Content teaching, criteria explanation and feedback on the student's own draft: part of the service. Writing, completing or supplying an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay: never, at any price, whatever the going rate for it in this market.

faqs.question: What does a full two-year IB Diploma tutoring plan cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A concentrated plan covering one weak subject through Year 12, supervision for an Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay, a second subject in Year 13 and a pre-series intensive comes to roughly sixty-five to eighty-five hours. At the published Dubai market range of AED 200 to 300 an hour for qualified and specialist IB tutors, that is the scale of the commitment. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates give the same picture from another angle: AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-tier support and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an exam year. These are market figures from named providers, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is searching for a tutor near me in Downtown Dubai actually a good way to choose?
faqs.answer: It is a good way to find someone quickly and a poor way to find the right person. A short radius around Downtown returns whoever lives nearby and is free when your child gets home, which is a small pool, and there is no reason the specialist who can diagnose a Higher Level Paper 3 problem happens to live inside it. For broad support a capable nearby generalist can work well. For a specific component in a specific subject, matching on the assessment produces a longer and better shortlist, and video delivery makes distance irrelevant.

faqs.question: Why does Higher Level tutoring cost more than Standard Level in the same subject?
faqs.answer: Because it is a bigger job rather than a higher rate. Higher Level carries additional syllabus content, an extra paper in most sciences and in mathematics, and questions that ask for sustained reasoning in an unfamiliar context rather than a recalled method. An efficient Standard Level plan might be twelve to twenty focused hours across the course; Higher Level in the same subject commonly needs thirty to forty-five, weighted towards the final two terms. Name the level in your first message so a tutor quotes against the real workload instead of guessing.

faqs.question: How many hours of Internal Assessment supervision should we budget for?
faqs.answer: Four to six hours per component is realistic, and they work best spread across the drafting period rather than clustered before the deadline. The first one or two narrow a research question that is almost always too broad. The next explain the assessment criteria letter by letter with their mark allocations, which is the part students rarely see in class. The rest are feedback sessions on drafts the student has written. No part of that involves a tutor producing text for submission, and any provider offering that is selling the student's qualification rather than a service.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office or send tutors to buildings in Downtown Dubai?
faqs.answer: Neither. IB Gram runs no office, centre or branch in the UAE and does not provide home visits anywhere in the country; home visiting is offered only in India. Diploma support for a family in this corridor is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The phrase near me is used on this page because it is what parents type, and the honest answer to it is that the useful search is for the right specialist rather than the closest one, since the lesson arrives the same way either way.

faqs.question: When do IB Diploma students in the UAE actually sit their exams?
faqs.answer: UAE schools use the May session. Beyond that, no date is published on this page, and the reason is worth knowing: the IB's own website blocks automated checking, so nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate specific windows and results dates for coming sessions, and several of them disagree. The only safe source for your child's dates is the school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates quoted elsewhere on this site are sourced from those boards and cited.

faqs.question: Can one tutor support two Diploma subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Mathematics and Physics pair naturally, as do Chemistry and Biology, and a tutor covering both sees the overlap in a way two separate tutors cannot. It stops being sensible at Higher Level in two unrelated subjects, where genuine depth in each is what you are paying for. If a tutor offers to cover four subjects at Higher Level, treat the offer as a signal about depth. Two related subjects with one specialist is efficient; four with a generalist is a coverage claim, not a plan.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 13 with eight months left. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but more expensive than starting a year earlier and narrower in what it can do. Eight months is enough to rebuild technique in one or two subjects, to rescue an Internal Assessment that has gone wrong if the school deadline still allows it, and to run a serious past-paper programme before the final series. It is not enough to relearn two Higher Level syllabuses from the beginning. The honest plan names what it will not attempt, which is why the first step is a diagnostic hour on a real script rather than a package.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to get Diploma support in this corridor?
faqs.answer: One diagnostic hour, then a single weekly hour in the one subject furthest below target, held for a term and reviewed against the next real school mark. At the published mid-tier Dubai band that sits inside Bestimate's AED 600 to 1,200 monthly estimate. Budget online tutoring is advertised far lower, from about AED 33 to 65 an hour by Tutopiya and EdFlik, and for straightforward content coverage it can be reasonable value. For Higher Level technique and Internal Assessment criteria, the cheap tier is usually the expensive choice.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor who is a current IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the premium should be a deliberate decision. Examiner-informed teaching helps most on extended-response technique and on reading what a mark scheme rewards, which matters at Higher Level in the final two terms. It adds little to Standard Level content coverage or early Year 12 foundations, where a strong subject teacher does the same job for less. There is also a credibility point: current examiner status is difficult to evidence, so treat an unverified claim about it as marketing rather than information, and never as access to papers or boundaries.

faqs.question: How do evening traffic and school timings affect when sessions can run?
faqs.answer: A Diploma student at a campus in Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf or Al Safa is usually home between four and five, and a parent commuting from DIFC or Business Bay often not before seven. That leaves roughly 4.30pm to 6pm and 7.30pm to 9pm as usable windows, and most Year 13 work happens in the later one. A travelling tutor prices a late slot higher or asks for a two-hour minimum to justify the trip. A video lesson costs the same at 7.30pm as at 4pm, so the slot is simply there.

faqs.question: Do lessons stop during Ramadan and the long Dubai holidays?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop. Ramadan shortens the school day and shifts energy levels, so sessions commonly run later in the evening, often after Iftar, for the weeks it covers. The December break and the spring break around the end of March are both natural pause points, and the summer is when families either stop entirely or use the gap for a transition block before a new course. A plan that ignores all three loses several weeks a year, which is why the calendar is set at the start rather than negotiated weekly.

faqs.question: Is the IB more expensive to support than IGCSE or A Level?
faqs.answer: Usually, for a structural reason rather than a rate one. A Diploma student carries six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, so there are more components where something can go wrong and more deadlines competing for the same weeks. A Level narrows to three or four subjects with deeper content, which concentrates the need. Published hourly rates reflect this too: Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The sensible response is concentration, not a larger budget spread across everything.

faqs.question: What questions should I ask before committing to a Diploma tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: Which component will you work on first, and how did you decide. How many hours do you expect this to take, and across which terms. Is the rate per hour or per lesson, and does it include VAT. What happens if we cancel, and with how much notice. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years. And what will you not do with my child's Internal Assessment. A provider who answers all six in writing is quoting a plan rather than an hour.

intro.heading: What a twenty-minute radius around Academic City actually contains
paragraphs: Take the search at face value for a moment. Draw a circle twenty minutes wide around Dubai International Academic City at five o'clock on a weekday. Inside it you have the university campuses the free zone was built for, Dubai English Speaking College on the British route, the apartment blocks of Dubai Silicon Oasis, the warehouses of Ras Al Khor, the clusters of International City around Dragon Mart, and a stretch of Al Ain Road. What you do not have is a concentration of IB Diploma teaching.

The nearest IB Diploma provision is GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis. After that the IB map moves outwards: Uptown International School in Mirdif, Universal American School in Al Warqa, GEMS Modern Academy and North London Collegiate School Dubai in Nad Al Sheba, Deira International School in Al Garhoud. Those schools employ Diploma teachers, and those teachers are generally not available as private tutors to students at their own school, because the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars it.

So the honest arithmetic of a proximity search here goes like this. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment. Spread that across PYP, MYP and DP and across the whole emirate, then filter for the eastern suburbs, then filter for people who teach a named Diploma subject at Higher Level, then filter again for willingness to drive to Al Ruwayyah in evening traffic. The result is not a shortlist. It is usually one name, or none.

That is the problem with the word 'near'. It is a proxy for 'available this week', and in this district it is a bad proxy. IB Gram answers the search by removing the radius: lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the subject and level. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service - and we say so here rather than letting you find out at the booking stage.

One more thing worth saying before the detail. A proximity search is usually made under pressure, after a report or a mock result, and pressure is what this market prices. The weeks when families most want a tutor near them are the weeks when the fewest specialists are free, which is how a generalist ends up charging specialist rates. Booking earlier is the only reliable protection, and it costs the same. What follows is written for somebody comparing options rather than being sold one. The four provider models in this market and what each actually costs. The HL and SL weightings that decide where revision should go. The availability table nobody else publishes, including what happens when a subject cannot be staffed. The regulator map across the emirates. And a list of questions worth asking any tutor, including us, before the first lesson is booked.
