dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-academic.programmesIntro: A proximity search rarely says which programme the child is in, and the answer changes completely between them. These are the three IB stages families in this cluster enquire about, with what each actually needs.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, no external examinations, reported against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages. The two things it does not systematically drill are number fluency and extended writing, and both reappear as problems in MYP. A parent reading a PYP report for the first time often cannot tell whether their child is doing well, which is itself a reason to ask someone to read it with you.
programmes.countryNote: Within reach of Academic City, the PYP runs at Universal American School in Al Warqa and Uptown International School in Mirdif. Both are a drive away, which means PYP parents here are already used to a school run. For tutoring, the useful ask at this age is specific and short: times tables to automatic recall, or a term of structured writing, rather than an open-ended weekly arrangement.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each graded 1-8 against four published criteria with a maximum of eight marks per criterion. In the sciences those criteria are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students who know the content still lose marks on criteria B and C, because investigation design and data evaluation are separate skills nobody taught them explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: MYP is where a proximity search is least damaging, because the work is skill-building rather than examination technique and a good generalist can help. It is also where the eastern-suburbs tutor pool is deepest. The one thing to get right is the transition year: a student finishing MYP 5 who moves into Diploma Mathematics without automatic algebra will struggle in DP1 regardless of how good the local tutor was.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Scored out of 45 including up to three points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the school and moderated externally, and HL papers include components SL candidates never see.
programmes.countryNote: This is where proximity fails hardest. A Diploma subject at Higher Level needs a specialist, and in the eastern suburbs the local supply of, say, Chemistry HL specialists is thin enough that families end up accepting a generalist and paying full specialist rates for it. UAE schools sit the May session, and demand for Diploma tutoring in Dubai peaks in the January and February window before it.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: TOK, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge runs as an exhibition in DP1 and a 1,600-word essay in DP2. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word supervised independent research piece. Together they carry up to three points. CAS is not graded but must be completed. The core is where the most Diploma points are quietly lost, because nobody treats it as a subject with a timetable.
programmes.countryNote: Core support is the most commonly mismatched request we see from this cluster. Families ask for an Extended Essay tutor and mean several different things: help choosing a question, help with research method, or - from a minority - somebody to write it. We do the first two. The student writes every word, and we say that explicitly because at least one operator in these search results does not.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-academic.subjectsIntro: What a near-me search cannot tell you is whether the nearest tutor teaches your child's actual subject at the right level. These are the Diploma subjects requested most from this cluster, with what the assessment demands.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus, algebraic fluency. HL adds induction, complex numbers, vectors and considerably heavier integration. The marks that go missing are method marks: answers presented without working, and calculator methods used where an analytic one was required.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. The failure is interpretive - a correct regression line followed by no statement of what the gradient means in context. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding inference.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 multiple choice and short response, Paper 2 extended response, Paper 3 experimental and option content. Marks go on explanations written in everyday language rather than with defined quantities, and on uncertainty handling in the Internal Assessment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics, equilibrium and acid-base chemistry carry the heaviest loads. Mechanism drawing is where marks disappear: arrows from the wrong origin, missing lone pairs, charges omitted. HL extends synthesis routes and quantitative equilibrium.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the grade more than content does. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'describe' carry different expectations and students answer all three identically. Data-based questions reward reading axes and error bars before writing anything at all.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams must be titled, labelled and referenced in the prose to score. HL adds a calculation-heavy paper. The Internal Assessment is three 800-word commentaries on recent news articles, and most lost marks sit in the evaluation rather than the theory.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of unseen non-literary text, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral on a global issue, and for HL a 1,200 to 1,500 word HL Essay. The commonest error is a global issue pitched so broadly that no specific text evidence supports it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The analytical toolkit is applied to stimulus material, not described. Higher mark bands need a justified judgement rather than a balanced list. HL candidates sit an additional paper based on pre-released stimulus issued ahead of the session.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be used as evidence for an argument rather than recited. Marks go missing on the critical-thinking strands: methodological limitations, cultural and gender considerations, and alternative explanations, all of which are teachable as a writing habit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The DP1 exhibition and the DP2 essay of 1,600 words. The exhibition fails when the three objects illustrate the prompt rather than evidencing a claim about knowledge. Support is Socratic questioning on the student's own objects and drafts, never supplied text.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Assessed on focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation and engagement. Most failures are structural and early: a question too broad to answer in the word count, or no stated method. The tutor interrogates the question and reads the student's drafts.

subjects.name: Internal Assessment coaching across the sciences
subjects.description: The scientific investigation carries roughly a fifth of each science grade. Coaching covers research-question framing, variable control, uncertainty propagation and the evaluation section, worked on the student's own data. The student designs, measures and writes.

sections.heading: The four provider models competing for this search, compared honestly
paragraphs: A near-me search returns four different kinds of business wearing similar websites, and the differences between them matter more than the differences in their copy. There is the specialist agency, which vets and assigns tutors and charges accordingly. There is the international marketplace, which lists tutors and takes a cut, usually pricing in dollars. There is the independent freelancer, found by word of mouth or a community group. And there is the tuition centre, which teaches in small groups on premises.

Each has a genuine case. A freelancer who has taught Physics HL in a Dubai school for a decade and lives in Mirdif may be the best option available to a Mirdif family, and no platform will beat that. A tuition centre is cheaper per hour because the cost is shared across four students, which suits content revision and suits individual diagnosis badly. A marketplace offers choice and leaves the vetting to you. An agency charges more and carries the replacement risk.

What none of them should do is compare themselves against an unnamed straw man, which is what most pages in this market do. So the table below compares models rather than brands, and the only rates in it are market bands attributed to whoever published them in October 2026. Our own column is honest about what we are not: no premises, no UAE office, no regulator approval, and no in-home option.

The practical use of this table is as a question list. Whichever model you choose, ask about permit status, replacement policy, whether a trial exists, and whether the rate quoted is per hour or per session. Those four questions eliminate most of the bad outcomes in this market.

sections.heading: HL against SL: where the extra hours should actually go
paragraphs: Families searching for a tutor near them rarely say which level the subject is at, and it is the most important variable in the request. Higher Level is not Standard Level plus enthusiasm. It is more syllabus content, longer papers, additional components SL candidates never sit, and a different grade distribution. A tutor who teaches SL comfortably may be out of their depth at HL in the same subject, and the parent cannot tell from a profile.

The practical consequence is where revision time goes. If a component is worth a fifth of the grade, a fifth of the preparation belongs to it, and the Internal Assessment is routinely the component students neglect while over-revising the paper they find most comfortable. Writing the weightings out, subject by subject, is a short exercise that redirects a whole term's work.

The second consequence is subject choice. Three HLs is the standard load and the combination matters: two heavily quantitative HLs plus a third with a demanding written component produces a January in DP2 that cannot be survived by effort alone. If your child is still choosing, map the assessment load across the two years rather than looking at interest alone.

sections.heading: Tutor availability, coverage limits and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-local delivery behind a phone number. We would rather publish the limit, because the alternative is a parent paying specialist rates for a generalist and discovering it in week three. There are IB subject and level combinations we can staff within days, some that take a couple of weeks, and a few we should decline.

The pattern is predictable. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English at both levels are generally straightforward. Business Management, Psychology and Geography are usually fine. The genuinely difficult ones are Further Mathematics, the less commonly taught Group 2 languages, Music, Film, and Physics HL at short notice in the eight weeks before mocks, when every Diploma family in the emirate is competing for the same people.

When a combination cannot be staffed properly, there are three honest responses and we use all three depending on the case: give a realistic wait, offer a tutor in the adjacent subject who can genuinely help with the overlapping content while being clear about the boundary, or say no. What we do not do is assign a generalist to an HL subject and let the trial lesson sell itself on personality.

This is also the right place to note what we are not. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit, because that is issued to training institutes with premises. We are not approved, accredited or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any page claiming otherwise about any provider is worth a second look.

sections.heading: Questions worth asking any tutor, including us, before the first lesson
paragraphs: A near-me search usually ends with a phone call, and the quality of that call determines most of what follows. The questions below are not a sales filter; they are the ones that surface the problems in this market, and any provider worth hiring will answer all of them without hesitation.

Start with the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted at you. Ask whether the person teaching your child holds a current permit and ask to see it.

Then ask the specifics. Which exact subject and level have you taught, and for how many cohorts? Who is the tutor - a name, not a tier? Is the quoted figure per hour or per session, and does it include VAT? What is the replacement policy if the match fails? Is there a trial, and what happens if we stop after it? What exactly will you do with my child's Internal Assessment, and what will you refuse to do?

The last question is the most revealing. A provider that will not say clearly where the line sits on coursework is a provider you should not hand an Extended Essay to. One operator competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. The malpractice consequence of that falls on the candidate, which is to say on your sixteen-year-old, not on the person who took the money.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the emirates
paragraphs: Families relocating within the UAE, or comparing a Dubai school against one in Sharjah or Abu Dhabi, hit a confusing fact: there is no single national school regulator. Each emirate has its own authority, with different names and somewhat different powers, and almost no tutoring page in this market mentions more than one of them.

In Dubai it is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae says supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. For Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, the federal Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role.

The powers are not purely inspectorial. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator, not only inspection. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

For a tutoring decision this matters in one concrete way. These bodies regulate schools, not private tutors. A private individual tutoring in Dubai operates under the MoHRE permit; a tutoring business with premises needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. So a provider describing its tutors as approved by KHDA is either misunderstanding the system or referring to a permit it should be able to show you.

sections.heading: How progress gets measured when nobody is in the room
paragraphs: The fair worry about an online tutor is not whether the lesson works but whether you can tell. With an in-home tutor you at least hear the session through a wall. With online delivery the evidence has to be deliberate, and a provider who cannot describe how progress is reported is a provider guessing.

The only measurement worth anything is the school's own marking. Our baseline is set from the student's existing marked work and, where the subject allows, two timed past papers marked against the published mark scheme. That produces a list of specific recurring errors rather than an impression. The error log the student keeps becomes the tracking document: every mark lost, the reason in their own words, and whether that reason has recurred since.

Reporting is short and written. Every few weeks a note saying what has moved, what has not, and what changes next. Not a grade prediction - we do not publish predicted scores or promise improvements, and any provider offering a guaranteed grade is making a claim they cannot honour and should not make. What we can report is whether the identified errors are still appearing in marked work.

If the numbers are not moving after a fair run, the honest options are to change the tutor, change the approach, or stop. We would rather reassign than defend a match. A tutor the student has stopped talking to is teaching nothing, and the parent is usually the last person to find out unless somebody asks the question directly.

sections.heading: The Diploma year as a timetable, not a vibe
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and the useful thing about saying that out loud is what follows from it. The pressure point in the Diploma is not May. It is the January and February window of DP2, when Internal Assessments across four or five subjects, the Extended Essay final submission, the TOK essay and the school's mock examinations all land inside a few weeks.

Counting backwards from there changes when tutoring is worth buying. A student with no Extended Essay progress by the October of DP2 is not behind on one piece of work; they are about to be behind on everything, because the hours have to come from somewhere and they will come from mock revision. Families who book core support in DP1 spend less in total than those who react in February.

We publish no specific IB session or results dates anywhere on this site. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date at all. Confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org directly. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications, the dates are sourced: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, the February/March series being offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

One further calendar item specific to this region. Ramadan shortens the school day and moves the useful part of the evening, and a session booked for late afternoon during the month is usually wasted. Weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots work. Fix the pattern before the month begins rather than renegotiating weekly, and remember that revision for a May session overlaps with it in most years.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: Whichever IB school your near-me search leads to, the timetable will include Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies. These are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states the requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. New arrivals in this cluster are regularly surprised by it at the first report rather than the open day.

The rules are quite specific and worth knowing before asking for tutoring. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is primary for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length so long as the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a checkable credential point rather than a vague assurance.

What constrains tutoring is a content rule: for these mandatory subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. So support for Arabic as an additional language is ordinary language teaching and freely available, while help with the mandatory Islamic Education and Social Studies content needs a conversation with the school about what material it will accept. For equivalency purposes, note that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five-subject GCSE and IGCSE count.

process.title: Say the subject, the level and the date
process.description: Not 'IB science'. Chemistry HL or Biology SL, which school, which session, and what the last marked assessment came back as. That sentence is enough for us to know whether a specialist exists and whether the timeline is realistic, which are the only two things that matter at this stage.

process.title: We check coverage and tell you what we find
process.description: If your combination is one of the hard ones to staff, you hear that now, with a realistic wait, rather than after a disappointing third session. If it is one we should decline, we decline. Publishing that limit is why the availability table on this page exists.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a written diagnosis
process.description: A real lesson on real content with the student working and the tutor diagnosing. Afterwards you get a plain written note: what the tutor found, which components are weakest, and what eight weeks would target. Say no and nothing further is owed.

process.title: Fix the slot around the school run
process.description: From Silicon Oasis or Mirdif, 4.45pm is realistic; from Academic City, 5pm; from International City, 6pm. We schedule on Gulf Standard Time against the worst-case journey rather than the average one, because ten minutes lost from every lesson adds up to a lot of paid time.

process.title: Review against the school's marking, not ours
process.description: Baseline from existing marked work and timed papers, an error log kept by the student, and a short written note every few weeks on what has moved. No predicted scores and no promised improvements. If the match is wrong, we reassign rather than argue for it.

whyPoints.title: We publish the coverage limit
whyPoints.description: No competitor page in this market discloses what it cannot staff. Ours does, by subject group, with realistic match times and what the fallback is. Knowing in advance that Further Mathematics is hard to find beats discovering it after two paid sessions with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: Proximity is not a quality filter here
whyPoints.description: A twenty-minute radius around Academic City contains university campuses, a British-route secondary and a lot of road. It does not contain a choice of Diploma Higher Level specialists. Removing travel from the match widens the pool rather than reducing it.

whyPoints.title: Model-level comparison instead of a straw man
whyPoints.description: The provider table on this page compares agency, marketplace, freelancer, tuition centre and us, with market rates attributed to whoever published them and dated. It names our weaknesses: no premises, no UAE office, no in-home option anywhere in the Emirates.

whyPoints.title: Measurement that does not rely on our own opinion
whyPoints.description: Baseline from the student's marked work and timed past papers, an error log the student maintains, and short written reviews. We publish no predicted grades and promise no improvement, because neither is something anybody can honestly guarantee.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts. Never supplied text, never a chosen topic, never generated data. An operator in these search results sells finished Internal Assessments; the malpractice finding from that lands on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Regulators named accurately, approval claimed nowhere
whyPoints.description: KHDA for Dubai, ADEK for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA for Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge for Ras Al Khaimah, the Ministry of Education for the rest. They regulate schools, not tutors, and none of them approves IB Gram.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: There is one-to-one IB tutoring available for a student living in Dubai International Academic City, delivered live online rather than by a tutor arriving at your door. The reason to prefer that here is specific: the nearest IB Diploma school is a junction away in Silicon Oasis, and the number of people within a short drive who teach a named Higher Level subject is very small. Online matching replaces the radius with the variable that decides the grade, which is whether the tutor actually teaches that subject at that level. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Why does the nearest tutor to Academic City often not teach the subject we need?
faqs.answer: Because the free zone was built around university campuses rather than around schools. Dubai English Speaking College sits inside it on the British route, so there is no IB Diploma teaching within the district itself. The Diploma schools this cluster uses are in Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Nad Al Sheba and Al Garhoud, and their teachers are generally unavailable to their own students as private tutors because the MoHRE permit code of conduct bars it. The result is that a proximity search returns availability rather than expertise, and the two are not the same thing.

faqs.question: Should we use an agency, a marketplace, a freelancer or a tuition centre?
faqs.answer: Each fits a different situation. A specialist agency costs more and carries the replacement risk for you. An international marketplace gives choice and leaves vetting to you, usually pricing in dollars rather than dirhams. An experienced independent freelancer in Mirdif may be the best option a Mirdif family has, with the caveat of being a single point of failure. A tuition centre is cheaper per hour because the cost is shared, which suits content revision and suits individual diagnosis poorly. Ask all four about permit status, replacement policy and whether the rate is per hour or per session.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a student in this cluster?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics, the sciences at Standard Level, Economics and English, usually within days. Physics at Higher Level in the eight weeks before mock examinations takes one to two weeks, because every Diploma family in the emirate wants the same specialists at the same moment. Less commonly taught Group 2 languages take two weeks or longer. Further Mathematics, Music and Film we often cannot staff at all, and in that case we say so rather than substituting a generalist. The availability table on this page is published precisely so you can see that before enquiring.

faqs.question: What should I ask a Dubai tutor before booking the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Five things. Does the person teaching my child hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? Which subject and level have you taught, and for how many cohorts? Is the quoted figure per hour or per session, and does it include VAT? What is the replacement policy if the match fails? And exactly what will you do with an Internal Assessment, and what will you refuse to do? The last question is the most revealing, because a provider that will not state the coursework boundary clearly is one to avoid.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching my child in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, so no tutor can price it into a rate, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you as unverified. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18.

faqs.question: Is my child's Higher Level subject harder to tutor than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Materially, yes, and the difference is not effort. Higher Level covers additional syllabus content on top of the core, sits longer papers, and includes components Standard Level candidates never see. A tutor comfortable at Standard Level in the same subject can be out of their depth at Higher Level, and a parent cannot tell that from a profile. The honest test is two marked Higher Level past papers: a tutor who can walk a student through the mark scheme on those, question by question, is the real thing. Ask for that before committing to a term.

faqs.question: How do I know an online tutor is actually working if I cannot hear the lesson?
faqs.answer: By insisting the measurement comes from the school's marking rather than the tutor's impression. Our baseline is the student's existing marked work plus, where the subject allows, two timed past papers marked against the published mark scheme, which produces a list of specific recurring errors. The student keeps an error log of every mark lost and the reason in their own words. Every few weeks you get a short written note on what has moved and what has not. We publish no predicted grades and promise no improvement, because neither can be honestly guaranteed.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do families in this radius actually send their children to?
faqs.answer: Within the immediate radius, GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis is the nearest IB Diploma provision; Dubai English Speaking College inside Academic City runs the British route instead. Beyond that the names that recur in enquiries from this cluster are Uptown International School in Mirdif, Universal American School in Al Warqa, GEMS Modern Academy and North London Collegiate School Dubai in Nad Al Sheba, and Deira International School in Al Garhoud. They are named here as local context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any school, and each is inspected and rated by KHDA.

faqs.question: Can we book just a few sessions rather than a whole term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for the Diploma core it is often the right shape. Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge support works as a finite block of four to eight sessions timed to the school's internal deadlines rather than as an open weekly commitment. Weekly sessions make more sense for a subject where content needs rebuilding over months. What we would discourage is a single session bought as a diagnosis, because the free trial already does that job and gives you a written summary without any money changing hands.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in each emirate?
faqs.answer: Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing private education quality. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education. All of them regulate schools; none licenses individual private tutors, which is MoHRE's permit.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office or centre in Dubai we could visit?
faqs.answer: No. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, and no page of ours should ever suggest one. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit either, because that permit is issued to training institutes that have premises and staff in Dubai, which we do not. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Several pages competing for this search imply otherwise about themselves, and it is worth asking any provider to show the permit they are referring to.

faqs.question: When is the Diploma year actually busiest for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The January and February window of the second Diploma year, not May. That is when Internal Assessments across four or five subjects, the Extended Essay final submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the school's mock examinations all arrive within a few weeks of each other. UAE schools sit the May session, so counting backwards from that crowded window is what produces a plan. Families who arrange core support during the first Diploma year consistently buy fewer total hours than those who react once the window has already arrived.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change tutoring arrangements in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, which frees the afternoon, but late-afternoon concentration is usually poor and a session booked then is often wasted. The two slots that work are weekend mornings and after Iftar on weekdays. Because no tutor is travelling, moving to a post-Iftar slot is a scheduling decision rather than a logistics problem. Fix the pattern before the month starts rather than renegotiating week by week, and bear in mind that in most years revision for the May examination session overlaps with Ramadan, so the plan has to account for both.

faqs.question: Will my child still have Arabic and Islamic Education at an IB school here?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, with KHDA's guidance requiring implementation from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on 40-minute lesson units. For these subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so ask the school what tutoring material it accepts.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-academic.closingHeading: Replace the radius with the right question
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-academic.closingBody: If you are in Dubai International Academic City, Silicon Oasis, International City, Al Warqa or Mirdif, the question that gets your child a good tutor is not how far away they live. It is which subject, which level, which session, and what the last marked piece of work said. Send us those four things and we will tell you honestly whether a specialist in that exact combination is available, how long a match would take, and whether we are the wrong people for it. The trial lesson is free and comes with a written diagnosis. Lessons are one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Count the whole education budget before you add a line to it
paragraphs: Most families searching for a tutor from this district are relatively new to Dubai, and tutoring is arriving on top of a budget that already surprised them. School fees are the headline, but they are not the whole of it: school transport is a separate charge and a substantial one when a child commutes out of a district with little school provision, and uniform, devices, trips and activity fees follow. Tutoring then appears as an extra line in a budget nobody has yet seen a full year of.

That is why this page starts with the whole figure rather than the hourly rate. A tutoring decision made against a complete picture is a different decision from one made in isolation, and in particular it exposes a question most families never ask: whether the school already provides, inside fees already paid, some of what the tutor is being hired to do. For an IB family that is often true of subject clinics and revision sessions, and it is the cheapest thing to check first.

The tutoring market itself is worth stating plainly, since most competitor pages will not. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with budget online tutors advertised from about AED 33 to 65 and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the figure. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, and they are market context rather than IB Gram's price list.

A near-me search from this district carries a particular premium. Dubai Creek Harbour is reached by a limited number of access roads with the Ras Al Khor crossings carrying the load, and a tutor driving in at four in the afternoon loses a substantial part of their working evening to the journey. They price for that, reasonably, and the result is that quotes here sit towards the upper half of the in-home band while buying nothing academic. The drive does not make anyone better at Higher Level Chemistry.

IB Gram delivers Diploma tuition to Dubai Creek Harbour as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the subject and level rather than the postcode, with no travel component inside the price. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below set out the full budget, the premium, and how to judge whether a tutoring line is earning its place in it.
Nothing here promises a grade. It gives a family in their first years in Dubai the figures and the test, which is more useful than a promise and considerably rarer in this market.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-creek-ha.subjectsIntro: A Diploma budget is allocated subject by subject, so the question is which subject earns the line. These are the courses we cover for this district, each noted for where marks are genuinely lost, because that determines whether a specialist rate is justified.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Cheap to fix early and expensive to leave. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes algebraic fluency, and Higher Level adds a third paper needing its own sessions rather than more of the same practice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led, with calculator competence examinable. Losses concentrate in explaining output the student can produce, which is a technique problem and among the faster things to correct.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two papers plus an independent investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Equilibrium reasoning, organic mechanism detail and significant figures in the data-based section are the reliable losses at both levels.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Weak algebra costs Physics marks unrelated to physics, so one maths block can reasonably be charged against two grades. Uncertainty treatment is the least-taught and most-penalised area.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision outweighs calculation. A fluent but imprecise writer plateaus, and command-term discipline moves the grade faster and cheaper than more content coverage.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment commentaries land alongside other subjects' deadlines in DP1, so the cost here is often scheduling rather than teaching. Evaluation depth separates Higher Level marks.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks are easy and evaluation is not. A student applying a tool without weighing it sits mid-band indefinitely, which is a technique loss and therefore the cheapest category to fix.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Carries the Individual Oral and the Higher Level essay. Describing texts rather than analysing construction is the standard loss, and a short targeted block beats a year of weekly sessions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Few tutors teach it, so it carries a scarcity cost rather than a difficulty cost. Support is structural: reading the prescribed title, building an argument, locating where marks are awarded.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research. One early session narrowing the question is the best value in the whole programme, because a poor question cannot be rescued later at any price.

sections.heading: The whole education budget a new arrival is carrying
paragraphs: A tutoring quote means little in isolation, and in a first or second year in Dubai it is particularly easy to misjudge, because the other lines are still unfamiliar. The table below sets out the full picture for a household in this district, with the tutoring bands from the market alongside the costs that come first. Figures for school-set charges are deliberately described rather than invented, because they vary enormously by school and the school publishes its own.

Two lines deserve attention because new arrivals consistently underestimate them. The first is school transport. In a district with little provision of its own, nearly every child commutes out, and a bus place is a separate annual charge that rises with route length. A family choosing a school further inland is choosing a higher transport bill as well as a longer journey, and both are recurring for as long as the child is there.

The second is the collection of smaller charges that arrive across a year: uniform, devices, trips, activity fees, examination-related costs. Individually modest and collectively material, and they land unevenly through the year, which is what makes a monthly tutoring commitment feel affordable in September and uncomfortable in February. A household that has seen a full year of these can budget confidently; one in its first year cannot, and should therefore prefer bounded blocks to open-ended arrangements.

The useful conclusion is not that tutoring is unaffordable. It is that the tutoring line should be sized against a complete picture and committed in defined blocks with end dates, rather than as an indefinite monthly payment entered into before the rest of the year is known. That is a cheaper pattern and also a better one, because a block with a purpose and a deadline gets reviewed.

sections.heading: Why quotes to this district sit high, and what the crossing costs
paragraphs: A near-me search from Dubai Creek Harbour returns quotes towards the upper half of the Dubai in-home band, and the reason is worth understanding rather than resenting. The district is reached by a limited number of access roads, with the Ras Al Khor crossings carrying the traffic, and a tutor coming from the city's teaching concentrations at four in the afternoon spends a large part of their working evening in the car.

A tutor's evening between four and eight is four hours. In a tower district close to the main teaching concentrations they might fit three sessions into it. Coming here, with a crossing at each end, they fit two. The rate per session rises to compensate, which is arithmetic rather than opportunism, and it is the same arithmetic that makes specialists in short supply decline the journey entirely when nearer work exists.

That second effect is the expensive one and it never appears in a quote. The narrower the pool willing to travel, the more likely it is that the in-home option delivers a generalist at a specialist price. A household here can pay the top of the band and get someone whose actual specialism is adjacent to what their child needs, because the filter that produced the shortlist was willingness to drive rather than having taught the subject.

Online delivery removes both effects at once: no crossing, and a shortlist drawn from every available specialist rather than the drivable subset. The honest counterpoint is presence, which matters for younger students and for a teenager who will not work unless somebody is in the room. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so for that household a local arrangement is the right answer and the bands here are what to judge it against.

sections.heading: Cost per outcome, not cost per hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for judging value, because the same hour produces entirely different results depending on what happens inside it. A more useful question is what a given purchase is supposed to change, and what it costs to change that one thing. Asked that way, the cheapest items in this market are not the low hourly rates but the small, well-timed interventions nobody advertises.

The clearest example is an internal assessment or Extended Essay question review. One or two sessions, a modest total at any rate, and it determines a large share of a component carrying a fifth of a subject grade, because a question that cannot be answered with the available resources cannot be rescued later by any amount of teaching. Nothing else in the Diploma offers that ratio, and almost nobody sells it as a product.

Next is a foundation block in DP1 on a subject chosen above the student's prior attainment. Six to ten sessions, bought while the gap is small, against weekly support across two years bought once the gap has widened. Then paper technique after a DP2 mock, where losses are procedural and marked practice moves them in weeks. The worst ratio in the market is open-ended revision of a whole course with no component named, which consumes the most and demonstrates the least.

The table sets the comparison out. Use it as a way of interrogating any proposal: what is this meant to change, how will we know, and how much is it. A tutor who can answer all three is selling an outcome; one who can only answer the third is selling hours, which is what most of this market sells and what parents in their first Dubai year are least equipped to evaluate.

sections.heading: What you are already paying for, and should use first
paragraphs: This section will save some households more than any negotiation would. A substantial amount of academic support is already inside the fees a family in this district pays, and new arrivals are the least likely to know it exists because nobody sends a list. It is delivered by the people who teach the course, administer the entries and write the predicted grades, which is a position no external tutor occupies.

Typical provision includes subject clinics at lunchtime or after school, departmental revision sessions nearer an examination session, access to practice material through the school's platform, a Diploma coordinator who holds the internal deadlines, and subject teachers who will read a draft internal assessment within the school's own rules. In a Diploma context the coordinator is particularly valuable, because the deadlines that actually constrain a student are internal and the coordinator sets them.

What school provision cannot do is diagnose one student against a mark scheme in an unhurried hour, set and mark individual practice weekly, or move to a time that suits one household's bus timetable. Those are the things worth buying. A household that uses the school provision first and buys the diagnosis afterwards typically spends a third of what it was about to, and gets a better result because the two are doing different jobs.

The practical step is a single email to the head of year or the coordinator asking what support is available and when. For a family in its first year in Dubai that email is the highest-value five minutes in this entire page, and it frequently changes the size of the tutoring purchase before any quote has been compared.

sections.heading: Where a first-year-in-Dubai family loses money
paragraphs: The waste patterns here are slightly different from those of a settled household, because they come from not yet knowing the system rather than from inattention. Naming them is the point of a cost-led page, and all six are avoidable without spending less per hour.

The first is buying before mapping the free provision, which produces a paid tutor re-covering what the department covers on a Wednesday. The second is duration bought before diagnosis: a weekly arrangement entered into in September, before the household has seen a full year of its own costs or a single marked paper. The third is paying a specialist rate for homework supervision, which is a real service and not a specialist one.

The fourth is specific to this district: paying the crossing premium for subjects where presence changes nothing, which at Diploma level is nearly all of them. The fifth is funding several subjects when one weakness underlies them, usually algebra under maths and two sciences or writing structure under two essay subjects. The sixth is the block that renews because stopping feels risky, long after its purpose was met.

What all six share is that none feels like waste while it is happening, because attendance is easy to observe and diagnosis is not. The remedy is mechanical rather than clever: write down at the start what the block is for, set a date to check it, and be willing to end it when the check comes back empty. In a first Dubai year that discipline is harder to apply and more valuable, because nothing else in the budget is yet predictable.

sections.heading: Counted backwards from the May session: when the money works
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and spending decisions make far more sense read backwards from it than forwards from today. For a family new to the system, the surprise is that the deadlines which actually constrain a Diploma student are set by the school rather than by the IB, so an internal assessment can fall due months before anything the IB publishes.

Before a family new to Dubai builds a budget on the table above, two limits on what it can tell you. The dates that matter are not ours to publish and are not published here: the IB holds the examination and results dates, and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, which are what actually govern internal assessments, Extended Essay drafts and Theory of Knowledge submissions. In a first year in the city the temptation is to lift a timetable from whichever tutoring website loads first, this one included, rather than approach a coordinator you have not yet met. Approach them anyway, inside the first term, and from the moment an internal deadline is announced treat it as firm.

Read for spending, the calendar gives a simple sequence. Spend small and early on anything irreversible. Spend moderately and steadily through DP1 on a diagnosed weakness. Spend heavily and briefly in the final window if the marked mock says you must, then stop. The pattern that fails is the inverse, and it is the one a new arrival is most likely to fall into: nothing in DP1 while the family settles, then a large open-ended commitment in DP2 when there is least time for it to work.

One further point worth asking the coordinator about early. Internal assessment deadlines cluster across subjects and sit near the Extended Essay deadline, so the weeks when a subject most needs attention are the weeks the student has least to give. Knowing where those collisions fall lets a household move a block earlier rather than bidding for evenings already committed, which is a saving that costs nothing to arrange.

sections.heading: KHDA, the fee freeze and judging whether the spend is working
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Annual inspection runs on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, published school by school, and for a family new to Dubai those reports are the most useful free document available. The departmental commentary matters more than the band.

The cost context this year is unusually favourable. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

With the largest line flat, a tutoring figure is more visible in a household budget than usual, which makes this a good year to apply a test rather than a feeling. At six weeks you should be able to see three things: a written statement of what was costing marks, marked practice showing that specific thing improving, and a mark or grade trend in the subject. If all three are absent, the spend is not working however agreeable the sessions are, and the test requires no subject knowledge at all.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Any service describing its individual tutors with that phrase is referring to something else or saying something untrue, which for a new arrival comparing quotes is a quick and useful filter.

sections.heading: What is never for sale, at any price
paragraphs: A cost-led page has to name the point at which the cheapest-looking option is the most expensive. At least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. To a family under deadline pressure in an unfamiliar system that can look like a solution with a known cost, which is precisely why it is dangerous. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic misconduct under IB rules, the student bears the consequence, which can be the loss of the Diploma, and the seller bears none of it.

What is legitimately for sale is substantial and represents the best value in this page's ordering. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the language the examiner uses, question a research question until it is answerable with the resources available, warn that a method will generate too little data, teach the underlying content, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written.

What is not available from us at any rate is choosing the question, supplying the method or the data, writing any part of the text, or editing a draft into its final form, nor handing over a worked example close enough to the student's own task that copying becomes the obvious next step. We state this to the student in the first session rather than in small print, because a sixteen-year-old new to a system and under deadline pressure deserves the boundary before they are standing on it.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and we do not host them for download. We reference them and link to the official source, which costs nothing, is the lawful position and is more useful anyway, because the official version is the current one while a stale file circulating in a parents' group is a reliable route to revising withdrawn content.

sections.heading: Getting started from Dubai Creek Harbour
paragraphs: Begin with two emails and one figure. Email the school to ask what academic support is already provided and when, and email the Diploma coordinator for the internal assessment deadline calendar. Then decide what you are willing to spend monthly and for how long. Those three pieces of information change the recommendation more than any detail about the subject does.

Then send the subject, the level, the latest grade labelled as mock or classwork, the teacher's last written comment quoted rather than summarised, and the time your child is actually home, including the bus route, because that sets which slots are real. A photograph of one marked paper is worth more than the grade, since it shows what is leaking marks rather than how much.

We propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson, which is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. Afterwards, ask for a written statement of what is costing marks and what the block is for, with a number of sessions and an end date attached. If that statement is general, do not book at any rate, because without it there is nothing to check at six weeks and no way to distinguish a working arrangement from a comfortable one.

And the honest part. Availability is finite and some areas are thin everywhere: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay supervision, Higher Level mathematics with Paper 3 experience, and second languages beyond the common ones. The early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots a commuting district needs also fill early. When what you want is unavailable we say so and offer another hour, a weekend morning, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time. We will also say when the school's own provision is enough.

faqs.question: What should we budget for education in total, not just tutoring?
faqs.answer: More lines than a prospectus implies. School fees are termly and published per school by KHDA. School transport is a separate charge and substantial from a district with little provision of its own, rising with route length. Uniform, devices and books are front-loaded in a first year, and trips and activity fees land unevenly through it. Tutoring then sits on top: roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month for one weekly subject at mid-tier online market rates, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year.

faqs.question: Why are tutor quotes to Dubai Creek Harbour higher than elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Access. The district is reached by a limited number of roads with the Ras Al Khor crossings carrying the load, so a tutor driving in at four in the afternoon loses a large part of their working evening. Where they might fit three sessions into an evening closer to town, they fit two here, and the rate rises to compensate. Market in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and quotes to this district cluster in the upper half of that range.

faqs.question: What does the extra money buy on a home visit here?
faqs.answer: A journey, a person in the room, and not having to set up a video call. For a younger child the presence can matter. What it does not buy is subject knowledge, because crossing the creek does not improve anyone's grasp of Higher Level Chemistry. It also narrows the shortlist to tutors willing to make a long evening journey, so a household here can pay the top of the band and still get a generalist whose actual specialism is adjacent to what their child needs.

faqs.question: Does our school already provide support we are paying for?
faqs.answer: Very probably, and new arrivals are least likely to know. Typical provision includes lunchtime or after-school subject clinics, departmental revision sessions nearer an examination session, practice material on the school's platform, and a Diploma coordinator who holds the internal assessment deadlines. One email to the head of year asking what exists and when is the highest-value five minutes on this page, and it frequently shrinks the tutoring purchase before any quote has been compared.

faqs.question: How should I compare quotes that are structured differently?
faqs.answer: Convert everything to a cost per teaching hour. A monthly in-home package of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits is eight contact hours; an online package advertised around AED 799 is eight sessions, which is eight hours only if a session is sixty minutes, so ask. Then ask what each includes beyond contact time: marked practice between sessions, written feedback, replacement if the match fails. And set aside any quote that will not say where the tutor is based.

faqs.question: Which purchase gives the most for the least in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: An internal assessment or Extended Essay question review, at one or two sessions. It determines a large share of a component carrying a fifth of a subject grade, because a question that cannot be answered with the available resources cannot be rescued later by any amount of teaching. Next is a DP1 foundation block of six to ten sessions on a subject chosen above the student's prior attainment, bought while the gap is small. The worst ratio is open-ended revision with no component named.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the money is working?
faqs.answer: Three signals at six weeks. A written statement from the tutor of what was costing marks. Marked practice in that specific area showing movement. And a mark or grade trend in the subject. If all three are present the spend is working even if the grade has not moved yet; if all three are absent it is not, however pleasant the sessions are. The test needs no subject knowledge from you and it applies identically at AED 60 an hour and at AED 450.

faqs.question: We have just arrived in Dubai. Should we start tutoring immediately?
faqs.answer: Usually not in the first term. A newly arrived student needs to settle, and you need a marked paper and a teacher's comment before anyone can diagnose anything. The exceptions are time-critical: an internal assessment question being chosen now, or a Higher Level subject the student is visibly unable to access. Otherwise the first term is better spent mapping what the school provides and letting evidence accumulate, which costs nothing and makes the eventual purchase smaller and better aimed.

faqs.question: Are school fees going up, and how should that shape our planning?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the largest education line flat, a tutoring figure is more visible in the household budget than usual. Practically, that makes this a good year to insist on a written purpose and a six-week check rather than absorbing an undifferentiated monthly payment into a general increase.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Al Quoz worth the journey from here?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for a named topic shared by several students, and it is the cheapest format in the market. The complication from this district is that the journey reappears: a return trip in the best hour of the evening, which is a real cost even though it is not on the invoice. It also works poorly for internal assessment feedback or anything personal, because an individual habit will not be noticed in a room of six. The test is whether you can name the gap.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions to manage cash flow through the year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery makes pausing cheap rather than disruptive, because no journey has to be renegotiated at either end. A holiday pause costs nothing but a held slot, and during Ramadan sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar time. The exception worth naming is the eight to ten weeks before the examination session, where pausing costs more than it saves. Agree any pause in advance so the slot is kept rather than released to another family.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's permit affect what we should be charged?
faqs.answer: It should not, because it costs them nothing. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications run through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects carry a scarcity premium?
faqs.answer: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision are thin everywhere, because almost nobody teaches them as a standalone subject, so they are worth booking earlier than feels necessary. Higher Level mathematics including Paper 3 is thinner than Standard Level, and second languages beyond the commonly taught ones are genuinely scarce. Mathematics at Standard Level, the main sciences, English A and Economics are comparatively well covered. We tell you which category applies before you book rather than after.

faqs.question: What if we start late in DP2 after a disappointing mock?
faqs.answer: It can still work with a changed plan. With eight to twelve weeks of usable time the first session should mark the mock question by question, and the plan that follows should abandon some topics deliberately rather than attempting everything. Expect a high monthly figure for a short bounded block rather than a modest figure spread thin. What you should not buy then is an open-ended arrangement, because the window closes before an open-ended plan can work, and nobody can promise a grade inside it.

faqs.question: Would a cheaper tutor ever be the right choice for us?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the problem does not need a specialist. A student who has missed two weeks to illness and needs one topic re-taught is well served by a competent budget tutor advertised from around AED 33 to 65 an hour, and paying AED 400 for that is a waste. Specialist rates are justified for paper technique, internal assessment feedback and mark-scheme judgement in an examination year. Matching the rung to the problem rather than to anxiety is the most effective cost control a family has.

faqs.question: Which six details let you propose something proportionate for a new arrival?
faqs.answer: Six things. The monthly figure you are comfortable with and for how long. What support the school already provides and when. The subject and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. The latest grade, labelled as mock or classwork. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than paraphrased. And the time your child is actually home, bus route included, because that decides which slots are real. A photograph of one marked paper beats most of the list.

Email the school for its own support provision and the coordinator for the internal deadlines, decide the monthly figure you are comfortable with, and send us the subject, the level, the latest grade and the time your child is really home. We will propose a tutor, run the first session at no cost, and tell you if the school's provision is enough.

intro.heading: The honest answer to "is there an IB tutor near me in Dubai Festival City"
paragraphs: Probably not for the subject you need, if the subject is a Higher Level science or Higher Level mathematics. That is the answer, and it is worth putting first because the alternative is a page that implies otherwise and wastes your week. The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of private school enrolment in Dubai in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum and 26 per cent Indian. The Diploma pool is therefore a thin slice of a very large market, and the Higher Level science slice of that is thinner again.

Now narrow it geographically. A tutor who will drive to Al Badia or Nad Al Hamar has to live within a workable radius of eastern Dubai, be free in the specific hour your child is home and functioning, and happen to teach the exact subject and level in question. Those three filters applied together leave very few people for Chemistry HL, Physics HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL. For Middle Years mathematics or Diploma Business Management the position is far better, and a local tutor is a perfectly reasonable choice.

This is why the better question is not who is nearby but how you tell whether someone knows the syllabus. The market makes that hard on purpose. Every tutoring site in this cluster claims IB expertise, several display self-asserted star ratings, one lists schools as trusted-by partners with no visible relationship, and one sells completed internal assessments outright. None of them tells you how to check. So the middle of this page is a set of questions that do check, and you can use them on us as readily as on anybody else.

What IB Gram actually offers a Dubai Festival City family is a live one-to-one video lesson with a tutor matched to the named subject and level, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. The reason that is a feature rather than an apology is the arithmetic above: removing the driving radius from the filter list means the only remaining filters are subject, level and hour, which is how you reach a specialist rather than a near neighbour.

The last part of the page is about verification: the permit a UAE tutor must hold, what each emirate regulator does, and the boundary around assessed work. Those are the three places where this market is weakest and where a parent has the most leverage. Ask the questions, expect specific answers, and treat vagueness as information.

One more framing worth holding. A tutor who is close by and good enough is not a bad outcome, and this page is not an argument that every Dubai Festival City family needs an online specialist. It is an argument that you should know which situation you are in before you choose. For Middle Years mathematics, a nearby tutor who understands criterion marking is an excellent answer. For Chemistry at Higher Level eight weeks before the papers, proximity is the filter most likely to cost a grade, and that is worth knowing in September rather than in April.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-festival.programmesIntro: Which IB programme your child is in changes how scarce a genuine specialist is, and that is the single most useful thing to know before you start searching. These three are the ones Dubai Festival City families ask about, in ascending order of how hard a local match becomes.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and continuous teacher assessment through transdisciplinary units. Support here is about reading stamina, number fluency and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud. The content is not where the difficulty lies, so a strong primary teacher of any background is a legitimate match.
programmes.countryNote: Local supply for PYP around Dubai Festival City and Mirdif is genuinely adequate, which makes this the one band where proximity is a reasonable filter. The vetting question that matters is whether the tutor understands inquiry-based reporting, because a PYP report reads nothing like a British-curriculum one and parents are often misled by it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, each on a 1 to 8 scale, with the total converted to a 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. Marks are lost on command verbs inside criterion strands far more often than on content, and on investigations where the method is sound and the evaluation is thin.
programmes.countryNote: The decisive vetting question for MYP is simple: ask a prospective tutor to name the four criteria for the subject in question and say what each is worth. A specialist answers in a sentence. A generalist talks about the subject instead, which is the tell. Local supply in the eastern suburbs is reasonable at this level.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Higher Level carries extra content and, in the sciences, additional paper demand. Each subject has an internal assessment marked against lettered criteria by the school's teacher and moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the local search usually fails for a Dubai Festival City family. Chemistry HL, Physics HL and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL are the three hardest matches in the emirate, and the honest options are an online specialist or a compromise. We think the compromise costs more in the end, which is why we removed the distance filter rather than the standard.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-festival.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, the description names the thing a specialist knows and a generalist usually does not. Use them as test questions. If a prospective tutor cannot talk fluently about the item named, they may still be a good teacher, but they are not yet an IB specialist in that subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask what Paper 3 is and how long it runs at HL. A specialist will tell you it is an extended problem-solving paper unique to Higher Level, and will know that Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where calculator-dependent students collapse.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask where AI students lose marks. The specialist answer is interpretation rather than computation: a regression correctly calculated and then described in words that say nothing about the context earns the calculation marks and loses the rest.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask what the data booklet contains and when it is provided. A specialist will add that most students under-use it, and will name organic mechanisms and energetics as the two topics where Dubai Diploma students most reliably stall.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask how uncertainty is treated in the scientific investigation. Thin uncertainty analysis is the single commonest weakness in Physics internal assessment reports, and a tutor who has read real ones will say so without prompting.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask why Biology answers lose marks when the student understood the content. The answer is imprecision: a response that does not name the structure, the process and the consequence scores nothing, however sound the underlying grasp.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what the individual oral requires. A specialist names the global issue and the two extracts, and knows that leaving the global issue unstated is the commonest avoidable loss in the whole component.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask what the internal assessment actually is. It is a portfolio of commentaries on published articles, and the commonest failure is a diagram drawn correctly and then never referred to in the analysis beneath it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask what the HL extension questions reward. Application to the stimulus organisation, not description of a tool. Students who have memorised frameworks and never applied one to an unfamiliar company lose marks in a predictable place.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Ask where the marks sit in the internally assessed solution. In the documentation, not the code. A working program with a thin design record scores badly, which surprises strong programmers every year.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Ask what TOK is assessed on. The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, with the essay externally marked. A tutor who treats TOK as general discussion rather than as an assessed component is not going to help in the weeks that matter.

regions.note: The community closest to Deira International School and the one with the best local supply in the cluster, because proximity to an IB continuum school attracts tutors who know it. Supply is strongest at Primary and Middle Years and thins sharply at Higher Level sciences.

regions.note: Apartment living with a transient tenancy pattern, which affects tutor continuity more than availability. Families here report losing a tutor mid-year to relocation more often than elsewhere in the cluster, so continuity is worth asking about explicitly.

regions.note: Villas with limited walkable provision, so local tutors tend to be people who already travel for work. That makes them more willing to drive and less likely to be free in the earliest afternoon window, which is the one most useful to a Diploma student.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: The deepest local tutor market in the eastern suburbs, helped by an IB continuum school of its own. Middle Years coverage is good. Diploma Higher Level coverage is the same thin layer found everywhere else in the emirate, which is the pattern worth internalising.

regions.note: Low-density villa areas where any visiting tutor is making a long trip. Local supply is sparse at every level, and families here are the quickest to conclude that an online specialist is simply the better answer rather than the fallback.

regions.note: Established housing with a mix of curricula, so local tutors here are more often British or Indian curriculum specialists than IB ones. A tutor who teaches IGCSE Chemistry well is not thereby a Chemistry HL tutor, and the distinction is frequently blurred.

regions.note: Denser and younger, with a large British-curriculum school and nearby university campuses. Undergraduate tutors are available and inexpensive, which suits homework support and does not suit Higher Level Diploma teaching.
