sections.heading: The arithmetic of a local IB tutor pool
paragraphs: Put numbers on the problem and it stops being a matter of opinion. Dubai had 227 private schools in 2024-25 serving 387,441 pupils across 17 curricula, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of that enrolment. Every other curriculum has a larger teaching workforce behind it, which means more people available to tutor it in the evenings. The Diploma teaching pool is small in absolute terms and it is spread across six subject groups and two levels.

Then divide by level. A school running the Diploma may have one or two teachers for Chemistry across both Higher and Standard Level, and those teachers are the most likely source of competent local tutors. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a comparable code of conduct, so a school's own teachers are not an open pool even where they are nearby.

Then apply the radius and the hour. A tutor must be willing to reach Al Badia or Al Khawaneej, free between roughly 4pm and 6pm when a Diploma student is both home and still capable, and teaching the exact subject at the exact level. The table below sets out how that filter cascade lands subject by subject. It is a description of the market rather than a complaint about it, and for several rows the honest conclusion is that a local tutor is a perfectly good answer.

sections.heading: Ten questions that separate a specialist from a confident generalist
paragraphs: Credentials in this market are mostly unverifiable, so stop asking about them and start asking about the syllabus. A teacher who has taught Diploma Chemistry answers these in sentences. Someone who has read a summary online answers in adjectives. You do not need subject knowledge yourself to hear the difference, which is the point of using questions with concrete answers.

Ask what the internal assessment in this subject is, and what the criteria are called. Ask how many papers there are at this level and what each is worth. Ask what Paper 3 is, if the subject has one. Ask which topic most students in this subject find hardest and why. Ask what the student is allowed to be given during the examination. Ask what the command terms evaluate and compare require that describe does not.

Then ask the five operational questions. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Will you be the person teaching every session, or could it be reassigned? What will you do with a draft internal assessment, exactly? What happens if my child's grade does not move? And what would make you tell me that you are not the right tutor for this student? The last one is the most informative question in the list, and almost nobody is asked it.

Two further habits make these questions work better. Ask them before the trial lesson rather than during it, so the answers are not softened by the tutor having already met your child and read the room. And write the answers down, because a week later every provider sounds similar in memory, and the difference between an answer with criterion letters in it and an answer without them is the only comparison that matters.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, and why letters matter more than enthusiasm
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment marked against lettered criteria by the school's own teacher, then moderated by the IB. The criteria are published in each subject guide, and they are the specification a student is actually being marked against. A tutor who has never read them can teach the content perfectly and still leave a student losing marks in a place neither of them is looking.

This is where the difference between a subject enthusiast and a Diploma specialist becomes concrete. Marks for an investigation do not come from having the right result. They come from a defined research question, a justified method, data handled with appropriate treatment of uncertainty, and an evaluation that engages with the limitations honestly. A student with an elegant experiment and a two-line evaluation loses a band in the criterion that carries it, every time.

The useful consequence for a Dubai Festival City parent is that you can ask to see the criteria. Not a copy from us; we do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson documents, because that is not ours to distribute. Your child's subject teacher has them and the school's IB coordinator can print them. Ask your tutor to work through the assessment with the school's own copy in front of both of them. A specialist will welcome that. Anyone who deflects it has told you something.

One caution about how this is sold. Several providers in this market advertise criteria familiarity in general terms and then teach content only, because content teaching is easier to deliver and harder for a parent to audit. The audit is straightforward: after three sessions, ask your child which criterion their last piece of work was weakest on. A student who can answer that has been taught the assessment. A student who cannot has been taught the subject.

sections.heading: Availability, honestly: what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No researched competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere on their pages, and several route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without saying where delivery happens. We would rather be dull about it. The after-school window on Gulf Standard Time is the busiest part of the week, and within it Chemistry HL, Physics HL and Mathematics AA HL fill first, because that is where demand and scarcity meet.

When your preferred hour and subject are both taken, you get one of three answers: the nearest available slot, a named wait, or an honest statement that we cannot cover this combination at present. What you will not get is a quiet substitution. A family who books Chemistry HL and receives a general science tutor finds out in week three, by which point the term has moved and the trust has gone.

There is one more disclosure worth making. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available for a niche subject, the tutor matched may be based elsewhere and teaching into Gulf Standard Time. That is normal for online delivery and it is not a secret; it is simply the mechanism that makes a specialist reachable from Al Khawaneej at all. What matters is that the hour suits your household and the person knows the paper.

Two practical responses to a wait. The first is to move the hour rather than the subject: a weekend morning or a 3.45pm slot often opens a match that a 5pm slot cannot. The second is to start with a component block rather than a weekly booking, because a four-session run on one assessed component is easier to place in a full diary than a recurring slot held for two terms.

sections.heading: Verifying the person: permit, identity and continuity
paragraphs: Three checks cover most of the risk. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae records that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published anywhere official.

The second is identity and continuity. Ask who will teach each session and whether it can be reassigned. Ask what happens if that person leaves. Transient tenancy in apartment communities like Festival Boulevard makes mid-year loss of a local tutor a real pattern rather than a rare event, and a handover in February costs a student more than a slightly weaker tutor in September would have.

The third is claims. Treat any self-asserted star rating with suspicion: competitors in this market publish review counts that contradict each other on the same page, and one shows a rating in its markup that differs from the figure visible to a reader. Treat examiner labelling the same way. We do not describe any tutor as a current IB or Cambridge examiner unless the status can be evidenced, because it is the cheapest unverifiable credential available and it is used constantly.

A fourth check costs nothing and catches a surprising amount. Ask for the tutor's own account of a student they could not help and why. Someone who has taught for years has that story and tells it without defensiveness. Someone who has not will either invent one or insist it has never happened, and both answers tell you how much of what you are hearing is experience and how much is a sales script.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the emirates
paragraphs: Parents moving within the UAE are often surprised that the regulator changes with the emirate. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The powers are not identical. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

Knowing the map is a defence against a specific marketing move. A provider that calls itself KHDA approved is not paying itself a loose compliment; it is invoking a KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, where initial approval comes first and renewal must be requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not claim one. Nor do we claim approval from ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because we hold none of them. You should ask every provider the same question and compare the answers.

sections.heading: The boundary around assessed work, stated plainly
paragraphs: A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion, press on a research question until it is answerable, model a comparable example on a different topic, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or any other assessed work. There is no premium version of this service and no discreet version of it either.

The reason is the consequence. Internal assessment is marked by the school's teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB, and the student declares the work as their own. Work that is not theirs is malpractice, and the outcome falls on the student rather than on whoever was paid. One site competing for these queries sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750. That is not a shortcut with a price; it is a finding with a price.

Practically, this changes how to buy coursework support. The hours worth paying for sit at the start, when a research question is still cheap to fix, and at the point of a complete first draft. The hours in between are usually someone watching a student type. Ask any provider to put in writing what they will and will not do with assessed work before money moves, and keep the reply. A provider unwilling to write it down has answered the question.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Festival City, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Send three things: the subject, the level, and the component that is going wrong. We match a tutor to that exact combination and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost. Ask the questions from the middle of this page during or before it. Afterwards you receive a short written note of where the marks are going, by topic and component, and a recommended number of hours.

The limits are stated rather than buried. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, has no office, centre or branch in the country, and does not claim one. We hold no regulator or board approval and do not imply any. We publish no IB examination or results dates, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a tutoring page is worse than silence; your child's IB coordinator holds the real calendar. And when a specialist is not available at your hour, we say so.

What is left is the thing you were actually searching for: somebody who knows the paper. The distance filter was never what you wanted, it was just the only filter a local search gives you. Remove it and the remaining question is whether this particular tutor can talk about your child's syllabus in specifics. That question has an answer, it costs nothing to test, and you should test it on us before you test it on anyone else.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor near me in Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: For Primary and Middle Years, very likely, and proximity is a reasonable filter at those levels. For Chemistry HL, Physics HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL, probably not within a workable radius of Al Badia or Nad Al Hamar. The International Baccalaureate was 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, so the Diploma teaching pool is small, and dividing it by subject, by level and by who is free at 4.30pm leaves very few people. Online matching removes only the distance filter.

faqs.question: What questions should I ask to test whether a tutor really knows the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Ask what the internal assessment in that subject is and what it is worth. Ask what the criteria are called and what each one assesses. Ask how many papers there are at this level and whether there is a Paper 3. Ask what the student is given in the examination. A specialist answers in sentences with specifics; someone working from a summary answers in adjectives. Then ask the operational question almost nobody asks: what would make you tell me you are not the right tutor for this student?

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Al Badia or Al Khawaneej?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Dubai Festival City families are delivered as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason this is an advantage rather than a limitation is the filter arithmetic: a visiting tutor must match subject, level and driving distance simultaneously, and it is the third filter that makes Higher Level science matches fail across eastern Dubai.

faqs.question: Could we just pay a teacher at our Dubai Festival City school for extra lessons?
faqs.answer: It should not be offered to you. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also restricts serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK position as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document. Either way, a provider marketing your child's own teacher privately is marketing a conflict.

faqs.question: How can I check whether a tutor is legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The u.ae guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years and lists eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it costs nothing, there is no reasonable excuse for not holding it. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma specialist know that a good general tutor does not?
faqs.answer: The assessment machinery. A general tutor can teach the chemistry; a specialist knows that the internal assessment is marked against lettered criteria by the school's teacher and moderated by the IB, that the data booklet is provided and under-used, and that evaluation and uncertainty treatment are where marks quietly disappear. That knowledge changes what a session does. Content teaching helps a student understand; assessment knowledge helps a student convert understanding into marks, which is a separate skill.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work as well as having someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For Diploma work it usually works better, because a shared screen beats a shared notebook. Both people see the same working at the same size, a past-paper question can be annotated live, and the published criteria can be open beside the student's own draft. What a video lesson needs is a quiet room, a charged device and occasional parental attention. What it removes is travel, late arrivals, and a radius limit on who is allowed to be your child's tutor.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find anyone for in eastern Dubai?
faqs.answer: Chemistry Higher Level first, then Physics Higher Level, then Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, with Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay process coaching close behind. The reason is the same in each case: a small Diploma teaching workforce, split by level, further reduced by who is free in the late-afternoon window. For Business Management, Economics, humanities and languages, local supply around Mirdif and Al Badia is noticeably better and worth trying.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find a specialist for our subject and hour?
faqs.answer: You get one of three answers: the nearest available slot, a named wait, or an honest statement that we cannot cover the combination at present. Higher Level sciences and Mathematics AA HL fill first in the after-school window on Gulf Standard Time. What you will not get is a quiet substitution with a generalist, which a family typically discovers in week three. None of the competitors researched in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere on their pages.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by KHDA or by the IB itself?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should tell you otherwise. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, requiring initial approval first and renewal at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, holds no IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, and occupies no UAE office, centre or branch. What we do is explain what each regulator governs so you can check any provider's claims against the authority rather than against its own marketing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with their Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: With teaching and feedback, yes. A tutor can explain each criterion, press on a research question until it is answerable, model a comparable example on an unrelated topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing. A tutor cannot write, draft, complete or supply any part of it. The work is declared as the student's own and moderated by the IB, so the consequence of anything else lands on your child rather than on the tutor.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Dubai Festival City family be matched to a tutor?
faqs.answer: For subjects with reasonable supply, usually within a few days, because the constraint is finding a mutually workable hour rather than finding a person. For Chemistry HL, Physics HL or Mathematics AA HL in the busiest after-school window, it can take longer and we will give you a named wait rather than a vague reassurance. If speed matters more than the exact hour, say so, because a weekend or earlier-afternoon slot usually opens the match immediately.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB exam dates for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified date that a parent plans around would be worse than publishing nothing. UAE schools sit the May examinations; your child's IB coordinator holds the actual windows and internal deadlines. For Cambridge and Pearson, sourced dates do exist, and those are the ones you will find elsewhere on this site.

faqs.question: Should I be suspicious of tutoring sites that show star ratings?
faqs.answer: Of self-asserted ones, yes. Competitors in this market publish review figures that contradict each other on the same page, and at least one shows a rating in its structured data that differs from the number a reader can see. Self-serving review markup is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. Ask where a rating comes from, how many reviews, over what period, and whether individual reviews are visible and dated.

faqs.question: What should the first month of tutoring actually produce?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them a grade. Your child should be able to say which paper and which component they are being prepared for. You should hold a written list of the topics costing marks. And one aspect of how an answer is structured should visibly improve, because technique moves faster than content. Grade movement takes longer and nobody can promise it. A provider that opens with a predicted grade instead of a diagnosis has shown you how it operates.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-festival.closingHeading: Stop searching for nearby and start testing for specific
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-festival.closingBody: Proximity was never the thing you wanted; it was the only filter a local search offered you. What you wanted was someone who can say what the internal assessment is called, what each criterion assesses and where this particular paper eats marks. That is testable, and testing it costs nothing: a free trial lesson with a tutor matched to your child's exact subject and level, delivered as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. Bring the questions from this page. Use them on us first, then on everyone else you are considering, and compare the specifics rather than the enthusiasm.

intro.heading: Distance is not the scarce thing; usable weeks are
paragraphs: A proximity search answers a question nobody in the Diploma actually has. The binding constraint on a DP student is not how far a tutor lives but how many usable weeks remain before the next fixed date, and which of those weeks the school has already claimed. Internal assessment deadlines, staged Extended Essay submissions, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, CAS checkpoints and the mock window all sit ahead of the external papers and all are set locally. A family who starts planning from the examination month has started from the one date nobody can influence.

Those local dates differ between schools in this cluster, which is why no generic Diploma timetable is useful. Two students in neighbouring Dubai Harbour towers can have internal assessment deadlines a month apart and Extended Essay drafts due in different terms. The first request to make of a school is therefore not advice but a list: every internal deadline for the year, in writing, plus the mock window and the reporting dates. With that list a plan can be sequenced. Without it, every session is scheduled against an impression.

This page publishes no IB examination or results date. None could be confirmed from the IB directly for this project, and a date a parent plans around is the worst possible thing to get wrong. UAE schools sit the May session; your Diploma coordinator holds the real calendar and should be the only source you act on. What can be stated reliably is the sequence, the relative timing, and the published ceilings on each component, and those are what the tables below set out.

Dubai Harbour adds its own arithmetic. The district is new, built around a cruise terminal and marina berths, approached through a single corridor off King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street that it shares with Emaar Beachfront and the Palm Jumeirah approach. There is no school and no tuition centre inside it. Children travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, leaving before 07:00 and returning after 15:30, so a weekday session realistically starts at 17:00 or later. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows sets out the two-year core calendar with who owns each milestone, the word and page ceilings across components, the honest arithmetic of a term once Ramadan and school trips are counted, what the mock script tells you that a grade cannot, and how a plan should name the work it will not do. Confirm every date and weighting with your school before building on it, because the IB revises subject guides and your school sets its own internal calendar.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-harbour.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects this district asks for most, described by the component that carries a deadline rather than by their content, because that is what determines when work has to happen.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher, plus the exploration. The exploration has an internal deadline usually falling in DP1 or early DP2, and its question has to be settled eight to ten weeks before any draft is due.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology assumed throughout, with the same exploration component and the same internal deadline. Explorations here are usually data-led, which adds a collection step that has to be planned rather than improvised.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A data-based and multiple-choice paper, an extended-response paper and a scientific investigation. The investigation's internal deadline is the earliest hard date in the subject and the one most often met with a design chosen too late.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across two years, with organic mechanisms arriving in the second. The scientific investigation carries roughly a fifth of the grade and its deadline typically falls while the heaviest content is being taught.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Wide content and a scientific investigation on the same criteria as the other sciences. Command-term discipline is the largest recoverable loss, and it is best repaired in the first term rather than after a mock has set the student's expectations.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published news articles, each within a tight word limit, plus diagram-led extended response. The commentaries have staged internal deadlines and are frequently left until all three are due at once.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A case-study examination plus a research project at Higher Level built on one real organisation. Access to that organisation has to be secured before the question is fixed, which makes it a scheduling problem as much as an analytical one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral and an additional essay at Higher Level. The Individual Oral has a school-set date and is the most coachable component in the Diploma because the student chooses the material.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects against a prescribed prompt and an essay on a prescribed title with a 1,600-word ceiling. Both have school-set submission dates and both feed the bonus points alongside the Extended Essay.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece with staged internal deadlines and criteria weighted towards critical thinking. Scope is decided in the first two sessions of the project, and after the first draft it cannot be changed.

subjects.name: CAS
subjects.description: Not graded but required for the Diploma, with reflection checkpoints and a project the school monitors. Students who leave CAS evidence until the final term create a deadline collision with the components that are graded.

sections.heading: The two-year core calendar, and who owns each date
paragraphs: The Diploma core is where the calendar bites hardest, because the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS all run alongside six subjects and none of them has an external date a family can look up. Every milestone is set by your school: the EE supervisor meetings and staged drafts, the TOK exhibition and essay submissions, the CAS reflection checkpoints and project review. Those dates are the spine of both years and they are frequently communicated once, in an assembly, and never written down anywhere a parent sees.

Ownership matters because it tells you who to ask. The EE coordinator owns the essay stages. The TOK teacher owns the exhibition and essay dates. Subject teachers own their own internal assessment deadlines. The CAS coordinator owns the reflection checkpoints. The year leader usually owns the mock window and the reporting dates. Five requests rather than one, and all five answerable in a sentence if asked directly and in writing.

With the full list in front of you, sequencing becomes a matter of arithmetic rather than judgement. Fixed deadlines outrank flexible revision. A deadline eight weeks away outranks one in six months. Two deadlines landing in the same fortnight means one of them has to be brought forward deliberately, which is a decision to take in week one rather than a crisis to have in week nine. This is the single most useful thing a family can do without buying anything, and the reason we ask for the list before proposing a tutor.

sections.heading: Word and page ceilings as design constraints
paragraphs: Every written Diploma component has a published ceiling and students treat them as targets to approach from below. That is the wrong model. In most cases material beyond the ceiling is simply not read, so the time spent producing it returns nothing, and in some cases the overrun itself is penalised. The useful way to think about a limit is as a design constraint that decides the scope of the question before any writing happens.

The Extended Essay allows 4,000 words. That is room for one narrow question investigated with a defensible method, and not room for a survey of a field. The Theory of Knowledge essay allows 1,600 words, which is room for one developed line of argument examined from two perspectives, and not room to address a prescribed title comprehensively. A mathematics exploration has a recommended page range rather than a word count. A science investigation has a ceiling set in the subject guide. Economics commentaries have tight individual limits.

This matters at the planning stage and almost nowhere else. A student who chooses a question that cannot be answered within the ceiling will produce either an overrun or a superficial treatment, and neither is recoverable later; the only fix is a narrower question, settled early. That is the single most valuable thing a tutor does on the Extended Essay, and it happens in the first two sessions or not at all. Confirm the current ceilings against your child's own subject guide, because the IB revises them.

sections.heading: How many weeks a term actually has
paragraphs: A plan written on the calendar's face is a plan written on a number that does not exist. Mid-term breaks, Model United Nations trips, sports fixtures, university open days, the school's own mock window and the Ramadan adjustment all take weeks out of a term, and they take them out of the middle rather than the ends. A family who believes they have twenty sessions before a deadline and actually has fourteen will plan for twenty, discover fourteen in week nine, and conclude that the tutoring underdelivered.

During Ramadan school hours shorten and the family day reorganises around iftar, which for a DP2 student can overlap the heaviest revision block of the two years. The pattern should be decided before it starts rather than improvised. A post-iftar evening session suits many students better than a 17:00 slot, and weekend mornings with reduced midweek frequency work for others. What fails is cancelling for the month and resuming in the final fortnight, because the content planned for those weeks has nowhere else to go.

The arithmetic changes the plan in a good way. Fourteen known sessions produce a different and better plan than twenty assumed ones: fewer topics covered properly, the lowest-value items dropped deliberately rather than abandoned by accident, and the coursework deadline protected ahead of the flexible revision. That is the first conversation to have, and it needs the school calendar in writing rather than a recollection of what was announced in September.

sections.heading: What a mock script tells you that a grade cannot
paragraphs: The mock window produces the single most useful document of the Diploma, and most families receive only a summary of it. A grade of 4 in a subject is a sum, and the same 4 can be produced by three different students needing three different things: one with two unsecured topics and good technique, one who understands the content and writes poor extended responses, and one whose internal assessment scored in the bottom band and dragged the papers down.

Ask the school to release the marked script. Many will, on request, because the whole point of a mock is diagnostic. With the script, lost marks sort into categories within minutes: content not known, command term misread, method not shown, arithmetic, and questions unattempted because of timing. The last of those is invisible in a percentage and is often the largest single item, and it is repaired with a pacing rule rather than with any teaching at all.

The sorting determines everything after it. A student losing twenty-six marks to technique and four to unknown content should spend a fortnight on technique and leave the content alone, which is the opposite of what usually gets bought. A student with a genuine content gap needs sessions on that content and will waste a fortnight on technique drills. Both plans look identical from the grade and completely different from the script, which is why our trial lesson opens with the script when the school releases it.

sections.heading: Sequencing a term you cannot finish
paragraphs: Most Diploma tutoring starts mid-year, which means every plan is a plan about what will not be done. Families find this uncomfortable and providers avoid saying it, with the result that a term's sessions spread thinly across everything and move nothing. The honest alternative is to rank the available work by marks per hour of effort and then draw a line, out loud, in the first session.

The ranking is usually stable. Fixed coursework deadlines come first, because they are dated and carry roughly a fifth of a subject grade. Technique habits come next, because they pay across every question in every paper and repair in weeks. One or two high-cost content gaps follow. Whole-paper timing work comes after that, once there is something worth timing. Low-cost content gaps and anything in a subject already secure come last, and in a short term they come not at all.

Writing the line down changes the term. The student knows what they are not doing and stops feeling behind on it. The tutor stops being pulled towards whatever was most recently difficult. And the review at the fortnight has a clear question: did the items above the line move? If they did not, the plan changes rather than extending, which is a conversation worth having in week three rather than week nine. We would rather lose a subject from a plan in week one than lose a term to covering everything lightly.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the deadline pressure that tests it
paragraphs: The weeks before a coursework deadline are when families are most tempted to cross a line they would never approach calmly, and this market is built to accommodate that. One page researched for this project sells completed internal assessments at a published price. A student who submits bought work risks the loss of the entire Diploma and the school is obliged to report it. The pressure is real and the consequence falls entirely on the student.

The permitted help is substantial and worth stating positively, because it covers nearly everything that genuinely moves a grade. A tutor may teach the content a piece depends on, explain what each lettered criterion requires and what separates the bands, help narrow a research question until it fits the ceiling, review a method and ask whether the data supports the conclusion, point out that a table has no uncertainties, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite or complete any part of the piece, supply paragraphs for insertion, select or process the data, or produce a worked version to adapt. Nor may any tutor supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those are referenced and linked to their official source. Our tutors work the first list, decline the second explicitly, and will say so to a student who asks rather than quietly obliging.

sections.heading: Getting the hour right in this district
paragraphs: Proximity decides one thing and it is worth taking seriously. Children in Dubai Harbour leave before 07:00 for schools in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah and return after 15:30, and the hour after that belongs to food and decompression rather than to calculus or an essay plan. A weekday session therefore starts at 17:00 at the earliest, and 17:30 where the school run is unreliable. Families consistently nominate 16:30 and then lose a third of the sessions, after which the conclusion drawn is that tutoring did not work.

Coursework sessions need different scheduling again. An internal assessment or Extended Essay session needs ninety uninterrupted minutes, which does not exist on a weekday evening in this district. Weekend mornings are the most productive slots we schedule here and they are where criterion-mapped work belongs. Splitting the week into one weekday subject slot and one weekend coursework slot is the arrangement that holds across a term for most Diploma students here.

The cruise terminal is the reason flexibility is worth more than precision. On call days the afternoon changes without much warning, and an arrangement that can shift by thirty minutes absorbs that while a fixed arrival time does not. This is the practical argument for the format rather than a claim about technology: a video slot moves, a journey across a single approach corridor either happens on time or eats the paid hour. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE, so this is the comparison that applies here.

sections.heading: Booking a specialist from Dubai Harbour
paragraphs: Send five things: the subjects and levels, the school, the full internal deadline list for the remainder of the year, the most recent marked work, and the hours that genuinely exist after the school run. The deadline list is the item most often omitted and the one that most changes our answer, because a plan that ignores a fixed date eight weeks out is not a plan but a wish.

We match one specialist per subject and level and propose slots in Gulf Standard Time, with coursework work placed at weekends. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, used to produce a written diagnosis and a sequenced plan rather than a sales conversation. If the match is wrong after the trial or in week two, we change the tutor; persisting with a poor match in a Diploma year is the most expensive decision available, because DP2 has no spare terms.

The limits, stated plainly. Higher Level sciences and Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the scarcest matches we make at popular spring evening hours, and when nobody suitable is free we say so and offer a weekend slot or a defined short block rather than substituting a near match. We cannot promise a grade and nobody who has read a mark scheme would. And the plan will name what it is not doing, because a term has a finite number of usable weeks and pretending otherwise wastes them.

process.title: Collect the deadline list from five people
process.description: Subject teachers for internal assessments, the EE coordinator for essay stages, the TOK teacher for the exhibition and essay, the CAS coordinator for reflection checkpoints, and the year leader for mocks and reporting. Five short requests, all answerable in a sentence, and together they are the spine of any plan.

process.title: Mark out the weeks that do not exist
process.description: Breaks, trips, fixtures, open days, the mock window and the Ramadan adjustment. A ten-week term is commonly eight usable weeks, and knowing which eight changes the plan for the better: fewer items, covered properly, with the lowest-value work dropped deliberately.

process.title: Ask for the marked mock script
process.description: Not the grade. The script sorts lost marks into content, command terms, method, arithmetic and unattempted questions, and those need opposite plans. Most schools release scripts on request because diagnosis is what a mock is for, and the request costs nothing.

process.title: Free trial, then a line drawn
process.description: One trial lesson per student, no card required, ending in a written diagnosis, a sequenced plan and an explicit statement of what will not be covered. You keep that document whether or not you continue, and it is useful to any tutor you engage instead.

process.title: Review at the fortnight against the line
process.description: The question is whether the items above the line moved, not whether sessions were attended. If they did not, the diagnosis or the format was wrong and the plan changes. Extending a plan that is not working is how eight usable weeks become four.

whyPoints.title: Sequenced from your school's dates
whyPoints.description: Every binding Diploma date except the papers is set locally and differs between schools in this cluster. We ask for the list first, because a plan built on the examination month alone is built on the only date nobody can influence.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates invented
whyPoints.description: This page carries no IB examination or results date, because none could be confirmed from the IB for this project. Your coordinator holds the calendar. A wrong date that a parent acts on is worse than an absent one.

whyPoints.title: Ceilings treated as design constraints
whyPoints.description: 4,000 words on the Extended Essay and 1,600 on the TOK essay decide the scope of the question, not the length of the writing. That decision happens in the first two sessions of a project or it does not happen at all.

whyPoints.title: The honest week count
whyPoints.description: We do the arithmetic on breaks, trips, mocks and Ramadan in the first session and plan on the weeks that remain. Fourteen known sessions produce a better plan than twenty assumed ones, and the difference shows in the spring.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from the script, not the grade
whyPoints.description: Lost marks sorted into content, command terms, method, arithmetic and timing. A technique deficit and a content gap produce the same grade and need opposite plans, and only the script distinguishes them.

whyPoints.title: A plan that says what it will not do
whyPoints.description: Ranking the work by marks per hour and drawing a line is the difference between a term that moves two grades and a term that touches six subjects lightly. We write the line down so the student stops carrying what was dropped.

faqs.question: Does an IB tutor for Dubai Harbour need to be local?
faqs.answer: Not for the lesson, and ours are not. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. What proximity genuinely affects is the hour a session can run, because children here leave before 07:00 and return after 15:30. What it does not affect is who can diagnose a Paper 2 script in your child's subject at their level, and for Higher Level subjects that pool is small before availability is even considered.

faqs.question: Which deadlines should I collect, and from whom?
faqs.answer: Five requests. Subject teachers for each internal assessment deadline, the Extended Essay coordinator for the staged submissions, the Theory of Knowledge teacher for the exhibition and essay dates, the CAS coordinator for reflection checkpoints, and the year leader for the mock window and reporting dates. Ask in writing and keep the list somewhere the family can see it. Those dates are the spine of both Diploma years and they differ between schools in this cluster.

faqs.question: How long can the Extended Essay be, and when is scope decided?
faqs.answer: The ceiling is 4,000 words and material beyond it is generally not read, so scope has to be settled at the research-question stage rather than during drafting. A question that cannot be answered within the ceiling produces either an overrun or a superficial treatment, and neither is recoverable once a draft exists. Narrowing the question until it is answerable with a defensible method is the most valuable thing a tutor does on an Extended Essay, and it happens in the first two sessions.

faqs.question: How many sessions will a term actually contain?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests. Once mid-term breaks, trips, fixtures, open days, the mock window and the Ramadan adjustment are marked out, a ten-week term is commonly eight usable weeks. We do that arithmetic in the first session because a plan built on twenty assumed sessions and delivered in fourteen reads as underperformance, while a plan built on fourteen named sessions produces a sharper set of priorities and a better result.

faqs.question: What should we do about sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Decide the pattern before it begins. School hours shorten and the family day reorganises around iftar, so a post-iftar evening session often works better than a 17:00 slot, and weekend mornings with reduced midweek frequency suit other families. What does not work is suspending for the month and resuming in the final fortnight, because the content planned for those weeks then has nowhere to go except the week before a deadline, which is where nothing new can be learned.

faqs.question: Why do you want the mock script rather than the grade?
faqs.answer: Because a grade is a sum and the script is the information. Three students can hold the same 4 for opposite reasons: unsecured topics with good technique, good content with poor extended responses, or a weak internal assessment dragging reasonable papers down. The script sorts lost marks into content, command terms, method, arithmetic and unattempted questions within minutes, and those categories need different tutors, different work and different session counts.

faqs.question: How do we decide what to drop from a plan?
faqs.answer: Rank the available work by marks per hour of effort and draw the line out loud in session one. Fixed coursework deadlines come first because they are dated and heavily weighted. Technique habits come next because they pay across every paper and repair in weeks. One or two high-cost content gaps follow, then whole-paper timing work. Low-cost gaps and subjects already secure come last, and in a short term they come not at all.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with TOK and the Extended Essay at once?
faqs.answer: They can be coached by the same person if that person works on argument rather than on subject content, because both reward a claim tested against evidence rather than described. In practice the two have separate school deadlines and are better given separate sessions, with the nearer deadline taking the slot. What a tutor may not do in either case is write or structure the piece as prose for submission; feedback is on the student's own draft.

faqs.question: Our child is in DP1. Is it too early to start?
faqs.answer: DP1 is the cheapest point in the two years and the least used. Command-term discipline, the habit of showing method, and the design stage of the first internal assessment are all addressable in the autumn of DP1 in a handful of sessions, and all three become expensive repairs in DP2 once a year of habit has formed. Families wait because the early reports look acceptable, which they usually do right up until the first mock.

faqs.question: What time should a Harbour family schedule a Diploma session?
faqs.answer: 17:00 at the earliest on a weekday and 17:30 if the school run from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh is unreliable, with coursework work placed on a weekend morning where ninety uninterrupted minutes exist. Be honest about the hour rather than optimistic: nominating 16:30 and losing a third of the sessions is the most common way a reasonable plan fails, and the failure then gets attributed to the tutoring rather than to the timetable.

faqs.question: Will you work to our school's internal deadlines or your own schedule?
faqs.answer: Your school's, because they are the only fixed dates in the year apart from the papers. Send the list at the start and the plan is sequenced against it, with coursework blocks counted backwards from each submission and revision filling the flexible weeks between. A provider who proposes a generic programme without asking for those dates is proposing a programme that will collide with at least one of them, usually in the fortnight when there is no room to move.

faqs.question: If nobody can teach Chemistry HL at 17:30, what are our options?
faqs.answer: We say so and set out the options rather than filling the slot. Higher Level sciences and Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the scarcest matches at popular spring evening hours, and the realistic alternatives are a weekend morning with the right specialist, a different subject started first while the scarce one waits, or a defined short block with someone whose weekly availability is limited. Discovering a coverage limit in week one costs nothing; discovering it in week eight costs a term.

faqs.question: Will you send us an archive of IB past papers to work from?
faqs.answer: No. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyrighted, and redistributing unreleased material creates an exposure for the student rather than for whoever hosts it. We reference and explain them in sessions and link the official source. Most schools release recent material on request, and the subject teacher is the right person to ask, since they also know which series are appropriate.

faqs.question: How quickly can sessions start from this district?
faqs.answer: For a widely taught Standard Level subject, usually within a few days, because the only variable is matching an hour. For a Higher Level specialist at a popular evening time it takes longer, and occasionally a particular subject and hour has nobody free that week. We would rather give you a date we can hold than a promise we cannot. The trial lesson is the first fixed point and the weekly slot is agreed immediately after it.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-harbour.closingHeading: Send the deadline list, not the postcode
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-harbour.closingBody: A proximity search answers a question about geography. The Diploma asks a question about weeks. Send the subjects and levels, the school, the full internal deadline list for the rest of the year, the most recent marked work, and the hours that genuinely exist after the run back to Dubai Harbour. We will match a specialist per subject, place coursework at weekends, and produce a plan sequenced against your school's own dates, including what it will not cover. One free trial lesson per student, no card required.

A DP1 student whose Extended Essay proposal is due in five weeks and a DP2 student eleven weeks from a mock need different people, different session lengths and different stopping points, and the calendar is what decides which.

intro.heading: The Diploma is decided in about six windows, not across two years
paragraphs: Parents reasonably assume the Diploma is a two-year accumulation, and in a learning sense it is. In an assessment sense it is not. The grade that reaches a university is produced in a small number of concentrated windows: the point where internal assessment drafts are due, the winter mock in the second year, the moment predicted grades are written, the examination session itself, and the enquiry window afterwards. Everything between those windows is preparation. Tutoring bought without knowing which window is next is tutoring aimed at an average rather than at a date.

That is why a search sorted by distance is the wrong tool. A tutor fifteen minutes from Maple who is free on Tuesdays is a convenient answer to a question nobody asked. The question that matters is whether somebody who has taught the exact course at the exact level is free in the weeks before the next marked thing. In Dubai Hills Estate, where the Al Khail campuses are minutes away and the resident population is large, the local pool is better than most. It still runs out at Higher Level in specific evening windows, every term.

The calendar is also where this market is most obviously empty. Searching the competitor pages for a session name, a registration deadline or a results date returns almost nothing: not one of the ranking pages in this cluster names a single one. That absence is strange, because reconstructing the calendar is usually what a parent is trying to do when they search. This page builds it out, with one deliberate restriction explained below, and then plans against it.

The restriction is about IB dates specifically. Exact IB examination and results dates for a given session are set by the IB and communicated through schools, and we will not print a date across thousands of pages that we have not read on ibo.org ourselves. So the Diploma calendar here is relative: counted in weeks and terms, anchored to the May session UAE schools sit, with the authoritative version in your child's school assessment schedule and with the Diploma coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates, for the IGCSE sibling in the same household, are published and are quoted with their sources further down.

What a family in Dubai Hills Estate gets from reading the rest of this page: a term-by-term map of what should already be finished, the three core components that collide in the first year, an explanation of how predicted grades are actually produced and the only window in which they can be influenced, an eight-week pre-mock plan written out week by week, what the market charges with a column on how to verify each claim yourself, and a plain account of how lessons are delivered and where our coverage stops.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-hills-es.programmesIntro: The Diploma is the destination, but the calendar pressure starts earlier and the right intervention differs by stage. These are the four stages Dubai Hills Estate families ask about, described by what their deadlines look like rather than by their philosophy.

programmes.name: The final Middle Years Programme year
programmes.description: The year the Personal Project is completed and the year subject and level choices for the Diploma are made. Both are deadline events and both arrive earlier than families expect. A student choosing three Higher Level subjects in MYP 5 is making a two-year commitment on the strength of criterion-marked evidence that does not translate directly into a 1 to 7 subject grade, which is why the choice is so often revisited in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai Hills Estate the MYP 5 decision is complicated by proximity: British campuses offering IGCSE and A Level sit minutes from IB continuum schools, so leaving the programme at 16 is a live option rather than a theoretical one. Families who treat it as a genuine fork, with evidence, make better choices than those who default to continuity.

programmes.name: Diploma year one
programmes.description: The year with no external examination and all the structural deadlines. Internal assessment proposals, the Extended Essay research question and supervision meetings, the TOK exhibition, and CAS commitments that are completion requirements rather than graded ones. DP1 is the year tutoring is most useful and least often bought, because nothing visible is at stake until the first report that looks wrong.
programmes.countryNote: The campuses around Dubai Hills Estate set their own DP1 internal deadlines, and the spread between two schools four minutes apart can be six weeks for the same component. A plan built from a generic IB timeline rather than from your school's own calendar will misfire, which is the mechanism behind almost every February emergency in this community.

programmes.name: Diploma year two
programmes.description: The year of the winter mock, predicted grades, final internal assessment submissions and the examination session. The useful tutoring sequence inverts here: content first in the autumn, paper discipline through the winter, and nothing new in the final fortnight. A student who starts tutoring after predicted grades are written has already missed the lever that most affects a university offer, which is worth knowing before booking.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Hills Estate households frequently run three school timetables at once, so the DP2 student is competing for an evening with siblings on different buses. Where two children attend different campuses, fitting two sessions into one weekday evening usually fails and a weekend morning is the realistic answer.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The three components that run alongside six subjects and compete with them for the same evenings. The TOK and Extended Essay combination contributes up to three points through the published matrix, and the Extended Essay carries a 4,000-word upper limit. CAS is a completion requirement rather than a graded one. Families routinely treat all three as administration while paying for extra subject hours, which is the wrong allocation for a student whose subject grades are stable.
programmes.countryNote: Extended Essay supervision is a school function with school-set meeting deadlines, and the useful tutoring work sits around it: testing whether a research question can produce an argument, teaching referencing discipline, and marking a draft against the published criteria. No tutor should write the Extended Essay or draft the TOK essay, and we decline those requests.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-hills-es.subjectsIntro: Requests from this corridor concentrate on Higher Level subjects in the second year and on the two mathematics routes at every stage. These are the courses we are asked for most from Dubai Hills Estate, with what the calendar does to each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The hardest single Higher Level course to staff locally, and the one whose exploration gets left latest because it carries no weekly homework. Calendar point: the exploration proposal deadline usually lands while the autumn content load is heaviest, so it has to be planned for in advance rather than absorbed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led and calculator-heavy, with the same exploration timing problem. The decision to take it instead of Analysis and Approaches has to be checked against the published entry requirements for the student's target courses, and that check belongs in the first year rather than the second.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is a fifth of the grade and depends on laboratory access, which makes its deadline the least movable in the Diploma. Research design has to be approved before data collection, so a late start here cannot be recovered by working harder in the spring.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes with the same investigation weighting and the same immovable laboratory dependency. Students who arrived with a strong IGCSE grade often stall in the first year because the algebra load rises faster than the physics, and the autumn is the window to catch that.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision rather than breadth decides most marks, and the investigation shares the same timing constraints as the other sciences. Biology students in a double science load face two investigation deadlines in the same weeks, which is a scheduling problem before it is an academic one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment commentaries require genuinely recent published articles and have a strict word limit, which makes them deadline-sensitive in a specific way: an article chosen too early can fall outside the permitted window by the time the commentary is written.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with marks for applying a tool to the specific organisation rather than describing it. The internal assessment needs primary or secondary research organised early, and students who leave the research until the writing stage lose marks they cannot recover.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to function as evidence for an argument rather than as a list. The internal assessment is an experimental replication with ethical constraints, so its planning stage is longer than students assume and its deadline is correspondingly less forgiving.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Individual oral, Paper 1 guided analysis and Paper 2 comparative essay, with the HL essay on top. The individual oral is the most under-rehearsed component in the Diploma and the one with a fixed school-set date, which makes it the clearest calendar win available.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three points through the published matrix, with a 4,000-word limit on the Extended Essay. Both have school-set internal deadlines that differ between campuses in this corridor, and both are routinely deprioritised in favour of subject hours that are worth less.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB tutor near me in Dubai Hills Estate is really asking
paragraphs: The literal answer first. A proximity search returns people sorted by distance from your address, which is a useful sort for a plumber and a misleading one for a Diploma subject. Distance correlates with nothing that appears on a mark scheme. What correlates is whether the person has taught the specific course at the specific level, and whether they are available in the weeks before the next thing that gets marked. In Dubai Hills Estate both of those are live constraints and neither is geographic.

The second answer is that the search is usually a proxy for something else. Parents type near me because they want reliability, a low chance of cancellation and someone who understands the school. Those are reasonable wants and only the third has anything to do with location, and even that is weaker than it looks: understanding a school means knowing its assessment calendar and its subject offer, which is a document rather than a postcode. We ask for that document in the first conversation precisely because it carries the information proximity is being used as a substitute for.

Dubai Hills Estate is the fairest test of the proximity argument available in Dubai. The Al Khail campuses are minutes away. The resident population is large, well educated and includes plenty of qualified teachers. If a local tutor market were going to supply Diploma specialists anywhere in the emirate, it would supply them here. In practice the requests that fall outside local availability in this corridor are the same ones that fall outside it in Arabian Ranches or Sobha Hartland: Higher Level mathematics, Higher Level sciences in early slots, several Group 2 languages and the less common Group 3 options.

So this page replaces distance with time. The rest of it is a calendar: the two Diploma years mapped term by term, the core components that collide in the first year, how predicted grades are produced, an eight-week pre-mock plan written out, what the market charges with a column on verifying each claim, and what happens after results. If you read nothing else, read the term map and then ask your child's school for its own assessment schedule.

sections.heading: The two Diploma years, term by term, and what should already be finished
paragraphs: This is the map families ask for and nobody in this market publishes. It is deliberately relative rather than dated: anchored to the May session UAE schools sit, counted in terms, with the authoritative dates sitting in your school's assessment calendar. The reason for that choice is simple and worth repeating. Exact IB examination and results dates are set by the IB and communicated through schools, and publishing an unverified date on thousands of pages would be publishing a guess at scale.

Read the right-hand column as a checklist rather than as advice. Most tutoring enquiries from this corridor arrive at a point where two or three items in that column are already overdue, and knowing which ones changes the plan entirely. A DP1 student in the spring term with no approved internal assessment research question is in a different situation from a DP1 student in the spring term whose research question is approved and whose data collection is scheduled, even though both will describe themselves as behind.

The item families most often discover late is the internal assessment research question approval, because it is a school process with a school deadline and it does not generate homework. A research question that cannot produce a usable range of data has to be replaced, and replacing it in the spring of the second year is a different exercise from replacing it in the autumn of the first. That single item is why the first question we ask a DP1 family is about their school calendar rather than about their grades.

The second most-missed item is the subject and level review at the end of the first year. Dropping a Higher Level subject to Standard Level is a decision with a last sensible moment, set by the school rather than by the IB, and it is taken best on two or three pieces of marked evidence rather than on one bad test. Families who have that conversation at the right time make it calmly. Families who have it in the second year make it under pressure, and often make it late.

sections.heading: The three core components that collide in the first year
paragraphs: Six subjects are what families plan for. The core is what breaks the plan, because Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS all run alongside the subjects and all have deadlines set by the school rather than by the subject teacher. Together the TOK and Extended Essay combination is worth up to three points through the published matrix, which is the difference between a 34 and a 37 and therefore between two quite different university conversations. CAS carries no points and is a completion requirement, which does not make it optional.

The Extended Essay is the component with the clearest specification and the vaguest timetable. It has a 4,000-word upper limit, a research question the student proposes, a supervisor inside the school and a set of supervision meetings with dates attached. What it does not have is weekly homework, which means it is invisible until it is late. The useful tutoring intervention is early and narrow: test whether the research question can actually generate an argument supportable in 4,000 words, and teach referencing properly before 4,000 words of it have been written the wrong way.

Theory of Knowledge has two assessed pieces, an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title, and students usually find the essay the harder of the two because it asks them to argue rather than to explain. Subject-strong students in the sciences are frequently weakest here, and they are also the students whose families are least likely to buy support for it, because it does not look like a subject. For a student whose six subject grades are already stable, the core is the better place to spend.

The boundary applies with particular force to the core, because these are the components where outsourcing is most often offered. A tutor may test a research question, teach argument structure, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, mark a draft against the published descriptors and teach referencing. No tutor should write the Extended Essay, draft the TOK essay or produce any part of them, and we decline those requests. The malpractice finding falls on the student, not on whoever helped.

sections.heading: Where predicted grades come from, and the only window to influence them
paragraphs: Predicted grades are written by subject teachers and sent to universities long before any real result exists, and they do a great deal of work in an application. Most teachers build them from the evidence in front of them, which in practice means the winter mock in the second year plus internal assessment performance plus the pattern of classwork. That has a direct consequence for timing that almost nobody acts on: a student who is going to be tutored at all is better tutored before the mock than after it, because the mock is the evidence the prediction rests on.

Families regularly arrive in March of the second year, having waited for the predicted grades to confirm a worry. The worry is confirmed and the lever is gone. That is not an argument against starting in March, because the real examination is still ahead and a grade can still move. It is an argument for understanding which outcome you are buying: March tutoring aims at the final result, autumn tutoring aims at the prediction and the result together. Those are different purchases at the same price.

The second thing worth knowing is that a prediction is a professional judgement rather than an arithmetic output, so the conversation with the school is legitimate and specific. Ask which evidence a prediction was built on, component by component. A student whose mock Paper 2 was weak and whose internal assessment is strong has a different case from one with the reverse pattern, and the school can see both. That conversation is more useful than any general appeal, and it is best had with marked evidence in hand.

What tutoring can honestly claim here is narrow. It can improve the evidence that exists before the prediction is written. It cannot change a prediction retrospectively and nobody should offer to. Tutoring is also not required for the award of the Diploma, for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and a page suggesting a regulatory or admissions process depends on buying hours is manufacturing urgency about something that does not work that way.

sections.heading: The eight weeks before a mock, planned week by week
paragraphs: Most tutoring sold as mock preparation is ordinary teaching compressed, which is the least effective version of it. A block built properly inverts the usual order: it starts with assessment, spends the middle on the specific units that cost marks, and ends with nothing but timed practice. The table below is the plan we actually use, written out so you can hold a tutor to it or run it yourself. The two features that make it work are both counter-intuitive: diagnosis before teaching, and a hard stop on new content.

Week one is a full paper under timing, marked against the published scheme question by question. This is non-negotiable because the mark total hides the shape of the loss. A student scoring 45% has not failed uniformly: they have usually failed in a pattern, with full marks on anything calculable and nothing on anything requiring explanation, or the reverse. Those two profiles need opposite interventions, and no school report shows which one you have because a report grade averages them away.

Weeks three to six are the only teaching weeks, and they are ordered by marks lost rather than by syllabus sequence. That ordering matters more than it sounds. Students and parents both prefer to start at the beginning of the course, which spends the most expensive weeks on content the student already has. A ranked list from the diagnostic sends those weeks to the two or three units carrying the loss, and the difference in outcome is large enough to be visible in a second full paper at week seven.

The hard stop on new content in week six is the part everyone argues about. The reasoning is that unfamiliar material introduced in the final fortnight competes for working memory with the retrieval the student needs on the day, and the marks available from consolidating are reliably higher than those available from one more topic. If the syllabus is genuinely incomplete at week six, that is a different problem and the plan should have been longer. Discovering it then is still better than discovering it in the examination hall.

sections.heading: After results: enquiries, retakes and the other session
paragraphs: The calendar does not end with the examination, and this is the part of it families know least. After results are issued there is a window in which a school can submit an enquiry upon results on a candidate's behalf, which some schools describe as a remark. It is a school-submitted process with a deadline set by the IB and communicated through the coordinator, it carries a fee in most cases, and it can move a mark in either direction. The decision is worth taking on evidence rather than on disappointment.

Retaking is a separate route and it has conditions. A candidate may sit a subject again in a later session, and the IB sets rules about how many sessions a candidate may use to be awarded the Diploma. Those rules are specific and they change, so the only safe source is the current IB documentation through your child's coordinator rather than any tutoring page including this one. What is worth saying is that a retake is a planned five-month project rather than a quick fix, and it works best when the original loss has been diagnosed from the actual component marks.

There is also the other session. UAE schools overwhelmingly sit the May session, but a November session exists and some candidates use it. Whether it is available to a particular student, and whether their school enters candidates for it at all, is a school-level question with a real answer. Families who discover in August that a retake route exists have usually lost two months of a short window, which is why this section sits inside a calendar page rather than at the end of a frequently asked questions list.

One note on what we will not do. We will not quote an IB results date, an enquiry deadline or a retake registration date on this page, because no IB session date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. The IB's own assessment pages and your child's coordinator hold those. Cambridge and Pearson, for the IGCSE sibling in the household, do publish theirs, and the only two series a UAE candidate can sit are June and November. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the November 2025 results before it reached students on 22 January 2026, which is a January verdict on an autumn paper. Cambridge entries for a June series close in the spring, several months before the first paper, and the exact date comes to you on the school's statement of entry rather than from a page like this one.

paragraphs: The most useful thing a cost section can give a parent is not a number but a method, because every number in this market is published by somebody with an interest in it. So the table below pairs each claim you are likely to encounter with how to verify it yourself before paying. The figures are real and attributed; the verification column is the part nobody else prints, and it is the reason this section is shaped differently from a rate card.

The headline bands, for reference. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above. One competitor's schema markup contradicts the price visible on its own page. Another publishes a discount table that contradicts itself. None of them cites a source for a single figure. Checking a quoted rate against a published source, and checking whether the hourly figure matches the monthly one, is therefore a genuinely discriminating test.
