sections.heading: Term dates, Ramadan and the weeks that vanish from a revision plan
paragraphs: Every eight-week plan assumes eight usable weeks and most calendars do not contain them. Start by subtracting the obvious: half-term, winter and spring breaks, and the week either side of each one, when nothing productive happens regardless of what the plan says. For a student in this corridor a notional autumn term of fourteen weeks usually contains ten that are genuinely usable, and a plan built on fourteen will be two units behind by December without anyone having done anything wrong.

Then subtract the timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates the required instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. Add CAS commitments, a sport and a sibling on a different bus, and the number of usable weekday evening slots in a Dubai Hills Estate household is typically one or two.

Ramadan changes the shape of the week rather than removing it. School days shorten, late-afternoon energy drops, and for many families the productive window moves after Iftar. A session that worked at 17:00 in January often works far better at 21:00 during Ramadan, and a student preparing for a spring session cannot afford to lose those weeks entirely. The practical advice is to agree the shift in advance as a standing arrangement rather than renegotiating it weekly, which is how the weeks actually get lost.

The flip side is that holiday weeks are the most productive block in the year and the most commonly wasted. A student with an internal assessment due in February gets more from four concentrated sessions in a winter break week than from eight spread across the following term. Online delivery also means the schedule follows a family that travels, which removes the usual pattern where tutoring stops in December and restarts in February two units behind.

sections.heading: How a lesson actually reaches Dubai Hills Estate
paragraphs: Plainly: IB Gram delivers tutoring to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every country page on this site says the same thing. The phrase in this page's address is what parents type, and it deserves an answer rather than a sidestep, so here it is in one sentence: if you want somebody physically present in Dubai Hills Estate, that market exists and the rates above tell you what it charges, and we are not in it.

The case for video delivery in this specific community is about supply rather than price. A proximity search narrows the Diploma specialist pool to whoever is both qualified and within a reasonable drive, and at Higher Level that pool is already small across the whole emirate. Removing the drive constraint means the binding constraint becomes the tutor's calendar instead, which is a much weaker constraint. A student gets the person who has taught their course rather than the nearest person who has taught something adjacent.

The operational argument is smaller but real. A tutor travelling across Dubai at 17:00 is travelling against the same traffic the school buses are stuck in, and in-home sessions in this corridor are lost to road conditions more often than families expect when they book. A video lesson begins when the student sits down. Across a twenty-four-session term that difference amounts to several whole sessions of recovered time, which is worth more than the hourly saving.

What video delivery genuinely requires is worth stating because it is where sessions fail. A stable connection, a device with a camera, and a way to show handwritten working: a document camera, or a phone on a stand pointing at the desk. Diploma marks live in the working rather than in the final answer, so a student who cannot show their page loses half the value of the session. That is a setup problem, it takes twenty minutes to solve properly, and it is worth doing in week one rather than tolerating for a term.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in the weeks when the line gets tested
paragraphs: Academic honesty is usually discussed as a principle and almost always breached as a deadline problem. Nobody sets out to buy an internal assessment in October. They buy one in February, three days before a submission, with a student in tears and a parent who has run out of options. So the useful place to put this section is inside a calendar page, next to the weeks when the pressure actually arrives, rather than as a clause at the end.

The boundary itself is not ambiguous. A tutor may teach content, test whether a research question can produce an argument, explain what a criterion descriptor rewards, mark a draft against the published descriptors and say which band it sits in and why, ask the questions that expose a conclusion going beyond the evidence, and teach referencing. All of that is substantial, and it transfers to the next piece of work. What a tutor may not do is write it. No tutor should write the Extended Essay, draft the TOK essay, complete the coursework or produce the internal assessment, and we decline those requests.

The asymmetry is the reason to decide this early. A malpractice finding falls on the student, not on the service that helped, and it can cost a Diploma for a document the student cannot defend in a conversation with a coordinator. There are providers in this market selling completed internal assessments outright with a price list attached. We do not compete with that and we are not quietly adjacent to it, and the way to tell the difference when you are shopping is to listen for the verb: review, question and mark is teaching; polish, finish, strengthen and complete is something else wearing a softer word.

There is also a copyright line in the same territory. IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the IB's property, as Cambridge and Pearson documents are theirs. We reference them, cite them and work from the student's own legitimately obtained copies through the school. We do not reproduce or distribute them, and any service offering a download pack of past papers is distributing material it does not own. Ask where a tutor's practice material comes from; the answer is informative.

process.title: Name the next marked thing
process.description: Not the subject, the date. A mock window, an internal assessment deadline, the moment predicted grades are written, or the session itself. That single piece of information decides whether the next eight weeks should be content, paper discipline or research design, and whether tutoring is the right spend at all right now.

process.description: The document, not a summary. Internal deadlines differ by up to six weeks between campuses minutes apart in this corridor, and a plan built from a generic IB timeline will misfire. This is the single most useful attachment a parent sends, and most families have never been asked for it.

process.description: Sixty minutes with the person who would teach the block, not a consultant. No card details are taken beforehand. The student brings a recent marked assessment and one question that has been bothering them, and the session ends with a specific observation about where marks are going.

process.title: A diagnostic paper, then a written plan
process.description: A full paper under timing in the first fortnight, marked against the published scheme question by question, and a ranked list of units by marks lost. The plan that follows orders weeks three to six by that ranking, stops new content two weeks before the target date, and arrives before the second paid session.

process.title: Fortnightly review against marked work
process.description: The plan is checked against evidence every two weeks rather than against how sessions felt. If the diagnosis was wrong, it changes. If the student has reached the point where further hours are better spent on a different subject or on the core, we say which and move them.

whyPoints.title: Booked against a date, not a term
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from the next thing that gets marked and from your school's own calendar. That is why the first document we ask for is an assessment schedule rather than a report card, and it is the difference between a sensible plan and a sensible plan aimed at the wrong eight weeks.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching, every time
whyPoints.description: A marked full paper in the first fortnight, scored against the published scheme question by question. A report grade averages content gaps, command-term errors, process slips and stamina problems into one number that hides which of the four you are paying to fix.

whyPoints.description: No IB session or results date appears on this page, because none has been confirmed from the IB itself for this project. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted with their sources. A page that prints an unsourced examination date is telling you how it handles facts generally.

whyPoints.description: Higher Level mathematics, Higher Level sciences in early slots and several Group 2 languages cannot always be covered in a specific weekday window. We say so first and offer a different slot, a weekend morning or a bounded block rather than filling the slot with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line set before the deadline
whyPoints.description: The internal assessment boundary is agreed in the first conversation, not renegotiated in February when a submission is three days away. Teaching, questioning and marking against published criteria, always. Drafting, completing or supplying text, never, and the request is declined rather than discussed.

faqs.question: Does hiring an IB tutor near me in Dubai Hills Estate actually help compared with hiring further away?
faqs.answer: Only marginally, and not for the reason people expect. A proximity sort returns people ranked by distance, which predicts nothing that appears on a mark scheme. What predicts a grade is whether the tutor has taught the exact course at the exact level and is free in the weeks before the next marked thing. Dubai Hills Estate has a better local pool than most Dubai communities because the Al Khail campuses are minutes away, and it still runs out at Higher Level in early evening slots every term. Ask what they have taught, not where they live.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years does tutoring give the most return?
faqs.answer: The autumn of the second year, by a clear margin, because it is the last point at which tutoring can improve both the predicted grade and the final result. Predictions are usually built on the winter mock, so work done before that mock affects the evidence the prediction rests on. The first year is the second-best window and the least used, because nothing external is at stake and families wait for a report that looks wrong. Starting in the spring of the second year still helps the final result; it has simply lost one of the two levers.

faqs.question: Why do internal assessment deadlines differ between schools a few minutes apart?
faqs.answer: Because they are school deadlines rather than IB ones. The IB sets a submission window; each campus sets its own internal draft and final dates inside it, built around its own staffing, mock timetable and reporting cycle. In the Al Khail corridor the spread between two schools four minutes apart can be six weeks for the same component. That is why any plan has to be built from your child's own school assessment calendar, and why a sibling at a different campus is on a different schedule even in the same subject.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school about how my child's predicted grades were decided?
faqs.answer: Ask which evidence each prediction was built on, component by component, rather than asking for the grade to be reconsidered in general terms. A prediction is a professional judgement assembled from the winter mock, internal assessment performance and classwork, so a student with a weak mock paper and a strong internal assessment has a specific case that a student with the reverse pattern does not. Bring the marked evidence to the conversation. A tutoring service cannot change a prediction and should not offer to; what it can do is improve the evidence before one is written.

faqs.question: How many usable weeks does an autumn term in Dubai actually contain?
faqs.answer: Around ten, out of a notional fourteen. Subtract half-term, the week either side of it, and the winter run-in where nothing lands regardless of the plan. Then subtract timetable load: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools, with KHDA calculating required instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. Add CAS, a sport and a sibling on a different bus, and most Dubai Hills Estate households have one or two genuinely usable weekday evening slots. A plan built on fourteen weeks runs two units behind by December.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay help rather than more subject hours?
faqs.answer: If the six subject grades are stable, usually yes, because the combination is worth up to three points through the published matrix and most families treat it as administration. Three points is the gap between two different university conversations. If a Higher Level subject is two bands below target, that subject comes first, because two points recovered from one subject matches the entire core at its maximum. Either way, support means teaching argument structure, research question framing and referencing on the student's own work, and never drafting any part of it.

faqs.question: What does an enquiry upon results involve after the Diploma session?
faqs.answer: It is a school-submitted request to have marking re-examined after results are issued, which some schools call a remark. The school initiates it on the candidate's behalf, the deadline is set by the IB and communicated through the coordinator, a fee usually applies, and a mark can move in either direction. The sensible basis for the decision is the component marks rather than the overall disappointment, because a near-miss concentrated in one component is a different case from one spread across a paper. Ask the coordinator for the component breakdown first.

faqs.question: Can my son retake one Diploma subject in a later session?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, and the specifics are set by current IB rules about how many sessions a candidate may use to be awarded the Diploma. Those rules are revised, so the only safe source is the current IB documentation through your child's coordinator rather than any tutoring page. Practically, a retake is a planned five-month project rather than a quick repair, and it works far better when the original loss has been diagnosed from the actual component marks. Families who only discover the route exists in August have usually already lost two months of a short window.

faqs.question: Should we book tutoring for all six Diploma subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Six subjects on a fixed budget is an allocation problem before a teaching one, and spreading hours evenly is how a year's tutoring budget disappears without a grade moving. Sit full papers in the two or three subjects that feel weakest, mark them against the published scheme, and rank them by how close they sit to a grade threshold and how much of the loss is recoverable in the weeks available. Concentrating on two subjects usually moves two grades; touching all six lightly usually moves none at the same cost.

faqs.question: What does a 45% mock paper actually tell us about what to fix?
faqs.answer: Very little on its own, which is why the mark total is the least useful part of a mock. A student at 45% has usually failed in a pattern rather than uniformly: full marks on anything calculable and nothing on anything requiring explanation, or correct explanations written for questions that asked them to deduce. Those two profiles need opposite interventions. Ask for the component breakdown and, better, have a full paper marked question by question against the published scheme. That is the document a plan should be built from.

faqs.question: Can lessons move after Iftar during Ramadan for a Dubai Hills Estate family?
faqs.answer: Yes, and agreeing it in advance as a standing arrangement works far better than renegotiating weekly. School days shorten during Ramadan and late-afternoon energy drops, so a slot that worked at 17:00 in January often works much better at 21:00. For a student preparing for a spring session those weeks cannot be written off. The failure mode is not the timing itself but the improvisation: families who leave it week to week lose most of the month to cancellations, while those who shift the standing slot keep the continuity.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to a house in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market here is real, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is included, so the option exists. If you hire into it, ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years and takes two working days.

faqs.question: What equipment does a Diploma student need for online lessons to be worth the money?
faqs.answer: A stable connection, a device with a camera, and a way to show handwritten working: a document camera, or a phone on a stand pointing at the desk. The third item is the one families skip and the one that decides whether the session works, because Diploma marks live in the working rather than in the final answer. A student who cannot show their page ends up reading answers aloud, which removes the tutor's ability to diagnose anything. It takes twenty minutes to set up properly and is worth doing in week one.

faqs.question: A deadline is three days away and my daughter is not finished. What can a tutor legitimately do?
faqs.answer: Teach, question and mark, which in three days means working out what is actually missing against the criterion descriptors and helping her prioritise what she can still do herself. What a tutor must not do is write, draft or complete any part of it, and we decline those requests however the deadline looks. The malpractice finding falls on the student, not on the service that helped, and it can cost a Diploma for a document she cannot defend. The honest version is a late submission conversation with the coordinator, which schools handle more often than families imagine.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Diploma tutor start, and what if the subject we need is not covered?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Standard Level subjects, usually within days. Higher Level mathematics, Higher Level sciences in early evening slots and several Group 2 languages can take longer, and in some weekday windows they cannot be covered with a genuine specialist at all. When that is the case we say so before you pay anything, and the alternatives are a different slot, a weekend morning, a short wait for a calendar to open, or a bounded clinic rather than weekly teaching. We will not put a generalist into a Higher Level slot and let you discover it in week four.

intro.heading: The map cannot tell you what the mark scheme wants
paragraphs: Dubai Internet City is a free zone in Al Sufouh with the Red Line Metro station that serves this whole strip, offices and innovation space, residential towers and no school. A Diploma student living here travels out to GEMS Wellington International School along the coast, to the Al Barsha cluster, or to the IB schools in Emirates Hills and the villa belt. A search for a tutor near that address ranks by distance and advertising, neither of which knows anything about Paper 3.

That is the gap this page is written to close. An IB Diploma student is carrying six subjects across six groups, each with a different assessment structure, a different Internal Assessment type and a different set of command terms that the mark scheme actually credits. A tutor who understands that structure is useful. A tutor who lives nearby and teaches the underlying subject well may still spend a term on the wrong thing, because the subject and the assessment are not the same object.

The clearest evidence is in how marks are lost. Students rarely fail because they do not know the material. They lose marks because they answered a describe question when evaluate was asked, because a correct conclusion arrived without the reasoning that earns the method marks, because the Internal Assessment question was unanswerable with the data available, or because a 4,000-word Extended Essay was written as an extended description. Those are assessment failures, and a tutor who has read the scheme can name them in one session.

The IB is also the thinnest curriculum in this city. KHDA's 2024-25 figures put 387,441 students across 227 private schools licensed for 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian schools 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate schools 7 per cent. Split that 7 per cent across three programmes, six subject groups and two levels, and the number of exactly matched specialists inside any radius of Al Sufouh is small enough to make proximity a poor filter.

What follows is therefore structural rather than motivational. The assessment shape of each subject group, the command terms that cross all of them, what a past-paper session should actually contain, the Internal Assessment types and their specific traps, and the two pieces of assessed writing in the core. It is the information a parent needs to tell a specialist from a generalist in one phone call.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm. A Diploma session is a shared past paper, a mark scheme open alongside it, and the student's own answer annotated line by line, all of which travel over a screen without loss.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-internet.programmesIntro: Internet City families ask about these three IB programmes and, frequently, about the British route their child's friends are taking. The assessment logic differs completely between them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade. The Diploma also has published conditions beyond a points total, covering low grades and the core, which your school's IB coordinator holds in its current form.
programmes.countryNote: UAE IB schools sit the May session, with November as the second sitting used mainly for retakes. Specific IB session and results dates are not published here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself; the coordinator at your child's school is the authority on them and on the current award conditions.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria out of eight, with the grade accumulating from tasks across the year rather than from papers. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project. A student here needs criterion literacy rather than past-paper technique, which is why a Diploma specialist is not automatically the right match for a younger sibling.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai IB schools run the MYP through all five years and others enter students for IGCSE at 16, so children in the same Internet City tower can be on different tracks. That matters when a family buys support for two children at once and assumes one tutor can serve both.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, organised by transdisciplinary themes rather than subjects, ending with the Grade 5 Exhibition. Reports describe approaches to learning rather than marks. Support at this stage is deliberately light: reading fluency, number sense and written expression, built so it feeds the inquiry rather than running a parallel curriculum.
programmes.countryNote: The nearest full IB continuum primaries to this strip are in Al Barsha South and Emirates Hills rather than in Al Sufouh, so primary families here already travel. Where the plan is to continue into the MYP, extended writing stamina matters more than curriculum coverage, because the criterion system arrives at MYP 1 and surprises most parents.

programmes.name: A Level as the alternative at 16
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, with no equivalent of the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge and no requirement to carry six subjects. Assessment is almost entirely by examination, which suits some students considerably better and is a legitimate choice rather than a lesser one.
programmes.countryNote: The decision between the two routes is usually made at the end of Year 11 or MYP 5 and is better made on assessment style than on prestige. A student who writes well and works steadily across many commitments tends to do better in the Diploma; a student who wants depth in three subjects tends to do better at A Level. Both are available within a short bus ride of this strip.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-internet.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects requested most from this strip, with what each component actually assesses and the specific trap in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, two at Standard, with HL Paper 3 given to extended problem-solving. The trap is reaching a correct answer by a route the examiner cannot see, which forfeits the method marks. The Exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics used.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a graphic display calculator throughout. The trap is reporting calculator output without interpreting it in context, which is precisely what the mark scheme is built to catch. Students who chose it as the lighter option meet demanding statistics at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 is extended response, and a data booklet is provided. The trap is an explanation answer that states a true fact and stops, where the scheme credits each link in the chain separately. The Internal Assessment is one investigation marked out of 24.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity, with Higher Level deepening energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. The trap is memorised reactions failing on an unfamiliar substrate, which Paper 2 supplies deliberately. Reasoning from electron movement generalises; reaction lists do not.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy content assessed through exact command terms. The trap is over-writing: a student who tells the examiner everything they know about a process scores below one who answers what was asked. Data-based questions are the cheapest marks and the least deliberately practised part of the course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries real weight and Higher Level adds quantitative work and a policy paper. The Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries on published articles, and the trap is summarising the article instead of applying a named concept and evaluating with it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a pre-released case for Paper 1 and an HL extension. The Internal Assessment is a research project on a real organisation, and the trap is choosing a company whose data cannot be obtained, which is usually discovered six weeks in.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis in Paper 1, a comparative essay in Paper 2, plus the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, the essay. The trap is narrating the text rather than analysing how meaning is constructed, which confident readers do most. Annotation discipline is the fix.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study recall tied to precise evaluation language, with an experimental Internal Assessment. The trap is accumulating studies without being able to deploy one against a command term. A small, well-rehearsed bank that answers several question types beats a long list that answers none.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source papers and essay papers, with an Internal Assessment that is a historical investigation. The trap is describing sources rather than using them as evidence for a claim, and writing narrative where the question asked for evaluation of a historiographical position.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title, both assessed. The trap is treating it as an opinion piece. The marks sit in handling knowledge claims and counterclaims with real examples, and in answering the prescribed title as worded rather than the topic it gestures at.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent research essay in a chosen subject with a supervisor at school. The trap is a question too broad to answer in the word limit, and a structure that describes rather than argues. A tutor may coach method, referencing and reflection and may write none of the essay.

sections.heading: What a proximity search cannot tell you about a Diploma subject
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in Dubai Internet City returns, in order, tuition centres inland in Al Barsha, agencies with local advertising, international marketplaces and a few independent tutors. The ordering reflects distance, advertising spend and review volume on map listings. None of those signals knows whether the person at the other end can tell you what Physics Paper 1 contains or how an Economics commentary is marked.

The information you need instead is short and factual. For each subject: how many papers, what each is weighted, how long each lasts, what is permitted in the room, which Internal Assessment type applies and out of how many marks. A tutor who has taught the subject repeatedly answers all six without pausing. One who has not answers in general terms about building foundations, which is an honest answer to a different question.

This matters more in the Diploma than almost anywhere, because the six subjects a student carries are assessed in six different ways. Mathematics rewards visible method. Physics rewards a chain of reasoning. Biology punishes over-writing. English rewards analysis of construction rather than content. Economics rewards diagram accuracy and applied evaluation. A single approach to revision applied across all six will succeed in two of them.

Once the subject and level are fixed, the tutor's address stops being interesting. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which puts a shared past paper and an open mark scheme on the screen and widens the pool from the handful of specialists within a drive of Al Sufouh to everyone teaching in this time zone.

sections.heading: Assessment structure by subject group
paragraphs: The Diploma organises subjects into groups, and each group has a characteristic assessment shape. Knowing the shape tells you what a term of support should be spent on, which is the single most useful planning fact a parent can hold.

Broadly: the sciences pair written papers with one investigation marked against published criteria. Mathematics pairs papers with the Exploration. The individuals and societies group pairs papers with a written assessment that is usually either a commentary set, a research project or a historical investigation. The language and literature group pairs papers with an oral component. Language acquisition pairs papers with oral and written assessment. The arts replace a written paper with portfolio and performance components.

The table below sets this out with the Internal Assessment type and what it is really testing. Exact weightings, durations and component names are set by the current subject guide and can change between versions, so confirm specifics with your child's school and the official documentation. The purpose here is to let you ask a prospective tutor a question with a right answer in it.

One structural point is worth drawing out. Because every subject has an internally assessed component with deadlines set by the school months before any examination, a DP2 student is almost always finishing coursework in the term when revision should be starting. That collision is a scheduling fact rather than a failing, and planning around it is more valuable than any individual lesson.

sections.heading: Command terms: the one trap that crosses every subject
paragraphs: If a student is losing marks in several subjects at once, command terms are the first thing to check and almost never the thing a family suspects. The Diploma uses a defined vocabulary of instructions, and each one specifies a different quantity and shape of answer. Students treat several of them as synonyms, and a paragraph of accurate material answering the wrong instruction scores very little.

The most expensive confusions are describe against explain, explain against evaluate, and state against justify. Describe asks what; explain asks why, with a mechanism; evaluate asks for a judgement with both sides present; justify asks for reasons supporting a stated position. A student who describes when asked to evaluate has not misunderstood the content, and will still lose most of the available marks.

This is cheap to fix and it transfers. Four to six sessions spent on command terms, practised on real past-paper questions with the student writing and the tutor marking against the scheme in front of them, improves answers in every subject the student takes rather than in the one being tutored. That makes it the best-value block in the Diploma, and almost nobody asks for it, because it does not look like subject teaching.

The table lists the terms that cost the most, with what each actually requires. The exact command-term list and its definitions sit in each subject guide, so check your child's subject for its own wording. The pattern, however, is consistent: the instruction tells you the shape, and the shape is worth marks independently of the content.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, group by group
paragraphs: Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra chapters, and treating it that way is how a DP1 student ends up in difficulty without anyone noticing until the first mock. In most groups Higher Level adds content and raises the depth of reasoning demanded across every component, which means the student needs a different kind of practice rather than more of the same.

In the sciences the additional content tends to arrive late in the course, often in the DP2 autumn when the Extended Essay and other Internal Assessments are live, and it is frequently half-learned as a result. Scheduling that content deliberately earlier is a planning decision that changes outcomes more than spring revision does. In mathematics, Higher Level adds a third paper devoted to extended problem-solving, which most students have practised least because there are fewer such questions about.

In the essay subjects the Higher Level demand is different again: a longer or additional written component, and a higher expectation of evaluation rather than exposition. A student who writes fluently and descriptively can do well at Standard Level and plateau at Higher Level for reasons that have nothing to do with effort or interest.

The practical point is about choosing and changing. Three Higher Levels plus the core is a genuinely heavy week, and a subject that consumes two evenings is being paid for by the other five. A move from Higher to Standard within the same subject is usually administratively simple early in DP1 and progressively harder after that. Check the intended university requirement first, because some programmes specify Higher Level, and requirements vary by institution, country and intake year.

sections.heading: What a past-paper session should actually contain
paragraphs: Most tutoring hours in this market are spent discussing content. A more productive hour has a specific shape, and it is worth insisting on because the difference is visible in marked work within a month.

The student attempts a question or section under time, before the session or at the start of it. The tutor then marks it in front of them, against the official scheme, out loud, saying which marks were awarded and which were not and why. The student rewrites one answer immediately, to the standard identified. The session ends with one line added to a running error log, naming the loss rather than the topic.

That structure does three things a discussion cannot. It produces evidence the parent can read. It teaches the student what the scheme credits, which is knowledge they can apply without the tutor present. And it builds an error log that becomes the revision document for the final term, written in the student's own losses rather than in a generic topic list.

What should not be in the session is the tutor solving problems while the student watches. It is comfortable, it feels productive, and it produces very little, because Diploma marks come from the student's own written output under time. A session in which the student writes nothing has taught them something about the subject and nothing about the examination, and in DP2 only one of those is still available to be fixed.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment types and the trap in each
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component, and they are not variations on one task. A science investigation, a mathematics Exploration, an economics commentary set, a business research project, a historical investigation and an arts process portfolio test genuinely different things and fail in genuinely different ways.

What they share is the timing problem. School deadlines fall months before any examination, so coursework and revision compete, and a student with three Internal Assessments live in the same term will do all three adequately rather than one well. The second shared feature is that the biggest single determinant of the mark is the decision made in the first week: the research question, the topic, the organisation, the source set. After that, the ceiling is largely fixed.

The table names the trap in each, because they are specific and predictable. A tutor who can name the trap for your child's subject has supervised these before. A tutor who talks about coursework support in general has not, and the distinction matters most in the month when the work is due and least when it is being chosen, which is the opposite of when families go looking.

The honesty boundary applies to all of them identically. A tutor may teach method, narrow a question, explain the criteria, teach referencing and data handling, and read the student's own draft and say precisely where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, redraft or restructure any part of it, and may not supply a model to adapt. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; the risk in that transaction sits with the student, and the school supervisor remains the authority on process throughout.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay as assessed writing
paragraphs: The two pieces of assessed writing in the core are treated by most students as obligations rather than as assessments, which is why they so often cost points. Theory of Knowledge produces an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words of independent research in a chosen subject, supervised at school. Both are marked against published criteria and both contribute to the final award.

The Theory of Knowledge trap is treating the prescribed title as a topic rather than as a question with specific wording. Marks sit in handling knowledge claims and counterclaims with real, specific examples, and in answering the title as it is worded rather than the general area it gestures towards. Students write opinion essays with examples attached, which reads well and marks poorly.

The Extended Essay trap is scope. A question too broad cannot be answered in 4,000 words, so the essay becomes a description of a field rather than an argument about a question, and the criteria that reward focus and argument are the ones that suffer. Narrowing the question is the single highest-value hour available, and it has to happen in DP1 rather than in the DP2 autumn when the deadline is visible.

Both are coached, never written. A tutor may teach question framing, scope, research method, referencing, academic register and reflection, and may read the student's own draft and name where it fails against a criterion. A tutor may not write any part of it, may not restructure a draft on the student's behalf, may not supply a model to adapt and may not produce the reflections. Your school's coordinator and supervisor hold the current requirements and own the process; ask them about the award conditions that involve the core rather than taking a figure from a tutoring website.
bullets: Theory of Knowledge marks sit in knowledge claims and specific examples, not opinion

sections.heading: Points, awards and the questions to put to the coordinator
paragraphs: The Diploma is scored out of 45: six subjects at up to seven points each, plus points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination. Beyond the total, the award has published conditions covering how many low subject grades are permitted and what the core must achieve. Those conditions change between versions of the regulations, and your school's IB coordinator holds the current set.

We deliberately do not publish those thresholds. ibo.org blocks automated checking, which means no IB figure in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a wrong threshold is the kind of error a family acts on. If a tutoring website quotes you a precise award condition without citing the IB or your school, treat it the way you would treat a quoted examination date from the same source.

There are four questions worth putting to the coordinator in DP1, and they are more valuable than any tutoring purchase. What are the current award conditions, including the core requirement? What are the school's internal deadlines for every Internal Assessment and for the Extended Essay? Which session will the cohort sit, and what is the school's position on retakes? And, if a subject or level change is being considered, what is the deadline after which it is no longer possible?

Those four answers shape where support should go and when. They also tend to reveal the real problem: a student who is short of points is usually short because of one subject and the core rather than across the board, and knowing which makes the difference between buying one well-targeted term and buying four thin ones. Separately, if you need the Diploma recognised in the UAE, Ministry of Education equivalency is a process you complete with the authority, no IB points figure for it appears in the source we could read, and tutoring is neither required for it nor able to accelerate it.

faqs.question: What six questions should I ask to tell an IB specialist from a general tutor?
faqs.answer: How many papers does this subject have at my child's level? What is each one weighted? How long is each? What is permitted in the examination room? Which Internal Assessment type applies and out of how many marks? And which command terms cost your students the most? Someone who has taught the subject repeatedly answers all six without pausing. Someone who has not answers in general terms about foundations and confidence, which is an honest answer to a different question than the one you asked.

faqs.question: My child is losing marks in several subjects at once. What is the likely cause?
faqs.answer: Command terms, before anything else. The Diploma uses a defined vocabulary of instructions and each specifies a different shape of answer, so a student who describes when asked to evaluate loses most of the marks on a question they understood perfectly well. Because the problem is in how answers are written rather than in any one subject, it shows up everywhere simultaneously. Four to six sessions on command terms, practised on real questions and marked against the scheme, improves all six subjects.

faqs.question: What is the difference between explain and evaluate in an IB paper?
faqs.answer: Explain asks why something happens, with each causal link made explicit: this rises, so that falls, so the outcome changes. Evaluate asks for a judgement, with both sides present and a conclusion that commits to one. A student who explains when asked to evaluate produces accurate work and leaves the judgement marks on the table. The exact command-term definitions sit in each subject guide, so check your child's subject, but the structural difference is consistent across the Diploma.

faqs.question: What should a productive IB tutoring hour actually look like?
faqs.answer: The student attempts a question under time, the tutor marks it out loud against the official scheme saying which marks were and were not awarded, the student rewrites one answer immediately to the identified standard, and one line goes into a running error log naming the loss. That produces evidence you can read and skills the student can use alone. What should not happen is the tutor solving problems while the student watches, which feels productive and changes very little.

faqs.question: How does the Internal Assessment differ between IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Substantially. The sciences require one investigation marked out of 24; mathematics requires the Exploration; economics requires commentaries on published articles; business management requires a research project on a real organisation; history requires a historical investigation; the arts require a process portfolio. They test different things and fail differently, but they share one feature: the ceiling is largely set by the decision made in the first week, whether that is a research question, a topic, an article or an organisation.

faqs.question: When is the right moment to get help with an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: At the choice, not at the write-up. The biggest determinant of the mark is the first-week decision: a research question that produces usable data, a topic whose mathematics is within the level, an article that supports a named concept, an organisation whose data can actually be obtained. One session then preserves the full ceiling. Three to five sessions during the write-up can only polish what the early decision made possible, and families almost always buy at the second point.

faqs.question: May a tutor help with the Extended Essay without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary. A tutor may teach question framing, scope, research method, referencing, academic register and reflective writing, and may read the student's own draft and say precisely where it fails against a criterion. A tutor may not write any part of it, restructure a draft on the student's behalf, supply a model to adapt, or produce the reflections. The school supervisor remains the authority on process, and the most valuable legitimate help is narrowing the question in DP1.

faqs.question: Why do strong writers underperform in Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Because fluency is not what is being marked. The marks sit in handling knowledge claims and counterclaims with specific, real examples, and in answering the prescribed title exactly as worded rather than the general topic it gestures towards. Students write well-structured opinion essays with examples attached, which reads persuasively and scores below a plainer essay that genuinely engages the title. One session on reading the title precisely often changes the approach completely.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level just more content than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: No. It adds content and raises the depth of reasoning demanded across components, so the student needs a different kind of practice rather than more of it. In the sciences the extra material often arrives late in DP2 alongside coursework deadlines and is half-learned as a result. In mathematics it adds a third paper of extended problem-solving that students have practised least. In essay subjects it raises the expectation of evaluation over exposition, which fluent describers find hard.

faqs.question: Can my child change a subject or a level partway through the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Often yes early in DP1, and progressively harder afterwards, with a deadline after which it is no longer possible. Ask the coordinator for that date specifically, in DP1, because it is the most useful piece of information nobody volunteers. Also check the intended university requirement before changing, since some programmes specify Higher Level in a particular subject and requirements vary by institution, country and intake year, including at the Dubai campuses of overseas universities.

faqs.question: How many points does my child need, and what else does the award require?
faqs.answer: The Diploma is scored out of 45, with six subjects and points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination, and there are published conditions beyond the total covering low grades and the core. We do not publish those thresholds, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB figure in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Your school's coordinator holds the current set, and a website quoting precise conditions without a source should be treated carefully.

faqs.question: Which four questions should I put to the IB coordinator in DP1?
faqs.answer: What are the current award conditions, including the core requirement? What are the school's internal deadlines for every Internal Assessment and for the Extended Essay? Which session will the cohort sit, and what is the school's position on retakes? And what is the deadline after which a subject or level change is no longer possible? Those four answers shape where support should go and when, and they usually reveal that a points shortfall comes from one subject plus the core rather than from everywhere.

faqs.question: Does living in Internet City limit the IB tutors available to us?
faqs.answer: Only if you insist on someone travelling to you. There is no school inside the free zone, the nearest tuition centres are inland in Al Barsha, and the IB holds roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment split across three programmes and two levels, so the matched pool within any drive radius is small. Lessons here run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which widens the pool to everyone teaching in this time zone and removes distance from the decision.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at the same time?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, chosen from marked work rather than from feeling. A student carrying six subjects plus the core has limited spare hours, and tutoring in three or four consumes the independent study time where most of the improvement actually has to happen. If marks are falling across the board, the likely cause is command terms, organisation or Higher Level over-commitment, and each of those is addressed better by one well-chosen intervention than by more hours.

faqs.question: Does the Diploma get recognised in the UAE automatically?
faqs.answer: Recognition for local purposes goes through the Ministry of Education equivalency process, which is separate from university admissions and is completed with the authority rather than with a school or a tutoring provider. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus A Level or AS Level evidence. No IB points threshold appears in the source we could read, so verify any figure on moe.gov.ae.

intro.heading: The school run decides the plan, not the postcode
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park sits in the southern corridor, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2, mixing industrial and commercial plots with residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj, served by Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Emirates Road and its own Metro station on the line towards Expo City. A British-curriculum school and two IB schools sit inside the district, and a much wider cluster of schools in Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, Dubai South and The Sustainable City takes the rest of its children.

That spread is why a proximity search is the wrong tool here. The useful variable is not how far a tutor lives from your villa; it is how far your child travels to school and back, because that number sets the earliest hour any session can begin. A child at a school inside DIP can start at 5pm. A child bussed to Al Barsha or across to Jebel Ali in traffic may not be settled before six, and a Dubai South run can be longer still.

Families consistently underestimate this and then blame the tutoring. A block is agreed at 5pm because that is what was offered, two sessions in three start fifteen minutes late with a tired student, and by week four the family has concluded that online tuition does not work for them. The format was never the problem. The plan was built on a school day that does not exist.

So this page starts from the household week. It sets out which clusters DIP children actually feed into and what each does to the arrival time, how to build a weekly pattern that survives a long run, what the bus does to DP2 revision specifically, and how Ramadan and the Dubai working week change the shape of the whole thing. The Diploma content sections follow, because they matter, but they matter less than whether the session happens.

There is a second reason the arithmetic matters, and it is about what happens between sessions rather than during them. A forty-five minute return journey is about seven and a half hours a week, which is more than a full school day. Those are precisely the hours in which a Diploma student would otherwise be doing the independent practice that makes a tutoring session compound, so a long run does not merely delay the lesson; it removes the work that was supposed to follow it.

One premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one Diploma tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. The direct benefit for a long-commute household is that the session has no travel time of its own, so it can sit wherever the household's real day leaves a gap, including at 8pm or on a Saturday morning.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-investme.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects DIP families ask for. Each description names what the subject assesses and, where relevant, how much unbroken session time it realistically needs, which matters when the evening is short.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with Paper 3 at Higher Level worth 20 per cent. Needs an unbroken hour: a derivation interrupted halfway is worse than no derivation, which is why a late but protected slot beats an early contested one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator-led interpretation, with Paper 3 at Higher Level. Works reasonably in shorter sessions because the work divides into discrete tasks more easily than Analysis does.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment, graphs with units, and explanations that apply a named principle rather than describe a phenomenon. Data questions need a full hour; command term practice can be done in forty minutes.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the most Higher Level weight, with the internal investigation at 20 per cent. Mechanism work is the most tiring thing in the subject and belongs in the freshest slot available.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the grade more than recall does, and statistical treatment is the weak point in most Higher Level investigations. Divides well into shorter sessions, which suits a long-commute household.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, labelling and evaluation that reaches a judgement, plus three internally assessed commentaries on published articles with strict word limits. Commentary work suits a weekend session where there is room to read.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, a comparative essay and the Individual Oral linking a global issue to two texts. Needs reading done in advance, so it is the subject most affected when a long bus journey eats the evening.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under time pressure plus an internal assessment on a real organisation. Choosing a company the student cannot get usable evidence about is the standard planning error and is found far too late.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay, contributing to the three bonus points. Students who treat a prescribed title as a topic rather than an arguable claim lose marks invisibly.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece with required reflection sessions recorded with the supervisor. The work needs long, uninterrupted blocks, which in this corridor means weekends and holidays rather than weekday evenings.

sections.heading: What near me means when the school run is the real constraint
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in Dubai Investments Park search returns results ranked by distance from your address. IB Gram answers the underlying need differently: one-to-one Diploma teaching delivered into DIP homes as live online sessions on Gulf Standard Time, matched on subject and level. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, because in-person home visits are a service we run only in India.

Proximity is a sensible filter when the service is interchangeable and the constraint is the provider's travel. Here neither holds. Diploma teaching is not interchangeable, since a Higher Level Chemistry candidate and a Mathematics Analysis candidate need different people. And the binding travel constraint in this corridor is not the tutor's journey; it is your child's, twice a day, on roads that are busiest exactly when school ends.

That inverts the usual argument. In a dense central district, an in-home tutor arriving at 5pm is a mild convenience. In the southern corridor, an in-home tutor is a second vehicle trying to reach your address at the same time your child's bus is trying to leave theirs, and both are in the same traffic. The practical result is late starts, shortened sessions and a slot that cannot move when the bus is delayed.

An online session has no travel time of its own, which means it can be placed wherever the household's real day leaves a gap and moved when the day goes wrong. For a family whose child gets home at 6.15pm, that is the difference between a workable plan and a plan that looks fine on paper.

Read the last column as a floor rather than a target. The arrival time is when the child is home; the session start should sit twenty to thirty minutes later, because a student who walks in and sits straight down in front of a screen is present without being available. That margin is the single most common omission in tutoring plans here, and it is free to include.

Note how wide the range is. Two children living two streets apart in Green Community can have arrival times an hour apart because one attends a school inside DIP and the other travels to Jebel Ali or Dubai South. This is why advice passed between neighbours about what time tutoring works is so often wrong, and why the question has to be answered household by household.

Confirm your own numbers rather than taking these. Bus routes change each year, the school's published end time is not the same as the bus arrival time, and a sibling on a different route can shift the whole household pattern. One week of actually writing down what time your child walks in is worth more than any estimate on a page.

sections.heading: Building a week that survives a long run
paragraphs: Once the arrival time is known, the week can be designed rather than hoped for. The principle is to match the work to the energy available, which sounds obvious and is almost never done, because sessions are usually booked by what the provider has free rather than by what the student can use.

High-cognitive work belongs in the best slot the week offers. For a long-commute household that is rarely a weekday evening; it is Friday, Saturday or Sunday morning. Mechanism work in chemistry, a full Paper 3 attempt, an Extended Essay draft review and a complete mathematics derivation all belong there. Putting them at 7pm after a 50-minute bus journey wastes both the session and the student's willingness to try.

Weekday evenings are better used for narrow, high-value technique work that can be done in forty minutes and does not require a cold start: marking a script against scheme wording, drilling command terms, uncertainty arithmetic, or reviewing one question type. These are the things that move Diploma grades most per hour anyway, so the constraint is less costly than it first appears.

The table below sets out a shape. Adapt it to your own household and to your school's deadline calendar, which the IB coordinator holds. The point is not the specific arrangement; it is that the arrangement exists in writing before week one, because an unwritten plan drifts towards whatever feels urgent on the night.

One addition that costs nothing. Agree in advance what happens when the bus is late, because in this corridor it will be. A session that can start ten minutes late and run ten minutes short, by prior agreement, survives; a session that gets cancelled and rescheduled twice a month does not, and the consistency is most of the value in a weekly slot.

sections.heading: What the bus does to DP2 revision specifically
paragraphs: DP2 is the year in which the commute stops being an inconvenience and starts affecting outcomes, for a reason that is arithmetic rather than attitudinal. A DP2 student needs independent practice between tutoring sessions, because the practice is where the learning consolidates and the session is where it is diagnosed. A long return journey removes exactly the hours in which that practice would happen.

The visible symptom is a student who appears to understand everything in the session and performs no better in the next mock. Families read that as a tutoring failure and sometimes change tutors, which solves nothing. The actual problem is that nothing happened between the sessions, so each one started from a cold restart and the gains never compounded.

There are two realistic responses and neither is working longer. The first is to shift the independent practice into the journey itself where the subject allows: command term lists, formula recall, flashcards for biology terminology and definitions are all genuinely doable on a bus, while anything requiring written working is not. The second is to move the practice to the weekend and accept fewer, better-used weekday sessions.

The third option, which should be stated because families reach for it, is to add more sessions. In a long-commute household that usually makes things worse: more sessions with no practice in between produces a student who is coached rather than independent, and examinations are sat alone. Two sessions a week with real practice between them beats four without, every time.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and the shape of the Dubai week
paragraphs: No competitor page in this research set discusses this, and every UAE household plans around it. The academic year here has its own rhythm, and in a long-commute corridor the rhythm matters more because there is less slack in the day to absorb a change.

During Ramadan the school day shortens and household routines reorganise around Iftar. In practice sessions move to post-Iftar slots for the month, which is agreed with the tutor rather than imposed, and attention in those sessions is frequently better than in a late-afternoon slot during a fasting day. Families who try to keep the pre-Ramadan timetable unchanged usually lose a fortnight to cancellations, and in DP2 a lost fortnight often carries an internal assessment deadline.

Prayer times shape the weekday evening too, and a session booked without regard to them will be interrupted or moved every week until somebody raises it. It is far easier to set the slot around them at the start. The same applies to after-school activities, which in this corridor often involve further travel and should be treated as part of the commute rather than as separate commitments.

The weekend and the holidays are where a long-commute household recovers the time. The winter break in particular sits after internal assessment drafts should exist and before the mock window, which makes it the one period in DP2 when a student can work on a component with no competing deadline. Four sessions in that break typically mean arriving at mocks with the component fixed rather than still being diagnosed, and nothing is tied to a Dubai address, so the sessions continue if the family travels.

sections.heading: Diploma deadlines against the household week
paragraphs: The Diploma's decisive moments are mostly internal, set by the school rather than the IB, and they arrive in clusters. A household with a long run has less capacity to absorb a cluster, which means knowing when they fall is worth more here than in a district where the school is ten minutes away.

The sequence runs: subject and level choices at the end of Year 11, internal assessment topics through DP1, the first Extended Essay reflection, internal assessment drafts across the DP2 terms, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, the school's mock window, then the May session. Each has a point after which it can no longer be influenced, and each belongs on one family calendar rather than in three separate places.

The planning rule that holds in this corridor is to put anything requiring sustained work into a weekend or a holiday as soon as the deadline is known, rather than discovering in the final fortnight that it needed four uninterrupted hours nobody had. Internal assessment drafts and Extended Essay progress are the two that reliably cause this.

IB session and results dates are not independently verified in this project, because ibo.org blocks automated access. UAE schools sit the May session, and anything more specific should come from your child's IB coordinator. For siblings on the British curriculum the position is published: Cambridge runs June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May and June and November, with June 2026 results having reached centres on 19 August 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: What the travel actually costs, in hours and in AED
paragraphs: It is worth costing the commute properly, because families in this corridor make tutoring decisions without doing so and then wonder where the time went. A 45-minute return journey is roughly seven and a half hours a week, which is more than a full school day and considerably more than any tutoring block a family is likely to buy.

That arithmetic changes how the tutoring budget should be spent. Hours are scarcer than money for most households here, so the right purchase is the intervention with the highest value per hour rather than the most hours. Component diagnosis, mark-scheme technique and uncertainty work all move Diploma grades more per hour than general content revision, which means the constrained household should be buying precisely those.

The market, attributed and dated October 2026, so any quote can be judged. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour; IB and A Level specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table, and in this corridor that travel component is doing more work than it would centrally. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

For wider context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the variable line in an education budget, and in a time-poor household the discipline that matters most is a block with a stated end rather than the lowest hourly rate.

sections.heading: Coursework, coverage and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Two boundaries first, because they matter more than any scheduling advice. One operator researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is an academic honesty breach that can cost the entire Diploma, and the consequence falls on the student. IB Gram writes, completes, edits to completion and supplies nothing, at any price. A tutor teaches the criteria, interrogates a research question, reads the student's own draft and says which criterion it fails and why. The test after a session is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words.

We also do not publish, reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads, because that material is the boards' copyright and unreleased content carries a malpractice exposure. We cite the official source, link to it, and work from what your child's school legitimately provides.

On coverage, the honest position for this corridor. Mainstream Diploma subjects at both levels can usually be matched within a few days. Higher Level Physics is the hardest specialism to cover at a peak hour, with Higher Level Chemistry and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches close behind, and the constraint is sharpest in the weeks before the May session. Where we cannot cover a request you will be told, offered the nearest workable alternative and given a realistic date, rather than being given a generalist described as a specialist.

And the claims that will not be made. No grade promise, because nobody can honestly make one. No suggestion that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression, which would be a false claim about a regulatory process. No regulator or board approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch. No satisfaction statistics, because a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: Send five things: the subject, the level, the school, the last two marked pieces of work, and the time your child actually walks through the door on a normal weekday. That last item is not a formality in this corridor; it is the variable that decides whether the plan survives, and it is the one most providers never ask for.

The free trial lesson comes before any payment and is diagnostic in purpose. A specialist reading two marked pieces can usually name the failing component in a sentence, and the trial is also where the slot gets tested in practice rather than in theory. If the agreed time turns out to be fifteen minutes too early, that is worth discovering before a term is booked around it.

Then the plan gets written down: which slot, what goes in it, what goes at the weekend, and when it is reviewed. The review point should be a real school checkpoint such as a mock or an internal assessment deadline, not a date on a calendar, and if the component is fixed the recommendation will be to stop.

One last fact to carry into any conversation with any provider here. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is granted free of charge for two years, eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

process.title: Write down the real arrival time
process.description: Not the school's published end time, and not the bus timetable, but what time your child actually walks in on a normal weekday for a week. Everything else in the plan is built on this number, and it is the one most families estimate and most providers never ask about.

process.title: Add a margin before the session
process.description: Twenty to thirty minutes between arriving home and starting. A student who sits straight down after a long run is present without being available, and a session that starts tired is the commonest reason a family concludes that tutoring is not working.

process.title: Match the work to the slot
process.description: Narrow technique work in weekday evenings, sustained work such as coursework drafts, derivations and full papers at weekends and in holidays. This is not a compromise; the high-value-per-hour work happens to be the work that fits a short evening.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used twice over
process.description: It diagnoses the failing component and it tests the proposed slot in practice. If the time turns out to be slightly too early or the session too long for the evening, that is far better learnt before a term is booked around it.

process.title: Review at a school checkpoint
process.description: The block ends at a real event, such as a mock or an internal assessment deadline, rather than at an arbitrary date. If the component is fixed, stopping is the recommendation, which keeps a tutoring budget variable in a year when hours are scarce.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from your day, not our diary
whyPoints.description: In this corridor the arrival time is the binding constraint, and a session booked at a standard hour because that is what was free will fail quietly. Later and protected beats earlier and contested, and online delivery makes later possible.

whyPoints.title: No travel time competing with your child's
whyPoints.description: An in-home tutor is a second vehicle trying to reach your address in the same traffic your child's bus is sitting in. An online session has no journey of its own, so it can be placed where the household has a gap and moved when the day goes wrong.

whyPoints.title: Weekends and holidays treated as the main asset
whyPoints.description: The winter break sits between internal assessment drafts and mocks, summer carries the transition work, and weekend mornings are the only slot that reliably holds a full Paper 3 or an Extended Essay review. In a long-commute household these windows do most of the work.

whyPoints.title: The practice problem named honestly
whyPoints.description: A long return journey removes the independent practice hours that make sessions compound. The answer is fewer, better-used sessions with real practice between them, not more sessions, which produce a coached student rather than an independent one.

whyPoints.title: The UAE calendar built in
