faqs.question: Why does a near me search not solve our tutoring problem out here?
faqs.answer: Because the binding travel constraint in this corridor is your child's journey, not the tutor's. A proximity search optimises for the wrong vehicle. DIP children travel to schools inside the district, to Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, Dubai South or further north, so arrival home ranges from about 3.45pm to past 6pm. What decides whether tutoring works is whether the session sits after that, with a margin, and whether the subject specialist is the right one. Neither question is geographic.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our home in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: No. We deliver one-to-one Diploma tuition into DIP homes as live online sessions on Gulf Standard Time, and we send no tutors to any UAE address; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. In this corridor that is a practical advantage rather than a limitation: an in-home tutor would be driving towards your address in exactly the traffic your child's bus is sitting in, which produces late starts and a slot that cannot move.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start if our child is at school in Jebel Ali?
faqs.answer: Usually about 6pm. The return journey from Jebel Ali in afternoon traffic typically puts a secondary student home between 4.45pm and 5.30pm, and a session should start twenty to thirty minutes after arrival rather than immediately, because a student who sits straight down is present without being available. For a Dubai South run the floor moves to around 6.45pm. Write down your own arrival times for a week rather than estimating them.

faqs.question: Is a 7pm or 8pm session too late to be useful?
faqs.answer: Later and protected is better than earlier and contested, which is the opposite of what most families assume. A session that starts on time with a settled student beats two that start fifteen minutes late with a tired one. What matters is matching the work to the slot: narrow technique work, script marking and command term drills work well late, while a first encounter with a hard new topic or a full past paper does not and belongs at the weekend.

faqs.question: Our child understands everything in sessions but mocks do not improve. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because nothing is happening between sessions. Independent practice is where the learning consolidates and the session is where it is diagnosed, and a long return journey removes exactly the hours that practice would occupy. Each session then starts from a cold restart and the gains never compound. The fix is not more sessions, which produces a coached student; it is moving the practice to the weekend and using weekday sessions for narrow, high-value work.

faqs.question: We can only protect one long slot a week. What belongs in it?
faqs.answer: Anything that does not survive interruption. A full Paper 3 attempt at Higher Level, an internal assessment draft review, a complete mathematics derivation, Extended Essay progress and Theory of Knowledge essay planning all need unbroken time and a fresh student. In a long-commute household the weekend morning is the best slot the week offers, and spending it on routine homework supervision is the most common way families waste their strongest hour.

faqs.question: Can work be done on the school bus?
faqs.answer: Some of it, and it is worth knowing which. Recall work travels well: command term lists, formula recall, biology terminology, definitions and vocabulary. Anything requiring written working, sustained reasoning or a calculator does not, and attempting it produces frustration rather than progress. For a student losing seven or more hours a week to the journey, shifting the recall component into it genuinely frees weekend time for the work that needs a desk.

faqs.question: How do we handle Ramadan without losing a fortnight?
faqs.answer: Move the slot rather than keeping it. The school day shortens and the household reorganises around Iftar, so sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar timing for the month, agreed with the tutor rather than imposed. Attention in those sessions is often better than in a late-afternoon slot during a fasting day. Families who leave the pre-Ramadan timetable unchanged tend to lose two weeks to cancellations, and in DP2 that fortnight usually carries an internal assessment deadline.

faqs.question: Should the slot be set around prayer times?
faqs.answer: Yes, and at the start rather than after three clashes. A session booked without regard to prayer times gets interrupted or rescheduled every week until somebody raises it, which erodes the consistency that makes a weekly slot valuable. The same applies to after-school activities, which in this corridor frequently involve further travel and should be treated as part of the commute rather than as separate commitments sitting outside the plan.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in Dubai Investments Park actually attend?
faqs.answer: A broad spread, which is the root of the scheduling problem. Two IB schools and a British-curriculum school sit inside the district, with another school in DIP running its own system. Beyond it, families travel to long-established British schools in Jebel Ali, a British school in Al Furjan, an IB school in The Sustainable City and newer provision around Dubai South. All are regulated by KHDA. We name them as market context only and have no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: Is the winter break worth booking sessions in, or should they rest?
faqs.answer: It is the most valuable block in the year for a household like yours, because it is the only period with no school run in it. It falls after internal assessment drafts should exist and before the mock window, so a student can work on one component with no competing deadline for the first time since September. Four focused sessions across that break typically mean arriving at mocks with the component fixed rather than still being diagnosed, and the sessions continue if the family travels.

faqs.question: Is it worth adding a second weekly session in DP2?
faqs.answer: Only if there is practice time between them, which in a long-commute household usually means putting the second session at the weekend rather than on another weekday evening. Two sessions with real independent practice between them outperform four without, every time, because examinations are sat alone. If the weekday evenings are already full, the honest answer is one protected weekday slot plus one weekend session, not three.

faqs.question: What does the commute actually cost us in hours?
faqs.answer: A 45-minute return journey is roughly seven and a half hours a week, which is more than a full school day and considerably more than any tutoring block a family is likely to buy. That arithmetic should change what you purchase: hours are scarcer than money in most households here, so the right spend is on the highest value per hour, which is component diagnosis, mark-scheme technique and uncertainty work rather than general content revision.

faqs.question: What happens if the slot we need is not available?
faqs.answer: You are told, offered the nearest workable alternative, and given a realistic date for when it opens. Mainstream Diploma subjects can usually be matched within a few days; Higher Level Physics is the hardest to cover at a peak hour, with Higher Level Chemistry and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches close behind, and the constraint is sharpest before the May session. A generalist will not be presented as the specialist you asked for, which is the standard failure in this market.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-investme.closingBody: The most useful thing a family in Dubai Investments Park can do before buying any tutoring is write down, for one week, what time their child actually walks through the door. That single number decides the slot, the slot decides what work can go in it, and the work decides whether the term achieves anything. Send us that number with the subject, the level, the school and the last two marked pieces of work, and take the free trial lesson, which tests both the diagnosis and the slot. Lessons run live online into your DIP home on Gulf Standard Time.

Each teaches a full trial lesson before any payment, and the rate conversation happens after you have watched the teaching rather than before.

intro.heading: Distance is the one thing you pay for and do not get back
paragraphs: Nearly every tutoring search starts with a location filter, because that is the filter a search box offers. It feels sensible. It is also the only input in this entire market that reliably increases what you pay while reducing what you receive, and a Marina household is more exposed to that than most. The reason is simple geography: the towers sit at the far western end of the city, the campuses families use are out along Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and towards Emirates Hills, and the hour when a tutor would travel is the hour when Sheikh Zayed Road is least willing to cooperate.

A tutor pricing that journey honestly has to charge for it, and the published figures show what the charge looks like. In-home one-to-one tutoring in this country is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 inclusive of travel, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online where Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The monthly packages make the gap starker still: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Every one of those numbers can be checked on the publishing provider's own page, which is worth pausing on. Of the ranking pages examined for this market, not one cites a source for a single AED figure, three publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in. A parent who wants to verify a rate on this page can do it in ten minutes. That is the standard every page in this market should meet and almost none does.

The second cost of the distance filter does not appear in any quote and is larger. Restricting the search to tutors willing to drive into the Marina restricts it to tutors who live nearby, and the IB accounts for about seven per cent of private school enrolment in an emirate with 227 private schools. The set of people teaching a particular Higher Level subject is small, and the subset who live within a short drive of a specific neighbourhood is smaller again. The parent paying the proximity premium is paying more in order to choose from fewer people, which is precisely the opposite of what they intend.

So this page treats cost as the subject rather than as a closing line. It prices the premium, opens up what an hourly rate contains, costs a two-year Diploma plan by component, names the coursework blocks families forget to budget for, and lists what to refuse. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we provide only in India, and lessons for Marina families are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The comparison below is made on published figures rather than on assertion.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-marina.programmesIntro: Each stage of the IB continuum carries a different cost profile, and the differences are not obvious from a prospectus. Below is what each programme actually commits a Marina household to, financially as well as academically.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led learning across six transdisciplinary themes with no external examinations. Because nothing is externally assessed, there is no mark for a tutor to work towards and very little that paid support can usefully do. The cost-effective interventions at this stage are reading volume and arithmetic fluency, both of which a household can deliver without buying anything.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where Marina families most often spend money with the least return, usually in response to a report they find hard to interpret rather than to a measurable problem. A single session to translate the report is a reasonable purchase; a weekly slot at this age rarely is.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four published criteria with achievement levels from one to eight, plus a Personal Project in the final year. The criteria are the whole game and they are where cheap gains live: a student who knows which criterion a task targets can aim at it, and most do not. That is a short, bounded purchase rather than a long one.
programmes.countryNote: The commonest sensible spend in this cluster at this stage is two or three sessions decoding the criteria and the school's reporting, not a weekly subject slot. Families who buy the weekly slot instead frequently discover in Year 12 that the money would have gone further in the Diploma.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Almost every subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria. The expensive feature is concurrency: coursework deadlines in several subjects land in the same weeks of the second year, which is when families buy help at the worst possible price.
programmes.countryNote: This is where nearly all genuine tutoring spend in the Marina cluster happens and where timing dominates the total. The same support costs a fraction in the first year that it costs in the second, because in the second year it is being bought under deadline pressure for scarce evening slots.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Fewer campuses offer it, so the tutoring market for its distinctive components barely exists and pricing for them is unreliable. Where the shared Diploma courses are concerned, costs behave exactly as they do for a Diploma student.
programmes.countryNote: Rarely offered in New Dubai. Named here because a family comparing schools may encounter it and should know that support for the reflective project is genuinely hard to source at any price in this emirate, which is a planning fact rather than a sales point.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects Marina families most often pay for, with the specific thing in each that determines whether the money is well spent. The pattern to notice is that the cheap wins are concentrated and the expensive ones are diffuse.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most supported subject in this cluster. Cheap gains sit in notation, method communication and calculator work that is not shown in the script, all of which are bounded. Expensive and diffuse: rebuilding algebraic fluency that was never solid, which is a term of work rather than a block.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology. The concentrated win is written interpretation: students compute correctly and then fail to say what the result means. A handful of sessions on explanation often moves more marks than weeks of additional content coverage.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The commonest Higher Level request here. Concentrated wins in uncertainty treatment and in evaluating rather than restating data in the investigation. Diffuse and costly: organic mechanisms a student never understood, which compound and cannot be patched in the final term.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Precision with units, prefixes and significant figures is the cheapest mark recovery in the subject and takes a fortnight. The expensive work is conceptual: a student who never built an intuition for fields will need sustained teaching rather than technique drills.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term precision is the concentrated win and content volume is the diffuse cost. This is the subject where a weekly hour most easily becomes companionable re-reading, which feels productive and moves nothing, so it needs the tightest review discipline of any subject on this list.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment commentaries are the highest-value paid hours in the subject: a clear link between a specific published article, a named concept and an accurate diagram. Diagram labelling is a one-session fix. Higher Level quantitative content is the slower, costlier part.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is the component students prepare least and where a weak global issue cannot be rescued late, so early support is far cheaper than late. Reading volume is the diffuse cost and the one thing no paid hour substitutes for, which an honest tutor will say.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Essay argument and source evaluation respond well to marked practice, which is a bounded purchase. The historical investigation is where money is wasted if the question is unbounded, so one hour stress-testing the question before any research begins is worth ten hours afterwards.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Higher Level research project fails on data access rather than on analysis, and it fails late. One early session asking whether the student can actually obtain the evidence is the single most cost-effective hour available in this subject.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Experimental study write-ups and inferential statistics are the concentrated wins. Worth noting as a budget risk rather than an opportunity: specialist cover is thin across the whole emirate, so this subject carries the longest wait and the least negotiating room in the cluster.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two assessed components, the exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, both marked against published criteria and both routinely left late. Impossible to revise and cheap to support early, which makes the timing of the spend more important than its size.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Not a subject but a project, and the one families least often budget for. Supervised in school, written by the student, and most efficiently supported by a specialist in the subject it sits in rather than by a generic essay coach. Costed as a block, not as a weekly slot.

sections.heading: What proximity actually costs in a Marina week
paragraphs: Price the journey rather than the idea of it. A tutor travelling to a Marina tower for a weekday evening session is committing not one hour but something closer to two and a half: the approach along Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Road at the worst hour, visitor parking in a residential tower, the lesson, and the return. Any rational person charges for that, and the published figures show them doing so. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 table and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors inclusive of travel, against AED 150 to 300 online.

The monthly packages are the cleaner comparison because they hold the hours constant in one direction. Roughly AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions in this market. Roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 buys four two-hour in-home visits, which is also eight hours. Same teaching time, roughly double the cost, and the difference is a car. For a household in a tower on the water, that is a transport subscription dressed as an education expense.

Then there is the part that is invisible in every quote. Dubai has 227 private schools and 387,441 private pupils across seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for seven per cent of enrolment. The number of people who teach a specific Diploma subject at Higher Level is therefore modest, and the number who do that and live within a short drive of this particular neighbourhood is a fraction of it. Filtering by distance does not just add a charge; it removes most of the candidates before you have seen any of them.

The table prices the premium against what it delivers. The row that decides it for most families is the earliest workable start: a visiting tutor arriving after the school run plus their own journey is rarely in the room before six, and a seventeen-year-old doing analytical work at seven in the evening is a worse investment than the same student at five, whatever the hourly rate says.

sections.heading: The price of a wrong match, which no budget contains
paragraphs: Families budget for tutoring and almost never budget for changing tutor, which is the cost that actually damages a Diploma year. The sequence is familiar. A tutor is hired in October on availability and recommendation. By December it is clear the fit is wrong, usually because the subject depth is not there. Nobody says so until February, because the student is polite, the tutor is pleasant and the parent has no way to judge. A replacement starts in March, four months before the papers.

Count what that cost. The paid hours in the first arrangement, which bought reliability rather than teaching. The weeks of the student's own evenings, which are the scarcest resource in the Diploma and are not recoverable. The replacement tutor's first few sessions spent undoing habits rather than building them. And the compression: work that should have been spread over two terms now happens in one, which is where panic buying at premium rates begins.

The defence is cheap and almost nobody uses it. Set a six-week review at the outset, with a specific test: a marked piece of work compared with an earlier one against the same criteria. Not a progress report, which is an opinion, and not a conversation about effort. If the comparison shows nothing, change in week seven rather than in month five. The entire cost of a wrong match is the delay in recognising it.

The second defence is testing subject depth before hiring rather than after. Give the tutor a piece of your child's own marked work in the trial and watch whether they find the pattern in it within a few minutes, name it, and refer to the criteria without being prompted. That takes an hour and it is free. The table prices the alternative.

sections.heading: What is inside a tutoring hour, and what you are really buying
paragraphs: An hourly rate implies you are buying an hour, and you are not. You are buying a bundle, and the bundles differ enormously between providers at identical prices. A family comparing two quotes of AED 250 may be comparing sixty minutes of conversation against sixty minutes of teaching plus marking, written feedback and a session note. That is not a price difference, it is a product difference, and almost nobody asks.

The components worth asking about are specific. Does the tutor read the student's work before the session or during it? Is marking between sessions included, and is it marking against the published criteria or general comment? Is there a written note after each session naming what was worked on, and does the parent receive it? Is coursework supervision included within the weekly hour or charged separately? Is the annotated work saved and sent, or does it exist only in the student's memory?

Each of those has a real cost to the provider, which means a rate that includes them all and a rate that includes none cannot be the same number honestly. The lowest band in this market, where EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, is priced for conversation and supervision; expecting criteria-based marking at that level is expecting something the rate does not fund. The specialist band, where TutorChase quotes AED 270 and Bestimate puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, should fund all of it, and a parent paying it is entitled to ask.

The useful move is to ask for the bundle in writing before agreeing a rate, and to compare bundles rather than numbers. The table lists the components with what each is worth in practice, so a Marina parent can run through it in two minutes on a trial call.

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma plan costed component by component
paragraphs: Most families buy Diploma support as an open-ended weekly slot and discover the total afterwards. The alternative is to cost it by component at the start of the first year, which produces a smaller number and a better plan. The components are known in advance: the subject that is going to be hard, the internal assessment in it, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and a technique block before the final papers. Each has a natural size and a natural timing.

Timing is where the money is made or lost, and the rule is counter-intuitive: the earlier blocks are cheaper and worth more. An hour spent in the first year stress-testing an internal assessment research question costs the same as an hour in the second year and prevents a problem that would otherwise consume ten. An hour on Theory of Knowledge in the first year is ordinary; the same hour in the final fortnight is bought at whatever the market will bear, for a component that cannot be rescued late.

The table costs a realistic plan using the published band for a qualified subject tutor working online, which is AED 150 to 300 an hour. The figures are deliberately a range rather than a price, because they are arithmetic on other providers' published rates and not an IB Gram quote: we publish no rate card on these pages, since the honest number depends on which subject, which components and how many weeks. What the table is for is showing that a planned two-year programme costs less than an unplanned one and achieves more.

Read the bottom row first. A componentised plan across two years comes out well below a weekly hour held for the same period, and it leaves the student with evenings. The households in this cluster that report the least wasted spend are, without exception, the ones that decided in the first year what they were going to buy.

sections.heading: The coursework blocks families forget to budget for
paragraphs: Ask a Marina parent what Diploma support will cost and they will think about subjects. The components that actually generate unplanned spending are the ones that are not subjects: the internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Each is marked against published criteria, each is supervised rather than taught in school, and each arrives in the second year alongside all the others.

The internal assessments are the clearest case. A student has one in most of six subjects, each with its own criteria and its own internal school deadline, and those deadlines cluster. The failure mode is identical across subjects and across years: a research question that cannot generate data capable of supporting a conclusion, identified far too late to change. An hour with a specialist before any data is collected costs the same as an hour in a crisis and prevents the crisis entirely. This is the best-value hour in the Diploma and most families do not know it exists.

The Extended Essay is a four-thousand-word independent project supervised by a member of school staff. What a specialist adds is not writing, which would be a malpractice risk falling on the student, but criteria literacy, a judgement on whether the question is answerable in the word count, and a deadline that is not the school's. Theory of Knowledge is the component that cannot be revised at all: the exhibition and the prescribed-title essay both need structured thinking practice spread over time, and buying it late is buying it at the worst price for the least benefit.

What a tutor may and may not do here is fixed, and we state it rather than leaving it to be assumed. A tutor teaches, explains the criteria letter by letter, comments on the student's own draft and holds them to a deadline. A tutor does not write, redraft or complete an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. Services in this market that advertise finished assessed work are selling something that puts the student's whole qualification at risk, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: Why paying per grade point does not work
paragraphs: Parents sometimes ask, reasonably, whether they can pay for the outcome instead of the hours. It is an honest instinct and the answer is no, for reasons worth setting out rather than deflecting. We do not offer outcome-linked pricing and we attach no promise to a grade, and any provider that does should be read very carefully.

The first reason is that the tutor does not control the variables. Whether a student does the work between sessions, how a school teaches the remaining five subjects, how a cohort performs, what happens in a particular examination hall on a particular morning: none of that is purchasable. A price attached to an outcome prices something the seller cannot deliver, which means either the terms are written to be unenforceable or the seller is relying on them never being tested.

The second reason is that outcome pricing distorts behaviour in the wrong direction. A provider paid on a grade has an incentive to take easy students, to discourage ambitious subject choices, and in the worst case to cross the line on coursework. The worst outcomes in this market, including services selling completed internal assessments, come from exactly that incentive structure. We would rather be paid for teaching and be judged on marked work.

What can be measured is progress on marked work against the same criteria, and that is what a review should use. Not a progress report, which is an opinion; not effort, which is unfalsifiable. A marked piece compared with an earlier one, every six weeks, with a stopping condition agreed in advance. That gives a family a real instrument for deciding whether to keep paying, which is what outcome pricing was reaching for in the first place.

sections.heading: Three things worth a premium, and four that are not
paragraphs: Worth paying more for, first. Subject-and-level depth in the exact course, especially the ability to look at an internal assessment question and say within a minute that it will not work. That judgement is learned by marking a great deal of student work and it is the hardest thing in this market to find. Continuity, meaning the same tutor throughout rather than a rota, because every change resets the diagnostic work. And criteria-based marking between sessions, which costs a provider real time and is the single most valuable item in the bundle for a Diploma student.

Not worth paying more for: proximity, which is the subject of this page. A claim of examiner status that cannot be evidenced, which the research into this market found being used to imply access to marking standards and boundary decisions that nobody outside a board has. Past papers and mark schemes, which the boards publish on their own sites and which no provider should be charging for. And a brand that quotes in a currency UAE families do not transact in, which two of the ranking pages in this market do.

A word on examiner claims in particular, because they command the largest premiums. A tutor's current examiner status is difficult for a parent to verify and the implied benefit is usually overstated: knowing a mark scheme well is valuable, and no examiner has access to unreleased papers or to boundary decisions. A tutor who has marked a lot of student work in the subject is what you actually want, and that is a different and checkable claim. Ask how many internal assessments in this subject they have supervised.

Finally, on urgency. Tutoring is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any page implying otherwise is making a claim about a regulatory process rather than about teaching. On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels; no IB points threshold appears in any source we can cite, so treat any published Diploma figure as unverified until you have read it on the Ministry's own site.

sections.heading: Where a Marina household can spend nothing and get the same result
paragraphs: Several of the things families pay for are available free, and a page about cost that omitted them would not be honest. Past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and assessment criteria are published by the boards and are the main revision currency of the Diploma; a tutor should reference and link them rather than charge for them. The school's own subject teacher is a resource most students under-use, and a specific question asked at a specific time usually gets a better answer than a general plea for help.

Timed practice costs nothing except discipline. A student who sits three full papers to time, marks them against the published scheme and writes down the three recurring errors has done most of what a pre-paper technique block does, and a parent can supervise the clock without teaching anything. The reason families buy this instead is that the discipline is hard to sustain, which is a real reason, but it should be a conscious purchase rather than an assumed one.

Reading volume is the clearest case of all. In English A and in History, and in the extended writing components everywhere, the binding constraint is how much the student reads, and no paid hour substitutes for it. A tutor who tells a family that is giving them the most valuable advice available and losing a sale in the process. We would rather do that than take money for an hour a week against a problem that an hour a week cannot touch.

What is genuinely worth buying, then, is narrow: diagnosis, criteria literacy, marking by somebody who knows where the marks go, and judgement on a coursework question before the work begins. Those four are hard to get free and they are where the whole value of this market sits. Everything else a determined household can do itself, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling the household's own capability back to it.

sections.heading: Why the five o'clock slot costs more than the seven o'clock one
paragraphs: Scheduling has a price in this cluster and it is rarely made explicit. Five and six in the evening are the two most requested hours in New Dubai, because they sit after the school run and before the point at which a teenager stops absorbing anything. Those slots fill first, and when a resource is scarce the people holding it are less flexible on everything else, including rate and including how long a family waits for the right specialist.

The geography drives it. No secondary campus sits inside Dubai Marina, so households here are already using the early afternoon on a run out to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Emirates Hills and back. That compresses the usable window at both ends. For a visiting tutor it compresses further, because their own journey has to fit inside the same congestion. The arithmetic means in-home arrangements in this neighbourhood drift towards six-thirty or seven, which is the cheapest hour to buy and the least productive one to use.

There are two sensible responses and both save money. The first is to take a weekend morning for anything extended: a timed paper, an Extended Essay session, internal assessment work. Those slots match almost immediately, they suit long-form work better than a weekday evening does, and they are not competing with every other household in the cluster. The second is to buy earlier in the course, when the five o'clock slots are not yet contested by families who have left it to the spring.

There is a practical point about Ramadan and the school calendar too, because it cuts the other way. A shortened school day frees afternoon slots that are simply unavailable for the rest of the year, and some families move sessions to after Iftar. Both are opportunities rather than disruptions, and a family that plans for them keeps continuity through a period when most arrangements quietly lapse for a month and then restart at a worse hour.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic hour before anything else
process.description: A specialist reads your child's marked work and tells you what the problem is and whether tutoring can touch it. Published market rates put that at AED 150 to 300. It is the only spend we recommend to everyone, because it regularly prevents a far larger one and occasionally ends with us advising nothing.

process.title: Cost the plan by component, not by term
process.description: The diagnostic hour, a weekly hour in the subject that is genuinely thin, an internal assessment block before data collection, an Extended Essay block, a Theory of Knowledge block and a pre-paper technique block. Each has a natural size. Written down in the first year, the total is smaller than an open weekly slot.

process.title: Ask for the bundle in writing before the rate
process.description: Preparation, marking against the criteria, session notes, saved annotation, whether coursework sits inside the hour, and whether your child keeps the same tutor. Two quotes at the same number can contain very different things, and comparing numbers without the bundle compares nothing.

process.title: Use the free trial to test subject depth
process.description: Send a piece of your child's marked work in advance and watch what the tutor does with it. A specialist finds the pattern within minutes, names it and refers to the criteria unprompted. This is also the hour in which to ask what would make them tell you to stop paying.

process.title: Set a six-week review with a real test
process.description: A marked piece compared with an earlier one against the same criteria, not a progress report. If nothing has moved, change in week seven rather than in month five; the entire cost of a wrong match is the delay in recognising it. If no specialist is free in your hour, we say so rather than substituting.

whyPoints.title: Proximity is priced rather than sold
whyPoints.description: Distance is the one input in this market that raises what you pay and reduces what you can choose from. We publish the premium with its sources and then explain what it buys, which is a journey and a smaller pool, rather than treating a location filter as a feature.

whyPoints.title: Every figure is checkable today
whyPoints.description: Each AED rate here is a named provider's published number for this market in 2026. Of the ranking pages researched for this market, none cites a source for a single AED figure, three publish no price at all and two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in. You can verify ours in ten minutes.

whyPoints.title: The plan is costed by component
whyPoints.description: Diagnostic hour, a weekly subject hour, an internal assessment block, an Extended Essay block, Theory of Knowledge and a pre-paper block. Written down in the first Diploma year, that total comes out below an open weekly slot held for two years and leaves the student with evenings.

whyPoints.title: No outcome-linked pricing
whyPoints.description: We do not price against a grade and we attach no promise to one, because a tutor does not control whether work gets done, how five other subjects are taught, or what happens in an examination hall. Outcome pricing also rewards exactly the behaviour that produces coursework scandals in this market.

whyPoints.title: The free things are named as free
whyPoints.description: Past papers, mark schemes and assessment criteria are published by the boards and no provider should charge for them. Timed practice costs discipline rather than money. Reading volume cannot be bought at all. Saying so loses sales and is the honest content of a page about cost.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. The in-home market rate is quoted above with its sources so the comparison rests on figures rather than on assertion.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives near Dubai Marina cost more or less?
faqs.answer: More, and the published figures show by roughly how much. In-home one-to-one tutoring in this country is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 inclusive of travel, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The package comparison is cleaner: about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, which is the same eight hours for roughly double. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: What does a quoted hourly rate actually include?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the provider, and two quotes at the same number can contain very different things. Ask six questions in writing: do you read my child's work before the session or during it, is marking between sessions included and marked against what, do we receive a note naming what was worked on, is the annotated work saved and sent, is internal assessment work inside the hour or extra, and will my child keep the same tutor. Each has a real cost to the provider, so a rate including all of them and a rate including none cannot honestly be the same figure.

faqs.question: How much does a full two-year Diploma support plan cost?
faqs.answer: Costed by component at the published band of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, a realistic plan runs to roughly forty-eight to fifty-six hours across two years: a diagnostic hour, about twenty-four weekly hours in the one thinly covered Higher Level subject, four to six on internal assessment question work, six to eight on the Extended Essay, four to six on Theory of Knowledge and eight to ten in a pre-paper technique block. That arithmetic uses other providers' published rates rather than an IB Gram price, and it comes out below an open weekly slot held for the same period.

faqs.question: We changed tutors twice. What did that actually cost us?
faqs.answer: More than the hours, and the hours were the small part. A wrong match recognised at month five rather than week six costs about twenty paid hours that bought reliability rather than teaching, twenty of your child's evenings which are the scarcest resource in the Diploma and are not recoverable, several sessions of the replacement's time undoing established habits, and the compression of two terms of work into one. The whole cost is the delay in recognising it, which is why a six-week review against marked work is the cheapest insurance available.

faqs.question: Should I budget separately for Extended Essay supervision?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a block rather than as a weekly slot, and ideally in the first year. The essay is a four-thousand-word independent project supervised by school staff, and what an external specialist adds is criteria literacy, a judgement on whether the question is answerable in the word count, and a deadline that is not the school's. Six to eight hours is a realistic size. Buy it from a specialist in the subject the essay sits in rather than from a general essay coach, and understand that the writing remains entirely the student's own throughout.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge support worth paying for?
faqs.answer: It is, and the timing matters more than the amount. The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay are both marked against published criteria and neither can be revised in the ordinary sense, so support has to be structured thinking practice spread over time rather than a rescue. Four to six hours in the first year is ordinary spending that works. The same four to six hours in the final fortnight is bought at whatever the market will bear for a component that cannot be fixed late, which is the worst purchase in the Diploma.

faqs.question: Why is the five o'clock slot harder to get than the seven o'clock one?
faqs.answer: Because it is the most requested hour in New Dubai, for good reasons: it falls after the school run and before the point at which a teenager stops absorbing anything. No secondary campus sits inside Dubai Marina, so the afternoon is already committed to a run out to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Emirates Hills and back, and that compresses the usable window at both ends. Two responses save money: take a weekend morning for anything extended, which matches almost immediately, and buy earlier in the course before the early slots are contested.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor a false economy at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is specific rather than snobbish. The lowest band in this market, where EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, is priced for supervision and company. What a Higher Level Diploma student needs is diagnosis and criteria-based marking, which take a learned skill and real time between sessions, and a rate at that level does not fund either. The cheap hour is not bad value for homework supervision; it is bad value for the thing you are actually trying to buy.

faqs.question: Can I pay for a grade improvement rather than for hours?
faqs.answer: We do not price against an outcome and we attach no promise to a grade, and a provider that does is worth reading very carefully. A tutor does not control whether the work gets done between sessions, how the other five subjects are taught, or what happens in an examination hall on a particular morning. Outcome pricing also rewards the wrong behaviour: it encourages taking easy students, discouraging ambitious subject choices, and at the extreme it produces the services in this market that sell completed internal assessments. What can be measured is marked work against the same criteria, every six weeks.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing that actually moves an IB grade?
faqs.answer: One hour with a specialist on an internal assessment research question, before any data is collected. The commonest failure across every Diploma subject is a question that cannot generate evidence capable of supporting a conclusion, identified far too late to change. That hour costs the same as any other hour and prevents roughly ten. After that, in order: criteria literacy, a pre-paper technique block built from a mock script, and timed papers which cost nothing but discipline. Reading volume is cheaper still and cannot be purchased at all.

faqs.question: Do we pay for the tutor's marking time between sessions?
faqs.answer: Somebody does, one way or another, and the honest question is whether it is included or extra. Criteria-based marking takes real time and it is the single most valuable item in the bundle for a Diploma student, because it is where the diagnosis actually happens. A provider at the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, as published by TutorChase at AED 270 and in Bestimate's 2026 table, should be funding it within the rate. A provider at the budget band is not, and a family expecting it there is expecting something the price does not cover.

faqs.question: Do providers quote a higher rate once they hear a Marina address?
faqs.answer: In-home quotes certainly reflect it, and the pattern across the cluster is consistent: quotes in JBR track the Marina almost exactly, JLT sits marginally lower because the approach is simpler, Bluewaters Island is steepest because a single bridge means pricing the risk of not arriving, and Al Furjan is visibly lower. That spread, for identical teaching, is the clearest evidence available that the premium is a transport charge rather than a quality signal. One-to-one over live video removes the variable entirely, because there is no journey to price.

faqs.question: How many hours does one internal assessment actually need?
faqs.answer: Four to six, if they are bought at the right moment. One hour stress-testing the research question before any data is collected. One or two reading the published criteria letter by letter with the student, which almost nobody does and which is where most avoidable marks sit. One or two on the student's own draft, as feedback rather than redrafting. And one near the end on presentation against the criteria. Bought in a crisis the same work takes far longer and achieves less, because the question is already fixed and the data is already collected.

faqs.question: What should we refuse to pay for?
faqs.answer: Four things. Proximity, which raises the price and shrinks the pool you choose from. A claim of examiner status that cannot be evidenced, especially where it is used to imply access to marking standards or boundary decisions that nobody outside a board has. Past papers and mark schemes, which the boards publish on their own sites and which no provider should charge for. And group classes sold as a cheaper substitute for diagnosis, which re-teach the lesson the student already sat and occupy the hour in which the specific problem could have been addressed.

faqs.question: When in the two years is the money best spent?
faqs.answer: Early, which is the opposite of when families actually spend it. The diagnostic hour, the internal assessment question work, the Extended Essay block and Theory of Knowledge all cost the same per hour in the first year and prevent problems that cost multiples later. Early slots are also less contested, so you get the specialist you want at the hour you want. By the second term of the second year a family is buying under deadline pressure, for scarce evenings, in a market where urgency is the most expensive thing a budget can contain.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying extra for a tutor described as an examiner?
faqs.answer: Be careful with this one, because it commands the largest premiums in the market and is the hardest claim for a parent to verify. Current examiner status is often stated and rarely evidenced, and the implied benefit is overstated: knowing a mark scheme thoroughly is genuinely valuable, and no examiner has access to unreleased papers or to boundary decisions. What you actually want is somebody who has marked a great deal of student work in that subject at that level, which is a checkable claim. Ask how many internal assessments in this subject they have supervised.

intro.heading: What a proximity search gives you, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: A phone searching for an IB tutor near me from Dubai Media City is answering a geography question. It ranks results by distance, by local business listings, by who has bought the local advertising, and by who has the most reviews attached to a map pin. None of those signals has any relationship to whether the person at the other end has taught Chemistry at Higher Level or supervised an Economics Internal Assessment through moderation. The search is doing its job. The job is simply not the one you need done.

That becomes clearer when you look at the district. Media City is a free zone of offices and studios in Al Sufouh, sandwiched between Sheikh Zayed Road and the coast, with Dubai Internet City on one side and Dubai Knowledge Park on the other. The Dubai Tram runs along the sea edge and the Red Line Metro stops at Dubai Internet City. There is no school inside the free zone. The nearest gates are in Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, and the nearest tuition centres are a cluster in Al Barsha and another near the Marina. Those are the businesses a proximity search surfaces.

The IB is also the thinnest of Dubai's four main curricula. KHDA's 2024-25 figures record 387,441 students across 227 private schools licensed to run 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum holding 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian schools 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate schools 7 per cent. Split that 7 per cent across three programmes, six Diploma subject groups and two levels, and the number of genuinely matched specialists within a 20-minute drive of Al Sufouh stops being a sensible pool to pick from.

This page is therefore written as a decision guide rather than a pitch. There are four models you can buy IB tutoring from in Dubai: a tuition centre with premises, an agency, an international marketplace, or an independent tutor you find yourself. Each has a different cost structure, a different pool, and a different answer to the question of who is accountable when it goes wrong. Comparing them properly takes one table, which is further down, and it is the part worth reading even if you choose someone else.

On delivery we are direct. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Media City families run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm on school nights. That is what lets the match be made on subject and level rather than on who can reach Al Sufouh before six.

One more thing worth saying before the detail. Nothing on this page argues that proximity is worthless. A tutor who knows your child's school, its reporting cycle and its internal deadlines is genuinely useful, and that knowledge is more common among people who live and work in the same corridor. The argument is narrower: proximity is a weak proxy for subject expertise, and when the two conflict, subject expertise is the one that shows up in marked work. Where both are available, take both.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-media-ci.programmesIntro: Families around Media City are usually asking about one of these three IB programmes, and occasionally about the British route their child's classmates are on. The programme changes what tutoring is for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher and three Standard levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The final score is out of 45. Internal Assessments carry between a fifth and a quarter of each subject grade, which means a large share of the Diploma is produced at home over months rather than in an examination hall.
programmes.countryNote: UAE IB schools sit the May session, with November as the second sitting, used mainly for retakes. Specific IB session and results dates are not published here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself; your school's IB coordinator is the authority. Around Media City, the Diploma is offered at GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh and Dubai American Academy in Al Barsha.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups studied together, each marked against four criteria out of eight, with the grade built from tasks across the year. There is no public paper in most subjects, so a weak term is costly and hard to see coming. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project, which is externally moderated and must be the student's own work throughout.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai complicates this. Some IB schools run the MYP for all five years; others stop at 14 and enter students for IGCSE instead. Children living in the same Al Sufouh tower can therefore be on different tracks while attending the same school. The examinations officer is the person who can tell you which, and the answer changes what tutoring should look like completely.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and organised by transdisciplinary themes rather than by subjects, ending with the Grade 5 Exhibition. Reports describe approaches to learning, which parents arriving from British, Indian or American systems find difficult to interpret. Support here is kept light: reading fluency, number sense and written expression, built so it feeds the inquiry rather than competing with it.
programmes.countryNote: The nearest full IB continuum primaries to Media City sit in Al Barsha South and Emirates Hills rather than in Al Sufouh itself, so primary-age families here are often bussing children a reasonable distance. Where a move into a British school at Year 7 is likely, a quiet programme of number and spelling work alongside the inquiry is the usual request.

programmes.name: The British route alongside
programmes.description: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, with syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 4PH1 Physics, taken by most 14 to 16 year olds in this part of Dubai. UAE candidates sit June and November with Cambridge, and May/June and November with Pearson. Preparation is past papers and mark schemes, which is a different discipline from MYP criterion work.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai College in Al Sufouh runs the British route and GEMS Wellington International School runs both, so siblings in this corridor are frequently on different systems. Families who assume one tutor covers both are usually disappointed in the detail: the assessment logic is not the same, and a tutor fluent in one can miss what the other rewards.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-media-ci.subjectsIntro: Requests from this corridor cluster in the sciences, mathematics and the social sciences, with a steady seasonal flow of Internal Assessment and Extended Essay work. These are the subjects and the specific marks at stake.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, two at Standard, with HL Paper 3 given to extended problem-solving. Proof and calculus technique cost the most marks, followed by conclusions that are correct but unjustified. The Exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics used.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a graphic display calculator used throughout. Students choose it expecting relief and meet dense statistics at Higher Level. Tutoring usually targets calculator fluency, reading output back into context, and answering the modelling question as asked rather than the one the student prefers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 divides into multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 is extended response, and the data booklet is permitted. Marks go missing on uncertainty treatment, on gradients quoted without units, and on explanation questions where the reasoning stays in the student's head. The Internal Assessment is one investigation marked out of 24.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity, with Higher Level deepening energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic chemistry is the most requested topic from Al Sufouh and the Marina. The usual failure is reaction recall without mechanism, which collapses the moment Paper 2 uses an unfamiliar substrate.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Large content load assessed through precise command terms. Students who write everything they know about a process score below those who answer exactly what was asked. Data-based questions are the cheapest marks available and the least deliberately practised part of the course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries real weight, and Higher Level adds quantitative work and a policy paper. The Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries on published articles, where students lose marks by summarising the article instead of applying a named concept and evaluating with it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven with a pre-released case for Paper 1. The Internal Assessment is a research project on a real organisation, and the common disaster is choosing a company with no accessible data. A tutor who changes the organisation in week one has done more than any later editing could.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, plus the Individual Oral and the HL essay. Confident readers narrate instead of analysing construction. The work is annotation discipline and a repeatable paragraph shape that can be applied to any unseen text under time.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study recall tied to precise evaluation language, with an experimental Internal Assessment. Students accumulate studies and cannot deploy them against a command term. Tutoring is usually about building a small, well-rehearsed bank of studies that can answer several question types rather than a long list that answers none.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and essay, and a 4,000-word Extended Essay in a chosen subject. Both are coached, not taught: framing, scope, method, referencing, reflection. A tutor gives feedback on the student's own drafts and writes none of the work, which is a rule rather than a preference.

sections.heading: What an IB tutor near me search returns from an Al Sufouh address
paragraphs: Searching for an IB tutor near me in Dubai Media City returns, in rough order: tuition centres in Al Barsha with premises and a map pin, agencies advertising a Dubai number, international marketplaces with no local presence at all, and a handful of independent tutors. The ranking reflects distance, local advertising spend and review volume on map listings. It does not reflect whether anyone in the list has taught your child's subject at your child's level.

This is worth stating plainly because the search feels authoritative. A map with five pins and a star rating looks like a shortlist. What it is, is a list of businesses that have invested in being findable from your postcode. Several ranking providers in this market publish self-asserted star ratings in their page markup, and the researched set included two pages showing different review counts for the same rating and one showing a five-star score from twenty reviews against a separate claim of a far larger student body. Treat the stars as advertising.

The useful alternative is to replace the geography question with a specification question. Which subject, which level, and which part of the assessment is failing. A Higher Level Chemistry student struggling with organic mechanisms needs a Chemistry specialist; a DP1 student who has over-committed on three Higher Levels needs a conversation about which to defend. Neither request is improved by the tutor living in Al Sufouh.

That is the reasoning behind online delivery for this corridor. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What you get instead is a match made on subject and level from everyone teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and a slot at 7pm that holds on a bad evening because nobody has to cross Sheikh Zayed Road to reach it.

sections.heading: The radius problem: what twenty minutes from Media City actually contains
paragraphs: It helps to make the radius concrete. Driving out of Media City, a five-minute radius reaches Al Sufouh, Knowledge Park and Internet City. Ten to fifteen minutes reaches Al Barsha, Barsha Heights, The Greens and the Marina. Twenty minutes, at a quiet hour, reaches Al Barsha South, JLT and the edge of the villa belt. At four in the afternoon, the same twenty minutes reaches considerably less.

Inside that area there are plenty of schools and a reasonable number of tuition centres. What there is not, reliably, is a specialist in the exact subject and level you need who is free in the exact slot your evening allows. The constraint is a product of three small numbers multiplied together: the IB's share of enrolment, the split across subject groups, and the split across Higher and Standard. The result is that a proximity search is drawing from a pool of perhaps a handful of genuinely matched people, and selecting from them by advertising.

The table below sets out the rings and what each realistically contains, so you can see where the arithmetic breaks. It also shows the thing most families discover only after booking: the ring that matters for an in-home arrangement is the tutor's ring, not yours. A specialist living in Mirdif is not in your twenty minutes, and will not be at six o'clock whatever the map says.

sections.heading: The four models you can buy IB tutoring from, compared
paragraphs: A tuition centre has premises, fixed hours and a licence to operate as a training institute. It is accountable in a tangible way, usually teaches in small groups as well as one to one, and is constrained to the teachers it employs locally. An agency brokers tutors, often with a travel-included rate, and its pool is the people willing to drive. An international marketplace offers a long list of tutors, frequently priced in dollars, with the platform taking no view on fit. An independent tutor you find yourself is the cheapest and the least underwritten: if it stops working, you start again.

The honest comparison is about cost, pool and what happens when it fails, not about which brand is better. Published rate bands differ sharply between the models. Budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified online subject tutors run AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 with travel included, and Bestimate's in-home band is AED 180 to AED 350. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

Two things are worth noticing in those numbers. First, three of the six strongest-ranking pages for Dubai tutoring publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do publish in dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. Second, the in-home premium is consistent across models, which tells you it is a travel cost rather than a quality cost. Comparing models on published rate, pool and remedy is the only comparison that holds, and it is set out below.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what changes if you move emirate
paragraphs: Dubai private schools fall under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the federal portal describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Families in Media City who relocate within the UAE discover that this is not a national system. The regulator changes, the inspection framework changes, and the attestation route for certificates changes with it.

Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are governed by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall to the federal Ministry of Education, which the portal describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in those three emirates. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the emirate body can shape more than inspection.

Two practical consequences for a Media City family. First, a KHDA inspection band is not comparable with an ADEK or SPEA judgement, so comparing a Dubai school's rating against an Abu Dhabi school's rating is not a like-for-like exercise. Second, Dubai's own context has moved recently: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no office in the UAE. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is useful; implying that one endorses a tutoring platform would not be true, and the phrase KHDA-approved tutor describes nothing that exists.

sections.heading: The Diploma core: who is actually allowed to help
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service sit outside the six subjects and are where outside help is most often misused. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece of research in a chosen subject with a supervisor at school. Theory of Knowledge produces an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Both are assessed, both are produced at home, and both are the student's own work by definition.

What a tutor may do is substantial and legitimate. They may help a student narrow a research question to something answerable with sources the student can actually reach. They may teach research method, source evaluation, referencing conventions and academic register. They may explain what each assessment criterion asks for. They may read the student's own draft and say, precisely, where a paragraph fails against a descriptor. All of that is teaching.

What a tutor may not do is equally clear. They may not write any part of the essay, may not restructure or rewrite a draft on the student's behalf, may not supply a model essay to be adapted, and may not generate the reflections. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For the student, that is an academic honesty finding and a potential loss of the Diploma; for the parent, it is money spent on a risk nobody disclosed.

Ask any provider what happens to a weak draft. The useful answer is that it is marked against the criteria and returned to the student to rewrite, with the specific failure named. Any answer involving the tutor improving the text has told you where that provider's line sits. We state ours on every page because the exposure lands on your child rather than on us.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context, against what Dubai families already spend
paragraphs: Tutoring does not get judged on its own. It gets judged against a school fee, a bus fee, an activity fee and everything else a Dubai family is already paying, which is why the cheapest option so often wins by default. Putting the numbers next to each other makes the decision less arbitrary.

The published monthly packages in this market are a useful anchor: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Against a Dubai private school fee, a single subject at the mid tier is a modest line item; against four subjects, it stops being modest quickly, which is the argument for fixing one subject properly rather than four approximately.

The fee context also moved recently. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That is one year in which the tutoring line is the variable rather than the fee, which makes it a sensible year to spend deliberately rather than reactively.

The practical guidance that follows from the numbers is unglamorous. Buy one subject, weekly, for a term, in the subject that is actually failing. Reassess from marked work rather than from feeling. If two subjects genuinely need help, buy two specialists rather than one generalist, and expect to drop back to one after six weeks. Spending more per hour matters far less than spending consistently in the right place.

sections.heading: The parts of the UAE school year nobody plans for
paragraphs: Two periods reliably break a tutoring plan in this city, and both are foreseeable. The first is Ramadan, when school days shorten and the useful study window moves to the evening. Families who treat it as a pause lose a month from a term that often contains Internal Assessment deadlines; families who shift sessions later keep continuity with very little friction, and online delivery makes the shift trivial because there is no travel to rearrange.

The second is the long summer. Dubai empties, families travel, and a student returning in late August to a DP2 year has had ten weeks away from the material. For a Diploma student that gap sits immediately before the heaviest coursework term of the two-year course. A short block of two or three sessions in the final fortnight of the holiday is the single most efficient purchase in the calendar, and almost nobody makes it.

There are smaller interruptions that matter more than they look: residential trips, national holidays, mock weeks that displace normal teaching, and the week after a set of mock results when motivation either arrives or collapses. A weekly slot absorbs these as long as lessons are recorded and the plan is written down. A fortnightly slot does not, because two cancellations in a row mean a month with no contact.

The reason this section exists is that the calendar, not the tutor, is usually what decides whether a term of tutoring was worth buying. Scheduling around Gulf Standard Time, keeping the same hour weekly, shifting rather than pausing during Ramadan and buying a short block before the summer return are all decisions a parent makes, not a tutor. They are also the cheapest improvements available.

sections.heading: What the first four sessions should actually produce
paragraphs: A reasonable way to judge any provider, including this one, is to ask what the first four sessions will deliver and then check whether they did. The answer should be specific enough to be wrong. Vague answers about confidence are unfalsifiable, which is precisely why they are popular.

In our case, session one is diagnostic: the student's own recent marked work, a question or two attempted live, and a written note afterwards naming what is costing marks. Session two targets the largest single loss, usually technique rather than content. Session three applies it to a new question cold, to see whether it transferred. Session four is a timed piece, marked against the real scheme, which gives a before-and-after that a parent can read without taking anyone's word for it.

What that process tends to find is unglamorous and consistent. Students lose marks on command terms, on working that stays unwritten, on data questions they have never deliberately practised, and on answering a slightly different question from the one set. Those are all cheap to fix and expensive to ignore, and none of them requires a premium tutor or a laboratory.

If after four sessions nothing in the marked work has moved, the useful conclusion is not that the student needs more hours. It is that the match or the diagnosis was wrong, and both are fixable. Being told that honestly at session four is worth considerably more than a term of pleasant lessons, which is why we would rather re-match than extend.
