process.title: Replace the map question with a specification
process.description: Subject, level, and which part of the assessment is failing. Those three facts predict usefulness; distance does not. If you have a marked piece of work or a mock paper, that is worth more than any description, because it shows how the student answers rather than what they have revised.

process.title: A short call, with limits stated
process.description: Ten minutes on the subjects, the school, the deadlines and what has already been tried. If no suitable specialist is free in your preferred slot, you are told that with the earliest realistic alternative, including when the match would be a tutor based outside the UAE teaching in Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Free trial lesson as a diagnostic
process.description: One lesson at no cost, spent on real work rather than on introductions, followed by a written note naming what is costing marks and what the first four sessions would target. Nothing is paid until you have read that note and agreed with it.

process.title: A weekly hour that survives the term
process.description: Booked in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm, in the same slot each week. Sessions shift later during Ramadan rather than pausing. Lessons are recorded, so a school trip or a mock week does not turn into a lost fortnight.

process.title: Judged on marked work at session four
process.description: A timed piece marked against the real scheme, compared with the diagnostic from session one. If nothing has moved, the honest reading is that the match or the diagnosis was wrong, and we re-match rather than sell more hours.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level rather than distance
whyPoints.description: A proximity search ranks by advertising and map pins. Matching on subject and level draws from everyone teaching in Gulf Standard Time, which for Higher Level sciences and mathematics is the difference between a specialist and the nearest competent generalist.

whyPoints.title: Models compared, not competitors attacked
whyPoints.description: Centres, agencies, marketplaces and independent tutors each have a different cost structure, pool and remedy. This page compares the models on published rates and states IB Gram's own position in the same terms, including that home visits are an India-only service.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium inside the rate
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor, and the monthly packages double the money for half the contacts. The premium is a travel cost, consistent across providers, not a quality signal.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on the Diploma core
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach method, criteria and referencing and give feedback on the student's own drafts. Nobody writes an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or an Internal Assessment, and nobody supplies a model to adapt. A provider in this market sells completed coursework, so the question is worth asking everywhere.

whyPoints.title: Regulators explained, never implied as endorsement
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education are described here with sources. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them, has no UAE office, and claims no relationship with any school named.

whyPoints.title: A test you can run at session four
whyPoints.description: A diagnostic in session one and a timed, scheme-marked piece in session four give you a before-and-after you can read yourself. If nothing moved, the match or the diagnosis was wrong, and re-matching is the honest response rather than selling a longer block.

faqs.question: Why does searching for an IB tutor near me return tuition centres rather than IB specialists?
faqs.answer: Because the search is ranking distance, local advertising and map reviews, none of which correlates with subject expertise. From a Media City address the nearest commercial cluster is in Al Barsha, so that is what appears. The IB holds roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, split across three programmes, six Diploma subject groups and two levels, so the number of exactly matched specialists inside any drive radius is small. Replacing the geography question with subject and level is what actually improves the result.

faqs.question: Should I trust the star ratings on local tutoring listings?
faqs.answer: Treat them as advertising rather than evidence. The researched competitor set included pages showing two different review counts against the same rating, and one showing a five-star score from twenty reviews alongside a separately stated student body many times that size. Self-asserted ratings in page markup are against Google's structured-data policy and are a manual-action risk, which tells you something about how they are produced. Ask instead for factual answers about paper structure, Internal Assessment marking and what happens to a weak draft.

faqs.question: How far would a tutor realistically travel to Al Sufouh at five in the afternoon?
faqs.answer: Far enough to make the arrangement expensive and fragile. A tutor living in Al Barsha South or Mirdif is not inside your twenty-minute ring at that hour, whatever a map says off-peak, and a one-hour lesson costs them roughly two hours of the day. That is what the in-home premium of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour reflects. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and lessons here run over live video instead.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a tuition centre, an agency and a marketplace?
faqs.answer: Accountability and pool. A centre has premises, fixed hours and the teachers it employs, so it is tangible but constrained. An agency brokers tutors who are willing to travel, which narrows the pool to drivers and adds the travel cost. A marketplace offers a very long list, often priced in dollars, and takes no view on fit, so the selection work lands on you. An independent tutor is usually cheapest and least underwritten: if it fails, you restart the search alone.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers my child's school, and does it change across the UAE?
faqs.answer: It changes. Dubai private schools fall under KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which also approve fees, curricula and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall to the federal Ministry of Education. Inspection ratings are therefore not comparable between emirates, which matters if you relocate and try to compare schools on their bands.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay or is that off limits?
faqs.answer: Help is permitted and useful, within a firm boundary. A tutor may narrow a research question to something answerable with reachable sources, teach research method and referencing, explain each criterion, and read the student's own draft and name exactly where it fails. A tutor may not write any part of it, may not redraft on the student's behalf, may not supply a model to adapt, and may not produce the reflections. The school supervisor remains the authority on the process throughout.

faqs.question: How much should one subject of IB tutoring cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 for a mid-tier tutor and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' figures. For most Diploma students, a mid-tier tutor held weekly for a term is the sensible purchase.

faqs.question: Did Dubai school fees go up this year, and does that affect tutoring budgets?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting support, that makes tutoring the variable line rather than the fee, which is an argument for spending deliberately: one subject, weekly, for a term, in the subject that is actually failing, reassessed from marked work.

faqs.question: How many IB subjects is it sensible to tutor at the same time?
faqs.answer: One, in almost every case. Two if two subjects are genuinely failing, and then with a specialist in each rather than one tutor covering both approximately. Tutoring in four or more subjects is usually a sign that the problem is organisation or Higher Level over-commitment rather than content, and more lessons make that worse by consuming the hours the student needs for their own work. Families who buy two often drop back to one after six weeks, which is the right outcome.

faqs.question: What should I expect to see by the fourth session?
faqs.answer: A timed piece of work marked against the real scheme, comparable with the diagnostic from the first session. Session one diagnoses from the student's own marked work, session two targets the largest single loss, session three tests whether it transferred to an unseen question, and session four measures it. If nothing has moved in marked work, the honest conclusion is that the match or the diagnosis was wrong, not that more hours are needed. Re-matching is the correct response at that point.

faqs.question: Do weekly IB sessions keep running through Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They shift rather than stop, for most families. School days shorten and the productive study window moves to the evening, so weekly slots move later in the day. Because lessons are delivered over live video there is no travel to rearrange, which makes the change simple to make and simple to reverse. Families who prefer to pause for the month do, but it is worth checking the term's Internal Assessment deadlines first, because a month off a term that contains three of them is expensive.

faqs.question: Is there any point in tutoring during the summer holiday?
faqs.answer: Two or three sessions in the last fortnight before term is the most efficient purchase in the calendar and almost nobody makes it. A DP1 student returning to DP2 after ten weeks away is walking into the heaviest coursework term of the course cold. A short block that reopens the material, confirms the Extended Essay position and sets the autumn plan prevents the September fortnight that is usually lost to re-acclimatising. Long summer programmes are rarely worth it; short reactivation blocks are.

faqs.question: Are IB Gram's tutors approved by KHDA or by the IB?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody's are. A training institute with premises can hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a business permit, not a tutor credential, and the phrase KHDA-approved tutor describes nothing that exists. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free for the subject and level we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with the earliest realistic alternative, rather than matched to the nearest available person. The hardest requests from this corridor are Higher Level Computer Science, Visual Arts, Design Technology and some language acquisition subjects, and the hardest window is the final term before the examination session. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, and that is said before you book rather than discovered afterwards.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a worse option for a student who says they learn better in person?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth taking seriously. A very young child, or a student who will not work without an adult physically present, is harder to teach over video, and if that describes your child the honest answer may be that we are not the right fit. For a motivated Diploma student working through Paper 2 technique on a screen-shared past paper with live annotation, online is not a compromise. It is the arrangement that gets them a subject specialist instead of the nearest available tutor.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-media-ci.closingHeading: Swap the map for a specification
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-media-ci.closingBody: If you have been searching for an IB tutor near me from a Dubai Media City address, the quickest improvement is to stop asking where and start asking who: which subject, which level, and which part of the assessment is losing marks. That specification can be matched from everyone teaching in Gulf Standard Time, which is a far better pool than everyone within a twenty-minute drive of Al Sufouh at five in the afternoon. A free trial lesson puts your child's own marked work in front of a specialist and produces a written diagnosis before anything is paid, and by the fourth session there is a timed, scheme-marked piece you can judge for yourself.

intro.heading: "Near me" is the wrong filter for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near Dubai Production City sorts results by how far somebody lives from IMPZ. That is a useful filter for a plumber. For a Diploma subject it filters on the one variable that has no bearing on the grade. What has a bearing is whether the person in front of your child knows that Paper 3 in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is twenty per cent of the grade and two extended problems, or that an explain question in Physics scores nothing for describing an outcome without naming the principle behind it.

There is no IB World School inside Dubai Production City. Students bus out to Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, to the Al Barsha ring, or to Fairgreen International School to the south. That means the pool of Diploma teachers who happen to live within fifteen minutes of IMPZ is small to begin with, and it thins out sharply the moment you need Chemistry at Higher Level rather than Maths at Standard.

So this page answers the search by subject rather than by geography. What the current syllabus actually contains, which components carry the weight, where the mark schemes catch students, what the Internal Assessment criteria ask for by letter, and what a sensible past-paper programme looks like. Those are the things a parent can judge a tutor on in the first twenty minutes of a trial lesson, and they are checkable in a way that a profile photograph is not.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. On a subject page that is not a limitation to apologise for. Subject precision is the entire argument: a Production City family working on Chemistry HL energetics should be taught by a chemist who marks energetics, and asking that person to also be within a twenty-minute drive of IMPZ at six in the evening narrows the field to almost nobody.

Everything below was reviewed in October 2026. We do not publish IB session or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be right. Confirm exact windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. What we can set out safely is the syllabus structure, the component weightings and the assessment criteria, because those are published in the subject guides your child's school already holds and they do not change between one year and the next. Those are also the only things in this market that a parent can check for themselves, which is why the whole page is built on them rather than on claims about our tutors.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-producti.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes matter to families in this cluster, and the subject demands differ sharply between them. The Diploma is where syllabus precision pays most, because it is the only one with external papers.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three Higher and three Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject has externally assessed papers and an internally assessed component. The internal piece is usually worth twenty to twenty-five per cent and is completed during the course, which makes it the most controllable part of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Production City Diploma students commute, and the long bus day compresses the usable study window into the evening. The practical consequence for subject work is that past-paper sessions need to be shorter and more frequent rather than long Saturday blocks, because a tired student working through a three-hour paper learns less than one doing two questions properly.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria scored one to eight and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. The criteria are labelled by letter rather than topic: in the sciences, Criterion B is inquiring and designing and Criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science. Communication marks, not content marks, are where most are lost.
programmes.countryNote: Because the MYP has no external examination, a Production City student entering DP1 has usually never sat a three-hour paper. The first Diploma mock then reads like a content failure when it is a pacing failure. Subject work in the final MYP year should introduce timed conditions and command-term reading before the Diploma does it abruptly.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Six transdisciplinary themes, continuous assessment, no external examination. The subject-specific work that pays off later is narrower than parents expect: number fluency, reading stamina and the ability to write a paragraph that answers the question asked. Those three carry directly into the MYP criteria and then into Diploma papers.
programmes.countryNote: PYP children from Production City are on early buses to Dubai Investments Park, Motor City or Al Barsha, so evening attention is limited. Short, frequent online sessions work far better at this age than a single long one, and a parent in the room for the first ten minutes makes a measurable difference to how the hour goes.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-producti.subjectsIntro: Eight Diploma subjects, with the syllabus content that carries the weight and the specific place the mark scheme catches students. These are the subjects Production City and Jebel Ali families request most, and the notes are the ones we would open a trial lesson with.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof by induction, calculus and complex numbers at HL. Paper 3 is two extended problems worth roughly a fifth of the grade and rewards starting an unfamiliar structure. The mark-scheme trap is method: an unjustified line loses marks a correct final answer cannot recover, because method marks are awarded separately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling, matrices and graph theory at HL. The graphical display calculator is assumed throughout, and students lose marks for not showing which test they ran or which regression model they fitted. Interpreting a p-value in context, rather than reporting it, is where the top band sits.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes with HL extensions since the 2023 syllabus. Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-analysis section; Paper 2 is extended response. The trap is uncertainty: students quote a value without propagating error, and lose the analysis marks the data section exists to award.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity as two integrated strands. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the papers. The trap is mechanistic notation: a correct product with no curly arrows, no lone pair shown and no intermediate scores a fraction of the available marks, however right the chemistry is.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. Command terms do more damage here than anywhere else: outline, explain, distinguish and suggest each buy a different number of marks, and a student writing an essay for a two-mark outline wastes minutes they need later.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and economic development. Diagrams are the grade. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram with analysis tied to it scores where prose does not. The portfolio of three commentaries, 800 words each, must cover different units and different articles.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral on a global issue, and at HL a 1,200-1,500 word essay. The trap in Paper 1 is answering the guiding question as a comprehension task rather than analysing how the text produces its effect.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computer organisation, networks, computational thinking, plus HL options such as resource management. The solution development Internal Assessment is a working product with documentation, and scope control decides the mark far more often than coding skill does.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on one of six prescribed titles and an exhibition of three objects with 950 words of commentary. The common failure is writing about the objects rather than about how they illustrate a knowledge question, which is what the assessment instrument actually asks for.

The tutor works from the published syllabus structure, not a generic textbook order.

sections.heading: Command terms are the single highest-return thing to teach
paragraphs: Most Diploma students who underperform know more than their script shows. The gap is almost always between what the question asked for and what they supplied, and the instruction is in the first word. State wants a one-line answer with no reasoning. Outline wants a brief account. Explain wants a reason or mechanism. Discuss wants a balanced review with evidence on both sides. Evaluate wants a judgement, which most students never actually make.

The arithmetic is unforgiving. A student who writes a paragraph for a two-mark state question has spent four minutes earning two marks and will run out of time on a six-mark discuss later in the paper. A student who describes what happens when a question says explain scores nothing at all, because the mark scheme awards the principle, not the observation. Both errors are invisible in classwork and lethal in a paper.

This is also the most teachable thing in the Diploma. It takes two or three sessions to make a student fluent at reading the verb, allocating time by mark value, and shaping an answer to the band descriptor. For a student sitting six subjects, the same skill pays in all six, which is why we start past-paper work here rather than with content.

The table below sets out the pattern. Exact command-term definitions are published in each subject guide, and your child's school holds those guides; we work from them rather than from a general list.

table.caption: COMMAND TERMS AND WHAT EACH ACTUALLY BUYS

sections.heading: Where the weight actually sits, component by component
paragraphs: Parents buy tutoring against a grade, but grades are built from components with very different weights, and effort put into the wrong one is wasted. The pattern worth knowing is that every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed piece completed during the course, worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the final mark, and that this is the only portion a student can finish calmly months before the exam hall.

In the sciences, the scientific investigation is a single piece of work worth twenty per cent. A student who produces a weak research question in DP1 has capped a fifth of their grade before any revision begins, and no amount of past-paper work in the spring recovers it. In Mathematics, the exploration is also twenty per cent and the same logic applies. In Economics, the portfolio of three commentaries at 800 words each carries a comparable share.

On the external side, the distribution surprises people. Mathematics AA HL has three papers rather than two, and the third is two extended problems that reward a specific skill: reading an unfamiliar structure, extracting what is being asked, and starting. Science Paper 1 now has a data-analysis section that examines a skill rarely taught explicitly, which is reading a graph and treating uncertainty in mark-scheme language.

The practical conclusion for a Production City family is to ask which component is currently weakest before buying hours. The answer is in the school's own subject handbook and in the last report, and it determines whether the sensible purchase is Internal Assessment supervision in DP1 or paper technique in DP2.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment criteria, by letter
paragraphs: Internal Assessment criteria are published, lettered and specific, and almost no competitor page in this market names a single one. That is odd, because the criteria are the whole instruction. A student who has read them before starting writes a different piece of work from one who reads them at the end, and the difference is usually worth several marks.

In the sciences, the investigation is assessed across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design is where the piece is won or lost, because a question that cannot produce enough data variation makes every subsequent criterion hard to satisfy. Students pick a question they find interesting rather than one that is measurable, and the marks follow the measurability.

In Mathematics, the exploration is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Personal engagement is the one students misunderstand most: it does not mean choosing a topic they enjoy, it means visible evidence of their own thinking and their own decisions in the work. Reflection means saying what the result means and what the limitations are.

Our role here is narrow and it is deliberately narrow. We teach what each criterion asks for, we question whether the chosen question can satisfy it, and we give feedback on the student's own drafts against the descriptors. We do not write, rewrite or complete the work. One operator in our research sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying that is a malpractice risk carried by the student, not the seller.

sections.heading: A past-paper programme that is not just more papers
paragraphs: Doing past papers is not a strategy. Doing them under timing, marking them against the published mark scheme rather than against a model answer, and keeping a categorised error log is a strategy. Most students do the first part and skip the other two, which is why their scores plateau after the third paper.

The order matters as well. Questions by topic first, so a student practises the thing they just learned while it is fresh. Then whole sections under timing. Then full papers, late, because a full paper early in the process mostly teaches a student that they cannot do a full paper. For a commuting Production City student with a late evening window, two targeted questions on a Tuesday beat a three-hour paper nobody has energy for.

The error log is the part that actually produces improvement, and it needs categories rather than a list. A student whose errors are eighty per cent command-term misreads has a reading problem. One whose errors concentrate in multi-step mole calculations has a specific content problem. One who runs out of time on Paper 2 every time has a pacing problem. Three completely different interventions, and the log is what distinguishes them.

We do not supply past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are IB copyright material. We work from papers the student or school legitimately holds and we reference the official source. Any provider offering to send you a library of mark schemes is distributing material they do not own.

sections.heading: What the subject pool near IMPZ actually looks like
paragraphs: This is the honest answer to the search term. The number of IB Diploma subject specialists living within a short evening drive of Dubai Production City is small, and it is smallest exactly where the need is greatest. Standard Level Mathematics is findable locally. Chemistry at Higher Level with current knowledge of the scientific investigation criteria, available at half past five on a Tuesday, is a much harder ask.

The reason is structural rather than regional. Diploma teachers are concentrated at the campuses that run the Diploma, and those campuses are in Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha and the southern corridor. A teacher finishing at a campus in Al Barsha at four does not arrive in IMPZ before five, and may be choosing between three families in different communities. The travel premium in the Dubai market, roughly AED 50-150 an hour on published rate differences, is that choice expressed as money.

The same constraint applies with more force to small-cohort subjects. Computer Science HL, Economics HL in the week before a mock, Arabic as a first language at Diploma level: the number of students taking each in any one community is small, so the number of local specialists is smaller. Removing the drive removes the geographic filter and leaves only the subject filter, which is the one that matters.

We also disclose when a specialist is not available rather than substituting. If the first Chemistry HL opening in your preferred slot is nine days away, we say so and give the date. If the specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say that before you book. No competitor page in our research discloses either.

sections.heading: What subject-level tuition costs in this market
paragraphs: Lead with the monthly figure, because that is what a family budgets. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Diploma student with one weekly session in two subjects sits at the upper end of that range for most of DP2.

Converted to hours, the Dubai market bands are these. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led at AED 500-650 or more, with BartyED at AED 650. All read in October 2026.

Context is worth adding. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family whose school fee is flat, a tutoring decision is a marginal decision rather than a compounding one.

These are market rates, not our prices. We do not publish a price list on these pages; we start with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many hours the specific goal requires, which for a technique problem is often far fewer than a package assumes.

sections.heading: The regulators, the permit, and what to verify
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah has SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by none of the competitors in our research, which tells you how shallow this layer of the market is.

For individual tutors, the relevant instrument is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The MoHRE service page lists a two-working-day completion time via the app, website or e-services system.

u.ae states that individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct with a similar restriction.

IB Gram is not IB authorised, KHDA approved, ADEK approved or Cambridge accredited, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and has no UAE office. We explain what each body does and link its own page. On a subject-led page the verification that matters most is simpler: ask the tutor which syllabus version they teach, which mark scheme they last marked against, and to talk you through one question in the trial lesson.

sections.heading: Judging a subject tutor in one trial lesson
paragraphs: A free trial lesson is the only evidence worth having, and twenty minutes of it is enough if you know what to listen for. The first signal is whether the tutor asks for a recent script before teaching anything. A specialist wants to see what the student actually wrote, because that is where the diagnosis is. A generalist asks which topic to cover.

The second signal is mark-scheme language. Ask the tutor what the mark scheme awards for a specific question your child got wrong. A specialist answers in marks and criteria: this line earns the method mark, this one does not, the band descriptor needs a judgement here. Somebody teaching from a textbook answers in content, which sounds competent and does not move a grade.

The third is the honest no. Ask whether they can get your child from a 4 to a 7 by May. The right answer names what is achievable and what is not, and refuses to promise a grade. Anybody who promises a specific score is either misunderstanding how the Diploma is marked or betting your money on it. We do not make grade promises and will say so directly if asked.

The fourth is the coursework boundary. Ask what they would do with a draft Internal Assessment. The answer should be feedback against criteria on work the student wrote. If the answer involves rewriting, supplying text, or producing anything, end the conversation there, because that is the risk sitting on your child's record rather than on the tutor's.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB tutor living near Dubai Production City?
faqs.answer: Some, and fewer than the search results suggest. There is no IB World School inside the community, so Diploma teachers are concentrated at the campuses that run the Diploma, in Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha and the southern corridor. Standard Level Mathematics is findable locally. Chemistry at Higher Level with current knowledge of the scientific investigation criteria, free at half past five on a weekday, is a much narrower ask. That is why we teach online: it removes the geographic filter and leaves the subject filter, which is the one with any bearing on the grade.

faqs.question: What single change improves my child's Diploma marks fastest?
faqs.answer: Command-term discipline, in almost every case. A student who writes a paragraph for a two-mark state question spends four minutes earning two marks and runs out of time later. A student who describes an outcome when the question says explain scores nothing, because the mark scheme awards the named principle rather than the observation. Both errors are invisible in classwork. Both are fixable in two or three sessions, and the skill transfers across all six subjects, which is why we start past-paper work there rather than with content revision.

faqs.question: How much of a science grade is the scientific investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Around twenty per cent, as a single piece of internally assessed work completed during the course. That makes it the most controllable part of the grade and the easiest to cap accidentally. A weak research question in DP1 constrains the data analysis, the conclusion and the evaluation criteria that follow, and no amount of past-paper work in the spring recovers it. This is why Internal Assessment supervision in DP1 is often a better purchase than exam technique in DP2, and why we ask which component is weakest before suggesting any hours.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 in Maths AA HL and why does it catch people out?
faqs.answer: It is two extended problem-solving questions, worth roughly a fifth of the Higher Level grade, and it examines a skill the rest of the course does not practise: reading an unfamiliar mathematical structure, working out what is being asked, and starting anyway. Students who have only ever met questions that resemble their textbook freeze on it. The fix is specific practice on starting, not more content. We work through the opening two minutes of unfamiliar problems repeatedly, because that is the part where the paper is won or lost.

faqs.question: Can you explain what the IA criteria letters actually require?
faqs.answer: Yes, and reading them early changes the work substantially. A science investigation is assessed across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and research design constrains everything after it: a question that cannot produce enough variation makes the later criteria hard to satisfy. A Mathematics exploration is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, where personal engagement means visible evidence of the student's own thinking rather than an enjoyable topic. We teach the descriptors and give feedback on the student's drafts, and we never write any part.

faqs.question: Does marking against a mark scheme really differ from using a model answer?
faqs.answer: Substantially. A model answer shows a student what a good response looks like. A mark scheme shows them which specific marks their own script earned and which it missed, line by line. The second produces improvement because it is diagnostic; the first mostly produces admiration. Marking properly also reveals the category of the problem: command-term misreads, a specific content gap, or pacing. Those three need completely different interventions, and a student working from model answers will usually guess wrong about which one they have.

faqs.question: How should a commuting student structure past-paper practice?
faqs.answer: Short and frequent rather than long and occasional. A Production City Diploma student on a bus to Al Barsha is home around half past four and has limited evening attention, so two timed questions on a Tuesday are worth more than a three-hour paper on a Saturday nobody has energy for. Sequence matters too: topic questions while the content is fresh, then whole sections under timing, then full papers late in the process. A full paper attempted early mostly teaches a student that they cannot yet sit a full paper.

faqs.question: How many of the 45 points come from the Extended Essay and TOK?
faqs.answer: Up to three points on the 45-point scale, awarded from a published matrix that combines the two grades. Three points crosses most university offer thresholds, and it is earned by writing done in DP1 and the first term of DP2 rather than in the exam hall. The pattern we see in this cluster is a capable science student who treats both as administration, finishes them late, and then spends spring revision time writing what should have been complete in the autumn. Finishing the Extended Essay early is the cheapest grade gain available.

faqs.question: What does Diploma subject tuition cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Converted to hours, the IB specialist band sits around AED 200-450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Those are market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to their publishers, not our price list. We start with a free trial lesson and work out how many hours the specific problem actually needs.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and the criteria letters confuse us both. Help?
faqs.answer: The MYP assesses four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. The letters refer to skills rather than topics: in the sciences, Criterion B is inquiring and designing and Criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science. The marks students most often leave behind are communication marks rather than content marks, because they know the answer and present it in a form the descriptor does not reward. Once a student reads the descriptor for the band above theirs, the gap is usually obvious and quick to close.

faqs.question: Can you supply IB mark schemes and grade boundary tables for us?
faqs.answer: No. IB papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables are copyright material and we do not reproduce or distribute them. We reference the official source, link to it, and work with papers your child or their school already holds legitimately. Any provider offering you a library of mark schemes is distributing material they do not own, which should make you ask what else they are casual about. Your school's subject teachers can supply past papers through the proper channel, and that is the route to use.

faqs.question: How do I check in a trial lesson whether a tutor really knows the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Does the tutor ask to see a recent marked script before teaching anything? Can they explain a specific lost mark in mark-scheme language, naming which line earns the method mark? Do they refuse to promise a grade when you ask directly? And what would they do with a draft Internal Assessment, where the only acceptable answer is feedback against criteria on work the student wrote? A specialist passes all four in twenty minutes. Somebody teaching from a textbook will sound competent on content and fail the second.

faqs.question: Do UAE Diploma students sit the May session or November?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates on these pages because the IB's own site blocks automated verification, and a date a parent plans around has to be correct; confirm exact windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. What does not move is the sequence: subject choices, Extended Essay question, Internal Assessment data collection, core essays, mocks in the winter term, internal uploads in the spring, then the written papers. Working backwards through that list is more useful than any single date.

faqs.question: What happens if no Computer Science HL specialist is free?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give you a date rather than a substitute. Computer Science HL is a small-cohort subject, so the specialist pool is genuinely limited and a wait of five to ten days is realistic. The alternative, putting a general programmer in front of a student who needs the solution development criteria and the HL options, wastes your money and the student's term. If the available specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book. No competitor page in our research discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Does your tutor come to our address in IMPZ for a subject session?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. On a subject-led page that is the point rather than a caveat: the local evening pool filters tutors by who can reach IMPZ by six, and the Dubai travel premium of roughly AED 50-150 an hour is that filter expressed as money. Independent home tutors do work in this area and for a younger child needing physical supervision they can be right. For Higher Level subject precision, the drive is what you are paying to remove.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics HL and Maths AA HL for my son?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, but we would rather not, and the reason is mark schemes. Physics HL rewards uncertainty treatment and named principles in explain questions; Maths AA HL Paper 3 rewards structural reading and visible method. Those are different marking cultures, and a tutor fluent in both is rarer than a tutor who is good at both subjects. Two specialists at one session each a week usually produces more than one person at two sessions. If budget makes a single tutor necessary, we will say which of the two subjects they are genuinely strongest in.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-producti.closingHeading: Judge the subject knowledge, not the postcode
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-producti.closingBody: The search put distance first because that is what search engines can measure. The Diploma measures something else: whether a student reads the command term, structures the answer to the band descriptor, treats uncertainty in the language the mark scheme uses, and chose a research question their data could actually support. All of that is subject knowledge, and none of it is improved by the tutor living closer to IMPZ. Send a recent marked script, take a free trial lesson, and use twenty minutes of it to check whether the person can explain one lost mark properly. That single test tells you more than any profile.

intro.heading: The Diploma is two years long and very unevenly loaded
paragraphs: Families in Dubai Silicon Oasis usually start searching at one of three moments. The first is early in DP1, when a capable student suddenly brings home grades they have never seen before. The second is the February or March of DP2, when several internal deadlines land in the same fortnight and the household stops functioning. The third is roughly ten weeks before the May examinations, when somebody realises how much of the grade is still unprepared.

Those three moments need entirely different things, and the mistake is treating them as the same request. The first is usually about adjusting to external examination standards and to the volume of independent reading, which is a term of adjustment rather than a crisis. The second is a scheduling problem dressed up as an academic one. The third is a consolidation job with a hard ceiling on what can be achieved.

What makes the Diploma hard to plan is that the calendar is not published in one place. The board sets the examination windows and the upload deadlines. The school sets the internal deadlines for every subject's internal assessment, the Extended Essay milestones, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay dates, and the mock window. The student discovers them one at a time, usually a week before each. A parent who collects all of them in September has an enormous advantage.

We publish no IB examination or results dates on this page, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and an unverified date that a family plans around is worse than no date at all. UAE schools sit the May examinations. Your child's IB coordinator holds the real windows, and the internal deadlines are the ones that drive tuition timing anyway.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis, Cedre Villas, Academic City, The Villa and Nad Al Sheba, lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For calendar work that matters: when a deadline moves or a mock week shifts, a session can be rescheduled in a message, which a visiting arrangement in this corridor cannot absorb nearly as easily.

The rest of this page is the calendar in detail. What each term of DP1 and DP2 is for. Why February is congested and what to do about it. How the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge timelines run underneath the subjects. What mocks are actually for. And what the final ten weeks can and cannot deliver, which is the single most useful thing to know before buying anything.

One more framing. A calendar plan is usually a smaller plan placed better rather than a larger one. Families who read the two years properly often buy fewer total hours than those who arrive in February, because the DP1 blocks do the structural work cheaply and the final stretch is then free to do the only thing it is actually good at. The saving comes from the sequencing, not from negotiating a rate.

programmes.description: Six subjects begin in parallel, Theory of Knowledge starts, the Extended Essay is introduced and a supervisor allocated, and Creativity, Activity, Service begins accumulating. programmes.countryNote: DP1 is the block with runway, and it is the one families in this corridor habitually leave alone because nothing is yet failing. Structural work on reading volume, written reasoning and mathematical fluency belongs here, where there is time for it to become habit rather than information.

programmes.name: Diploma year two
programmes.description: Internal assessments fall due across every subject, the Extended Essay reaches submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay is written against a prescribed title, mocks are sat, and the May examinations follow. University applications overlay the first half of the year with their own deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: DP2 is where the congestion lives. The internal deadlines cluster because every subject sets one and the school places them within the board's windows, so three in a fortnight is routine rather than unlucky. A parent holding the full list in September can spread the work; one discovering them individually cannot.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is usually set in DP1 and due in DP2. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, and Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level. Paper 3 strategy is the component that responds least well to late preparation, so it belongs in the DP1 and early DP2 blocks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same exploration weighting and the same Higher Level Paper 3, with the calculator permitted throughout. The calendar risk here is different: statistics and modelling content often arrives late in the scheme of work, compressing it against the exploration deadline.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The scientific investigation carries a fifth of the grade and its school deadline is typically in DP2. Organic chemistry is usually taught late, which means it lands beside mocks and the investigation, and that collision is the reason chemistry requests spike in the second term.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Also carries a scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade, with the same deadline congestion. Nuclear and quantum physics is generally taught last, so it is met under time pressure, and uncertainty treatment is needed for both the investigation and Paper 1.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Large content volume spread across both years, with the investigation in DP2. The calendar risk is cumulative rather than acute: biology rewards steady revision and punishes a student who leaves it until the final block, because there is simply too much to compress.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is scheduled by the school, usually in DP2, and the Higher Level essay has its own deadline. Both are internal dates rather than board ones, and both are frequently placed in the same term as the science investigations.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of commentaries on published articles, written across both years rather than in one block. That makes it the most calendar-friendly internal assessment in the Diploma, provided the student does not leave all three commentaries until DP2.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A research project with its own internal deadline, plus Higher Level extension content. Students often underestimate how early the research has to begin, because the project depends on access to information about a real organisation.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed through the exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, the latter externally marked. The exhibition generally sits in DP1 and the essay in DP2, and the essay deadline is almost always inside the congested fortnight.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay with a school supervisor and staged milestones running from DP1 into DP2. Because its milestones are internal, they vary between schools, and they are the single most commonly underestimated item on the Diploma calendar.

sections.heading: The two-year calendar, term by term
paragraphs: Laid out properly, the Diploma stops looking like two undifferentiated years and starts looking like six blocks with distinct jobs. DP1 autumn is adjustment: six subjects beginning at once, Theory of Knowledge starting, and a student discovering that external examination standards are not Middle Years standards. DP1 spring is where the Extended Essay question should be settled and where mathematical and written fluency can still be built from the ground up.

DP1 summer term and the holiday after it are the most under-used stretch in the whole programme. Internal assessments have been introduced, the Extended Essay has a supervisor, and nothing is due. A student who uses that summer to get a first Extended Essay draft written and to finish one internal assessment arrives at DP2 with the congested fortnight already half dismantled. Almost nobody does this, and the families who do describe DP2 completely differently.

DP2 autumn carries university applications, the Theory of Knowledge essay against a prescribed title, and the beginning of internal assessment submissions. DP2 winter and early spring is the congestion: multiple internal deadlines, the Extended Essay final submission, and mocks, frequently overlapping. DP2 final block is consolidation before the May examinations, and it can do technique and nothing structural.

The table below is the shape to fill in with your own school's dates. Treat the final column as the honest answer to what tutoring can achieve in each block, because that is the column that determines whether money spent will do anything. A family that reads it in September of DP1 has roughly four times the options of one reading it in February of DP2.

sections.heading: Why February is congested, and what to do in September
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment, and the school places each one inside the board's windows. With six subjects plus the Extended Essay plus the Theory of Knowledge essay, that is eight substantial pieces of work with eight internal deadlines, and schools inevitably cluster several of them in the same part of DP2. Three deadlines in one fortnight is not bad luck. It is arithmetic, and it is predictable a year in advance.

The intervention that works is not more tutoring in February. It is collecting all eight dates in September of DP1, writing them on one page, and then moving whatever can be moved earlier. An Economics commentary can be written in DP1. A mathematics exploration topic can be chosen in DP1. An Extended Essay draft can exist by the end of the DP1 summer. None of that requires paid help; it requires knowing the dates.

Where paid help earns its place is at the front of each component rather than the back. One session narrowing a research question, one on a complete first draft, and nothing in between. A weak research question is cheap to fix in September and impossible to fix in February, because by then the data has been collected or the reading has been done. That asymmetry is the whole argument for front-loading.

There is also a triage version for families already inside the congestion. Put the eight items in order of marks at stake and of how much is already done, decide explicitly which one will be finished to a lower standard, and tell the student that decision has been made. Students collapse in that fortnight because they are trying to do everything well. A parent who removes that expectation changes the outcome more than an extra tutor would.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay timeline, which nobody respects early enough
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research essay with a supervisor at the school and staged milestones running from DP1 into DP2. Because every milestone is internal rather than set by the board, they vary between schools in this corridor, and because they are internal they are often treated by students as advisory. They are not: a missed interim milestone compresses everything after it.

The commonest failure is a research question that is too broad, chosen because it sounded serious, and not narrowed until a supervisor sees a draft. By then the reading has been done against the wrong question and much of it cannot be reused. Narrowing takes one conversation and belongs in DP1. It is the single highest-value hour available anywhere in the Diploma core, and it costs almost nothing.

The second failure is the reflection and process element being reconstructed at the end. Supervisors expect a record of how the thinking developed, and a record written from memory in DP2 reads exactly like one written from memory. Keeping it as the work proceeds is a habit rather than a skill, which is why establishing it in DP1 is worth more than any amount of help later.

The boundary here is absolute and it is where this market bends most often. A tutor may discuss the research question, explain what the assessment criteria reward, model a comparable essay on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation and referencing properly. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of it. The essay is declared as the student's own work.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge, and why it lands at the worst moment
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through the exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, with the essay externally marked. The exhibition generally sits in DP1 and the essay in DP2, and the essay deadline is almost always inside the congested fortnight, competing with internal assessments that feel more urgent because they belong to named subjects.

Students consistently underrate it for a structural reason: Theory of Knowledge has no content to revise, so it does not feel like a subject with work attached. What it has instead is a way of arguing, and that is built through practice rather than preparation. A student who has written two or three practice responses in DP1 writes a competent prescribed-title essay quickly. One who has written none finds the task genuinely alien.

The essay is written against a title released by the board, which means the specific question cannot be prepared in advance, and that is precisely why the general skill has to be. The skill is identifying knowledge claims, choosing areas of knowledge that genuinely illuminate the title, and using real examples rather than invented ones. All three are teachable, and all three take practice rather than explanation.

For a tutoring plan the implication is clear: Theory of Knowledge support belongs in DP1, cheaply, as practice, and in DP2 only as feedback on a draft the student has written. A family buying Theory of Knowledge help for the first time three weeks before the deadline is buying the hardest version of the task. A family that spent two hours on it in DP1 usually needs nothing in DP2 at all.

sections.heading: What mocks are actually for
paragraphs: Diploma mocks are marked by the school at no cost and they are the best diagnostic available in the two years. Most families read the predicted grade and respond emotionally to it. The grade is the least useful output. The useful output is the distribution of lost marks across components and the pattern of why they were lost, and extracting that takes about an hour and no subject expertise.

Sort every lost mark into five categories: did not know the content, knew it but ran out of time, misread what the command term required, knew it and wrote an answer that did not earn the marks, or lost it to presentation and working. Count the five. Nearly every student produces a heavily skewed result, and the largest category dictates what the final block should contain.

The categories map onto very different purchases. A content category means revision, which is the cheapest help available and can often be supervised rather than taught. A timing category means question selection and pacing, which moves fast. A command-term category is close to a single session. An answer-structure category is the most teachable thing on the list and the one that most often converts a 5 into a 6.

Mocks are also the right moment to cut. A subject that has stabilised since DP1 does not need the remaining months of weekly lessons, and redirecting that booking to whatever the mock newly exposed is free. Nobody in the market has an incentive to prompt that review, which is exactly why it belongs on a page like this one rather than in a sales conversation.

sections.heading: The final ten weeks, honestly
paragraphs: Ten weeks before the May examinations is when the largest share of Diploma tutoring in Dubai is bought, and it is the block with the hardest ceiling. What it reliably delivers is technique: command-term reading, extended-response structure, timing and question selection, working layout, and consolidation of content the student has already met. Those are real marks and they are frequently worth a grade boundary.

What it does not deliver is fluency or coverage. A Higher Level mathematics student who cannot manipulate algebra confidently in March will still hesitate in May. A chemistry student who has never understood organic mechanisms cannot acquire mechanistic reasoning in ten weeks, because that is pattern recognition built through exposure over months. A physics student who has avoided uncertainty treatment all year can learn the procedures, and that is one of the few structural-looking gaps that is genuinely closable late.

So a final-block plan should be built from an explicit list of what is in scope and what is not, and the student should be told which is which. Plans that quietly include an impossible goal produce a sense of failure rather than progress, and they are also the plans that end with a family concluding tutoring does not work. Naming the ceiling is the thing that makes the block succeed.

One practical note about intensity. A student revising at maximum intensity in the last two weeks arrives at the papers depleted, and the marginal topic learned in that fortnight is worth less than the alertness lost. The plans that work taper: heavier at weeks ten to four, lighter at three to one, with the final week spent on an error tally rather than on new material.

sections.heading: Creativity, Activity, Service and the time nobody budgets
paragraphs: Creativity, Activity, Service runs across both Diploma years with its own requirements and its own reflective record. It is not graded like a subject, which leads students to treat it as optional until a deadline appears, and then it consumes evenings in exactly the fortnight when internal assessments are due. That is a calendar problem rather than an academic one and it is entirely avoidable.

The avoidance is straightforward: ask the coordinator what the requirements and the checkpoints are, in September of DP1, and put them on the same page as the eight academic deadlines. A student who accumulates experiences and writes reflections as they happen spends very little time on it. One who reconstructs a two-year record in DP2 spends a great deal, at the worst possible moment.

University applications belong in the same category of invisible load. For a DP2 student applying overseas, the autumn term carries personal statements, references and institutional deadlines that have nothing to do with the Diploma and compete directly with the Theory of Knowledge essay and the first internal assessment submissions. Families who map those dates alongside the academic ones in September avoid the collision.

The honest point for a tutoring page is that neither of these is something to buy help with. They are things to schedule. A parent who collects every date from the coordinator in September of DP1 and keeps them on one page has done more for the outcome than several hundred dirhams of tuition would, and it is free. That is worth saying even though it does not sell an hour.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Silicon Oasis, and the limits we state
paragraphs: Send four things: the subject and level, which block of the calendar you are in, the school's internal deadline list if you have it, and the hour your child is realistically at a desk. If you do not have the deadline list, ask the coordinator for it before you ask us for anything, because it changes what we would recommend more than any other single input.

We match a tutor to the subject and level and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost. Afterwards you receive a written note setting out which gaps are reachable in the block you are in and which needed an earlier one. If you are calling in March about a Higher Level fluency problem, the note will say so plainly and propose what the remaining weeks can actually do.

The limits. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch and we claim none. We hold no IB, regulator or board approval. We do not supply subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or Extended Essay exemplars as downloads, because reproducing them is not ours to do; we reference them and link to the official source.

And no dates presented as authority. We publish no IB examination or results dates anywhere on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date a family plans around is the worst error a tutoring page can make. UAE schools sit the May examinations. Your child's IB coordinator holds the real windows, and the internal calendar is what should drive your spending anyway.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai Silicon Oasis family start IB Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: DP1 if the weakness is structural, because that is the only part of the programme with enough runway to turn information into habit. Mathematical fluency, written reasoning that names a mechanism, and reading volume all need months. Technique, command terms and timing can wait until DP2 and still move marks. Most families do the reverse, spending nothing in DP1 and a great deal in the spring of DP2, which is the most expensive distribution available.

faqs.question: Why do so many IB deadlines land in the same fortnight?
faqs.answer: Because six subjects each carry an internal assessment, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay add two more, giving eight substantial pieces of work placed by the school inside the board's windows. Clustering is arithmetic rather than misfortune, and it is predictable a year in advance. The fix is to collect all eight dates in September of DP1 and move earlier whatever can move, which costs nothing but knowing the dates.

faqs.question: What should we do with the DP1 summer holiday?
faqs.answer: Get a first Extended Essay draft written, and finish one internal assessment. It is the most under-used stretch in the entire Diploma: internal assessments have been introduced, a supervisor is allocated, and nothing is due. A student who arrives at DP2 with an Extended Essay draft in hand has dismantled half the congested fortnight before it starts. Families who use that summer describe the second year in completely different terms from those who do not.

faqs.question: How much can tutoring achieve in the ten weeks before the May exams?
faqs.answer: Technique reliably: command-term reading, extended-response structure, timing, question selection and working layout, plus consolidation of content already met. Uncertainty treatment in the sciences is also genuinely closable late because the procedures are finite. What ten weeks cannot do is build algebraic fluency or organic mechanistic reasoning, both of which are habits formed over months. A good plan names which of your gaps sit on which side of that line.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near Silicon Oasis who understands the internal deadlines?
faqs.answer: The question to ask is whether a prospective tutor requests the school's internal deadline list in the first conversation. Someone who has worked with Diploma students in Dubai asks for it unprompted, because the internal calendar governs everything. Someone who starts teaching the current topic without asking has told you how they work. Local supply is thin in any case: IB enrolment was 7 per cent of Dubai's private market in 2024-25, and Higher Level specialists are thinner still.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to homes in Silicon Oasis or Nad Al Sheba?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For calendar-driven Diploma work the online format has a concrete advantage: when an internal deadline moves or a mock week shifts, the session can be rescheduled in a message. Along this corridor, where journeys run twenty-five to forty minutes in the late afternoon, a visiting arrangement cannot absorb that kind of change nearly as easily.

faqs.question: At what point in DP1 should a Silicon Oasis student narrow their EE question?
faqs.answer: In DP1, before serious reading begins. The commonest failure is a question too broad, chosen because it sounded serious, and not narrowed until a supervisor sees a draft, by which point the reading has been done against the wrong question and much of it cannot be reused. Narrowing takes one conversation and is the highest-value hour available anywhere in the Diploma core. The process record should also be kept as the work proceeds, not reconstructed later.

faqs.question: Why do students underestimate Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Because it has no content to revise, so it does not feel like a subject with work attached. What it has is a way of arguing, built through practice rather than preparation. The prescribed-title essay is written against a title released by the board, so the specific question cannot be prepared, which is exactly why the general skill must be. Two or three practice responses in DP1 remove most of the DP2 difficulty, and the essay deadline usually sits in the congested fortnight.

faqs.question: How should we use my child's Diploma mock results?
faqs.answer: Sort every lost mark into five categories: did not know the content, ran out of time, misread the command term, knew it and wrote an answer that did not earn the marks, or lost it to presentation and working. Count the five. Nearly every student is heavily skewed, and the largest category dictates the final block. It takes about an hour, needs no subject expertise, and is more useful than any paid assessment.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Internal Assessment under deadline pressure?
faqs.answer: With the thinking and with feedback, yes; with the writing, never, and no deadline changes that. A tutor may press on a research question, explain each lettered criterion, model a comparable example on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or supply any part of it. The work is declared as the student's own and moderated by the IB.

faqs.question: Does Creativity, Activity, Service really take up study time?
faqs.answer: It does when it is reconstructed rather than recorded. CAS runs across both years with its own requirements and reflective record, and because it is not graded like a subject students leave it until a checkpoint appears, usually in the fortnight when internal assessments are due. Ask the coordinator for the requirements and checkpoints in September of DP1 and put them on the same page as the academic deadlines. Recorded as it happens, it costs very little time.

faqs.question: Do university applications clash with the Diploma calendar?
faqs.answer: For DP2 students applying overseas, yes, and the clash is in the autumn term. Personal statements, references and institutional deadlines compete directly with the Theory of Knowledge essay and the first internal assessment submissions, and none of it appears on the academic calendar the school hands out. Mapping application dates alongside the eight academic deadlines in September avoids the collision, and it is a scheduling exercise rather than something to buy help with.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to find a specialist for near Academic City?
faqs.answer: Chemistry at Higher Level first, then Physics at Higher Level, then Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, with Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge process coaching close behind. The reason is the same in each case: a small Diploma teaching pool divided by subject and by level, then reduced again by who is free in the late-afternoon window. Economics, Business Management, humanities and languages are noticeably better served.

faqs.question: Why do you not publish IB exam dates on this page?
faqs.answer: Because the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and an unverified date that a family plans around is the worst error a tutoring page can make. UAE schools sit the May examinations. Your child's IB coordinator holds the real windows and the internal deadlines, and it is the internal calendar that should drive your spending in any case.

faqs.question: What should the first month of a Diploma plan actually produce?
faqs.answer: A single page carrying every internal deadline, which most families do not have and which changes decisions more than any lesson. A written note saying which gaps are reachable in the block you are currently in and which needed an earlier one. And one measurable technique change, most often in extended-response structure or in timing. No grade prediction, because nobody can honestly give one this early or at all.

Then send us the subject, the level and the block you are in. intro.heading: Why a radius is the wrong way to find an IB tutor in Dubai South
paragraphs: A near-me search is a geography query. It returns whoever is close. For most services that is the right instinct: a plumber's skill does not vary with the subject of the leak. The IB Diploma is the opposite case. It is six separate courses, each with its own published subject guide, its own command terms, its own internally assessed component and its own markbands. A tutor who is excellent at Biology Standard Level is not, by that fact, any use to a Chemistry Higher Level candidate. Distance tells you nothing about which of those a person can teach.

For a family in Dubai South the radius filter bites harder than it would in Jumeirah or Al Barsha, simply because the residential density that supports a deep local tutor market is still building out here. Dubai South, Emaar South and the communities around Dubai Investments Park are newer. A near-me search from The Pulse or Expo Golf Villas returns a short list, and the people on it are selected by their willingness to drive the southern corridor at 17:00 rather than by what they have taught.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Dubai South students are taught live, one-to-one, over video, with their own marked script on screen and the official markband beside it. Stating that plainly is the point: a page that implies a car will arrive at a Dubai South villa is misdescribing what it sells. What the online model buys instead is access to the person who teaches that subject guide every week, wherever they happen to live.

The rest of this page is about the material that specialist actually works with. The IB publishes its command terms and defines each one: analyse, evaluate, justify, outline, state, suggest, discuss. Those verbs are not stylistic. They determine the length, structure and content of a correct answer, and misreading one costs the whole question. Alongside them sit the markbands, which are the descriptive bands an examiner matches a long answer against. Students who have never read a markband are writing blind, and most have never read one.

One factual note so expectations are right. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually and publishes the ratings. KHDA does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership, and runs no UAE centre. For individual tutors the real credential is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Ask to see it. It is a legal licence to teach privately rather than a statement about teaching quality, so the second question is always which subject guide at which level the holder has actually taught, and for how many cohorts.
