dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-south.programmesIntro: Dubai South families ask about all three IB stages, with Diploma demand heaviest and Middle Years rising as Emaar South households move through secondary. Each note below is specific to this part of the emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, labelled A to D, each marked 0 to 8 and then converted to a 1-7 grade. The criteria are not the same across subject groups: in Sciences, criterion B is inquiring and designing and criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science, while in Individuals and Societies criterion B is investigating. A student can know the content thoroughly and still sit in the middle bands because the process criteria were never taught explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in the Dubai Investments Park cluster usually continue into the Diploma at the same school. The transition that hurts is assessment style rather than content: criterion marking rewards reflection and communication, while Diploma Paper 1 rewards accuracy under time. Naming that difference in Year 11 rather than Year 12 is worth more than any amount of extra content coverage.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, each graded 1 to 7, plus up to three bonus points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, giving a maximum of 45. The Diploma requires 24 points and a set of pass conditions that catch students who ignore the core. Each subject's internal assessment is worth 20% to 25%, which is the proportion a student can secure months ahead of the papers.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai South Diploma candidates sit the May session, the session UAE schools use. The dates that govern a Year 13 autumn are the school coordinator's internal deadlines for the internal assessment and Extended Essay, not the examination window. A tutoring plan built around examinations alone will arrive after those deadlines have already passed.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary, organised around units of inquiry, with continuous descriptive assessment rather than grades. Parents arriving from a system with termly examinations often cannot tell whether a child is behind. The three things that transfer into later success are number fluency, reading stamina and the ability to structure a written explanation, and tutoring at this stage is short, frequent and built on those.
programmes.countryNote: Primary Years children in Dubai private schools also take KHDA's mandatory subjects alongside the inquiry units. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are compulsory whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in several of them. Families moving into Emaar South frequently learn this at enrolment rather than before it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It suits a student who wants Diploma-standard academics in a narrow set of subjects alongside a vocational specialism. Tutoring demand falls almost entirely on the Diploma courses within it and on the reflective project's argument structure.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is uncommon in this part of Dubai, so a family whose child is on it has nobody nearby to compare notes with. That isolation has a cost in the reflective project, where parents cannot judge whether a draft is on track. A specialist who has supervised the component elsewhere resolves it, and online delivery is the only route to one from Dubai South.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects Dubai South families request most. Each note names the command terms or markband feature that decides the grade, rather than restating the syllabus title.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Mathematics uses its own command set: show that, hence, deduce, verify. Hence signals that the previous part must be used, and ignoring it loses method marks even when the answer is right. Paper 1 is non-calculator, so hand algebra is the deciding skill. The exploration is marked on five criteria, two of which reward process rather than mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with statistics, modelling and finance carrying the weight. Marks are lost not on calculation but on interpretation: stating a hypothesis, justifying the choice of model, explaining what a correlation coefficient means in the context given. Higher Level adds graph theory and matrices, both of which reward drilled procedure.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Determine, estimate and deduce each demand something different in physics, and Paper 1 gives no method credit at all. Paper 2 rewards structure, graph work and an uncertainty stated to a defensible number of significant figures. Higher Level adds fields and quantum phenomena. The investigation needs a measurable independent variable and real uncertainty analysis.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Deduce and explain are the high-tariff verbs, and a mechanism drawn with an arrow starting in the wrong place earns nothing. Multi-step calculations punish early rounding, because the error propagates to a final answer carrying most of the marks. The data booklet is permitted and most candidates have never located anything in it before the paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides the grade more than recall does. Outline, describe, explain and suggest demand different lengths and structures, and writing an explanation where outline was asked spends time without gaining credit. Higher Level adds plant biology and physiology depth that reward structured note-making over rereading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, and the markband for an evaluation question specifically rewards a judgement supported by the diagram rather than a list of advantages and disadvantages. Higher Level adds quantitative questions. The internal assessment is three 800-word commentaries, each applying one syllabus unit to a news article, and summarising the article scores nothing.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 prints a guided question above the passage and the markbands reward answering it. Candidates who write a general appreciation lose the top bands regardless of the quality of their prose. The individual oral links a global issue to one literary and one non-literary text; Higher Level adds the essay at 1,200 to 1,500 words.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Higher Level sits a pre-released case study for Paper 2, which rewards months of structured preparation. Tools such as Ansoff and investment appraisal must be applied to the named firm, not described. The Higher Level internal assessment is a 1,800-word research project based on primary research into a real organisation.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Examine and evaluate carry the highest tariff, and both require a judgement rather than coverage. Case-study specificity is what separates bands: a named place with figures beats a generic example every time. The fieldwork internal assessment needs a question answerable with data the student can actually collect.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The examination uses the IB's own pseudocode notation rather than any real language, and candidates who have coded only in Python lose marks on syntax they never practised. Trace tables are reliable marks and rarely drilled. The internal assessment is a solution for a real client with documented design, so the client conversation has to happen.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on one of six prescribed titles plus an exhibition of three objects with commentaries. The essay fails when it discusses the topic rather than the knowledge question in the title. Together with the Extended Essay it carries up to three bonus points, which students regularly discard and then finish short of their offer.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent essay in one Diploma subject, marked on five criteria with critical thinking carrying twelve of the available marks. The usual failure is a research question too broad to answer in the word limit. A supervisor may give substantive feedback on one complete draft; writing any part of it is malpractice.

sections.heading: What a near-me search returns in Dubai South, and what it filters out
paragraphs: Run the search honestly and look at what the result set is selected on. A near-me query ranks by proximity and by whoever has done enough local optimisation to appear in a map pack. Neither signal has anything to do with whether the person has taught Chemistry Higher Level. For Dubai South the problem compounds, because the list is short to begin with: this is a newer district and the local supply of subject teachers is thinner than in the Jumeirah or Al Barsha belt.

The arithmetic a parent is unknowingly performing is this. Start with everyone who can teach Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level. Remove everyone who will not drive to Dubai South for a single evening session. Remove everyone whose free slot does not match your child's. What remains is the pool a near-me search is choosing from, and at each step the cut is made on logistics rather than on competence. For a Standard Level subject the pool is wide enough that the cuts do not hurt. For a Higher Level science, Computer Science or Arabic B, they remove almost everyone.

Online delivery removes only the second cut, but that is the expensive one. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so there is no pretence of presence here; the trade is stated openly. What you get in exchange is the first pool rather than the third: a tutor matched to the subject guide and the level your child is actually sitting. The table sets out how that changes by subject, which is a more useful comparison than any claim about quality.

sections.heading: Command terms: the verbs that decide the answer
paragraphs: The IB publishes definitions for the command terms used across its subject guides, and the definitions are operative rather than decorative. State requires no justification. Outline requires a brief account. Describe requires a detailed account. Explain requires reasons or causes. Discuss requires a balanced review with evidence on both sides. Evaluate requires a judgement with the strengths and limitations weighed. A student who writes a balanced discussion where state was asked has spent four minutes to earn one mark.

This is the single most common reason a competent student scores mid-band. Content knowledge is present; the answer is simply the wrong shape for the verb. It is also among the easiest things to fix, because the terms are a finite published list and a student can learn what each one demands in a handful of sessions. The surprising part is how few students have ever been shown the list. They have been taught the subject and left to infer the grammar of the examination.

The table below gives the verbs that cost the most marks across the subjects Dubai South families ask about. Use it with a marked script: take any answer that scored below its band and check whether the shape matches the verb. More often than not it does not, and the fix is structural rather than academic. A tutor working this way can shift a script a band without teaching any new content, which is also why a diagnostic first session matters more than an impressive subject CV.

sections.heading: How a past-paper session actually runs
paragraphs: Most tutoring sessions are explanations. The tutor talks, the student nods, the hour feels productive and the next script comes back the same. A script-led session inverts that. The student's marked work is on screen with the official markband next to it, and the first twenty minutes are spent establishing, answer by answer, where the written response fell short of the band. Not whether the student understood the topic, which they usually did, but what the band required that the answer did not contain.

The second half is production under conditions. A short timed section from the same component, written while the tutor watches the pacing rather than the content. Timing is the hidden variable in most underperformance: a student who writes well and slowly loses the last question in every paper, and that pattern is invisible in untimed homework. Measuring it takes one session and changes what the remaining sessions are for.

Between sessions the student completes a set section and marks it themselves against the scheme before sending it. Self-marking is uncomfortable and it is where the learning sits, because reading a markband while holding your own answer forces the comparison the examiner will make. The tutor then checks the self-marking at the start of the next session, which surfaces a second category of error: students who award themselves marks for things the band does not credit. That diagnosis is unavailable any other way, and it is the reason the homework is self-marking rather than simply answering questions. A student who can audit their own script against a published band has acquired the skill that keeps improving after the sessions stop.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what actually changes
paragraphs: Parents are often told Higher Level is harder, which is true and unhelpful. What matters is how it is harder, because that determines how many weeks of support a student needs and in which component. Higher Level adds syllabus content, but it also adds a paper in the sciences, shifts the weightings, and raises the analytical demand of the markbands at the top end. Those are four different changes and they need four different responses.

The extra content is the easiest to plan for: it is listed in the subject guide and can be covered. The extra paper is harder, because Paper 3 in the sciences examines a different skill set — data analysis and the option topic — and students frequently prepare for it last. The weighting shift matters because the internal assessment stays at 20% while the external papers redistribute, so a weak paper costs more at Higher Level than the same weakness costs at Standard. The markband shift is the subtlest: top bands at Higher Level reward evaluation and synthesis that Standard Level bands do not require.

For a Dubai South student the practical question is usually whether to drop a Higher Level subject to Standard. The table gives the comparison that conversation needs. The honest answer is that dropping is sometimes right and often done too late — a student struggling in three Higher Level subjects in the autumn of Year 13 has fewer options than one who made the same decision a year earlier. The university prerequisite is the deciding factor, because some courses specify Higher Level by name, and that should be checked before the subject is dropped rather than after.

sections.heading: Markbands and what an examiner is matching against
paragraphs: In the long-answer subjects, examiners do not add marks up from a list. They read the answer, decide which descriptive band it sits in, and then place it within that band. This is why two students with the same knowledge can receive different marks, and why a student who is used to point-scoring arithmetic finds the result arbitrary. It is not arbitrary. The bands are published and they describe specific qualities: the presence of a judgement, the use of evidence, the extent of the conceptual link.

The practical consequence is that adding more correct material to a mid-band answer does not necessarily move it. A Geography answer stuffed with accurate facts and no evaluation stays in the band below the one that requires a judgement, however many facts arrive. An Economics answer with four correct diagrams and no conclusion does the same. Students work harder and stay put, which is demoralising in a way that has nothing to do with ability.

Teaching this is straightforward once a student can read a band. The method is to take their own answer, read the band above where it was placed, and identify the single missing quality. Usually it is one of three: no judgement, no evidence tied to the claim, or no explicit link back to the question. The table names the pattern across the subjects this cluster asks about. A student who learns to audit their own writing this way becomes self-correcting, which is the only sustainable outcome tutoring can produce.

sections.heading: The core: three points most students leave on the table
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three bonus points to the Diploma total out of 45. Students treat them as administrative obligations because they are not subjects and nobody examines them in a hall. The arithmetic says otherwise. A student holding a conditional offer two points short has usually not lost those points in a paper; they have declined to collect them from the core, which was available months in advance and depended on planning rather than performance.

The Extended Essay is 4,000 words in one Diploma subject, marked on five criteria with critical thinking worth twelve marks on its own. The commonest failure is a research question too broad to answer in the word limit, which caps the mark before a word is written. Theory of Knowledge is a 1,600-word essay on one of six prescribed titles plus an exhibition of three objects with commentaries, and the essay fails when it discusses the topic instead of the knowledge question in the title.

Both are improvable with ordinary work, and both have a hard boundary. A supervisor or tutor may discuss the question, explain the criteria, and give substantive feedback on one complete draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit the work to completion. That limit is not a service restriction; it is the IB's academic-honesty rule, and a finding of malpractice falls on the student's Diploma rather than on the person who helped. Any provider offering a finished essay should be declined on that basis alone.

sections.heading: What a Dubai South family pays, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Lead with the premium, because that is the decision in front of a near-me searcher. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The difference between those bands is not teaching quality. It is a car on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at 16:30.

What the premium actually buys is presence and the parent's ability to observe from the next room. For a seven-year-old who will not sit at a screen, that is worth paying for. For a Diploma student working through a marked script against a published markband, it buys very little, because the material is two documents that read better shared on a monitor than passed across a table. The premium also costs flexibility: a visiting tutor fits one session an evening, so a household with two secondary children is choosing between them.

The monthly packages published in this market put the trade in plain numbers: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four in-home sessions of two hours. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, typically delivered by university students. At the top, TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for named premium tutors. Every figure here belongs to the provider named; these are market bands and not an IB Gram price list, and our own conversation starts with a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Grades 1 to 7, and what a point actually means
paragraphs: Each Diploma subject is graded 1 to 7 and the grade boundaries are set after each session, not published in advance, because they are adjusted to the difficulty of that session's papers. That is a genuinely useful fact for a parent, because it explains why last year's percentage threshold is not a target. What transfers between sessions is the relationship between components, not the raw mark needed.

The Diploma requires 24 points plus a set of pass conditions, which catch students who have the total but a failing grade in the wrong place. For university purposes the relevant number is usually a total plus specified subject grades: an offer of 36 points with 6 in Higher Level Chemistry is two separate requirements, and a student can hit the total and miss the offer. Reading an offer carefully in Year 12 changes which subject gets the tutoring hours.

The practical planning move is to work out where points are cheapest. One grade in a subject the student is close to a boundary in is cheaper than a grade in a subject they are two bands below. The three core points are usually the cheapest of all, because they depend on planning rather than examination performance. A session spent working out that arithmetic with a parent and a student is worth more than several spent teaching, and it is the conversation nobody has until the mock results arrive. The same calculation also settles whether a retake in November is worth entering, since a single subject grade is often all that separates a held offer from a lost one.

sections.heading: Fitting a session into a Dubai South evening
paragraphs: A plan that ignores the school run fails in week three. Dubai South and Emaar South households are usually home between 16:00 and 16:45 after a run into Dubai Investments Park or out to the Dubailand corridor. Green Community families manage 15:45. Dubai Production City families driving to Motor City are closer to 17:00. That spread sets the earliest realistic weekday slot anywhere between 16:00 and 17:30 depending on the street.

The second constraint is what a teenager can do after a full school day. A ninety-minute session at 16:30 immediately after a commute produces less than a sixty-minute session at 18:00 after a break and a meal. Families who book the earliest available slot because it is available often find attendance slipping by half term. The better pattern in this cluster is one weekday evening session between 17:00 and 19:30, with longer work moved to a weekend morning.

Weekend mornings are the underused resource. Internal assessment drafting, Extended Essay work and full timed papers all need uninterrupted stretches that a weekday evening cannot give. The UAE calendar supplies two more: the winter break and the spring break, when school workload drops to nothing and a student has more usable hours in a fortnight than in the six weeks either side. During Ramadan the pattern shifts again, with sessions moving after iftar and shortening, and content teaching giving way to timed practice, which costs less concentration per mark gained. Planning that shift in February rather than improvising it in March is what keeps a plan alive through the spring term in this cluster.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Chemistry Higher Level with a weak Paper 2 and a finished investigation is a different request from Chemistry Higher Level with strong papers and no investigation started. Naming the component means the first session is a diagnosis rather than an introduction, and it is the most useful thing a Dubai South parent can put in a first message.

process.title: Send the most recent marked script
process.description: A mock paper with the examiner's marks shows a specialist in five minutes what a conversation approximates in an hour. Where marks were lost is visible on the page, and so is whether the losses are content or technique. With no script, the first session produces one from a short timed section.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One full session, no charge, no card, taught by the person who would take the term. It returns a written diagnosis naming the command terms, topics and pacing problems found, and a plan for the first four sessions. A wrong match is rematched rather than persevered with.

process.title: Fix the slot around the actual school run
process.description: Not the earliest slot available, the one your child can work in. For most Dubai South households that is between 17:00 and 19:30 on a weekday, with weekend mornings held for internal assessment work and full timed papers. The slot is held for the term unless you move it.

process.title: Run the self-marking cycle
process.description: Work set at the end of each session, self-marked by the student against the official scheme, audited by the tutor at the start of the next. The audit catches a second category of error: marks the student awarded themselves for things the band does not credit. That diagnosis is not available any other way.

process.title: Recalculate after every mock
process.description: Mock results are the point at which the point arithmetic should be redone. Where is the cheapest grade? Is the core on track for its bonus points? Does the university offer require a named Higher Level subject the plan is not prioritising? Thirty minutes here redirects a term of hours.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the subject guide, not the map
whyPoints.description: The IB is six separate courses with six separate guides, and the relevant question is which of them a tutor has taught. Proximity answers a different question. Matching online means a Higher Level request from Emaar South is filled from the same pool as one from Jumeirah, which is where the near-me filter was costing a Dubai South family most.

whyPoints.title: Command terms and markbands taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Most competent students who score mid-band are writing the wrong shape of answer for the verb. The IB publishes the command-term definitions and the markbands, and a student who has read both writes differently. Teaching this takes a handful of sessions and shifts scripts without any new content.

whyPoints.title: Sessions anchored to the student's own script
whyPoints.description: The working documents are a marked paper and the official markband, open side by side on a shared screen. That arrangement is more legible than paper across a table, and it keeps every session tied to how marks are awarded rather than to how a topic is explained in a textbook.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty boundary is explicit
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach content, explain criteria by letter and give feedback on the student's own draft. They do not write, rewrite or edit coursework to completion. The limit is stated to the student at the first session, which protects the Diploma the family is paying to improve.

whyPoints.title: Thin availability is disclosed, not concealed
whyPoints.description: Diploma Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English A match within a few days. Computer Science Higher Level, Arabic B and Theory of Knowledge can take a week or more, and we say so with a date rather than seating a generalist in a specialist's chair. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership and operates no office in the UAE. The regulators appear on this page because explaining what they do is useful to a parent, not because the names add anything to us.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in Dubai South who can visit the house?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with their own marked script and the official markband shared on screen. Independent in-home tutors do work in this part of Dubai, and Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350 an hour. The trade is presence against specialism, and for a Higher Level Diploma subject the specialism is usually the scarcer thing.

faqs.question: Why does a near-me search return so few IB tutors in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Because Dubai South is a newer district and the resident supply of experienced subject teachers is thinner than in the older Jumeirah and Al Barsha school belt. A proximity-ranked search then cuts that short list further, by removing anyone whose free slot does not match yours. For a Standard Level subject the remaining pool is usually workable. For Chemistry or Physics at Higher Level, or for Computer Science and Arabic B, the proximity filter removes almost everybody who could actually teach the course.

faqs.question: What are IB command terms and why do they matter so much?
faqs.answer: They are the verbs the IB uses in examination questions, each with a published definition that determines the shape of a correct answer. State needs one line with no justification. Outline needs a brief account. Explain needs reasons. Discuss needs a balanced review with evidence. Evaluate needs a judgement with strengths and limitations weighed. A student who writes a balanced discussion where state was asked spends four minutes earning one mark. Most students have never seen the list, which makes it one of the fastest mark gains available to a competent candidate.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but keeps scoring in the middle band. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer is the wrong shape for the command term, or because it lacks the one quality the band above requires. In the long-answer subjects examiners place an answer in a descriptive band rather than totalling points, so adding more correct material to a mid-band answer does not necessarily move it. The missing quality is usually a judgement, evidence tied explicitly to the claim, or a direct link back to the question. Reading the band above their own mark with their own answer in hand fixes this faster than further teaching does.

faqs.question: How does a tutor use a past paper in a session?
faqs.answer: The marked script goes on screen with the official markband beside it, and the first part of the session establishes answer by answer what the band required that the writing did not contain. The second part is a short timed section written while the tutor watches pacing rather than content, because timing is invisible in untimed homework. Work is then set for the student to complete and self-mark against the scheme, and that self-marking is audited at the start of the next session, which surfaces marks the student awarded themselves wrongly.

faqs.question: Should my child drop a Higher Level subject to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision is usually made later than it should be. The deciding factor is the university prerequisite, because some courses specify a subject at Higher Level by name, so check the actual offers on the shortlist before dropping anything. Beyond that, the honest test is whether the student is a band below target in one component or across all of them. One weak component is a technique problem worth fixing; weakness across every component in three Higher Level subjects is a workload problem, and a student who faces it in Year 12 has far more options than one who faces it in Year 13.

faqs.question: How many points do Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay add?
faqs.answer: Up to three bonus points on top of the 42 available from six subjects, giving a maximum of 45. Students routinely treat the core as administrative because nobody examines it in a hall, and then finish two points short of a conditional offer. Those are usually the cheapest points on the table, because they depend on planning months in advance rather than on performance on one morning. The Extended Essay's critical thinking criterion alone is worth twelve marks, and a research question too broad to answer in 4,000 words caps the result before writing starts.

faqs.question: Why are IB grade boundaries not published in advance?
faqs.answer: Because they are set after each examination session and adjusted to the difficulty of that session's papers. A percentage that reached a 6 last year may not reach a 6 this year, and vice versa. What that means practically is that last year's threshold is not a target. The relationship between components does transfer, so a student can plan around the fact that the internal assessment is 20% of each subject and that one paper carries the largest external share. Aiming a clear band above the target rather than at it is the sensible response.

faqs.question: What time should a Dubai South session start on a school night?
faqs.answer: Later than the earliest available slot, in most cases. Households here are usually home between 16:00 and 16:45 after a run into Dubai Investments Park or the Dubailand corridor, and a ninety-minute session straight off that commute produces less than a sixty-minute session at 18:00 after a break. Green Community families can genuinely manage 16:00 because the school is minutes away; Dubai Production City families are closer to 17:30. Booking the slot a child can work in rather than the first one free is what keeps attendance intact past half term.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Theory of Knowledge essay?
faqs.answer: Within the IB's limits, yes. A tutor may discuss the prescribed title, help turn it into a workable knowledge question, explain the assessment criteria and what separates the bands, and give feedback on one complete draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit the essay to completion. The practical test is whether every sentence in the submitted document was composed by the student. A finding of malpractice falls on the student's Diploma, which is why any provider offering a finished essay should be refused outright.

faqs.question: Do I need more than one session a week for an IB subject?
faqs.answer: Usually not, outside an examination term. One session a week works when the cycle runs: diagnose in the session, practise and self-mark between sessions, audit at the start of the next. The limiting factor is how much independent practice a student can finish between sessions, not how much teaching they can sit through. Two a week makes sense when an internal assessment deadline and a mock paper collide, or in the four to six weeks before papers. More than two in one subject rarely pays, and adding a second subject before the first is stable usually slows both.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 add for a Higher Level science student?
faqs.answer: A separate skill set, examined separately, and usually prepared last. Paper 3 in the Higher Level sciences covers data analysis and the option topic rather than the core content of Papers 1 and 2, which means revising the core thoroughly does not prepare a student for it. Students who have built a plan around the main papers reliably arrive at Paper 3 underprepared and lose marks that were straightforwardly available. It needs its own block of sessions, placed deliberately rather than squeezed into the final fortnight with everything else.

faqs.question: Which schools do IB students in Dubai South attend?
faqs.answer: Most are in the Dubai Investments Park and Green Community cluster, where IB continuum, British and SABIS provision sit within minutes of one another, or travel east to the Dubailand corridor for an IB continuum school. The British-curriculum schools around Al Furjan and Jebel Ali run IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the Diploma. KHDA publishes annual inspection ratings for every one of them on its own site, which is the document worth reading before an admissions conversation. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named here.

faqs.question: Are IB tutors in Dubai licensed or approved by anyone?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private lessons need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. That is a legal licence to tutor, not a quality credential, and it says nothing about which subject guide the holder has taught. There is no such thing as a KHDA-approved tutor: KHDA oversees schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, which is a different instrument entirely. IB Gram holds no KHDA approval, accreditation or partnership and runs no UAE centre.

faqs.question: How do online IB lessons work in practice from Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Live video, one-to-one, with screens shared in both directions. The working documents are the student's own marked script and the published markband, open side by side and annotated as the session runs. Work is set at the end and audited at the start of the next session, and a short written note goes to the parent naming what was covered and the next target. A tablet with a stylus is helpful for mathematics and the sciences but not required; a phone camera over a worked page does the same job less comfortably.

faqs.question: What if no specialist in my child's subject is free this week?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a date rather than offering a substitute. Diploma Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English A usually match within a few days. Computer Science Higher Level, Arabic B and Theory of Knowledge are thinner and can take a week or more. Seating a general science tutor opposite a Chemistry Higher Level candidate costs a family money and a student confidence while teaching nothing the textbook would not have supplied. Where a wait is unworkable we propose a shorter block with a different specialist on the single most urgent component.

intro.heading: The search is about time, not distance
paragraphs: Nobody types 'near me' at the start of the school year. The phrase appears when something has already happened: a grade dropped in a report, a coursework deadline missed, a mock paper that came back worse than expected. The word 'near' is standing in for 'now'. Distance feels like the thing that will make help arrive quickly, and for a visiting tutor in Dubai Sports City it genuinely is.

Once lessons are delivered online, distance stops being the constraint and the calendar becomes the only real one. The question that decides whether a block works is how many weeks are left before the thing that matters, and what can honestly be achieved in them. Eight weeks will move a paper technique. Eight weeks will not rebuild two years of absent algebra. Both statements are useful; only one of them gets said by most providers.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a Sports City address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. What that means for a family in a hurry is that matching takes hours rather than days, because the pool is not restricted to people who can reach Victory Heights by six o'clock on a Tuesday.

It also changes what the first session is for. A diagnostic built around the calendar asks three questions: what is the next fixed date, what has to be true by then, and what is the gap. The answer produces a block with a measurable target — a Paper 1 score, an Internal Assessment criterion, a topic rebuilt — rather than an open-ended weekly hour that drifts to the end of term.

Dubai's Diploma students sit the May session, and the school's own internal deadlines are the dates that bind in practice. Because IB session and results dates could not be verified from the IB directly, this page does not publish any, and recommends confirming every one with the school's Diploma coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates, which many Sports City households are also working to, are sourced and stated below.

The rest of the page is a calendar: the Diploma year in phases, what each term is for, what eight weeks can achieve, where Ramadan and summer sit, and what the market charges when you buy tutoring by the term rather than by the hour. If you read one section, read the one on the fortnight after mocks. It contains the only free diagnostic a family gets all year, it needs no tutor to carry out, and almost nobody in Sports City does it, which is why the same marks get lost twice in the same subject within a single academic year.

sections.heading: What 'near me' means when the lesson arrives over video
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IB tutor near me in Dubai Sports City is asking for help that can start quickly and fit around a school week. IB Gram answers that with live one-to-one online lessons in Gulf Standard Time rather than with a visitor to a Sports City address. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and no UAE page here promises otherwise.

The irony of the phrase is that proximity slows things down. A visiting tutor has to be available in the right corridor on the right evening, which is a two-variable problem that often takes a week to solve and breaks the first time a fixture moves. Matching online removes one variable entirely, so a specialist for a named course and level can usually be proposed within a day, with the trial lesson in the same week.

Speed is worth more than it sounds in this context, because the searches happen at bad moments in the calendar. A family that finds a tutor in four days after mock results has eight working weeks before the spring; one that takes three weeks has five. The second block is a different piece of work with a lower ceiling, and most of the difference was spent waiting.

What does not change is the honesty about availability. Specialist supply in Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics tightens across every Dubai cohort at the same point in the year. Where nobody suitable is free, the answer is a stated wait or a referral elsewhere, because putting a general tutor into an eight-week exam block spends the one resource that cannot be replaced.

sections.heading: The Diploma year in four phases
paragraphs: A Diploma year is not a uniform stretch of time. It has four phases with different jobs, and knowing which phase a student is in tells you what tutoring should be doing. Treating September like March is the most common planning error in Sports City households, and it works in both directions: wasted months early and panic later.

Phase one, from the start of the academic year to the winter break, is for content and foundations. This is the only phase in which a genuine gap can be rebuilt without borrowing time from something else. Phase two, from January to the mock window, is for technique and for finishing internally assessed work. Phase three is the mocks themselves and the fortnight of review afterwards, which is the most information-dense part of the year.

Phase four is the run to the written papers, and the correct posture there is triage. Decisions about what not to revise are more valuable than extra hours, because the marks a student can still reach are a subset of the syllabus and the subset shrinks weekly. A plan that still aims at full coverage in the last six weeks will leave the recoverable marks undrilled.

The table below sets the phases against what should be finished by the end of each. It is deliberately written as a checklist rather than as advice, because the only useful version of this is one a parent can hold against their own child's position in November.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can honestly achieve
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the length most families ask about, usually because that is what sits between a mock result and the next fixed date. It is a real unit of work and it has a real ceiling. Within eight weekly sessions a student can change how they approach a paper, learn the command terms that recur in their courses, fix presentation habits that cost one or two marks per question, and rebuild two or three specific topics properly.

What eight weeks cannot do is teach a year of content, convert a Standard Level student into a Higher Level one, or repair algebraic foundations that were never laid. Providers who accept an eight-week booking for that work are selling hope. The honest version is to say what the block will target, say what it will leave untouched, and set the target in a form that can be measured at session four.

The arithmetic of marks matters here. Across six Diploma subjects, a habit that loses one mark per question costs more than a topic nobody understands. Units dropped before substitution, working held in a calculator instead of written down, an 'evaluate' question answered with a balanced list and no judgement — those are mechanical, teachable and fast. Content gaps are slow. A block with eight weeks should spend six of them on the fast category.

The exception is coursework. An Internal Assessment can move a long way in eight weeks, because the criteria are published, the mark ceilings are known, and most students have never read either. Teaching the criteria, having the student self-mark their own draft against them, and giving feedback on what they wrote is high-yield work. The tutor does not write, complete or produce any part of the submission; that boundary is an IB rule and breaking it is a malpractice finding against the student.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson dates a Dubai family can rely on
paragraphs: Many Sports City households are running an IGCSE student and a Diploma student at the same time, which means two calendars. The Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and verifiable, so they can be stated here. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.

The February/March series is offered to India only. A UAE candidate plans around June, with November as the resit route, and advice found online that references a February window is written for a different country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong version.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For the most recently completed cycles, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables before each series, so a school should always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

For the Diploma itself, this page publishes no dates. IB session and results dates could not be verified from the IB directly, and a wrong date on a page a parent acts on is worse than no date at all. Dubai Diploma students sit the May session; everything else — the exact window, the results day, the review-of-marking deadline — should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator and against the IB's own site.

sections.heading: What a term of tutoring costs, by the term rather than the hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a calendar-led decision, because what a family commits to is a block. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai table gives monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions: roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Over a three-month term those become AED 720 to 1,800, AED 1,800 to 3,600 and AED 3,000 to 6,000 or more respectively.

The hourly bands behind them are published too. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate puts specialist rates at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent tutors once travel is counted.

Packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. All of these are figures published by the providers named and read in October 2026. None is IB Gram's price list, and the reason for printing them is that most pages competing for this search publish no price at all.

The calendar reading is the useful one. A two-term rebuild bought at the mid band costs more in total than an eight-week specialist block but less per week, and it is the only version that fixes foundations. A pre-paper triage block is expensive per week and cheap in total because it is short. The error families make is paying mid-band rates for three terms of unmeasured weekly support, which costs the same as a rebuild and achieves what a triage block would have.

sections.heading: Ramadan, summer and the three windows families waste
paragraphs: Three parts of the Dubai academic year are routinely written off and should not be. The first is Ramadan. School days shorten and afternoon concentration drops, so the instinct is to pause. For Diploma students a session placed after Iftar generally produces more work than the same hour at four o'clock, and because lessons are online the slot can move without any journey being rearranged. Coursework process work suits the period better than timed papers.

The second is the long summer between the two Diploma years. It is the single largest block of uncommitted time a student will have, and it sits precisely at the point where first-year gaps are still cheap to fix. Six sessions across July and August, aimed at the two topics a student knows they never understood, removes a problem that would otherwise surface in a February mock.

The third is the fortnight immediately after mocks, which families spend being upset about the grades. That fortnight contains more diagnostic information than any other point in the year: a full set of papers, marked, with the student's own errors visible. Sorting those errors by cause rather than by subject produces the plan for the rest of the year. Left unexamined, the papers go in a drawer and the same marks are lost again in the spring.

Set against those three, the periods families do protect — the weeks immediately before a school assessment, the final fortnight before the papers — are the least movable. By then the work is triage. Spending the recoverable time earlier is the whole of good calendar planning, and it is why the first conversation here is about dates rather than about hours.

Summer between DP1 and DP2: six sessions on known gaps, cheaply
The fortnight after mocks: the richest diagnostic data of the year
The final fortnight: triage only, and expectations set accordingly

sections.heading: Mock season, and the review nobody does
paragraphs: Mocks exist to generate information, and most of that information is thrown away. A student receives six grades, a parent receives a report, and the papers themselves — which contain the actual evidence — go unread. The review that matters takes about ninety minutes per subject and produces a list of lost marks sorted by cause rather than by topic.

The categories are consistent across subjects. Content not known. Content known but not retrieved under time pressure. Command term misread, so a correct piece of knowledge answered the wrong question. Working not shown, so method marks were unavailable. Arithmetic, units or significant figures. Question not attempted because time ran out. Each category has a different remedy, and three of the six are faster to fix than any of them look.

Done properly, that review changes what the next block does. A student losing most marks to timing does not need more content; they need three papers sat to time with a stopwatch and a decision about question order. A student losing marks to command terms needs fifteen definitions and four weeks of applying them. A student with genuinely absent content needs a rebuild, and if there are eight weeks left, needs to be told which parts of the syllabus will be sacrificed.

This is the one piece of work that Sports City families can do themselves without paying anybody. Take the marked papers, sit with the student, and sort the lost marks into those six categories. If the biggest category is not content, the next block is a technique block, and it will be cheaper and faster than the one most providers would have proposed.

sections.heading: KHDA, mandatory subjects and the hours that are actually free
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Elsewhere the regulator differs: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A Sports City family reading an inspection report is reading a KHDA document.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited.

For calendar planning that is not a footnote. A Diploma student in Sports City carries more timetabled subjects than the six on the IB transcript, so the free hours in a week are fewer than a revision plan drawn from the IB subject list assumes. Plans that allocate study time per subject without accounting for the mandatory subjects run short by several hours a week, and the shortfall is absorbed by whichever subject the student enjoys least.

The wider context is worth one line. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula; seven new private schools arrive for 2026-27 creating 16,846 places, after six opened in 2025-26 with enrolment up 6%, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not rise for 2026-27. Against school fees at that scale, a well-timed eight-week block is a small cost. A badly timed year of weekly sessions is not.

process.title: Name the next fixed date
process.description: The enquiry that works names the course, the level and the next immovable date: a mock window, a coursework deadline, the written papers. That single piece of information decides whether the right answer is a rebuild, an eight-week block or triage, and it is the question most providers never ask.

process.title: Trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: A full online session with the proposed specialist, spent on the student's most recent marked paper. Lost marks are sorted by cause, and the session ends with a target that can be measured. Parents receive it in writing. No card is required and there is no obligation to continue afterwards.

process.title: Agree the target and the omissions
process.description: The block is defined by what it will move and by what it will deliberately leave alone. Stating the omissions is the part that makes the plan honest, particularly inside eight weeks, and it prevents the slow drift towards covering everything badly rather than something well.

process.title: Weekly sessions against the calendar
process.description: Work is sequenced backwards from the fixed date rather than forwards from today, with past-paper tasks set and marked against the published scheme before the next session. The note home records what was covered, what was set and how far the target has moved.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: Halfway through an eight-week block the target is measured. If it has not moved, the honest options are a different diagnosis, a different tutor or a different frequency. Making that decision at week four rather than week eight is the difference between one wasted month and two.

whyPoints.title: Planned backwards from your school's dates
whyPoints.description: Mock windows and internal coursework deadlines differ by several weeks between schools in the same community. A block built against a general Dubai calendar misses them. The plan here starts from the student's own school dates, which is why the first enquiry question is about the next fixed deadline.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what a block can do
whyPoints.description: Eight weeks moves technique, timing and two or three topics. It does not rebuild absent foundations, and saying so costs a booking occasionally. The alternative is taking the money for work that cannot succeed in the time, which is the most common quiet failure in this market.

whyPoints.title: Fast matching because distance is irrelevant
whyPoints.description: A specialist for a named course and level can usually be proposed within a day, with a trial lesson in the same week. For a family searching after mock results, the days spent waiting come directly off the length of the block, and that is the part proximity was supposed to solve.

whyPoints.title: Board dates sourced, IB dates deferred
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's June and November series and Pearson's May/June and November windows are stated from the boards' own pages. No IB session or results date appears here, because none could be verified from the IB directly, and a wrong date a parent plans around does real damage.

whyPoints.title: A firm boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria, question method and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not write, complete or produce any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay. Work a student did not produce is a malpractice finding against the student, whatever the deadline pressure.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits on the page
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are live, one-to-one and online in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram sends no tutor to a home in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE, holds no regulator or board accreditation, and claims none. Where no specialist is free, you are told rather than matched to a substitute.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near Dubai Sports City who can start this week?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and faster than a visiting tutor could. Because lessons are delivered live online, matching does not depend on who is free within a drive of Sports City on a particular evening, so a specialist for a named course and level can normally be proposed within a day and a trial lesson held in the same week. The honest exception is Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics in the second Diploma year, when demand across every Dubai cohort peaks at once and a short wait is sometimes unavoidable.

faqs.question: My child's mocks were three weeks ago. Is it too late to act on them?
faqs.answer: No, but the papers have to come out of the drawer. The review that matters takes about ninety minutes per subject: sit with the marked scripts and sort every lost mark by cause rather than by topic. Content not known, content not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not shown, arithmetic and units, question not attempted. If the largest category is not content, the next block is a technique block, which is faster and cheaper than the content block most providers would propose.

faqs.question: How long before the May session should a Diploma student start tutoring?
faqs.answer: If the problem is foundations, the back half of the first Diploma year, because that is the last point at which a rebuild does not borrow time from something else. If the problem is technique or timing, eight weeks before the target date is enough. If there are fewer than six weeks, the work becomes triage: decide which marks are recoverable, drill those, and accept explicit omissions. Each of those is a different block, and treating them as the same thing is the usual planning mistake.

faqs.question: What should a Sports City student do over the summer between DP1 and DP2?
faqs.answer: Fix the two topics they already know they never understood. The summer is the largest block of uncommitted time in the two years and it sits exactly where first-year gaps are still cheap to close. Six sessions across July and August, aimed at specific named topics rather than general revision, removes a problem that otherwise reappears in a February mock. Students who instead use the summer to read ahead usually arrive in the second year with the same gap plus more content on top.

faqs.question: Can tutoring continue through Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the timing usually improves rather than worsens. School days shorten and late-afternoon concentration drops, so a session placed after Iftar produces more work than the same hour at four o'clock. Because lessons are online, moving a slot requires no journey rearranged on either side. The period suits coursework process work and criterion review better than full timed papers, which is a reason to schedule the timed work either side of it rather than pausing entirely.

faqs.question: Which exam series do Cambridge candidates in the UAE actually sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in those two series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE family reading advice that references a February window is reading guidance for a different country. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential.

faqs.question: What does an eight-week block actually cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Using Bestimate's published monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions, two months at the mid band of AED 600 to 1,200 a month is roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400, and at the specialist exam-year band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more it is roughly AED 2,000 to 4,000. Those are market figures from a published rate table read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices. Hourly bands behind them run from AED 33 to 65 at the university-student end up to AED 650 for premium named tutors.

faqs.question: How do I know whether to book one session a week or three?
faqs.answer: By how many weeks are left and what the target is. One a week suits a rebuild across two terms, because the limiting factor is how much a student can absorb rather than how much teaching is available. Two or three a week suits the final weeks, when the work is timed papers and immediate mark-scheme review and the limiting factor is how many papers can be sat and marked. Three a week for a foundations rebuild usually produces unmarked homework and no extra progress.

faqs.question: Will a tutor work to my child's school deadlines or to the exam board's?
faqs.answer: To the school's, because those are the dates that bind first. Internal coursework deadlines, the mock window and the Individual Oral date are all set by the school and usually sit well before the examination series. Schools in neighbouring Dubailand communities differ by several weeks on all three, so a block planned against a general Dubai calendar will miss them. The first thing asked in an enquiry is the next fixed date on the student's own school calendar.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child finish an Internal Assessment that is nearly due?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the assessment criteria, explain the mark ceiling on each, question the research design, discuss whether the data supports the conclusion and give feedback on what the student has already written. A tutor cannot write, complete or produce any part of it, however close the deadline. That is an IB academic-honesty rule, and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the student rather than against whoever supplied it.

faqs.question: Does the school report tell me enough to plan a block?
faqs.answer: Rarely. A report gives a grade and a comment, and neither says which component produced the grade or which category the lost marks fell into. The marked paper does. A student can hold a 5 in a subject with strong coursework and weak timed papers, or the reverse, and the two situations need opposite blocks. Sending the most recent marked assessment rather than the report is the single most useful thing a parent can do when enquiring.

faqs.question: What happens at the four-session review?
faqs.answer: The target agreed in session one is measured, in writing. If it has moved, the block continues to its end. If it has not, there are three honest answers — the diagnosis was wrong, the tutor is not the right match, or the frequency is too low — and all three are changeable at no cost. Making that call at week four rather than week eight halves the time lost. Families who never review a block are the ones who pay for a term of no movement.

faqs.question: Are Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay worth spending sessions on?
faqs.answer: Yes, because together they carry up to three diploma points and both are governed by fixed internal deadlines that students leave late. The highest-return work is early and structural: choosing a prescribed title that can actually be argued, and settling a research question with a supervisor while there is still time to change it. That takes one or two sessions. Leaving both to the term they are due is how students lose points that affect a university offer.

faqs.question: Why does the number of timetabled subjects matter for a revision plan?
faqs.answer: Because a Dubai Diploma student is not studying six subjects. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A revision plan built from the six IB subjects therefore assumes free hours that do not exist, and the shortfall lands on whichever subject the student likes least. Counting the real timetable first makes the plan survivable.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.tutorsIntro: Below are the Diploma Programme and Middle Years Programme teachers who work with students across the Dubailand communities. Each profile names the course and level, and availability is shown by hour, because in this belt the hour is the part that fails first.

intro.heading: The school run decides when tutoring is possible in Dubailand
paragraphs: Nobody plans a tutoring schedule around a map, but that is what a proximity search gives you. The useful variables in the Dubailand belt are what time the bus arrives home, how long the student needs before they can think, and what else is already in the evening. Get those right and almost any format works. Get them wrong and the best subject specialist in Dubai will be talking to a tired child who stopped absorbing anything twenty minutes ago.

The belt makes the timing unusually hard. Dubailand is a development zone running south-east along Al Ain Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, taking in Arabian Ranches and its two later phases, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills, Town Square, Mudon and Remraam. Primary provision sits inside several of those communities. Secondary provision largely does not, so Year 7 upward usually travels, often toward Al Khail Road, Al Barsha or the Jumeirah corridor. A bus route that collects across two communities adds half an hour at each end before any traffic is considered.

Then there is what the evening is already full of. Dubai Sports City and Motor City households run on academy timetables; training occupies five until seven on several weekdays, and the serious study window moves to the weekend morning. Mudon and Remraam families frequently need two children covered on the same evening. Arabian Ranches secondary students are often the last home in the belt. None of this is visible from a tutor directory sorted by distance.

There is a less obvious timing factor as well. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates instructional time for those subjects on a 40-minute lesson unit, advising that no mandatory subject lesson should run shorter than 25 minutes. The taught week is therefore fuller than a six-subject Diploma list implies. A revision plan built from the IB subject blocks alone over-counts the free evening hours a student actually has.

IB Gram's answer to all of this is to remove travel from the equation rather than to negotiate with it. We do not send a tutor to a Dubailand address; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the session can start minutes after the student is home, can move to a weekend morning without anybody rearranging a car, and can place two siblings back to back with different specialists. The rest of this page is the timing detail: the school run community by community, the schools involved, what the belt pays, how Ramadan shifts everything, and where the honest limits are.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes and one post-16 alternative are in play across the Dubailand belt. The notes below concentrate on what each one does to a weekly timetable, because that is the question this page exists to answer.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations. Progress is judged on units of inquiry, a portfolio and the Year 6 Exhibition. Because primary provision exists inside several Dubailand communities, these are the students with the shortest journeys and the most usable late-afternoon time. Short frequent sessions work far better at this age than long weekend ones.
programmes.countryNote: A PYP student living in Mudon or Arabian Ranches 2 is often home by two in the afternoon, which makes a 3.30pm slot genuinely possible here and impossible for their secondary sibling. That split within one household is the most common scheduling puzzle the belt produces.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each on a 0-8 scale, with the Personal Project in the final year. This is where the journey lengthens: MYP students travel out of the belt, arrive home late, and carry more homework than their primary siblings. Criterion-based feedback is the work that moves grades, and it needs the student alert rather than exhausted.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 students from Town Square and DAMAC Hills are frequently the latest home in the belt. For them a 6.30pm start that holds every week beats a 5pm start that collapses after a fortnight, and an online slot is the only version that can be pinned that precisely.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across two levels plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments are marked against published criteria and moderated by the IB, and the school sets its own internal deadlines months ahead of the board's. Candidates at UAE schools sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this belt are old enough to work independently and least likely to have a free evening. The pattern that survives is one weekday slot plus a longer weekend morning block, with the weekend used for internal assessment and essay work where sustained concentration matters more than frequency.

programmes.name: A Level alternative in the same belt
programmes.description: Many Dubailand families choose A Levels rather than the Diploma after International GCSE, and siblings are often split across the two. Cambridge International A Level runs in June and November series. Where a household holds both, the timetable problem doubles because the two routes peak at different points in the year.
programmes.countryNote: A household with one Diploma student and one A Level student needs two different calendars respected in one week. That is manageable when nobody is driving and awkward when somebody is, which is the practical reason mixed-route families in this belt tend to end up online.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: These are the IB courses most requested from the Dubailand communities, with a note on what each one demands of the student's energy as well as their knowledge. Scheduling a demanding course into a depleted hour is the most common waste of money in this market.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the extended HL investigation. This is the course that most needs a student who is awake, because method communication cannot be learned passively. It belongs in the best hour of the week, not the leftover one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led and calculator-active, with modelling questions that must be answered in words as well as numbers. Slightly more tolerant of a tired session than the Analysis route, because much of the work is interpretation rather than construction.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity carry the marks and are taught early, so gaps compound across two years. Unit and significant-figure discipline is the recurring leak. Works well in a shorter midweek slot with the heavier problem sets reserved for a weekend block.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics. The failure is answering a describe command term when the question says explain. Mechanism practice needs continuous attention, so this is another course that should not be timetabled last in the evening.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense and vocabulary-dependent, with six-mark questions that reward structure over recall. Statistical treatment of internal assessment data is where strong candidates drop a band. Tolerates a later slot better than the physical sciences.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks. The internal assessment commentaries depend on choosing usable news articles, which is a task that fits a weekend morning rather than a squeezed weekday half hour.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two assessed orals and papers on unseen texts. Oral preparation needs the student able to talk at length, which rules out the twenty minutes after a two-hour training session. Weekend slots suit this course unusually well.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. Progress depends on discussion rather than practice, so the session needs time to breathe. Short weekday slots rarely achieve anything here; a fortnightly longer block does more.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Research question viability, method and structure, with the student writing every word. The useful work happens in longer sessions spaced weeks apart, timed around the school's own internal deadlines rather than a weekly rhythm.

subjects.name: Arabic B and ab initio
subjects.description: Compulsory provision in Dubai private schools means almost every IB student here carries Arabic in some form, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. Productive skills carry the weight and benefit from short frequent practice rather than long sessions.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-dubailand.regionsIntro: The following notes are about time rather than geography. Each community in and beside the belt produces a different arrival-home pattern, and that pattern is what should decide the slot.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Primary provision on the community, secondary largely out. Secondary buses commonly arrive back between four and half past four, making a 5.30pm or 6pm start the first one that holds across a term.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2 and 3
regions.note: Younger populations with heavier primary and lower-MYP demand. Afternoon slots from 3.30pm are genuinely workable here, which is unusual in the belt and worth using while it lasts.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: Shorter journeys than the Ranches, but the heaviest evening sports calendar. Training between five and seven removes the obvious slot, so sessions land either immediately after school or after half past seven.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Academy timetables dominate the week. Most students here do their serious work on a weekend morning, and a tutor who cannot offer that hour is not usable regardless of how close they live.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills and Town Square
regions.note: The longest outbound commutes in the belt for anyone attending a coastal-corridor school. Later starts are the norm, and these are the communities where a visiting tutor's travel premium is highest.

regions.name: Mudon and Remraam
regions.note: Community schooling for younger years and longer journeys from Year 7, which is why two-sibling evenings are requested from here most often. Back-to-back slots with two specialists solve it cleanly.

schoolClusters.city: Where Dubailand secondary students actually travel
schoolClusters.note: Secondary provision for the belt sits mainly along Al Khail Road and in the Al Barsha and Jumeirah corridor, which is what creates the long afternoon journey. Finish times cluster between half past two and half past three, and the journey rather than the bell sets the usable slot.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Schools inside the Dubailand communities
schoolClusters.note: On-community provision shortens the journey dramatically and is why primary-age slots can start in the afternoon here. Several of these schools serve more than one neighbouring community, which lengthens the bus route even over a short distance.

modes.title: Short fixed weekday slot
modes.description: Forty-five to sixty minutes at the same hour each week, placed immediately after the real arrival time or after training, whichever the household actually has. Shorter and reliable beats longer and negotiable in this belt, because a slot that has to be moved twice a month stops producing anything.

For academy families in Sports City and Motor City this is often the only hour of the week that is genuinely available.
