sections.heading: Online one-to-one from Green Community, and where it falls short
paragraphs: The case for online delivery here is partly about supply and partly about the clock. Supply, because the Diploma specialists this community needs are mostly not local. The clock, because a session that does not wait for a cross-city drive can start at 4.30pm, and a Diploma student working at 4.30pm is a different student from one working at 6.15pm after six subjects and a bus.

The work also suits the format. Diploma tutoring is largely reading documents together: a marked script, a draft investigation, an Extended Essay outline, a Theory of Knowledge paragraph that needs an example attaching to it. A shared screen where both people annotate the same page beats one paper copy across a table, and the session can be reviewed afterwards.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and this page states it near the top rather than leaving it to be discovered, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote.

Where it falls short is specific. A student who will not begin work without an adult physically present does better with one. A weak connection shortens the hour whatever the invoice says. A shared study space, more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas, undermines the lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room. If one of those applies, hire locally and ask two questions first: does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and have they taught that subject at that level to IB criteria?

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the claims to set aside
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit, and families hiring directly should ask about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule.

Never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher. The permit carries a code of conduct, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff are reported as barring paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Dubai sits under KHDA rather than ADEK, and the principle holds.

On coursework, the boundary is firm regardless of how close a deadline is. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion and its mark ceiling, help narrow a research question, discuss method and sources, explain referencing and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, supply a question, or produce data. Services in this market sell completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and submitting bought work risks the Diploma itself.

What we do not claim: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation or partnership, do not describe tutors as IB examiners, publish no self-asserted ratings, promise no grade or points outcome, and quote no statistic without its source and date.

sections.heading: Starting, with the term as the first question
paragraphs: Send three things: which term your child is in, the subject and level, and whichever document is the live pressure - a marked script, a draft internal component, or an Extended Essay question that is not yet narrow enough. The term tells us what is possible. The document tells us what is wrong.

The first session is diagnostic rather than introductory, and it ends in one of three honest statements: habit marks recoverable in the weeks available, content gaps needing more time than remains, or both at once with a decision to make about what gets sacrificed. The third is the answer families least want and most need, and it is better delivered in the first session than in the final term.

Matching runs on subject and level. Standard Level subjects and both mathematics courses usually match within a day. Higher Level sciences, Arabic B and less common language B courses take two or three days, because the pool is narrow and a near-miss in front of a Higher Level draft is worse than a short wait. Extended Essay support is matched to the essay's subject rather than to a general essay tutor.

The trial lesson is free, taught by the matched specialist, and built on the document you sent. It finishes with a written note that is yours whether or not you continue. When nobody suitable has a slot at your hour, we say so and offer a different weekday, a shorter block, or an honest recommendation to look locally. No competitor in this market publishes its unavailable case, and a family planning a final term deserves to know it in advance.

process.description: First year or second, before or after the mocks, and what the next school deadline is. The term determines what tutoring can achieve and what we should decline to promise, and it is a more useful opening than naming a topic.

process.title: Send the live document
process.description: A marked script, a draft internal component, or an Extended Essay question still too broad to answer in 4,000 words. The document makes the first session diagnostic rather than a conversation about how the term has felt.

process.title: Specialist matched by subject and level
process.description: Standard Level and both mathematics courses usually within a day; Higher Level sciences and language B in two or three. Extended Essay support is matched to the essay's subject rather than to a general essay tutor.

process.title: Free diagnostic trial lesson online
process.description: A real one-to-one lesson with the matched specialist on the document you sent, finishing with a written note of what it showed and what the remaining weeks should target. No card details and nothing to commit to.

process.title: A plan re-cut at each calendar edge
process.description: The same tutor at the same Gulf Standard Time hour weekly, with the plan rewritten at the internal deadlines, after the mocks, around Ramadan and again for the final stretch of timed papers.

whyPoints.title: The term is the first question, not the topic
whyPoints.description: The same weakness needs different work in the first year, the collision term and the final stretch. Starting new content in the last term is the most reliable way to leave a grade exactly where the mocks put it.

whyPoints.title: The collision term planned rather than survived
whyPoints.description: Internal deadlines, the Extended Essay and mocks land together in most schools here, and the Extended Essay is what gets sacrificed because nobody is waiting for it day to day. Sequencing it takes one session.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts read instead of mock grades
whyPoints.description: A grade is a summary; the script is the evidence, and it usually shows two or three habits repeating across questions. Families who choose a subject by grade rather than by script often spend the last weeks in the wrong place.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan in the plan from the start
whyPoints.description: School hours shorten and the usual slot becomes unusable for a month that currently falls in the spring term. Protecting frequency over length holds quantitative fluency that a pause would cost.

whyPoints.title: Supply, not search skill, is the local problem
whyPoints.description: The IB is 7% of Dubai private enrolment and this catchment is not where it concentrates. A radius search returns general tutors readily and criteria-literate Diploma specialists rarely.

whyPoints.title: Figures and rules cited, never asserted
whyPoints.description: AED bands are attributed to their publishers with the month read, regulatory points come from u.ae, MoHRE and KHDA, and IB dates are not published here because they cannot be confirmed from the IB.

faqs.question: Are there Diploma tutors actually based in Green Community?
faqs.answer: A few general tutors live locally, and criteria-literate Diploma specialists are rare here. KHDA reported the International Baccalaureate at 7% of Dubai private enrolment across 227 schools and 17 curricula, and this catchment is not where that minority concentrates, so the surrounding tutoring market grew up around UK and Indian curricula instead. A radius search from Dubai Investments Park returns general tutors and IGCSE specialists in reasonable numbers and Internal Assessment readers rarely. That is a supply fact rather than a failure of searching.

faqs.question: Which Diploma term should we start tutoring in?
faqs.answer: The first year, if there is any choice, because that is where habits are cheap to build and where the Extended Essay question and internal assessment designs can be settled without competing with anything. The most common starting point is just after the mocks in the second year, which is workable for habit repair and timed practice and poor for unmet content. The honest first session says which of those two you are dealing with, and that answer determines what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve.

faqs.question: What is the collision term and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: In most schools serving this catchment, the first term of the second Diploma year carries internal assessment deadlines for several subjects, the Extended Essay deadline, Theory of Knowledge work and the mock papers, all within a few weeks. The thing that gets sacrificed is predictable: whatever has no immediate audience, which is almost always the Extended Essay. That is why Extended Essay marks here sit below subject marks so often. Sequencing the term takes one session with a calendar, and the student should do the mapping.

faqs.question: How should we use my child's IB mock results?
faqs.answer: Ignore the grades for the first hour and read the scripts. A mock script usually shows two or three habits repeating across several questions: method lines not written, command terms answered at one depth, multi-part questions abandoned, units omitted. Those move in weeks. It also often shows that the subject with the lowest grade is not the one with the most recoverable marks, which is how families end up spending their last weeks in the wrong subject. A mock mark is not a prediction; boundaries move between sessions.

faqs.question: Can lessons shift to post-iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we plan for it rather than reacting. School hours shorten during Ramadan and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so the usual late-afternoon slot generally becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. The advice we give is to protect frequency over length, because quantitative fluency decays fastest when sessions stop and a complete pause usually means relearning in the first week back. Because nobody is travelling to your address, the change is a shared-diary adjustment rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute.

faqs.question: What should happen in the final weeks before the May session?
faqs.answer: Timed papers and marking, and nothing new. The student sits full papers under real conditions, including Paper 3 where Higher Level requires it, and someone who is not the student marks them against the official scheme. The output is a ranked list of repeated habits, which the next session attacks rather than moving on to a fresh paper. New content in this window displaces the practice that converts existing knowledge into marks, which is why a late content push so reliably leaves the result unchanged.

faqs.question: When should the Extended Essay question be settled for a Green Community student?
faqs.answer: Subject chosen in the second half of the first Diploma year, question narrowed before the long summer break. The limit is 4,000 words, and the commonest cause of a disappointing core grade is a question that would need a book, producing a survey rather than an investigation. The school sets the internal deadlines and they land earlier than families expect because the supervisor and school both need time. The summer break is the natural research window precisely because nothing else is competing for it.

faqs.question: Does the winter break help or hurt a second-year Diploma student?
faqs.answer: It hurts unless something is set for it, because it falls inside the collision term. A fortnight with no school structure, arriving in the middle of internal deadlines and mock preparation, usually produces two weeks of nothing followed by a worse January. The fix is modest: agree one deliverable for the break - a complete Extended Essay draft, or one internal component finished to criteria - rather than a vague intention to catch up. One session before the break to set it is normally enough.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a Higher Level specialist for this community?
faqs.answer: Standard Level subjects and both mathematics courses usually match within a day. Higher Level sciences, Arabic B and less common language B courses take two or three days, because the specialist pool is genuinely narrow and we will not put a near-miss in front of a Higher Level draft. We state the expected wait at the enquiry rather than afterwards. If nobody suitable has a slot at the hour you want, we say so and offer a different weekday, a shorter block, or a recommendation to look locally.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying in-home rates for a Diploma subject in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: Look at what the premium buys. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 per hour with independent tutors to AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200-450 and above for specialists. Those bands overlap almost entirely, which means a family can pay specialist money for a generalist with the premium covering a journey. Where the local Diploma supply is as thin as it is here, that is the default outcome of a radius search rather than a remote risk.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram publish the IB examination dates?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is worth stating. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one almost all UAE schools enter candidates for and goes no further. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we cite those where they are relevant. The dates that actually drive a term plan are internal anyway - the internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay deadline, the mock window - and the school's Diploma coordinator holds all three.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 5 and starts the Diploma next year. What should we do with the summer?
faqs.answer: Close the transition gap, which is narrow and specific. The Middle Years Programme builds inquiry, independent work and reflective writing well, and does not require timed writing, formal mathematical notation at speed or recall at volume. The Diploma assumes all three from the first week. A summer of weekly timed writing, daily algebraic manipulation by hand and deliberate retrieval practice removes most of the first-term shock. It is far cheaper than discovering the gap in the second term of the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: Should we pause tutoring during the mock weeks themselves?
faqs.answer: Reduce rather than pause, and change what the sessions do. During mock weeks the school timetable is disrupted and the student's time is already committed, so a weekly session should become technique only: one paper type, one habit, no new content. Cramming content in mock week defeats the purpose of mocks, which is to generate honest diagnostic data about where marks are leaking. A mock sat on the back of a content push produces a flattering score and a useless script, which is the worst of both outcomes.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson produce for a Diploma family here?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis that is yours whether or not you continue. The matched specialist, not a salesperson, teaches a real one-to-one lesson online on the document you sent - a marked script, a draft internal component, or an Extended Essay question - and finishes by writing down what it showed and what the weeks remaining in your child's term can realistically achieve. No card details are required to book it and there is no package to agree beforehand.

intro.heading: What an IB request from this part of Deira usually turns out to be
paragraphs: Hor Al Anz sits in Deira, inland from Al Mamzar, next to Abu Hail and Al Muteena, with the Green Line of the Metro running through it. The school market immediately around it is dominated by Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum provision. International Baccalaureate schools used by families here tend to be across the Creek or further out, which produces a particular pattern: an IB student in Hor Al Anz usually has a long commute and almost never has an IB school on the doorstep.

That matters for a near me search in a specific way. The tutors who happen to live nearby are overwhelmingly experienced in the curricula taught nearby, which is to say CBSE, ICSE and IGCSE rather than the Diploma. A search sorted by distance from Hor Al Anz will therefore return people who are perfectly competent in a different system, and the mismatch is invisible in the results. It only shows up three sessions in, when the student asks about criterion wording or a command term and gets a confident answer from the wrong framework.

So this page is written about the IB itself rather than about geography. It sets out the six subject groups and what each one's components actually assess, explains what higher level adds beyond extra hours, covers the three core components, and maps the internal assessment deadlines that shape a Diploma term more than the external session does. A parent who reads it should be able to tell whether a tutor is talking about the right programme within two minutes of a conversation.

There is also a Middle Years Programme population here, and it generates a different kind of enquiry. MYP reports carry no percentages: each subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked from zero to eight, combining into a grade from one to seven. Parents arriving from a percentage-based system reasonably find that opaque, and the most useful first step is reading the report properly rather than buying anything.

On delivery we are direct. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Hor Al Anz family is one-to-one, online, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For an IB student in this district that is not a compromise but the obvious arrangement: the student already spends an hour a day travelling to a school that teaches the programme, and the tutor pool for a specific Diploma subject is national rather than local in any case.

What follows is the substance. If you only read one section, read the one on internal assessments, because the school's own deadlines are what determine whether a Diploma year feels manageable or frantic, and almost nobody asks for them in writing early enough.

sections.heading: The six subject groups and what each one's components actually assess
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes six subjects, normally one from each of the first five groups plus a sixth from group six or a second from another group, with three at higher level and three at standard. That structure is widely described and rarely explained in terms that help a parent judge what tutoring is for. What matters is what each group's assessment actually rewards, because that is what a tutor works on.

Studies in language and literature reward analysis of how a text is constructed, which is not the same as writing fluently about what it means. Language acquisition rewards accurate, appropriate production under time. Individuals and societies rewards argued judgement supported by evidence, where a well-informed summary scores poorly. The sciences reward reasoning from data, with command-term precision and uncertainty handling carrying a surprising share of the marks. Mathematics rewards method and justification as much as answers. The arts reward documented process alongside the finished work.

Within every group there is an internal assessment marked in school against published criteria, and across most subjects it carries a substantial share of the final grade. That is the component families most often ask for the wrong help with and the one where a tutor's limits matter most. We coach the process and never produce the work, and we say so in every subject rather than leaving it to be inferred.

The table below sets out the six groups with what the written papers reward and what the internal assessment rewards, which are frequently different things. A student can be strong at one and weak at the other within the same subject, and a plan built from a marked paper alone will miss half the picture.

sections.heading: Higher level and standard level: what actually changes
paragraphs: Families often hear that higher level is harder, which is true and not useful. The accurate statement is that higher level is a different syllabus: it contains material the standard level course does not cover, its papers include components the standard level student never sits, and in the sciences the additional material sits inside each topic rather than in a separate block. That last detail has a practical consequence for revision, because HL content taught at the end of a topic tends never to be revisited.

The selection consequence is the one that affects hiring a tutor. A teacher who has taught the standard level course thoroughly may have no experience of the higher level material at all, and the gap will not appear in a conversation about the subject in general. It appears when a student asks about a specific HL extension and receives a plausible answer that is slightly off. This is the main reason we list tutors by level taught rather than by subject, and the main reason we tell families the expected wait for a genuinely specialist HL match.

The workload difference is also structural rather than proportional. Three higher level subjects plus the core is a substantially heavier commitment than the subject count suggests, and for a student commuting from Hor Al Anz across the Creek the binding constraint is often hours in the day rather than ability. A sensible plan looks at the whole timetable before adding a weekly session, and sometimes the right advice is a shorter, more targeted block rather than a standing commitment.

sections.heading: The core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
paragraphs: The three core components sit outside the six subjects and shape a Diploma year more than their timetabled hours suggest. Theory of Knowledge asks students to examine how knowledge is produced and justified, assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. The Extended Essay is a supervised independent research piece of around four thousand words in a subject of the student's choosing. CAS is a programme of creativity, activity and service with reflective requirements rather than an assessed grade.

All three have the same practical characteristic: no weekly homework forces progress, so they slide. A student with six subjects setting work every week will reliably postpone a component that nobody chases, and the result is a compressed and stressful period in the second year when the internal deadlines arrive together. For a commuting student in this district, who has less slack in the day to begin with, that compression is the single most common reason a Diploma year goes badly.

The useful intervention is calendar work rather than content teaching. Obtain the school's internal deadlines for the Extended Essay proposal, drafts and final submission, and for the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, in writing, at the start of the year. Put them on one page with the subject internal assessment deadlines. The clashes become visible immediately, and they are almost always resolvable in September and almost never resolvable in February.

On support, the limits are the same as everywhere else and worth repeating because the core is where they are tested. A tutor can help narrow an Extended Essay question until it is genuinely answerable in four thousand words, teach how sources are evaluated and cited, help structure a Theory of Knowledge essay around a real example, and respond to the student's own drafts with the questions an examiner would ask next. A tutor must not write, draft, complete or rewrite any part of either, and the school supervisor is the authority on what help is permitted.

sections.heading: Internal assessments: the deadlines that actually run the year
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment, marked in school against published criteria, and together they are the largest block of marks a student directly controls. They are also the thing most families discover late. External session dates are published and widely discussed; internal deadlines are set by each department, communicated once, and frequently cluster in the same weeks of the second year.

The practical consequence is a traffic problem rather than an academic one. A student with three higher level subjects may have three substantial pieces of coursework due within a month of each other, alongside the Extended Essay and a mock series. No amount of subject teaching helps with that. What helps is sequencing: knowing the dates early, starting the piece with the longest lead time first, and accepting that one of them will be done in a holiday rather than in term.

There is a quality point too. Across subjects, internal assessments fail for the same three reasons: a question or focus too broad to handle in the word count, data or material too thin to support the conclusion attempted, and an evaluation that lists apologies instead of identifying which limitation actually mattered. All three are planning failures, all three are cheap to prevent in the first fortnight, and all three are expensive to rescue in the last.

The table maps the common subjects to the form their internal assessment takes and what it genuinely rewards. Use it with your child's own deadline list rather than instead of it; the dates are the part only the school can supply.

sections.heading: Arriving in the Diploma from IGCSE, CBSE or another system
paragraphs: Most Diploma students from this district arrive from one of three places, and each arrives with a different profile. From IGCSE, students bring solid content and recall and meet three new demands at once: uncertainty arithmetic in the sciences, literal command terms, and the expectation that a conclusion is argued from data rather than stated. None is conceptually difficult and all three are unfamiliar, which is why a strong Extended-tier grade does not predict a comfortable first term.

From CBSE or ICSE, students typically bring stronger procedural fluency and systematic practice than average, and less experience of open-ended written reasoning, source evaluation and the long argued answer. The gap is in form rather than in substance. Six to eight sessions on structuring an argument, writing to a mark allocation and handling an unfamiliar question is usually the whole intervention, and it is far cheaper in the summer before the course than in the second term of it.

From the Middle Years Programme, students arrive strong on inquiry, research and reflection, which are genuine advantages in the core and in internal assessments, and short on sustained technical fluency. Higher level mathematics and the sciences assume from the first week that algebra is automatic and that an uncertainty can be carried through a calculation. MYP builds those skills in service of inquiry rather than drilling them.

In all three cases the right first step is the same and is not teaching. It is an audit: what was covered, to what depth, and which of the Diploma's particular demands has the student never actually practised. One session produces a short written list, and the list is usually three or four items rather than a syllabus. Selling a general revision programme to a transferring student is the standard offer in this market and it is almost always the wrong purchase.

sections.heading: Reading an MYP report, for the families who have just started
paragraphs: A sizeable share of enquiries from this district concern the Middle Years Programme rather than the Diploma, and they almost always begin with a report that is hard to interpret. There are no percentages. Each subject shows four criterion levels, each from zero to eight, and a subject grade from one to seven derived from them using boundaries published in the subject guide. Your school can show you the conversion it uses.

The way to read it is to lay the four criterion levels for each subject side by side and look for the outlier. Levels of six, six, three and six point at one specific skill rather than at the subject, and lifting that one is the shortest route to a different grade. Levels of four, four, four and four point at something else entirely, usually task literacy or self-management rather than a subject weakness, and the plan should differ accordingly.

The second reading is across subjects at the same criterion type. A low communicating or organising criterion in three subjects at once is one problem with three symptoms, usually about structure rather than content in any of them. That pattern is invisible when the report is read subject by subject, which is how everybody reads it, and spotting it is the most valuable five minutes a parent can spend each term.

Then ask the school three specific questions: which task produced the lowest criterion level, what its task-specific clarification asked for, and what a higher level would have looked like on that task. Those get precise answers. Asking how my child is doing gets a reassuring answer that changes nothing. For a working parent, sending the questions in writing beforehand often produces a better reply than a crowded parents' evening does.

sections.heading: Scheduling around a commute, and the weekend slot nobody books
paragraphs: A Diploma student commuting from Hor Al Anz to a school across the Creek loses a real part of the day to travel, and a tutoring plan that ignores that will not survive. Students on the Green Line have a more predictable arrival than those on a bus in traffic, but neither is early. Most are home between 16:00 and 17:00, and after food the usable window starts around 17:30. For a student carrying three higher level subjects and the core, that window is already contested.

Two adjustments make a real difference. The first is session length: sixty focused minutes on a travel day beats ninety that drift, and the work set between sessions should be sized for a student who has already spent an hour commuting. The second is using the weekend properly. Weekend mornings are the best slot available for whole papers, long coursework sessions and anything needing sustained attention, and they are consistently the least requested.

Apartment conditions matter here as much as anywhere in Deira. A hard surface rather than a sofa, the student's own calculator rather than a phone, squared paper for graph work, headphones so a busy household is not part of the lesson, and the camera angled at the page rather than the face. Where siblings share a room, staggered evenings work and shared sessions do not.

Ramadan reshapes several weeks each year and schools adjust their hours. The arrangement that works is fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work between, agreed before the month starts. For a Diploma student those weeks frequently sit near a mock series or an internal deadline, which is precisely why the shift should be planned rather than improvised.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the things to verify yourself
paragraphs: Start from the fact that this is lawful, regulated work and not an informal arrangement. The instrument is a private tuition work permit: introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through MoHRE, valid for two years and granted free of charge. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with the application filed through its smart app, website and e-services system. In Hor Al Anz, where a good many tutors are teachers and office staff fitting sessions around the Deira commute, the paperwork is plainly not the obstacle. Eligibility is correspondingly broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Working without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, a specific dirham amount quoted at you by anybody, this page included, should be treated as unverified.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will claim one. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We do not enter candidates for examinations and we do not perform Ministry equivalency. Where this page names a regulator, it is to explain what that body does and to point you at its own pages.

On assessed work the limit is absolute. A tutor teaches, explains, sets work, marks it and gives feedback on the student's own writing. For internal assessments, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge or an MYP Personal Project, that means coaching the process and nothing more. One provider examined for this project advertises completed internal assessments at a published price; that is an academic-malpractice trigger under the International Baccalaureate's own rules and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

What to verify independently: the examination session and any dates with the school's IB coordinator and the board's own site, since we deliberately publish no IB examination or results dates here; the school's internal deadlines, in writing, from each department; what coursework support is permitted, from the supervisor; and any individual tutor's permit status, directly. Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

faqs.question: Why are there so few IB tutors near Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: Because there are few IB schools immediately around it. The provision used by families in this district mostly sits across the Creek or towards Al Mamzar and Festival City, and the schools nearest Hor Al Anz are predominantly Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum. Tutors who live nearby are therefore mostly experienced in those systems rather than in the Diploma, and a search sorted by distance will not show the difference. The mismatch usually appears three sessions in, when a question about a command term gets a confident answer from the wrong framework.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a tutor to our apartment in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Sessions are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For an IB student in this district the logic is straightforward: the pool of people who have taught a specific Diploma subject at a specific level is national rather than local, the student already loses time to a commute, and an online session removes any further travel from the evening.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between higher and standard level?
faqs.answer: Higher level is a different syllabus rather than a longer one. It contains material the standard level course does not cover, its assessment includes components the standard level student never sits, and in the sciences the additional material is woven inside each topic rather than placed in a separate block. That last point matters for revision, because HL content taught at the end of a topic is easy to skip. It also matters for choosing a tutor: a teacher experienced only in the standard level course cannot cover the HL extensions, and the gap is invisible in a general conversation.

faqs.question: Which internal assessment should our child start first?
faqs.answer: The one with the longest lead time, which is usually a science investigation or the Extended Essay rather than the one due soonest. Internal deadlines across departments tend to cluster in the same weeks of the second year, and a student with three higher level subjects can face several substantial pieces within a month. Get every date in writing in September, put them on one page, and sequence from the longest lead time backwards. For a commuting student, assume one piece will have to be done in a holiday rather than in term.

faqs.question: What makes a science investigation fail in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Three things, and all are planning failures rather than writing failures. A research question too broad or involving an effect too small to measure reliably with school equipment, which produces data that supports nothing. A data set too thin for the analysis then attempted. And an evaluation that lists apologies instead of identifying which limitation actually mattered and what would be done differently. All three are cheap to prevent in the first fortnight and expensive to rescue in the last, which is why the first useful session is about design rather than about content.

faqs.question: How does the Extended Essay fit into a commuting student's year?
faqs.answer: Badly, unless it is planned deliberately. Nothing chases it weekly, so it loses every contest with six subjects that set homework, and the result is a compressed and stressful period when internal deadlines arrive together. For a student losing an hour or more a day to travel there is no slack to absorb that. The practical answer is to get the school's proposal, draft and submission dates in September, choose a question narrow enough to answer in four thousand words, and schedule the reading into weekends rather than weekday evenings.

faqs.question: Our child is moving from IGCSE into the Diploma. What should we prepare?
faqs.answer: Three specific things rather than general revision. Uncertainty arithmetic in the sciences, which IGCSE barely touches and the Diploma assumes can be carried through a calculation. Command terms, which the Diploma applies literally where IGCSE was more forgiving about answer length. And the expectation that a conclusion is argued from evidence rather than stated. Six to eight focused sessions in the summer before the course closes most of that gap, and it costs a fraction of repairing the same thing in the second term of the first year.

faqs.question: Our child is coming from CBSE. Is the Diploma a big jump?
faqs.answer: It is a change of form more than of substance. Students arriving from CBSE or ICSE usually bring stronger procedural fluency and more systematic practice than average, and less experience of open-ended written reasoning, evaluating sources and sustaining a long argued answer. Those are learnable and they are not what a general revision programme addresses, which is the offer most transferring families receive. One audit session establishes which of the Diploma's demands the student has genuinely never practised, and the list is normally three or four items.

faqs.question: How do we read an MYP report with no percentages on it?
faqs.answer: Four criterion levels per subject, each marked from zero to eight, combining into a grade from one to seven using boundaries published in the subject guide, which your school can show you. Lay the four levels side by side per subject and find the outlier: six, six, three and six points at one skill rather than at the subject. Then look across subjects at the same criterion type, because a low communicating criterion in three subjects at once is usually one problem with three symptoms. Then ask the teacher which task produced the lowest level.

faqs.question: Does CAS need any kind of tutoring support?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering it should be treated with suspicion. CAS is a programme of creativity, activity and service with reflective requirements rather than an assessed grade, and its value depends on the student actually doing and reflecting on their own activities. Where families struggle it is usually with record-keeping and reflection habits rather than with the activities themselves, and that is a conversation with the CAS coordinator. We would rather point you there than invent a service around something that does not need one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the help is structural rather than content-based. A tutor can teach how a claim and counterclaim are built, how a real example is used to do work in an argument rather than to decorate it, and how an essay answers the prescribed title rather than something adjacent to it. A tutor can respond to the student's own draft with the questions an examiner would ask next. A tutor must not write, draft or rewrite any part of it. The school supervisor sets the rules for permitted support in your child's case.

faqs.question: When should a session start for a student commuting across the Creek?
faqs.answer: Around 17:30 or later. Students from this district attending schools in Al Garhoud, Festival City or further out are typically home between 16:00 and 17:00, and after food the usable window starts later than parents expect. Sixty focused minutes on a travel day is more productive than ninety drifting ones. The genuinely underused slot is weekend mornings, which suit whole papers, long coursework sessions and anything needing sustained attention, because nothing competes and the student is not already tired.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB examination and results dates?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The International Baccalaureate's own site is the authoritative source for session and results dates, and it is the place to check them, either directly or through your school's IB coordinator. We will say that UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, because that is stable and useful. Beyond that, publishing a specific date that later changes would be worse than publishing nothing, especially on a page a parent might read a year after it was written. The dates that actually run a student's term are internal to the school in any case.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a specialist IB tutor from here?
faqs.answer: Standard level maths and sciences, English A, Economics and most MYP subject groups are usually matched quickly. Higher level requests with a specific named gap draw on a genuinely short list, because the level, the topic and your preferred slot all act as filters at once. Less commonly taught Diploma subjects may not be available at all, and we say so rather than placing a generalist. Where a wait is involved you get the expected length in writing before booking, and we tell you where the tutor is based.

intro.heading: What a proximity search returns from Al Warsan
paragraphs: Take the search literally. Draw a short radius around the clusters of International City and you capture Dragon Mart, Warsan Village, a stretch of the Dubai-Hatta road, the Ras Al Khor industrial strip and a very large number of apartments. What you do not capture is an IB World School, because there is not one in the district, nor a concentration of people who teach the Diploma for a living.

The nearest Diploma teaching is in Silicon Oasis, with Universal American School carrying IB programmes in Al Warqa and Uptown International School running the continuum in Mirdif. Those schools employ Diploma teachers, and those teachers are generally unavailable as private tutors to students at their own school, because the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

So the honest arithmetic: Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment. Spread that across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes and across the whole emirate, then narrow it to the eastern edge, then to people who teach a named Diploma subject at Higher Level, then to those willing to drive to Al Warsan at half past six. The result is not a shortlist.

Which means the word 'near' is doing the wrong job in the search. It is standing in for 'available this week', and in this district that proxy fails badly. IB Gram answers the search by taking the radius out of it: one-to-one lessons over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the subject and level. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are an India-only service for us.

The second half of the problem is the evening itself. A Diploma student from these clusters leaves early, comes back late, and arrives with Creativity, Activity, Service commitments, internal assessment deadlines and six subjects setting work. Fitting tutoring into that week is a scheduling exercise as much as an academic one, and most arrangements that fail here fail on the timetable rather than on the teaching.

There is a third element specific to online delivery that nobody in this market writes about, and it matters most in exactly this kind of district. A one-to-one video session in a busy flat succeeds or fails on setup rather than on bandwidth: a door that closes, a table rather than a lap, paper and a camera angle that lets the tutor see handwritten working. None of that costs money and all of it is routinely overlooked. So this page covers both. What the Diploma evening actually contains, term by term. The core deadlines counted backwards from the crowded January and February window. What a usable online setup needs in a shared flat, which nobody writes about and everybody discovers. And the honest limits on what we can staff, published rather than hidden.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-international-.programmesIntro: Three IB stages, and what each one does to the week of a student who travels out of the district every day.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led with no external examinations and no marks on the report. Tutoring is most useful for the two things it does not drill: number fluency to automatic recall and structured writing. Short sessions suit this age, and short sessions suit a child who has already spent an hour on a bus.
programmes.countryNote: For a family in these clusters the practical constraint at primary age is tiredness rather than timetable. A child commuting to Al Warqa or Al Qusais is genuinely spent by five, so a weekend-morning slot usually produces more than a weekday one even though the weekday one looks more convenient on paper.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each graded 1 to 8 against four published criteria marked out of eight. The efficient tutoring targets the single weak criterion rather than the subject, which is why the criterion breakdown from the school matters more than the report itself.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years evening is lighter than the Diploma evening, which makes this the stage where a weekday session fits comfortably. It is also when the Personal Project arrives in MYP 5 and collides with everything else, and a commuting student has less slack to absorb that than a student who lives near their school.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45 with up to three points from the core. Every subject carries an internally marked, externally moderated assessment with its own school deadline.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the commute bites. A Diploma student travelling from International City to Silicon Oasis loses roughly ten hours a week to the journey, and those hours have to come out of the same week that contains six subjects, the core and service commitments. Tutoring has to be planned around that rather than added on top of it.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: TOK, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge runs as an exhibition in the first year and a 1,600-word essay in the second. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word supervised independent piece. Together they carry up to three points. Creativity, Activity, Service is not graded but must be completed, and it occupies real evenings.
programmes.countryNote: For a commuting student the core is where time disappears invisibly, because none of it has a weekly lesson to anchor it. Service activities are frequently arranged around the school rather than the home, which for a family in Al Warsan means another journey. Mapping the core deadlines in the first Diploma year is the single most useful planning act available.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-international-.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects students from these clusters most often need help with, described by what the assessment actually demands.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, calculus and proof, with induction, complex numbers and vectors at Higher Level. Most lost marks are method: working omitted, rounding applied early, analytic methods replaced by calculator work where the question required otherwise.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. The characteristic failure is interpretive rather than computational - a correct regression line followed by no statement of what the gradient means in context.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty propagation and graph linearisation carry a large share of recoverable marks and are rarely taught as lessons in their own right. Explanations written in everyday language rather than with defined quantities account for most of the rest.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations underpin every theme, so weakness there costs marks across the whole paper. Organic mechanism marks are lost on conventions - arrow origin, lone pairs, charges - rather than on understanding the chemistry.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume rather than conceptual difficulty, with command terms deciding the grade. Data-based questions reward reading the axes and error bars before writing, which is a habit that can be established in two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams must be titled, labelled and referenced in the prose to score, and Higher Level adds a calculation-heavy paper. The internal assessment is three 800-word commentaries on recent news articles, with the marks concentrated in the evaluation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Applied analysis of stimulus material, where higher bands require a justified judgement rather than a balanced list. Higher Level candidates sit an additional paper based on pre-released stimulus issued ahead of the session.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen non-literary analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral on a global issue and, at Higher Level, an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. The Individual Oral usually fails on a global issue pitched far too broadly for the texts chosen.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies used as evidence for an argument rather than recited. Marks sit in the critical-thinking strands: methodological limitations, cultural and gender considerations, and alternative explanations, all of which are teachable as writing habits.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition in the first year and the 1,600-word essay in the second, scored with the Extended Essay for up to three points. The exhibition fails when objects illustrate the prompt rather than evidencing a claim about knowledge.

subjects.name: Extended Essay

sections.heading: What a Diploma evening in these clusters actually contains
paragraphs: Parents underestimate this and students rarely explain it. A Diploma student travelling from International City to Silicon Oasis or Mirdif spends something like two hours a day in transit, which is ten hours a week gone before any homework begins. On top of that sit six subjects setting work, Creativity, Activity, Service commitments that often meet near the school rather than near the home, and internal assessment deadlines that arrive without a weekly lesson to anchor them.

The consequence is that adding a tutoring session without removing something produces a student who attends the session and stops doing the school's work. That is a net loss at full price. The sessions that produce results are the ones with agreed work between them, which means the week has to have room for both the hour and its homework.

The load also shifts across the two years in a predictable way. The first Diploma year is relatively open until the internal assessments begin in the second half. The second year's first term is the heaviest stretch in the whole programme, with assessments, the Extended Essay and mock preparation overlapping. The final term is intense but narrower, because by then the work is timed practice rather than production.

The table below sets out that load term by term with the tutoring shape that fits each. The pattern it produces is modest by design: in this district an ambitious schedule that collapses in week three is the commonest failure, and a plan the household can sustain for two terms beats a better plan abandoned in October.

sections.heading: The core deadlines, mapped before they collide
paragraphs: The Diploma core - Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service - carries up to three points and no weekly lesson. That combination is why it is the part of the Diploma that most often goes wrong, and a commuting student has less slack to absorb a late start than one who lives beside their school.

The pressure point is not May. It is the January and February window of the second year, when internal assessments across four or five subjects, the Extended Essay final submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the school's mock examinations all land within a few weeks. A student with no Extended Essay progress by the October of the second year is not behind on one piece of work; they are about to be behind on everything, because the hours have to come from somewhere.

So the planning act worth doing in the first Diploma year is simple and nobody does it: ask the Diploma coordinator for every internal deadline for both years, in writing, and put them on one page. Not the examination dates - the school's own deadlines, which are the ones that actually govern the student's life. From that one page the whole tutoring plan follows.

We publish no specific IB session or results dates on this site. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date, so confirm every IB date with the coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the dates are sourced: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November.

sections.heading: Why the nearest tutor is rarely the right one here
paragraphs: The structural reason is that International City was not built around schools. It is a dense residential and commercial district, its children travel out in every direction, and the adults who teach the Diploma in Dubai live close to the schools that employ them. So a proximity search returns people who are available rather than people who teach your child's subject at your child's level.

There is a second reason that catches families by surprise. Diploma teachers at the schools this district feeds are generally not available to their own students privately: the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. 'Your child's own teacher, privately' is an offer to decline.

What follows is not that distance is irrelevant but that it is the wrong thing to optimise. The variables that decide a Diploma outcome are whether the tutor teaches that subject at that level, whether they can coach an internal assessment through its criteria without writing it, and whether the session actually happens every week. Distance affects only the third, and online delivery solves that one outright.

A fair caveat: online is not automatically better, it is better for this problem. A student who will not engage with a screen, or who has nowhere quiet to work, has a real obstacle that honest advice should acknowledge rather than dismiss. The next section is about exactly that, because in a shared flat it is the practical question nobody writes about.

sections.heading: What a usable online setup needs in a shared flat
paragraphs: This is the part of online tutoring that providers skip and families discover. A one-to-one video session works well when the student can see the tutor's working and the tutor can see the student's, and badly when the student is on a phone in a room with a television on. The difference is not the internet connection, which in these clusters is generally fine. It is the arrangement of the hour.

The three things that matter most are a door, a surface and a second screen or a camera angle. A door because an hour of concentration needs an hour of quiet, which in a family flat usually means a bedroom rather than a living room. A surface because mathematics and science require writing by hand, and a laptop balanced on a lap cannot support that. And a way for the tutor to see the handwritten working, which is usually a phone propped to point at the page.

The rest is marginal. Headphones help more than people expect, because they cut the room out and make the session feel like a conversation rather than a broadcast. A notebook kept specifically for tutoring, with the error log in the front, means the previous week's work is findable in ten seconds. Charging the device before rather than during the session removes a recurring five-minute interruption.

The table below sets out what makes a session work and what quietly degrades it. None of this costs money, which is why it is worth saying: the gap between a good online session and a mediocre one in a busy household is almost entirely about setup rather than about equipment or bandwidth.

sections.heading: Subject and level choices for a student who commutes
paragraphs: Three Higher Level subjects is the standard Diploma load and the combination matters more for a commuting student than for one who lives near school, because the recoverable hours in the week are fewer. Two heavily quantitative Higher Level subjects plus a third with a demanding written component produces a second-year January that effort alone cannot solve, and the commute is an hour a day of that effort already spent.

The honest advice when choices are still open is to map the assessment load across both years rather than looking only at interest. Which subjects have internal assessments requiring laboratory access, which require data collection outside school hours, and which can be completed with reading and writing alone. For a student who cannot easily return to a Silicon Oasis laboratory after dinner, that distinction has real consequences.

The other question is university prerequisites, and it should be settled in the first Diploma year. Some courses specify Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, some specify it at Higher Level, and some sciences are required at Higher Level for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and engineering. Read the published requirements for the specific institutions and courses, including the UAE universities, because dropping from Higher to Standard Level is usually possible and moving up usually is not.

None of this is advice to choose an easier Diploma. It is advice to choose a Diploma whose assessment deadlines can actually be met from this address, which is a different question and one that nobody asks at the options evening. A student who is well matched to their subjects and has time to do the work beats a student carrying a prestigious combination they cannot service.

sections.heading: Internal assessments when the laboratory is a bus ride away
paragraphs: Every Diploma science carries a scientific investigation worth roughly a fifth of the subject grade, assessed against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation - four criteria of six marks each, twenty-four in total. For a student living in International City and studying in Silicon Oasis, the binding constraint is not the analysis but access to the apparatus.

That makes feasibility the first question rather than a later one. Can the investigation be completed within the laboratory sessions the school timetables, with the equipment the school has, at the precision the research question needs? A design that requires an extra afternoon of readings is a design that will not be finished, because the extra afternoon means another journey the household cannot easily make.

The work around the apparatus is where the marks mostly sit, and all of it is possible from home: framing a research question, identifying and controlling variables, choosing a range and interval, propagating uncertainty, linearising and plotting, calculating gradient uncertainty, and writing an evaluation that names the dominant error source and proposes one specific change. A tutor is useful for every item on that list.

The boundary is firm and worth stating because the search results this page sits in include an operator selling completed assessments at a published price. The student chooses the question, designs the method, takes the measurements, processes the data and writes the report. The tutor tests feasibility, explains the criteria, questions the design and comments on drafts. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate, not on the seller.

sections.heading: Coverage, availability and what we will not claim
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes what it cannot staff, and several conceal non-local delivery behind a phone number. We publish it, because a family that discovers a mismatch in week three has paid specialist rates for a generalist. Mathematics in both courses, the sciences at Standard Level, Economics, Business Management and English are generally available within days.

Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level take longer, particularly in the fortnight either side of mock examinations, when demand across the emirate concentrates on the same people. Less commonly taught Group 2 languages take two weeks or more. Further Mathematics, Music and Film we often cannot staff at all, and in that case we say no rather than substituting somebody adjacent and hoping.

On rates, every figure we publish is attributed and dated. Read in October 2026: qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270; premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650; in-home one-to-one with travel at AED 180 to 500. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

And what we do not claim: no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE; no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson; no guaranteed grades or published predicted scores; and no star ratings we cannot evidence with countable, dated reviews.

sections.heading: The permit question, and how a parent checks it
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and this is the clearest question on the page. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, so no tutor can legitimately price it into a rate, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

How you check it: ask directly whether the individual teaching your child holds a current permit, and ask to see it. Somebody who holds one shows it without hesitation. A provider who treats the question as an insult has told you something useful. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which has its own process and renewal timetable.

For completeness on the regulators: KHDA oversees private education quality in Dubai, ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. All of them regulate schools; none licenses individual tutors.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in International City?
faqs.answer: There is one-to-one IB tutoring available for a student living in International City, delivered live online rather than by a tutor coming to your flat. The reason to prefer that here is structural: there is no IB World School inside the district and almost no Diploma teaching within a short drive, so a proximity search returns people who are free rather than people who teach your child's subject at their level. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Why is there so little IB teaching near these clusters?
faqs.answer: Because the district was not built around schools. International City is dense residential and commercial, its children travel out in every direction, and the adults who teach the Diploma in Dubai generally live near the schools that employ them. The nearest Diploma provision is GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis, with Universal American School in Al Warqa and Uptown International School in Mirdif beyond. Those schools' own teachers are also barred from tutoring their own students privately under the permit's code of conduct.

faqs.question: How much of the week does the commute actually take?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma student travelling from these clusters to Silicon Oasis or Mirdif, something like two hours a day, which is ten hours a week gone before homework starts. That matters because tutoring added on top of a full week does not create time; it displaces the work the school already set. The arrangement that works here is one fixed weekday session with a named evening for its homework, plus a weekend morning, and a protected rest day.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma session start on a weekday from Al Warsan?
faqs.answer: Around six, and from the China Cluster or on a bus route, 6.30pm is more honest. The school day may end at half past two, but the afternoon return makes multiple stops and the Dragon Mart and Ras Al Khor junctions are slower then, so a student travelling from Silicon Oasis often reaches home well after four and then needs to eat. Setting the slot against a bad day rather than an average one is what keeps it in the diary in February.

faqs.question: Which part of the Diploma causes the most trouble for students here?
faqs.answer: The core, because it carries up to three points and has no weekly lesson to anchor it. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and service commitments all slip, and a commuting student has less slack to absorb a late start. The collision point is the January and February window of the second year, when internal assessments, the Extended Essay submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the mocks all land within a few weeks of each other.

faqs.question: What should I ask the Diploma coordinator for?
faqs.answer: Every internal deadline for both Diploma years, in writing, on one page. Not the examination dates - the school's own deadlines for internal assessments, the Extended Essay drafts, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, and the mock timetable. Those are what actually govern your child's life, they vary between schools in this part of Dubai by weeks, and the entire tutoring plan follows from that single sheet. Almost no family asks for it in the first year.

faqs.question: My daughter has nowhere quiet to work. Will online sessions still work?
faqs.answer: It is the right question and it deserves a practical answer rather than reassurance. What matters is a door that closes, a table rather than a lap, paper and a pen with a phone propped to show the tutor the handwritten working, and headphones. Headphones help more than people expect, because they cut the room out. None of that costs money, and it is most of the difference between a good online session and a mediocre one in a busy flat.

faqs.question: Can my son do his science investigation if he cannot get back to the lab?
faqs.answer: Only if the design is feasible within the laboratory sessions the school timetables, which is why feasibility is the first conversation rather than a later one. A design needing an extra afternoon of readings is a design that will not be finished from this district. Everything around the apparatus - research question, variable control, uncertainty propagation, linearising, gradient uncertainty, and an evaluation naming the dominant error source - can be done from home, and that is where most of the twenty-four marks sit.

faqs.answer: It should be part of the conversation, which it almost never is. Two heavily quantitative Higher Level subjects plus a third with a demanding written component produces a second-year January that effort alone cannot solve, and an hour a day of that effort is already spent travelling. Map which subjects have assessments needing laboratory access or out-of-hours data collection. Then check university prerequisites, because dropping from Higher to Standard Level is usually possible later and moving up usually is not.

faqs.question: Can we book just a block of sessions for the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for the core it is usually the right shape. Four to eight sessions timed backwards from the school's internal deadline, with the session count agreed at the start so the total is known. The tutor interrogates the research question, explains what the assessment criteria reward, and comments on your child's own drafts. The student writes every word. faqs.question: How do we know the tutoring is working if we cannot sit in?
faqs.answer: By insisting the measurement comes from the school's marking rather than the tutor's impression. The baseline is the student's existing marked work plus, where the subject allows, timed past papers marked against the published mark scheme, which produces a list of specific recurring errors. The student keeps an error log of every mark lost and why. Every few weeks you get a short written note on what has moved. We publish no predicted grades and promise no improvement.

intro.heading: Why a proximity search is the wrong tool for an IB household in JBR
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in JBR is a search for convenience, and convenience is a reasonable thing to want. The problem is that the map answers a question nobody asked. What a map can tell you is who lives within twenty minutes of Murjan or Sadaf. What it cannot tell you is whether any of those people have taught Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, marked a scientific investigation against the four published criteria, or sat with a student through the week a Theory of Knowledge essay is due. Those are the things that change a grade. Proximity is not one of them.

JBR makes this sharper than most Dubai neighbourhoods. There is no IB school inside the forty-odd towers. The Walk and The Beach are residential and retail; the schools sit outside, and every IB family here is a commuting family. Students travel to Al Sufouh, to Al Barsha and Al Barsha South, to The Meadows, to Emirates Hills, to Jumeirah Village Triangle. That commute is the single largest constraint on when tutoring can happen, and it is also the reason a tutor who happens to live in Dubai Marina offers you nothing a tutor working from anywhere else does not.

The second constraint is the Diploma itself. A student takes six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, and adds the three core requirements on top: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Nobody is weak at all of it. Students are weak at one paper in one subject, or at the write-up stage of one internal assessment, or at the command terms that separate a four from a six. Matching to that specific failure point is what a tutoring decision is for, and the pool of people who can do it is national and international, not local.

Dubai is also the densest private-school market in the country. KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. In 2024-25 the emirate ran 227 private schools teaching 387,441 pupils across 17 different curricula, with the British curriculum taking the largest share of enrolment and the IB around a fourteenth of it. Seven more private schools open for 2026-27, three of them IB, adding 16,846 places. Supply is rising and it is still not the same thing as supply of the specific Higher Level teacher your child needs in February.

So this page does the thing the map cannot. It sets out which schools JBR students actually attend and what time they get home, what the six subject groups demand, what the core requires and when, what the Dubai market charges with every figure attributed, what the regulator's inspection band does and does not tell you, and what the Ministry of Education requires for equivalency. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India.
