dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes and JBR children pass through up to three of them before they leave school. The notes below describe each programme as it is actually taught in this part of Dubai, including the ages involved and what tutoring tends to be bought for at each stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses, with no external examination at any point. Assessment is continuous and teacher-led, which means a parent sees a portfolio and a report rather than a mark out of a hundred. Tutoring at this stage is almost never remedial in the examination sense. It is reading fluency, number sense, written English for children whose home language is not English, and the exhibition in the final year.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools that run the Diploma at the top end run the PYP at the bottom, so a JBR family choosing a primary school is often choosing a fifteen-year route. Arabic is compulsory from the start in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate Arabic classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils, so a PYP child here carries a second language load most PYP children elsewhere do not.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP covers eight subject groups and assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a one to seven grade after a published conversion. There are no public papers unless the school enters students for eAssessment. The criterion language is where marks are won and lost: a student who writes a good answer without addressing criterion B explicitly will score below a weaker student who did. The Personal Project in the final MYP year is the first independent piece of work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP competes directly with IGCSE for the same two years, and the choice matters for JBR parents because many of the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh schools their children attend run IGCSE at 16 and the Diploma at 18. A student arriving in DP1 from the MYP has stronger investigation and reflection habits; one arriving from IGCSE usually has stronger examination technique. Tutoring in DP1 fixes whichever of the two is missing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, one from each of six groups, with three taken at Higher Level and three at Standard. Each subject is graded one to seven, giving 42 subject points, and up to three further points come from the combination of the Theory of Knowledge grade and the Extended Essay grade, for a maximum of 45. Twenty-four points is the floor for the award of the diploma, subject to a set of conditions on failing conditions that catch more candidates than the raw total does.
programmes.countryNote: This is the programme almost every search for an IB tutor from a JBR address is really about. Dubai schools sit the May session, which puts the written papers at the end of Year 13 and every internal deadline in the eight months before. The practical effect for a JBR household is that DP1 feels slow and DP2 collapses into a single term where four internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay all land within weeks of each other.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two Diploma Programme courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning requirement, a personal and professional skills course and a language development component. It is graded differently from the Diploma: the DP courses carry their one to seven grades, and the core is reported separately rather than converted into points. Universities read it as a vocational qualification with academic anchors.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is rare in Dubai compared with the Diploma, offered by a small number of schools rather than the mainstream IB sector. A JBR parent is far more likely to meet it as an option a school proposes for a student who is strong in two subjects and sinking in the other four. If that conversation arrives, the useful question is which two DP courses are being kept, because those are the ones where tutoring still changes an outcome.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: Requests from JBR addresses cluster tightly: Mathematics in both of its routes, the three experimental sciences, the two Group 3 subjects that dominate Dubai timetables, and English A for students who read fluently but write thin commentary. Each entry below names what the subject assesses and where marks go missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Five topics, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator at both levels. Higher Level adds a Paper 3 worth 20% that asks two extended problems and rewards students who can sustain an argument over twenty minutes. Marks go missing in proof by induction, in complex numbers and in the calculus questions where a student can differentiate but cannot say what the derivative means.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted in every paper, with statistics, modelling and financial mathematics carrying far more weight than in Analysis. The common failure is treating it as the easy route: Higher Level Applications includes matrices, graph theory and a demanding statistics strand, and students who chose it to avoid algebra meet algebra anyway inside the modelling questions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised since the 2023 syllabus into Structure and Reactivity themes rather than numbered topics. Paper 1 carries 36% and splits into multiple choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 carries 44%. The scientific investigation is worth 20%. Mole calculations, energetics sign conventions and organic mechanism arrows are where the marks leave.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Also restructured in 2023, with the former Paper 3 absorbed into a data-and-practical section inside Paper 1. Students lose marks on units and significant figures long before they lose them on concepts, and the Higher Level extension topics in fields and quantum physics are routinely taught last and revised least.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Built around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change. The assessment rewards precise terminology: a student who writes about something increasing where the mark scheme wants a named process scores nothing. Data analysis questions on unfamiliar experiments are the most reliably under-practised part of the course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three papers at Higher Level, including a quantitative paper that catches students who chose Economics expecting essays. The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries on published news articles, each with a strict word limit, and the commonest fault is a commentary that summarises the article instead of applying a diagram to it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study heavy, with a pre-released case for Paper 1 that rewards preparation and punishes students who meet it late. Higher Level adds a Paper 3 built on a scenario and a stakeholder recommendation. The research project is where tutoring helps most, because the problem is usually question design rather than business knowledge.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, Paper 2 is comparative, and the internal assessment is an individual oral on a global issue linked to two texts. Fluent speakers of English routinely underperform here because the course rewards structured argument about how a text works, not confidence about what it says.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A paper-based course with a substantial internal assessment in the form of a developed solution and its documentation. Students write working code and then lose marks on the design and evaluation records that carry the criteria. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management, which is where most of the gap between a five and a seven sits.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Available as a Group 3 or Group 4 subject, which makes it useful for a student trying to keep a sciences place without a third laboratory subject. It is not a soft option: the assessment demands systems diagrams, named case studies and value-perspective arguments, and vague answers about sustainability score at the bottom of every band.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.regionsTitle: JBR and the neighbourhoods that share its school routes
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.regionsIntro: JBR does not operate alone. It shares bus routes, school gates and traffic with the strip of New Dubai around it, and a parent comparing options is usually comparing these places. The notes below describe how each one relates to a JBR tutoring schedule rather than repeating a list of amenities.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Immediately inland across Al Mamsha Street, sharing the same tram stops and most of the same school buses. A Marina family and a JBR family on the same route reach home within ten minutes of each other, which is why their session windows are effectively identical.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Connected to JBR by a single bridge and a footbridge over the road. Journey time to any school is JBR time plus the bridge, and the bridge is the variable: at 15:00 it adds minutes, at 18:00 on a weekend it adds considerably more.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: On the far side of Sheikh Zayed Road, with its own cluster towers and the DMCC metro station. JLT students often attend the same Al Barsha schools as JBR students but cross the highway twice a day, which pushes the realistic start of an evening session later.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The nearest real school district to JBR and the shortest school run in the set. Families here sit in a different position: the commute is short enough that an after-school activity and a tutoring hour can both fit on a Tuesday.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise apartment communities off Sheikh Zayed Road with primary schools inside them. JBR families with younger children sometimes drive here rather than to Al Barsha, which changes the afternoon shape entirely because the younger child is home first.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Springs
regions.note: The villa belt where several Diploma schools sit. A JBR student attending school here has one of the longer commutes in this cluster, often forty minutes inbound in the morning and a similar return, which places the earliest workable session well past 16:30.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Triangle and Circle
regions.note: Newer communities with IB and British schools that have absorbed a lot of New Dubai demand. The route from JBR runs against the afternoon flow rather than with it, which makes the return slightly more predictable than the morning run.

regions.name: Dubai Media City and Knowledge Park
regions.note: Not residential for most JBR families, but the location of university campuses and several training premises. Parents often mistake a training institute here for a schools regulator matter; the permit that governs premises is a different instrument from the one that governs an individual tutor.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and the Media City edge
schoolClusters.note: The closest school district to JBR and the one that produces the shortest commute. Students from the JBR towers reach these gates in well under twenty minutes outside peak flow, which is why families here can realistically hold a 16:15 session on a school night without the child arriving already tired.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: Where most JBR Diploma students actually go. The run inbound is manageable and the run home is the problem, because it coincides with the wider Al Barsha school exodus. Allow thirty to forty-five minutes door to door and treat any session starting before 16:30 as optimistic.

schoolClusters.city: The villa belt and Jumeirah Village
schoolClusters.note: The longest commutes in the JBR set, and the reason some families here move a Diploma tutoring hour to a Friday or a Saturday morning rather than fighting a weekday. Students arriving home after 16:45 generally do better with a weekend session than a tired weekday one.

modes.title: The weekly subject hour
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same slot every week for a term. This is the right purchase in DP1 and in the first half of DP2, when the job is to keep pace with a syllabus that moves whether or not a student has understood the previous unit. The tutor works from the school's own scheme of work, not a generic plan, so the hour reinforces what was taught that week rather than competing with it.

modes.title: A pre-examination block
modes.description: A fixed number of hours bought for a defined window, usually the six to ten weeks before mocks or before the May papers. The content is past-paper work under timing, mark-scheme reading and the specific topics a student has been avoiding. It is a different product from the weekly hour and should be priced and planned as one rather than extended out of habit.

modes.title: Independent-component coaching
modes.description: Support for the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the subject internal assessments, delivered as process coaching. The tutor teaches research design, argument structure, criterion reading and referencing, and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. The tutor does not write, co-write or rewrite any part of the submitted work, and says so to the student in the first session.

sections.heading: What a 'near me' search actually returns from a JBR address
paragraphs: It returns a radius, and inside that radius it returns Dubai Marina, JLT, Al Sufouh and whatever listings have paid to appear. It does not return an IB school, because there is not one inside JBR. That single fact reframes the whole search: your child is already travelling, the travel is already fixed by the school you chose, and the only variable left is the window between arriving home and being too tired to think.

So the useful version of the question is not who is nearby. It is what time does my child actually walk through the door, and who is free then. The table below sets out the school districts JBR students commute to, what they offer at 16 to 19, roughly how long the return leg takes on a weekday afternoon by car, and the earliest hour at which a session is worth paying for. Treat the journey figures as allowances rather than promises; Sheikh Zayed Road does what it does.

Two patterns show up repeatedly in this cluster. Families whose children attend Al Sufouh schools have the most flexible afternoons and often run tutoring at 16:15 without difficulty. Families whose children attend the villa-belt schools around Emirates Hills and The Meadows are frequently better off moving the session to a weekend morning, because a 17:30 start after a forty-minute bus ride buys an hour of a tired student. That is a worse hour than a rested Saturday one, at the same price.

sections.heading: Six groups, three Higher Levels, and the two subjects a JBR household usually buys help for
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes one subject from each of six groups: studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, the sciences, mathematics, and the arts. Three of the six are Higher Level, carrying roughly 240 teaching hours each, and three are Standard at roughly 150. The arts group can be substituted with a second subject from another group, which almost every Dubai school with a science-heavy cohort allows and most JBR students take up.

Requests from this neighbourhood are not spread evenly across those six. They cluster on mathematics and on one science, usually Chemistry or Physics at Higher Level, with a long tail of Economics and English A. That pattern is not an accident of local taste. It is the shape of the subject combinations Dubai schools build for students aiming at engineering, medicine and business degrees, and it is where the two years place the heaviest content load.

The practical consequence is that a JBR family should expect to buy one or at most two subject hours a week, not six. A student weak across all six subjects has a workload or an organisation problem, and six tutors will not fix it. A student at a five in Higher Level Chemistry and a seven in everything else has a Chemistry problem, and one well-matched hour a week from January of DP1 changes that outcome more reliably than three hours in April of DP2.

Where a second hour earns its place is the independent components. The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay and four or five internal assessments all have to be produced alongside the taught course, and no school timetable protects that work. A fortnightly hour on those, starting early, removes the DP2 pile-up that most families here describe as the hardest part of the two years.
bullets: Three Higher Level subjects at around 240 hours each, three Standard at around 150
The arts group may be substituted, and in science-heavy Dubai cohorts usually is
Mathematics plus one Higher Level science is the commonest JBR request pattern
Up to three extra points come from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination
Twenty-four points is the floor for the award, with separate conditions that catch candidates above it

sections.heading: The Diploma core, and the deadlines nobody sets for your family
paragraphs: The three core requirements sit outside the six subjects and they are where the two years go wrong for organised students. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a 4,000-word ceiling, supervised by a school teacher who is permitted a limited number of formal check-ins. Theory of Knowledge requires an exhibition of three objects with a written commentary and an essay of up to 1,600 words on a prescribed title released by the IB. Creativity, Activity, Service runs across both years and has to be evidenced, not merely done.

What makes these hard is not difficulty. It is that the school imposes internal deadlines on them while simultaneously teaching six syllabuses, and those deadlines move. A JBR parent typically discovers the Extended Essay exists in the term it is due, by which point the research question has already been chosen badly. The students who come out of DP2 calmly are the ones who settled a workable research question in the summer between the two years and had a full draft before the autumn term ended.

The honest boundary matters here more than anywhere else on the page. A tutor may teach research design, explain what each criterion rewards, read a draft and return comments, and coach a student through a redraft. A tutor may not write any part of the essay, supply text to be inserted, or edit a draft to the point where the words are no longer the student's. The IB treats that as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor. Any provider offering a completed internal assessment should be treated as a risk to your child's diploma rather than a shortcut.

There is one further UAE-specific wrinkle. Dubai schools sit the May session, so every core deadline sits inside the Gulf academic year that begins in late August and is interrupted by Ramadan and by the winter break. Families who plan the Extended Essay around those interruptions rather than through them tend to get a better piece of work and a less corrosive final term.
bullets: Extended Essay: independent research, 4,000-word ceiling, school-supervised
Theory of Knowledge: an exhibition with commentary plus an essay of up to 1,600 words
Creativity, Activity, Service: evidenced across both years, not assessed for points
The Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grades combine for up to three points

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs around JBR, and what you can verify without asking anyone
paragraphs: Start with what is checkable. Every figure in the table below was published by the named provider and read in October 2026, which means you can open the same pages and confirm them yourself before you accept any rate as normal. That is deliberate: the majority of pages ranking for Dubai tutoring queries quote no price at all, and of those that do, several quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. A rate you cannot trace is not market information.

Working from the published figures: EdFlik lists an entry tier from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour. Tutopiya's comparison panel opens at AED 33 to AED 52, although that panel carries a revision date roughly twenty-one months old, which is worth knowing before you treat it as current. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. BartyED quotes AED 650 at the examiner end.

Monthly packaging is where the arithmetic gets clearer. Online packages around AED 799 a month for eight sessions appear repeatedly in this market, as do in-home packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Set that against the KHDA confirmation of 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for 2026-27, and the tutoring line becomes the part of the education budget that is still moving.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page. What we do instead is start with a free trial lesson, one per student, with no card details taken, and quote after the match is made and the component is known, because the honest rate for Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3 coaching and for Standard Level Biology revision are not the same number.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor driving into the JBR towers
paragraphs: This is the comparison a JBR parent is really weighing, and the honest answer is not that one format wins everywhere. In-home tuition has a real advantage for a young child who needs an adult physically present, and a real cost structure: the published in-home band sits at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor, and that difference buys travel rather than teaching. The towers add their own friction. A tutor arriving at Murjan or Bahar at 17:00 deals with visitor parking, a security desk and a lift, and that is time inside the paid hour unless the contract says otherwise.

The structural point is larger than the money. Hiring within a twenty-minute drive of JBR means hiring from the people who happen to live in Dubai Marina, JBR, JLT and Al Sufouh and who are free at the hour you need. Hiring online means hiring the person who has taught Higher Level Chemistry to the 2023 syllabus and marked the scientific investigation against the four published criteria. For a Standard Level subject the local pool is usually adequate. For a Higher Level subject with a specific weak component, it usually is not.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. Every UAE lesson is one to one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing for annotating a past-paper script, and a saved record of the worked solutions. That is stated plainly because the alternative, implying a tutor will arrive and then explaining later that they will not, is the single most common complaint parents make about tutoring platforms in this market.

One practical note specific to these towers. Several JBR households run two children off the same table in a two-bedroom flat, which makes the audio the thing to solve before the first lesson. A wired headset, a closed door and a laptop rather than a phone resolves nearly all of it, and the trial lesson is the right place to find out rather than week three.

sections.heading: KHDA's inspection bands, and what a school report does not tell you
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects private schools annually against a six-band scale running from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable down to Weak and Very Weak. Those reports are published and they are genuinely useful. They are also read badly, which costs JBR parents money, because a band describes a whole school across every phase and subject, and a Diploma parent is interested in one department in one year group.

A school can hold a high overall band while a single Higher Level subject is thinly staffed, taught by a teacher new to the syllabus, or running two years behind on past-paper practice. Equally, a school in a middle band can have an outstanding mathematics department. The band is an institutional judgement, not a departmental one, and no inspection report answers the question a parent actually has, which is whether the person teaching Chemistry to my child in DP2 has taken a cohort through the 2023 assessment model.

The questions that get at that are specific and polite. How many years has this teacher taught the current syllabus. How many past papers will the cohort sit under timed conditions before the mock. When are the internal assessment deadlines, in writing. Which examination board does each department use. Schools answer these readily; parents mostly do not ask them, and then buy tutoring to patch a gap they never diagnosed.

Dubai's private sector is also expanding, which changes the staffing picture year to year. Six new private schools opened during 2025-26, enrolment rose by six per cent, and seven more schools open for 2026-27, four British and three IB, adding 16,846 places. New schools staff up quickly and sometimes unevenly. A parent choosing a school in this cluster for 2026-27 should ask about the Diploma teaching team specifically, not the school's opening promises.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and KHDA required its current mandatory-subject arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. This is the part of a JBR child's timetable that no IB tutoring page mentions, and it is also the part that most often produces a grade a parent cannot explain.

The rules are specific. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Islamic Education for Arab pupils and Arabic as a first language are taught in Standard Arabic; Social Studies for Arab pupils is taught in Arabic; non-Arab pupils take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than 25 minutes. There is also a hard constraint on content: using different or additional material for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. That matters for tutoring. Support for these subjects means working with the school's own prescribed material, not substituting a different scheme because it is easier to teach.

For a JBR Diploma student the practical question is usually sequencing. Arabic sits in the timetable alongside six IB subjects, and it is the first thing a stressed DP2 student drops attention from. A fortnightly hour early in DP1 is a far cheaper intervention than a scramble in the final term, and it protects a grade that appears on a school report a university may well read.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the figure we will not publish
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a school-leaving qualification obtained under a foreign curriculum, and it is a requirement a family meets at the point of university application rather than at the end of DP2. It is also where the ranking pages in this market make their most confident mistakes. One competitor currently states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five.

For the British track, the Ministry requires proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB there is a figure circulating on tutoring sites and we are not going to repeat it. Nothing in the sourcing available for this page confirms an IB points threshold for UAE equivalency from the Ministry's own publications, and a wrong number on a page like this costs a family a university cycle. The correct instruction is to confirm the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the school's own university counselling office before you plan around it.

Two further things are worth saying plainly. IB Gram does not perform, submit, expedite or guarantee equivalency or attestation; it is a Ministry process and the official channel is the one to use. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Anyone telling a UAE parent otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Starting from a JBR address, including what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The first conversation takes about ten minutes and it is mostly logistics. We need the school and the year group, the subject and the level, the examination session the student is working towards, and the window the school run leaves open on specific weekdays. For a Diploma student we also ask which internal assessments are outstanding and what the school's own deadlines are, because that calendar drives the plan more than the syllabus does.

Then there is a free trial lesson, one per student, held in the slot you intend to keep rather than whenever a tutor happens to be free. No card details are taken for it. The point of running it in the real slot is that a 17:00 Tuesday that works in theory and a 17:00 Tuesday after an Al Barsha bus are different things, and it is better to discover that before a term is booked.

Availability is where most providers go quiet, so here is the honest position. Common Standard Level subjects can usually be covered in the week. Higher Level subjects with a narrow component requirement, and the less commonly taught Group 3 and Group 6 options, sometimes take longer or cannot be staffed in the slot requested. When that happens we say so, offer the nearest workable slot, or say that we cannot cover it. We do not put a student with a tutor who does not know the component, because an hour with the wrong tutor costs more than no hour at all.

If a match is wrong, say so after the second session rather than the tenth. Changing tutor early is normal and costs nothing; persevering with a mismatch for a term is the most expensive thing a tutoring budget can do. Progress notes go to you in writing after each session, and if the school asks what outside support a student is receiving, that record is available to share.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: Subject alone is not enough to match well. Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, a Chemistry scientific investigation at the evaluation stage and an English A individual oral need three different people. Ten minutes on the phone naming the paper, the level and the deadline is what makes the first lesson useful rather than diagnostic.

process.title: A free trial in the slot you will actually keep
process.description: One trial lesson per student, no card details taken, scheduled in the real weekday window your school run leaves rather than a convenient demonstration hour. You get the tutor's read on where the marks are going and the student gets to test whether that time of day works after a commute from Al Barsha or Emirates Hills.

process.title: A plan tied to the school's own calendar
process.description: Before the second session the tutor writes down what will be covered and when, sequenced against your child's school scheme of work and its internal assessment deadlines rather than a generic syllabus order. If the school moves a deadline, the plan moves with it, which is the whole reason for asking for those dates up front.

process.title: Written notes, and a change of tutor if it is wrong
process.description: A short note after each session names what was covered, what the student did unaided and what is still open. Those notes are the record you use to decide whether to continue, and they are available to share with the school. If the match is not working, changing tutor after two sessions is normal and costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool that is not limited to your postcode
whyPoints.description: There is no IB school inside JBR, so the local tutor pool was never aligned to your child's school in the first place. Matching online means choosing the person who has taught the exact course and marked the exact component, instead of the person who lives nearest and is free at five.

whyPoints.title: Rates on this page are traceable
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Most pages ranking for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and some quote in US dollars. A rate you can open and verify is worth more to a parent than a reassuring adjective.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on independent work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach research design, explain criteria, read drafts and return comments. They do not write, co-write or edit to completion any Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or internal assessment. That boundary protects your child's diploma, and in a market where completed coursework is openly sold, saying it out loud is the point.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the commute, not around us
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set after we know which school gate your child leaves from and when. For a villa-belt commute that often means a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening, because a rested Saturday hour and a tired 17:30 hour cost the same and are not worth the same.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no tutor covers your child's component in the slot you want, we say so and offer the nearest workable alternative instead of filling the hour with someone who does not know the paper. Coverage limits are disclosed up front rather than discovered in week two.

faqs.question: Why does an IB tutor near me search in JBR return so few relevant results?
faqs.answer: Because the search filters on distance and there is no IB World School inside JBR to anchor a local IB tutoring market. What sits within twenty minutes of the towers is Dubai Marina, JLT, Al Sufouh and Media City, and the people available there are whoever happens to live nearby and be free in the late afternoon. Your child, meanwhile, is commuting to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or the villa belt. Matching to the subject group and the specific assessment component produces a much shorter but far more useful list than matching to a radius does.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do children living in the JBR towers usually attend?
faqs.answer: The commute splits three ways. The shortest run is to the Al Sufouh and Media City edge, reached in fifteen to twenty-five minutes outside peak flow. The largest group travels to Al Barsha and Al Barsha South, where several IB Diploma schools sit, on a thirty to forty-five minute return leg. A smaller number go out to the villa belt around Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Springs, or to Jumeirah Village, where the return can reach fifty minutes. Which of those three your family is in determines when a session can realistically start.

faqs.question: How many of my child's six IB subjects should we actually buy tutoring for?
faqs.answer: One, usually, or two at most. A student struggling in all six has a workload or organisation problem that six tutors will not solve, and the cost of trying is substantial. The pattern that produces results is a single well-matched hour a week in the Higher Level subject where the grade is sitting a band below the rest, started in DP1 rather than in the final term. A second slot earns its place on the independent components, the Extended Essay and internal assessments, which no school timetable protects.

faqs.question: What is the Extended Essay word limit, and when should my child really start it?
faqs.answer: The ceiling is 4,000 words, and the research question matters more than the word count. The students who finish DP2 calmly are the ones who settled a workable question in the summer between the two years and had a complete draft before the autumn term ended. A question chosen in the term the essay is due is almost always too broad, and no amount of writing rescues a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words. Supervision sits with a school teacher; outside help is for research design, criterion reading and feedback on the student's own drafts.

faqs.question: How long is the Theory of Knowledge essay and does it affect my child's points?
faqs.answer: The essay runs to a maximum of 1,600 words on a prescribed title released by the IB, and it sits alongside the exhibition of three objects with its written commentary. It affects the total indirectly: the Theory of Knowledge grade combines with the Extended Essay grade to award up to three additional points on top of the 42 available from the six subjects. Those points decide university offers more often than families expect, which is why leaving both pieces to the final term is a costly habit rather than a scheduling preference.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session start if my child buses back to JBR from Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Treat 16:45 as the earliest honest start. The inbound run to Al Barsha in the morning is manageable; the return coincides with the wider school exodus, so allow thirty to forty-five minutes door to door and then allow the child ten minutes to stop being in a car. A 16:15 start works for families whose children attend the Al Sufouh schools. For the villa-belt commute a weekend morning frequently buys a better hour than a weekday evening at the same price.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor teaching my child in JBR need a permit from MoHRE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can we hire a teacher from my child's own school to tutor privately?
faqs.answer: It is the worst available option even where it is permitted. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Beyond the rules, it places the person who marks your child's internal assessment in a paid relationship with your household. Verify any current position against the regulator before pursuing it.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely effective for a Diploma student, or just cheaper?
faqs.answer: For Higher Level work it is usually better, not merely cheaper. The teaching happens on a shared document: the tutor annotates the student's own past-paper script, the mark scheme sits beside it, and the worked solutions are saved for revision later. That is harder to do across a kitchen table. The decisive factor is the match. An online specialist who has taught the exact course beats a competent generalist who lives nearby, and for a narrow component the local pool rarely contains the right person at all.

faqs.question: What does KHDA's inspection band actually tell me about my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. The six bands, Outstanding through to Very Weak, judge a whole school across every phase and subject. A school in a high band can still have one thinly staffed Higher Level department, and a school in a middle band can have an excellent mathematics team. The report will not tell you whether the teacher taking Chemistry in DP2 has carried a cohort through the current assessment model. That question has to be asked directly, and schools answer it when asked.

faqs.question: Do IB students in Dubai still have to study Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit.

faqs.question: For equivalency, how many IGCSE passes does the Ministry actually ask for?
faqs.answer: Five. The Ministry requires proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One page currently ranking for these queries states six, which is wrong and worth checking against the Ministry's own guidance before you plan a subject block around it.

faqs.question: Is there an IB points score required for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Nothing we can source confirms one, so this page does not publish a figure. The British-track and American-track requirements are published and quoted above; the IB threshold circulating on tutoring sites is not traceable to the Ministry's own material in the sources available here. Confirm the current IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or through your school's university counselling office before building a plan around it. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our tower in JBR for the lesson?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. UAE lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing for working through a past-paper script, and a saved record of the solutions. The published in-home market band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour is quoted on this page so you can compare formats honestly, not because we are offering the visit.

faqs.question: Can sessions continue through Ramadan and the summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the timing usually changes rather than the frequency. During Ramadan school days shorten and families commonly move a session to a post-Iftar slot, which for a Diploma student in DP2 is often a more productive hour than a late afternoon one. Over the summer the useful work is the Extended Essay research question and the internal assessment that will otherwise collide with the autumn term. Sessions can also pause for travel; the slot is held rather than cancelled where the gap is a few weeks.

faqs.question: If nobody covers my child's Higher Level option, what do you tell us?
faqs.answer: We say so. Common Standard Level subjects can usually be matched within the week. Narrow Higher Level components and the less commonly taught Group 3 and Group 6 options sometimes cannot be staffed in the slot requested, and when that is the case we offer the nearest workable time or tell you we cannot cover it. Placing a student with a tutor who does not know the component costs more than leaving the hour empty, so we do not do it. Coverage limits are stated before anything is paid.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.closingHeading: Start with the component and the window, not the postcode
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jbr.closingBody: A JBR family already knows the two facts that matter: which school gate the day ends at, and which paper the grade is leaking from. Bring those to the first conversation and the match takes ten minutes. We will tell you plainly what the market charges, where our own rate sits once the component is known, and whether we can staff the slot you want. Lessons run one to one on live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the first one free, one per student, and no card details taken. If the match is wrong after two sessions, change it.

intro.heading: Why "near me" is the wrong search filter for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: A parent types "IB tutor near me" because that is how every other local service is found. A plumber near me, a dentist near me. The logic holds when the service requires presence and the supply is dense. It breaks for IB Diploma subjects, because the supply is thin and the thing you are buying is not presence.

Consider what you are actually looking for. Not a person who knows mathematics, but a person who knows how the IB marks mathematics: which Paper 1 answers earn method marks without a final answer, what criterion B of the Mathematics Internal Assessment is asking for, how the moderator reads a rationale. That is a narrow specialism. Filter it by a ten-kilometre radius around Jebel Ali and you may well have filtered it to zero.

The mathematics of this is unforgiving. Dubai has 227 private schools across 17 curricula, and KHDA reported that the International Baccalaureate accounts for 7% of private enrolment. Seven per cent of a large number is still a lot of students, but it is spread thinly, and the Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park catchment is not where the emirate's IB density is highest. The pool of people within driving distance who teach HL Chemistry to IB criteria is small.

So this page does the opposite of a radius search. It sets out what a Diploma subject specialist actually does - the criteria letters, the command terms, the component weightings, the core requirements - and then explains how a Jebel Ali family gets one. Lessons are live, one-to-one and over video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India.

There is a second reason the distance filter misleads, and it is about time rather than skill. A tutor who agrees to drive to Jebel Ali Village or Emaar South cannot start before the traffic clears, which in term time means a 5.30pm or 6pm arrival. On a school night, for a Diploma student already carrying six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and a CAS commitment, the difference between a 4.30pm start and a 6pm start is whether the session happens while the student can still think. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour with independent tutors advertising up to AED 500, and a substantial part of that figure is the journey. You are paying a premium for the latest usable hour of the day.

If after reading it you still want someone in the room, that is a legitimate choice and this page gives you the AED bands and the permit questions to ask a local tutor. What it will not do is pretend that a tutor who happens to live in Al Furjan is, for that reason, the right person to read an HL Physics investigation.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jebel-ali.programmesIntro: Three parts of the IB generate almost all the tutoring requests from this catchment, and they fail in different ways. The Diploma fails in components. The MYP fails in criteria that parents cannot interpret. The core fails on deadlines.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme subjects
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1 to 7 from externally marked papers plus an internally assessed component moderated by the IB. HL carries additional content and, in the sciences and mathematics, an additional paper that rewards sustained problem-solving across linked parts.
programmes.countryNote: Jebel Ali students reach the Diploma either through an IB continuum school in the Dubai Investments Park and Sustainable City belt, or by transferring from an IGCSE school at 16. The transfer route generates most requests, because an IGCSE grade 9 in a subject does not predict the HL grade in it.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core contributes up to three points on top of the 42 available from subjects, and it is where students lose points to deadlines rather than to difficulty. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an essay and an exhibition. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a 4,000-word limit. CAS is not graded but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded.
programmes.countryNote: Core deadlines in this catchment are set by each school rather than by the IB, and they land earlier than families expect. The commonest failure we see is an Extended Essay research question that is too broad to answer in 4,000 words, chosen in a hurry and never narrowed before the first supervisor meeting.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each worth up to eight marks, with grades derived from descriptors rather than percentages. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project, which has its own criteria, and some schools enter students for optional eAssessments.
programmes.countryNote: Parents in Al Furjan and Green Community frequently ask whether an MYP criterion score of 5 out of 8 is a problem. The answer sits in the descriptor for that criterion in that subject, and reading it with a tutor is usually more productive than a term of general practice.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: Below is what the internally assessed component looks like in each subject Jebel Ali families ask about, because that is the part of the grade a tutor can most directly help a student improve without touching their work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is the internal component: a student-chosen mathematical investigation marked against criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics itself. Most lost marks sit in reflection, which students treat as a conclusion rather than as critical evaluation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same exploration criteria, different mathematics. Modelling and statistics dominate, and the common failure is quoting a regression output without stating the model, the variables or whether the fit is meaningful. Technology use must be purposeful rather than decorative.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is internally assessed and marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Uncertainty propagation and whether a gradient actually supports the claim being made are where strong candidates lose marks they never notice losing.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same investigation structure as Physics. Chemistry drafts most often fail on a research question that cannot be answered by the data collected, and on conclusions that restate the trend without engaging with the chemistry that explains it.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The investigation plus heavy command-term sensitivity in the written papers. "Outline", "describe", "explain" and "discuss" set four different depths, and a student who answers all four at the same depth caps their paper mark regardless of content knowledge.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral links a global issue to two texts and is internally assessed. Paper 1 is unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, and HL adds the written essay. Marks follow analysis of technique and effect; paraphrase earns almost nothing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal portfolio consists of commentaries on published news articles. Article choice decides the mark ceiling before any writing happens, because an article with no usable economics in it cannot support diagram-led analysis.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A research project on a real organisation, marked on the quality of the question, the tools applied and the evaluation reached. Candidates who describe a company thoroughly and never evaluate score well below those who use less material better.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and Design Technology
subjects.description: Portfolio and process-journal components where documentation of thinking carries the marks as much as the finished object. Students in this catchment often under-document, then cannot evidence the development the criteria ask to see.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Productive and receptive skills across prescribed themes, with an individual oral. Relevant because KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, so a Diploma language B grade sits alongside that mandatory provision.

sections.heading: Criteria by letter: the detail nobody in this market publishes
paragraphs: The internally assessed component of an IB subject is marked against criteria identified by letter, each with its own maximum mark. This sounds like administrative trivia and it is the most actionable fact about the Diploma. A student who has written a genuinely good investigation can still be capped because one criterion was never engaged with, and nothing in the quality of the rest recovers those marks.

That failure mode is invisible from the inside. The student reads their draft, sees good work, and cannot tell that a whole criterion is unaddressed, because they have nothing to compare it against. A teacher managing a full cohort flags it in a sentence on a feedback sheet. A tutor working on one document can go criterion by criterion and say: this one is worth marks, and your draft does not currently engage with it at all.

The second recurring failure is misreading what a criterion rewards. Reflection in the mathematics exploration is not a conclusion. Evaluation in a science investigation is not an apology for errors. Personal engagement is not enthusiasm. Each has a descriptor, and the descriptor is the specification. Students who read the descriptors once, early, outperform students who read the task sheet repeatedly.

None of this requires anyone in the room. It requires the draft on a shared screen, the published criteria beside it, and a reader who knows how the moderator will see it. That is why the radius around Jebel Ali is the wrong thing to be optimising.

sections.heading: Command terms set the depth, and most students answer at one depth
paragraphs: Every IB subject guide publishes a list of command terms with definitions. "State" asks for a fact. "Describe" asks for an account without reasons. "Explain" asks for reasons or causes. "Discuss" asks for a balanced review leading somewhere. "Evaluate" asks for a judgement supported by evidence. The mark allocation follows the term, not the length of the answer.

What we see in students arriving from the Jebel Ali and Al Furjan schools is not ignorance of these definitions. Most can recite them. The problem is that under time pressure every answer comes out at the student's default depth, which is usually description. A student with a description default scores well on "describe" questions, loses half the marks on "explain", and loses most of them on "evaluate" - consistently, paper after paper, without ever identifying the pattern.

The drill that fixes it is unglamorous. Take twenty question stems from the subject guide, sort them by command term, and answer them in isolation with the term visible. Then the student marks their own answer against what the term demanded rather than against what they knew. Three or four sessions of this typically changes the default, because the student starts hearing the term before they start writing.

This matters more in the essay and science subjects than in mathematics, where the command terms are fewer and the marks follow method. In Biology, Economics, Business Management and History it is often the single largest recoverable block of marks in the whole paper.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay, counted backwards from 4,000 words
paragraphs: The Extended Essay has a 4,000-word limit and that limit is the design constraint everybody ignores at the start. A research question that would need a book cannot be answered in 4,000 words, and the essay that results reads as a survey rather than an investigation. It is the commonest reason a capable student scores a grade below their subject work.

Narrowing is therefore the first job and it is a job a tutor can do without touching the writing. The method is mechanical: take the question, ask what evidence would answer it, ask whether the student can get that evidence, and repeat until both answers are yes. A question about renewable energy policy becomes a question about one scheme, in one place, measured one way. The scope shrinks and the essay gets better.

The second job is the internal calendar. The Extended Essay deadlines in this catchment are set by each school, not by the IB, and they sit much earlier than families expect because the supervisor needs time and the school needs time before submission. A student who has not chosen a subject by the end of the first Diploma year is already compressing the research phase.

The third job is the boundary. A tutor may discuss the question, teach the subject content, explain the assessment criteria, check referencing conventions and read a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not supply the question, write any part of the essay, or edit it to a finished state. Services in this market sell completed coursework, one advertising finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; submitting bought work risks the Diploma itself.

sections.heading: What a local search returns around Jebel Ali, and what it costs
paragraphs: Run the radius search honestly and here is the shape of what comes back. Plenty of general tutors offering homework help across all subjects. A reasonable number of IGCSE maths and science tutors, because the UK curriculum accounts for 37% of Dubai's private enrolment and the supply follows demand. Very few people who can read an HL Chemistry investigation against the criteria. Possibly none available at 5pm on a weekday.

The prices attach to the format rather than to the specialism, which is the trap. Published Dubai figures from October 2026: budget online tuition from AED 33-65 an hour at EdFlik and Tutopiya; qualified online subject tutors from AED 150-200 at Unitors; in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 per Dubai rate guidance, with independent home tutors up to AED 500; specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase around AED 270; and one premium provider, BartyED, at AED 650.

Notice that the in-home band overlaps the specialist band. A family in Emaar South can easily pay specialist money for a generalist, because the premium they are paying is for the drive rather than for criteria literacy. That is the specific inefficiency this page exists to point out, and it is worse the further south you live.

None of these are IB Gram prices; our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson because it depends on subject and level. The bands are here so that any quote you receive can be read against something published, which is more than three of the pages ranking for this search offer.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one from Jebel Ali: what it does well and where it fails
paragraphs: The format suits this work unusually well. Diploma tutoring is mostly reading documents together - a marked script, a draft investigation, a past-paper question - and a shared screen with both people annotating beats one paper copy between two people across a table. Sessions start at 4pm rather than 5.30pm because nobody is driving down Sheikh Zayed Road. Lessons do not cancel for traffic or road closures around the port.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and we say so here rather than leaving a parent to discover it after a booking. Two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without mentioning that delivery is remote; naming the delivery model up front is the minimum.

The failures are specific and worth knowing. A student who will not begin work without an adult physically present does better with one. Younger children lose focus faster on screen. A shared or noisy study space - a real constraint in Discovery Gardens apartments - undermines any format but hurts online most, because the tutor cannot manage the room. And a weak connection turns a 60-minute lesson into 45 regardless of what the invoice says.

If one of those describes your household, hire locally and ask the tutor two questions: do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and have they taught that subject at that level to IB criteria before. Both are fair questions and a good tutor answers them without hesitation.

sections.heading: The honesty rules a Diploma family should hold a tutor to
paragraphs: The IB treats submitting work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence can be the loss of the Diploma rather than a mark penalty. That makes the honesty boundary the most important thing in any tutoring arrangement for a Diploma student, and it is routinely blurred by the services competing for this search.

The legitimate boundary is wide. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each lettered criterion and its mark ceiling, help narrow a research question, discuss method design, explain referencing conventions, mark a draft against the descriptors and explain the marking. That covers almost everything a student genuinely needs.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite or complete any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or Personal Project, supply the research question wholesale, produce the data, or edit the work to a finished state. The test is simple and worth applying after every session: has every sentence in the document been typed by your child? If a tutor offers more than that, decline and tell the school.

Two related claims to be sceptical of. First, examiner status: no tutoring service should describe a tutor as an IB examiner without evidence, and examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because nobody has that. Second, regulatory endorsement: we are not KHDA approved, hold no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, and operate no UAE premises. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises; ask for the number from anyone claiming it.

sections.heading: Starting from Jebel Ali, including the honest unavailable case
paragraphs: Send three things: the subject and level, the school, and a photograph of the most recent marked assessment or the current draft of the internal component. The document is the useful part. Twenty minutes of conversation about how the term has gone tells us less than two minutes with a marked script.

We match on subject and level rather than on who is free. For SL subjects and the two mathematics courses that is usually a match within a day. For HL sciences, Arabic B or a less common language B it can be two or three days, and we say which case you are in rather than filling the slot with a near-miss. A general science tutor in front of an HL Physics investigation wastes the family's money and the student's time.

Sometimes the honest answer is that no suitable specialist has a slot at the hour you want. When that happens we offer the real options: a different weekday with the right tutor, a short block until a regular slot opens, or a recommendation to look locally with the two questions above in hand. No competitor in this market publishes what happens when they cannot help, which is exactly why it belongs on the page.

The trial lesson is free, is taught by the matched specialist rather than a salesperson, and ends with a written note of what the document showed and what the first month should target. No card details are required to book it and there is no package to commit to beforehand.

faqs.question: Are there IB tutors actually based near Jebel Ali?
faqs.answer: There are tutors based nearby, and very few of them specialise in Diploma subjects at Higher Level. KHDA reported the International Baccalaureate at 7% of Dubai private enrolment, and that minority is not concentrated in the Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park belt, so the local market has grown around UK and Indian curricula instead. A radius search from here returns general tutors and IGCSE specialists in reasonable numbers and criteria-literate Diploma tutors rarely. That is the gap online delivery closes, by making geography irrelevant to the match.

faqs.question: What does "criterion C" mean on my child's IB feedback sheet?
faqs.answer: The internally assessed component of each Diploma subject is marked against criteria identified by letter, each with its own maximum mark, and the letters mean different things in different subjects. Criterion C in one subject may cover analysis and in another communication. The subject guide publishes the descriptor for each, and the descriptor is the specification. The practical move is to read the descriptor for the criterion your child scored lowest on, then compare it against what their draft actually does. That comparison is usually where the missing marks turn out to be.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with their Internal Assessment without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the legitimate space is wide. A tutor can teach the subject content the investigation needs, explain each lettered criterion and its mark ceiling, help narrow a research question until the evidence can answer it, discuss method design, explain referencing conventions, and mark a draft against the descriptors. What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the question, or produce the data. The test after every session is whether every sentence in the document was typed by your child.

faqs.question: Why does my child keep losing marks on questions they understand?
faqs.answer: Usually because every answer is coming out at one depth. IB subject guides define command terms precisely: "state" wants a fact, "describe" wants an account, "explain" wants a causal chain, "evaluate" wants a judgement with evidence. A student whose default is description scores well on "describe" and loses most of the marks on "evaluate", consistently, without noticing the pattern. The fix is a drill rather than revision: question stems sorted by command term, answered in isolation with the term visible, until the student hears the term before writing.

faqs.question: How early should an Extended Essay question be settled?
faqs.answer: The subject should be chosen in the second half of the first Diploma year and the question narrowed before the long summer break. The limit is 4,000 words, and the commonest cause of a disappointing grade is a question that would need a book, which produces a survey rather than an investigation. School internal deadlines in this catchment are set by the school rather than the IB and land earlier than families expect, because the supervisor and the school both need time before submission. Narrowing early is the cheapest intervention available.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying in-home rates for a Diploma subject out in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Look carefully at what the premium buys. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 per hour with independent tutors to AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Those bands overlap the specialist band of AED 200-450, which means a family far from the city can pay specialist money for a generalist, with the premium covering the drive rather than criteria knowledge. For HL sciences the specialist matters more than the presence. For a child who needs an adult in the room, presence wins.

faqs.question: Do your tutors have access to IB grade boundaries or marking information?
faqs.answer: No, and neither does anyone else offering you tutoring. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence for individuals, and examiner status is routinely used in this market to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content that nobody has. We also do not host or distribute IB papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, which are copyright material. We reference and link the official sources and work from your school's licensed copies.

faqs.question: My child moved from IGCSE to the Diploma and is struggling. What changed?
faqs.answer: The assessment changed more than the content did. IGCSE rewards accurate recall and clean method; the Diploma rewards judgement, evaluation and sustained argument, and it adds an internally assessed component marked against criteria the student has never seen before. A grade 9 at IGCSE predicts the content will be manageable and says nothing about whether the student can write an evaluation or design an investigation. Most transfer students in this catchment need criteria work and command-term work rather than more content, and that is diagnosable from one marked Diploma assessment.

faqs.question: Which schools near Jebel Ali teach the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The IB provision serving this catchment sits mainly outside Jebel Ali proper. Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park runs an IB continuum, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City is an IB school, and Sunmarke School in Al Furjan offers the Diploma alongside a UK-curriculum route. The surrounding schools - The Winchester School Jebel Ali, Delhi Private School Dubai, The International School of Choueifat Dubai, Dove Green Private School, The Arbor School and South View School - follow other curricula. Confirm current authorisation on each school's own site, since offerings change.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match an HL Physics or Arabic B tutor here?
faqs.answer: SL subjects and both mathematics courses usually match within a day. HL sciences, Arabic B and less common language B courses can take two or three days, because the pool is genuinely narrow and we will not fill the slot with a near-miss. We tell you which case you are in at the enquiry rather than after you have waited. If no suitable specialist has a slot at the hour you need, we say so and offer a different weekday, a short block, or an honest suggestion to look locally.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson for a Jebel Ali student actually involve?
faqs.answer: A real one-to-one lesson online, taught by the matched specialist rather than by a salesperson, built around the document you sent - the marked script or the current draft of the internal component. The tutor works through it with the student writing rather than watching, and finishes with a short written note of what the document showed and what the first month should target. No card details are needed to book it and there is no package to commit to beforehand. The written note is yours whether or not you continue.

faqs.question: Does Theory of Knowledge need tutoring, or is it just an essay?
faqs.answer: It needs process help more than content help. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition, and students lose marks by writing abstractly: large claims about knowledge with no worked example to test them against. The useful work is anchoring every knowledge question to a specific, real example the student can actually interrogate, and then checking the essay structure answers the prescribed title rather than the title the student wishes had been set. That is coaching on their own thinking, not writing it for them.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around a long school run from Emaar South?
faqs.answer: That is one of the clearer advantages here. Because nobody is travelling to your address, a slot can start as soon as your child is home and settled rather than after a tutor has crossed the city. Families in Emaar South and Dubai South typically take a 4.30pm or 5pm start that would not be offered by an in-home tutor at any price, and the lesson does not cancel when the port roads or Sheikh Zayed Road seize up. Slots also shift for Ramadan and examination weeks as a calendar change rather than a renegotiation.

faqs.question: What should I ask a local Jebel Ali tutor before hiring them directly?
faqs.answer: Two questions settle most of it. First, do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023? The UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no reason for a legitimate tutor to be without one, and tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Second, have they taught that specific subject at that specific level to IB criteria, and can they name the criteria? A good tutor answers both without hesitation.

intro.heading: The map answers a question JLT does not have
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in JLT is a reasonable thing to type and an expensive way to sort the answer. Jumeirah Lake Towers is a tower district built around four man-made lakes, wrapped by Sheikh Zayed Road on one side and the DMCC free zone in its middle. It has nurseries. It has no secondary school of its own. Every school-age child living in these clusters commutes out, most of them across Sheikh Zayed Road into Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, or up the interchange towards Jumeirah Village and The Meadows. Distance from your tower therefore tells you almost nothing about who can teach a Diploma component, and quite a lot about who is willing to spend an hour in traffic to try.

Price is where that confusion becomes visible. Published Dubai figures, read in October 2026, run from AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya, through AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB at Unitors, to AED 270 at TutorChase and AED 650 at BartyED. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Those are other providers' numbers, not ours. Read together, they say something useful: the spread is driven as much by format and travel as by teaching, and three of the six pages currently ranking for these searches publish no price at all.

This page is written from the money, because that is the decision a JLT family is actually making. Four leaks account for most of the waste we see. Families buy hours instead of naming a component, so nothing gets diagnosed and the same hours get bought again next term. They pay a travel premium for a tower address, which buys a car journey rather than better teaching. They buy at the wrong level, paying Standard Level depth for a Higher Level problem. And they compress the whole budget into the six weeks before papers, which is the most expensive hour in the calendar and the least able to rebuild a topic that was never learned.

A plain word on delivery before any of the rest matters. Sessions are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time so they sit between the school bus and the hour when a 17-year-old stops absorbing anything. IB Gram does not offer home visits in JLT, in Dubai, or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The exchange is deliberate and worth stating in cash terms: you give up the person at the door and you stop paying for the Sheikh Zayed Road crossing, which on the published in-home bands is a meaningful share of every hour billed.

There is a regulatory reason the nearest qualified adult is also the wrong default. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Its code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff are reported to do the same. So the physics teacher two towers away may be the one person legally unable to take your child.

None of this makes proximity worthless. It sets the clock. The school bus route decides when your child is home, fed and still functional, and in JLT that hour varies by half an hour or more depending on which school the family chose and which exit the bus uses. That is a real constraint and this page takes it seriously. What proximity does not decide is who should teach Chemistry at Higher Level, and paying as though it did is the single most reliable way to spend AED 20,000 across a Diploma and change nothing.
