That makes a 4pm slot genuinely available for the younger child, and it is the one age group where a short online session before the family evening starts tends to work better than anything scheduled later.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: Below, the place inside each subject where JLT families most often decide to start paying. Not the whole syllabus: the specific component where a cohort stalls, which is also where an hour converts into marks fastest and therefore where the money should go first.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Equilibrium and energetics at Standard Level; organic mechanisms, buffers and the data-analysis demands of the extended papers at Higher Level. Requests cluster in DP1 term two, when the internal investigation design lands in the same fortnight as the first serious equilibrium questions and the family suddenly needs two different kinds of help.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circular motion and the written-explanation questions that want a reason rather than a number. Students who handle the algebra comfortably often arrive needing help only with the prose half of the paper, which is a cheaper fix than it looks and a different lesson from the one parents usually ask for.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline and the long-answer questions where a correct idea scores nothing because it is not expressed in the scheme's terms. Biology shares enough molecular content with chemistry that one teacher can often carry both, which is where a real reduction in total spend comes from rather than from a package discount.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route taken by most JLT students aiming at engineering, economics or medicine. One paper is sat without a calculator, which is the component that exposes gaps in algebraic fluency carried over from IGCSE, and the one most often fixed with a short block rather than a year of weekly sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-active and statistics-heavy, with a modelling emphasis. Students arrive needing help with interpretation rather than manipulation: reading what a regression output means, justifying a model choice, and writing the sentence the mark scheme is waiting for after the calculation is done.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the internal assessment commentaries, which are short, heavily criterion-referenced and routinely underprepared. Higher Level adds quantitative work that catches students who chose the subject expecting an essay course. A JLT cohort with parents working in DMCC asks for this subject more each year.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application under time pressure, and the written project at Higher Level. Marks are lost by describing a business rather than analysing it, which is a habit of writing, not a gap in knowledge, and responds to a handful of sessions on structure faster than to content revision.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The unseen analysis paper and the oral, where students lose marks for summarising a text instead of arguing about how it works. For the many JLT students who speak English as an additional language at home, the fix is usually a framework for analysis rather than more reading.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies support
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever curriculum they are licensed for, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Non-Arab families in JLT often need help here precisely because it sits outside the IB subject list they were planning for.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jlt.regionsIntro: Proximity in JLT decides the clock, not the teacher. The notes below record what each neighbouring area does to a school evening and what a local search returns there, which is the part of the Dubai map that still has consequences once lessons run over video.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Ten to twenty minutes across Sheikh Zayed Road, and the densest supply of tuition centres and freelance generalists near JLT. What it does not contain is an IB World School, so a search that points here returns availability rather than Diploma expertise.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: The easiest hop from JLT and home to Regent International School, British curriculum through IGCSE. Children on this run are usually back by around 3.30pm, which makes it the one corridor where a 4pm start is comfortable rather than optimistic.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and Al Barsha
regions.note: Where most JLT Diploma students actually go to school, and a twenty to thirty-five minute drive each way in the early evening. A visiting tutor serving JLT from here spends more time on the road than in the lesson, and the published in-home bands reflect it.

regions.name: The Meadows and Emirates Hills
regions.note: Villa communities with full IB continuum provision, so JLT families often school here while living in a tower. The mismatch between home and school postcode is routine in this part of Dubai and it breaks any tutoring arrangement built around a map.

regions.name: The Lakes and The Springs
regions.note: Short hops inland with their own British-curriculum provision. Families here sometimes offer to share a tutor with a JLT household, which halves the hourly rate on paper and in practice halves the attention each child gets in a Higher Level session.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens and Al Furjan
regions.note: Ten to twenty minutes south, with substantial primary provision and The Winchester School in Jebel Ali. The lower published rate bands circulate most actively on this corridor, which is why JLT parents hear two very different prices for apparently the same service.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island and Al Sufouh Gardens
regions.note: Small residential pockets with no school inside them, in the same position as JLT itself. A proximity search from any of these addresses returns the same handful of Marina providers, which is a useful demonstration of what the map is actually sorting.

schoolClusters.city: IB World Schools JLT Diploma families travel to
schoolClusters.note: Students we support from JLT most often attend one of these, and almost always after a bus or car journey of twenty minutes or more. Knowing which one matters for tutoring because the school sets the internal deadline calendar, and a tutor who ignores that calendar will be teaching the wrong topic in the wrong week.

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum schools on the same JLT bus corridors
schoolClusters.note: Many JLT households have one child in the Diploma and a younger sibling in a British-curriculum school on the same run. That is the household where spending goes wrong most easily, because a single weekly tutor gets bought for two very different assessment systems and serves neither properly.

sections.heading: What a 20-minute radius from a JLT address actually contains
paragraphs: JLT is a residential district of towers built around four man-made lakes, bounded by Sheikh Zayed Road and holding the DMCC free zone in its middle. It has nurseries and no secondary school. Every school-age child here travels out, and a tutor who drives in is making the same journey in reverse at the same hour, which is the hour the roads around the interchange are at their worst.

That matters to the invoice, because travel is billed whether or not it appears as a line item. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against AED 45 to 65 for budget online tuition at EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. The academic difference between those bands is real but it does not account for the whole spread. A large part of it is the car, the visitor parking at a tower, and the two hours a travelling tutor cannot sell to anybody else.

The table below is the version of the JLT map that still has consequences. It records what a family here can actually reach on a weekday evening, what is there for a Diploma student when they arrive, and what the round trip takes out of the usable part of the evening.

Read it the other way round as well. A tutor willing to serve JLT inside twenty minutes is drawing on the same few communities, which is exactly why a proximity search returns centres in Al Barsha and generalists in Marina rather than a Higher Level Chemistry teacher. The pool is set by the road network, not by the subject. Online delivery is the one change that detaches those two things from each other.

sections.heading: What the hour contains at each published price point
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no hourly figure at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. One of them asks the price question in its own FAQ and declines to answer it. That is the market a JLT parent is trying to compare, and it is why the same service appears to cost AED 45 and AED 650 in the same week.

The bands are not arbitrary once you ask what each hour contains. At the bottom of the market the hour is a person working through the textbook with your child, which is genuinely useful for primary consolidation and almost never useful for a Higher Level component. In the middle the hour is a qualified subject teacher who knows the specification, and the open question is whether marking is inside the fee or outside it. At the top the hour is level-specific teaching with a marked script attached, and the premium above that is paying for a name.

The table sets out the published bands with the provider who publishes each one, read in October 2026. These are other providers' figures, quoted so a JLT family can see where a quote sits rather than guess. The column that matters most is the one listing what the hour does not include, because that is where an apparently cheap rate becomes expensive.

IB Gram does not print a single hourly number on this page, and the reason is honest rather than coy: the answer depends on the subject, the level and whether marking and written feedback sit inside the session fee. What we do publish is the market we sit inside, with a source and a date against every figure, and a free trial lesson that happens before any payment is discussed at all.

sections.heading: Four places a JLT tutoring budget leaks
paragraphs: The first leak is buying hours instead of a component. A family worried about maths books a weekly hour, the tutor works through whatever came home that week, and twelve months later the report says the same thing it said before. Nothing was diagnosed, so nothing changed. The cure costs nothing: name the subject, the level, the paper and the question type before you agree a rate, and ask what will arrive in writing after the session.

The second is the travel premium. On the published bands, moving the same teaching from a screen into a JLT apartment adds meaningfully to the hour, and the addition is the Sheikh Zayed Road crossing rather than anything academic. Families who want a person in the room should buy that deliberately and know what it costs. Families who assumed the premium bought better teaching are paying for a commute they could have kept.

The third is level drift. Standard Level and Higher Level are different products with different supply, and a tutor priced at the Standard Level end of the market is usually priced there for a reason. The reverse happens too: a Standard Level student put in front of a Higher Level specialist for a year is paying for depth the examination will never ask about. Both are expensive and both are avoided by writing the level into the arrangement.

The fourth is timing, and it is the costliest. Spend concentrated into the six weeks before papers buys the most expensive hours in the calendar at the moment they can do least, because six weeks cannot rebuild a topic nobody learned in DP1. The same money spread as a short block in DP1 term two, a fortnightly slot through DP2, and a tight intensive at the end does more and usually totals less. A fifth leak worth naming: paying twice for uncertainty, significant figures and graph linearisation, which are marked in physics, chemistry and biology alike and only need teaching once.
bullets: Name the component, not the subject, before agreeing any hourly rate
Ask whether marking and written feedback sit inside the fee or outside it
Write the level into the arrangement, in words, at the start
Spread spend across DP1 and DP2 rather than banking it for the final weeks

sections.heading: One illustrative budget, spent three ways
paragraphs: Arithmetic makes the argument better than adjectives, so the table below takes a single illustrative figure and spends it differently. It is a worked example built from the published market bands above, not a price list and not a quote. The point is not the total; it is that the same money produces entirely different outcomes depending on what it is pointed at and when it is spent.

What the comparison shows is that cheap hours bought without a diagnosis are the worst value in the table, and that the most expensive single pattern is good teaching bought too late. The pattern that works is unglamorous: a small number of hours aimed at a named component early, then a maintained rhythm, then a short intensive built on a marked script. It also happens to be the pattern least likely to be sold to you, because it bills fewer hours.

Two practical notes on reading it. First, every figure in the second column comes from the published bands in the previous section, so a family can substitute the rate they have actually been quoted and redo the sum in a minute. Second, the fourth column is the part worth arguing about at the kitchen table, because every one of those failures is a thing a JLT family we have spoken to has described after the fact.

The last row is the one we would recommend to most Diploma families here, and it is deliberately the least tidy. It mixes a fortnightly rhythm with a short criterion-referenced block on the internal assessment, which means the family has to hold a schedule through the weeks when school pressure spikes. That is the real cost of the best-value pattern, and it is worth knowing before you pick it.

sections.heading: The permit question, and why the teacher two towers away is the wrong hire
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a JLT family can check the position in a few minutes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service listing for it is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow for a parent. The permit is free, so a tutor who tells you the paperwork is expensive is telling you something else. And individuals providing private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts has been published, so any specific figure quoted at you, including the one that circulates on forums, is not something anybody can evidence.

The second part is the one that surprises JLT families most. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. So the convenient option, your child's own subject teacher who lives three towers over, is often the one arrangement that should not be made. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on the detail.

A separate licence governs anyone running a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai: KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, does not operate premises in the UAE, and claims no endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board. A provider that implies otherwise is making the single most dangerous claim available in this market.

sections.heading: What JLT households ask for, and the honest answer on availability
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is a strange silence given that every agency has one. Ours is specific: supply is good across the Diploma sciences, both mathematics routes, economics and English, and genuinely thin in a handful of places. Saying so costs us a few enquiries and saves families the version where a weak match is dressed up as a specialist and discovered in week three.

The table below pairs the subjects JLT families ask about with the moment in the Diploma they usually ask, the realistic time to a named match, and what happens when nobody suitable is free. The second column is more useful than it looks: a request made in DP1 term two gets a better answer than the same request made in March, because the specialists are not yet committed.

The fallback column is where most providers would write something comfortable. We will offer a named waiting date rather than a substitute, or a teacher whose depth is at a different level with that stated in writing, or a specialist outside the Gulf time zone with the clock difference agreed before anything is booked. Where the honest answer is no, it is no, and the reason is given.

One recurring request deserves its own line. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction for each. Non-Arab families in JLT frequently need help in exactly the subject nobody planned for, and this is the thinnest part of any tutoring pool in Dubai, ours included.

sections.heading: The Dubai market numbers worth putting next to a tutoring budget
paragraphs: Tutoring spend is a decision made inside a household budget that already contains school fees, and in Dubai that budget changed this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second Dubai economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a JLT family, the practical effect is that the largest education line is flat, which is the year to make a tutoring decision properly rather than reactively.

The supply side moved as well. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four on UK curricula and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More Diploma places within reach of JLT is good news for choice and a complication for tutoring, because transfer students arrive mid-course from other systems and need transition support rather than general tuition.

The scale figures are worth holding too. The Dubai Media Office reported 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across 17 different curricula, with UK curricula at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. That last number is the whole reason a proximity search disappoints a Diploma family: most of the schools near you, and therefore most of the tutoring market near you, are not teaching your child's programme.

The table collects the figures with their sources, because a number without a provenance is worth nothing in a budgeting conversation. Each row also says what it changes about a JLT tutoring plan, which is the only reason to put market statistics on a tutoring page at all.

sections.heading: Starting from a JLT address: the five lines we need
paragraphs: The fastest route out of a proximity search is to stop describing the problem and start naming it. Five lines do more than a long conversation about how your child is finding school: the subject, the level, the component losing marks, the date of the next assessment that actually counts, and the hour your child is genuinely home in JLT and still able to think. With those five we can check real availability in that exact subject and level before anybody promises you anything.

What comes back is a named specialist, a stated match time and a free trial lesson with no card details taken. The trial produces a written diagnosis: what the marked work shows, which topics are costing marks, and what a realistic sequence looks like between now and the assessment you named. That diagnosis is yours whether or not you continue, which is the only version of a free trial that means anything.

If nobody suitable is free, you get told that instead of being matched sideways. The options are a named date to wait for, a teacher with depth at a different level with the compromise written down, or a specialist outside the Gulf time zone with the clock difference agreed first. We would rather lose the booking than take money for a match we know is wrong, because the alternative is discovered in week three and costs the family the whole block.

Two last practical points for a tower household. Sessions are online, so they survive a move between clusters, a move out of JLT, and the summer the family spends elsewhere. And they can be rescheduled around Ramadan into post-Iftar slots, around prayer times, and around the study-leave weeks when school stops running a normal timetable. None of that requires renegotiating with the traffic on Sheikh Zayed Road, which is the quiet advantage of having bought the teaching rather than the journey.

process.title: Send the five lines
process.description: Subject, level, the component losing marks, the date of the next assessment that counts, and the hour your child is actually home in JLT. Five lines let us check genuine availability in that subject at that level, which is the only honest basis for any promise about timing.

process.title: Get the honest match time
process.description: We tell you how long a named specialist in that exact combination will take, including when the answer is a wait rather than a match. In March and April for Higher Level sciences that answer is longer, and you are better off knowing it before you plan the term.

process.title: Free trial lesson, no card details
process.description: A full session with the named specialist, built around a marked script if you have one. Nothing is charged and no payment method is collected beforehand, so the decision after the trial is made on the teaching rather than on a cancellation window.

process.title: Read the written diagnosis
process.description: After the trial you receive a written account of what the work shows, which topics are costing marks and what sequence of sessions would address them. It is yours whether or not you continue, and it is the document to take to another provider if you would rather compare.

process.title: Review at week six
process.description: Six weeks in, we compare a new piece of marked work against the script from the trial. If the evidence says the arrangement is not working, we say so and change the tutor, the format or the recommendation rather than selling you the next block on the strength of the first.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the cluster
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry means a Higher Level Chemistry teacher, named before you book. Because the lesson runs over video, that match is drawn from the whole pool rather than from the communities inside a twenty-minute drive of JLT, which is precisely where the specialists are not.

whyPoints.title: Marking happens between sessions
whyPoints.description: Scripts are marked outside the paid hour, so the hour is spent teaching rather than reading. Ask any provider whether marking sits inside the fee before you compare rates, because the same number means two different things depending on the answer.

whyPoints.title: The permit position stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Tutors working in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is free for two years. We say what the rule is, who it excludes, and what we do not hold, including any KHDA Educational Services Permit for premises.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor near me search actually return from a JLT address?
faqs.answer: It returns providers whose published address or claimed service area sits near your tower, which is a different thing from Diploma expertise. JLT has no secondary school of its own, so the nearest results are tuition centres in Al Barsha and Dubai Marina and freelancers advertising a driving radius. Dubai has 227 private schools across 17 curricula and the International Baccalaureate accounts for 7% of enrolment, so most of the market within twenty minutes of JLT is not teaching your child's programme at all. Sorting by distance surfaces availability, not the person who teaches your component.

faqs.question: How much do Dubai providers publish per hour for IB tuition right now?
faqs.answer: Figures read in October 2026 run from AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya at the budget end, AED 200 an hour for IB at Unitors in the middle, AED 270 at TutorChase, and AED 650 at BartyED at the premium end. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level work at AED 200 to 450 and in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. Those are other providers' published numbers, not IB Gram's prices. Our own figure depends on subject, level and whether marking is included.

faqs.question: Is a visiting tutor or an online specialist cheaper for a tower in JLT?
faqs.answer: On the published bands, the same teaching delivered in a JLT apartment costs materially more than the same teaching delivered over video, and the difference is travel rather than quality. Bestimate puts in-home work at AED 180 to 350 against AED 45 to 150 for budget online tuition. There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice: a visiting tutor serving JLT from Al Barsha spends 60 to 70 minutes on the round trip, which limits how many evenings they can offer and which slots you can have. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: What is the most common way a JLT family wastes tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Buying hours instead of naming a component. A parent worried about maths books a weekly session, the tutor works through whatever came home that week, and a year later the school report says what it said before. Nothing was diagnosed, so nothing changed, and the spend repeats. The fix costs nothing at all: write down the subject, the level, the paper and the question type that is losing marks before you agree a rate, and ask what will arrive in writing after each session. A provider who cannot answer that is selling hours rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Is marking between sessions charged separately?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the provider, and it is the question that makes two identical hourly rates mean different things. In our arrangement, scripts are marked outside the paid hour so the session is spent teaching rather than reading. Elsewhere, marking is either billed on top or quietly not done, which is why a mid-band quote can turn out to include less than a higher one. Ask the question in exactly these words before comparing numbers: is marking of my child's work included in the hourly rate, and what do I receive in writing afterwards?

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Diploma student in JLT start with?
faqs.answer: One a week on one subject at a named level, for most families, for the first six weeks. One session is enough to produce a diagnosis and a rhythm, and six weeks is long enough to test whether the arrangement is working against a real piece of marked work. Starting with two or three subjects at once makes it impossible to tell which change produced which result, and it commits a budget before anything has been learned about the match. Scale up after the week-six review, and only in the subject where the evidence says the hours are converting.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a UAE permit to teach our child privately in JLT?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time through the ministry's app and website. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any specific figure as unverified.

faqs.question: Is hiring a teacher from my child's own school the cheap option?
faqs.answer: It is usually the arrangement to avoid rather than the shortcut. The MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled where the teacher works. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and check the current policy. Beyond the rules, there is a practical problem: the person who set the assessment cannot give you an independent reading of why your child lost marks on it.

faqs.question: What time can a session start if my child buses back to JLT from Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Count two numbers before you book anything. The first is when your child is physically home, which the bus route sets and nothing else changes; from the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh schools most JLT families are looking at somewhere between 4pm and 4.45pm. The second is the hour at which a teenager stops absorbing new content, usually between 7.30pm and 8pm. The usable window is often around three hours, and an online session can sit anywhere inside it. A visiting tutor spends a third of that window in the car.

faqs.question: What does the 2026-27 fee decision mean for our tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. The practical effect for a JLT household is that the largest education line is flat for a year. That is the year to make a tutoring decision on evidence rather than in a panic, and to spread spend across DP1 and DP2 instead of banking it for the weeks before papers, where it buys the least per dirham.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects take longest to staff for a JLT family?
faqs.answer: Across the Diploma sciences and both mathematics routes, supply is generally good and a named match usually takes about a week in term time. It gets longer through March and April, when specialists are committed to exam-term students. The genuinely thin areas are Arabic as an additional language and UAE Social Studies, which Dubai schools must teach whatever curriculum they are licensed for, and some of the smaller group-six and group-three options. Where we cannot staff something properly we say so and give a reason, rather than offering a near-miss at the full rate.

faqs.question: Where must paid help stop on an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: At the point where the work stops being the student's own. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, discuss whether a research question is viable, ask hard questions about a method, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply text for any part of it. Some providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright; that is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's diploma at risk, and it is the clearest line on this page.

faqs.question: Does our child need tutoring to pass Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and anybody implying otherwise is making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process. Equivalency is an administrative assessment of certificates, not of tutoring. For the British track, reporting of the UAE requirements describes five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Verify the current rules and the IB position on the Ministry's own channels, because no sourced IB points threshold exists to publish.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free in the slot we want?
faqs.answer: You are told, before any money changes hands. The options are a named date to wait for, a teacher whose depth sits at a different level with that compromise written down, or a specialist outside the Gulf time zone with the clock difference agreed first. What we will not do is fill the brief with somebody who does not teach the component, because that gets discovered in week three and costs the family the whole block. No provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, and that silence is worth noticing when you compare.

faqs.question: Is the free trial lesson genuinely free, and what do we get from it?
faqs.answer: It is a full session with the named specialist, no charge and no card details collected beforehand. There is no trial length to run out of and no automatic conversion to a paid plan. What you receive afterwards is a written diagnosis: what the marked work shows, which topics are costing marks, and a realistic sequence between now and the assessment you named. That document is yours whether you continue or not, and you are welcome to take it to another provider and compare what they would do with it.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause during Ramadan or when we travel over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, and the online format is what makes it straightforward. During Ramadan sessions commonly move to post-Iftar slots, and they can be scheduled around prayer times and the shortened school day. Over the summer, families travelling out of Dubai keep the same tutor and the same subject, with the session time shifted to the new zone rather than the arrangement being abandoned and rebuilt in September. Nothing about this depends on a person being able to reach a JLT address, which is the part of the arrangement that usually breaks in July.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-1.tutorsIntro: These are the kinds of Diploma and Middle Years specialists a Jumeirah 1 enquiry is normally matched to: subject teachers who work in one or two subjects at one or two levels, rather than generalists who cover everything from Year 4 maths to HL Chemistry.

intro.heading: Proximity is the wrong variable, and this page explains what the right one is
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah 1 carries a hidden assumption: that the useful tutor is the nearest one. For most subjects at most levels that assumption used to hold, because a tutor who could not reach your villa on Jumeirah Beach Road could not teach your child at all. It no longer holds. The constraint that decides whether tutoring works is whether the person on the other side of the lesson has taught your child's exact course, at your child's exact level, through a full assessment cycle. Distance decides nothing about that.

Jumeirah 1 makes the point sharply. It is a low-rise villa district running along Jumeirah Beach Road between the Dubai Water Canal mouth and Jumeirah 2, with Al Wasl Road inland and Sheikh Zayed Road behind that. Jumeirah Mosque, the Etihad Museum, Mercato Shopping Centre and the beach parks sit inside it. What it does not have is a cluster of Diploma Programme sixth forms. The schools inside Jumeirah 1 skew primary and all-through, and the Diploma teaching your child needs is often delivered a few kilometres away in Al Safa, Umm Suqeim or Al Sufouh. A parent drawing a circle on a map is drawing it around the wrong thing.

The second problem with the circle is who is inside it. A twenty-minute radius from Jumeirah 1 contains a reasonable number of people willing to tutor, and a very small number who have examined or taught, say, Higher Level Chemistry or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL. Those two populations are not the same population. Narrow the search to the first and you will fill the slot quickly with somebody who learned the subject in a different system. Narrow it to the second and the geography stops mattering, because the lesson happens over video anyway.

So this page is written as a comparison. It puts Jumeirah 1 beside Jumeirah 2 and 3, Al Safa, Umm Suqeim, Al Wasl, City Walk, Pearl Jumeira and Palm Jumeirah, sets out what genuinely differs between them for a tutoring plan, and shows that the differences are about traffic windows and school-run timings rather than about who can teach the Diploma. Four tables carry the detail: the neighbourhood comparison, what the Dubai market charges in AED, the three delivery options weighed against each other, and the permit position for anybody teaching privately in this emirate.

IB Gram delivers all of this online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated plainly here rather than buried, because the alternative is a parent booking something we do not sell. What a Jumeirah 1 family gets instead is a tutor chosen from a subject pool rather than a travel radius, and a session that starts at the agreed minute because nobody is sitting on Al Wasl Road at 16:10.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-1.programmesIntro: An IB enquiry from Jumeirah 1 can land anywhere across the continuum, because the all-through schools in this part of Dubai run the Primary Years and Middle Years frameworks alongside the Diploma. The four programmes below behave differently enough that the tutoring plan changes completely between them.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than subject timetables, with no external examinations and reporting against learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning. Support at this stage is mostly about numeracy fluency, reading stamina and the habit of explaining a method out loud, which is the skill the Middle Years Programme will start marking.
programmes.countryNote: Several Jumeirah 1 and Al Safa families sit children in a PYP school and then move them into a British-curriculum secondary at Year 7, so the useful work in Years 5 and 6 is often closing arithmetic and written-accuracy gaps that a unit-of-inquiry report card does not surface.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight and reported on a 1-7 scale converted from criterion totals. Students lose marks less for not knowing content than for not addressing the criterion the task was set against, which is a teachable, diagnosable failure.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Dubai the MYP decision point arrives in Year 9, when families choose between staying on the continuum into the Diploma or moving to a school running IGCSE at 16. A tutor who knows both routes can tell you which gaps matter for which choice.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Level and three Standard Level courses, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment sits inside every subject, and the two-year shape means the autumn of the second year is already late for a student who has not started coursework.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the proximity question actually bites for Jumeirah 1 households. A Diploma student needs three Higher Level specialists at once, and no realistic travel radius around Jumeirah Beach Road contains all three for the particular combination your child chose.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A career-related study taken with at least two Diploma courses, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. It suits a student who wants depth in two academic subjects without carrying six.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by far fewer Dubai schools than the Diploma, so a Jumeirah 1 family exploring it is usually also weighing a move across the city, and wants subject support that will transfer either way.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: The subject list below is ordered by how often a Jumeirah 1 or Al Safa enquiry names it, and each entry says what the assessment actually rewards. A request for general IB help almost always resolves into one or two of these within the first conversation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation carry the grade, and the Higher Level paper set rewards students who can run a method cleanly under time pressure. Marks go on unjustified steps, abandoned algebra and the calculator paper treated as a shortcut rather than a separate skill.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with the graphic display calculator central rather than incidental. The common loss is interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence explaining what it means in context collects fewer marks than students expect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields and the Higher Level extensions, assessed through multiple choice, data analysis and extended response. Units, significant figures and the difference between describing a graph and explaining the physics behind it account for a large share of lost marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity organised around themes rather than old topic silos, with organic mechanisms and energetics the usual pressure points. The data booklet is a skill in itself, and students who have not practised finding things in it lose time they cannot recover.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led content with a heavy command-term load: state, outline, explain and evaluate each want a different shape of answer. Students who revise content without practising the command terms plateau around the middle grades.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, real-world examples and the internal assessment commentaries. The common failure is a technically correct diagram with no evaluation attached, which caps an answer well below the marks available.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided textual analysis, comparative essay work, the individual oral and the Higher Level essay. Students who read widely but never practise timed close analysis of an unseen extract find the paper harder than their reading suggests.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools applied to real organisations, with the Higher Level extension questions demanding evaluation rather than recall. The research project rewards a narrow, answerable question and punishes a broad one.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study discipline is the whole game: named places, numbers and dates attached to the right process. The fieldwork-based internal assessment needs a question that the data a student can actually collect is able to answer.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, data structures and the Higher Level abstract machine content, plus a solution-building internal assessment. Students who can code but cannot trace an algorithm on paper lose marks on exactly the questions they expect to find easy.

regions.note: High-density low-rise apartments on the Al Wasl side, with a younger resident profile and more Primary Years and Middle Years enquiries than Diploma ones. Session timing here is set by activity schedules more than by traffic.

regions.note: Across to the west, reached from Jumeirah 1 along Al Sufouh Road. Fronds have one road in and one road out, so a late lesson and a missed lesson are the same thing for a tutor who commutes, and neither applies to a video session.

sections.heading: What a 'near me' search is actually asking for
paragraphs: A parent typing "IB tutor near me" from a Jumeirah 1 address is rarely asking about geography for its own sake. The question underneath it is about three things: can somebody start soon, will the timing work around school and activities, and is this person real and accountable rather than an anonymous listing. Proximity used to be a reasonable proxy for all three, because a nearby tutor was easier to meet, easier to check and easier to fit into an evening.

Two of those three no longer depend on distance at all. A video lesson can start this week regardless of where the tutor sleeps, and it can start at 18:30 sharp because nobody is parking. The third, accountability, is better served by asking what the tutor has taught and under what permit than by asking which community they live in. The one thing proximity genuinely buys is the option of physical presence, and that is the thing IB Gram does not sell in the UAE.

It is worth being precise about what is lost. A tutor in the room can take a pen out of a student's hand and write on their page. A video tutor annotates a shared document instead, which is slower for the first lesson and faster thereafter because the annotated page still exists the following week. For a student who needs supervision rather than teaching, presence matters more. For a student who needs a Higher Level specialist, the specialist matters more, and there is no version of a twenty-minute radius around Jumeirah Beach Road that contains every Higher Level specialist a Diploma cohort needs.

So the honest reframing is this: stop asking who is nearest and start asking who has taught this exact course at this exact level. Everything below is organised around that question, beginning with the comparison a Jumeirah 1 family is usually running in their head anyway.

sections.heading: Jumeirah 1 against the next postcode over
paragraphs: Families in this corridor compare neighbourhoods constantly, usually because a sibling is at a school in one and a cousin at a school in another. The table below sets out what genuinely differs for a tutoring plan between Jumeirah 1 and the areas a proximity search returns alongside it. The pattern in the right-hand column is the point of the exercise: the differences are all about when a session can start, and none of them are about who is able to teach the Diploma.

The reason is structural. Dubai's private-school market is large and concentrated, with 227 private schools and 387,441 students across 17 curricula in 2024-25, and International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for 7% of that enrolment. A 7% share spread across a city of that size means IB sixth-form teaching clusters in a limited number of schools rather than appearing in every community, and the coastal corridor's share of those clusters sits in Al Safa, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh rather than in Jumeirah 1 itself.

Which means a Jumeirah 1 family and an Umm Suqeim family are often choosing from the same small pool of Diploma teachers, and both are choosing from a much larger pool once the lesson stops requiring a car. The practical advice that falls out of the table is to pick the session time around your own school run and ignore the tutor's address entirely, because the address has no bearing on a video lesson and the school run has a great deal of bearing on whether your child is awake enough to learn anything.

One caveat worth stating: drive times in the right-hand column describe the direction and nature of the journey rather than a measured duration, because Dubai traffic on Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road varies far too much by day and season for a single figure to be honest.

sections.heading: The variable that actually decides it: Higher Level subject depth
paragraphs: Once geography is set aside, the real scarcity shows up. A Diploma student takes six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, and the Higher Level content is where tutoring is normally needed. The subject combinations are numerous, the number of people who have taught any one of them through a full assessment cycle in a given city is not, and the two facts together explain why a local search feels thin for one family and abundant for another depending on which subjects they name.

That is also why we publish what happens when the match is hard. Most requests for Mathematics, the sciences, Economics and English at both levels are straightforward. A request for a less commonly taught Higher Level subject takes longer, and sometimes the right specialist is not in the UAE at all. When that happens the honest answer is to say so, offer a tutor based elsewhere teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and let the family decide. The alternative, which several pages in this market practise, is to accept the booking and allocate whoever is free.

The table below is written as a coverage disclosure rather than a sales list. Nothing in it promises a named individual, because availability changes weekly; it describes how the matching behaves by subject type so that a parent knows which conversation they are about to have. Where a fallback applies, the lesson format and the rate band are the same as for a UAE-based specialist, because the lesson is identical.

The practical consequence for a Jumeirah 1 household is that the subject you name matters more than the postcode you type. Two families on the same street, one asking for Standard Level Biology and one asking for Higher Level Computer Science, are running two completely different searches, and only one of them was ever going to be solved by somebody living nearby.

Context helps here too. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition weighed honestly for this corridor
paragraphs: A Jumeirah 1 parent choosing how to buy tutoring has three real options, and each is genuinely better at something. Group tuition at a centre is the cheapest per hour and the best at pacing a reluctant student through a syllabus with peers. In-home one-to-one is the best at supervision, which matters enormously for a twelve-year-old who will not open a book unless an adult is sitting there. Online one-to-one is the best at subject precision, because the pool it draws from is not bounded by a drive.

What makes the comparison concrete in this area is the access geometry. Beach Road is two lanes for much of Jumeirah 1, the school-gate congestion on Al Wasl Road runs well past 15:00, and Pearl Jumeira and the Palm fronds each have a single access route. A tutor committing to arrive at 16:30 in that environment is committing to something outside their control, and the cost of being wrong is paid in lesson minutes. A centre-based option moves the same journey onto your family instead.

IB Gram does not run in-person sessions in Dubai, so the comparison below is not a sales device; it is there so a family who genuinely needs supervision in the room can recognise that and go and find it. For the much larger group whose problem is that nobody at their school teaches Higher Level Chemistry the way their child needs it explained, the online column is the answer, and the reason is subject depth rather than convenience.

The practical test is simple. Ask what would fix the problem: somebody sitting next to your child to keep them on task, or somebody who has taught this exact course and can see in ten minutes which step they are skipping. The first is a supervision problem and the second is a teaching problem, and they have different solutions.

sections.heading: Who regulates this, and what a parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Across the UAE the map is: KHDA in Dubai, the Department of Education and Knowledge in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods, not just inspection outcomes.

A school regulator is not a tutor regulator, and the distinction matters when reading tutoring advertising. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that hold premises and employ staff, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific licence for a specific kind of business. No tutoring platform should describe itself as approved by a school regulator unless it holds the relevant permit and can show the number, and IB Gram does not hold one.

Individual private tutoring runs on a different instrument. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting a specific amount is quoting something unverified.

In Abu Dhabi there is an additional layer worth knowing even from Dubai, because families move between emirates: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. The practical reading for a parent anywhere in the UAE is to be wary of an offer to arrange your child's own classroom teacher privately.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's help on IB coursework has to stop
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internal assessment, and the Diploma core adds the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. These components are assessed as the student's own work, and the rules around them are the single most important thing a parent should check before paying anybody. This market contains operators who sell finished internal assessments outright; one advertises completed work at a four-figure AED price. A student who submits that is exposed to a malpractice finding, and a malpractice finding can end a Diploma.

The boundary is not difficult to describe. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, discuss a proposed research question, point at a paragraph and say that the reasoning does not follow, and show the student how to reference properly. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections into a finished state, or hand over anything the student then submits as their own. The test a parent can apply is whether the words on the page were generated by the student. If any of them were not, the line has been crossed.

In practice the useful help is earlier than most families expect. Most internal-assessment marks are lost at the design stage, on a question too broad to answer with the data a sixteen-year-old can actually collect, and on criterion coverage rather than content. A tutor who reads a draft against the criterion descriptors and says which criterion is unaddressed is doing the legitimate, high-value version of this work. One who returns an improved draft is doing something else.

IB Gram's position is stated here rather than implied: support on internal assessment, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay is teaching, feedback and process coaching. Nothing is supplied for submission, and no tutor will provide text that becomes part of an assessed piece. That is a constraint, and it is the constraint that keeps a student's grade safe.

sections.heading: Starting, including what happens when it does not go smoothly
paragraphs: The process is short. You describe the subject, the level, the school and what has actually gone wrong; we propose a specialist with the relevant experience and a time that fits around the Jumeirah 1 school run; you take a free trial lesson, which is one lesson at a time you choose, with no charge and no card details taken for it; and if the match is right the slot becomes weekly. If it is not right, say so and we propose somebody else. Changing tutor after two lessons is normal and costs nothing but the scheduling.

Some things go wrong often enough to be worth describing in advance. A specialist for an unusual Higher Level subject may take several days to find, and in the meantime nothing useful happens, which is better than a lesson with the wrong person. A tutor may be the right teacher and the wrong fit for a particular teenager, which is a real outcome and not a failure of diagnosis. And a student who starts eight weeks before a mock will improve exam technique but not fill two years of content gaps, which is worth saying before the money is spent rather than after.

What we will not do is promise an outcome. No tutor can commit to a grade, and any page that does is selling something it cannot deliver. What is reasonable to expect is a diagnosis within the first two or three lessons that names the specific gaps, a plan with dates attached, and a written note after each session so a parent who was not in the room knows what happened in it.

If you are comparing Jumeirah 1 against another part of the city as part of a school decision, the sister pages for Dubai Marina, JBR, JLT, Emirates Hills, The Springs, The Meadows, The Lakes and The Greens cover the same ground for those catchments, and the Jumeirah 1 area page sets out the full local picture.

faqs.question: Does searching for an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah 1 mean the tutor has to live nearby?
faqs.answer: No. The phrase is how parents search, and it is the right phrase to search with, but the thing it finds is not the thing that matters. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, so the tutor's address has no bearing on the lesson. What does matter is whether they have taught your child's exact course at the exact level. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist four time zones away who teaches on Gulf Standard Time is more useful than a generalist two streets away, and the comparison table above shows why distance changes almost nothing for a Jumeirah 1 family.

faqs.question: Is a tutor based in Jumeirah 2 or Al Safa meaningfully closer than one anywhere else?
faqs.answer: For a video lesson, no, because nobody travels. If you were hiring somebody to arrive, the honest answer is that Jumeirah 2 and Al Safa are both short journeys in the evening and unpredictable ones between about 14:00 and 15:30 when the school gates in this corridor empty. Pearl Jumeira and the Palm fronds are worse again because each has a single access route. That variability is the practical argument against buying proximity: you pay for the journey in the hourly rate and then pay for it again in lost lesson minutes when the journey goes wrong.

faqs.question: What do Dubai families typically pay per hour for IB tutoring in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published market figures as at October 2026 put budget online tutors at AED 45-150, qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 with travel included, and IB or A-Level specialists at AED 200-450 and above. Those are other providers' published rates, not an IB Gram price list; our arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: What exactly does a Jumeirah 1 family give up by choosing online over a tutor who arrives?
faqs.answer: One real thing: physical presence. A tutor in the room can keep a distractible student on task and write directly on their page, which matters most for younger children and for students whose problem is motivation rather than understanding. Everything else is either neutral or better online, including punctuality, the written record of annotated work, and above all the size of the pool you are choosing from. If your child's issue is supervision, buy supervision. If it is that nobody has explained Higher Level calculus in a way that landed, buy the specialist.

faqs.question: Which schools do secondary students living in Jumeirah 1 usually attend?
faqs.answer: The schools inside Jumeirah 1 and the strip behind it skew primary and all-through, including Jumeirah English Speaking School, Latifa School for Girls, Al Ittihad Private School Jumeirah, Emirates International School Jumeirah and the Dubai Japanese School. Most secondary and sixth-form teaching for this corridor happens a short drive away, in Al Safa, Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh, at schools such as Jumeirah College, Kings' School Dubai, Raffles World Academy and Dubai College. These are named as catchment context only; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: Can my child get a Higher Level specialist for a subject their school teaches thinly?
faqs.answer: That is the main reason families here use online tutoring. A school with a small sixth form may run Higher Level Computer Science, Global Politics or Design Technology with one teacher and a handful of students, and if the explanation is not landing there is nowhere else inside the school to go. Because matching starts from subject experience rather than geography, the pool for those courses is far larger than any Dubai travel radius. If no UAE-based specialist is free, we say so and offer somebody elsewhere teaching on Gulf Standard Time before you book.

faqs.question: How late can a weekday lesson start if the school run gets us home at 16:00?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, and that is one of the quiet advantages of video delivery. Because nobody is driving to you, a slot can be placed at 18:00, 19:00 or 20:00 without a tutor refusing it on travel grounds, and it starts at the agreed minute rather than whenever Al Wasl Road releases them. Families in Jumeirah 1 and Pearl Jumeira commonly take the first slot after dinner. The slot is fixed weekly, and it moves rather than vanishes when travel, exams or Ramadan timings change the household's rhythm.

faqs.question: Do people who tutor Jumeirah 1 households privately need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE regulates private tutoring through a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you read as unverified.

faqs.question: Does KHDA approve private tutors working with Dubai families?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most commonly misused claim in Dubai tutoring advertising. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects private schools, and it issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that hold premises and staff, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit is for a business with a physical centre. Individual private tutoring sits with MoHRE instead. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and does not describe itself as approved by any regulator, and you should be sceptical of any provider that does without showing a number.

faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content, explain what each assessment criterion asks for, discuss a proposed research question, challenge reasoning that does not follow and show a student how to reference. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a draft into a finished state, or provide anything the student submits as their own. The test is whether every word on the page was generated by the student. This matters because operators in this market sell finished internal assessments, and a student who submits purchased work risks a malpractice finding that can end the Diploma.

faqs.answer: Common subjects at common levels, which means Mathematics, the sciences, Economics and English at Standard and Higher Level, are normally resolved within a few working days. faqs.question: Is the rate different for a Jumeirah 1 address than for Dubai Marina or Palm Jumeirah?

A good trial lesson is diagnostic rather than impressive: the tutor should spend most of it finding out where the gaps actually are and then tell you, in writing, what they found and what they would do next. Nothing here is tied to a minimum number of weeks.

faqs.answer: Yes, and both are usually easier than term time. Holiday weeks are when content gaps can actually be closed, because there is no homework competing for the evening, and families travelling abroad keep their slot by shifting the time rather than cancelling the tutor. During Ramadan, sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot or earlier in the day, which works because no tutor is driving across the city to reach you. intro.heading: The variable that decides this is not distance; it is whether the knowledge is current
paragraphs: A proximity search is a reasonable instinct and it answers the wrong question. The risk for a Diploma student in Jumeirah 2 is not that their tutor lives in Al Barsha rather than two streets away. It is that the person teaching them is working from a version of the course that no longer exists, and is doing so with complete confidence, because nothing in a conversation reveals it.

This is not a hypothetical. The IB rewrites subject guides on a rolling cycle, and several of the courses Dubai students most commonly take have changed substantially inside the last few years. The sciences lost their option topics and their third paper, gained a split Paper 1 and a single scientific investigation, and had their content reorganised into themes or units with different names. Mathematics was replaced by two courses with different philosophies. English A Language and Literature changed its oral assessment entirely.

A tutor who taught the previous version well will say sensible things about the subject and prepare a student for an assessment that is not the one they will sit. The student revises option topics that are no longer examined. Nobody practises the data and experimental questions in Paper 1B, because in the old structure they did not exist as a separate component. An investigation gets planned against criteria that have been renamed and reweighted. The marks then come in low and everyone blames effort.

What a parent can do about this is specific rather than vague. Ask about the assessment rather than the subject. Ask what the components are called and what each is worth. Ask what the internal assessment is marked out of and how many criteria it has. Ask who authenticates it. Those are closed questions with checkable answers, and a tutor currently teaching the course answers them in a sentence each while a tutor who is not will reach for generalities.

The Jumeirah 2 geography is worth stating once and then setting aside. There is no Diploma school inside the district; students commute to Jumeirah Baccalaureate School one district over, to Raffles World Academy or Emirates International School in the Umm Suqeim cluster, or inland to Dubai International Academy and Dubai American Academy. They are home between 15:45 and 16:45, which makes 17:00 workable and 18:30 reliable. None of that changes which tutor is right; it only changes what time the lesson happens.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Jumeirah 2 address, or to any UAE address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The rest of this page is the material a parent needs to interrogate a match: what changed in the guides, how each internal assessment is marked and by whom, how the three core points are produced, what distinguishes a 6 from a 7, what to ask the school, which dates can be verified and which cannot, and what the Dubai market charges with a source for each figure.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: TOK, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition; the Extended Essay is an independent research piece of up to 4,000 words. The two combine to award up to three points on the diploma total, and a very low grade in either is a failing condition in combination with a low points total.
programmes.countryNote: The core is the part Dubai families most often leave unsupervised, because no weekly lesson forces it to the top of the pile. Schools set internal milestones for both, usually with a full Extended Essay draft due in the autumn of the second year, and those dates are in the Diploma handbook rather than anywhere a parent would naturally look.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the Diploma as a Jumeirah 2 household meets it, with the component a tutor has to understand rather than the content a brochure would list. Where a course was recently rewritten, the note says what the change was, because that is the thing to ask about.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Content reorganised into Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3. Options and the third paper are gone; Paper 1 now has a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, and there is a single scientific investigation marked out of 24.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Content reorganised into themes A to E, from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics. Same assessment shape as the other sciences, with the data and experimental questions of Paper 1B the component least practised at school.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content reorganised around unifying themes rather than a linear topic list. The lightest calculation load of the three sciences, and the heaviest demand on using describe, explain and suggest as the mark scheme distinguishes them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: One of the two courses that replaced the former Mathematical Studies, Standard and Higher Level courses. Calculus, trigonometry, algebra and proof, with a mathematical exploration marked out of 20 across five criteria.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The other replacement course: modelling, statistics and technology-led solutions, with the same exploration. A different course rather than an easier one, and a tutor who treats it as the old Studies course will under-prepare a Higher Level student.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis with a guiding question, Paper 2 comparative essay, an individual oral built around a global issue and two extracts, and an additional essay at Higher Level. The oral assessment changed substantially and is where out-of-date teaching shows first.

subjects.name: English B and other Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Productive, receptive and interactive skills with an individual oral built on a stimulus. Interaction is assessed as a distinct strand, which is the detail a fluent speaker without the descriptors will not mention.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with an internal assessment portfolio of commentaries written on published news articles. The compliance requirements around the articles are as examined as the economics.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a pre-released case study for one paper and a research task at Higher Level. Another course recently revised, so the component names are worth confirming.

subjects.name: History and Geography
subjects.description: Source papers, essay papers and an internal investigation or fieldwork report. The marks reward argument structure and source handling, which are teachable skills rather than content, and the investigation has its own criteria.

subjects.name: Computer Science and Design Technology
subjects.description: Both carry substantial internal assessment projects that compete for the same months as the science investigations. Families choosing them rarely discover the coursework load until the deadlines collide in the second year.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition, and an independent research essay of up to 4,000 words. Together worth up to three points. Support is process coaching: framing, narrowing, and reading drafts in order to ask questions about them.

sections.heading: What changed in the subject guides, and what an out-of-date tutor does wrong
paragraphs: The IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle, and the courses Dubai students most commonly take have seen real structural change rather than cosmetic updating. Knowing the changes is the most practical thing a parent can hold, because each one produces a specific, identifiable error in a tutor who has not kept up. The errors are not subtle. They show up as a student revising material that will not be examined.

The sciences changed most. Option topics were removed, the third paper went with them, and Paper 1 was split into a multiple-choice section and a separate set of data-based and experimental questions. The individual investigation became a single scientific investigation marked out of 24 across four criteria, and the old group project was replaced by a collaborative sciences project that is not assessed for marks. Content was reorganised: Chemistry into Structure 1 to 3 and Reactivity 1 to 3, Physics into themes A to E, Biology around unifying themes.

Mathematics was replaced wholesale. The former Mathematical Studies, Standard Level and Higher Level courses gave way to Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each available at both levels, with a mathematical exploration as the internal assessment. A tutor treating Applications and Interpretation as the old Studies course will under-prepare a Higher Level student considerably, because the statistics and modelling content at that level is substantial.

English A Language and Literature changed its oral assessment to an individual oral built around a global issue and two extracts, with an additional essay at Higher Level, and Business Management has been revised more recently again. The point is not that a parent should memorise all of this. It is that asking what my child's components are called and what each is worth is a question with a right answer, and the answer tells you whether you are talking to somebody who taught the course last year or five years ago.

sections.heading: Internal assessment across the groups, and who authenticates it
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internal assessment, and it is the part of the course where an out-of-date or non-specialist tutor does the most damage, because the criteria are specific and they have changed. It is also where the academic-honesty boundary lives, which makes understanding it a safety matter rather than only a technical one.

Two of them can be stated precisely and are worth memorising as benchmarks. The science scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria, each worth six marks, and contributes 20 per cent of the subject grade. The mathematical exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria and also contributes 20 per cent. If a prospective tutor cannot produce those figures for the relevant subject, they are not currently teaching it, and that is a reasonable inference to draw from a single question.

For the other groups the criteria and weights vary and should be confirmed with the subject teacher rather than taken from any website, including this one. What does not vary is the authentication. Each internal assessment is supervised by the student's own teacher at the school, who confirms the work is the student's own. That signature is the reason the boundary around outside help is firm. A tutor is working alongside a formal authentication process, not instead of it.

Internal deadlines are also set by the school, not by the IB, and they sit earlier than families expect because departments need time to mark and moderate before anything is uploaded. The dates live in the Diploma handbook. A parent who reads them in September and writes them into a calendar removes most of the crises this part of the course generates, and gives any tutor the one document that makes planning possible.
