sections.heading: The three extra points, and the component nobody supervises
paragraphs: The Diploma total of 45 is six subject grades out of 7, giving 42, plus up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combined. Those three points are the cheapest marks in the whole Diploma and the ones Dubai families most reliably ignore, because no weekly lesson exists to force them up the pile and no parent receives a reminder.

Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title, published by the IB for each session, and an exhibition. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece of up to 4,000 words on a topic the student chooses, supervised by a teacher at the school. The two grades combine on a published matrix to award 0 to 3 points, and a very low grade in either is a failing condition in combination with a low overall total. The current wording of that condition should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator.

Where students lose these points is predictable. Theory of Knowledge essays fail when they answer the prescribed title with opinion rather than with a structured treatment of knowledge claims and counterclaims drawn from different areas of knowledge. Extended Essays fail when the research question is too broad to answer within the word limit, which is a problem created in the first month and discovered in the last. Both are fixable early and expensive to fix late.

What a tutor can do here is narrow in a useful sense. Help a student understand what a prescribed title is asking before they start writing. Help narrow a research question until it can actually be answered with available sources or data. Explain what each assessment criterion rewards. Read a draft and ask which claim is not yet supported. What a tutor must not do is write, restructure or rewrite any of it, because the school supervisor authenticates both pieces as the student's own work.

sections.heading: What separates a 6 from a 7, in practice
paragraphs: Parents often ask what the gap between a 6 and a 7 consists of, and the useful answer is that it is a change in kind rather than in quantity. The IB publishes grade descriptors for each subject, and across all of them the lower bands describe recall and routine application while the upper bands describe evaluation, synthesis and the handling of unfamiliar material. A student who knows more facts moves up inside a band. A student who starts doing something different moves between bands.

In a science, that difference is visible in the extended-response questions. A 6 answer explains the physics or chemistry correctly in a familiar context. A 7 answer handles an unfamiliar context, states assumptions, says what the data does and does not support, and distinguishes a correlation from a mechanism. None of that is extra content. It is a habit of answering that can be taught directly, and it is what a specialist spends the final term on.

In mathematics it shows in the unstructured questions, where nothing signals which tool the examiner had in mind. A 6 student solves the problems that tell them what to do. A 7 student recognises the structure of a problem that does not. In an essay subject it shows in the handling of counter-argument: a 6 essay argues a position well, while a 7 essay engages with the strongest objection to it and resolves that engagement rather than noting it.

This is the reason a tutor's currency matters more at the top of the range than the bottom. Moving a 3 to a 5 is largely content and procedure, and a competent generalist can often do it. Moving a 6 to a 7 is about what the current mark scheme rewards in the upper bands of a specific component, which requires somebody who has seen those scripts marked. It is also the move most Dubai families are actually paying for, and the one where hiring by distance fails hardest.

sections.heading: Four questions worth asking your child's Diploma coordinator
paragraphs: Before hiring anybody, there is free information available from the school that changes what a family should buy, and almost nobody asks for it. Four questions produce most of the value, and Dubai coordinators generally answer them straightforwardly because they are reasonable questions about provision rather than challenges to it.

First: how large is the cohort in each of my child's Higher Level subjects, and is any of them taught in a combined class with Standard Level. A small or combined class is not a failing, but it tells a family where external support will produce the most return, and it is usually the third Higher Level. Second: who supervises the Extended Essay, and what are the internal milestone dates. Those dates are the planning calendar and they are not published anywhere a parent would stumble across.

Third: what are the internal deadlines for each subject's internal assessment, and in which term do they fall. In Dubai schools these commonly cluster, so three pieces can be due within a fortnight in the autumn of the second year, which is also when university applications are submitted. Knowing that in September is the difference between a plan and a crisis. Fourth: how are predicted grades decided, and from which evidence.

That last question is the most consequential and the least asked. University offers are made against predicted grades, which schools derive from internal assessment and the autumn mock of the second year. A family that understands this plans support for the first Diploma year and the early part of the second, which is when the number that reaches an admissions office is actually being set. A family that does not tends to buy expensive hours in the spring, after the prediction has already travelled.

sections.heading: Verified dates, and the ones we will not print
paragraphs: A page that publishes exam dates it has not verified is telling a parent something about everything else on it, so the position here is explicit. Cambridge and Pearson publish their timetables and key dates on their own sites and those are cited on these pages with the source. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, which means no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and none is published here.

That is a real limitation rather than a stylistic choice, and it has a practical remedy. The school's Diploma coordinator holds the official session timetable and the registration and results dates for the session a student is entered for. Those are the dates a revision plan should be built on, confirmed in writing. Secondary sources converge on particular windows, but a plan built on a date that turns out to be wrong by a week cannot be recovered, especially a retake entry.

The board dates that are sourced are worth knowing for the IGCSE siblings in the same household, since many Jumeirah 2 families run both qualifications at once. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and those two are what a UAE candidate sits. It publishes key dates for each series, and it allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable for each, warning explicitly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. The version that counts is the one the child's own centre issues, printed and dated.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the right habit for any family is to read the live official timetable rather than a date restated on a tutoring page.

sections.heading: The Dubai rate bands, and how to check each one yourself
paragraphs: Every figure in the table below comes from a published rate table or a provider's own published price, read in October 2026, and the last column says where a parent can look rather than asking anybody to trust the number. That matters in this market because the competitor research behind these pages found that no ranking page cited a source for a single AED figure, and two published prices that contradicted each other on the same site.

The spread is wide. Budget online tutoring, usually university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, which works out around AED 240 to 600 a month on one weekly session. A qualified subject teacher online is quoted at about AED 150 to 300, roughly AED 600 to 1,200 monthly. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with exam-year estimates of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more on two sessions a week. Premium named or examiner-led tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and above.

In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, travel included, with monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits and online packages at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. The in-home premium is the journey, and from a Jumeirah 2 address the relevant journey is the inland run at around six in the evening. It buys presence. It has no relationship at all to whether the person teaches the current subject guide, which is the thing this page argues matters more.

One piece of regulator context belongs beside any family budget. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. On VAT, the only claim any provider can honestly make is whether its own price includes it; the general treatment of tuition fees should be confirmed with the Federal Tax Authority. IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages and these bands are not ours.

sections.heading: Where help on assessed work becomes malpractice
paragraphs: Every Diploma student carries work that must be their own and is formally authenticated by a teacher at their school: a scientific investigation in each science, a mathematical exploration, a commentary portfolio or investigation in group 3, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay. The boundary around outside help is therefore not a matter of taste. It protects the candidate, and crossing it risks the diploma rather than a grade.

On the permitted side, a tutor may teach the underlying content, narrow a research question until it can be answered with available resources, point out that a variable is not controllable or a chosen article does not meet the requirements, explain what each criterion rewards and what it does not, and read a draft in order to ask questions about it. Questions are the whole instrument: which claim does the evidence not support, where is the counter-argument, what assumption is this conclusion resting on.

On the prohibited side, a tutor does not supply a research question as a finished product, process the data, write or rewrite any section, or return a corrected draft repeatedly until it is right. The student makes every change. The research behind these pages found a site in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is not a cheaper form of tutoring but a route to a candidate losing a qualification under IB academic-honesty rules.

Materials follow the same principle. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and the right behaviour is to reference them and link the official source rather than redistribute them. Sessions work from material the student or their school already accesses legitimately. A provider offering to send a library of papers and schemes is offering to distribute what it does not own, which is informative about the rest of the arrangement.

sections.heading: Starting from Jumeirah 2, with the limits named first
paragraphs: The useful first message from a Jumeirah 2 household is short and specific: the six subjects with Higher or Standard marked against each, the school, the component currently losing marks, and the internal deadline dates from the Diploma handbook if they are to hand. That is enough to say whether a specialist in the current guide is available at that level in that slot, which is the only question that needs answering before anything else.

If the answer is no, it is said in that first conversation. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a combination at a household's preferred time, the alternative offered is an IB specialist teaching the same syllabus from elsewhere, on Gulf Standard Time, and the family is told that is what is happening before any booking. No competitor in the research set discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a foreign phone number. Disclosure is cheaper than discovery.

The limits are worth restating plainly in one place. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International, Pearson or the IB. It holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a document issued to training institutes with premises. It occupies no office in the UAE, it has no relationship with any school named on this page, and it does not send tutors to UAE addresses.

What follows a first message is a short call to confirm the subject, level and slot, then a free trial lesson on the student's own marked work with nothing payable and no card details taken, then a written diagnosis naming the component, the cause of the losses and the first two priorities. Lessons then run as a fixed weekly hour on Gulf Standard Time, usually at 17:00 or 18:30 for a Jumeirah 2 household, with work set and marked between sessions.

process.title: List the six subjects with their levels
process.description: One sheet: each subject, Higher or Standard, the school and the year group. A Diploma student is a combination rather than a subject, and this list is what makes a match possible. It also makes it obvious which subject is the third Higher Level, which is usually where support pays most.

process.title: Ask the candidate about components, not content
process.description: What are my child's components called, what is each worth, what is the internal assessment marked out of and how many criteria does it have. Four closed questions with checkable answers. Somebody teaching the course now answers each in a sentence; somebody who taught the previous version reaches for generalities.

process.title: Send a marked script and the handbook dates
process.description: A photograph of the last marked paper and the school's internal deadline dates from the Diploma handbook. The script shows where the marks are leaving. The dates show which deadline binds. Between them they turn a general request into a plan that can be written down.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, nothing payable, no card details, built around a question or a draft the student has already been marked on. It demonstrates whether the tutor knows the assessment as opposed to the subject. If the answer is no, a different tutor is proposed rather than the same one defended.

process.title: Get the diagnosis in writing
process.description: A short note naming the component, the cause of the losses, the first two priorities and the evidence that will show whether they moved. Brief by design, so that in four weeks it can be checked against a second marked script rather than reinterpreted in conversation.

process.title: Review at week four against evidence
process.description: If the targeted marks moved, the next priority is chosen. If they did not, the diagnosis was wrong and it changes, rather than the student being asked to work harder against the same plan. That review is also the point at which a mismatch surfaces cheaply instead of in February.

whyPoints.title: Current guide, not a remembered one
whyPoints.description: Several Diploma courses have been restructured, and a tutor working from a superseded version will prepare a student for an assessment that no longer exists. The component names and weightings for the student's own subject are stated in the first conversation, because that is the check that matters most.

whyPoints.title: Criteria by letter, with their marks
whyPoints.description: The science scientific investigation is 24 marks across four criteria at 20 per cent of the grade; the mathematical exploration is 20 marks across five criteria at the same weight. Where a weight varies by subject we say to confirm it with the teacher rather than guessing on a web page.

whyPoints.title: The core counted, not forgotten
whyPoints.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three points, which makes them the cheapest marks in the Diploma and the ones most often left unsupervised. They are planned against the school's own milestone dates rather than left to appear on their own.

whyPoints.title: Only dates we can source
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates are cited from the boards' own published pages. No IB session or results date appears here, because the IB's site cannot be verified by automated checking, and a plan built on a wrong date cannot be recovered. The coordinator holds the official timetable.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a place to check them
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names where it came from and the month it was read, so a parent can verify rather than trust. The competitor research found no ranking page in this market citing a source for a single AED figure, and one publishing two contradictory prices.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated before booking
whyPoints.description: No accreditation from any regulator or board, no UAE office, no school partnerships, no in-home service anywhere in the UAE, and no promise about a grade. Where no specialist is free at the level and time a family needs, that is said in the first call and the alternative is named.

faqs.question: How do I know a tutor is working from the current subject guide?
faqs.answer: Ask four closed questions about assessment rather than content: what are the components of my child's subject called, what is each one worth, what is the internal assessment marked out of, and how many criteria does it have. Somebody teaching the course now answers each in a sentence. Somebody who taught the previous version will describe the subject instead, or talk about option topics and a third paper in the sciences, both of which were removed. It takes about two minutes and it is the single most informative thing a parent can do before hiring anybody, at any price.

faqs.question: Why do some tutors still talk about IB science options?
faqs.answer: Because they are describing the earlier course. The previous science guides had option topics that students chose between and a third paper that examined them. Both were removed when the courses were rewritten, and Paper 1 was split into a multiple-choice section and a separate set of data-based and experimental questions instead. A tutor who sets option-topic revision is sending a student to study material that will not be examined, while the data and experimental questions, which are reliably the least practised component, go untouched. It is a confident, plausible and completely wasted term.

faqs.question: What replaced Mathematical Studies, and does it matter now?
faqs.answer: Mathematical Studies, Standard Level and Higher Level mathematics were replaced by two courses, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each available at Standard and Higher Level, with a mathematical exploration as the internal assessment. It matters because Applications and Interpretation is not the old Studies course with a new name. At Higher Level it carries substantial statistics and modelling content, and a tutor who assumes it is the lighter option will under-prepare a student considerably. The course name appears on the student's school report and is worth confirming before any arrangement is agreed.

faqs.question: How is the mathematical exploration marked?
faqs.answer: Out of 20 marks across five criteria, contributing 20 per cent of the subject grade. The criteria reward presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics, and the last of those carries the most marks, which is why a well-written exploration on trivial mathematics scores poorly. A tutor may help a student find a topic capable of being developed to the right level, explain what each criterion rewards, and read a draft in order to ask questions about it. A tutor may not select the topic, do the mathematics, or write any part of the submission.

faqs.question: Who authenticates my child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: The student's own teacher at the school, who supervises the work and confirms it is the student's own. That signature is the reason the boundary around outside help is firm rather than a matter of style: a tutor is working alongside a formal authentication process rather than instead of it. The school also sets the internal deadlines for the plan, the draft and the final submission, because the department needs time to mark and moderate before anything is uploaded. Those dates are in the Diploma handbook and are usually earlier than families expect.

faqs.question: How are the three extra diploma points actually awarded?
faqs.answer: From Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an essay on a prescribed title published by the IB for each session, plus an exhibition; the Extended Essay is an independent research piece of up to 4,000 words supervised by a school teacher. The two grades combine on a published matrix to award between 0 and 3 points on top of the six subject grades, which total a maximum of 42. Those three points are the cheapest marks in the Diploma and the ones Dubai families most often leave unsupervised, because no weekly lesson forces them up the pile.

faqs.question: Can a low Theory of Knowledge grade stop the diploma being awarded?
faqs.answer: A very low grade in either Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is a failing condition in combination with a low overall points total, so it is not merely a matter of losing bonus points. The exact current wording of the condition should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from any website, because the regulations are revised. The practical consequence is that the core deserves scheduled attention in the first Diploma year, when a research question can still be narrowed cheaply, rather than attention in the final weeks when the word limit has already made the problem permanent.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a 6 and a 7 in a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: A change in kind rather than in quantity. The published grade descriptors across subjects distinguish recall and routine application in the lower bands from evaluation, synthesis and the handling of unfamiliar material in the upper ones. In a science a 6 explains correctly in a familiar context while a 7 handles an unfamiliar one, states assumptions and says what the data does not support. In mathematics a 7 recognises the structure of a problem that gives no instructions. In an essay subject a 7 engages with the strongest objection rather than noting it. None of that is extra content, and all of it can be taught.

faqs.question: What four questions should I ask my child's Diploma coordinator?
faqs.answer: How large is the cohort in each Higher Level subject and is any of them taught in a combined class. Who supervises the Extended Essay and what are the internal milestone dates. What are the internal assessment deadlines for each subject and in which term do they fall. And how are predicted grades decided, from what evidence. That last one is the most consequential and the least asked, because university offers are made against predictions derived from internal assessment and the autumn mock of the second year, which means the number reaching an admissions office is set long before the papers are sat.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the IB exam dates on this page?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the IB directly. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and publishing an unverified one would be worse than publishing none. Secondary sources converge on particular windows, but a revision plan built on a date that is wrong by a week cannot be recovered, and a missed retake entry certainly cannot. The school's Diploma coordinator holds the official timetable for the session a student is entered for, and those dates should be obtained in writing.

faqs.question: Where can I check Cambridge and Pearson dates myself?
faqs.answer: On the boards' own sites, and it is worth doing because many Jumeirah 2 households run an IGCSE sibling alongside a Diploma student. Cambridge publishes key dates and zone-specific timetables for each series, and a UAE candidate sits either the June series or the November series. It allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version, so the timetable that matters is the one the centre issues. Pearson publishes final and provisional timetables on its support pages: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma tutor cost in Dubai, and where can I check the figure?
faqs.answer: Published bands read in October 2026 run from about AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject teacher online, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500 to 650 and above at the premium end. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Those figures come from published market rate tables and providers' own published pages, and the table on this page names the source for each band. None of them is an IB Gram price list, and none of them tells you whether the tutor teaches the current guide.

faqs.question: Is a tutor living in Jumeirah 2 any use to a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and location is not the reason. Jumeirah 2 has no Diploma school inside it, and the nearby teaching population works mainly in British-curriculum and primary schools on the Jumeirah strip, so a proximity search returns excellent teachers of a different qualification. What makes somebody useful is whether they teach the named subject at the named level on the current guide. If a person two streets away does, that is a good outcome. If they do not, the two streets buy nothing, and the lesson is online in either case so the distance changes nothing operationally.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our house in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not sell in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for a Jumeirah 2 household run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's marked work and the assessment criteria on screen together and the session available to rewatch. That is also what allows the match to be made on current course knowledge rather than on willingness to drive. The Dubai in-home market exists and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, which is a fair comparison to weigh.

faqs.question: Where does help on an Extended Essay become malpractice?
faqs.answer: At the point where somebody other than the student produces part of it. A tutor may help a student understand what a research question has to do, narrow one until it can be answered within the word limit and with available sources, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, teach the underlying subject content, and read a draft in order to ask questions about it. A tutor may not supply the question as a finished thing, restructure the essay, or rewrite sections. The school's supervisor authenticates the work as the student's own, and producing assessed work for a candidate puts the whole diploma at risk.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a Jumeirah 2 student need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Anybody providing private tutoring in the UAE does. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services under Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts has been published.

intro.heading: Proximity is the wrong filter for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: When a Jumeirah 3 parent types "IB tutor near me" into Google, the search engine answers a question about geography. The problem on the table is almost never geographic. A Diploma student losing marks in Chemistry Paper 2 is losing them on a specific command term, on a specific sub-topic, in a specific question style that the published mark scheme rewards in a specific way. The tutor who fixes that is the one who has marked forty of those scripts, not the one who lives eleven minutes away on Al Wasl Road.

That is why this page is built around subject content rather than around a map. Below you will find what each of the six Diploma groups assesses, which papers carry which weighting, the command terms that decide whether a correct idea earns a mark, and the way a past paper has to be worked for the exercise to be worth the two hours it costs. Those are the things a parent can judge a tutor against before the first invoice.

Jumeirah 3 sits between two heavy school catchments. Families on this stretch send children north towards Jumeirah 1 and Al Safa, west towards Umm Suqeim and Al Sufouh, and inland towards Al Barsha and Al Quoz. The result is that two neighbours on the same street can be sitting completely different syllabus combinations: one on a full IB continuum from Primary Years through to Diploma, the other switching into DP1 from a British Year 11 and meeting Theory of Knowledge for the first time at sixteen. A single local tutor cannot credibly cover both.

IB Gram works the other way round. The subject requirement is taken first, a tutor who teaches that component at that level is matched to it, and the lesson runs over live video at a time that fits the Jumeirah school run. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India, and every country page on this site says the same thing. What a Jumeirah 3 family gets instead is a tutor chosen from the whole pool rather than from a twenty-minute radius, which matters most for the subjects a small radius never covers: Physics HL, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, Economics HL and the language B options.

The rest of this page is deliberately technical. Dubai has no shortage of pages telling parents that tuition builds confidence. It has very few that name a paper, state its weighting, and explain where the marks go. The competitor pages ranking for this query average around 2,300 words and almost none of them print a single syllabus detail or a single dirham figure. Everything below is checkable against the published assessment documents or against a source that is named.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes and Dubai schools licence them in different combinations. Knowing which one your child is actually on changes what tuition should be doing, because only one of the four ends in external examinations.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations and no numerical grades in most schools. Assessment is teacher judgement against learner-profile attributes and conceptual understanding. Support at this stage is about literacy fluency, number sense and the written reflection habits that MYP criteria will later be marked against, rather than about test technique.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving the Jumeirah 3 catchment run a full IB continuum, so a child can move from PYP into MYP without changing site. Dubai private schools must also deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the licensed curriculum, and at primary age that is where most of the extra load sits for a non-Arabic-speaking family.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria scored 0-8, with the Personal Project in the final year. Grades are generated from criterion totals rather than from percentages, which is why an MYP report can read strangely to a parent used to British percentage marks. Interdisciplinary units and service as action also carry assessment weight.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma step is the sharpest one in Dubai because MYP 5 students are not sitting external papers while their British-curriculum neighbours in Year 11 are sitting International GCSEs. Students arriving in DP1 from MYP are often strong on inquiry and weak on timed paper technique, and the first term of tuition usually goes on closing exactly that gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries internally assessed coursework worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, with the remainder examined externally in the May session that UAE schools enter.
programmes.countryNote: This is where almost all Jumeirah 3 enquiries land. Dubai schools enter the May session, and the compression between the January mock window, the internal assessment deadlines set by the school, and the external papers is what drives the demand for one-to-one help on this stretch of coast between October and March.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller framework combining at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, language development and personal and professional skills. The Diploma courses inside it are examined exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so tuition for those components is identical in content.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is licensed by only a handful of UAE schools, so Jumeirah 3 families on it usually need help with a named DP subject taken inside the CP frame plus the reflective project. The reflective project is the student's own work and is coached, never drafted.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Jumeirah 3 families ask for most often, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to disappear. A tutor should be able to talk about the component, not just the subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with a non-calculator paper at both levels. Marks are lost on unjustified steps rather than on wrong answers: method marks require the working to be visible. The exploration is assessed against five criteria and is where presentation and personal engagement are most often underweighted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted problem solving throughout, with no non-calculator paper. Students who moved here from Analysis often lose marks by under-using the graphic display calculator when the question expects it. Interpretation sentences carry real marks and are regularly left blank.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is multiple choice plus data analysis, Paper 2 extended response. The scientific investigation is marked against four criteria. Marks go on unit and significant-figure handling, on uncertainty propagation, and on explanation questions where a student describes an effect instead of giving a mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity taught together, with a data booklet supplied in the examination. Organic mechanisms and equilibrium reasoning are the two reliable mark sinks. Students who have memorised reactions without mechanisms stall at a predictable point in DP2, usually right after the mock.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. Extended-response marks depend on using the command term's demanded level of detail. A student who writes fluent prose but never names a named example loses marks they believe they have earned.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with three portfolio commentaries internally assessed. Diagram accuracy is worth real marks and is the fastest thing to fix. Higher Level adds a policy paper that rewards quantitative reasoning many students have never practised.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a research project at Higher Level and a written commentary at Standard Level. Tool application is assessed, not tool recall: a student who can define a Boston matrix but not apply it to the case study scores in the middle band.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, plus the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the essay. The individual oral is where the global issue is most often stated too broadly, which caps the marks available for every criterion that follows.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, with a developed solution internally assessed. Pseudocode accuracy in the written paper and documented testing in the solution are the two areas where otherwise capable programmers lose marks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay. Both are marked against a single holistic rubric, and the commonest failure is an essay that discusses knowledge in general rather than answering the prescribed title with specific, contrasting examples from two areas of knowledge.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 3 search for an IB tutor is really asking
paragraphs: The short answer: it is asking for somebody who can teach a named Diploma component at a named level, and the IB Gram answer is a one-to-one online lesson on Gulf Standard Time with a tutor matched to that component. Distance from Jumeirah 3 does not appear in the matching decision, because it does not appear in the mark scheme either.

The reason the query is phrased geographically is historical. For a decade the only way to buy tutoring in Dubai was to find somebody who would drive to the villa, and the search habit has outlasted the constraint. The market still prices that way: in-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on level, and a meaningful share of that figure is travel rather than teaching. A family in Jumeirah 3 paying the upper end of that band is paying partly for a car on Al Wasl Road at 4pm.

There is also a supply problem that a radius search makes worse rather than better. Diploma subjects are narrow. A student who needs Physics HL Paper 3 technique, or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL calculus, or Economics HL policy questions, needs a tutor who teaches exactly that. In a twenty-minute radius around Jumeirah 3 the number of people who genuinely teach any one of those is small, and the shortlist shrinks further once you require a slot after 6pm on a weekday.

So the honest framing is this. The geographic search is a reasonable question that the market has trained parents to ask, and the right answer to it is to drop the geography and keep the standard. The sections that follow give you the standard: what each group assesses, what the command terms demand, how a past paper is worked, and what the local market charges so you can see what the alternative costs.

sections.heading: The six groups, the papers and what each component is worth
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject splits into externally examined papers and internally assessed coursework. The proportions differ by group, and knowing them changes where tuition hours should go. A student who is strong in class but weak in timed papers and a student who is fine in papers but has a failing investigation are two different problems, and they cost different numbers of hours to fix.

The internally assessed component is the one most Jumeirah 3 families underestimate. It is marked by the school against published criteria, moderated by the IB, and in most subjects it sits around a fifth to a quarter of the final grade. It is also the only part of the Diploma where a student can bank marks calmly, months before the examination room, under no time pressure at all. Students who treat it as an afterthought are giving away the easiest marks in the programme.

The table below sets out the shape of each group's assessment. Read it alongside your child's own subject guide from school, because option choices and the exact component names vary by subject within a group. The point of the table is the proportion, not the fine detail: it tells you whether a term of tuition should be spent on paper technique or on coursework supervision.

One caution on figures. Weightings are revised when a subject guide is reissued, so the authoritative number is always the one in the guide your child's school is teaching from. Ask the subject teacher for the assessment outline rather than relying on any website, including this one, for the exact percentage in the year your child sits the examination.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that decides whether a right answer scores
paragraphs: This is the single most transferable thing a Diploma tutor teaches, and it is almost never taught explicitly at school. IB mark schemes are written against command terms, and each term carries an expected depth of response. A student who answers an "explain" question with a "describe" answer has said something true, relevant and well-written, and will still lose most of the marks. Parents reading a mock script often cannot see why, because nothing in the answer is wrong.

The effect compounds across a paper. On an extended-response science paper, four questions answered one command level too shallow is the difference between a 5 and a 6, and no amount of additional content revision fixes it, because the content was already there. This is why a tutor who marks against the published criteria finds marks that a tutor who re-teaches the topic does not.

Teaching it is mechanical. The student takes their own marked script, identifies the command term in each question they dropped marks on, states what that term requires, and rewrites the answer to that specification. After a dozen of these, the pattern transfers, and the student starts reading the command term before the content of the question - which is the habit the whole exercise is for.

The table below lists the terms that account for most of the lost marks on the scripts we see from Dubai schools, with what each one demands. Terms vary slightly in definition between subject guides, so it is worth checking the glossary in your child's own guide.

table.caption: COMMAND TERMS AND WHAT THE MARKER IS LOOKING FOR
rows: A single fact or value, no reasoning required
Students write a paragraph and waste examination time
An account of features or a sequence, no causation
Causation added, which earns nothing extra here
Reasons or mechanism, each step linked to the next
A description with the word 'because' inserted once
A balanced review of more than one position
One position argued well, the counter-position ignored
Advantages and disadvantages listed with no judgement
A conclusion reached from given information, with the reasoning
The conclusion stated without showing what it came from

sections.heading: How a past paper is actually worked, and how it is usually wasted
paragraphs: Most Jumeirah 3 students have done plenty of past papers by DP2 and have learned very little from them. The common pattern is: sit the paper, check the answers, note a percentage, feel either relieved or frightened, move on. That produces a score and no information. The paper has told you where the marks went and nobody has read the message.

The version that works is slower and covers fewer papers. The student sits one section under proper timing. The tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, not against a worked solution, because the mark scheme shows where the marks are allocated within a question rather than just whether the final answer is right. Then every dropped mark is classified: content not known, command term misread, method not shown, arithmetic, or time ran out. Those five categories have five different remedies and only one of them is revision.

The classification is what makes the exercise worth the time. A student dropping marks because the method was not written down does not need more topics taught; they need to be made to write the line they did in their head. A student running out of time needs a timing strategy and a decision rule about which question to abandon. A student misreading command terms needs the exercise in the previous section. Re-teaching content to any of those three is wasted money.

On sourcing papers: IB, Cambridge and Pearson materials are copyright, and IB Gram does not host, reproduce or supply past papers, mark schemes, subject guides or grade-boundary tables. Your child's school holds its own licensed access, and official material is available through the IB's own channels and the school's coordinator. A tutor works from whatever the student legitimately has.

sections.heading: Where the marks disappear, group by group
paragraphs: Patterns repeat across the scripts that come in from Dubai schools, and they are specific enough to be worth naming. In the sciences, uncertainty and significant figures account for a steady trickle of marks that students regard as pedantry right up until they see the total. In mathematics, unshown method is the single largest category, and it is entirely self-inflicted: the student knew the step and did not write it.

In the individuals and societies group, diagrams are the fastest fix available. An Economics diagram with unlabelled axes, no initial equilibrium marked, or no direction of shift indicated loses marks that take twenty minutes to learn to keep. Across a full paper that is often a grade boundary. Source-based questions in History lose marks on provenance: students evaluate content and ignore origin and purpose.

In language and literature, the recurring issue is the gap between a fluent essay and an answer to the question asked. Paper 2 answers that discuss two texts intelligently but never sustain a comparison score in the middle bands regardless of how well written they are. The individual oral loses marks earlier than students think, at the point the global issue is defined too broadly to be evidenced in the extracts chosen.

None of this is mysterious and none of it requires a tutor who lives nearby. It requires somebody who has read enough marked scripts in that subject to recognise the pattern in week one rather than week six, which is the whole argument for matching by component instead of by distance.

sections.heading: Coursework: what a tutor may do, and what would be malpractice
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component, and the boundary around it is strict. The work must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain the mark allocations, challenge a research question, point out where a draft does not meet a criterion, and teach the skills the task needs. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit the work to completion, and may not supply content for the student to submit as their own.

This is not a cautious house rule. Under IB academic-honesty regulations, work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student: the component can be invalidated and the Diploma can be withheld. Dubai parents are approached regularly by services that offer completed internal assessments, including at published prices. Those offers put the student's Diploma at risk, and no legitimate tutor makes them.

The practical version looks like this. The tutor reads the criteria aloud with the student and states what each one is worth. The student brings a research question; the tutor asks whether it can be answered with the data the student can realistically collect, and whether it is narrow enough to be analysed rather than described. The student collects, writes and submits. The tutor reads a draft and says which criterion is underserved and why. The school's supervisor does the formal sign-off.

Said plainly, because it is a genuine difference between providers in this market: IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work. The teaching is the product, and asking for anything else is asking for something that would harm the student it was meant to help.

sections.heading: What Diploma tuition costs around Jumeirah 3, in dirhams
paragraphs: Start with the monthly number, because that is the one a household budget is actually built on. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026 puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Packages advertised in this market include online blocks at around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home blocks at roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

Converted to an hourly view, the published bands run as follows. Budget online tutoring and university-student tutors sit between AED 45 and 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online run roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's band at AED 180 to 350. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tuition reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED advertising AED 650.

Those are market figures published by the providers named, read in October 2026, and they are not IB Gram's price list. What they are useful for is a sanity check. If you are quoted AED 600 an hour for a Standard Level subject in Jumeirah 3, you now know that sits at the very top of a published range. If you are quoted AED 60, you know which band you are buying from and what the person's likely background is.

The gap worth noticing is between the online specialist band and the in-home band for the same level of teacher. Most of that difference is the car. For a family off Jumeirah Beach Road, three or four hours of a tutor's week can disappear into Al Wasl Road traffic, and somebody pays for those hours. IB Gram's own arrangement is a free trial lesson first and a consultation that sets the plan before any money moves, which is the point at which a specific figure for your child's specific subject makes sense.

sections.heading: Getting started from Jumeirah 3, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The useful first message is short and specific: subject, level, which component is the problem, which school, and two time windows that genuinely work on a weekday. With that, a match can be proposed against a real requirement rather than against a general wish for help. Without it, the first paid lesson gets spent on discovery that an email could have covered.

Then a free trial lesson runs. It is a real lesson on a real topic with the tutor proposed for the ongoing work, not a sales call, and the output is a short written view of what is actually wrong - which of the five dropped-mark categories dominates, and roughly how many hours the fix needs. Parents are welcome to read that and stop there. Several do, decide the problem is smaller than they feared, and come back in January when the mock lands.

Now the part most providers leave out. Diploma subjects are narrow and specialists are not always free at 7pm on a Tuesday in February. When no suitable tutor is available for a requested subject, level and slot, IB Gram says so rather than substituting a generalist. The options offered are a different time with the right specialist, a short wait for one to open up, or a referral elsewhere. A Physics HL student taught by somebody who last saw the subject at Standard Level is worse than a fortnight's delay.

Scheduling notes specific to this coast. The 4pm slot is fragile for families whose school run runs inland to Al Barsha or Al Quoz, and the 6.30pm to 8.30pm window holds far more reliably. During Ramadan, sessions move later and post-Iftar slots are normal. Across the UAE winter and spring breaks, families either pause or switch to an intensive block, and both are straightforward to arrange with a week's notice.

faqs.question: Does an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah 3 mean somebody comes to the house?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one Diploma tuition over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service offered only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. The phrase is kept on this page because it is what parents search, and the honest answer is that the lesson happens on screen. What you gain is the reason the arrangement works: your child is matched to a tutor who teaches their exact component at their exact level, rather than to whoever teaches the subject and happens to live within driving distance of Jumeirah Beach Road.

faqs.question: My child's answers look correct but the marks are low. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually a command-term mismatch. IB mark schemes award against the command term, so an "explain" question answered at "describe" depth contains nothing wrong and still scores poorly. Across four or five questions on one paper that is a grade boundary. The fix is mechanical rather than academic: take the marked script, name the command term in each question where marks went, state what that term requires, and rewrite the answer to that specification. After a dozen rewrites students start reading the command term before the content, which is the habit the exercise is for.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used so they are not a waste of two hours?
faqs.answer: Sit one section under proper timing rather than skimming three whole papers. Mark it against the published mark scheme rather than a worked solution, because the mark scheme shows where marks sit inside a question. Then sort every dropped mark into one of five causes: content not known, command term misread, method not written down, arithmetic, or time ran out. Those have five different remedies and only one is revision. Most students who feel they have done hundreds of papers have never done this classification once.

faqs.question: Which part of the Diploma do Jumeirah 3 families most often underestimate?
faqs.answer: The internally assessed component. In most subjects it is worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the final grade, it is marked against published criteria, and it is the only part of the programme where marks can be banked calmly months ahead with no time pressure at all. Students who leave it late hand back the easiest marks available. Supervision is straightforward to schedule as checkpoints across a term, and the tutor's role is teaching the criteria and reading drafts, never writing any of it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an exploration or investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may explain each criterion and what it is worth, challenge whether a research question can be answered with the data available, teach the skills the task needs, and tell a student which criterion a draft underserves. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit the work to completion, or supply content for submission. Work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, so any offer of a finished internal assessment should be refused.

faqs.question: What do Dubai providers publish for Diploma tuition per hour in dirhams?
faqs.answer: Published 2026 bands run from AED 45 to 150 for budget online and university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors working online, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits with travel included, AED 200 to 450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists, and AED 500 to 650 upwards at the premium end. Named examples include Unitors from AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Those are the providers' own published figures, read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home tutor in this part of Dubai more expensive per hour?
faqs.answer: Because the hour includes a car. In-home rates in Dubai are published at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalently qualified tutor working online, and the difference is largely travel. A tutor crossing Al Wasl Road or Sheikh Zayed Road at 4pm can lose an hour either side of the lesson, and those hours are priced in. For a Jumeirah 3 family the same budget buys either fewer hours with travel included or more hours of a narrower specialist.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to move one Diploma subject by a grade?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which of the five dropped-mark causes is dominant, which is why the trial lesson produces a diagnosis before a plan. A command-term or method-mark problem can show up within six to eight focused sessions because the content is already known. A genuine content gap across several topics is a term's work at one session a week. Anybody quoting a number of hours before seeing a marked script is guessing, and anybody promising a specific grade should be declined outright.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to find a tutor for near Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: The narrow Higher Level components. Physics HL, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, Chemistry HL option content, Economics HL policy papers and the language B options all have small local supply, and the shortlist shrinks further once a weekday evening slot is required. This is the clearest case for dropping the distance filter: the same subject taught at the wrong level, or by somebody who has only taught Standard Level, does not fix a Higher Level paper problem.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Jumeirah 3 families need a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, and a parent can simply ask a tutor to show their permit.

faqs.question: What does KHDA actually do, and does it approve tutors?
faqs.answer: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. It licenses schools and, separately, issues educational services permits to training institutes that operate premises with staff. It does not certify individual private tutors; that sits with MoHRE. IB Gram is not accredited or endorsed by KHDA and does not claim to be. An inspection report is still worth reading, because it names the subjects where a school's own teaching was judged weakest.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Mathematics with Physics is a common pairing because the mechanics and calculus overlap heavily. Chemistry with Biology works for medicine applicants. Two Group 3 subjects rarely pair well, because the assessment technique differs more than the content suggests. Where a pairing is not credible the honest answer is two tutors, and it is better to be told that than to have one person cover a second subject they teach a level below the first.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education requirement affect Diploma students?
faqs.answer: It affects the timetable rather than the Diploma grade. All Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student the practical effect is less free periods than a parent expects, which changes how much work realistically goes home.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for my child's subject and time?
faqs.answer: You are told, and you are offered a choice: a different slot with the right specialist, a short wait for one to open, or a referral elsewhere. No generalist is quietly substituted for a specialist. Diploma components are narrow and February evenings are the tightest window in the year, so this does happen. Being told is better than the alternative: a Higher Level student taught by somebody whose experience stops at Standard Level loses a term before anybody notices.

faqs.question: When can a weekday Diploma session realistically start for a Jumeirah 3 family?
faqs.answer: If the school run stays on the coast, a 4.30pm start is usually workable. If it runs inland to Al Barsha, Al Quoz or Al Sufouh, the 4pm slot is fragile and the 6.30pm to 8.30pm window holds far better. Because lessons are online there is no travelling tutor to be delayed, so a late start costs nothing beyond the family's own evening. During Ramadan the whole pattern shifts later and post-Iftar sessions are normal rather than exceptional.

intro.heading: Why "near me" is the wrong filter in a villa community
paragraphs: Search "IB tutor near me" from a villa in Jumeirah Golf Estates and the results will be shaped by proximity, which is the one variable that does not predict whether a tutor can help. This community holds a few thousand households spread around two golf courses. The number of adults inside that circle who teach a specific IB course to examination standard is small, and for Higher Level sciences it is frequently zero. Proximity is easy to measure, which is why search engines use it, and almost irrelevant to a Diploma grade.

What does predict the outcome is time. Not the tutor's travel time but your child's. The campuses Jumeirah Golf Estates families use for IB are not the ones closest to the gates: the immediate ring is largely British curriculum, and the IB continuum schools sit further out towards Al Barsha South, JVT, the Meadows and Arabian Ranches. That means a longer run twice a day, a later arrival home, and a much narrower usable window for anything requiring concentration.

So this page is written from the school day outwards. It maps the real finish-and-drive arithmetic for each cluster a Jumeirah Golf Estates child might attend, then sets out what should happen inside the window that is left: criteria work for a Middle Years Programme student, paper technique for a Diploma student, supervision blocks for the core components. Getting the content right in forty-five usable minutes beats getting ninety minutes of the wrong thing.

IB Gram delivers that as one-to-one live video tuition at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The practical gain is that no part of your child's remaining evening is spent waiting for somebody to arrive, and the tutor can be the person who teaches that exact course rather than the person who lives nearest.

It is worth being blunt about what the local search result is doing in the meantime. A place-name query is answered by whoever has optimised for that place name, and research across sixty-odd competitor pages in October 2026 found agencies routing UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, one page displaying a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page, and several listing twenty-five or more schools as clients with no visible relationship. Proximity in a search result is a marketing claim. A tutor's school, the papers they have marked and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit are facts you can check, and those are the three questions worth asking anybody.

The sections that follow name the school clusters and their timings, explain what the Diploma points structure actually rewards, set out the Middle Years Programme criteria by letter, price the Dubai market with attribution, and state the academic-honesty boundary that matters most in the Internal Assessment weeks. There are no grade promises here and no statistics we cannot source.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-golf-.subjectsIntro: The requests we receive from this part of New Dubai cluster in the Higher Level sciences and mathematics, with English A and the core components arriving in the second Diploma year. Here is what each one assesses and where the marks go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus, complex numbers and the Higher Level Paper 3 investigation. Marks disappear on unwritten method lines, on radians quietly reverting to degrees, and on "show that" questions answered by restating the result rather than deriving it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling, financial mathematics and, at Higher Level, graph theory. The characteristic failure is interpretation: a regression run correctly on the calculator and then described in words that do not match the context the question set.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity, with organic mechanisms and energetics carrying the heaviest mark losses. The extended-response paper rewards state symbols, significant figures and correct data-booklet use, and penalises loose language about bond strength and stability.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields and waves, extended at Higher Level into rotational dynamics and quantum physics. Units, vector direction and naming the controlled variable in data analysis are where otherwise capable candidates lose a grade boundary's worth of marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Organised around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and continuity. Command terms carry more weight here than in any other science: outline and explain attract different mark allocations and students regularly answer the wrong one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, the Individual Oral on a global issue, and the HL Essay at Higher Level. The Individual Oral repays coaching fastest because it is a structured fifteen-minute performance with a published mark scheme.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and a three-commentary Internal Assessment portfolio. Diagrams must be fully labelled and then used in the prose; an unmentioned diagram earns very little whatever its quality.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Analytical tools and finance assessed through structured response and a research project. The ceiling is almost always application: tools reproduced accurately but never applied to the stimulus organisation in front of the candidate.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, contributing with the Extended Essay up to three points. Support is about framing a knowledge question precisely and holding a counterargument, not about supplying content or opinions.

subjects.name: Extended Essay

sections.heading: What the school day leaves you, campus by campus
paragraphs: An IB session time is decided by arithmetic, not preference. Take the campus finish, add the gate queue, add the drive, add the twenty minutes a teenager needs before they can think. For a Jumeirah Golf Estates family whose child attends in Al Barsha South, that chain typically ends somewhere after 4.30pm, and if there is a club in Dubai Sports City afterwards it ends after six.

The reason this matters more for IB than for other curricula is the homework load. A Diploma student arriving home at 4.35pm already has two or three hours of subject work plus whatever the core components demand that week. A tuition session dropped into the middle of that at 5pm competes with the school's own deadlines. Dropped in at 7.15pm, after the first pass at homework, it has something concrete to work on.

There is a quieter advantage to the later slot. A student who has already attempted the problem set arrives with a specific confusion rather than a general feeling of being behind, and a specific confusion is what a specialist can fix in forty minutes. Sessions scheduled too early in the evening tend to become supervised homework, which is a much lower-value use of a subject teacher.

sections.heading: What "near me" returns, and why it misleads
paragraphs: A local search is answered by whoever has optimised for the place name, which in this market is often a provider with no presence here at all. Research across sixty-odd competitor pages in October 2026 found agencies routing UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, one page showing a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page, and several listing twenty-five or more schools as clients with no apparent relationship. Proximity in a search result is a claim, not a fact.

The second problem is that even genuine local supply is thin for the courses that matter. A school needs one chemistry teacher per few hundred students, and only some of those have taught the Diploma rather than A Level. Narrow the catchment to one gated community and the expected count for Higher Level Chemistry is below one. That is arithmetic, not a judgement about the neighbourhood.

Our response is to publish the coverage position rather than imply it is universal. The table sets out, by course, how a match typically resolves for a family in this part of New Dubai and what we tell you when the answer is no. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is exactly why ours is worth reading before you book anything.

The right question to ask any provider is therefore not whether they have somebody nearby. It is which school that tutor teaches at, which papers they have marked, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Those three answers are checkable; a pin on a map is not.

sections.heading: How the Diploma actually scores, and what tuition can move
paragraphs: Parents often arrive wanting a higher total without a clear picture of where the total comes from. Six subjects, each marked out of 7, gives 42. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three more, to a maximum of 45. Each subject's grade is built from externally assessed papers plus an Internal Assessment marked by the teacher and externally moderated.

That structure tells you where tuition is efficient and where it is not. A student sitting on 4 in a Higher Level science is usually losing marks to technique, which responds to a term of focused work. A student sitting on 6 and wanting 7 is a different project: the final boundary is won on precision, data-booklet discipline and extended-response structure, and it takes paper-by-paper work rather than more content.

The core is the most undervalued part of the total. Up to three points sits in two pieces of work that are planned and written over many months, and both are highly coachable at the framing stage without anyone crossing an honesty line. A badly framed Extended Essay question cannot be rescued in April; a well-framed one makes the writing straightforward.

What tuition cannot do is change an Internal Assessment after submission, or substitute for the student's own attempt at a problem. We say no to both, and the second one is the reason we keep sessions weekly rather than daily: a student needs unassisted practice between lessons, because the unassisted attempt is where the learning actually happens.

sections.heading: Middle Years Programme criteria, by letter
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme reports confuse parents more than any other document in Dubai schooling, because the numbers look like marks and behave like something else. Each subject group is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, each scored on a published band, with the classroom teacher writing task-specific clarifications that say what the criterion means for that particular piece of work.

The useful consequence is diagnostic. A student scoring consistently well on knowledge and understanding and consistently badly on the criterion that asks for evaluation or reflection has a very specific, very fixable problem: they are writing what they know instead of what the criterion asked for. Nobody has usually told them that, because the criterion language is written for teachers.

This is why Middle Years Programme tuition should be short and targeted. Four to six sessions, working from the teacher's own clarifications and the student's own returned tasks, usually moves the weak criterion. Then it should stop. A standing weekly slot through Years 7 to 9 is rarely the right answer and is the most common way money gets wasted in this part of the market.

One Dubai-specific point: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Middle Years Programme in all Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. That is additional timetable load which the programme brochure does not show, and it is worth factoring in before adding a weekly tuition commitment.

sections.heading: What IB tuition costs around here, and what you are paying for
paragraphs: Begin with what the travel premium buys, because that is the comparison a Jumeirah Golf Estates family is implicitly making. An in-home one-to-one visit in Dubai is advertised at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with one provider publishing monthly packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. The difference is a car, not teaching minutes.

Against that, a qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, one UK-based agency at AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led provision as high as AED 650. Budget online tuition, typically a university student, runs from AED 45 to AED 150. Monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

All of those figures were researched in October 2026 from the providers and rate surveys named, and they describe the market rather than IB Gram. Our own fee is quoted after the free trial lesson. What we will not do is publish a price we cannot explain or a package whose conditions are not on the same screen as the word free.

One piece of budget context worth having: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are the fixed line in your planning this year; tuition is the one you control.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment weeks: where families get into trouble
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment, and the weeks before the school's internal deadline are when the pressure in a household peaks. It is also when a certain kind of provider becomes very helpful. One operator in this market was found advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller.

The boundary is clear and worth stating in plain terms. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion, interrogate and narrow a research question, point out that a method will not produce analysable data, mark a draft against the criteria and say which criterion is losing marks and why, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not write any part of the work, rewrite sentences into their own prose, hand over a finished research question, supply data the student has not collected, or edit a draft to completion.

There is a related rule about materials that parents should expect. We do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. Tutors reference them and link to the official source. A provider offering a folder containing everything is telling you something about the rest of their practice.

One defensive habit: keep the written notes a tutor sends after each session. If authenticity is ever questioned, a dated record showing the help given was feedback on the student's own drafts is the best protection available, and it costs nothing.
