sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor in the UAE, and what nobody is approved for
paragraphs: A proximity search returns a distance and a star rating. It does not return the one document that governs whether the person may lawfully teach your child for money, which is the private tuition work permit. That permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years at a time. The route to it is the MoHRE smart app, the website or the e-services system, and MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Nothing about a Jumeirah Golf Estates pin on a map result tells you whether any of that was ever done, so ask the tutor directly, and treat a vague reply as an answer in itself.

The eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Knowing that last one explains a good deal about the lower end of the rate table. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted and we will not quote one.

A boundary to respect: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That has been reported in the regional press and should be checked against the current ADEK policy document before being treated as exact wording. The practical rule is to never engage your child's own classroom teacher privately.

Finally, what nobody here is approved for. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We name regulators to explain what they govern, which is a different thing entirely.

sections.heading: Starting from Jumeirah Golf Estates, and what can go wrong
paragraphs: The three things worth sending first are the programme and exact course, the campus and the last marked assessment, and the two or three evening windows that genuinely survive the drive and the clubs. With those, matching is usually quick. Without the third, we will propose a slot that collapses within a month and both of us will have wasted a term.

Then take the free trial lesson. Its only real purpose is to test whether this tutor can explain your child's specific confusion, so hand them a lost question from the last assessment beforehand. A trial spent on introductions tells you nothing you could not have read on a profile.

What can go wrong, said honestly. Sometimes no specialist in the exact course is free in your windows, particularly for Higher Level Physics close to the May session and for Theory of Knowledge support; you get the wait and, where the available tutor is outside the UAE, you are told that before paying. Sometimes the match is wrong on personality, and we change the tutor without arguing. And sometimes the diagnosis is wrong: a student described as weak in a subject turns out to be losing marks on reading questions, which is a different and shorter piece of work.

Nothing here is a promise about a grade. We publish no guaranteed outcomes, no satisfaction percentages without a sample size and method, and no self-asserted ratings. In this market, the absence of those claims is itself a useful signal.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah Golf Estates who comes to the house?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach Jumeirah Golf Estates students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do operate in this part of Dubai, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. What you gain by dropping the visit is a tutor chosen for the exact course your child sits rather than for how far they live from the Earth course.

faqs.question: Which schools near Jumeirah Golf Estates actually teach the IB?
faqs.answer: Not the closest ones. The immediate ring around this community is largely British curriculum, and IB provision sits a ring further out: fifteen to twenty-five minutes towards Al Barsha South and JVT, or twenty to thirty minutes towards the Meadows, Emirates Hills and Arabian Ranches. That extra distance is the main reason IB families here report later homework starts than their neighbours. Schools are named on this page only to describe the local environment; IB Gram has no affiliation, endorsement or partnership with any of them, and none is a client.

faqs.question: What is a realistic session time for an IB student living in Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: Between 6pm and 8.15pm on weekdays, and the later end of that if there is a club involved. Work it out from your own row: campus finish, ten to twenty minutes of gate queue, twelve to thirty-five minutes of driving, then twenty minutes before a teenager is useful. A Diploma student travelling from Al Barsha South is rarely settled before 4.40pm, and the first pass at school homework should come before tuition, not after. Weekend mornings are the most underused slot here and the best one for Extended Essay work.

faqs.question: Should tuition come before or after my child's own homework?
faqs.answer: After, in almost every case. A student who has already attempted the problem set arrives with a specific confusion, and a specific confusion is what a subject specialist can resolve in forty minutes. A session scheduled before homework tends to become supervised homework, which is a low-value use of a Higher Level teacher and builds dependence rather than technique. The exception is the week before a mock, when working straight through a past paper under timed conditions is more useful than anything the school has set.

faqs.question: How are IB Diploma points actually made up?
faqs.answer: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each marked out of 7, giving 42. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three more, to a maximum of 45. Each subject grade combines externally assessed papers with an Internal Assessment marked by the teacher and externally moderated. Knowing the structure tells you where effort pays: moving a 4 to a 5 is usually technique work, moving a 6 to a 7 is precision on papers, and the core points are won months earlier at the question-framing stage.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report has numbers I do not understand. What are they?
faqs.answer: Each Middle Years Programme subject is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, each scored on a published band, with the teacher writing task-specific clarifications describing what the criterion means for that task. The numbers are criterion scores, not percentages. They are extremely useful diagnostically: a student strong on knowing and understanding but weak on the thinking-critically criterion is describing where evaluation was wanted. That is a reading-the-task problem, usually fixable in four to six sessions, after which the tuition should stop rather than continue.

faqs.question: How much does IB tuition cost for a family in this part of New Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market research across published UAE provider pages in October 2026 found qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, in-home visits including travel at AED 180 to AED 500, budget online tuition from AED 45 to AED 150, and premium examiner-led provision quoted as high as AED 650. Monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Is the in-home premium worth paying for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is arithmetic rather than principle. The gap between an online qualified tutor at AED 150 to AED 300 and an in-home visit at AED 180 to AED 500 is travel time, not teaching time. In this community that travel is substantial, and it also shrinks the pool of tutors to those willing to make the drive, which is exactly the wrong constraint for a Higher Level science. For a Primary Years child the in-person advantages are real and we would say so; from Year 10 upwards the tutor's subject knowledge dominates.

faqs.question: Which IB exam session do Dubai students sit, and when should support start?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. We deliberately publish no IB examination or results dates here, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unchecked date is worse than none; get yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org. On timing, work backwards: Internal Assessment deadlines are set by the school and sit a term or more ahead of the papers, mocks sit roughly a term ahead, and the last eight weeks belong to past papers under timed conditions. Beginning after mocks means several useful levers have already gone.

faqs.question: Where does Extended Essay help stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the most valuable help comes earliest. A tutor can interrogate and narrow the research question until the available evidence can actually answer it, check that a method will produce usable material, explain what each criterion rewards, mark a draft against those criteria, and teach citation properly. A tutor cannot write or rewrite any part of it, supply a finished question, provide data the student has not gathered, or edit it to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that boundary, and a badly framed question is not rescuable in the final month.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to take Arabic alongside the IB in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Because outside content for these subjects needs Ministry of Education permission, support follows the school's own material.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor really knows the IB or just the subject?
faqs.answer: Ask three concrete questions during the free trial. Which papers does this subject have, and what is each worth at my child's level? What are the Internal Assessment criteria for it, by letter, and what are the mark allocations? And can you mark this specific lost question and tell me what the mark scheme wanted? A specialist answers the first two without hesitation and the third with a mark scheme open. A capable generalist will talk about confidence and study skills instead, which is a different and much cheaper service.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or around school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the clearest practical benefit of online delivery here. Sessions shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan, move within the week when an Internal Assessment deadline or a tournament collides, and pause through mock and final examination weeks. None of that requires anyone's round trip to be renegotiated, so it is usually settled in the same week. We also agree a stop date at the outset, typically a named deadline or study leave, so the commitment is reviewed deliberately rather than renewed by default.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for my child's Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You are told the realistic wait, offered a shorter diagnostic block in the meantime if that is useful, and told where the available specialist is based if they are outside the UAE, all before any payment. Availability is thinnest for Higher Level Physics in the weeks before the May session, for Computer Science, and for Theory of Knowledge support. What we will not do is put a generalist in front of a Higher Level student and let the term run. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is why ours is here.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold any IB or KHDA approval I should be looking for?
faqs.answer: No, and treat that claim as a warning wherever you meet it. IB Gram is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the permit issued specifically to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and we operate no UAE office or centre. Regulators are named on this page to explain what each governs. No individual tutor anywhere holds a KHDA licence, because that permit covers premises rather than people.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-golf-.closingHeading: Plan the slot, then pick the specialist
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-golf-.closingBody: Searching for an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah Golf Estates is a reasonable instinct and the wrong first move. Start with the school day instead: the campus, the finish time, the drive, and the two evening windows that survive the clubs. Then pick the person who teaches your child's exact course, wherever they are. intro.heading: The number before the name
paragraphs: The published Dubai tutoring market runs from about AED 33 an hour to about AED 650. That is a twentyfold spread for something sold under one word, and it tells you immediately that 'tutor' describes several different products. Three of the six strongest competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote US dollars at families who transact in dirhams.

So the first thing this page does is put the figures in one place, attributed to whoever published them, with the month we read them. The second is to convert them into the number that actually matters, which is what two years of Diploma support costs rather than what one hour costs. Nobody buys an hour, and an arrangement priced optimistically stops in week six.

The third thing, and the most useful, is to say where the money should go. In the Diploma that is not obvious, because a substantial share of each subject grade sits in criterion-marked coursework with deadlines set by your child's school, and that coursework is the most coachable part of the course. Families routinely spend on content revision in the final term and nothing on the component that was winnable a year earlier.

On the geography in the search phrase: proximity costs more and buys less. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's survey, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The premium is a commute, and in a gated community reached from Sheikh Zayed Road at half past five that commute is long.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are an India-only service and there is no office or centre here. What a Jumeirah Islands family gets is live online one-to-one tuition on Gulf Standard Time, matched by subject and level. We target the near-me phrase because that is what parents search, and then describe what the service actually is.

There is also a scarcity question inside the price, and it is subject-specific rather than general. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, and within that the Higher Level sciences and Analysis and Approaches are the combinations fewest tutors can teach well. Those are the subjects where you will meet the specialist band and a quoted wait in the spring term.

One piece of household context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. The school-fee line in your budget is therefore stable while you plan this one, which is a better starting position than families here have had for several years.

sections.heading: What the near-me search is really asking about
paragraphs: It is usually a price question in geographic clothing. The parent wants someone competent, soon, without another journey, at a figure they can sanity-check against a neighbour's. Proximity serves as a proxy for convenience and for a price that feels local, and in this market neither proxy holds.

On convenience, IB Gram's answer is live online one-to-one teaching scheduled around when your child reaches home. Since Jumeirah Islands has no school and no tuition centre inside the gates, the day already contains two journeys, and online removes the third rather than adding one. There are no UAE home visits and no UAE centre.

On price, the published figures are the opposite of the intuition. The cheapest band in this market is online supervision at AED 33-65 an hour on Tutopiya's and EdFlik's figures. The most expensive band for equivalent teaching is in-home, at AED 180-500 including travel. Hiring locally does not reduce the price; it increases it and narrows the pool.

The reason it narrows the pool is simple scarcity. A tutor willing to drive into a gated community at half past five, for that rate, in the spring term, is drawn from a smaller and less specialised group, because a sought-after Higher Level specialist has no reason to spend ninety minutes in traffic.

Where in-person provision is genuinely worth the premium is with a child who will not stay on task without an adult present, a household with nowhere quiet in the early evening, or hands-on equipment work. If that is your situation, pay it, hire locally, and treat the published in-home band above as the market you are buying in.

sections.heading: Two years of Diploma support, costed
paragraphs: This is the arithmetic that decides whether an arrangement lasts, and it should be done before the first session rather than discovered in February. Bestimate's Dubai survey estimates AED 240-600 a month for a weekly one-hour arrangement at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support in a single subject.

Two Higher Level subjects at one session each therefore sits in four figures monthly through the Diploma, and that is before anything is added for coursework blocks or the final-term rise in frequency. A family planning from an hourly rate rather than a monthly one typically commits to roughly twice what they intended and stops in the second term.

The alternative shape costs less and works better. One weekly hour in the single subject that most needs it from the start of the first Diploma year, plus one defined coursework block per major component, plus a rise to two or three sessions a week in the last six weeks. That spreads the spend, keeps it cancellable and avoids the compounding that makes late intervention expensive.

Two costs belong in the same budget and are not tutoring. Examination entry fees, which the school charges and which rise for late or private-candidate entries. And, for a student who may need it, the cost of a retake session, which is a second entry plus a university application cycle carried out on a provisional result.

sections.heading: Where the spend should go inside a Diploma subject
paragraphs: This is the part almost nobody sets out, and it changes outcomes more than the hourly rate does. A Diploma subject grade is not one thing. Written papers carry most of it, and internal assessment carries a substantial share, commonly around a fifth, marked against published criteria with a deadline set by your child's school rather than by the IB.

That coursework share is the most coachable part of the course. Criterion descriptors are published, the failure modes are predictable, and a tutor can legitimately teach the criteria, narrow the research question, teach the writing conventions and give feedback on the student's own drafts. Six to ten sessions, timed to the school's deadline, is a defined piece of work with a visible result.

Content revision in the final term is the opposite: open-ended, expensive per unit of improvement, and competing for the scarcest slots in the market. Families spend here because it feels like the exam is the thing, and the exam is indeed the thing, but by April the available gains are in technique and conduct rather than in content.

The third category is data and technique skills that pay twice. Data analysis and uncertainties in the sciences appear in the written papers and in the investigation. Command-term discipline in biology and the humanities appears in every answer on every paper. Both are cheap to teach and are routinely skipped because they are not topics.

sections.heading: Why some subjects cost more than others
paragraphs: Price in this market tracks scarcity rather than difficulty, and the scarcity is specific. Teaching Higher Level physics or chemistry well requires depth in fields and induction, or in organic mechanisms and quantitative equilibrium, plus familiarity with how the investigation is marked. Those combinations are thin everywhere and thinner in any single neighbourhood.

Demand is also concentrated in the same weeks and hours across the whole city. Every Diploma family wants a weekday slot between 17:00 and 19:00 in the spring term. A specialist with four Higher Level students already has a full early evening, and insisting that they also drive to a gated community removes most of the remaining candidates.

The practical consequence is that timing is leverage you can use for free. A weekly Higher Level chemistry slot booked in September costs the same per hour as one booked in March and gets a materially better tutor, because in September the specialist's calendar is still open. That is not a scarcity tactic; it is how any calendar of appointments fills.

We publish the position rather than imply unlimited supply. Where a combination is not available you are told, with a date, and offered an off-peak slot with the specialist, an interim tutor with a stated handover, or a wait. Where a tutor covering a UAE family is based outside the UAE and teaches on Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

sections.heading: The cheapest things that actually work, ranked
paragraphs: If the budget is the constraint, these are the interventions with the best return, cheapest first. Several of them cost nothing at all, and a provider who tells you about them is reducing their own invoice, which is a reasonable test of whether you are being advised or sold to.

Free: asking the school which criterion scores or component marks produced a disappointing grade. Free: asking for the school's internal assessment and Extended Essay calendar in September so the deadlines stop being surprises. Free: reading a marked paper with your child and asking, question by question, what they were thinking.

One session: a diagnostic with a subject specialist that produces a written read of where the student actually sits. One to three sessions: command-term work, which transfers across every paper in every subject. One to three sessions: narrowing an Extended Essay or internal assessment research question before any writing starts, which is where most of that component's marks are decided.

Six to ten sessions: a coursework block timed to the school's deadline, or a defined topic block attacking a named weakness from a marked paper. These have scope and an end point, which is what makes them measurable and what stops them becoming an open-ended monthly charge.

The most expensive pattern, and the one most families buy, is two or three sessions a week per subject from February. It costs the most per unit of improvement and competes for the scarcest slots in the city. The table ranks all of this so you can spend the first fifty dirhams well.

sections.heading: Questions to ask before you pay anyone
paragraphs: Hidden extras are where a quoted rate stops resembling the invoice. Ask these in writing, of us or of anyone else, and treat evasion as an answer. None of them is an awkward question and all of them have a short factual reply.

Start with the unit. Is the price per hour or per lesson, and how many minutes is a lesson? A fifty-minute lesson charged as an hour is a difference nobody mentions. Then ask whether the dirham figure quoted is the figure you will be charged. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a general fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, so ask the provider directly.

Then the mechanics. What happens to a session you cancel with a day's notice, and to one the tutor cancels? Is there a minimum commitment? What happens to unused sessions in a package? Does the rate change closer to the examinations, as it does with several providers? Is the trial genuinely free, with no card details taken?

Then the people. Who is the tutor, where are they based, do they hold a Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit, and have they taught this subject at this level to a May session? And if an examiner claim is being made, what evidences it, given that examiner status must never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

Finally the question that sorts providers fastest: what will you not do? The right answer includes not writing any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, and not promising a grade. Anything else tells you what you need to know before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: The cost of a badly chosen hour
paragraphs: A session at the wrong time of day is not cheaper for being wasted, and in this community that risk is higher than average. No school sits inside Jumeirah Islands, so every child travels out and the return leg usually serves two or three other communities first, putting arrivals home between roughly 15:40 and 16:50.

A 16:30 session therefore starts before a teenager has eaten or changed, and the first twenty minutes go on settling. At the mid-market band that is a recurring weekly loss for no benefit, and it is the mechanism by which arrangements quietly end in week five with nobody quite able to say why.

17:00 is the dependable start here, 17:30 for children travelling from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. Second-year Diploma students frequently work better at 19:30 for essay and Theory of Knowledge work, when they can sustain an argument rather than race. For mathematics and quantitative work, earlier is better because accuracy is the first thing tiredness takes.

Weekend slots are underused and they are where the long work belongs. A Saturday morning session is the only ninety-minute block in a Jumeirah Islands week, which makes it the right place for a full timed paper or a proper drafting session, with Sunday used to review what came out of it.

Bus routes are built around schools rather than communities, so ask your transport office for your own route timings rather than copying a neighbour's slot. Twenty minutes is the difference between an hour that works and an hour you have paid for twice.

sections.heading: What no amount of money buys
paragraphs: A cost page should be honest about the ceiling. The first thing money cannot buy is coursework. A tutor may teach criteria, narrow a research question, teach referencing and give feedback on the student's own drafts, and may not write, part-write, rewrite or supply any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project.

Operators in this market do sell completed internal assessments at four-figure prices. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller, which is precisely why no price makes it a sensible purchase.

The second is a grade. No honest provider can promise a score, a number of marks or a percentage improvement, and anyone offering a money-back grade guarantee is telling you something about their business rather than their teaching. We publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage either, because a statistic without its sample size, date and method is unverifiable.

The third is official material. We do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They are cited and linked, and your child's school holds licensed access to what it needs.

The fourth is a regulator's endorsement. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit. Any provider implying that a regulator has vetted its tutors is worth questioning closely.

Add school examination entry fees, which are not tutoring costs but belong in the same budget. None of these is our price.

faqs.question: Is a local tutor cheaper than an online one in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published figures say the opposite. The cheapest band in this market is online supervision at AED 33-52 on Tutopiya's figures and AED 45-65 on EdFlik's. In-home one-to-one is the most expensive band for equivalent teaching, at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's survey and AED 200-500 for independent home tutors. You are paying for travel, and in a gated community reached off Sheikh Zayed Road in the evening peak that travel is forty to ninety minutes round trip.

faqs.question: Which part of a Diploma subject is worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: The coursework, and the technique that pays twice. Internal assessment commonly carries around a fifth of a subject grade, is marked against published criteria, and has a deadline set by your child's school a long way before the papers. It is the most coachable component in the course. Data analysis and command-term discipline are the other two, because they earn marks across every paper and in the coursework as well. Content revision in April is the most expensive and least efficient purchase.

faqs.question: Why do physics and chemistry cost more than economics?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, not difficulty. Teaching Higher Level physics or chemistry well needs depth in fields and induction, or organic mechanisms and quantitative equilibrium, plus knowledge of how the investigation is marked. Those combinations are thin in any one city. Demand is also concentrated in the same weeks and the same early-evening hours, so the specialists fill up. Economics and English are better staffed and usually available at the qualified band within the same week.

faqs.question: What can we do that costs nothing at all?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they are the best-value items on this page. Ask the school which component or criterion scores produced a disappointing grade, which converts an unreadable report into a plan. Ask in September for the internal assessment, Extended Essay and mock calendar, so the deadlines stop arriving as surprises. And read a marked paper with your child question by question, asking what they were thinking, which distinguishes a content gap from a method problem from a misread question.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to houses in Jumeirah Islands?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no office or centre here either. Lessons for families inside these gates are live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time. Given there is no school and no tuition centre in the community, online removes a journey rather than adding one. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour including travel if presence in the room is essential.

faqs.question: Should we buy a discounted package up front?
faqs.answer: Not before the match has been tested. Published monthly packages in Dubai run from around AED 799 for eight online sessions to AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and the risk in buying early is unused sessions, which is the most common complaint in this market. Take a free trial, buy six sessions, review on marked timed work, then consider a package if the price genuinely improves. Ask in writing what happens to sessions you do not use.

faqs.question: How much does a wasted session actually cost us?
faqs.answer: More than people assume, because it recurs. A 16:30 session for a child who reaches home at 16:20 spends its first twenty minutes on settling, which at the mid-market band is a weekly loss for no benefit and the usual reason an arrangement ends in week five. In this community, where no school sits inside the gates and arrivals run from 15:40 to 16:50, 17:00 is the dependable start and 17:30 is safer for a long commute.

faqs.question: Does the rate go up closer to the May session?
faqs.answer: With several providers it does, and it is worth asking before you commit. Demand concentrates in the spring term, specialist slots between 17:00 and 19:00 fill across the city, and the market prices accordingly. The practical consequence is that booking in September both secures the slot and avoids the squeeze, at the same hourly figure. Ask any provider directly whether the rate quoted in October is the rate you will pay in March, and get it in writing.

faqs.question: Is a premium examiner-led tutor ever worth the money?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, with caution. The top of this market reaches AED 650 an hour on BartyED's published figures, and for a scarce Higher Level subject in the final weeks genuine expertise can justify it. But current examiner status is hard to verify, must never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, and is not a substitute for teaching skill. Ask what evidences the claim. For most subjects the AED 200-450 specialist band does the work.

faqs.question: Can two children share a session to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: Only if they are genuinely matched on subject and level. Two siblings taking the same subject at the same level can share an hour productively, and some providers price that below two separate hours. Two children in different years, different subjects or different levels cannot, and the attempt produces two half-sessions. Matched levels matter far more than matched addresses, which is also why sharing with a neighbour's child rarely works as well as parents hope.

faqs.question: What is the single most expensive mistake in IB tutoring here?
faqs.answer: Starting in the spring of the second Diploma year. By then the coursework that carried a fifth of each subject grade has been submitted, the content gains are largely gone, two or three sessions a week are needed instead of one, and the scarcest specialists have full calendars. The same money spent as one weekly hour from the first Diploma year buys more improvement, costs less per month, and secures a better tutor at the same rate.

faqs.question: How do we compare two quotes that look nothing alike?
faqs.answer: Reduce both to four numbers and two questions. The numbers: cost per sixty minutes of actual teaching, cost per month at the frequency you need, what happens to a cancelled session, and what happens if you change tutor. The questions: who employs the tutor and where are they based, and does the tutor hold a Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition permit. Most quotes that look cheaper turn out to be shorter lessons, group sessions, or supervision sold as teaching.

faqs.question: Is the Middle Years Programme cheaper to support than the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Usually, and for a reason worth knowing. In the Middle Years Programme the problem is almost always a specific criterion rather than general knowledge, so two or three sessions timed to a real task, with the task sheet and descriptors open, often changes more than a term of content teaching. That makes it a short, cheap and measurable purchase. A weekly open-ended arrangement at that stage is the easiest money in IB tutoring to spend without being able to say what it did.

faqs.question: What would make you tell us not to buy anything?
faqs.answer: Several things, and we say them. If a marked paper shows the issue is that your child has not attempted their own teacher's homework for three weeks, a tutor makes it worse rather than better and the conversation belongs with the school. If there are too few weeks left for a subject to move meaningfully, we say so. And if a single diagnostic session shows the student is secure, we tell you that rather than proposing a programme.

intro.heading: The honest answer to 'is there anyone near me who knows this'
paragraphs: Probably not many, and that is not a marketing line. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum. IB families are a minority of a very large market. Scale that down to one villa community in west Dubai and one subject at one level, and the pool of genuine specialists within a short drive is small.

That matters because IB subject knowledge is not transferable in the way parents assume. A tutor who is excellent at A Level Chemistry is not automatically useful for IB Chemistry HL, because the internal assessment is criterion-marked, Paper 3 has a different shape, and the command terms carry specific expectations. A tutor who cannot name the paper weightings for the course they are teaching is a generalist, however good they are in a room.

So the search term is right and the filter is wrong. 'Near me' selects for drive time. What decides the grade is whether the tutor has taken students through that exact course to a May session and knows where the marks disappear. Those two things are independent, and when you insist on both you usually end up compromising the one that matters.

There is a second reason distance misleads. The constraint on a weekday evening in this part of Dubai is not kilometres but the clock. A tutor five minutes away who can only come at 18:45 is less useful than a specialist on video at 17:00, because the hour your child can actually concentrate is short and fixed by the school run. Jumeirah Park has no metro station inside it, so none of that is solvable by changing how anyone travels.

Here is what IB Gram actually does. We match a Jumeirah Park student to a tutor chosen for the subject and the level, and the lesson happens live on video, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. That is stated plainly here because you will otherwise find it out at the worst possible moment.

It is also worth being clear about what a tutor cannot change. A tutor cannot add hours to a Diploma timetable that already carries six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, alongside the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies periods that KHDA requires of every Dubai private school whatever its licensed curriculum. What a tutor can do is make one subject's hour count for more than three unsupervised ones, and tell you honestly which subject that should be.

The rest of this page is built to be useful whether or not you hire us. It sets out how thin specialist supply is by subject, the eight questions that separate a specialist from a confident generalist, what the UAE tutoring permit regime actually requires, and where a Jumeirah Park family's money tends to go to waste. Use it as a checklist against any provider, including this one.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-park.programmesIntro: Jumeirah Park's IB students sit across three programmes, and the phrase 'IB tutor' means something different in each. Matching the programme is the first filter, before subject or level.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no subject syllabus to revise and no external examination. A tutor here is working on underlying capability: number fluency, reading inference, written explanation. The parent's difficulty is that PYP reporting describes dispositions rather than attainment, so a gap can sit hidden for a year.
programmes.countryNote: Because Jumeirah Park's in-community school is British curriculum, local PYP pupils travel to continuum schools in Al Barsha or further. Many switch systems at some point, which makes a diagnostic session more valuable here than a fixed programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked 1-8, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school's own boundaries. Marks are lost on process: an unlabelled axis, a method with no evaluation, a conclusion that restates the data. A tutor who has not worked from an MYP task sheet will teach content the student already has.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP tutor near Jumeirah Park needs the student's own task sheet and criterion descriptors to be useful at all. Those come from the school, not from a textbook, which is one reason screen sharing suits this programme particularly well.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with final written papers in the May session for UAE schools. This is where specialist scarcity bites hardest, because HL depth in physics, chemistry and Analysis and Approaches is genuinely rare in any one neighbourhood.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP candidates sit the May session, and internal coursework deadlines fall roughly a year earlier. A Jumeirah Park family's most common mistake is treating the exam date as the deadline that matters.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more DP courses combined with a career-related study and a reflective project. Provision in the UAE is limited to a handful of schools. Tutoring normally targets the DP courses inside the programme plus the personal and professional skills component, which students under-estimate.
programmes.countryNote: With CP offered by so few UAE schools, local word of mouth produces nobody who has taught it. This is the clearest case where searching by distance returns an empty set and searching by subject does not.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-park.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Jumeirah Park families ask for, listed with the question a specialist in that subject should be able to answer instantly. Use them as a test, not just a menu.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask any tutor why Paper 1 changes how you teach algebra. The answer is that no calculator is allowed, so manipulation has to be exact and fast. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers, Maclaurin series and vector geometry. A tutor who treats AA and AI as the same course is not a specialist.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, statistics-heavy, with graph theory at HL. Ask what distinguishes a strong AI internal assessment: the answer is a data set the student genuinely owns and interprets in context, not a borrowed one with a regression line drawn through it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask what Paper 3 contains. A specialist will say data analysis plus an option topic, and will add that significant figures and units cost more marks in long answers than physics errors do. Fields, induction and quantum phenomena are the HL extensions that most often need rebuilding.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask how they teach organic mechanisms. A specialist teaches arrow-pushing and electron movement; a generalist teaches products to memorise. HL adds spectroscopic identification and harder equilibrium work, and the internal assessment demands uncertainty handling most students have never been taught.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask which command terms cost students the most. Outline, explain, evaluate and distinguish each demand a different answer shape, and examiner reports repeat the point every session. Content recall is rarely the problem; answer construction almost always is.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask about the internal assessment. Three commentaries, each 800 words, on published news articles, and the article choice is half the mark because a badly chosen article cannot carry a diagram. HL adds quantitative work and an extra paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what the Individual Oral requires. A global issue, two texts, one of them in translation at HL, and a sustained argument rather than a summary. Paper 1 is unseen analysis and Paper 2 is comparative; students who summarise instead of analysing lose marks consistently.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask which part catches out the strong writers. Investment appraisal and cash-flow forecasting, every time. The research project needs a real organisation and a question narrow enough to answer in the word limit, which is where most of them go wrong.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Ask what makes an internal assessment fail. Scope: a project too ambitious to document against the criteria inside the word limit. HL adds abstract data structures and resource management, and the written papers want pseudocode, not a language the student happens to know.

subjects.name: TOK, Extended Essay and IA coaching
subjects.description: Ask what a tutor will and will not do. The correct answer is teaching research question design, argument structure and referencing, plus feedback on the student's own drafts, and nothing that involves writing any part of it. Any other answer is a reason to stop the conversation.

sections.heading: Why distance is the wrong filter for an IB tutor
paragraphs: An IB tutor near me in Jumeirah Park, taken literally, means a tutor within a short drive. The problem is that the two things that determine whether tutoring works -- command of the specific course and a slot your child can actually use -- have nothing to do with the tutor's address. Filtering by distance throws away the first in order to buy the second, when the second is obtainable another way.

Think about what the local pool really is. It is people who hold a Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit, teach your child's subject at your child's level, have a free evening slot in your window, and are willing to drive into Jumeirah Park in the 17:00 peak. Each condition cuts the list. The last one cuts it most, because an in-demand specialist has no reason to spend ninety minutes in traffic.

IB Gram removes the travel condition and keeps the rest. Lessons are live, one to one, on video, scheduled around your household's evening. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists in India only. The result is that your child is matched on syllabus and level, which is where the marks are, rather than on geography, which is where the convenience is.

In exchange you give up physical presence, and for some students that is the wrong trade. A child who needs an adult beside them to stay on task, a household with no quiet room at six o'clock, or hands-on equipment work are all better served face to face. If that describes your situation, hire locally and budget for the travel premium the Dubai market charges.

paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is why most parents discover one only after paying. Ours is published here. The scarce combinations are HL sciences, HL Analysis and Approaches, Computer Science and the less commonly taught options, and the scarce hours are weekday 17:00 to 19:00 Gulf Standard Time in the spring term.

A parent is entitled to know who is teaching their child and from where, and two ranking competitors route UAE families to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it.

What this means in practice is that timing your request matters as much as making it. A family that books a weekly Chemistry HL slot in September holds it all year. A family that asks for the same slot in March is choosing from what is left. That is not a scarcity tactic; it is how any calendar of one-to-one appointments fills, and it is true of local in-home tutors too.

If a combination genuinely is not available, you will be told the position and offered a choice: a different time with the specialist you wanted, an immediate start with a strong generalist while that slot opens, or a wait with a date attached. What you will not get is a confident yes followed by a substitution.

sections.heading: Eight questions that tell you whether a tutor knows the course
paragraphs: You do not need to be an IB expert to test one. You need eight questions whose answers a specialist produces instantly and a generalist either hedges or gets wrong. Ask them in the trial session, before any discussion of price, and listen for specificity rather than confidence. This is the most portable thing on this page, and it works on us as well as on anyone else.

Notice what none of these questions is about. None asks how many years they have taught, which school they worked at, or how passionate they are about the subject. Those answers are unfalsifiable. The questions below have right answers, and a tutor who cannot produce them has not taught the course to a May session recently.

The table gives each question with the shape of a good answer and the tell-tale weak one. Use three or four rather than all eight if time is short; the paper weighting question and the internal assessment criterion question are the two that discriminate hardest.

Ask them in that order, too. A tutor who has just told you the paper weightings and the criterion letters is giving you a verifiable account of the course, and everything they say afterwards about method can be judged against it. A tutor who opens with their years of experience and their passion for the subject has told you nothing you can check, and in a market with no published coverage data that is all most parents ever get.

One final question to ask, which is not in the table: what will you not do? A specialist answers that they will not write any part of the internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay, and will not promise a grade. If a tutor answers that question by promising a seven, you have learned everything you need to know.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level are different jobs
paragraphs: Parents book an IB tutor by subject. Tutors should be booked by subject and level, because the gap between Standard and Higher Level in the sciences and mathematics is wider than most people outside the system expect. It is not the same course with extra chapters; the additional content changes the character of the questions and the depth of understanding the papers probe.

This is also where local supply breaks first. A tutor can be genuinely strong at SL across two sciences and out of their depth in HL in either. That is not a criticism; HL depth takes sustained specialist teaching to maintain. It is, however, the single most common mismatch in Dubai IB tutoring, and it is invisible for about four weeks.

The practical implication for a Jumeirah Park family choosing by distance is uncomfortable. The nearer you insist the tutor lives, the more likely you are to be sold SL competence for an HL course. Ask the level question directly and ask for the HL paper structure, as in the table above.

There is a university dimension that parents in this community raise often. For several subjects the degree requirement specifies the Higher Level version, and a Standard Level pass will not satisfy it. That is worth checking against the actual admissions pages of the universities your child is considering, in the UAE and abroad, before anyone drops a level to reduce workload. The decision is easy to make in September of the first Diploma year and painful in March of the second.

Use it when planning rather than when panicking: an HL subject identified as weak in the autumn of the first Diploma year is a different problem from the same subject identified in March of the second.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor near you
paragraphs: This is a question almost nobody asks and everybody should. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with the service listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing and a two-working-day completion time.

Eligibility is broader than parents expect. u.ae lists teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. So a university student tutoring your Year 10 for AED 50 an hour can be entirely legitimate. The permit is not a quality signal; it is a legality signal, and the two are often confused in marketing.

There are limits that matter. u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor; in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram does not hold one and does not describe itself as KHDA approved. Ask any tutor you hire whether they hold a MoHRE permit, and ask any agency what it actually holds rather than what it implies.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it costs
paragraphs: Since 'near me' is partly a question about money, here is the arithmetic from the other direction: what you pay extra for proximity, and what that extra actually buys. Bestimate's Dubai survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online on Unitors' published figures, where IGCSE starts at AED 150 and IB at AED 200.

So the premium is real but modest in cash terms. What it costs in selection is larger. The tutor willing to make that drive at 17:30 is drawn from a smaller and less specialised group, and the hour you buy includes somebody's commute in its price whether or not it appears as a line item. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52, which buys supervision rather than specialist teaching.

At the top, TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier reaches AED 650. Treat examiner claims with care: current examiner status is hard to verify and should never be used to imply access to marking or boundaries. Monthly packages in this market run from around AED 799 for eight online sessions to AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour home visits. All figures are the providers' own, read in October 2026.

None of these is an IB Gram price and this page does not publish one, because the right number depends on subject, level and how many weeks remain. The honest guidance is to start with the free trial session and a conversation, then commit to six sessions rather than twenty, and judge on marked timed work.

sections.heading: The IB core, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS are where Diploma students lose points they cannot recover, because the deadlines are internal and the work is independent. They are also where the tutoring market behaves worst. One operator in this SERP sells completed internal assessments outright at four-figure prices, which is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger for the student.

The legitimate version is narrower and more useful. A tutor can teach research question design, explain the assessment criteria, teach referencing and academic conventions, help plan a structure, and read and comment on drafts the student has written. The tutor says which descriptor band the work currently meets and names what is missing. The student then fixes it. That is where the learning is.

What a tutor cannot do is write, part-write, rewrite to completion or supply content for an internal assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or Personal Project. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; those are cited and linked, and your child's school holds licensed access.

CAS is the component families forget until it becomes urgent. It is not graded, but it has to be completed and evidenced, and a Diploma is not awarded without it. No tutor can do CAS for a student; what a tutor can do is point out in September that the reflection record is part of the requirement, not an afterthought, and that leaving it to the final term adds pressure in exactly the weeks when past papers matter most.

If you are comparing providers near you, this is the fastest way to sort them. Ask what they will do with a draft. The answer either describes feedback against criteria, or it describes improving the writing. The second answer is the one that puts your child's Diploma at risk.

sections.heading: Scheduling from a Jumeirah Park address
paragraphs: Even when distance stops deciding who teaches, it still decides when. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30, and a Jumeirah Park bus route that also serves Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village puts most children home between 15:20 and 16:40. There is no metro station inside the community, so the nearest Route 2020 stations at Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens play no part in a tutoring timetable.

That leaves a usable window from about 16:30 to 21:00 on weekdays. Students at the school inside the community can hold a 16:00 slot. Second-year Diploma students often do better at 19:30, after dinner, than at five o'clock when they are still carrying the school day. Booking the wrong hour is the commonest reason a tutoring arrangement stops after five weeks, and it has nothing to do with the tutor.

The week shape matters too. With the weekend on Saturday and Sunday, a Saturday morning slot is the only place a ninety-minute past paper genuinely fits, and Sunday afternoon is the natural time to mark it. For Diploma students in the spring term that pairing does more than two extra weekday hours would.

During Ramadan, school hours shorten and households run later; a post-Iftar session or a late-morning weekend slot usually works better than anything at five. We reschedule rather than cancel, because the May session does not move. Sessions also follow you to another time zone if you travel, provided we know the week before.

For most families that means 16:30 or 17:30, and for second-year Diploma students often after dinner. Getting this right is what makes the arrangement last a year.

process.description: After about six sessions there is real evidence. We look at timed work rather than impressions and decide whether to continue, add a subject, switch to coursework coaching or stop. Stopping is a legitimate result and better reached deliberately than by drifting out of the habit.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB specialist living near Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: Some, but fewer than you would hope, and that is a function of the market rather than the neighbourhood. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, so IB families are a minority of a large market. Narrow that to one subject at Higher Level and one villa community in west Dubai and the pool of people who have taught that exact course to a May session is genuinely small. Matching online rather than by distance is how we get around it.

faqs.question: What single question most reliably exposes a tutor who does not know the course?
faqs.answer: Ask for the paper weightings at the level your child is sitting, including the internal assessment percentage. A specialist gives the split without hesitating and usually adds where the marks disappear. A generalist either hedges, quotes the Standard Level structure for a Higher Level course, or talks about experience instead. Follow it with a question about the internal assessment criterion letters. Those two questions together take four minutes and separate specialists from confident generalists more reliably than any amount of credential-reading.

faqs.question: Will my child get a tutor based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes not, and we tell you which before you book. All lessons are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so the timetable is identical either way, but a parent is entitled to know who is teaching their child and from where. Some subject specialists covering UAE families are based elsewhere. Two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without disclosing it, which we think is the wrong way to handle the same fact.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches A Level also teach IB Chemistry HL?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but do not assume it. The content overlaps substantially; the assessment does not. IB Chemistry has an internal assessment marked against published criteria, a Paper 3 with data analysis and an option topic, and command terms with specific expectations. A strong A Level chemist who has never marked an IB internal assessment will teach the chemistry well and the assessment badly. Ask what they will do with an internal assessment draft and whether they can name the criteria before you decide.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a specialist for a Jumeirah Park student?
faqs.answer: For most subjects, within the same week. For Physics HL, Chemistry HL, Maths Analysis and Approaches HL and Computer Science in a weekday 17:00 to 19:00 slot during the spring term, it can be up to two weeks and we quote a date rather than a hope. The alternatives we offer are an off-peak slot with the specialist you wanted, an interim start with a strong generalist and a stated handover, or a wait. You will not be given a confident yes and a quiet substitution.

faqs.question: Is a MoHRE permit something I should be asking a tutor to show me?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private lessons needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is free of charge, valid for two years, and applied for through MoHRE's app, website or e-services with a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. u.ae states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine amounts are published.

faqs.question: My child is choosing Higher Level subjects next term. Can tutoring help with the decision?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a single diagnostic session is usually enough. A specialist works through material at the Higher Level standard with the student and reports back on whether the prior attainment and study habit are there, rather than whether the student likes the subject. Higher Level is wider and less scaffolded than Standard Level, not simply longer, and a mid-course change is disruptive. Check the degree requirement too: for several subjects, universities expect the Higher Level version and a Standard Level pass will not satisfy it.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a compromise for Diploma students?
faqs.answer: For Diploma students, we do not think so. What moves a Diploma grade is command of the syllabus, criterion knowledge and timed past-paper practice, all of which work at least as well with a shared screen as with two people over one sheet of paper. A sixteen-year-old can also hold a focused hour on video. The real exceptions are younger children who cannot sustain attention, households without a quiet room, and hands-on equipment work. Say so at the consultation if that is your situation.

faqs.question: What should I pay for a Higher Level science tutor in this area?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200, and specialist IB and IGCSE work at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270. In-home visits carry a travel premium at AED 180-500. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65, which buys supervision rather than Higher Level teaching. Those are the providers' own figures read in October 2026. We publish no rate card because the right number depends on subject, level and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Which schools near Jumeirah Park actually run the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Within a reasonable radius, families most often name Sunmarke School in Jumeirah Village Triangle, Nord Anglia International School Dubai in Al Barsha South, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and GEMS World Academy Dubai in Al Barsha, Emirates International School Meadows, Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim and Fairgreen International School. The school inside Jumeirah Park itself is British curriculum. We have no affiliation with any of these schools and name them as context; confirm current programmes on KHDA's own school listing before enrolling.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in supporting Extended Essay work?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help your child write it in the sense of teaching research question design, method, structure and referencing, and giving feedback on drafts your child has produced. A tutor cannot write, part-write or rewrite any of it, and we will not. Submitting work that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter the IB handles, and the consequence falls on the student. There are operators in this market selling completed internal assessments at four-figure prices; treat that offer as a reason to walk away.

faqs.question: Suppose the first match does not suit my child. Then what?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we change the tutor rather than asking your child to persist. That is the point of running a free trial session first: the pairing is tested before you pay for a term of it. Fit failures are usually not about competence. A tutor who talks for fifty minutes can be entirely expert and still wrong for a student who needs to be made to work. Judge the trial on whether your child spoke and whether the tutor diagnosed rather than lectured.

faqs.question: Are weekend sessions better than weekday ones for Diploma work?
faqs.answer: For long work, yes. With the UAE weekend on Saturday and Sunday, a Saturday morning slot is the only place in the week where a full timed paper genuinely fits, and marking it with the tutor on Sunday is where most of the learning happens. Weekday evenings suit shorter targeted work on a single topic. Many Jumeirah Park Diploma families settle on one weekday hour plus a weekend pairing in the spring term rather than three weekday evenings.

faqs.question: Does my child's school inspection rating tell me whether they need a tutor?
faqs.answer: Almost nothing. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the result, which is genuinely useful when choosing a school. It tells you nothing about whether your child is secure in equilibrium calculations or can structure a Paper 2 comparative essay. Use the inspection rating for enrolment decisions and your child's own marked work for tutoring decisions. We read the school report and the last timed paper, not the inspection band.

faqs.question: Should we wait until after the mocks to start?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Waiting for the mock means losing the autumn term and then competing for spring slots in exactly the scarce subjects where supply is tightest. If you already suspect a Higher Level subject is weak, a single diagnostic session now tells you whether you are right, costs little and does not commit you to anything. If the mock then confirms it, the tutor is already in place and the marked paper becomes the plan rather than the starting gun.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-villa.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Jumeirah Village Circle students are proposed with their subject, level and the specific papers they teach. That is deliberate: the useful question about an IB tutor is which components they know, not how close they live to the Circle.

intro.heading: Test the syllabus knowledge, not the distance
paragraphs: A local search is a reasonable instinct and a poor filter. It ranks whoever has optimised for the place name, and research across sixty-odd competitor pages in this market in October 2026 found agencies routing UAE parents to Indian phone numbers, one page displaying a Dubai footer address on an Abu Dhabi page, and several listing twenty-five or more schools as clients with no apparent relationship. Proximity in a search result is a marketing claim rather than a fact, and it would not predict a grade even if it were true.

What does predict a grade is whether the tutor knows the components. The IB Diploma is not assessed as general subject knowledge; it is assessed through named papers with published weightings, through command terms that carry specific mark allocations, and through Internal Assessments marked against lettered criteria. A tutor who can tell you that a science Internal Assessment typically carries 20 per cent, or that a Higher Level Mathematics student sits a third paper worth 20 per cent, is working inside the actual assessment. A tutor who talks about confidence and study skills is selling something else.

So this page is built as a set of tests you can apply to anybody, us included. It sets out the paper structures of the main Diploma subjects so you can ask which components your child sits. It gives the command terms with what each one actually requires, because that vocabulary is where most marks are lost. It names the mark-scheme traps subject by subject. And it explains what past-paper work looks like when it is done properly rather than handed out.

There is a reason this matters more in Jumeirah Village Circle than in some communities. It is one of the largest and newest residential areas in Dubai, full of families who arrived recently, with a correspondingly large and unregulated local tutoring market. The variation in quality inside the same advertised rate band is wide, and the only reliable way through it is to ask component-level questions.

One thing is worth saying before the detail starts, because it changes what you should buy. The commonest situation we are asked about is a student who clearly knows the content and whose grades do not show it. That is almost never a knowledge problem; it is a mark-scheme problem, and it is diagnosable from one marked script. Tangled extended responses where only one of three correct points can be credited, command terms answered in the wrong register, units and significant figures lost on numerically correct answers. None of it requires new content to be learned, which is why it is both the fastest thing to improve and the most frustrating to leave alone.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, matched by subject and level. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Confirm every weighting below against your child's school subject guide, because assessment models are periodically revised and the version your cohort sits is the only one that counts.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-villa.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes reach Jumeirah Village Circle families, and the assessment vocabulary differs completely between them. A tutor fluent in one is not automatically useful in another.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, each marked out of 7 through a combination of externally assessed papers and an internally assessed component, plus up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, to a maximum of 45. The assessment detail is the subject matter of this page: which papers, what each is worth, and what the command terms in them require.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no IB examination or results dates on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification; take yours from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. For a Jumeirah Village Circle family the dates that actually govern planning are the school's Internal Assessment deadlines, which are published locally and rarely requested.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each scored on a published band, with task-specific clarifications written by the teacher. There are no external papers in most schools and no command terms in the Diploma sense, so the assessment language is entirely different and so is the teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools near Jumeirah Village Circle run the Middle Years Programme while neighbouring campuses switch to Cambridge IGCSE at 14, so children of the same age in the same building can be on different models. If your family may move campuses, the transferable gap is extended writing under time pressure rather than content.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Units of inquiry with no external examination and a Year 6 Exhibition. Tuition should be narrow and short at this stage: a specific reading fluency gap, number facts, or written English for a child arriving from another language of instruction. There is no assessment technique to teach, which is why long-running primary tuition usually indicates a misdiagnosis.
programmes.countryNote: Primary provision close to Jumeirah Village Circle is dense, so families here often have a short run for a younger child and a longer one for a Diploma student. Video delivery exists partly so those two journeys do not have to collide in the same hour.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-villa.subjectsIntro: Each Diploma subject is assessed through its own set of components, and knowing the structure is how you judge both a tutor and a revision plan. Confirm each one against your school's subject guide.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher Level, plus the exploration. The Higher Level third paper is a small number of extended investigative questions where each part feeds the next, which rewards a skill nothing else in the course trains.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same component structure as Analysis and Approaches, with technology permitted throughout. Mark schemes here reward interpretation sentences: a regression run correctly and then described in words that do not fit the question's context scores poorly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two papers plus the scientific investigation, with the first paper divided between multiple choice and data analysis. Mark schemes penalise loose language about bond strength and reward correct state symbols, significant figures and data-booklet use.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The same structure as chemistry, with data analysis assessed separately from content. Units, vector direction and naming the controlled variable are where capable candidates lose a grade boundary's worth of marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Two papers plus the investigation. Command terms matter more here than in any other science: outline and explain attract different mark allocations and students regularly answer the wrong one, which is a vocabulary problem rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral on a global issue and, at Higher Level, the HL Essay. The Individual Oral is a structured fifteen-minute performance with a published mark scheme, which makes it the most coachable component in the subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Two papers at Standard Level, three at Higher Level, plus a three-commentary Internal Assessment portfolio. Diagrams must be fully labelled and then referred to in the prose; an unmentioned diagram earns very little whatever its quality.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Two papers plus a research project. The ceiling is application: tools reproduced accurately and never applied to the stimulus organisation is the standard reason a confident student plateaus below their expectation.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A source-based paper, a thematic essay paper, a regional paper at Higher Level, and a historical investigation. The source paper has a fixed question architecture that rewards rehearsal more than reading, which surprises students every year.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, plus a 4,000-word independent research piece, together worth up to three points. Both are won at the question-framing stage, months before the writing, and both are supervised by school staff.
