sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that carries the marks
paragraphs: If a single thing separates Diploma candidates with similar knowledge, it is command terms. The IB publishes them, examiners apply them, and most students have never had them explained as a list. State wants a short answer with no working. Outline wants a brief account. Describe wants a detailed account without reasons. Explain wants reasons or causes. Discuss wants a balanced review including opposing arguments. Evaluate wants judgements supported by evidence. Compare and contrast wants similarities and differences together, not in sequence.

The mathematical and scientific terms are stricter still. Show that requires a derivation ending at the stated result, and quoting the result earns nothing. Hence means the previous part must be used, and a correct answer obtained another way can lose marks. Deduce requires a conclusion drawn from given information. Determine implies a specific numerical or algebraic answer. Suggest asks for a plausible proposal where more than one answer is acceptable.

The practical consequence is a mark allocation mismatch. A question worth two marks using outline does not want the four-paragraph answer a student gives; a question worth five marks using evaluate does not want the description they write instead. Students lose marks in both directions and the loss is invisible to them, because they knew the content perfectly well.

This is also the cheapest grade improvement in the Diploma, because it transfers across every subject at once. Two or three sessions working through a student's own lost answers against the command term and the mark allocation usually produces a visible change at the next assessment. Ask any prospective tutor to explain the difference between discuss and evaluate, and to show you a mark scheme where it matters.

sections.heading: Paper structures, subject by subject
paragraphs: You cannot plan revision without knowing what each component is worth, and most families have never seen the figures. The pattern across the Diploma is that external papers carry the large majority and an internally assessed component carries the rest, typically a fifth to a third depending on the subject.

In the sciences, the internal investigation commonly carries 20 per cent with two papers carrying the remainder, the first of which splits between multiple choice and data analysis. In Mathematics, both routes have two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher Level, with the exploration at 20 per cent. In English A, the Individual Oral is a substantial weighting at Standard Level and sits alongside an additional HL Essay at Higher Level. In Economics and History the internal component is weighted more heavily than in the sciences, and Higher Level adds a third paper in both.

Three things follow for a Jumeirah Village Circle family planning work. First, the internal component is worth as much as a whole paper in several subjects, and it is the one where work is done in advance with full access to help — which makes neglecting it the single largest unforced error in the Diploma. Second, at Higher Level the third paper in Mathematics, Economics and History each needs separate preparation, because each rewards a different skill from the first two. Third, revision spread evenly across components is revision spread wrongly.

Confirm all of this against your child's school subject guide. Assessment models are periodically revised, schools work from the version their cohort sits, and no tutoring page — including this one — is the authority on your child's weightings. A tutor who cannot tell you the structure of the subject they are being hired for has told you something important.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme traps, by subject
paragraphs: Mark schemes are lists of discrete creditable points, and most lost marks come from writing in a way that prevents a point being awarded rather than from not knowing it. The commonest trap across the whole Diploma is tangling: three correct ideas woven into one flowing sentence, of which an examiner can credit one. The fix is one point per sentence, in the order the question implies, which feels mechanical and earns marks.

In the sciences, the traps are specific. Units omitted on a numerically correct answer. Significant figures copied from the calculator rather than matched to the data. Explanations given in the wrong register — temperature where particle behaviour was wanted, bond strength where intermolecular forces were wanted. Experiments described without naming the controlled variable, which is a mark explicitly available for a single sentence.

In mathematics, missing method lines on multi-mark questions, intermediate values rounded and carried forward, and calculator mode left in degrees for a radian question. In English, extended paraphrase where short comment on selected evidence was wanted. In Economics and Business Management, a fully correct diagram or tool that the prose never refers to, which earns almost nothing on its own.

Every one of those is visible in a single marked paper, which is why we ask for one before quoting a session count. It is also why the most useful thing a tutor does is mark, with the scheme visible to the student. A question discussed produces agreement; a question marked produces a list of specific sentences that did not earn what they should have.

sections.heading: Past-paper work done properly
paragraphs: Every provider says they use past papers. Almost nobody describes what doing it properly involves, so here is the version worth paying for. The student sits a paper, or a defined section of one, under genuine timed conditions, without notes and without stopping. Then the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, with the scheme visible, annotating where a mark was available and not earned. Then the next session works on what was lost and nothing else.

What is not past-paper work: going through questions together as they arise, which removes the timed element and the independent attempt. Handing over a folder of papers for the student to do alone, which produces unmarked work and false confidence. Working through answers the student has already seen, which tests recall of the answer rather than the skill.

There is a scarcity point worth knowing. The number of past papers in existence for any component is finite, and for Higher Level third papers it is small. Spending them early, untimed, or without marking is wasteful, because they cannot be re-used as genuine diagnostics once a student has seen the questions. The sensible pattern is a few early for diagnosis, the bulk in the final eight weeks under conditions.

One rule about materials. We do not reproduce or distribute IB past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables, syllabus documents or subject guides as downloads. Tutors reference them and work from the copies the school provides, linking to the official source. A provider offering a complete folder of everything is describing something they should not be doing, and it is a reasonable signal about the rest of their practice.

sections.heading: Internal Assessments: criteria, not impressions
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component, marked by the teacher against published lettered criteria and externally moderated. The weighting is substantial — commonly a fifth of the grade in the sciences and more in some other subjects — and it is the only part of the course completed in advance with full access to help, which makes it the most efficient place to earn marks and the most dangerous place to cross a line.

The criteria are the whole of it. A science investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A mathematics exploration is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest allocation. Knowing which criterion carries the most marks tells you where the work should go, and students who do not know usually distribute effort by what feels most enjoyable.

The highest-value help is always earliest. Interrogating a research question so the available evidence can answer it, checking a method will produce analysable data, confirming the mathematics is at the level of the course: three sessions at that stage is a small block with a large effect. Trying to rescue a finished piece built on an unworkable question in the final fortnight is expensive and usually unsuccessful.

The boundary is firm and worth stating because this market contains providers who ignore it. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion, question a research question, point out that a method will not work, mark a draft against the criteria and teach referencing. A tutor may not write any part of the work, rewrite prose, supply a finished question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit to completion. Our tutors decline when asked. One operator in this market was found advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is malpractice and the student carries the consequence.

sections.heading: Five questions that identify a real IB specialist
paragraphs: Since distance tells you nothing, here is what to ask instead, and it works on any provider including us. First: which components does my child's subject have, and what is each one worth? A specialist answers without hesitating and adds that you should confirm it against the school's subject guide. Second: what is the difference between discuss and evaluate, and can you show me a mark scheme where it matters?

Third: what are the Internal Assessment criteria for this subject, by letter, and which carries the most marks? This is the question that most cleanly separates somebody who teaches the course from somebody who knows the content. Fourth: can you mark this specific question my child lost, with the mark scheme, and tell me which available marks were not earned and why?

Fifth, and the one nobody asks: do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and under which category? Private tutoring in the UAE requires that permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. It is a fair question and a permitted tutor will answer it in a sentence.

Those five questions take about ten minutes and they are considerably more informative than any amount of profile reading. A capable generalist will answer the first two approximately and the third not at all, and will steer the conversation towards confidence, motivation and study skills. That is a real service and a different one, and it should not be bought at a specialist rate.

sections.heading: What this costs, and which band to buy
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level provision is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one UK-based agency publishing AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led provision as high as AED 650. Budget online tuition, typically a university student, is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150, one platform listing from AED 33 to AED 52 and another from AED 45 to AED 65.

For the work described on this page — component technique, command terms, mark-scheme marking, Internal Assessment criteria — the specialist band is the right one, because the whole value is in knowing the assessment. The budget band buys supervision and structure, which is a real service for a student who will not start homework unaided and useless for a Higher Level mark scheme. Paying a specialist rate for homework supervision is equally wasteful in the other direction.

The premium band, up to AED 650, buys scarcity and reputation. Where a claim of examiner status is attached to it, ask what evidence supports it: current examiner status for a named individual cannot be verified from a website, and nobody should be implying it confers access to marking or grade boundaries. We make no such claims about any tutor.

In blocks, the figures are modest. A command-term block is two or three sessions. A component block is four to six. An Internal Assessment question-stage block is three. Every figure above was read from the provider's own published page in October 2026 and describes the market rather than IB Gram, whose fee follows a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Fitting subject work into a Jumeirah Village Circle week
paragraphs: The afternoon here has a particular shape. Most students travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South, or eight to fifteen to Motor City, so they are home earlier than families in the outlying villa communities — often by 3.45pm. Dubai Sports City is immediately next door, though, and academies there take students out again between four and six, which closes the window that short commute appeared to open.

So the workable slots are around 5.30pm for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for the many with one. Students travelling in from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square are home after 4.30pm and sit at the back of that range.

Place the session after a first attempt at the school's work rather than before it. A student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, which is what a specialist resolves in forty minutes; a session before homework becomes supervised homework. This matters more for the work described on this page than for content teaching, because command-term and mark-scheme work needs the student's own flawed answer to work on.

Weekend mornings are underused in this community and they are the right slot for whole timed papers, which need ninety uninterrupted minutes. Online delivery keeps all of it flexible: sessions move within the week when a deadline or a fixture collides, shift post-Iftar during Ramadan, and stop cleanly at study leave, which is agreed at the start.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah Village Circle who visits the apartment?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors serve this community readily, since it is central and dense, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. What dropping the visit buys you is a tutor chosen for the components your child sits rather than for the drive.

faqs.question: What should I ask an IB tutor to find out if they really know the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Five things. Which components does my child's subject have and what is each worth? What is the difference between discuss and evaluate, and can you show me a mark scheme where it matters? What are the Internal Assessment criteria by letter, and which carries the most marks? Can you mark this specific lost question with the scheme and name the marks that were available? And do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, under which category? Ten minutes of concrete answers beats any amount of profile reading.

faqs.question: Why do command terms matter so much in the IB?
faqs.answer: Because they determine what an examiner can credit. State wants a short answer, outline a brief account, describe a detailed account without reasons, explain reasons or causes, discuss a balanced review including opposing arguments, evaluate judgements supported by evidence. In mathematics and the sciences they are stricter: show that needs a derivation ending at the stated result, and hence means the previous part must be used. Students lose marks in both directions — essays for two-mark outlines, descriptions for five-mark evaluations — while knowing the content perfectly well.

faqs.question: How much is the Internal Assessment worth in my child's subjects?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject and is substantial everywhere. In the sciences the investigation commonly carries 20 per cent; in Mathematics the exploration carries 20 per cent; in Economics and History the internal component is weighted more heavily again; in English A the Individual Oral is a significant weighting at Standard Level. Confirm the exact figures against your child's school subject guide, because assessment models are periodically revised. The planning point is that it is worth as much as a whole paper and is done in advance with access to help.

faqs.question: What does proper past-paper work actually involve?
faqs.answer: Three stages, and most providers skip two of them. The student sits a paper or a defined section under genuine timed conditions, without notes and without stopping. The tutor then marks it against the published scheme, with the scheme visible, annotating where a mark was available and not earned. The next session works only on what was lost. Going through questions together as they arise removes the timed independent attempt; handing over a folder produces unmarked work and false confidence. Papers are also finite, so they should be spent deliberately.

faqs.question: Which mark-scheme trap costs the most marks across subjects?
faqs.answer: Tangling: three correct ideas woven into one flowing sentence, of which an examiner can credit one. Mark schemes are lists of discrete creditable points, so the fix is one point per sentence in the order the question implies, which feels mechanical and earns marks. After that come subject-specific traps — units and significant figures in the sciences, missing method lines in mathematics, paraphrase instead of selected evidence in English, and a correct diagram the prose never refers to in Economics or Business Management.

faqs.question: Does the Higher Level third paper need separate preparation?
faqs.answer: Yes, in every subject that has one. In Mathematics it is a small number of extended investigative questions where each part feeds the next, so an early slip propagates and there is little room to recover; the skill is following an unfamiliar chain of reasoning, which nothing else in the course trains. Economics and History each add a third paper rewarding different skills from the first two. Available past-paper material for third papers is scarce, which is an argument for spending it late and under timed conditions.

faqs.question: What is the boundary on Internal Assessment help, component by component?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary, and earliest is best. A tutor can teach content, explain what each lettered criterion rewards, interrogate and narrow a research question, point out that a method will not produce analysable data, mark a draft against the criteria and teach referencing. A tutor cannot write any part of it, rewrite prose, supply a finished question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line; one operator in this market was found selling completed Internal Assessments outright.

faqs.question: Which single block improves the most subjects at once?
faqs.answer: A command-term and technique block, two or three sessions, worked on the student's own lost answers across their whole subject set. Describe, explain, discuss and evaluate mean the same things in every Diploma subject, and the one-point-per-sentence habit applies to every extended response in the course. It is the cheapest improvement available and almost nobody sells it, because it does not look like teaching a subject and it finishes in three sessions rather than running for a year.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but the grades do not reflect it. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost always a mark-scheme problem rather than a knowledge problem, and it is diagnosable from one marked paper. The usual combination is tangled extended responses where only one of three correct points can be credited, command terms answered in the wrong register, and in the sciences units or significant figures lost on numerically correct answers. None of it requires new content to be learned, which is why this particular situation is the fastest to improve and the most frustrating to leave alone.

faqs.question: Does the Individual Oral in English really repay coaching?
faqs.answer: More than almost any component in the Diploma. It is a structured performance of about fifteen minutes with a published mark scheme, which means the format, the timing and the criteria are all known in advance and all rehearsable. A student who has run it twice with feedback performs differently from one who has only discussed it. The global issue and the extract choice also matter considerably and are decided weeks earlier, so the useful conversation happens before any rehearsal starts.

faqs.answer: Published rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with specialist IB provision quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above and premium examiner-led work as high as AED 650. For the work on this page the specialist band is the right one, because the value is entirely in assessment knowledge. The blocks are small: two or three sessions for command terms, four to six for a component, three at an Internal Assessment question stage. Market rates researched October 2026.

faqs.question: When can a session happen for a Diploma student in the Circle?
faqs.answer: Around 5.30pm for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for the many with one. Most Jumeirah Village Circle students travel only five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South and are home by 3.45pm, but Dubai Sports City is next door and its academies take students out again between four and six. Students commuting in from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square are home after 4.30pm. Weekend mornings are the right slot for whole timed papers.

faqs.answer: You get the realistic wait and the tutor's location rather than a substitute. Availability is thinnest for Higher Level Physics and Computer Science, for Theory of Knowledge support, and for Higher Level third papers in the weeks before the May session. In the meantime a command-term block or a marking session on a recent mock can often run with a different specialist, which is useful work rather than filler. Where the available tutor is based outside the UAE, we say so, including the time zone, before any payment.

intro.heading: Why distance is the weakest filter you can apply
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah Village Triangle is applying a sensible-sounding filter to a problem it does not fit. Distance decides how convenient a lesson is. It has no bearing on whether the person teaching it has marked an Extended Essay against Criterion C, or knows that the Theory of Knowledge essay is capped at 1,600 words, or can tell a DP2 student why their History Paper 3 answers read as narrative rather than argument.

The arithmetic is worth laying out. Dubai's private sector holds 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula, and the International Baccalaureate accounts for 7% of enrolment. Apply that proportion to a radius of a few kilometres around the Triangle and the IB-taught population is modest. Now restrict to tutors rather than students, then to tutors who teach the specific subject at the specific level, then to those free at 17:00 on a Tuesday. The pool that survives those four filters is frequently a single digit, and sometimes zero.

None of that is an argument that tutors living near the Triangle are weak, and several are excellent. It is an argument about how many candidates a distance filter leaves standing, and about what happens to a Diploma student when the answer is two. A parent choosing between two people is not choosing; they are accepting whichever is available, and then discovering in February whether that person has taught the paper. It is an argument about sample size. A Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL student needs somebody who has taught graph theory and hypothesis testing to that level. If three people within driving distance of JVT have, your choice is between three people. Remove the distance filter and it is between everyone who has.

The second thing this page does is point at the part of the Diploma that most often goes unsupported. Families fund subject tutoring and leave the core alone, yet Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together carry up to three bonus points, which is the difference between 34 and 37 on an offer. The core is also the part with the hardest internal deadlines, set by the school rather than by the IB, and the part where academic-honesty boundaries matter most.

So the structure here is: the radius problem laid out properly, what the core actually demands and when, how HL and SL differ in a way that changes tutoring hours, the Dubai rate bands with sources, a direct in-home against online comparison for this community, the regulator picture, and an honest account of availability. Delivery is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that is said at the top rather than in the footnotes.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a source-based question on a prescribed subject and rewards provenance analysis, not summary. Paper 2 is comparative essay work on world history topics. subjects.description: Studies must be named, dated and evaluated, not described. HL adds extra approaches and the quantitative methods content. The internal assessment is a replication of a simple experiment with full statistical treatment, and students routinely pick a study they cannot ethically replicate.

subjects.description: Tools applied to the stimulus earn marks; the same tools described in general do not. Ansoff, break-even, ratio analysis and the Boston Matrix all appear. HL Paper 3 responds to a social-enterprise case. Students often choose an internal-assessment company whose real data they cannot obtain.

subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided analysis of unseen non-literary text; Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works. HL adds the 1,200-1,500 word HL Essay. The Individual Oral links a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract, and extract choice is where it is usually won or lost.

subjects.description: Paper 1 is a written task in a specified text type, so register and format carry marks independently of grammar. Paper 2 covers listening and reading. The individual oral uses a visual stimulus at SL and a literary extract at HL, and preparation is usually too content-focused and not enough spoken.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Correctly labelled and shifted diagrams score separately from the prose around them. The portfolio of three commentaries uses real published articles and caps each at 800 words. HL Paper 3 is quantitative, where arithmetic slips cost more marks than conceptual gaps do.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two assessed components: the exhibition of three objects with a commentary capped at 950 words, and a 1,600-word essay on one of the prescribed titles. Students lose marks describing the objects rather than using them to explore the knowledge question they illustrate.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent 4,000-word research essay in a chosen subject, supervised in school and marked against criteria covering focus, knowledge, critical thinking, presentation and engagement. The research question is where most essays are decided; a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words cannot score well.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Included here because it is the course most often mismatched to a student. Calculator-permitted and statistics-led, with HL adding graph theory and matrices. Check the degree prerequisite first: several engineering and mathematics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches instead.

sections.heading: The radius calculation behind "near me"
paragraphs: Searching for an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah Village Triangle asks Google to rank by distance. It is worth seeing what that filter leaves you with. Dubai's private-school sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the IB at 7% of enrolment against UK curricula at 37%, Indian at 26% and US at 14%. The IB is a minority curriculum in a large market.

Now narrow it the way a search does. Take the population within a short drive of the Triangle. Keep only those connected to the IB rather than to a British or Indian curriculum. Keep only tutors, not students or parents. Keep only those who teach your child's subject. Keep only those who teach it at the level your child sits — HL and SL are different courses with different papers. Keep only those with a free slot in the narrow window between the school run and bedtime. Each filter cuts hard, and the last two cut hardest.

The honest result is that for a mainstream Diploma subject you may find a handful of credible local options, and for anything narrow you will find none. A Psychology HL student needing help with the quantitative methods content, or a Spanish B HL student preparing an individual oral on a literary extract, is not choosing from a list. They are hoping one exists within range.

Removing distance from the filter set does not lower the bar; it raises the number of candidates who clear it. That is the entire argument for online delivery in this market, and it is an argument about arithmetic rather than about technology.

sections.heading: The IB core: three bonus points and the deadlines nobody diarises
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points to a Diploma total out of 45. Three points is routinely the gap between a conditional offer met and missed, and yet the core is the part families most often leave entirely to the school. Subject tutoring gets funded; TOK does not.

The components are concrete. The TOK exhibition requires three objects and a commentary capped at 950 words, and the TOK essay is 1,600 words on one of the prescribed titles released for the session. The Extended Essay is an independent research essay with a 4,000-word upper limit, supervised in school and marked against criteria covering focus and method, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and engagement. Creativity, Activity, Service is not graded but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded.

The deadlines that bite are internal. Your school sets the dates for the EE research question, the first draft, the reflection sessions and the final submission, and those dates fall far earlier in DP1 and DP2 than most parents expect. By the time a family decides the Extended Essay needs help, the research question has often been locked for months and the real problem is a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words.

What a tutor can legitimately do here is narrower than in subject teaching, and worth stating precisely. They can interrogate a research question until it becomes answerable. They can check that a method will generate usable evidence. They can explain what each criterion credits using the official descriptors. They can read a draft the student wrote and name where it fails a criterion. They cannot write, rewrite, restructure by rewriting, or edit prose into a standard the student cannot produce. Every submitted word is the student's.

sections.heading: HL against SL, and what the difference costs in tutoring hours
paragraphs: Parents often assume Higher Level is the same course with harder questions. It is not. HL carries additional syllabus content, additional examination papers in most subjects, and in the sciences and mathematics an extra paper of a different type entirely. That changes the hours a tutor needs, which is why a quote for HL support is not a quote for SL support with a surcharge.

In the sciences, HL adds substantial content and a Paper 3 covering experimental technique and option material. In Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, HL Paper 3 is a two-question extended investigation worth 20% of the grade, unlike anything in the textbook and frequently absent from school mock papers. In History, HL adds Paper 3, three essays in two and a half hours on a regional option. In English A, HL adds a 1,200-1,500 word HL Essay on a studied text.

The practical consequence is about sequencing. An SL student short of a grade usually needs technique on existing content. An HL student short of a grade may need both technique and content that has not yet been taught, and if the examination is eight weeks away the honest answer is sometimes that the target is not reachable and a different target is. A tutor who agrees to any target you name is not giving you information.

The other consequence is subject choice. Three HLs is the requirement, and students choosing three HLs in the sciences and mathematics together take on the heaviest internal-assessment load in the Diploma: multiple investigation reports, all internally assessed, all due in overlapping windows set by the school.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates let you price the convenience of proximity directly. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is folded in. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150-300, and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or above. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work. At the entry end, Tutopiya publishes from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. BartyED sits at AED 650 for a premium named tutor. All figures are provider-published and were read in October 2026.

Subtract the bands and the travel premium is roughly AED 30-150 an hour over an equivalent online session. That buys a person in the room. It does not buy more teaching time, better subject knowledge or familiarity with HL Paper 3. In a market where the specialist pool is already thin, paying a premium that narrows the pool further is a difficult trade to defend on a Diploma grade.

There is also a hidden cost in session structure. A tutor spending forty to sixty minutes each way on Al Khail Road in term-time traffic will usually require a two-hour minimum booking to make the journey worthwhile. That removes the 45-minute session from the menu, which is often the right length for a focused component repair, and it fixes the latest workable start at roughly 18:30.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for one weekly hour come out at approximately AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support. Published packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. IB Gram publishes no fixed rate on this page because subject, level and urgency move it; the free diagnostic lesson comes before any quote.

sections.heading: In-home against online for a Triangle household
paragraphs: Both formats work; they work for different students. A Year 7 or 8 child who cannot yet hold attention on a screen does better with an adult sitting beside them. A student whose working needs physical correction as it is written benefits from presence. Parents who want to overhear the session find in-person easier to supervise. None of that is in dispute, and it is why the in-home market in Dubai is large and charges more.

For a Diploma student the balance usually tips the other way, and for a specific reason: the thing that limits the result is the match, not the medium. A DP2 student needs somebody who has taught their course at their level and read their mark schemes. The online format puts the whole field in reach; the in-home format puts whoever will drive into Jumeirah Village Triangle at five in reach.

Practical differences follow. Online sessions can be 45 or 60 minutes rather than a two-hour minimum. A 20:00 slot after a late school fixture is possible without anyone driving at night. Recordings mean a session on Extended Essay structure in October can be rewatched in February at no cost. A shared whiteboard the student writes on keeps working visible, which matters in mathematics and the sciences.
IB Gram offers only the online format in the UAE. Home visits are an India-only service. The table lays out both honestly so the decision rests on the trade rather than on a sales line.

sections.heading: KHDA, the schools near the Triangle and what a report really tells you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak and publishes the reports. The emirate's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six openings during 2025-26 and a 6% rise in enrolment.

The band at the top of a report is the least useful line in it. What is useful is the subject-level commentary, which often names the precise weakness in a cohort: attainment in mathematics, progress in Arabic as an additional language, the quality of students' independent research. If you are deciding which subject to fund tutoring in, that paragraph is better evidence than a grade on a child's report, because it tells you where the teaching itself is thin.

The second thing worth knowing is that the Dubai timetable is not fully international. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because expectations and language of instruction differ. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

A caution to close on. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to training institutes, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE office and makes no claim of approval or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge.

sections.heading: Getting matched, and what we say when nobody is free
paragraphs: Send three things: subject and level, the component that is weak, and a marked piece of work. A specialist then runs a free diagnostic lesson and sends a written note within a working day naming the error patterns and estimating the number of sessions. You decide after reading it; nothing is charged first. If the honest estimate is that the remaining time cannot reach your target, the note says that and suggests what can be reached.

Availability deserves a direct answer because no competitor in this market gives one. Mainstream Diploma subjects — Mathematics AA and AI, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, English A, Business Management, History — have deep cover for UAE evening slots and usually match in one to three working days. Narrow courses are a different matter: a minority Group 2 language at HL, a specific Computer Science option, a Career-related Programme reflective project. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before you book.

Scheduling around the Triangle is straightforward in practice. Families with children at Sunmarke School or Arcadia Global School inside the community can take 16:30 slots. Families driving back from Arabian Ranches, Dubai Hills or The Sustainable City generally want 17:30 or later. Ramadan moves sessions to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00, often at 45 minutes rather than an hour. Internal examination weeks are usually paused outright so the student owns their own evenings.

On permits, since parents ask and should. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here. The route is MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, no listed fee, two working days.

faqs.question: Why does searching "IB tutor near me" in JVT return so few real options?
faqs.answer: Because five filters stack. Dubai's private sector holds 387,441 students across 227 schools, and the IB accounts for 7% of enrolment against 37% for UK curricula. Narrow that to a neighbourhood-sized radius around Jumeirah Village Triangle, then to tutors rather than students, then to your child's subject, then to the level they sit, then to whoever is free between the school run and bedtime. Each cut is severe and the last two are the worst. For a mainstream subject you may find a handful; for anything narrow, often none. Removing distance from the filter set is what restores a real choice.

faqs.question: Do you send an IB tutor to a villa in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits in Dubai are widely available from independent tutors and agencies, priced at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and reaching AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included, but IB Gram does not provide them anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service. UAE families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a session recording. The trade is that you choose a tutor by what they have taught rather than by how far they will drive on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Should we be paying for Theory of Knowledge support at all?
faqs.answer: It is worth considering before subject tutoring in some cases. TOK and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points to a total out of 45, and three points frequently decides whether a conditional offer is met. The TOK essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title and the exhibition is three objects with a commentary capped at 950 words, so the volume of work is small and the leverage is high. The most common failure is writing about the objects or the title rather than about the knowledge question, which is a structural problem a tutor can name quickly.

faqs.question: When do Extended Essay deadlines actually fall for a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families plan for, and your school sets them rather than the IB. The sequence typically runs: subject and supervisor allocated, research question agreed, first formal reflection, full draft, final reflection, submission — spread across DP1 and the early part of DP2. By the time a parent concludes the Extended Essay needs help, the research question is often locked and the real problem is a question that cannot be answered inside 4,000 words. Ask your Diploma coordinator for the internal calendar in the first term of DP1 and work backwards from it.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level really just Standard Level with harder questions?
faqs.answer: No, and the assumption costs money. Higher Level carries additional syllabus content as well as additional papers. In the sciences HL adds a Paper 3 on experimental technique and option material. In Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, HL Paper 3 is a two-question extended investigation worth 20% of the grade. In History, HL adds three essays in 150 minutes on a regional option. In English A, HL adds a 1,200-1,500 word essay. That is why an HL student short of a grade may need content taught, not just technique repaired, and why the hours differ.

faqs.question: How much is the travel premium on a home visit in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Roughly AED 30-150 an hour, comparing published bands. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500 with travel included, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. What the premium buys is a person in the room. It does not buy additional teaching time or familiarity with HL Paper 3, and because it narrows the available pool to those willing to drive into JVT at five, it can reduce the quality of the match it is paying to improve.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child choose an Extended Essay research question?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the highest-value things a tutor legitimately does. A question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words produces an essay that cannot score well no matter how it is written, and students almost always start too broad. A tutor can interrogate a proposed question, test whether the evidence to answer it is obtainable, and push it until it is specific enough. What the tutor must not do is supply the question, write any part of the essay, or edit prose into a standard the student cannot produce themselves.

faqs.question: Are three Higher Level sciences a sensible combination?
faqs.answer: It is permitted and some students handle it, but understand the internal-assessment load before committing. Each Group 4 subject carries an internally assessed investigation worth 20% of its grade, all marked in school and moderated externally, and the school's deadlines for them tend to fall in overlapping windows. Add the Extended Essay and the TOK essay in the same period and DP2 becomes crowded in a way a timetable does not show. If the degree target only requires two sciences at HL, the third HL slot is often better spent elsewhere.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the May session dates on this page?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the IB itself. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, and an examination date is something a family plans a term around, so an unconfirmed one is worse than none. UAE candidates sit the May session; for the window, the results date and the candidate release time, ask your school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org directly. In practice the dates that constrain your child first are internal anyway: the school's own deadlines for internal assessments, Extended Essay drafts and the TOK exhibition.

faqs.question: Which schools near Jumeirah Village Triangle run the full IB continuum?
faqs.answer: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City and Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park are the closest full continuum options, running from the Primary Years Programme through to the Diploma. For the Diploma specifically, families also look at JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, North London Collegiate School Dubai and Emirates International School Meadows. None of these sits inside the Triangle itself, which is part of why a proximity search behaves oddly here. We name schools as market context only and have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Can we book sessions later than 19:00 on a school night?
faqs.answer: Yes, up to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and for Triangle families it is one of the more useful features of the online format. A student with a late school fixture, a music lesson or a long drive back from Arabian Ranches does not have to lose the week's session. Nobody is driving home afterwards either, which is the practical constraint that caps an in-home visit at roughly 18:30. Sessions can also run 45 minutes rather than an hour when the work is a single focused component, which suits a later start.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor you match is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: Tell us after the session and we change the match. The free diagnostic lesson exists partly for this: it lets you see the person teaching before any commitment, which is the opposite of the common market pattern where a tutor is allocated after payment. Fit is not only subject knowledge. A student who needs patience and a student who needs pace are badly served by each other's tutor. If a review against the next marked assessment shows no movement, changing the tutor is one of the three options we put on the table, alongside changing focus or closing the block.

faqs.question: Does Dubai's mandatory Arabic requirement apply at an IB school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate approval to teach those subjects. Practically, that load competes with Diploma work for the same evenings.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram registered or endorsed by KHDA in any way?
faqs.answer: No, and the phrasing matters. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises and staff in Dubai, requiring initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, occupies no UAE office or centre, and claims no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. This page explains what those bodies do because parents need to know; none of them endorses us, and any provider implying otherwise should be checked.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Diploma tutor start for a student in the Triangle?
faqs.answer: One to three working days for a mainstream course in a UAE evening slot — Mathematics AA and AI, the three sciences, Economics, English A, Business Management and History all have deep cover. Narrow courses take longer and sometimes cannot be filled from UAE-resident tutors: a minority Group 2 language at Higher Level, a particular Computer Science option, a Career-related Programme reflective project. Where that is the case, the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking rather than afterwards.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-villa.closingHeading: Drop the distance filter and keep the course filter
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-jumeirah-villa.closingBody: The useful question is not who teaches the IB near Jumeirah Village Triangle. It is who has taught your child's course at your child's level and read the mark schemes for the component that is losing marks. With the IB at 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, those two questions give very different answers, and only one of them improves a grade. Add the core to the list while you are at it: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three points and have the earliest deadlines in the Diploma. Send the subject, the level and a marked script, and take the free diagnostic lesson before committing to anything.

intro.heading: Why distance is the wrong filter for a Diploma tutor
paragraphs: Karama is one of the most walkable parts of Dubai and one of the most school-dense. A parent searching for a tutor nearby is applying a reasonable instinct from almost every other kind of service: find the competent person who is closest. For the IB Diploma that instinct produces a worse result than almost any other filter, because the Diploma is not one subject. It is six subjects at two different levels, plus a core worth three points, and a tutor who is excellent in one of those cells is useless in another.

Work through what the search actually returns. Within a short drive of Karama there will be tutors who teach maths well, several who cover IGCSE science, a few who have taught Diploma subjects at Standard Level, and very few who have taken a Higher Level subject through to final papers more than once or twice. If your child needs Economics HL paper technique or a Physics HL specialist, distance has filtered that person out and replaced them with whoever is available at five o'clock. The grade does not care how close the tutor lives.

The second problem with the proximity filter is that it quietly costs money. An in-home hour in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's rate table, with independent home tutors going to AED 500, and a substantial part of that premium is the car. Travel buys presence in the room, which matters for a ten-year-old and matters much less for a seventeen-year-old working through a past paper on a shared screen. In the Diploma, the money spent on travel is money not spent on subject depth.

Our position on this is fixed and worth stating before anything else. Every UAE lesson is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists in India only, and no tutor will arrive at a Karama address. The reason is the one above: we would rather match a Karama student to the right Higher Level specialist than to the nearest available generalist.

What follows is the Diploma itself rather than a pitch. How the 45 points are built and why 42 of them come from subjects. The pass conditions that sit behind the 24-point minimum, which catch families by surprise every year. The six groups and what the level choice inside them commits a student to. How Karama compares with Oud Metha, Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai, and why the comparison matters less than it looks. What the market charges, with every figure attributed. And where the academic-honesty line sits around the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-karama.programmesIntro: Karama and the neighbouring areas feed students into several routes, and the IB is only one of them. These are the programmes we teach around, with what each means for a family in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme

Subjects are graded 1 to 7 for a maximum of 42 points, with up to three further points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination, giving the familiar 45.

Because Diploma cohorts in old Dubai are concentrated in relatively few schools, Higher Level sets can be small, which is good for attention and bad for availability when a student needs catch-up help in a subject the school teaches to twelve people.

programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against published criteria rather than mark schemes, with a Personal Project in the final year. The MYP builds research and inquiry habits that the Extended Essay later rewards, and does not build the timed-paper discipline the Diploma assumes from the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Students arriving in a Karama-area Diploma class from an MYP school usually need exam technique before new content. Students arriving from IGCSE usually need the opposite. Knowing which route a student came through is the first useful thing a tutor learns, and it changes what the first six weeks contain.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE, as the route in
programmes.description: The dominant pre-Diploma route in old Dubai. IGCSE builds paper technique and content coverage but does not build the quantitative or essay-length demands of Higher Level subjects. The gap is predictable, subject by subject, and it can be closed in a short block of work before the Diploma begins rather than discovered in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Karama, Oud Metha and Al Mankhool have a heavy concentration of British and Indian-curriculum schools running IGCSE at 16. A student with strong IGCSE grades who then struggles in DP1 is the single most common enquiry we receive from this area, and it is almost never a lack of ability.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme and A Level alternatives
programmes.description: The Diploma is not the only honest answer at 16. A Career-related Programme, or A Levels with three or four subjects and no core requirements, suits some students better. A tutor who has watched a student fight the Diploma for a term is often well placed to say so, and the conversation belongs with the school's coordinator.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private sector ran 227 schools and 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curricula at 37% of enrolment against 7% on IB programmes, and seven more schools opening for the 2026-27 intake. dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-karama.subjectsIntro: A Diploma tutor is hired for a specific cell in a grid of six groups and two levels. These are the subjects most often requested from Karama and the neighbouring areas, with what actually costs marks in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The hardest subject to rescue late, because it is cumulative and the HL paper assumes two years of accumulated fluency. Marks are lost in proof structure, in calculus applications set in unfamiliar contexts, and in the exploration where a weak research question caps the mark before any mathematics is done.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy work. Students choose it expecting an easier course and meet a different difficulty: interpreting output and justifying a model in words. The HL route is substantial and should not be treated as the soft option some school corridors claim it is.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Punishes unit and uncertainty sloppiness harder than any other Group 4 subject. Fields and circular motion are the commonest HL stall points, and the internal investigation lives or dies on whether uncertainty was planned for at the design stage rather than bolted on afterwards.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Built on Structure and Reactivity themes with HL depth inside each. Multi-step enthalpy cycles, equilibrium justification and mechanism notation are where Higher Level marks go. The scientific investigation carries a fifth of the grade and is usually designed too broadly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest content volume in Group 4 and the subject most often revised by rereading notes. Extended response marks require explanation chains rather than fact lists, and data-based questions require interpretation rather than description.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline and command-term precision decide the grade. Students who draw a correct diagram and then fail to refer to it in the written answer lose marks they have already earned. HL adds quantitative work that catches students who chose Economics to avoid calculation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application rather than theory recall. The commonest failure is writing a textbook definition where the question asked for an evaluation of the organisation in the stimulus material. The internal assessment rewards a narrow, answerable research question.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under time pressure, and the skill is framing an argument quickly rather than noticing more devices. Students lose marks by cataloguing techniques without connecting them to meaning, and HL adds the written essay on a studied work.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay feed the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. Most TOK marks are lost on structure: a student who argues from examples rather than from knowledge questions writes a good essay for the wrong assessment.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words on a research question of the student's choice, supervised by a school-appointed supervisor. Failure is almost always scope: a question too broad to answer in the length or too narrow to sustain it. Our role is question shaping, source criticism and feedback on the student's own drafts.

sections.heading: What a near-me search actually buys, and what it costs you
paragraphs: A proximity search answers one question well: who can be physically present in this room soon. For a Diploma student that is rarely the binding problem. The binding problem is whether the person teaching has taken this subject at this level through to final papers and can read a mark scheme the way an examiner reads it. Proximity and subject depth are unrelated variables, and sorting by the first discards most of the second.

There is a measurable cost to the sort order too. The in-home premium in Dubai sits at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's published table, with independent home tutors quoted as high as AED 500, and most of the gap above the online specialist band is travel rather than teaching. A Karama family paying it is buying a car journey. For a seventeen-year-old working through a past paper on a shared screen, that journey adds nothing the lesson needed.

The reliability cost is smaller but it lands at the worst time. A tutor driving into Karama at five o'clock has come through some of the densest street parking in Dubai, and the lost fifteen or twenty minutes comes out of an hour that was paid in full. During the term when internal assessment deadlines and mocks collide, those sessions get shortened, moved or dropped. The table below sets out what proximity genuinely delivers against what it does not, because both columns are worth knowing before booking anything.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of 45 points
paragraphs: Most parents can name the number 45 and very few can say how it is assembled, which makes it hard to judge where tutoring money should go. Six subjects are each graded from 1 to 7, which gives a maximum of 42. The remaining three come from the combination of the Extended Essay grade and the Theory of Knowledge grade, read together on a published matrix. Creativity, Activity, Service carries no points at all but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded.

The consequence is that the core is worth about the same as a whole subject, and it is the part of the Diploma that receives the least structured teaching in most schools. A student who converts a C and a C into a B and a B across the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge can gain points more cheaply than by grinding a Higher Level subject from a 5 to a 6. For a family budgeting tutoring hours from Karama, that is a genuinely useful piece of arithmetic.

The second consequence concerns level choice. Three subjects are normally taken at Higher Level and three at Standard, and the points scale is identical in both. A 6 at Standard Level is worth exactly as many points as a 6 at Higher Level. Universities differentiate, which is why Higher Level choices matter for admission, but the Diploma total does not. Students carrying four Higher Levels for prestige rather than for an entry requirement are paying in workload for points they could get more safely.

sections.heading: The pass conditions behind the 24-point minimum
paragraphs: Twenty-four points is the headline threshold and it is not the whole requirement. A candidate can reach 24 and still not be awarded the Diploma, because several separate conditions sit alongside the total. A grade 1 in any subject blocks the award. So does more than a limited number of grade 2s, and more than a limited number of grades at 3 or below. Higher Level and Standard Level grades each carry their own minimum aggregate. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge cannot both sit at the bottom of the scale. Creativity, Activity, Service must be complete, and any finding of academic misconduct is disqualifying on its own.

This matters for how tutoring is bought, and it is the opposite of what most families do. The instinct is to put money into the strongest subject to push a 6 to a 7, because that is where progress feels visible. The arithmetic says to put it into the weakest subject first, because a grade 2 or a grade 1 does not just cost points, it can cost the Diploma outright. A student at risk in one subject and comfortable in five is in more danger than a student with five 5s and no risk anywhere.

The precise thresholds are published by the IB and are revised from time to time, so a family should confirm the current conditions with their school's Diploma coordinator rather than from any tutoring page, including this one. What a tutor can do is read the student's current grade profile against the shape of those conditions and say plainly where the risk sits. That conversation is usually fifteen minutes long and it changes how the next six months are spent.

sections.heading: The six groups, and the level decision inside them
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate takes one subject from each of six groups: studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the arts, with the arts replaceable by a second subject from another group. Three subjects are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard, and some schools permit four at Higher. The structure is fixed; the choices inside it are where students make the decisions they later regret.

The commonest regret in this cluster is a Higher Level subject chosen for prestige rather than for a university requirement. Higher Level carries more teaching hours, longer papers and deeper content, and the points scale gives it no advantage. If an intended degree does not demand the subject at Higher Level, the honest question is whether the student is more likely to reach a 6 at Standard than a 5 at Higher. The second regret is the mathematics route, where Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation lead to different university doors.

A tutor is often the first adult to look at this without an institutional interest. Schools have timetables and set sizes to fill, and university counsellors see the application rather than the weekly workload. Someone who has taught both levels of a subject can say what the gap between them actually feels like for a student with this particular profile, and can say it in DP1 when changing is still straightforward. A Karama family with a student halfway through DP1 and struggling in two Higher Level subjects should be having that conversation now rather than in the final year.

sections.heading: Karama against Oud Metha, Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai
paragraphs: Comparing these four neighbourhoods is useful precisely because the comparison comes out flat. Karama is walkable and school-dense with short school runs. Oud Metha next door holds some of the largest campuses in the city and most of the nearby IB provision. Al Mankhool is residential and central with quick access across the Creek. Bur Dubai is the oldest of the four in school terms, with heavy Indian-curriculum representation. Those are real differences and they affect a family's daily logistics.

None of them affect the Diploma. The subject grade scale is the same, the core matrix is the same, the internal assessment deadlines are set by the student's own school rather than by the emirate, and the exam session is the same one across all four. A student in Al Mankhool and a student in Karama sitting the same Higher Level subject face identical papers. The only variable that moves between the four is how far someone would have to drive to reach them, and that variable only matters if you insist on buying tuition by distance.

Where the neighbourhoods genuinely diverge is session timing. A Karama or Al Mankhool family with a walking school run can hold a four o'clock slot comfortably. A family commuting from Bur Dubai to a school across the Creek, or from Al Qusais to Festival City, is realistically looking at six or seven o'clock on a weekday. That is a scheduling fact rather than a quality difference, and it is the one piece of local knowledge that genuinely changes a tutoring plan.

sections.heading: What Diploma tutoring costs, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Separate the rate into the part that pays for teaching and the part that pays for a car, because the second is larger than most families assume. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one tutoring at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors sit lower: Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 and IB tutoring from AED 200. The difference between those bands is mostly travel time billed back to the family, and in a Diploma subject it buys no additional syllabus depth.

At the budget end, EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. That band buys guided practice during the hour and usually nothing between lessons, which is enough for a student who will not revise alone and not enough for a Higher Level gap. At the top, TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Monthly packages in this market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Three honest notes. These are market figures published by the named providers and read in October 2026; they are not IB Gram's price list, and we quote after the free trial because the number depends on subject, level and frequency. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. And for context on household budgets, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one, in-home, or a group class nearby
paragraphs: The three formats answer three different questions and families often buy the wrong one. A group class at a centre in Karama or Al Mankhool is a good purchase for broad revision coverage and for a student who works better in company. It is a poor purchase for a specific Higher Level gap, because the class moves at the group's pace and the gap survives. It is also a second journey at the end of a school day.

In-home one-to-one buys a person in the room, which genuinely helps younger students and students who cannot hold attention without someone beside them. The costs are the rate, the usual two-hour minimum, and the hostage-to-traffic problem. IB Gram does not sell this format in the UAE at all: home visits are an India-only service, and no tutor will come to a Karama address. We would rather state that in the first paragraph of a page than have a parent discover it after a booking call.

Online one-to-one is what we do sell here, and the argument for it in the Diploma is pool depth rather than convenience. A Karama student who needs Economics HL paper technique or Physics HL uncertainty work is matched to someone who teaches that cell of the grid, and the shared screen with a past paper on it is closer to the assessed task than a kitchen table is. Sessions start on the stated minute and the whiteboard is still there the next morning.

sections.heading: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and where a tutor must stop
paragraphs: The core is where the academic-honesty line gets tested, so it is worth drawing precisely. The Extended Essay is four thousand words on a research question the student chooses, with a school-appointed supervisor who has a formal role in the process. Theory of Knowledge comprises an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Together they are worth up to three points. Both are assessed as the student's own work and both are submitted through processes designed to detect work that is not.

A tutor may do a great deal here. Interrogating a research question until it is answerable in four thousand words is probably the highest-value single hour available on the Diploma, because scope errors cap the grade before the writing begins. Teaching how to read the assessment criteria, how to criticise a source, how to structure an argument around a knowledge question rather than around examples, and giving written feedback on a draft the student has produced, are all legitimate and all useful.

A tutor may not write, co-write, draft, restructure by rewriting, or edit to completion any part of the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, an internal assessment or any other assessed work, and may not supply a model essay to be adapted. Operators in this market sell completed internal assessments outright; that is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student, and a finding of misconduct is disqualifying for the whole Diploma. The downside risk is the entire qualification, which is why the line is not negotiable and why we state it rather than leaving it vague.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and what a Karama parent can check
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, so the regulator's role is broader than inspection alone.

Private tutoring is governed separately. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere we could read, so any amount quoted to a parent is unverified.

Two checks follow. The permit is free, so cost is never a legitimate reason for a tutor not to hold one, and the official route is MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service through its app, website and e-services system. And no individual tutor should be described as approved by a regulator: the KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises and is not what a one-to-one tutor holds. IB Gram does not hold one, operates no Dubai centre, and claims no endorsement from KHDA, the Ministry or any examination board. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school.
