process.title: Tell us the cell, not the subject
process.description: Which subject, at which level, and which year of the Diploma. Economics HL in DP2 and Economics SL in DP1 are different jobs needing different tutors. This single detail is what makes a first reply specific instead of generic.

process.title: Send the last marked work
process.description: A photographed marked paper or a returned internal assessment draft shows whether the loss is content, technique, structure or scope. A description of the problem from a parent is honest but second-hand, and the script is first-hand.

process.title: Free diagnostic hour
process.description: One hour one-to-one over live video at a Gulf Standard Time slot that fits the school day. The tutor works the weakest part of that script with the student and writes up what is costing marks and how long it realistically takes to recover.

process.title: Read the grade profile against the pass conditions
process.description: Fifteen minutes that most families have never had. Where the Diploma risk actually sits across six subjects and the core, and which subject should receive the next tutoring hour. It is often not the one the family expected.

process.title: Work set, marked and returned
process.description: Past-paper questions organised by paper rather than by topic, marked against the scheme with the reasoning shown. For core support, criterion-referenced feedback on drafts the student has written, with nothing rewritten.

process.title: Review every four sessions
process.description: Against school assessment results rather than against how the lessons feel. If the plan is not working the tutor or the plan changes, and we raise it rather than waiting for a parent to ask.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject and level
whyPoints.description: A Diploma request is matched to someone who teaches that subject at that level, not to whoever is free and nearby. For Higher Level subjects in old Dubai, the locally available pool is thin, and a travel-radius filter removes exactly the people a Higher Level student needs.

whyPoints.title: The pass conditions read properly
whyPoints.description: Twenty-four points is not the whole test, and most families have never seen the conditions that sit alongside it. Reading a student's grade profile against the shape of those conditions usually changes which subject gets the next hour of help.

whyPoints.title: The core treated as three real points
whyPoints.description: The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are worth about as much as a whole subject and receive the least structured teaching. Scoping a research question properly in DP1 is among the highest-return hours available on the entire course.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated in plain terms
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is written, co-written or supplied as a model. Operators in this market sell completed internal assessments; a misconduct finding can cost the whole Diploma, which is why we will not go near it.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, claims absent
whyPoints.description: Every AED rate here names the provider that published it and the month it was read. No invented satisfaction percentages, no self-assigned ratings, no grade guarantees, and no suggestion that KHDA, the Ministry or any examination board endorses us.

whyPoints.title: A free first hour, no card
whyPoints.description: The diagnostic hour costs nothing and nothing renews automatically. If the honest read is that the student needs the school's own support sessions and a past-paper routine rather than a paid tutor, that is what the written summary will say.

faqs.question: Is there an IB tutor near me in Karama, or will the tutor be online?
faqs.answer: Online. Every lesson for a UAE family runs one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we provide in India only, and no tutor will come to a Karama address. The reason is the one this page is built around: a Diploma grade depends on whether the tutor teaches that subject at that level, and hiring inside a travel radius filters for where someone lives rather than what they teach. The practical effect for you is a wider choice of specialists and a session that starts when it is supposed to.

faqs.question: How are the 45 Diploma points actually made up?
faqs.answer: Six subjects are each graded 1 to 7, giving a maximum of 42. The remaining three points come from the combination of the Extended Essay grade and the Theory of Knowledge grade, read together on a published matrix. Creativity, Activity, Service carries no points but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded. A point from a Standard Level subject is worth exactly as much as a point from a Higher Level one, which is why carrying extra Higher Levels without a university requirement buys workload rather than score.

faqs.question: Can my child reach 24 points and still not get the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this surprises families every year. Alongside the points total there are separate conditions: a grade 1 in any subject blocks the award, limits apply to the number of grade 2s and to grades of 3 or below, Higher and Standard Level grades each carry a minimum aggregate, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge cannot both sit at the bottom of the scale, Creativity, Activity, Service must be complete, and a misconduct finding is disqualifying. Confirm the current thresholds with your school's Diploma coordinator, since the IB revises them.

faqs.question: Which subject should we spend tutoring money on first?
faqs.answer: Usually the weakest, not the strongest, which is the opposite of most families' instinct. A very low grade in one subject can block the Diploma outright under the award conditions, while a 6 pushed to a 7 adds a single point. After the weakest subject, the next best value is often the core, because the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together are worth up to three points and receive the least structured teaching in most schools. A fifteen-minute read of the full grade profile usually reorders a family's priorities.

faqs.question: Do you tutor students at schools in Oud Metha and Bur Dubai too?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction barely exists online. Students we support in this cluster attend schools in Karama, Oud Metha, Al Mankhool, Bur Dubai, Deira and Al Garhoud, including The Indian High School in Oud Metha, Dubai Gem Private School, The Millennium School and Deira International School. Naming them implies no affiliation, partnership or endorsement of any kind. What matters operationally is that the tutor works to the student's own school assessment calendar, which differs between campuses even when the syllabus does not.

faqs.question: My child has strong IGCSE grades but is struggling in DP1. Why?
faqs.answer: It is the most common enquiry we receive from this part of Dubai and it is rarely about ability. IGCSE builds paper technique and content coverage; the Diploma assumes quantitative fluency, essay length and independent research habits that IGCSE does not require. Higher Level subjects compound all three at once, in the same term as the first internal assessment deadlines. The fix is usually a specific skills gap rather than a content gap, and identifying which gap takes one diagnostic hour with the student's own marked work in front of the tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may interrogate the research question until it is answerable in four thousand words, teach how to read the assessment criteria, criticise sources, discuss method, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not write, co-write, restructure by rewriting or edit to completion any part of it, and may not supply a model essay to adapt. The school-appointed supervisor keeps their formal role throughout. A misconduct finding is disqualifying for the Diploma, so the limits protect the student more than anyone.

faqs.question: Should my child take four Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Only if a university course actually requires the fourth one at Higher Level. The points scale treats Higher and Standard Level identically, so a 6 at Standard is worth as much as a 6 at Higher. A fourth Higher Level adds teaching hours, longer papers and deeper content across a timetable that already includes three internal assessments and the core. Students carrying it for prestige frequently finish with lower totals than they would have had on the standard combination. The decision belongs with the school's coordinator, with the university's published requirements in hand.

faqs.question: Which maths route should a Diploma student in Karama choose?
faqs.answer: It depends on the intended degree rather than on which course sounds easier. Analysis and Approaches is algebra and proof-heavy and is the route most engineering, mathematics and quantitative economics courses expect. Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling and technology-led, and is substantial in its own right rather than a soft option. Higher and Standard Level exist in both. Check the published entry requirements of the specific universities on the student's list for the year of entry, because they differ by country and they change.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Diploma families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One hour a week per subject is the common starting point, and it is enough for most situations if the work between lessons is actually done. Two sessions a week makes sense in the final stretch before papers, or where a single subject is at genuine risk under the award conditions. More than two subjects at once rarely works: four or five unfamiliar tutoring hours in a week displaces the independent study that converts teaching into marks. We would rather stabilise one subject and add the next a month later.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor know my child's school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Only if they ask, and that is a fair test of any tutor. Internal assessment deadlines in the Diploma are set by the school rather than by the IB, and they differ between campuses in the same neighbourhood. We ask for the school's assessment calendar at the start and plan backwards from it, because an internal assessment due in six weeks changes what this month's sessions should contain. A tutor who has not asked which school the student attends is planning against a generic timeline rather than the real one.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium in Dubai actually pay for?
faqs.answer: Mostly travel. Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour with independent tutors quoted to AED 500, while Unitors publishes online IB tutoring from AED 200 and TutorChase quotes AED 270. The gap buys a car journey and a person in the room. For a younger child that presence has real value. For a Diploma student working through a past paper on a shared screen it adds nothing the lesson needed, and the two-hour minimum typical of in-home bookings adds cost again. Those figures are the providers' own, read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tutoring in the final term of DP2?
faqs.answer: Worth doing, but the plan has to be honest about what fits. A final term can move paper technique, command-term discipline and two or three specific topics identified from a marked mock. It cannot rebuild two years of missing content, and a tutor who implies otherwise is selling rather than teaching. Where a late start pays best is a subject sitting just under a boundary, or a core component that has drifted. Where it pays worst is a Higher Level subject the student has been lost in since the first term.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free in the slot we need from Karama?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of filling the slot with a generalist. Three things usually resolve it. A different hour in the week, which works easily for Karama families with a short or walking school run. A tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus to Gulf Standard Time, with their location disclosed before the free trial rather than after booking. Or sequencing, starting with the subject doing the most damage and adding the second a month later. A Higher Level request is never staffed with a Standard Level-only tutor.

faqs.question: How do I verify that a private tutor in Dubai is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it is free, cost is never a reason for a tutor not to hold one. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts. Separately, no individual tutor can hold the KHDA permit, which is issued to institutes with premises.

dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-karama.closingHeading: Sort by subject and level, not by distance
dubai/ib-tutor-near-me-in-karama.closingBody: If your child is taking the IB Diploma at a school in or near Karama, the useful first message names the subject, the level and the year of the course, and carries a photograph of the last marked piece of work. The diagnostic hour that follows is free, runs one-to-one over live video at a Gulf Standard Time slot built around the school day, and ends with a written read on where the marks are going and where the Diploma risk actually sits across all six subjects. No card is needed to book it and nothing renews. If the honest answer is that a tutor is not what your child needs, we will say so.
